m.@GlobalScope.KEY_NONE: Enum value which doesn't correspond to any key. This is used to initialize Key properties with a generic state.
m.@GlobalScope.KEY_SPECIAL: Keycodes with this bit applied are non-printable.
m.@GlobalScope.METHOD_FLAG_OBJECT_CORE: Used internally. Allows to not dump core virtual methods (such as Object._notification()) to the JSON API.
m.@GlobalScope.METHOD_FLAG_VARARG: Flag for a method with a variable number of arguments.
m.@GlobalScope.METHOD_FLAG_VIRTUAL_REQUIRE: Flag for a virtual method that is required. In GDScript, this flag is set for abstract functions.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_ACTIVE_SENSING: MIDI message sent repeatedly while the MIDI device is idle, to tell the receiver that the connection is alive. Most MIDI devices do not send this message.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_AFTERTOUCH: MIDI message sent to indicate a change in pressure while a note is being pressed down, also called aftertouch.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_CHANNEL_PRESSU: MIDI message sent to indicate a change in pressure for the whole channel. Some MIDI devices may send this instead of MIDI_MESSAGE_AFTERTOUCH.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_CONTINUE: MIDI message sent to resume from the point the current sequence or song was paused.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_CONTROL_CHANGE: MIDI message sent when a controller value changes. In a MIDI device, a controller is any input that doesn't play notes. These may include sliders for volume, balance, and panning, as well as switches and pedals. See the General MIDI specification [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_MIDI#Controller_events] for a small list.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_NONE: Does not correspond to any MIDI message. This is the default value of InputEventMIDI.message.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_NOTE_OFF: MIDI message sent when a note is released.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_NOTE_ON: MIDI message sent when a note is pressed.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_PITCH_BEND: MIDI message sent when the value of the pitch bender changes, usually a wheel on the MIDI device.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_PROGRAM_CHANGE: MIDI message sent when the MIDI device changes its current instrument (also called program or preset).
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_QUARTER_FRAME: MIDI message sent every quarter frame to keep connected MIDI devices synchronized. Related to MIDI_MESSAGE_TIMING_CLOCK.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_SONG_POSITION_: MIDI message sent to jump onto a new position in the current sequence or song.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_SONG_SELECT: MIDI message sent to select a sequence or song to play.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_START: MIDI message sent to start the current sequence or song from the beginning.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_STOP: MIDI message sent to pause the current sequence or song.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_SYSTEM_EXCLUSI: MIDI system exclusive (SysEx) message. This type of message is not standardized and it's highly dependent on the MIDI device sending it.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_SYSTEM_RESET: MIDI message sent to reset a MIDI device to its default state, as if it was just turned on. It should not be sent when the MIDI device is being turned on.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_TIMING_CLOCK: MIDI message sent 24 times after MIDI_MESSAGE_QUARTER_FRAME, to keep connected MIDI devices synchronized.
m.@GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_TUNE_REQUEST: MIDI message sent to request a tuning calibration. Used on analog synthesizers. Most modern MIDI devices do not need this message.
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT: Primary mouse button, usually assigned to the left button.
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT: Primary mouse button mask, usually for the left button.
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_RIGHT: Secondary mouse button mask, usually for the right button.
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_NONE: Enum value which doesn't correspond to any mouse button. This is used to initialize MouseButton properties with a generic state.
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT: Secondary mouse button, usually assigned to the right button.
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_LEFT: Mouse wheel left button (only present on some mice).
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_RIGHT: Mouse wheel right button (only present on some mice).
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_XBUTTON1: Extra mouse button 1. This is sometimes present, usually to the sides of the mouse.
m.@GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_XBUTTON2: Extra mouse button 2. This is sometimes present, usually to the sides of the mouse.
m.@GlobalScope.OK: Methods that return Error return OK when no error occurred.
m.@GlobalScope.OP_MAX: Represents the size of the Variant.Operator enum.
m.@GlobalScope.OP_XOR: Logical XOR operator (not implemented in GDScript).
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_ARRAY_TYPE: Hints that a property is an Array with the stored type specified in the hint string. The hint string contains the type of the array (e.g. "String").
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_COLOR_NO_ALPH: Hints that a Color property should be edited without affecting its transparency (Color.a is not editable).
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_DICTIONARY_TY: Hints that a property is a Dictionary with the stored types specified in the hint string. The hint string contains the key and value types separated by a semicolon (e.g. "int;String").
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_DIR: Hints that a String property is a path to a directory. Editing it will show a file dialog for picking the path.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM: Hints that an int, String, or StringName property is an enumerated value to pick in a list specified via a hint string.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM_SUGGESTI: Hints that a String or StringName property can be an enumerated value to pick in a list specified via a hint string such as "Hello,Something,Else". See PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM for details.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_EXPRESSION: Hints that a String property is an Expression.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_EXP_EASING: Hints that a float property should be edited using a curve editor showing an exponential easing function. The hint string can include "attenuation" to flip the curve horizontally and/or "positive_only" to exclude in/out easing and limit values to be greater than or equal to zero. This displays differently to a property that uses PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE with the "exp" keyword, as it's edited with a sl…
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_FILE: Hints that a String property is a path to a file. Editing it will show a file dialog for picking the path. The hint string can be a set of filters with wildcards like "*.png,*.jpg". By default the file will be stored as UID whenever available. You can use ResourceUID methods to convert it back to path. For storing a raw path, use PROPERTY_HINT_FILE_PATH.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_FILE_PATH: Like PROPERTY_HINT_FILE, but the property is stored as a raw path, not UID. That means the reference will be broken if you move the file. Consider using PROPERTY_HINT_FILE when possible.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_FLAGS: Hints that an int property is a bitmask with named bit flags.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_GLOBAL_DIR: Hints that a String property is an absolute path to a directory outside the project folder. Editing it will show a file dialog for picking the path.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_GLOBAL_FILE: Hints that a String property is an absolute path to a file outside the project folder. Editing it will show a file dialog for picking the path. The hint string can be a set of filters with wildcards, like "*.png,*.jpg".
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_GLOBAL_SAVE_F: Hints that a String property is a path to a file. Editing it will show a file dialog for picking the path for the file to be saved at. The dialog has access to the entire filesystem. The hint string can be a set of filters with wildcards like "*.png,*.jpg". See also FileDialog.filters.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE: Hints that a boolean property will enable the feature associated with the group that it occurs in. The property will be displayed as a checkbox on the group header. Only works within a group or subgroup.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_HIDE_QUATERNI: Hints that a quaternion property should disable the temporary euler editor.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_INPUT_NAME: Hints that a String or StringName property is the name of an input action. This allows the selection of any action name from the Input Map in the Project Settings. The hint string may contain two options separated by commas:
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_INT_IS_OBJECT: Deprecated: This hint is not used by the engine.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_INT_IS_POINTE: Hints that an int property is a pointer. Used by GDExtension.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LAYERS_2D_NAV: Hints that an int property is a bitmask using the optionally named 2D navigation layers.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LAYERS_2D_PHY: Hints that an int property is a bitmask using the optionally named 2D physics layers.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LAYERS_2D_REN: Hints that an int property is a bitmask using the optionally named 2D render layers.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LAYERS_3D_NAV: Hints that an int property is a bitmask using the optionally named 3D navigation layers.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LAYERS_3D_PHY: Hints that an int property is a bitmask using the optionally named 3D physics layers.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LAYERS_3D_REN: Hints that an int property is a bitmask using the optionally named 3D render layers.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LAYERS_AVOIDA: Hints that an integer property is a bitmask using the optionally named avoidance layers.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LINK: Hints that a vector property should allow its components to be linked. For example, this allows Vector2.x and Vector2.y to be edited together. This hint is supported on Vector2, Vector2i, Vector3, Vector3i, Vector4, and Vector4i. The hint string can be used to specify a suffix indicating each value's unit with the "suffix:px/s" syntax.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LOCALE_ID: Hints that a string property is a locale code. Editing it will show a locale dialog for picking language and country.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_LOCALIZABLE_S: Hints that a dictionary property is string translation map. Dictionary keys are locale codes and, values are translated strings.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_MAX: Represents the size of the PropertyHint enum.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_MULTILINE_TEX: Hints that a String property is text with line breaks. Editing it will show a text input field where line breaks can be typed.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_NODE_PATH_TO_: Deprecated: This hint is not used by the engine.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_NODE_PATH_VAL: Hints that the hint string specifies valid node types for property of type NodePath.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_NODE_TYPE: Hints that a property is an instance of a Node-derived type, optionally specified via the hint string (e.g. "Node2D"). Editing it will show a dialog for picking a node from the scene.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_NONE: The property has no hint for the editor. However, the hint string is still read, which can be used to specify a suffix for a property that has no range limit (see PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE's description).
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_OBJECT_ID: Hints that the property's value is an object encoded as object ID, with its type specified in the hint string. Used by the debugger.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_OBJECT_TOO_BI: Hints that an object is too big to be sent via the debugger.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_ONESHOT: Hints that a property will be changed on its own after setting, such as AudioStreamPlayer.playing or GPUParticles3D.emitting.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_PASSWORD: Hints that a string property is a password, and every character is replaced with the secret character.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_PLACEHOLDER_T: Hints that a String property should show a placeholder text on its input field, if empty. The hint string is the placeholder text to use.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE: Hints that an int, float, or packed/typed Array property containing int or float types should be within a range specified via the hint string "min,max" or "min,max,step". The hint string can optionally include "or_greater" and/or "or_less" to allow manual input going respectively above the max or below the min values.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE: Hints that a property is an instance of a Resource-derived type, optionally specified via the hint string (e.g. "Texture2D"). Editing it will show a popup menu of valid resource types to instantiate.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_SAVE_FILE: Hints that a String property is a path to a file. Editing it will show a file dialog for picking the path for the file to be saved at. The dialog has access to the project's directory. The hint string can be a set of filters with wildcards like "*.png,*.jpg". See also FileDialog.filters.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_TOOL_BUTTON: Hints that a Callable property should be displayed as a clickable button. When the button is pressed, the callable is called. The hint string specifies the button text and optionally an icon from the "EditorIcons" theme type.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING: If a property is String, hints that the property represents a particular type (class). This allows to select a type from the create dialog. The property will store the selected type as a string.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_ALWAYS_DUPLI: When duplicating a resource with Resource.duplicate(), and this flag is set on a property of that resource, the property should always be duplicated, regardless of the subresources bool parameter.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_ARRAY: The property is the element count of a property array, i.e. a list of groups of related properties. Properties defined with this usage also need a specific class_name field in the form of label,prefix. The field may also include additional comma-separated options:
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_CATEGORY: Used to categorize properties together in the editor.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_CHECKABLE: The property can be checked in the EditorInspector.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_CHECKED: The property is checked in the EditorInspector.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_CLASS_IS_BIT: The property is a bitfield, i.e. it contains multiple flags represented as bits.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_CLASS_IS_ENU: The property is a variable of enum type, i.e. it only takes named integer constants from its associated enumeration.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_DEFERRED_SET: Deprecated: This flag is not used by the engine.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR: The property is shown in the EditorInspector (default for exported properties).
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR_BASIC: The property is considered a basic setting and will appear even when advanced mode is disabled. Used for project settings.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR_INSTA: When this property is a Resource and base object is a Node, a resource instance will be automatically created whenever the node is created in the editor.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_GROUP: Used to group properties together in the editor. See EditorInspector.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_HIGH_END_GFX: The property is only shown in the editor if modern renderers are supported (the Compatibility rendering method is excluded).
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_INTERNAL: The property is excluded from the class reference.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_KEYING_INCRE: Inserting an animation key frame of this property will automatically increment the value, allowing to easily keyframe multiple values in a row.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_NEVER_DUPLIC: When duplicating a resource with Resource.duplicate(), and this flag is set on a property of that resource, the property should never be duplicated, regardless of the subresources bool parameter.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_NIL_IS_VARIA: If property has nil as default value, its type will be Variant.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_NODE_PATH_FR: The NodePath property will always be relative to the scene's root. Mostly useful for local resources.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_NONE: The property is not stored, and does not display in the editor. This is the default for non-exported properties.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_NO_EDITOR: Default usage but without showing the property in the editor (storage).
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_NO_INSTANCE_: The property does not save its state in PackedScene.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_READ_ONLY: The property is read-only in the EditorInspector.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_RESOURCE_NOT: Use when a resource is created on the fly, i.e. the getter will always return a different instance. ResourceSaver needs this information to properly save such resources.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_RESTART_IF_C: Editing the property prompts the user for restarting the editor.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_DEFAU: Deprecated: This flag is not used by the engine.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIA: The property is a script variable. PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE can be used to distinguish between exported script variables from built-in variables (which don't have this usage flag). By default, PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE is not applied to variables that are created by overriding Object._get_property_list() in a script.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_SECRET: An export preset property with this flag contains confidential information and is stored separately from the rest of the export preset configuration.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE: The property is serialized and saved in the scene file (default for exported properties).
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_STORE_IF_NUL: The property value of type Object will be stored even if its value is null.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_SUBGROUP: Used to group properties together in the editor in a subgroup (under a group). See EditorInspector.
m.@GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_UPDATE_ALL_I: If this property is modified, all inspector fields will be refreshed.
m.@GlobalScope.SIDE_BOTTOM: Bottom side, usually used for Control or StyleBox-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.SIDE_LEFT: Left side, usually used for Control or StyleBox-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.SIDE_RIGHT: Right side, usually used for Control or StyleBox-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.SIDE_TOP: Top side, usually used for Control or StyleBox-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.TYPE_MAX: Represents the size of the Variant.Type enum.
m.@GlobalScope.UINT8_MAX: Maximum value of an 8-bit unsigned integer.
m.@GlobalScope.VERTICAL: General vertical alignment, usually used for Separator, ScrollBar, Slider, etc.
m.@GlobalScope.VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_BOTTOM: Vertical bottom alignment, usually for text-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER: Vertical center alignment, usually for text-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_FILL: Expand rows to fit height, usually for text-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_TOP: Vertical top alignment, usually for text-derived classes.
m.@GlobalScope.abs: Returns the absolute value of a Variant parameter x (i.e. non-negative value). Supported types: int, float, Vector2, Vector2i, Vector3, Vector3i, Vector4, Vector4i.
m.@GlobalScope.absf: Returns the absolute value of float parameter x (i.e. positive value).
m.@GlobalScope.absi: Returns the absolute value of int parameter x (i.e. positive value).
m.@GlobalScope.acos: Returns the arc cosine of x in radians. Use to get the angle of cosine x. x will be clamped between -1.0 and 1.0 (inclusive), in order to prevent acos() from returning @GDScript.NAN.
m.@GlobalScope.acosh: Returns the hyperbolic arc (also called inverse) cosine of x, returning a value in radians. Use it to get the angle from an angle's cosine in hyperbolic space if x is larger or equal to 1. For values of x lower than 1, it will return 0, in order to prevent acosh() from returning @GDScript.NAN.
m.@GlobalScope.angle_difference: Returns the difference between the two angles (in radians), in the range of [-PI, +PI]. When from and to are opposite, returns -PI if from is smaller than to, or PI otherwise.
m.@GlobalScope.asin: Returns the arc sine of x in radians. Use to get the angle of sine x. x will be clamped between -1.0 and 1.0 (inclusive), in order to prevent asin() from returning @GDScript.NAN.
m.@GlobalScope.asinh: Returns the hyperbolic arc (also called inverse) sine of x, returning a value in radians. Use it to get the angle from an angle's sine in hyperbolic space.
m.@GlobalScope.atan: Returns the arc tangent of x in radians. Use it to get the angle from an angle's tangent in trigonometry.
m.@GlobalScope.atan2: Returns the arc tangent of y/x in radians. Use to get the angle of tangent y/x. To compute the value, the method takes into account the sign of both arguments in order to determine the quadrant.
m.@GlobalScope.atanh: Returns the hyperbolic arc (also called inverse) tangent of x, returning a value in radians. Use it to get the angle from an angle's tangent in hyperbolic space if x is between -1 and 1 (non-inclusive).
m.@GlobalScope.bezier_derivative: Returns the derivative at the given t on a one-dimensional Bézier curve [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve] defined by the given control_1, control_2, and end points.
m.@GlobalScope.bezier_interpolate: Returns the point at the given t on a one-dimensional Bézier curve [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve] defined by the given control_1, control_2, and end points.
m.@GlobalScope.bytes_to_var: Decodes a byte array back to a Variant value, without decoding objects.
m.@GlobalScope.bytes_to_var_with_objects: Decodes a byte array back to a Variant value. Decoding objects is allowed.
m.@GlobalScope.ceil: Rounds x upward (towards positive infinity), returning the smallest whole number that is not less than x. Supported types: int, float, Vector2, Vector2i, Vector3, Vector3i, Vector4, Vector4i.
m.@GlobalScope.ceilf: Rounds x upward (towards positive infinity), returning the smallest whole number that is not less than x.
m.@GlobalScope.ceili: Rounds x upward (towards positive infinity), returning the smallest whole number that is not less than x.
m.@GlobalScope.clamp: Clamps the value, returning a Variant not less than min and not more than max. Any values that can be compared with the less than and greater than operators will work.
m.@GlobalScope.clampf: Clamps the value, returning a float not less than min and not more than max.
m.@GlobalScope.clampi: Clamps the value, returning an int not less than min and not more than max.
m.@GlobalScope.cos: Returns the cosine of angle angle_rad in radians.
m.@GlobalScope.cosh: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of x in radians.
m.@GlobalScope.cubic_interpolate: Cubic interpolates between two values by the factor defined in weight with pre and post values.
m.@GlobalScope.cubic_interpolate_angle: Cubic interpolates between two rotation values with shortest path by the factor defined in weight with pre and post values. See also lerp_angle().
m.@GlobalScope.cubic_interpolate_angle_in_: Cubic interpolates between two rotation values with shortest path by the factor defined in weight with pre and post values. See also lerp_angle().
m.@GlobalScope.cubic_interpolate_in_time: Cubic interpolates between two values by the factor defined in weight with pre and post values.
m.@GlobalScope.db_to_linear: Converts from decibels to linear energy (audio).
m.@GlobalScope.deg_to_rad: Converts an angle expressed in degrees to radians.
m.@GlobalScope.ease: Returns an "eased" value of x based on an easing function defined with curve. This easing function is based on an exponent. The curve can be any floating-point number, with specific values leading to the following behaviors:
m.@GlobalScope.error_string: Returns a human-readable name for the given Error code.
m.@GlobalScope.exp: The natural exponential function. It raises the mathematical constant e to the power of x and returns it.
m.@GlobalScope.floor: Rounds x downward (towards negative infinity), returning the largest whole number that is not more than x. Supported types: int, float, Vector2, Vector2i, Vector3, Vector3i, Vector4, Vector4i.
m.@GlobalScope.floorf: Rounds x downward (towards negative infinity), returning the largest whole number that is not more than x.
m.@GlobalScope.floori: Rounds x downward (towards negative infinity), returning the largest whole number that is not more than x.
m.@GlobalScope.fmod: Returns the floating-point remainder of x divided by y, keeping the sign of x.
m.@GlobalScope.fposmod: Returns the floating-point modulus of x divided by y, wrapping equally in positive and negative.
m.@GlobalScope.hash: Returns the integer hash of the passed variable.
m.@GlobalScope.instance_from_id: Returns the Object that corresponds to instance_id. All Objects have a unique instance ID. See also Object.get_instance_id().
m.@GlobalScope.inverse_lerp: Returns an interpolation or extrapolation factor considering the range specified in from and to, and the interpolated value specified in weight. The returned value will be between 0.0 and 1.0 if weight is between from and to (inclusive). If weight is located outside this range, then an extrapolation factor will be returned (return value lower than 0.0 or greater than 1.0). Use clamp() on the resu…
m.@GlobalScope.is_equal_approx: Returns true if a and b are approximately equal to each other.
m.@GlobalScope.is_finite: Returns whether x is a finite value, i.e. it is not @GDScript.NAN, positive infinity, or negative infinity. See also is_inf() and is_nan().
m.@GlobalScope.is_inf: Returns true if x is either positive infinity or negative infinity. See also is_finite() and is_nan().
m.@GlobalScope.is_instance_id_valid: Returns true if the Object that corresponds to id is a valid object (e.g. has not been deleted from memory). All Objects have a unique instance ID.
m.@GlobalScope.is_instance_valid: Returns true if instance is a valid Object (e.g. has not been deleted from memory).
m.@GlobalScope.is_nan: Returns true if x is a NaN ("Not a Number" or invalid) value. This method is needed as @GDScript.NAN is not equal to itself, which means x == NAN can't be used to check whether a value is a NaN.
m.@GlobalScope.is_same: Returns true, for value types, if a and b share the same value. Returns true, for reference types, if the references of a and b are the same.
m.@GlobalScope.is_zero_approx: Returns true if x is zero or almost zero. The comparison is done using a tolerance calculation with a small internal epsilon.
m.@GlobalScope.lerp: Linearly interpolates between two values by the factor defined in weight. To perform interpolation, weight should be between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). However, values outside this range are allowed and can be used to perform extrapolation. If this is not desired, use clampf() to limit weight.
m.@GlobalScope.lerp_angle: Linearly interpolates between two angles (in radians) by a weight value between 0.0 and 1.0.
m.@GlobalScope.lerpf: Linearly interpolates between two values by the factor defined in weight. To perform interpolation, weight should be between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). However, values outside this range are allowed and can be used to perform extrapolation. If this is not desired, use clampf() on the result of this function.
m.@GlobalScope.linear_to_db: Converts from linear energy to decibels (audio). Since volume is not normally linear, this can be used to implement volume sliders that behave as expected.
m.@GlobalScope.log: Returns the natural logarithm [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_logarithm] of x (base e [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_(mathematical_constant)], with e being approximately 2.71828). This is the amount of time needed to reach a certain level of continuous growth.
m.@GlobalScope.max: Returns the maximum of the given numeric values. This function can take any number of arguments.
m.@GlobalScope.maxf: Returns the maximum of two float values.
m.@GlobalScope.maxi: Returns the maximum of two int values.
m.@GlobalScope.min: Returns the minimum of the given numeric values. This function can take any number of arguments.
m.@GlobalScope.minf: Returns the minimum of two float values.
m.@GlobalScope.mini: Returns the minimum of two int values.
m.@GlobalScope.move_toward: Moves from toward to by the delta amount. Will not go past to.
m.@GlobalScope.nearest_po2: Returns the smallest integer power of 2 that is greater than or equal to value.
m.@GlobalScope.pingpong: Wraps value between 0 and the length. If the limit is reached, the next value the function returns is decreased to the 0 side or increased to the length side (like a triangle wave). If length is less than zero, it becomes positive.
m.@GlobalScope.posmod: Returns the integer modulus of x divided by y that wraps equally in positive and negative.
m.@GlobalScope.pow: Returns the result of base raised to the power of exp.
m.@GlobalScope.print: Converts one or more arguments of any type to string in the best way possible and prints them to the console.
m.@GlobalScope.print_rich: Converts one or more arguments of any type to string in the best way possible and prints them to the console.
m.@GlobalScope.print_verbose: If verbose mode is enabled (OS.is_stdout_verbose() returning true), converts one or more arguments of any type to string in the best way possible and prints them to the console.
m.@GlobalScope.printerr: Prints one or more arguments to strings in the best way possible to standard error line.
m.@GlobalScope.printraw: Prints one or more arguments to strings in the best way possible to the OS terminal. Unlike print(), no newline is automatically added at the end.
m.@GlobalScope.prints: Prints one or more arguments to the console with a space between each argument.
m.@GlobalScope.printt: Prints one or more arguments to the console with a tab between each argument.
m.@GlobalScope.push_error: Pushes an error message to Godot's built-in debugger and to the OS terminal.
m.@GlobalScope.push_warning: Pushes a warning message to Godot's built-in debugger and to the OS terminal.
m.@GlobalScope.rad_to_deg: Converts an angle expressed in radians to degrees.
m.@GlobalScope.rand_from_seed: Given a seed, returns a PackedInt64Array of size 2, where its first element is the randomized int value, and the second element is the same as seed. Passing the same seed consistently returns the same array.
m.@GlobalScope.randf: Returns a random floating-point value between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).
m.@GlobalScope.randf_range: Returns a random floating-point value between from and to (inclusive).
m.@GlobalScope.randfn: Returns a normally-distributed [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution], pseudo-random floating-point value from the specified mean and a standard deviation. This is also known as a Gaussian distribution.
m.@GlobalScope.randi: Returns a random unsigned 32-bit integer. Use remainder to obtain a random value in the interval [0, N - 1] (where N is smaller than 2^32).
m.@GlobalScope.randi_range: Returns a random signed 32-bit integer between from and to (inclusive). If to is lesser than from, they are swapped.
m.@GlobalScope.randomize: Randomizes the seed (or the internal state) of the random number generator. The current implementation uses a number based on the device's time.
m.@GlobalScope.remap: Maps a value from range [istart, istop] to [ostart, ostop]. See also lerp() and inverse_lerp(). If value is outside [istart, istop], then the resulting value will also be outside [ostart, ostop]. If this is not desired, use clamp() on the result of this function.
m.@GlobalScope.rid_allocate_id: Allocates a unique ID which can be used by the implementation to construct an RID. This is used mainly from native extensions to implement servers.
m.@GlobalScope.rid_from_int64: Creates an RID from a base. This is used mainly from native extensions to build servers.
m.@GlobalScope.rotate_toward: Rotates from toward to by the delta amount. Will not go past to.
m.@GlobalScope.round: Rounds x to the nearest whole number, with halfway cases rounded away from 0. Supported types: int, float, Vector2, Vector2i, Vector3, Vector3i, Vector4, Vector4i.
m.@GlobalScope.roundf: Rounds x to the nearest whole number, with halfway cases rounded away from 0.
m.@GlobalScope.roundi: Rounds x to the nearest whole number, with halfway cases rounded away from 0.
m.@GlobalScope.seed: Sets the seed for the random number generator to base. Setting the seed manually can ensure consistent, repeatable results for most random functions.
m.@GlobalScope.sign: Returns the same type of Variant as x, with -1 for negative values, 1 for positive values, and 0 for zeros. For nan values it returns 0.
m.@GlobalScope.signf: Returns -1.0 if x is negative, 1.0 if x is positive, and 0.0 if x is zero. For nan values of x it returns 0.0.
m.@GlobalScope.signi: Returns -1 if x is negative, 1 if x is positive, and 0 if x is zero.
m.@GlobalScope.sin: Returns the sine of angle angle_rad in radians.
m.@GlobalScope.sinh: Returns the hyperbolic sine of x.
m.@GlobalScope.smoothstep: Returns a smooth cubic Hermite interpolation between 0 and 1.
m.@GlobalScope.snapped: Returns the multiple of step that is the closest to x. This can also be used to round a floating-point number to an arbitrary number of decimals.
m.@GlobalScope.snappedf: Returns the multiple of step that is the closest to x. This can also be used to round a floating-point number to an arbitrary number of decimals.
m.@GlobalScope.snappedi: Returns the multiple of step that is the closest to x.
m.@GlobalScope.sqrt: Returns the square root of x, where x is a non-negative number.
m.@GlobalScope.step_decimals: Returns the position of the first non-zero digit, after the decimal point. Note that the maximum return value is 10, which is a design decision in the implementation.
m.@GlobalScope.str: Converts one or more arguments of any Variant type to a String in the best way possible.
m.@GlobalScope.str_to_var: Converts a formatted string that was returned by var_to_str() to the original Variant.
m.@GlobalScope.tan: Returns the tangent of angle angle_rad in radians.
m.@GlobalScope.tanh: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of x.
m.@GlobalScope.type_convert: Converts the given variant to the given type, using the Variant.Type values. This method is generous with how it handles types, it can automatically convert between array types, convert numeric Strings to int, and converting most things to String.
m.@GlobalScope.type_string: Returns a human-readable name of the given type, using the Variant.Type values.
m.@GlobalScope.typeof: Returns the internal type of the given variable, using the Variant.Type values.
m.@GlobalScope.var_to_bytes: Encodes a Variant value to a byte array, without encoding objects. Deserialization can be done with bytes_to_var().
m.@GlobalScope.var_to_bytes_with_objects: Encodes a Variant value to a byte array. Encoding objects is allowed (and can potentially include executable code). Deserialization can be done with bytes_to_var_with_objects().
m.@GlobalScope.var_to_str: Converts a Variant variable to a formatted String that can then be parsed using str_to_var().
m.@GlobalScope.weakref: Returns a WeakRef instance holding a weak reference to obj. Returns an empty WeakRef instance if obj is null. Prints an error and returns null if obj is neither Object-derived nor null.
m.@GlobalScope.wrap: Wraps the Variant value between min and max. min is inclusive while max is exclusive. This can be used for creating loop-like behavior or infinite surfaces.
m.@GlobalScope.wrapf: Wraps the float value between min and max. min is inclusive while max is exclusive. This can be used for creating loop-like behavior or infinite surfaces.
m.@GlobalScope.wrapi: Wraps the integer value between min and max. min is inclusive while max is exclusive. This can be used for creating loop-like behavior or infinite surfaces.
m.AABB.abs: Returns an AABB equivalent to this bounding box, with its width, height, and depth modified to be non-negative values.
m.AABB.encloses: Returns true if this bounding box completely encloses the with box. The edges of both boxes are included.
m.AABB.end: The ending point. This is usually the corner on the top-right and back of the bounding box, and is equivalent to position + size. Setting this point affects the size.
m.AABB.expand: Returns a copy of this bounding box expanded to align the edges with the given to_point, if necessary.
m.AABB.get_center: Returns the center point of the bounding box. This is the same as position + (size / 2.0).
m.AABB.get_endpoint: Returns the position of one of the 8 vertices that compose this bounding box. With an idx of 0 this is the same as position, and an idx of 7 is the same as end.
m.AABB.get_longest_axis: Returns the longest normalized axis of this bounding box's size, as a Vector3 (Vector3.RIGHT, Vector3.UP, or Vector3.BACK).
m.AABB.get_longest_axis_index: Returns the index to the longest axis of this bounding box's size (see Vector3.AXIS_X, Vector3.AXIS_Y, and Vector3.AXIS_Z).
m.AABB.get_longest_axis_size: Returns the longest dimension of this bounding box's size.
m.AABB.get_shortest_axis: Returns the shortest normalized axis of this bounding box's size, as a Vector3 (Vector3.RIGHT, Vector3.UP, or Vector3.BACK).
m.AABB.get_shortest_axis_index: Returns the index to the shortest axis of this bounding box's size (see Vector3.AXIS_X, Vector3.AXIS_Y, and Vector3.AXIS_Z).
m.AABB.get_shortest_axis_size: Returns the shortest dimension of this bounding box's size.
m.AABB.get_support: Returns the vertex's position of this bounding box that's the farthest in the given direction. This point is commonly known as the support point in collision detection algorithms.
m.AABB.get_volume: Returns the bounding box's volume. This is equivalent to size.x * size.y * size.z. See also has_volume().
m.AABB.grow: Returns a copy of this bounding box extended on all sides by the given amount by. A negative amount shrinks the box instead.
m.AABB.has_point: Returns true if the bounding box contains the given point. By convention, points exactly on the right, top, and front sides are not included.
m.AABB.has_surface: Returns true if this bounding box has a surface or a length, that is, at least one component of size is greater than 0. Otherwise, returns false.
m.AABB.has_volume: Returns true if this bounding box's width, height, and depth are all positive. See also get_volume().
m.AABB.intersection: Returns the intersection between this bounding box and with. If the boxes do not intersect, returns an empty AABB. If the boxes intersect at the edge, returns a flat AABB with no volume (see has_surface() and has_volume()).
m.AABB.intersects: Returns true if this bounding box overlaps with the box with. The edges of both boxes are always excluded.
m.AABB.intersects_plane: Returns true if this bounding box is on both sides of the given plane.
m.AABB.intersects_ray: Returns the first point where this bounding box and the given ray intersect, as a Vector3. If no intersection occurs, returns null.
m.AABB.intersects_segment: Returns the first point where this bounding box and the given segment intersect, as a Vector3. If no intersection occurs, returns null.
m.AABB.is_equal_approx: Returns true if this bounding box and aabb are approximately equal, by calling Vector3.is_equal_approx() on the position and the size.
m.AABB.is_finite: Returns true if this bounding box's values are finite, by calling Vector3.is_finite() on the position and the size.
m.AABB.merge: Returns an AABB that encloses both this bounding box and with around the edges. See also encloses().
m.AABB.position: The origin point. This is usually the corner on the bottom-left and forward of the bounding box.
m.AABB.size: The bounding box's width, height, and depth starting from position. Setting this value also affects the end point.
m.AESContext.MODE_CBC_DECRYPT: AES cipher block chaining decryption mode.
m.AESContext.MODE_CBC_ENCRYPT: AES cipher block chaining encryption mode.
m.AESContext.MODE_MAX: Maximum value for the mode enum.
m.AESContext.finish: Close this AES context so it can be started again. See start().
m.AESContext.get_iv_state: Get the current IV state for this context (IV gets updated when calling update()). You normally don't need this function.
m.AESContext.start: Start the AES context in the given mode. A key of either 16 or 32 bytes must always be provided, while an iv (initialization vector) of exactly 16 bytes, is only needed when mode is either MODE_CBC_ENCRYPT or MODE_CBC_DECRYPT.
m.AESContext.update: Run the desired operation for this AES context. Will return a PackedByteArray containing the result of encrypting (or decrypting) the given src. See start() for mode of operation.
m.AStar2D._compute_cost: Called when computing the cost between two connected points.
m.AStar2D._estimate_cost: Called when estimating the cost between a point and the path's ending point.
m.AStar2D._filter_neighbor: Called when neighboring enters processing and if neighbor_filter_enabled is true. If true is returned the point will not be processed.
m.AStar2D.add_point: Adds a new point at the given position with the given identifier. The id must be 0 or larger, and the weight_scale must be 0.0 or greater.
m.AStar2D.are_points_connected: Returns whether there is a connection/segment between the given points. If bidirectional is false, returns whether movement from id to to_id is possible through this segment.
m.AStar2D.clear: Clears all the points and segments.
m.AStar2D.connect_points: Creates a segment between the given points. If bidirectional is false, only movement from id to to_id is allowed, not the reverse direction.
m.AStar2D.disconnect_points: Deletes the segment between the given points. If bidirectional is false, only movement from id to to_id is prevented, and a unidirectional segment possibly remains.
m.AStar2D.get_available_point_id: Returns the next available point ID with no point associated to it.
m.AStar2D.get_closest_point: Returns the ID of the closest point to to_position, optionally taking disabled points into account. Returns -1 if there are no points in the points pool.
m.AStar2D.get_closest_position_in_segment: Returns the closest position to to_position that resides inside a segment between two connected points.
m.AStar2D.get_id_path: Returns an array with the IDs of the points that form the path found by AStar2D between the given points. The array is ordered from the starting point to the ending point of the path.
m.AStar2D.get_point_capacity: Returns the capacity of the structure backing the points, useful in conjunction with reserve_space().
m.AStar2D.get_point_connections: Returns an array with the IDs of the points that form the connection with the given point.
m.AStar2D.get_point_count: Returns the number of points currently in the points pool.
m.AStar2D.get_point_ids: Returns an array of all point IDs.
m.AStar2D.get_point_path: Returns an array with the points that are in the path found by AStar2D between the given points. The array is ordered from the starting point to the ending point of the path.
m.AStar2D.get_point_position: Returns the position of the point associated with the given id.
m.AStar2D.get_point_weight_scale: Returns the weight scale of the point associated with the given id.
m.AStar2D.has_point: Returns whether a point associated with the given id exists.
m.AStar2D.is_point_disabled: Returns whether a point is disabled or not for pathfinding. By default, all points are enabled.
m.AStar2D.neighbor_filter_enabled: If true enables the filtering of neighbors via _filter_neighbor().
m.AStar2D.remove_point: Removes the point associated with the given id from the points pool.
m.AStar2D.reserve_space: Reserves space internally for num_nodes points. Useful if you're adding a known large number of points at once, such as points on a grid.
m.AStar2D.set_point_disabled: Disables or enables the specified point for pathfinding. Useful for making a temporary obstacle.
m.AStar2D.set_point_position: Sets the position for the point with the given id.
m.AStar2D.set_point_weight_scale: Sets the weight_scale for the point with the given id. The weight_scale is multiplied by the result of _compute_cost() when determining the overall cost of traveling across a segment from a neighboring point to this point.

m.AStarGrid2D._compute_cost: Called when computing the cost between two connected points.
m.AStarGrid2D._estimate_cost: Called when estimating the cost between a point and the path's ending point.
m.AStarGrid2D.cell_shape: The cell shape. Affects how the positions are placed in the grid. If changed, update() needs to be called before finding the next path.
m.AStarGrid2D.cell_size: The size of the point cell which will be applied to calculate the resulting point position returned by get_point_path(). If changed, update() needs to be called before finding the next path.
m.AStarGrid2D.clear: Clears the grid and sets the region to Rect2i(0, 0, 0, 0).
m.AStarGrid2D.default_compute_heuristic: The default Heuristic which will be used to calculate the cost between two points if _compute_cost() was not overridden.
m.AStarGrid2D.default_estimate_heuristic: The default Heuristic which will be used to calculate the cost between the point and the end point if _estimate_cost() was not overridden.
m.AStarGrid2D.diagonal_mode: A specific DiagonalMode mode which will force the path to avoid or accept the specified diagonals.
m.AStarGrid2D.fill_solid_region: Fills the given region on the grid with the specified value for the solid flag.
m.AStarGrid2D.fill_weight_scale_region: Fills the given region on the grid with the specified value for the weight scale.
m.AStarGrid2D.get_id_path: Returns an array with the IDs of the points that form the path found by AStar2D between the given points. The array is ordered from the starting point to the ending point of the path.
m.AStarGrid2D.get_point_data_in_region: Returns an array of dictionaries with point data (id: Vector2i, position: Vector2, solid: bool, weight_scale: float) within a region.
m.AStarGrid2D.get_point_path: Returns an array with the points that are in the path found by AStarGrid2D between the given points. The array is ordered from the starting point to the ending point of the path.
m.AStarGrid2D.get_point_position: Returns the position of the point associated with the given id.
m.AStarGrid2D.get_point_weight_scale: Returns the weight scale of the point associated with the given id.
m.AStarGrid2D.is_dirty: Indicates that the grid parameters were changed and update() needs to be called.
m.AStarGrid2D.is_in_bounds: Returns true if the x and y is a valid grid coordinate (id), i.e. if it is inside region. Equivalent to region.has_point(Vector2i(x, y)).
m.AStarGrid2D.is_in_boundsv: Returns true if the id vector is a valid grid coordinate, i.e. if it is inside region. Equivalent to region.has_point(id).
m.AStarGrid2D.is_point_solid: Returns true if a point is disabled for pathfinding. By default, all points are enabled.
m.AStarGrid2D.jumping_enabled: Enables or disables jumping to skip up the intermediate points and speeds up the searching algorithm.
m.AStarGrid2D.offset: The offset of the grid which will be applied to calculate the resulting point position returned by get_point_path(). If changed, update() needs to be called before finding the next path.
m.AStarGrid2D.region: The region of grid cells available for pathfinding. If changed, update() needs to be called before finding the next path.
m.AStarGrid2D.set_point_solid: Disables or enables the specified point for pathfinding. Useful for making an obstacle. By default, all points are enabled.
m.AStarGrid2D.set_point_weight_scale: Sets the weight_scale for the point with the given id. The weight_scale is multiplied by the result of _compute_cost() when determining the overall cost of traveling across a segment from a neighboring point to this point.
m.AStarGrid2D.update: Updates the internal state of the grid according to the parameters to prepare it to search the path. Needs to be called if parameters like region, cell_size or offset are changed. is_dirty() will return true if this is the case and this needs to be called.
m.AcceptDialog.add_button: Adds a button with label text and a custom action to the dialog and returns the created button.

m.AcceptDialog.get_label: Returns the label used for built-in text.

m.AcceptDialog.register_text_enter: Registers a LineEdit in the dialog. When the enter key is pressed, the dialog will be accepted.
m.AcceptDialog.remove_button: Removes the button from the dialog. Does NOT free the button. The button must be a Button added with add_button() or add_cancel_button() method. After removal, pressing the button will no longer emit this dialog's custom_action or canceled signals.

m.AnimatedSprite2D.animation: The current animation from the sprite_frames resource. If this value is changed, the frame counter and the frame_progress are reset.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.animation_finished: Emitted when the animation reaches the end, or the start if it is played in reverse. When the animation finishes, it pauses the playback.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.autoplay: The key of the animation to play when the scene loads.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.centered: If true, texture will be centered.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.flip_h: If true, texture is flipped horizontally.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.flip_v: If true, texture is flipped vertically.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.frame: The displayed animation frame's index. Setting this property also resets frame_progress. If this is not desired, use set_frame_and_progress().
m.AnimatedSprite2D.frame_progress: The progress value between 0.0 and 1.0 until the current frame transitions to the next frame. If the animation is playing backwards, the value transitions from 1.0 to 0.0.

m.AnimatedSprite2D.is_playing: Returns true if an animation is currently playing (even if speed_scale and/or custom_speed are 0).
m.AnimatedSprite2D.pause: Pauses the currently playing animation. The frame and frame_progress will be kept and calling play() or play_backwards() without arguments will resume the animation from the current playback position.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.play: Plays the animation with key name. If custom_speed is negative and from_end is true, the animation will play backwards (which is equivalent to calling play_backwards()).
m.AnimatedSprite2D.play_backwards: Plays the animation with key name in reverse.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.set_frame_and_progress: Sets frame and frame_progress to the given values. Unlike setting frame, this method does not reset the frame_progress to 0.0 implicitly.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.speed_scale: The speed scaling ratio. For example, if this value is 1, then the animation plays at normal speed. If it's 0.5, then it plays at half speed. If it's 2, then it plays at double speed.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.sprite_frames: The SpriteFrames resource containing the animation(s). Allows you the option to load, edit, clear, make unique and save the states of the SpriteFrames resource.
m.AnimatedSprite2D.stop: Stops the currently playing animation. The animation position is reset to 0 and the custom_speed is reset to 1.0. See also pause().

m.AnimatedSprite3D.pause: Pauses the currently playing animation. The frame and frame_progress will be kept and calling play() or play_backwards() without arguments will resume the animation from the current playback position.
m.AnimatedSprite3D.play: Plays the animation with key name. If custom_speed is negative and from_end is true, the animation will play backwards (which is equivalent to calling play_backwards()).
m.AnimatedSprite3D.play_backwards: Plays the animation with key name in reverse.
m.AnimatedSprite3D.set_frame_and_progress: Sets frame and frame_progress to the given values. Unlike setting frame, this method does not reset the frame_progress to 0.0 implicitly.
m.AnimatedSprite3D.speed_scale: The speed scaling ratio. For example, if this value is 1, then the animation plays at normal speed. If it's 0.5, then it plays at half speed. If it's 2, then it plays at double speed.
m.AnimatedSprite3D.sprite_frames: The SpriteFrames resource containing the animation(s). Allows you the option to load, edit, clear, make unique and save the states of the SpriteFrames resource.
m.AnimatedSprite3D.stop: Stops the currently playing animation. The animation position is reset to 0 and the custom_speed is reset to 1.0. See also pause().
m.AnimatedTexture.MAX_FRAMES: The maximum number of frames supported by AnimatedTexture. If you need more frames in your animation, use AnimationPlayer or AnimatedSprite2D.
m.AnimatedTexture.current_frame: Sets the currently visible frame of the texture. Setting this frame while playing resets the current frame time, so the newly selected frame plays for its whole configured frame duration.
m.AnimatedTexture.frames: Number of frames to use in the animation. While you can create the frames independently with set_frame_texture(), you need to set this value for the animation to take new frames into account. The maximum number of frames is MAX_FRAMES.
m.AnimatedTexture.get_frame_duration: Returns the given frame's duration, in seconds.
m.AnimatedTexture.one_shot: If true, the animation will only play once and will not loop back to the first frame after reaching the end. Note that reaching the end will not set pause to true.
m.AnimatedTexture.pause: If true, the animation will pause where it currently is (i.e. at current_frame). The animation will continue from where it was paused when changing this property to false.
m.AnimatedTexture.set_frame_duration: Sets the duration of any given frame. The final duration is affected by the speed_scale. If set to 0, the frame is skipped during playback.
m.AnimatedTexture.set_frame_texture: Assigns a Texture2D to the given frame. Frame IDs start at 0, so the first frame has ID 0, and the last frame of the animation has ID frames - 1.
m.AnimatedTexture.speed_scale: The animation speed is multiplied by this value. If set to a negative value, the animation is played in reverse.
m.AnimationLibrary.add_animation: Adds the animation to the library, accessible by the key name.
m.AnimationLibrary.animation_added: Emitted when an Animation is added, under the key anim_name.
m.AnimationLibrary.animation_changed: Emitted when there's a change in one of the animations, e.g. tracks are added, moved or have changed paths. anim_name is the key of the animation that was changed.
m.AnimationLibrary.animation_removed: Emitted when an Animation stored with the key anim_name is removed.
m.AnimationLibrary.animation_renamed: Emitted when the key for an Animation is changed, from old_name to new_name.
m.AnimationLibrary.get_animation: Returns the Animation with the key name. If the animation does not exist, null is returned and an error is logged.
m.AnimationLibrary.get_animation_list: Returns the keys for the Animations stored in the library.
m.AnimationLibrary.get_animation_list_size: Returns the key count for the Animations stored in the library.
m.AnimationLibrary.has_animation: Returns true if the library stores an Animation with name as the key.
m.AnimationLibrary.remove_animation: Removes the Animation with the key name.
m.AnimationLibrary.rename_animation: Changes the key of the Animation associated with the key name to newname.
m.AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_D: An Animation.UPDATE_DISCRETE track value takes precedence when blending Animation.UPDATE_CONTINUOUS or Animation.UPDATE_CAPTURE track values and Animation.UPDATE_DISCRETE track values.
Always treat the Animation.UPDATE_DISCRETE track value as Animation.UPDATE_CONTINUOUS with Animation.INTERPOLATION_NEAREST. This is the default behavior for AnimationTree.

An Animation.UPDATE_CONTINUOUS or Animation.UPDATE_CAPTURE track value takes precedence when blending the Animation.UPDATE_CONTINUOUS or Animation.UPDATE_CAPTURE track values and the Animation.UPDATE_DISCRETE track values. This is the default behavior for AnimationPlayer.
m.AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_M: Batch method calls during the animation process, then do the calls after events are processed. This avoids bugs involving deleting nodes or modifying the AnimationPlayer while playing.
Make method calls immediately when reached in the animation.
m.AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_P: Process animation during process frames (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS).
Do not process animation. Use advance() to process the animation manually.
Process animation during physics frames (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS). This is especially useful when animating physics bodies.
m.AnimationMixer._post_process_key_value: A virtual function for processing after getting a key during playback.
m.AnimationMixer.active: If true, the AnimationMixer will be processing.
m.AnimationMixer.add_animation_library: Adds library to the animation player, under the key name.
m.AnimationMixer.advance: Manually advance the animations by the specified time (in seconds).
m.AnimationMixer.animation_finished: Notifies when an animation finished playing.
m.AnimationMixer.animation_libraries_updat: Notifies when the animation libraries have changed.
m.AnimationMixer.animation_list_changed: Notifies when an animation list is changed.
m.AnimationMixer.animation_started: Notifies when an animation starts playing.
m.AnimationMixer.audio_max_polyphony: The number of possible simultaneous sounds for each of the assigned AudioStreamPlayers.
m.AnimationMixer.caches_cleared: Notifies when the caches have been cleared, either automatically, or manually via clear_caches().
m.AnimationMixer.callback_mode_discrete: Ordinarily, tracks can be set to Animation.UPDATE_DISCRETE to update infrequently, usually when using nearest interpolation.
m.AnimationMixer.callback_mode_method: The call mode used for "Call Method" tracks.
m.AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process: The process notification in which to update animations.
m.AnimationMixer.capture: If the animation track specified by name has an option Animation.UPDATE_CAPTURE, stores current values of the objects indicated by the track path as a cache. If there is already a captured cache, the old cache is discarded.
m.AnimationMixer.clear_caches: AnimationMixer caches animated nodes. It may not notice if a node disappears; clear_caches() forces it to update the cache again.
m.AnimationMixer.deterministic: If true, the blending uses the deterministic algorithm. The total weight is not normalized and the result is accumulated with an initial value (0 or a "RESET" animation if present).
m.AnimationMixer.find_animation: Returns the key of animation or an empty StringName if not found.
m.AnimationMixer.find_animation_library: Returns the key for the AnimationLibrary that contains animation or an empty StringName if not found.
m.AnimationMixer.get_animation: Returns the Animation with the key name. If the animation does not exist, null is returned and an error is logged.
m.AnimationMixer.get_animation_library: Returns the first AnimationLibrary with key name or null if not found.
m.AnimationMixer.get_animation_library_lis: Returns the list of stored library keys.
m.AnimationMixer.get_animation_list: Returns the list of stored animation keys.
m.AnimationMixer.get_root_motion_position: Retrieve the motion delta of position with the root_motion_track as a Vector3 that can be used elsewhere.
m.AnimationMixer.get_root_motion_position_: Retrieve the blended value of the position tracks with the root_motion_track as a Vector3 that can be used elsewhere.
m.AnimationMixer.get_root_motion_rotation: Retrieve the motion delta of rotation with the root_motion_track as a Quaternion that can be used elsewhere.
m.AnimationMixer.get_root_motion_rotation_: Retrieve the blended value of the rotation tracks with the root_motion_track as a Quaternion that can be used elsewhere.
m.AnimationMixer.get_root_motion_scale: Retrieve the motion delta of scale with the root_motion_track as a Vector3 that can be used elsewhere.
m.AnimationMixer.get_root_motion_scale_acc: Retrieve the blended value of the scale tracks with the root_motion_track as a Vector3 that can be used elsewhere.
m.AnimationMixer.has_animation: Returns true if the AnimationMixer stores an Animation with key name.
m.AnimationMixer.has_animation_library: Returns true if the AnimationMixer stores an AnimationLibrary with key name.
m.AnimationMixer.mixer_applied: Notifies when the blending result related have been applied to the target objects.
m.AnimationMixer.mixer_updated: Notifies when the property related process have been updated.
m.AnimationMixer.remove_animation_library: Removes the AnimationLibrary associated with the key name.
m.AnimationMixer.rename_animation_library: Moves the AnimationLibrary associated with the key name to the key newname.
m.AnimationMixer.reset_on_save: This is used by the editor. If set to true, the scene will be saved with the effects of the reset animation (the animation with the key "RESET") applied as if it had been seeked to time 0, with the editor keeping the values that the scene had before saving.
m.AnimationMixer.root_motion_local: If true, get_root_motion_position() value is extracted as a local translation value before blending. In other words, it is treated like the translation is done after the rotation.
m.AnimationMixer.root_motion_track: The path to the Animation track used for root motion. Paths must be valid scene-tree paths to a node, and must be specified starting from the parent node of the node that will reproduce the animation. The root_motion_track uses the same format as Animation.track_set_path(), but note that a bone must be specified.
m.AnimationMixer.root_node: The node which node path references will travel from.
m.AnimationNode.FILTER_BLEND: Paths matching the filter will be blended (by the blend value).
m.AnimationNode.FILTER_PASS: Paths matching the filter will be allowed to pass.
m.AnimationNode.FILTER_STOP: Paths matching the filter will be discarded.
m.AnimationNode._get_caption: When inheriting from AnimationRootNode, implement this virtual method to override the text caption for this animation node.
m.AnimationNode._get_child_by_name: When inheriting from AnimationRootNode, implement this virtual method to return a child animation node by its name.
m.AnimationNode._get_child_nodes: When inheriting from AnimationRootNode, implement this virtual method to return all child animation nodes in order as a name: node dictionary.
m.AnimationNode._get_parameter_default_val: When inheriting from AnimationRootNode, implement this virtual method to return the default value of a parameter. Parameters are custom local memory used for your animation nodes, given a resource can be reused in multiple trees.
m.AnimationNode._get_parameter_list: When inheriting from AnimationRootNode, implement this virtual method to return a list of the properties on this animation node. Parameters are custom local memory used for your animation nodes, given a resource can be reused in multiple trees. Format is similar to Object.get_property_list().
m.AnimationNode._has_filter: When inheriting from AnimationRootNode, implement this virtual method to return whether the blend tree editor should display filter editing on this animation node.
m.AnimationNode._is_parameter_read_only: When inheriting from AnimationRootNode, implement this virtual method to return whether the parameter is read-only. Parameters are custom local memory used for your animation nodes, given a resource can be reused in multiple trees.
m.AnimationNode._process: Deprecated: Currently this is mostly useless as there is a lack of many APIs to extend AnimationNode by GDScript. It is planned that a more flexible API using structures will be provided in the future.
m.AnimationNode.add_input: Adds an input to the animation node. This is only useful for animation nodes created for use in an AnimationNodeBlendTree. If the addition fails, returns false.
m.AnimationNode.animation_node_removed: Emitted by nodes that inherit from this class and that have an internal tree when one of their animation nodes removes. The animation nodes that emit this signal are AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D, AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D, AnimationNodeStateMachine, and AnimationNodeBlendTree.
m.AnimationNode.animation_node_renamed: Emitted by nodes that inherit from this class and that have an internal tree when one of their animation node names changes. The animation nodes that emit this signal are AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D, AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D, AnimationNodeStateMachine, and AnimationNodeBlendTree.
m.AnimationNode.blend_animation: Blends an animation by blend amount (name must be valid in the linked AnimationPlayer). A time and delta may be passed, as well as whether seeked happened.
m.AnimationNode.blend_input: Blends an input. This is only useful for animation nodes created for an AnimationNodeBlendTree. The time parameter is a relative delta, unless seek is true, in which case it is absolute. A filter mode may be optionally passed.
m.AnimationNode.blend_node: Blend another animation node (in case this animation node contains child animation nodes). This function is only useful if you inherit from AnimationRootNode instead, otherwise editors will not display your animation node for addition.
m.AnimationNode.find_input: Returns the input index which corresponds to name. If not found, returns -1.
m.AnimationNode.get_input_count: Amount of inputs in this animation node, only useful for animation nodes that go into AnimationNodeBlendTree.
m.AnimationNode.get_input_name: Gets the name of an input by index.
m.AnimationNode.get_parameter: Gets the value of a parameter. Parameters are custom local memory used for your animation nodes, given a resource can be reused in multiple trees.
m.AnimationNode.get_processing_animation_t: Returns the object id of the AnimationTree that owns this node.
m.AnimationNode.is_path_filtered: Returns true if the given path is filtered.
m.AnimationNode.is_process_testing: Returns true if this animation node is being processed in test-only mode.
m.AnimationNode.node_updated: Experimental: This signal may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AnimationNode.remove_input: Removes an input, call this only when inactive.
m.AnimationNode.set_filter_path: Adds or removes a path for the filter.
m.AnimationNode.set_input_name: Sets the name of the input at the given input index. If the setting fails, returns false.
m.AnimationNode.set_parameter: Sets a custom parameter. These are used as local memory, because resources can be reused across the tree or scenes.
m.AnimationNode.tree_changed: Emitted by nodes that inherit from this class and that have an internal tree when one of their animation nodes changes. The animation nodes that emit this signal are AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D, AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D, AnimationNodeStateMachine, AnimationNodeBlendTree and AnimationNodeTransition.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.advance_on_start: If true, on receiving a request to play an animation from the start, the first frame is not drawn, but only processed, and playback starts from the next frame.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.animation: Animation to use as an output. It is one of the animations provided by AnimationTree.anim_player.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.loop_mode: If use_custom_timeline is true, override the loop settings of the original Animation resource with the value.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.play_mode: Determines the playback direction of the animation.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.start_offset: If use_custom_timeline is true, offset the start position of the animation.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.stretch_time_scal: If true, scales the time so that the length specified in timeline_length is one cycle.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.timeline_length: The length of the custom timeline.
m.AnimationNodeAnimation.use_custom_timeli: If true, AnimationNode provides an animation based on the Animation resource with some parameters adjusted.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.BLEND_MODE_DIS: The blend space plays the animation of the animation node which blending position is closest to. Useful for frame-by-frame 2D animations.
Similar to BLEND_MODE_DISCRETE, but starts the new animation at the last animation's playback position.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.BLEND_MODE_INT: The interpolation between animations is linear.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.SYNC_MODE_CYCL: All animations are time-scaled so they complete one cycle in cyclic_length seconds, keeping them in sync regardless of their individual lengths.
All animations are time-scaled so they stay in sync, with the cycle length dynamically computed from active blend weights. This is self-normalizing: a solo animation plays at normal speed.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.SYNC_MODE_INDE: Inactive animations advance with a weight of 0. This is equivalent to the previous sync = true behavior.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.SYNC_MODE_NONE: Inactive animations are frozen and do not advance.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.add_blend_poin: Adds a new point with name that represents a node on the virtual axis at a given position set by pos. You can insert it at a specific index using the at_index argument. If you use the default value for at_index, the point is inserted at the end of the blend points array.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.cyclic_length: The cycle length in seconds used by SYNC_MODE_CYCLIC_CONSTANT. All animations are time-scaled so they complete one full cycle in this duration. Must be greater than 0 for cyclic sync to take effect.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.find_blend_poi: Returns the index of the blend point with the given name. Returns -1 if no blend point with that name is found.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.get_blend_poin: Returns the number of points on the blend axis.
Returns the name of the blend point at index point.
Returns the AnimationNode referenced by the point at index point.
Returns the position of the point at index point.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.max_space: The blend space's axis's upper limit for the points' position. See add_blend_point().
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.min_space: The blend space's axis's lower limit for the points' position. See add_blend_point().
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.remove_blend_p: Removes the point at index point from the blend axis.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.reorder_blend_: Swaps the blend points at indices from_index and to_index, exchanging their positions and properties.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.set_blend_poin: Sets the name of the blend point at index point. If the name conflicts with an existing point, a unique name will be generated automatically.
Changes the AnimationNode referenced by the point at index point.
Updates the position of the point at index point on the blend axis.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.snap: Position increment to snap to when moving a point on the axis.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.sync_mode: Controls how animations are synced when blended. See SyncMode for available options.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D.value_label: Label of the virtual axis of the blend space.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.BLEND_MODE_DIS: The blend space plays the animation of the animation node which blending position is closest to. Useful for frame-by-frame 2D animations.
Similar to BLEND_MODE_DISCRETE, but starts the new animation at the last animation's playback position.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.BLEND_MODE_INT: The interpolation between animations is linear.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.SYNC_MODE_CYCL: All animations are time-scaled so they complete one cycle in cyclic_length seconds, keeping them in sync regardless of their individual lengths.
All animations are time-scaled so they stay in sync, with the cycle length dynamically computed from active blend weights. This is self-normalizing: a solo animation plays at normal speed.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.SYNC_MODE_INDE: Inactive animations advance with a weight of 0. This is equivalent to the previous sync = true behavior.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.SYNC_MODE_NONE: Inactive animations are frozen and do not advance.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.add_blend_poin: Adds a new point with name that represents a node at the position set by pos. You can insert it at a specific index using the at_index argument. If you use the default value for at_index, the point is inserted at the end of the blend points array.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.add_triangle: Creates a new triangle using three points x, y, and z. Triangles can overlap. You can insert the triangle at a specific index using the at_index argument. If you use the default value for at_index, the point is inserted at the end of the blend points array.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.auto_triangles: If true, the blend space is triangulated automatically. The mesh updates every time you add or remove points with add_blend_point() and remove_blend_point().
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.cyclic_length: The cycle length in seconds used by SYNC_MODE_CYCLIC_CONSTANT. All animations are time-scaled so they complete one full cycle in this duration. Must be greater than 0 for cyclic sync to take effect.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.find_blend_poi: Returns the index of the blend point with the given name. Returns -1 if no blend point with that name is found.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.get_blend_poin: Returns the number of points in the blend space.
Returns the name of the blend point at index point.
Returns the AnimationRootNode referenced by the point at index point.
Returns the position of the point at index point.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.get_triangle_c: Returns the number of triangles in the blend space.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.get_triangle_p: Returns the position of the point at index point in the triangle of index triangle.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.max_space: The blend space's X and Y axes' upper limit for the points' position. See add_blend_point().
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.min_space: The blend space's X and Y axes' lower limit for the points' position. See add_blend_point().
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.remove_blend_p: Removes the point at index point from the blend space.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.remove_triangl: Removes the triangle at index triangle from the blend space.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.reorder_blend_: Swaps the blend points at indices from_index and to_index, exchanging their positions and properties.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.set_blend_poin: Sets the name of the blend point at index point. If the name conflicts with an existing point, a unique name will be generated automatically.
Changes the AnimationNode referenced by the point at index point.
Updates the position of the point at index point in the blend space.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.snap: Position increment to snap to when moving a point.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.sync_mode: Controls how animations are synced when blended. See SyncMode for available options.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.triangles_upda: Emitted every time the blend space's triangles are created, removed, or when one of their vertices changes position.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.x_label: Name of the blend space's X axis.
m.AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.y_label: Name of the blend space's Y axis.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.add_node: Adds an AnimationNode at the given position. The name is used to identify the created sub animation node later.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.connect_node: Connects the output of an AnimationNode as input for another AnimationNode, at the input port specified by input_index.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.disconnect_node: Disconnects the animation node connected to the specified input.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.get_node: Returns the sub animation node with the specified name.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.get_node_list: Returns a list containing the names of all sub animation nodes in this blend tree.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.get_node_position: Returns the position of the sub animation node with the specified name.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.graph_offset: The global offset of all sub animation nodes.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.has_node: Returns true if a sub animation node with specified name exists.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.node_changed: Emitted when the input port information is changed.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.rename_node: Changes the name of a sub animation node.
m.AnimationNodeBlendTree.set_node_position: Modifies the position of a sub animation node.
m.AnimationNodeExtension._process_animatio: A version of the AnimationNode._process() method that is meant to be overridden by custom nodes. It returns a PackedFloat32Array with the processed animation data.
m.AnimationNodeExtension.get_remaining_tim: Returns the animation's remaining time for the given node info. For looping animations, it will only return the remaining time if break_loop is true, a large integer value will be returned otherwise.
m.AnimationNodeExtension.is_looping: Returns true if the animation for the given node_info is looping.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.MIX_MODE_ADD: Blends two animations additively. See also AnimationNodeAdd2.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.MIX_MODE_BLEND: Blends two animations. See also AnimationNodeBlend2.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_AB: The request to stop the animation connected to "shot" port.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FA: The request to fade out the animation connected to "shot" port.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FI: The request to play the animation connected to "shot" port.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_NO: The default state of the request. Nothing is done.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.abort_on_reset: If true, the sub-animation will abort if resumed with a reset after a prior interruption.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.autorestart: If true, the sub-animation will restart automatically after finishing.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.autorestart_delay: The delay after which the automatic restart is triggered, in seconds.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.autorestart_random_: If autorestart is true, a random additional delay (in seconds) between 0 and this value will be added to autorestart_delay.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.break_loop_at_end: If true, breaks the loop at the end of the loop cycle for transition, even if the animation is looping.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.fadein_curve: Determines how cross-fading between animations is eased. If empty, the transition will be linear. Should be a unit Curve.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.fadein_time: The fade-in duration. For example, setting this to 1.0 for a 5 second length animation will produce a cross-fade that starts at 0 second and ends at 1 second during the animation.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.fadeout_curve: Determines how cross-fading between animations is eased. If empty, the transition will be linear. Should be a unit Curve.
m.AnimationNodeOneShot.fadeout_time: The fade-out duration. For example, setting this to 1.0 for a 5 second length animation will produce a cross-fade that starts at 4 second and ends at 5 second during the animation.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.STATE_MACHINE_: This is a grouped state machine that can be controlled from a parent state machine. It does not work independently. There must be a state machine with state_machine_type of STATE_MACHINE_TYPE_ROOT or STATE_MACHINE_TYPE_NESTED in the parent or ancestor.

Seeking to the beginning is treated as seeking to the beginning of the animation in the current state. Transition to the end state, or the absence of transitions in each state, is treated as exiting the state machine.
Seeking to the beginning is treated as playing from the start state. Transition to the end state is treated as exiting the state machine.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.add_node: Adds a new animation node to the graph. The position is used for display in the editor.
