m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.add_transition: Adds a transition between the given animation nodes.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.allow_transiti: If true, allows teleport to the self state with AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.travel(). When the reset option is enabled in AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.travel(), the animation is restarted. If false, nothing happens on the teleportation to the self state.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.get_graph_offs: Returns the draw offset of the graph. Used for display in the editor.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.get_node: Returns the animation node with the given name.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.get_node_list: Returns a list containing the names of all animation nodes in this state machine.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.get_node_name: Returns the given animation node's name.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.get_node_posit: Returns the given animation node's coordinates. Used for display in the editor.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.get_transition: Returns the number of connections in the graph.
Returns the given transition's start node.
Returns the given transition's end node.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.has_node: Returns true if the graph contains the given animation node.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.has_transition: Returns true if there is a transition between the given animation nodes.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.remove_node: Deletes the given animation node from the graph.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.remove_transit: Deletes the transition between the two specified animation nodes.
Deletes the given transition by index.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.replace_node: Replaces the given animation node with a new animation node.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.reset_ends: If true, treat the cross-fade to the start and end nodes as a blend with the RESET animation.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.set_graph_offs: Sets the draw offset of the graph. Used for display in the editor.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.set_node_posit: Sets the animation node's coordinates. Used for display in the editor.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachine.state_machine_: This property can define the process of transitions for different use cases. See also StateMachineType.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.get_cu: Returns the currently playing animation state.
Returns the playback position within the current animation state.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.get_fa: Returns the playback state length of the node from get_fading_from_node(). Returns 0 if no animation fade is occurring.
Returns the starting state of currently fading animation.
Returns the playback position of the node from get_fading_from_node(). Returns 0 if no animation fade is occurring.
Returns the length of the current fade animation. Returns 0 if no animation fade is occurring.
Returns the playback position of the current fade animation. Returns 0 if no animation fade is occurring.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.get_tr: Returns the current travel path as computed internally by the A* algorithm.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.is_pla: Returns true if an animation is playing.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.next: If there is a next path by travel or auto advance, immediately transitions from the current state to the next state.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.state_: Emitted when the state finishes playback. If state is a state machine set to grouped mode, its signals are passed through with its name prefixed.
Emitted when the state starts playback. If state is a state machine set to grouped mode, its signals are passed through with its name prefixed.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.travel: Transitions from the current state to another one, following the shortest path.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.ADVA: Automatically use this transition if the advance_condition and advance_expression checks are true (if assigned).
m.AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.SWIT: Wait for the current state playback to end, then switch to the beginning of the next state animation.
Switch to the next state immediately. The current state will end and blend into the beginning of the new one.
Switch to the next state immediately, but will seek the new state to the playback position of the old state.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.adva: Turn on auto advance when this condition is set. The provided name will become a boolean parameter on the AnimationTree that can be controlled from code (see Using AnimationTree). For example, if AnimationTree.tree_root is an AnimationNodeStateMachine and advance_condition is set to "idle":

Use an expression as a condition for state machine transitions. It is possible to create complex animation advance conditions for switching between states and gives much greater flexibility for creating complex state machines by directly interfacing with the script code.

Determines whether the transition should be disabled, enabled when using AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.travel(), or traversed automatically if the advance_condition and advance_expression checks are true (if assigned).
m.AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.brea: If true, breaks the loop at the end of the loop cycle for transition, even if the animation is looping.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.prio: Lower priority transitions are preferred when travelling through the tree via AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.travel() or advance_mode is set to ADVANCE_MODE_AUTO.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.rese: If true, the destination animation is played back from the beginning when switched.
m.AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.xfad: Ease curve for better control over cross-fade between this state and the next. Should be a unit Curve.
The time to cross-fade between this state and the next.
m.AnimationNodeSync.sync: If false, the blended animations' frame are stopped when the blend value is 0.
m.AnimationNodeTimeSeek.explicit_elapse: If true, some processes are executed to handle keys between seeks, such as calculating root motion and finding the nearest discrete key.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.allow_transition: If true, allows transition to the self state. When the reset option is enabled in input, the animation is restarted. If false, nothing happens on the transition to the self state.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.input_count: The number of enabled input ports for this animation node.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.is_input_loop_br: Returns whether the animation breaks the loop at the end of the loop cycle for transition.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.is_input_reset: Returns whether the animation restarts when the animation transitions from the other animation.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.is_input_set_as_: Returns true if auto-advance is enabled for the given input index.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.set_input_as_aut: Enables or disables auto-advance for the given input index. If enabled, state changes to the next input after playing the animation once. If enabled for the last input state, it loops to the first.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.set_input_break_: If true, breaks the loop at the end of the loop cycle for transition, even if the animation is looping.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.set_input_reset: If true, the destination animation is restarted when the animation transitions.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.xfade_curve: Determines how cross-fading between animations is eased. If empty, the transition will be linear. Should be a unit Curve.
m.AnimationNodeTransition.xfade_time: Cross-fading time (in seconds) between each animation connected to the inputs.
m.AnimationPlayer.animation_changed: Emitted when a queued animation plays after the previous animation finished. See also queue().
m.AnimationPlayer.animation_get_next: Returns the key of the animation which is queued to play after the animation_from animation.
m.AnimationPlayer.animation_set_next: Triggers the animation_to animation when the animation_from animation completes.
m.AnimationPlayer.assigned_animation: If playing, the current animation's key, otherwise, the animation last played. When set, this changes the animation, but will not play it unless already playing. See also current_animation.
m.AnimationPlayer.autoplay: The key of the animation to play when the scene loads.
m.AnimationPlayer.current_animation: The key of the currently playing animation. If no animation is playing, the property's value is an empty string. Changing this value does not restart the animation. See play() for more information on playing animations.
m.AnimationPlayer.current_animation_length: The length (in seconds) of the currently playing animation.
m.AnimationPlayer.current_animation_positi: The position (in seconds) of the currently playing animation.
m.AnimationPlayer.get_blend_time: Returns the blend time (in seconds) between two animations, referenced by their keys.
m.AnimationPlayer.get_playing_speed: Returns the actual playing speed of current animation or 0 if not playing. This speed is the speed_scale property multiplied by custom_speed argument specified when calling the play() method.
m.AnimationPlayer.get_queue: Returns a list of the animation keys that are currently queued to play.
m.AnimationPlayer.get_section_end_time: Returns the end time of the section currently being played.
m.AnimationPlayer.get_section_start_time: Returns the start time of the section currently being played.
m.AnimationPlayer.has_section: Returns true if an animation is currently playing with a section.
m.AnimationPlayer.is_animation_active: Returns true if the an animation is currently active. An animation is active if it was played by calling play() and was not finished yet, or was stopped by calling stop().
m.AnimationPlayer.is_playing: Returns true if an animation is currently playing (even if speed_scale and/or custom_speed are 0).
m.AnimationPlayer.movie_quit_on_finish: If true and the engine is running in Movie Maker mode (see MovieWriter), exits the engine with SceneTree.quit() as soon as an animation is done playing in this AnimationPlayer. A message is printed when the engine quits for this reason.
m.AnimationPlayer.pause: Pauses the currently playing animation. The current_animation_position will be kept and calling play() or play_backwards() without arguments or with the same animation name as assigned_animation will resume the animation.
m.AnimationPlayer.play: Plays the animation with key name. Custom blend times and speed can be set.
m.AnimationPlayer.play_backwards: Plays the animation with key name in reverse.
m.AnimationPlayer.play_section: Plays the animation with key name and the section starting from start_time and ending on end_time. See also play().
m.AnimationPlayer.play_section_backwards: Plays the animation with key name and the section starting from start_time and ending on end_time in reverse.
m.AnimationPlayer.play_section_with_marker: Plays the animation with key name and the section starting from start_marker and ending on end_marker.
Plays the animation with key name and the section starting from start_marker and ending on end_marker in reverse.
m.AnimationPlayer.playback_auto_capture: If true, performs AnimationMixer.capture() before playback automatically. This means just play_with_capture() is executed with default arguments instead of play().
m.AnimationPlayer.playback_auto_capture_ea: The ease type of the capture interpolation. See also EaseType.
m.AnimationPlayer.playback_auto_capture_tr: The transition type of the capture interpolation. See also TransitionType.
m.AnimationPlayer.playback_default_blend_t: The default time in which to blend animations. Ranges from 0 to 4096 with 0.01 precision.
m.AnimationPlayer.queue: Queues an animation for playback once the current animation and all previously queued animations are done.
m.AnimationPlayer.reset_section: Resets the current section. Does nothing if a section has not been set.
m.AnimationPlayer.seek: Seeks the animation to the seconds point in time (in seconds). If update is true, the animation updates too, otherwise it updates at process time. Events between the current frame and seconds are skipped.
m.AnimationPlayer.set_blend_time: Specifies a blend time (in seconds) between two animations, referenced by their keys.
m.AnimationPlayer.set_section: Changes the start and end times of the section being played. The current playback position will be clamped within the new section. See also play_section().
m.AnimationPlayer.set_section_with_markers: Changes the start and end markers of the section being played. The current playback position will be clamped within the new section. See also play_section_with_markers().
m.AnimationPlayer.speed_scale: The speed scaling ratio. For example, if this value is 1, then the animation plays at normal speed. If it's 0.5, then it plays at half speed. If it's 2, then it plays at double speed.
m.AnimationPlayer.stop: Stops the currently playing animation. The animation position is reset to 0 and the custom_speed is reset to 1.0. See also pause().
m.AnimationTree.advance_expression_base_no: The path to the Node used to evaluate the AnimationNode Expression if one is not explicitly specified internally.
m.AnimationTree.anim_player: The path to the AnimationPlayer used for animating.
m.AnimationTree.animation_player_changed: Emitted when the anim_player is changed.
m.AnimationTree.tree_root: The root animation node of this AnimationTree. See AnimationRootNode.
m.Area2D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_COMBINE: This area adds its gravity/damping values to whatever has been calculated so far (in priority order).
m.Area2D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_COMBINE_REPLACE: This area adds its gravity/damping values to whatever has been calculated so far (in priority order), ignoring any lower priority areas.
m.Area2D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_DISABLED: This area does not affect gravity/damping.
m.Area2D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_REPLACE: This area replaces any gravity/damping, even the defaults, ignoring any lower priority areas.
m.Area2D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_REPLACE_COMBINE: This area replaces any gravity/damping calculated so far (in priority order), but keeps calculating the rest of the areas.
m.Area2D.angular_damp: The rate at which objects stop spinning in this area. Represents the angular velocity lost per second.
m.Area2D.angular_damp_space_override: Override mode for angular damping calculations within this area.
m.Area2D.area_entered: Emitted when the received area enters this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.area_exited: Emitted when the received area exits this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.area_shape_entered: Emitted when a Shape2D of the received area enters a shape of this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.area_shape_exited: Emitted when a Shape2D of the received area exits a shape of this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.audio_bus_name: The name of the area's audio bus.
m.Area2D.audio_bus_override: If true, the area's audio bus overrides the default audio bus.
m.Area2D.body_entered: Emitted when the received body enters this area. body can be a PhysicsBody2D or a TileMap. TileMaps are detected if their TileSet has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.body_exited: Emitted when the received body exits this area. body can be a PhysicsBody2D or a TileMap. TileMaps are detected if their TileSet has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.body_shape_entered: Emitted when a Shape2D of the received body enters a shape of this area. body can be a PhysicsBody2D or a TileMap. TileMaps are detected if their TileSet has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.body_shape_exited: Emitted when a Shape2D of the received body exits a shape of this area. body can be a PhysicsBody2D or a TileMap. TileMaps are detected if their TileSet has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area2D.get_overlapping_areas: Returns a list of intersecting Area2Ds. The overlapping area's CollisionObject2D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject2D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area2D.get_overlapping_bodies: Returns a list of intersecting PhysicsBody2Ds and TileMaps. The overlapping body's CollisionObject2D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject2D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area2D.gravity: The area's gravity intensity (in pixels per second squared). This value multiplies the gravity direction. This is useful to alter the force of gravity without altering its direction.
m.Area2D.gravity_point: If true, gravity is calculated from a point (set via gravity_point_center). See also gravity_space_override.
m.Area2D.gravity_point_center: If gravity is a point (see gravity_point), this will be the point of attraction.
m.Area2D.gravity_point_unit_distance: The distance at which the gravity strength is equal to gravity. For example, on a planet 100 pixels in radius with a surface gravity of 4.0 px/s², set the gravity to 4.0 and the unit distance to 100.0. The gravity will have falloff according to the inverse square law, so in the example, at 200 pixels from the center the gravity will be 1.0 px/s² (twice the distance, 1/4th the gravity), at 50 pixe…
m.Area2D.gravity_space_override: Override mode for gravity calculations within this area.
m.Area2D.has_overlapping_areas: Returns true if intersecting any Area2Ds, otherwise returns false. The overlapping area's CollisionObject2D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject2D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area2D.has_overlapping_bodies: Returns true if intersecting any PhysicsBody2Ds or TileMaps, otherwise returns false. The overlapping body's CollisionObject2D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject2D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area2D.linear_damp: The rate at which objects stop moving in this area. Represents the linear velocity lost per second.
m.Area2D.linear_damp_space_override: Override mode for linear damping calculations within this area.
m.Area2D.monitorable: If true, other monitoring areas can detect this area.
m.Area2D.monitoring: If true, the area detects bodies or areas entering and exiting it.
m.Area2D.overlaps_area: Returns true if the given Area2D intersects or overlaps this Area2D, false otherwise.
m.Area2D.overlaps_body: Returns true if the given physics body intersects or overlaps this Area2D, false otherwise.
m.Area2D.priority: The area's priority. Higher priority areas are processed first. The World2D's physics is always processed last, after all areas.
m.Area3D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_COMBINE: This area adds its gravity/damping values to whatever has been calculated so far (in priority order).
m.Area3D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_COMBINE_REPLACE: This area adds its gravity/damping values to whatever has been calculated so far (in priority order), ignoring any lower priority areas.
m.Area3D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_DISABLED: This area does not affect gravity/damping.
m.Area3D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_REPLACE: This area replaces any gravity/damping, even the defaults, ignoring any lower priority areas.
m.Area3D.SPACE_OVERRIDE_REPLACE_COMBINE: This area replaces any gravity/damping calculated so far (in priority order), but keeps calculating the rest of the areas.
m.Area3D.angular_damp: The rate at which objects stop spinning in this area. Represents the angular velocity lost per second.
m.Area3D.angular_damp_space_override: Override mode for angular damping calculations within this area.
m.Area3D.area_entered: Emitted when the received area enters this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.area_exited: Emitted when the received area exits this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.area_shape_entered: Emitted when a Shape3D of the received area enters a shape of this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.area_shape_exited: Emitted when a Shape3D of the received area exits a shape of this area. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.audio_bus_name: The name of the area's audio bus.
m.Area3D.audio_bus_override: If true, the area's audio bus overrides the default audio bus.
m.Area3D.body_entered: Emitted when the received body enters this area. body can be a PhysicsBody3D, SoftBody3D or GridMap. GridMaps are detected if their MeshLibrary has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.body_exited: Emitted when the received body exits this area. body can be a PhysicsBody3D, SoftBody3D or GridMap. GridMaps are detected if their MeshLibrary has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.body_shape_entered: Emitted when a Shape3D of the received body enters a shape of this area. body can be a PhysicsBody3D, SoftBody3D or GridMap. GridMaps are detected if their MeshLibrary has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.body_shape_exited: Emitted when a Shape3D of the received body exits a shape of this area. body can be a PhysicsBody3D, SoftBody3D or GridMap. GridMaps are detected if their MeshLibrary has collision shapes configured. Requires monitoring to be set to true.
m.Area3D.get_overlapping_areas: Returns a list of intersecting Area3Ds. The overlapping area's CollisionObject3D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject3D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area3D.get_overlapping_bodies: Returns a list of intersecting PhysicsBody3Ds, SoftBody3Ds, and GridMaps. The overlapping body's CollisionObject3D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject3D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area3D.gravity: The area's gravity intensity (in meters per second squared). This value multiplies the gravity direction. This is useful to alter the force of gravity without altering its direction.
m.Area3D.gravity_point: If true, gravity is calculated from a point (set via gravity_point_center). See also gravity_space_override.
m.Area3D.gravity_point_center: If gravity is a point (see gravity_point), this will be the point of attraction.
m.Area3D.gravity_point_unit_distance: The distance at which the gravity strength is equal to gravity. For example, on a planet 100 meters in radius with a surface gravity of 4.0 m/s², set the gravity to 4.0 and the unit distance to 100.0. The gravity will have falloff according to the inverse square law, so in the example, at 200 meters from the center the gravity will be 1.0 m/s² (twice the distance, 1/4th the gravity), at 50 meters…
m.Area3D.gravity_space_override: Override mode for gravity calculations within this area.
m.Area3D.has_overlapping_areas: Returns true if intersecting any Area3Ds, otherwise returns false. The overlapping area's CollisionObject3D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject3D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area3D.has_overlapping_bodies: Returns true if intersecting any PhysicsBody3Ds, SoftBody3Ds, or GridMaps, otherwise returns false. The overlapping body's CollisionObject3D.collision_layer must be part of this area's CollisionObject3D.collision_mask in order to be detected.
m.Area3D.linear_damp: The rate at which objects stop moving in this area. Represents the linear velocity lost per second.
m.Area3D.linear_damp_space_override: Override mode for linear damping calculations within this area.
m.Area3D.monitorable: If true, other monitoring areas can detect this area.
m.Area3D.monitoring: If true, the area detects bodies or areas entering and exiting it.
m.Area3D.overlaps_area: Returns true if the given Area3D intersects or overlaps this Area3D, false otherwise.
m.Area3D.overlaps_body: Returns true if the given physics body intersects or overlaps this Area3D, false otherwise.
m.Area3D.priority: The area's priority. Higher priority areas are processed first. The World3D's physics is always processed last, after all areas.
m.Area3D.reverb_bus_amount: The degree to which this area applies reverb to its associated audio. Ranges from 0 to 1 with 0.1 precision.
m.Area3D.reverb_bus_enabled: If true, the area applies reverb to its associated audio.
m.Area3D.reverb_bus_name: The name of the reverb bus to use for this area's associated audio.
m.Area3D.reverb_bus_uniformity: The degree to which this area's reverb is a uniform effect. Ranges from 0 to 1 with 0.1 precision.
m.Area3D.wind_attenuation_factor: The exponential rate at which wind force decreases with distance from its origin.
m.Area3D.wind_force_magnitude: The magnitude of area-specific wind force.
m.Area3D.wind_source_path: The Node3D which is used to specify the direction and origin of an area-specific wind force. The direction is opposite to the z-axis of the Node3D's local transform, and its origin is the origin of the Node3D's local transform.
m.AreaLight3D.area_attenuation: Controls the distance attenuation function for this area light.
m.AreaLight3D.area_normalize_energy: Defines whether the energy is normalized (divided) by the surface area of the light. If set to true, changing the size does not affect the total energy output, and does not dramatically alter the brightness of the scene.
m.AreaLight3D.area_range: The range of the area in meters. This determines the maximum distance from any point on the area at which the area can still emit light.
m.AreaLight3D.area_size: The extents (width and height) of the area in meters.
m.AreaLight3D.area_texture: An optional texture to use as a light source. Changing the texture at runtime might impact performance, as it needs to be drawn to the area light atlas with filtered mipmaps.
m.Array.all: Calls the given Callable on each element in the array and returns true if the Callable returns true for all elements in the array. If the Callable returns false for one array element or more, this method returns false.
m.Array.any: Calls the given Callable on each element in the array and returns true if the Callable returns true for one or more elements in the array. If the Callable returns false for all elements in the array, this method returns false.
m.Array.append_array: Appends another array at the end of this array.
m.Array.assign: Assigns elements of another array into the array. Resizes the array to match array. Performs type conversions if the array is typed.
m.Array.back: Returns the last element of the array. If the array is empty, fails and returns null. See also front().
m.Array.bsearch: Returns the index of value in the sorted array. If it cannot be found, returns where value should be inserted to keep the array sorted. The algorithm used is binary search [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_search_algorithm].
m.Array.bsearch_custom: Returns the index of value in the sorted array. If it cannot be found, returns where value should be inserted to keep the array sorted (using func for the comparisons). The algorithm used is binary search [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_search_algorithm].
m.Array.clear: Removes all elements from the array. This is equivalent to using resize() with a size of 0.
m.Array.count: Returns the number of times an element is in the array.
m.Array.duplicate: Returns a new copy of the array.
m.Array.duplicate_deep: Duplicates this array, deeply, like duplicate() when passing true, with extra control over how subresources are handled.
m.Array.erase: 移除指定值的所有出现。
m.Array.fill: Assigns the given value to all elements in the array.
m.Array.filter: Calls the given Callable on each element in the array and returns a new, filtered Array.
m.Array.find: Returns the index of the first occurrence of what in this array, or -1 if there are none. The search's start can be specified with from, continuing to the end of the array.
m.Array.find_custom: Returns the index of the first element in the array that causes method to return true, or -1 if there are none. The search's start can be specified with from, continuing to the end of the array.
m.Array.front: Returns the first element of the array. If the array is empty, fails and returns null. See also back().
m.Array.get: Returns the element at the given index in the array. If index is out-of-bounds or negative, this method fails and returns null.
m.Array.get_typed_builtin: Returns the built-in Variant type of the typed array as a Variant.Type constant. If the array is not typed, returns @GlobalScope.TYPE_NIL. See also is_typed().
m.Array.get_typed_class_name: Returns the built-in class name of the typed array, if the built-in Variant type @GlobalScope.TYPE_OBJECT. Otherwise, returns an empty StringName. See also is_typed() and Object.get_class().
m.Array.get_typed_script: Returns the Script instance associated with this typed array, or null if it does not exist. See also is_typed().
m.Array.has: Returns true if the array contains the given value.
m.Array.hash: Returns a hashed 32-bit integer value representing the array and its contents.
m.Array.insert: Inserts a new element (value) at a given index (position) in the array. position should be between 0 and the array's size(). If negative, position is considered relative to the end of the array.
m.Array.is_empty: Returns true if the array is empty ([]). See also size().
m.Array.is_read_only: Returns true if the array is read-only. See make_read_only().
m.Array.is_same_typed: Returns true if this array is typed the same as the given array. See also is_typed().
m.Array.is_typed: Returns true if the array is typed. Typed arrays can only contain elements of a specific type, as defined by the typed array constructor. The methods of a typed array are still expected to return a generic Variant.
m.Array.make_read_only: Makes the array read-only. The array's elements cannot be overridden with different values, and their order cannot change. Does not apply to nested elements, such as dictionaries.
m.Array.map: Calls the given Callable for each element in the array and returns a new array filled with values returned by the method.
m.Array.max: Returns the maximum value contained in the array, if all elements can be compared. Otherwise, returns null. See also min().
m.Array.min: Returns the minimum value contained in the array, if all elements can be compared. Otherwise, returns null. See also max().
m.Array.pick_random: Returns a random element from the array. Generates an error and returns null if the array is empty.
m.Array.pop_at: Removes and returns the element of the array at index position. If negative, position is considered relative to the end of the array. Returns null if the array is empty. If position is out of bounds, an error message is also generated.
m.Array.pop_front: Removes and returns the first element of the array. Returns null if the array is empty, without generating an error. See also pop_back().
m.Array.push_back: Appends an element at the end of the array. See also push_front().
m.Array.push_front: Adds an element at the beginning of the array. See also push_back().
m.Array.reduce: Calls the given Callable for each element in array, accumulates the result in accum, then returns it.
m.Array.remove_at: Removes the element from the array at the given index (position). If the index is out of bounds, this method fails. If the index is negative, position is considered relative to the end of the array.
m.Array.resize: Sets the array's number of elements to size. If size is smaller than the array's current size, the elements at the end are removed. If size is greater, new default elements (usually null) are added, depending on the array's type.
m.Array.reverse: Reverses the order of all elements in the array.
m.Array.rfind: Returns the index of the last occurrence of what in this array, or -1 if there are none. The search's start can be specified with from, continuing to the beginning of the array. This method is the reverse of find().
m.Array.rfind_custom: Returns the index of the last element of the array that causes method to return true, or -1 if there are none. The search's start can be specified with from, continuing to the beginning of the array. This method is the reverse of find_custom().
m.Array.set: Sets the value of the element at the given index to the given value. This will not change the size of the array, it only changes the value at an index already in the array. This is the same as using the [] operator (array[index] = value).
m.Array.shuffle: Shuffles all elements of the array in a random order.
m.Array.slice: Returns a new Array containing this array's elements, from index begin (inclusive) to end (exclusive), every step elements.
m.Array.sort: Sorts the array in ascending order. The final order is dependent on the "less than" (<) comparison between elements.
m.Array.sort_custom: Sorts the array using a custom Callable.
m.ArrayMesh.add_blend_shape: Adds name for a blend shape that will be added with add_surface_from_arrays(). Must be called before surface is added.
m.ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays: Creates a new surface. Mesh.get_surface_count() will become the surf_idx for this new surface.
m.ArrayMesh.clear_blend_shapes: Removes all blend shapes from this ArrayMesh.
m.ArrayMesh.clear_surfaces: Removes all surfaces from this ArrayMesh.
m.ArrayMesh.custom_aabb: Overrides the AABB with one defined by user for use with frustum culling. Especially useful to avoid unexpected culling when using a shader to offset vertices.
m.ArrayMesh.get_blend_shape_count: Returns the number of blend shapes that the ArrayMesh holds.
m.ArrayMesh.get_blend_shape_name: Returns the name of the blend shape at this index.
m.ArrayMesh.lightmap_unwrap: Performs a UV unwrap on the ArrayMesh to prepare the mesh for lightmapping.
m.ArrayMesh.regen_normal_maps: Regenerates tangents for each of the ArrayMesh's surfaces.
m.ArrayMesh.set_blend_shape_name: Sets the name of the blend shape at this index.
m.ArrayMesh.shadow_mesh: An optional mesh which can be used for rendering shadows and the depth prepass. Can be used to increase performance by supplying a mesh with fused vertices and only vertex position data (without normals, UVs, colors, etc.).
m.ArrayMesh.surface_find_by_name: Returns the index of the first surface with this name held within this ArrayMesh. If none are found, -1 is returned.
m.ArrayMesh.surface_get_array_index_len: Returns the length in indices of the index array in the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays()).
m.ArrayMesh.surface_get_array_len: Returns the length in vertices of the vertex array in the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays()).
m.ArrayMesh.surface_get_format: Returns the format mask of the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays()).
m.ArrayMesh.surface_get_name: Gets the name assigned to this surface.
m.ArrayMesh.surface_get_primitive_type: Returns the primitive type of the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays()).
m.ArrayMesh.surface_remove: Removes the surface at the given index from the Mesh, shifting surfaces with higher index down by one.
m.ArrayMesh.surface_set_name: Sets a name for a given surface.
m.ArrayMesh.surface_update_attribute_regio: Updates the attribute buffer of this mesh's surface with the given data. The expected data per attribute is 12 or 8 bytes (4 bytes per float, 2 floats per Vector2, and 3 floats per Vector3) depending on if the mesh is using Vector3 or Vector2 vertices. This value can be determined with RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_format_attribute_stride().
m.ArrayMesh.surface_update_skin_region: Updates the skin buffer of this mesh's surface with the given data. The expected data per skin is 12 or 8 bytes (4 bytes per float, 2 floats per Vector2, and 3 floats per Vector3) depending on if the mesh is using Vector3 or Vector2 vertices. This value can be determined with RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_format_skin_stride().
m.ArrayMesh.surface_update_vertex_region: Updates the vertex buffer of this mesh's surface with the given data. The expected data per vertex is 12 or 8 bytes (4 bytes per float, 2 floats per Vector2, and 3 floats per Vector3) depending on if the mesh is using Vector3 or Vector2 vertices. This value can be determined with RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_format_vertex_stride().
m.ArrayOccluder3D.indices: The occluder's index position. Indices determine which points from the vertices array should be drawn, and in which order.
m.ArrayOccluder3D.set_arrays: Sets indices and vertices, while updating the final occluder only once after both values are set.
m.ArrayOccluder3D.vertices: The occluder's vertex positions in local 3D coordinates.
m.AspectRatioContainer.ALIGNMENT_BEGIN: Aligns child controls with the beginning (left or top) of the container.
m.AspectRatioContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER: Aligns child controls with the center of the container.
m.AspectRatioContainer.ALIGNMENT_END: Aligns child controls with the end (right or bottom) of the container.
m.AspectRatioContainer.STRETCH_COVER: The width and height of child controls is automatically adjusted to make their bounding rectangle cover the entire area of the container while keeping the aspect ratio.
m.AspectRatioContainer.STRETCH_FIT: The bounding rectangle of child controls is automatically adjusted to fit inside the container while keeping the aspect ratio.
m.AspectRatioContainer.STRETCH_HEIGHT_CONT: The width of child controls is automatically adjusted based on the height of the container.
m.AspectRatioContainer.STRETCH_WIDTH_CONTR: The height of child controls is automatically adjusted based on the width of the container.
m.AspectRatioContainer.alignment_horizonta: Specifies the horizontal relative position of child controls.
m.AspectRatioContainer.alignment_vertical: Specifies the vertical relative position of child controls.
m.AspectRatioContainer.ratio: The aspect ratio to enforce on child controls. This is the width divided by the height. The ratio depends on the stretch_mode.
m.AspectRatioContainer.stretch_mode: The stretch mode used to align child controls.
m.AtlasTexture.atlas: The texture that contains the atlas. Can be any type inheriting from Texture2D, including another AtlasTexture.
m.AtlasTexture.filter_clip: If true, the area outside of the region is clipped to avoid bleeding of the surrounding texture pixels.
m.AtlasTexture.margin: The margin around the region. Useful for small adjustments. If the Rect2.size of this property ("w" and "h" in the editor) is set, the drawn texture is resized to fit within the margin.
m.AtlasTexture.region: The region used to draw the atlas. If either dimension of the region's size is 0, the value from atlas size will be used for that axis instead.
m.AudioEffect._instantiate: Override this method to customize the AudioEffectInstance created when this effect is applied on a bus in the editor's Audio panel, or through AudioServer.add_bus_effect().
m.AudioEffectAmplify.volume_db: Amount of amplification in dB. Positive values make the sound louder, negative values make it quieter. Value can range from -80 to 24.
m.AudioEffectAmplify.volume_linear: Amount of amplification as a linear value.
m.AudioEffectCapture.buffer_length: Length of the internal ring buffer, in seconds. Higher values keep data around for longer, but require more memory. Value can range from 0.01 to 10.
m.AudioEffectCapture.can_get_buffer: Returns true if at least frames samples are available to read in the internal ring buffer.
m.AudioEffectCapture.get_buffer: Gets the next frames samples from the internal ring buffer.
m.AudioEffectCapture.get_buffer_length_fra: Returns the total size of the internal ring buffer in number of samples.
m.AudioEffectCapture.get_discarded_frames: Returns the number of samples discarded from the audio bus due to full buffer.
m.AudioEffectCapture.get_frames_available: Returns the number of samples available to read using get_buffer().
m.AudioEffectCapture.get_pushed_frames: Returns the number of samples inserted from the audio bus.
m.AudioEffectChorus.dry: The volume ratio of the original audio. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectChorus.get_voice_cutoff_hz: Returns the frequency threshold of a given voice_idx's low-pass filter in Hz. Frequencies above this value are removed from the voice.
m.AudioEffectChorus.get_voice_delay_ms: Returns the delay of a given voice_idx in milliseconds, compared to the original audio.
m.AudioEffectChorus.get_voice_depth_ms: Returns the depth of a given voice_idx's low-frequency oscillator in milliseconds.
m.AudioEffectChorus.get_voice_level_db: Returns the gain of a given voice_idx in dB.
m.AudioEffectChorus.get_voice_pan: Returns the pan position of a given voice_idx. Negative values mean the left channel, positive mean the right.
m.AudioEffectChorus.get_voice_rate_hz: Returns the rate of a given voice_idx's low-frequency oscillator in Hz.
m.AudioEffectChorus.set_voice_cutoff_hz: Sets the frequency threshold of a given voice_idx's low-pass filter in Hz. Frequencies above cutoff_hz are removed from voice_idx. Value can range from 1 to 20500.
m.AudioEffectChorus.set_voice_delay_ms: Sets the delay of a given voice_idx in milliseconds, compared to the original audio. Value can range from 0 to 50.
m.AudioEffectChorus.set_voice_depth_ms: Sets the depth of a given voice_idx's low-frequency oscillator in milliseconds. Value can range from 0 to 20.
m.AudioEffectChorus.set_voice_level_db: Sets the gain of a given voice_idx in dB. Value can range from -60 to 24.
m.AudioEffectChorus.set_voice_pan: Sets the pan position of a given voice_idx. Negative values pan the sound to the left, positive pan to the right. Value can range from -1 to 1.
m.AudioEffectChorus.set_voice_rate_hz: Sets the rate of a given voice_idx's low-frequency oscillator in Hz. Value can range from 0.1 to 20.
m.AudioEffectChorus.voice_count: The number of voices in the effect. Value can range from 1 to 4.
m.AudioEffectChorus.wet: The volume ratio of all voices. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectCompressor.attack_us: Compressor's reaction time when the audio exceeds the volume threshold level, in microseconds. Value can range from 20 to 2000.
m.AudioEffectCompressor.gain: Gain of the audio signal, in dB. Value can range from -20 to 20.
m.AudioEffectCompressor.mix: Balance between the original audio and the compressed audio. Value can range from 0 (totally dry) to 1 (totally wet).
m.AudioEffectCompressor.ratio: Amount of compression applied to the audio once it passes the volume threshold level. The higher the ratio, the stronger the compression applied to audio signals that pass the volume threshold level. Value can range from 1 to 48.
m.AudioEffectCompressor.release_ms: Compressor's delay time to stop decreasing the volume after the it falls below the volume threshold level, in milliseconds. Value can range from 20 to 2000.
m.AudioEffectCompressor.sidechain: Audio bus to use for the volume threshold detection.
m.AudioEffectCompressor.threshold: The volume level above which compression is applied to the audio, in dB. Value can range from -60 to 0.
m.AudioEffectDelay.dry: The volume ratio of the original audio. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectDelay.feedback_active: If true, feedback is enabled, repeating taps after they are played.
m.AudioEffectDelay.feedback_delay_ms: Feedback delay time in milliseconds. Value can range from 0 to 1500.
m.AudioEffectDelay.feedback_level_db: Gain for feedback, in dB. Value can range from -60 to 0.
m.AudioEffectDelay.feedback_lowpass: Low-pass filter for feedback, in Hz. Frequencies above this value are filtered out. Value can range from 1 to 16000.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap1_active: If true, the first tap will be enabled.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap1_delay_ms: First tap delay time in milliseconds, compared to the original audio. Value can range from 0 to 1500.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap1_level_db: Gain for the first tap, in dB. Value can range from -60 to 0.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap1_pan: Pan position for the first tap. Negative values pan the sound to the left, positive pan to the right. Value can range from -1 to 1.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap2_active: If true, the second tap will be enabled.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap2_delay_ms: Second tap delay time in milliseconds, compared to the original audio. Value can range from 0 to 1500.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap2_level_db: Gain for the second tap, in dB. Value can range from -60 to 0.
m.AudioEffectDelay.tap2_pan: Pan position for the second tap. Negative values pan the sound to the left, positive pan to the right. Value can range from -1 to 1.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.MODE_ATAN: Flattens the waveform in a smooth manner, following an arctangent curve. The audio decreases in volume, before flattening peaks to PI * 4.0 (linear value), if it was normalized beforehand.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.MODE_CLIP: Flattens the waveform at 0 dB in a sharp manner. drive increases amplitude of samples exponentially. This mode functions as a hard clipper if drive is set to 0, and is the only mode that clips audio signals at 0 dB.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.MODE_LOFI: Decreases audio bit depth to achieve a low-resolution audio signal, going from 16-bit to 2-bit. Can be used to emulate the sound of early digital audio devices.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.MODE_OVERDRIVE: Emulates the warm distortion produced by a field effect transistor, which is commonly used in solid-state musical instrument amplifiers. drive has no effect in this mode.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.MODE_WAVESHAPE: Flattens the waveform in a smooth manner, until it reaches a sharp peak at drive = 1, following a generic absolute sigmoid function.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.drive: Distortion intensity. Controls how much of the input audio is affected by the distortion curve by moving from a linear function to a nonlinear one. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.keep_hf_hz: High-pass filter, in Hz. Frequencies higher than this value will not be affected by the distortion. Value can range from 1 to 20000.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.mode: Distortion type. Changes the nonlinear function used to distort the waveform. See Mode.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.post_gain: Gain after the effect, in dB. Value can range from -80 to 24.
m.AudioEffectDistortion.pre_gain: Gain before the effect, in dB. Value can range from -60 to 60.
m.AudioEffectEQ.get_band_count: Returns the number of bands of the equalizer.
m.AudioEffectEQ.get_band_gain_db: Returns the band's gain at the specified index, in dB.
m.AudioEffectEQ.set_band_gain_db: Sets band's gain at the specified index, in dB.
m.AudioEffectFilter.FILTER_12DB: Cutting off at 12 dB per octave. One octave is twice the frequency above cutoff_hz, or half the frequency below cutoff_hz.
m.AudioEffectFilter.FILTER_18DB: Cutting off at 18 dB per octave. One octave is twice the frequency above cutoff_hz, or half the frequency below cutoff_hz.
m.AudioEffectFilter.FILTER_24DB: Cutting off at 24 dB per octave. One octave is twice the frequency above cutoff_hz, or half the frequency below cutoff_hz.
m.AudioEffectFilter.FILTER_6DB: Cutting off at 6 dB per octave. One octave is twice the frequency above cutoff_hz, or half the frequency below cutoff_hz.
m.AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz: Frequency threshold for the filter, in Hz. Value can range from 1 to 20500.
m.AudioEffectFilter.db: Steepness of the cutoff curve in dB per octave (twice the frequency above cutoff_hz, or half the frequency below cutoff_hz), also known as the "order" of the filter. Higher orders have a more aggressive cutoff.
m.AudioEffectFilter.gain: Gain of the frequencies affected by the filter. This property is only available for AudioEffectLowShelfFilter and AudioEffectHighShelfFilter. Value can range from 0 to 4.
m.AudioEffectFilter.resonance: Gain at or directly next to the cutoff_hz frequency threshold. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectHardLimiter.ceiling_db: The waveform's maximum allowed value, in dB. This value can range from -24 to 0.
m.AudioEffectHardLimiter.pre_gain_db: Gain before limiting, in dB. Value can range from -24 to 24.
m.AudioEffectHardLimiter.release: Time it takes in seconds for the gain reduction to fully release. Value can range from 0.01 to 3.
m.AudioEffectInstance._process: Called by the AudioServer to process this effect. When _process_silence() is not overridden or it returns false, this method is called only when the bus is active.
m.AudioEffectInstance._process_silence: Override this method to customize the processing behavior of this effect instance.
m.AudioEffectLimiter.ceiling_db: The waveform's maximum allowed value, in dB. Value can range from -20 to -0.1.
m.AudioEffectLimiter.soft_clip_db: Modifies the volume of the limited waves, in dB. Value can range from 0 to 6.
m.AudioEffectLimiter.soft_clip_ratio: This property has no effect on the audio. Use AudioEffectHardLimiter instead, as this Limiter effect is deprecated.
m.AudioEffectLimiter.threshold_db: The volume threshold level from which the limiter begins to be active, in dB. Value can range from -30 to 0.
m.AudioEffectPanner.pan: Pan position. Negative values pan the sound to the left, positive pan to the right. Value can range from -1 to 1.
m.AudioEffectPhaser.depth: Intensity of the effect. Value can range from 0.1 to 4.0.
m.AudioEffectPhaser.feedback: The volume ratio of the filtered audio that is fed back to the all-pass filters. The higher the value, the sharper and louder the peak filters created by the effect. Value can range from 0.1 to 0.9.
m.AudioEffectPhaser.range_max_hz: Determines the maximum frequency affected by the low-frequency oscillator modulations, in Hz. Value can range from 10 to 10000.
m.AudioEffectPhaser.range_min_hz: Determines the minimum frequency affected by the low-frequency oscillator modulations, in Hz. Value can range from 10 to 10000.
m.AudioEffectPhaser.rate_hz: Adjusts the rate in Hz at which the effect sweeps up and down across the frequency range. Value can range from 0.01 to 20.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.FFT_SIZE_1024: Use a buffer of 1024 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. This is a compromise between latency and stability over time.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.FFT_SIZE_2048: Use a buffer of 2048 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. High latency, but stable over time.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.FFT_SIZE_256: Use a buffer of 256 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. Lowest latency, but least stable over time.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.FFT_SIZE_4096: Use a buffer of 4096 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. Highest latency, but most stable over time.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.FFT_SIZE_512: Use a buffer of 512 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. Low latency, but less stable over time.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.FFT_SIZE_MAX: Represents the size of the FFTSize enum.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.fft_size: The size of the Fast Fourier transform [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Fourier_transform] buffer. Higher values smooth out the effect over time, but have greater latency. The effects of this higher latency are especially noticeable on audio signals that have sudden amplitude changes.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.oversampling: The oversampling factor to use. Higher values result in better quality, but are more demanding on the CPU and may cause audio cracking if the CPU can't keep up.
m.AudioEffectPitchShift.pitch_scale: The pitch scale to use. 1.0 is the default pitch and plays sounds unaffected. pitch_scale can range from 0 (infinitely low pitch, inaudible) to 16 (16 times higher than the initial pitch).
m.AudioEffectRecord.format: Specifies the format in which the sample will be recorded.
m.AudioEffectRecord.is_recording_active: Returns whether the recording is active or not.
m.AudioEffectRecord.set_recording_active: If true, the sound will be recorded. Note that restarting the recording will remove the previously recorded sample.
m.AudioEffectReverb.damping: Defines how reflective the imaginary room's walls are. The more reflective, the more high frequency content the reverb has. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectReverb.dry: The volume ratio of the original audio. At 0, only the modified audio is outputted. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectReverb.hipass: High-pass filter allows frequencies higher than a certain cutoff threshold and attenuates frequencies lower than the cutoff threshold. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectReverb.predelay_feedback: Gain of early reflection copies. At higher values, early reflection copies are louder and ring out for longer. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectReverb.predelay_msec: Time between the original audio and the early reflections of the reverb signal, in milliseconds. Value can range from 20 to 500.
m.AudioEffectReverb.room_size: Dimensions of simulated room. Bigger means more echoes. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectReverb.spread: Widens or narrows the stereo image of the reverb tail. At 1, it fully widens. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectReverb.wet: The volume ratio of the modified audio. At 0, only the original audio is outputted. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.FFT_SIZE_102: Use a buffer of 1024 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. This is a compromise between latency and stability over time.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.FFT_SIZE_204: Use a buffer of 2048 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. High latency, but stable over time.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.FFT_SIZE_256: Use a buffer of 256 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. Lowest latency, but least stable over time.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.FFT_SIZE_409: Use a buffer of 4096 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. Highest latency, but most stable over time.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.FFT_SIZE_512: Use a buffer of 512 samples for the Fast Fourier transform. Low latency, but less stable over time.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.FFT_SIZE_MAX: Represents the size of the FFTSize enum.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.buffer_lengt: The length of the buffer to keep, in seconds. Higher values keep data around for longer, but require more memory. Value can range from 0.1 to 4.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.fft_size: The size of the Fast Fourier transform [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Fourier_transform] buffer. Higher values smooth out the spectrum analysis over time, but have greater latency. The effects of this higher latency are especially noticeable with sudden amplitude changes.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzerInstance.MAGN: Use the average value across the frequency range as magnitude.
Use the maximum value of the frequency range as magnitude.
m.AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzerInstance.get_: Returns the magnitude of the frequencies from from_hz to to_hz in linear energy as a Vector2. The x component of the return value represents the left stereo channel, and y represents the right channel.
m.AudioEffectStereoEnhance.pan_pullout: Gain of the side channels, if they exist. A value of 0 will downmix stereo to mono. Value can range from 0 to 4.
m.AudioEffectStereoEnhance.surround: Widens the stereo image through phase shifting in conjunction with time_pullout_ms. Just pans sound to the left channel if time_pullout_ms is 0. Value can range from 0 to 1.
m.AudioEffectStereoEnhance.time_pullout_ms: Widens the stereo image through phase shifting in conjunction with surround. Just delays the right channel if surround is 0. Value is in milliseconds, and can range from 0 to 50.
m.AudioListener2D.clear_current: Disables the AudioListener2D. If it's not set as current, this method will have no effect.
m.AudioListener2D.is_current: Returns true if this AudioListener2D is currently active.
m.AudioListener2D.make_current: Makes the AudioListener2D active, setting it as the hearing point for the sounds. If there is already another active AudioListener2D, it will be disabled.
m.AudioListener3D.DOPPLER_TRACKING_IDLE_ST: Simulate Doppler effect [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect] by tracking positions of objects that are changed in _process. Changes in the relative velocity of this listener compared to those objects affect how audio is perceived (changing the audio's AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale).
m.AudioListener3D.DOPPLER_TRACKING_PHYSICS: Simulate Doppler effect [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect] by tracking positions of objects that are changed in _physics_process. Changes in the relative velocity of this listener compared to those objects affect how audio is perceived (changing the audio's AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale).
m.AudioListener3D.clear_current: Disables the listener to use the current camera's listener instead.
m.AudioListener3D.doppler_tracking: If not DOPPLER_TRACKING_DISABLED, this listener will simulate the Doppler effect [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect] for objects changed in particular _process methods.
m.AudioListener3D.get_listener_transform: Returns the listener's global orthonormalized Transform3D.
m.AudioListener3D.is_current: Returns true if the listener was made current using make_current(), false otherwise.
m.AudioListener3D.make_current: Enables the listener. This will override the current camera's listener.
m.AudioServer.PLAYBACK_TYPE_DEFAULT: Experimental: This constant may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.PLAYBACK_TYPE_MAX: Experimental: This constant may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.PLAYBACK_TYPE_SAMPLE: Experimental: This constant may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.PLAYBACK_TYPE_STREAM: Experimental: This constant may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.SPEAKER_MODE_STEREO: Two or fewer speakers were detected.
m.AudioServer.SPEAKER_SURROUND_31: A 3.1 channel surround setup was detected.
m.AudioServer.SPEAKER_SURROUND_51: A 5.1 channel surround setup was detected.
m.AudioServer.SPEAKER_SURROUND_71: A 7.1 channel surround setup was detected.
m.AudioServer.add_bus_effect: Adds an AudioEffect effect to the bus bus_idx at at_position.
m.AudioServer.bus_layout_changed: Emitted when an audio bus is added, deleted, or moved.
m.AudioServer.bus_renamed: Emitted when the audio bus at bus_index is renamed from old_name to new_name.
m.AudioServer.generate_bus_layout: Generates an AudioBusLayout using the available buses and effects.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_channels: Returns the number of channels of the bus at index bus_idx.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_effect: Returns the AudioEffect at position effect_idx in bus bus_idx.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_effect_count: Returns the number of effects on the bus at bus_idx.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_effect_instance: Returns the AudioEffectInstance assigned to the given bus and effect indices (and optionally channel).
m.AudioServer.get_bus_index: Returns the index of the bus with the name bus_name. Returns -1 if no bus with the specified name exist.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_name: Returns the name of the bus with the index bus_idx.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_peak_volume_left_db: Returns the peak volume of the left speaker at bus index bus_idx and channel index channel.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_peak_volume_right_db: Returns the peak volume of the right speaker at bus index bus_idx and channel index channel.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_send: Returns the name of the bus that the bus at index bus_idx sends to.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_volume_db: Returns the volume of the bus at index bus_idx in dB.
m.AudioServer.get_bus_volume_linear: Returns the volume of the bus at index bus_idx as a linear value.
m.AudioServer.get_driver_name: Returns the name of the current audio driver. The default usually depends on the operating system, but may be overridden via the --audio-driver command line argument. --headless also automatically sets the audio driver to Dummy. See also ProjectSettings.audio/driver/driver.
m.AudioServer.get_input_buffer_length_fram: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.get_input_device_list: Returns the names of all audio input devices detected on the system.
m.AudioServer.get_input_frames: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.get_input_frames_available: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.get_input_mix_rate: Returns the sample rate at the input of the AudioServer.
m.AudioServer.get_mix_rate: Returns the sample rate at the output of the AudioServer.
m.AudioServer.get_output_device_list: Returns the names of all audio output devices detected on the system.
m.AudioServer.get_output_latency: Returns the audio driver's effective output latency. This is based on ProjectSettings.audio/driver/output_latency, but the exact returned value will differ depending on the operating system and audio driver.
m.AudioServer.get_time_since_last_mix: Returns the relative time since the last mix occurred, in seconds.
m.AudioServer.get_time_to_next_mix: Returns the relative time until the next mix occurs, in seconds.
m.AudioServer.input_device: Name of the current device for audio input (see get_input_device_list()). On systems with multiple audio inputs (such as analog, USB and HDMI audio), this can be used to select the audio input device. The value "Default" will record audio on the system-wide default audio input. If an invalid device name is set, the value will be reverted back to "Default".
m.AudioServer.is_bus_bypassing_effects: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is bypassing effects.
m.AudioServer.is_bus_effect_enabled: If true, the effect at index effect_idx on the bus at index bus_idx is enabled.
m.AudioServer.is_bus_mute: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is muted.
m.AudioServer.is_bus_solo: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is in solo mode.
m.AudioServer.is_stream_registered_as_samp: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.lock: Locks the audio driver's main loop.
m.AudioServer.move_bus: Moves the bus from index index to index to_index.
m.AudioServer.output_device: Name of the current device for audio output (see get_output_device_list()). On systems with multiple audio outputs (such as analog, USB and HDMI audio), this can be used to select the audio output device. The value "Default" will play audio on the system-wide default audio output. If an invalid device name is set, the value will be reverted back to "Default".
m.AudioServer.playback_speed_scale: Scales the rate at which audio is played (i.e. setting it to 0.5 will make the audio be played at half its speed). See also Engine.time_scale to affect the general simulation speed, which is independent from playback_speed_scale.
m.AudioServer.register_stream_as_sample: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.remove_bus: Removes the bus at index index.
m.AudioServer.remove_bus_effect: Removes the effect at index effect_idx from the bus at index bus_idx.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_bypass_effects: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is bypassing effects.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_effect_enabled: If true, the effect at index effect_idx on the bus at index bus_idx is enabled.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_mute: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is muted.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_name: Sets the name of the bus at index bus_idx to name.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_send: Connects the output of the bus at bus_idx to the bus named send.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_solo: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is in solo mode.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db: Sets the volume in decibels of the bus at index bus_idx to volume_db.
m.AudioServer.set_bus_volume_linear: Sets the volume as a linear value of the bus at index bus_idx to volume_linear.
m.AudioServer.set_enable_tagging_used_audi: If set to true, all instances of AudioStreamPlayback will call AudioStreamPlayback._tag_used_streams() every mix step.
m.AudioServer.set_input_device_active: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioServer.swap_bus_effects: Swaps the position of two effects in bus bus_idx.
m.AudioServer.unlock: Unlocks the audio driver's main loop. (After locking it, you should always unlock it.)
m.AudioStream._get_bar_beats: Override this method to return the bar beats of this stream.
m.AudioStream._get_beat_count: Overridable method. Should return the total number of beats of this audio stream. Used by the engine to determine the position of every beat.
m.AudioStream._get_bpm: Overridable method. Should return the tempo of this audio stream, in beats per minute (BPM). Used by the engine to determine the position of every beat.
m.AudioStream._get_length: Override this method to customize the returned value of get_length(). Should return the length of this audio stream, in seconds.
m.AudioStream._get_parameter_list: Return the controllable parameters of this stream. This array contains dictionaries with a property info description format (see Object.get_property_list()). Additionally, the default value for this parameter must be added tho each dictionary in "default_value" field.
m.AudioStream._get_stream_name: Override this method to customize the name assigned to this audio stream. Unused by the engine.
m.AudioStream._get_tags: Override this method to customize the tags for this audio stream. Should return a Dictionary of strings with the tag as the key and its content as the value.
m.AudioStream._has_loop: Override this method to return true if this stream has a loop.
m.AudioStream._instantiate_playback: Override this method to customize the returned value of instantiate_playback(). Should return a new AudioStreamPlayback created when the stream is played (such as by an AudioStreamPlayer).
m.AudioStream._is_monophonic: Override this method to customize the returned value of is_monophonic(). Should return true if this audio stream only supports one channel.
m.AudioStream.can_be_sampled: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioStream.generate_sample: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioStream.get_length: Returns the length of the audio stream in seconds. If this stream is an AudioStreamRandomizer, returns the length of the last played stream. If this stream has an indefinite length (such as for AudioStreamGenerator and AudioStreamMicrophone), returns 0.0.
m.AudioStream.instantiate_playback: Returns a newly created AudioStreamPlayback intended to play this audio stream. Useful for when you want to extend _instantiate_playback() but call instantiate_playback() from an internally held AudioStream subresource. An example of this can be found in the source code for AudioStreamRandomPitch::instantiate_playback.
m.AudioStream.is_meta_stream: Returns true if the stream is a collection of other streams, false otherwise.
m.AudioStream.is_monophonic: Returns true if this audio stream only supports one channel (monophony), or false if the audio stream supports two or more channels (polyphony).
m.AudioStream.parameter_list_changed: Signal to be emitted to notify when the parameter list changed.
m.AudioStreamGenerator.MIX_RATE_CUSTOM: Custom mixing rate, specified by mix_rate.
m.AudioStreamGenerator.MIX_RATE_MAX: Maximum value for the mixing rate mode enum.
m.AudioStreamGenerator.buffer_length: The length of the buffer to generate (in seconds). Lower values result in less latency, but require the script to generate audio data faster, resulting in increased CPU usage and more risk for audio cracking if the CPU can't keep up.
m.AudioStreamGenerator.mix_rate: The sample rate to use (in Hz). Higher values are more demanding for the CPU to generate, but result in better quality.
m.AudioStreamGenerator.mix_rate_mode: Mixing rate mode. If set to MIX_RATE_CUSTOM, mix_rate is used, otherwise current AudioServer mixing rate is used.
m.AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.can_push_bu: Returns true if a buffer of the size amount can be pushed to the audio sample data buffer without overflowing it, false otherwise.
m.AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.clear_buffe: Clears the audio sample data buffer.
m.AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.get_frames_: Returns the number of frames that can be pushed to the audio sample data buffer without overflowing it. If the result is 0, the buffer is full.
m.AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.get_skips: Returns the number of times the playback skipped due to a buffer underrun in the audio sample data. This value is reset at the start of the playback.
m.AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.push_buffer: Pushes several audio data frames to the buffer. This is usually more efficient than push_frame() in C# and compiled languages via GDExtension, but push_buffer() may be less efficient in GDScript.
m.AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.push_frame: Pushes a single audio data frame to the buffer. This is usually less efficient than push_buffer() in C# and compiled languages via GDExtension, but push_frame() may be more efficient in GDScript.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.AUTO_ADVANCE_ENAB: Enable auto-advance, a clip must be specified.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.AUTO_ADVANCE_RETU: Enable auto-advance, but instead of specifying a clip, the playback will return to hold (see add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.CLIP_ANY: This constant describes that any clip is valid for a specific transition as either source or destination.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.FADE_AUTOMATIC: Use automatic fade logic depending on the transition from/to. It is recommended to use this by default.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.FADE_DISABLED: Do not use fade for the transition. This is useful when transitioning from a clip-end to clip-beginning, and each clip has their begin/end.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.FADE_IN: Use a fade-in in the next clip, let the current clip finish.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.FADE_OUT: Use a fade-out in the current clip, the next clip will start by itself.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.TRANSITION_FROM_T: Transition when the current clip finished playing.
Start transition as soon as possible, don't wait for any specific time position.
Transition when the clip playback position reaches the next bar.
Transition when the clip playback position reaches the next beat.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.TRANSITION_TO_TIM: Transition to the last played position in the destination clip, if there was a previous transition from that clip. Otherwise, plays from the start of the destination clip.
Transition to the same position in the destination clip. This is useful when both clips have exactly the same length and the music should fade between them.
Transition to the start of the destination clip.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.add_transition: Add a transition between two clips. Provide the indices of the source and destination clips, or use the CLIP_ANY constant to indicate that transition happens to/from any clip to this one.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.clip_count: Amount of clips contained in this interactive player.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.erase_transition: Erase a transition by providing from_clip and to_clip clip indices. CLIP_ANY can be used for either argument or both.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_clip_auto_adv: Return whether a clip has auto-advance enabled. See set_clip_auto_advance().
Return the clip towards which the clip referenced by clip_index will auto-advance to.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_clip_name: Return the name of a clip.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_clip_stream: Return the AudioStream associated with a clip.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_transition_fa: Return the time (in beats) for a transition (see add_transition()).
Return the mode for a transition (see add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_transition_fi: Return the filler clip for a transition (see add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_transition_fr: Return the source time position for a transition (see add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_transition_li: Return the list of transitions (from, to interleaved).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.get_transition_to: Return the destination time position for a transition (see add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.has_transition: Returns true if a given transition exists (was added via add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.initial_clip: Index of the initial clip, which will be played first when this stream is played.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.is_transition_hol: Return whether a transition uses the hold previous functionality (see add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.is_transition_usi: Return whether a transition uses the filler clip functionality (see add_transition()).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.set_clip_auto_adv: Set whether a clip will auto-advance by changing the auto-advance mode.
Set the index of the next clip towards which this clip will auto advance to when finished. If the clip being played loops, then auto-advance will be ignored.
m.AudioStreamInteractive.set_clip_name: Set the name of the current clip (for easier identification).
m.AudioStreamInteractive.set_clip_stream: Set the AudioStream associated with the current clip.
m.AudioStreamMP3.bar_beats: The number of beats within a single bar in the audio track.
m.AudioStreamMP3.beat_count: The length of the audio track, in beats. The actual duration of the audio file might be longer than what is indicated by this property. It defines the end of the audio for looping, AudioStreamPlaylist, and AudioStreamInteractive.
m.AudioStreamMP3.bpm: The tempo of the audio track, measured in beats per minute.
m.AudioStreamMP3.data: Contains the audio data in bytes.
m.AudioStreamMP3.load_from_buffer: Creates a new AudioStreamMP3 instance from the given buffer. The buffer must contain MP3 data.
m.AudioStreamMP3.load_from_file: Creates a new AudioStreamMP3 instance from the given file path. The file must be in MP3 format.
m.AudioStreamMP3.loop: If true, the stream will play again from the specified loop_offset once it reaches the end of the audio track, or once it reaches the end of the last beat according to the amount specified in beat_count. Useful for ambient sounds and background music.
m.AudioStreamMP3.loop_offset: Time in seconds at which the stream starts after being looped.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.bar_beats: The number of beats within a single bar in the audio track.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.beat_count: The length of the audio track, in beats. The actual duration of the audio file might be longer than what is indicated by this property. It defines the end of the audio for looping, AudioStreamPlaylist, and AudioStreamInteractive.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.bpm: The tempo of the audio track, measured in beats per minute.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.load_from_buffer: Creates a new AudioStreamOggVorbis instance from the given buffer. The buffer must contain Ogg Vorbis data.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.load_from_file: Creates a new AudioStreamOggVorbis instance from the given file path. The file must be in Ogg Vorbis format.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.loop: If true, the stream will play again from the specified loop_offset once it reaches the end of the audio track, or once it reaches the end of the last beat according to the amount specified in beat_count. Useful for ambient sounds and background music.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.loop_offset: Time in seconds at which the stream starts after being looped.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.packet_sequence: Contains the raw Ogg data for this stream.
m.AudioStreamOggVorbis.tags: Contains user-defined tags if found in the Ogg Vorbis data.
m.AudioStreamPlayback._get_loop_count: Overridable method. Should return how many times this audio stream has looped. Most built-in playbacks always return 0.
m.AudioStreamPlayback._get_parameter: Return the current value of a playback parameter by name (see AudioStream._get_parameter_list()).
m.AudioStreamPlayback._get_playback_positi: Overridable method. Should return the current progress along the audio stream, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayback._is_playing: Overridable method. Should return true if this playback is active and playing its audio stream.
m.AudioStreamPlayback._mix: Override this method to customize how the audio stream is mixed. This method is called even if the playback is not active.
m.AudioStreamPlayback._seek: Override this method to customize what happens when seeking this audio stream at the given position, such as by calling AudioStreamPlayer.seek().
m.AudioStreamPlayback._set_parameter: Set the current value of a playback parameter by name (see AudioStream._get_parameter_list()).
m.AudioStreamPlayback._start: Override this method to customize what happens when the playback starts at the given position, such as by calling AudioStreamPlayer.play().
m.AudioStreamPlayback._stop: Override this method to customize what happens when the playback is stopped, such as by calling AudioStreamPlayer.stop().
m.AudioStreamPlayback._tag_used_streams: Overridable method. Called whenever the audio stream is mixed if the playback is active and AudioServer.set_enable_tagging_used_audio_streams() has been set to true. Editor plugins may use this method to "tag" the current position along the audio stream and display it in a preview.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.get_loop_count: Returns the number of times the stream has looped.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.get_playback_positio: Returns the current position in the stream, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.get_sample_playback: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.is_playing: Returns true if the stream is playing.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.mix_audio: Mixes up to frames of audio from the stream from the current position, at a rate of rate_scale, advancing the stream.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.seek: Seeks the stream at the given time, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.set_sample_playback: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioStreamPlayback.start: Starts the stream from the given from_pos, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlaybackInteractive.get_curre: Return the index of the currently playing clip. You can use this to get the name of the currently playing clip with AudioStreamInteractive.get_clip_name().
m.AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.INVALID_ID: Returned by play_stream() in case it could not allocate a stream for playback.
m.AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.is_stream_: Returns true if the stream associated with the given integer ID is still playing. Check play_stream() for information on when this ID becomes invalid.
m.AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.play_strea: Play an AudioStream at a given offset, volume, pitch scale, playback type, and bus. Playback starts immediately.
m.AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.set_stream: Change the stream pitch scale. The stream argument is an integer ID returned by play_stream().
Change the stream volume (in db). The stream argument is an integer ID returned by play_stream().
m.AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.stop_strea: Stop a stream. The stream argument is an integer ID returned by play_stream(), which becomes invalid after calling this function.
m.AudioStreamPlaybackResampled._get_stream: Returns an AudioStream's sample rate, in Hz. Used to perform resampling.
m.AudioStreamPlaybackResampled._mix_resamp: Called by begin_resample() to mix an AudioStream to AudioServer.get_mix_rate(). Uses _get_stream_sampling_rate() as the source sample rate. Returns the number of mixed frames.
m.AudioStreamPlaybackResampled.begin_resam: Called when an AudioStream is played. Clears the cubic interpolation history and starts mixing by calling _mix_resampled().
m.AudioStreamPlayer.MIX_TARGET_CENTER: The audio will be played on the second channel, which is usually the center.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.MIX_TARGET_STEREO: The audio will be played only on the first channel. This is the default.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.MIX_TARGET_SURROUND: The audio will be played on all surround channels.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.autoplay: If true, this node calls play() when entering the tree.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.bus: The target bus name. All sounds from this node will be playing on this bus.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.finished: Emitted when a sound finishes playing without interruptions. This signal is not emitted when calling stop(), or when exiting the tree while sounds are playing.
