m.AudioStreamPlayer.get_playback_position: Returns the position in the AudioStream of the latest sound, in seconds. Returns 0.0 if no sounds are playing.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.get_stream_playback: Returns the latest AudioStreamPlayback of this node, usually the most recently created by play(). If no sounds are playing, this method fails and returns an empty playback.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.has_stream_playback: Returns true if any sound is active, even if stream_paused is set to true. See also playing and get_stream_playback().
m.AudioStreamPlayer.max_polyphony: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Calling play() after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.mix_target: The mix target channels. Has no effect when two speakers or less are detected (see SpeakerMode).
m.AudioStreamPlayer.pitch_scale: The audio's pitch and tempo, as a multiplier of the stream's sample rate. A value of 2.0 doubles the audio's pitch, while a value of 0.5 halves the pitch.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.play: Plays a sound from the beginning, or the given from_position in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.playback_type: Experimental: This property may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.playing: If true, this node is playing sounds. Setting this property has the same effect as play() and stop().
m.AudioStreamPlayer.seek: Restarts all sounds to be played from the given to_position, in seconds. Does nothing if no sounds are playing.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.stop: Stops all sounds from this node.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.stream: The AudioStream resource to be played. Setting this property stops all currently playing sounds. If left empty, the AudioStreamPlayer does not work.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.stream_paused: If true, the sounds are paused. Setting stream_paused to false resumes all sounds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.volume_db: Volume of sound, in decibels. This is an offset of the stream's volume.
m.AudioStreamPlayer.volume_linear: Volume of sound, as a linear value.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.area_mask: Determines which Area2D layers affect the sound for reverb and audio bus effects. Areas can be used to redirect AudioStreams so that they play in a certain audio bus. An example of how you might use this is making a "water" area so that sounds played in the water are redirected through an audio bus to make them sound like they are being played underwater.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.attenuation: The volume is attenuated over distance with this as an exponent.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.autoplay: If true, audio plays when added to scene tree.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.bus: Bus on which this audio is playing.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.finished: Emitted when the audio stops playing.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.get_playback_positio: Returns the position in the AudioStream.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.get_stream_playback: Returns the AudioStreamPlayback object associated with this AudioStreamPlayer2D.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.has_stream_playback: Returns whether the AudioStreamPlayer can return the AudioStreamPlayback object or not.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.max_distance: Maximum distance from which audio is still hearable.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.max_polyphony: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Playing additional sounds after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.panning_strength: Scales the panning strength for this node by multiplying the base ProjectSettings.audio/general/2d_panning_strength with this factor. Higher values will pan audio from left to right more dramatically than lower values.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.pitch_scale: The pitch and the tempo of the audio, as a multiplier of the audio sample's sample rate.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.play: Queues the audio to play on the next physics frame, from the given position from_position, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.playback_type: Experimental: This property may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.playing: If true, audio is playing or is queued to be played (see play()).
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.seek: Sets the position from which audio will be played, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.stream: The AudioStream object to be played.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.stream_paused: If true, the playback is paused. You can resume it by setting stream_paused to false.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.volume_db: Base volume before attenuation, in decibels.
m.AudioStreamPlayer2D.volume_linear: Base volume before attenuation, as a linear value.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.ATTENUATION_DISABLED: No attenuation of loudness according to distance. The sound will still be heard positionally, unlike an AudioStreamPlayer. ATTENUATION_DISABLED can be combined with a max_distance value greater than 0.0 to achieve linear attenuation clamped to a sphere of a defined size.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.ATTENUATION_INVERSE_: Attenuation of loudness according to linear distance.
Attenuation of loudness according to squared distance.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.ATTENUATION_LOGARITH: Attenuation of loudness according to logarithmic distance.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.DOPPLER_TRACKING_IDL: Executes doppler tracking during process frames (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS).
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.DOPPLER_TRACKING_PHY: Executes doppler tracking during physics frames (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS).
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.area_mask: Determines which Area3D layers affect the sound for reverb and audio bus effects. Areas can be used to redirect AudioStreams so that they play in a certain audio bus. An example of how you might use this is making a "water" area so that sounds played in the water are redirected through an audio bus to make them sound like they are being played underwater.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.attenuation_filter_c: The cutoff frequency of the attenuation low-pass filter, in Hz. A sound above this frequency is attenuated more than a sound below this frequency. To disable this effect, set this to 20500 as this frequency is above the human hearing limit.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.attenuation_filter_d: Amount how much the filter affects the loudness, in decibels.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.attenuation_model: Decides if audio should get quieter with distance linearly, quadratically, logarithmically, or not be affected by distance, effectively disabling attenuation.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.autoplay: If true, audio plays when the AudioStreamPlayer3D node is added to scene tree.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.bus: The bus on which this audio is playing.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.doppler_tracking: Decides in which step the Doppler effect should be calculated.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.emission_angle_degre: The angle in which the audio reaches a listener unattenuated.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.emission_angle_enabl: If true, the audio should be attenuated according to the direction of the sound.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.emission_angle_filte: Attenuation factor used if listener is outside of emission_angle_degrees and emission_angle_enabled is set, in decibels.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.finished: Emitted when the audio stops playing.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.get_playback_positio: Returns the position in the AudioStream.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.get_stream_playback: Returns the AudioStreamPlayback object associated with this AudioStreamPlayer3D.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.has_stream_playback: Returns whether the AudioStreamPlayer can return the AudioStreamPlayback object or not.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.max_db: Sets the absolute maximum of the sound level, in decibels.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.max_distance: The distance past which the sound can no longer be heard at all. Only has an effect if set to a value greater than 0.0. max_distance works in tandem with unit_size. However, unlike unit_size whose behavior depends on the attenuation_model, max_distance always works in a linear fashion. This can be used to prevent the AudioStreamPlayer3D from requiring audio mixing when the listener is far away, w…
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.max_polyphony: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Playing additional sounds after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.panning_strength: Scales the panning strength for this node by multiplying the base ProjectSettings.audio/general/3d_panning_strength by this factor. If the product is 0.0 then stereo panning is disabled and the volume is the same for all channels. If the product is 1.0 then one of the channels will be muted when the sound is located exactly to the left (or right) of the listener.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale: The pitch and the tempo of the audio, as a multiplier of the audio sample's sample rate.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.play: Queues the audio to play on the next physics frame, from the given position from_position, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.playback_type: Experimental: This property may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.playing: If true, audio is playing or is queued to be played (see play()).
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.seek: Sets the position from which audio will be played, in seconds.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.stream: The AudioStream resource to be played.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.stream_paused: If true, the playback is paused. You can resume it by setting stream_paused to false.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.unit_size: The factor for the attenuation effect. Higher values make the sound audible over a larger distance.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.volume_db: The base sound level before attenuation, in decibels.
m.AudioStreamPlayer3D.volume_linear: The base sound level before attenuation, as a linear value.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.MAX_STREAMS: Maximum amount of streams supported in the playlist.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.fade_time: Fade time used when a stream ends, when going to the next one. Streams are expected to have an extra bit of audio after the end to help with fading.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.get_bpm: Returns the BPM of the playlist, which can vary depending on the clip being played.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.get_list_stream: Returns the stream at playback position index.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.loop: If true, the playlist will loop, otherwise the playlist will end when the last stream is finished.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.set_list_stream: Sets the stream at playback position index.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.shuffle: If true, the playlist will shuffle each time playback starts and each time it loops.
m.AudioStreamPlaylist.stream_count: Amount of streams in the playlist.
m.AudioStreamPolyphonic.polyphony: Maximum amount of simultaneous streams that can be played.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.PLAYBACK_RANDOM: Pick a stream at random according to the probability weights chosen for each stream. If only 1 sound is present in the pool, the same sound will always play.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.PLAYBACK_RANDOM_NO: Pick a stream at random according to the probability weights chosen for each stream, but avoid playing the same stream twice in a row whenever possible. If only 1 sound is present in the pool, the same sound will always play, effectively allowing repeats to occur.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.PLAYBACK_SEQUENTIA: Play streams in the order they appear in the stream pool. If only 1 sound is present in the pool, the same sound will always play.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.add_stream: Insert a stream at the specified index. If the index is less than zero, the insertion occurs at the end of the underlying pool.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.get_stream: Returns the stream at the specified index.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.get_stream_probabi: Returns the probability weight associated with the stream at the given index.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.move_stream: Move a stream from one index to another.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.playback_mode: Controls how this AudioStreamRandomizer picks which AudioStream to play next.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.random_pitch: The largest possible frequency multiplier of the random pitch variation. Pitch will be randomly chosen within a range of 1.0 / random_pitch and random_pitch. A value of 1.0 means no variation. A value of 2.0 means pitch will be randomized between double and half.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.random_pitch_semit: The largest possible distance, in semitones, of the random pitch variation. A value of 0.0 means no variation.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.random_volume_offs: The intensity of random volume variation. Volume will be increased or decreased by a random value up to random_volume_offset_db. A value of 0.0 means no variation. A value of 3.0 means volume will be randomized between -3.0 dB and +3.0 dB.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.remove_stream: Remove the stream at the specified index.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.set_stream: Set the AudioStream at the specified index.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.set_stream_probabi: Set the probability weight of the stream at the specified index. The higher this value, the more likely that the randomizer will choose this stream during random playback modes.
m.AudioStreamRandomizer.streams_count: The number of streams in the stream pool.
m.AudioStreamSynchronized.MAX_STREAMS: Maximum amount of streams that can be synchronized.
m.AudioStreamSynchronized.get_sync_stream: Get one of the synchronized streams, by index.
m.AudioStreamSynchronized.get_sync_stream_: Get the volume of one of the synchronized streams, by index.
m.AudioStreamSynchronized.set_sync_stream: Set one of the synchronized streams, by index.
m.AudioStreamSynchronized.set_sync_stream_: Set the volume of one of the synchronized streams, by index.
m.AudioStreamSynchronized.stream_count: Set the total amount of streams that will be played back synchronized.
m.AudioStreamWAV.FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM: Audio is lossily compressed as IMA ADPCM.
m.AudioStreamWAV.FORMAT_QOA: Audio is lossily compressed as Quite OK Audio [https://qoaformat.org/].
m.AudioStreamWAV.LOOP_BACKWARD: Audio loops the data between loop_begin and loop_end, playing backward only.
m.AudioStreamWAV.LOOP_FORWARD: Audio loops the data between loop_begin and loop_end, playing forward only.
m.AudioStreamWAV.LOOP_PINGPONG: Audio loops the data between loop_begin and loop_end, playing back and forth.
m.AudioStreamWAV.data: Contains the audio data in bytes.
m.AudioStreamWAV.load_from_buffer: Creates a new AudioStreamWAV instance from the given buffer. The buffer must contain WAV data.
m.AudioStreamWAV.load_from_file: Creates a new AudioStreamWAV instance from the given file path. The file must be in WAV format.
m.AudioStreamWAV.loop_begin: The loop start point (in number of samples, relative to the beginning of the stream).
m.AudioStreamWAV.loop_end: The loop end point (in number of samples, relative to the beginning of the stream).
m.AudioStreamWAV.mix_rate: The sample rate for mixing this audio. Higher values require more storage space, but result in better quality.
m.AudioStreamWAV.save_to_wav: Saves the AudioStreamWAV as a WAV file to path. Samples with IMA ADPCM or Quite OK Audio formats can't be saved.
m.AudioStreamWAV.tags: Contains user-defined tags if found in the WAV data.
m.AwaitTweener.set_timeout: Sets the maximum time an AwaitTweener can wait for the signal. Can be used as a safeguard for signals that may never be emitted. If not specified, the tweener will wait indefinitely.
m.BackBufferCopy.COPY_MODE_DISABLED: Disables the buffering mode. This means the BackBufferCopy node will directly use the portion of screen it covers.
m.BackBufferCopy.rect: The area covered by the BackBufferCopy. Only used if copy_mode is COPY_MODE_RECT.
m.BaseButton.ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_PRESS: Require just a press to consider the button clicked.
m.BaseButton.ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_RELEASE: Require a press and a subsequent release before considering the button clicked.
m.BaseButton.DRAW_DISABLED: The state of buttons are disabled.
m.BaseButton.DRAW_HOVER: The state of buttons are hovered.
m.BaseButton.DRAW_HOVER_PRESSED: The state of buttons are both hovered and pressed.
m.BaseButton.DRAW_NORMAL: The normal state (i.e. not pressed, not hovered, not toggled and enabled) of buttons.
m.BaseButton.DRAW_PRESSED: The state of buttons are pressed.
m.BaseButton._pressed: Called when the button is pressed. If you need to know the button's pressed state (and toggle_mode is active), use _toggled() instead.
m.BaseButton._toggled: Called when the button is toggled (only if toggle_mode is active).
m.BaseButton.action_mode: Determines when the button is considered clicked.
m.BaseButton.button_down: Emitted when the button starts being held down.
m.BaseButton.button_group: The ButtonGroup associated with the button. Not to be confused with node groups.
m.BaseButton.button_mask: Binary mask to choose which mouse buttons this button will respond to.
m.BaseButton.button_pressed: If true, the button's state is pressed. Means the button is pressed down or toggled (if toggle_mode is active). Only works if toggle_mode is true.
m.BaseButton.button_up: Emitted when the button stops being held down.
m.BaseButton.disabled: If true, the button is in disabled state and can't be clicked or toggled.
m.BaseButton.get_draw_mode: Returns the visual state used to draw the button. This is useful mainly when implementing your own draw code by either overriding _draw() or connecting to "draw" signal. The visual state of the button is defined by the DrawMode enum.
m.BaseButton.is_hovered: Returns true if the mouse has entered the button and has not left it yet.
m.BaseButton.keep_pressed_outside: If true, the button stays pressed when moving the cursor outside the button while pressing it.
m.BaseButton.pressed: Emitted when the button is toggled or pressed. This is on button_down if action_mode is ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_PRESS and on button_up otherwise.
m.BaseButton.set_pressed_no_signal: Changes the button_pressed state of the button, without emitting toggled. Use when you just want to change the state of the button without sending the pressed event (e.g. when initializing scene). Only works if toggle_mode is true.
m.BaseButton.shortcut_feedback: If true, the button will highlight for a short amount of time when its shortcut is activated. If false and toggle_mode is false, the shortcut will activate without any visual feedback.
m.BaseButton.shortcut_in_tooltip: If true, the button will add information about its shortcut in the tooltip. This includes the shortcut's events and its Resource.resource_name. If both events and name are empty, the shortcut will not be included.
m.BaseButton.toggle_mode: If true, the button is in toggle mode. Makes the button flip state between pressed and unpressed each time its area is clicked.
m.BaseButton.toggled: Emitted when the button was just toggled between pressed and normal states (only if toggle_mode is active). The new state is contained in the toggled_on argument.
m.BaseMaterial3D.ALPHA_ANTIALIASING_ALPHA_: Enables AlphaToCoverage. Alpha values in the material are passed to the AntiAliasing sample mask.
Enables AlphaToCoverage and forces all non-zero alpha values to 1. Alpha values in the material are passed to the AntiAliasing sample mask.
m.BaseMaterial3D.ALPHA_ANTIALIASING_OFF: Disables Alpha AntiAliasing for the material.
m.BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_ENABLED: The object's Z axis will always face the camera.
m.BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_FIXED_Y: The object's X axis will always face the camera.
m.BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_PARTICLES: Used for particle systems when assigned to GPUParticles3D and CPUParticles3D nodes (flipbook animation). Enables particles_anim_* properties.
m.BaseMaterial3D.BLEND_MODE_ADD: The color of the object is added to the background.
m.BaseMaterial3D.BLEND_MODE_MIX: Default blend mode. The color of the object is blended over the background based on the object's alpha value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.BLEND_MODE_MUL: The color of the object is multiplied by the background.
m.BaseMaterial3D.BLEND_MODE_PREMULT_ALPHA: The color of the object is added to the background and the alpha channel is used to mask out the background. This is effectively a hybrid of the blend mix and add modes, useful for effects like fire where you want the flame to add but the smoke to mix. By default, this works with unshaded materials using premultiplied textures. For shaded materials, use the PREMUL_ALPHA_FACTOR built-in so that li…
m.BaseMaterial3D.BLEND_MODE_SUB: The color of the object is subtracted from the background.
m.BaseMaterial3D.CULL_BACK: Default cull mode. The back of the object is culled when not visible. Back face triangles will be culled when facing the camera. This results in only the front side of triangles being drawn. For closed-surface meshes, this means that only the exterior of the mesh will be visible.
m.BaseMaterial3D.CULL_DISABLED: No face culling is performed; both the front face and back face will be visible.
m.BaseMaterial3D.CULL_FRONT: Front face triangles will be culled when facing the camera. This results in only the back side of triangles being drawn. For closed-surface meshes, this means that the interior of the mesh will be drawn instead of the exterior.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DEPTH_DRAW_ALWAYS: Objects will write to depth during the opaque and the transparent passes. Transparent objects that are close to the camera may obscure other transparent objects behind them.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DEPTH_DRAW_DISABLED: Objects will not write their depth to the depth buffer, even during the depth prepass (if enabled).
m.BaseMaterial3D.DEPTH_DRAW_OPAQUE_ONLY: Default depth draw mode. Depth is drawn only for opaque objects during the opaque prepass (if any) and during the opaque pass.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DEPTH_TEST_DEFAULT: Depth test will discard the pixel if it is behind other pixels.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DEPTH_TEST_INVERTED: Depth test will discard the pixel if it is in front of other pixels. Useful for stencil effects.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DETAIL_UV_1: Use UV with the detail texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DETAIL_UV_2: Use UV2 with the detail texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DIFFUSE_LAMBERT_WRAP: Extends Lambert to cover more than 90 degrees when roughness increases.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DIFFUSE_TOON: Uses a hard cut for lighting, with smoothing affected by roughness.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DISTANCE_FADE_OBJECT_DITH: Smoothly fades the object out based on the object's distance from the camera using a dithering approach. Dithering discards pixels based on a set pattern to smoothly fade without enabling transparency. On certain hardware, this can be faster than DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_ALPHA and DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_DITHER.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_ALPHA: Smoothly fades the object out based on each pixel's distance from the camera using the alpha channel.
m.BaseMaterial3D.DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_DITHE: Smoothly fades the object out based on each pixel's distance from the camera using a dithering approach. Dithering discards pixels based on a set pattern to smoothly fade without enabling transparency. On certain hardware, this can be faster than DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_ALPHA.
m.BaseMaterial3D.EMISSION_OP_ADD: Adds the emission color to the color from the emission texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY: Multiplies the emission color by the color from the emission texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FEATURE_MAX: Represents the size of the Feature enum.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_ALBEDO_FROM_VERTEX_C: Set ALBEDO to the per-vertex color specified in the mesh.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_ALBEDO_TEXTURE_FORCE: Forces the shader to convert albedo from nonlinear sRGB encoding to linear encoding. See also albedo_texture_force_srgb.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_ALBEDO_TEXTURE_MSDF: Enables multichannel signed distance field rendering shader.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_AO_ON_UV2: Use UV2 coordinates to look up from the ao_texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_BILLBOARD_KEEP_SCALE: Shader will keep the scale set for the mesh. Otherwise the scale is lost when billboarding. Only applies when billboard_mode is BILLBOARD_ENABLED.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_DISABLE_DEPTH_TEST: Disables the depth test, so this object is drawn on top of all others drawn before it. This puts the object in the transparent draw pass where it is sorted based on distance to camera. Objects drawn after it in the draw order may cover it. This also disables writing to depth.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_DISABLE_FOG: Disables receiving depth-based or volumetric fog.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_DONT_RECEIVE_SHADOWS: Disables receiving shadows from other objects.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_EMISSION_ON_UV2: Use UV2 coordinates to look up from the emission_texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_FIXED_SIZE: Object is scaled by depth so that it always appears the same size on screen.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_INVERT_HEIGHTMAP: Invert values read from a depth texture to convert them to height values (heightmap).
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_MAX: Represents the size of the Flags enum.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_PARTICLE_TRAILS_MODE: Enables parts of the shader required for GPUParticles3D trails to function. This also requires using a mesh with appropriate skinning, such as RibbonTrailMesh or TubeTrailMesh. Enabling this feature outside of materials used in GPUParticles3D meshes will break material rendering.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_SRGB_VERTEX_COLOR: Vertex colors are considered to be stored in nonlinear sRGB encoding and are converted to linear encoding during rendering. See also vertex_color_is_srgb.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_SUBSURFACE_MODE_SKIN: Enables the skin mode for subsurface scattering which is used to improve the look of subsurface scattering when used for human skin.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_USE_POINT_SIZE: Uses point size to alter the size of primitive points. Also changes the albedo texture lookup to use POINT_COORD instead of UV.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_USE_SHADOW_TO_OPACIT: Enables the shadow to opacity feature.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_USE_TEXTURE_REPEAT: Enables the texture to repeat when UV coordinates are outside the 0-1 range. If using one of the linear filtering modes, this can result in artifacts at the edges of a texture when the sampler filters across the edges of the texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_UV1_USE_TRIPLANAR: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use UV.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_UV1_USE_WORLD_TRIPLA: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use UV.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_UV2_USE_TRIPLANAR: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use UV2.
m.BaseMaterial3D.FLAG_UV2_USE_WORLD_TRIPLA: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use UV2.
m.BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_MAX: Represents the size of the ShadingMode enum.
m.BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_PER_PIXEL: The object will be shaded per pixel. Useful for realistic shading effects.
m.BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_PER_VERTEX: The object will be shaded per vertex. Useful when you want cheaper shaders and do not care about visual quality.
m.BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED: The object will not receive shadows. This is the fastest to render, but it disables all interactions with lights.
m.BaseMaterial3D.SPECULAR_DISABLED: No specular blob. This is slightly faster to render than other specular modes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.SPECULAR_TOON: Toon blob which changes size based on roughness.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_COMPARE_EQUAL: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is equal to the existing stencil value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_COMPARE_GREATER: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is greater than the existing stencil value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_COMPARE_GREATER_O: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is greater than or equal to the existing stencil value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_COMPARE_LESS: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is less than the existing stencil value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_COMPARE_LESS_OR_E: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is less than or equal to the existing stencil value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_COMPARE_NOT_EQUAL: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is not equal to the existing stencil value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_FLAG_READ: The material will only be rendered where it passes a stencil comparison with existing stencil buffer values.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_FLAG_WRITE: The material will write the reference value to the stencil buffer where it passes the depth test.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_FLAG_WRITE_DEPTH_: The material will write the reference value to the stencil buffer where it fails the depth test.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_MODE_CUSTOM: Enables stencil operations without a preset.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_MODE_OUTLINE: Stencil preset which applies an outline to the object.
m.BaseMaterial3D.STENCIL_MODE_XRAY: Stencil preset which shows a silhouette of the object behind walls.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_AMBIENT_OCCLUSION: Texture specifying per-pixel ambient occlusion value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_BENT_NORMAL: Texture specifying per-pixel bent normal vector.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_CHANNEL_ALPHA: Used to read from the alpha channel of a texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_CHANNEL_BLUE: Used to read from the blue channel of a texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_CHANNEL_GRAYSCALE: Used to read from the linear (non-perceptual) average of the red, green and blue channels of a texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_CHANNEL_GREEN: Used to read from the green channel of a texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_CHANNEL_RED: Used to read from the red channel of a texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_DETAIL_MASK: Texture specifying per-pixel detail mask blending value.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WIT: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance.

The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces t…
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_FILTER_MAX: Represents the size of the TextureFilter enum.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel only. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WI: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance.

The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that…
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_FLOWMAP: Texture specifying per-pixel flowmap direction for use with anisotropy.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_MAX: Represents the size of the TextureParam enum.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_ORM: Texture holding ambient occlusion, roughness, and metallic.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_SUBSURFACE_TRANSM: Texture specifying per-pixel transmittance for subsurface scattering.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA: The material will use the texture's alpha values for transparency. This is the slowest to render, and disables shadow casting.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_DEPTH_: The material will use the texture's alpha value for transparency, but will discard fragments with an alpha of less than 0.99 during the depth prepass and fragments with an alpha less than 0.1 during the shadow pass. This also supports casting shadows.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_HASH: The material will cut off all values below a spatially-deterministic threshold, the rest will remain opaque. This is faster to render than alpha blending, but slower than opaque rendering. This also supports casting shadows. Alpha hashing is suited for hair rendering.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_SCISSO: The material will cut off all values below a threshold, the rest will remain opaque. The opaque portions will be rendered in the depth prepass. This is faster to render than alpha blending, but slower than opaque rendering. This also supports casting shadows.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_DISABLED: The material will not use transparency. This is the fastest to render.
m.BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_MAX: Represents the size of the Transparency enum.
m.BaseMaterial3D.albedo_texture: Texture to multiply by albedo_color. Used for basic texturing of objects.
m.BaseMaterial3D.albedo_texture_force_srgb: If true, forces a conversion of the albedo_texture from nonlinear sRGB encoding to linear encoding. See also vertex_color_is_srgb.
m.BaseMaterial3D.albedo_texture_msdf: Enables multichannel signed distance field rendering shader. Use msdf_pixel_range and msdf_outline_size to configure MSDF parameters.
m.BaseMaterial3D.alpha_antialiasing_edge: Threshold at which antialiasing will be applied on the alpha channel.
m.BaseMaterial3D.alpha_antialiasing_mode: The type of alpha antialiasing to apply.
m.BaseMaterial3D.alpha_hash_scale: The hashing scale for Alpha Hash. Recommended values between 0 and 2.
m.BaseMaterial3D.alpha_scissor_threshold: Threshold at which the alpha scissor will discard values. Higher values will result in more pixels being discarded. If the material becomes too opaque at a distance, try increasing alpha_scissor_threshold. If the material disappears at a distance, try decreasing alpha_scissor_threshold.
m.BaseMaterial3D.anisotropy: The strength of the anisotropy effect. This is multiplied by anisotropy_flowmap's alpha channel if a texture is defined there and the texture contains an alpha channel.
m.BaseMaterial3D.anisotropy_enabled: If true, anisotropy is enabled. Anisotropy changes the shape of the specular blob and aligns it to tangent space. This is useful for brushed aluminum and hair reflections.
m.BaseMaterial3D.anisotropy_flowmap: Texture that offsets the tangent map for anisotropy calculations and optionally controls the anisotropy effect (if an alpha channel is present). The flowmap texture is expected to be a derivative map, with the red channel representing distortion on the X axis and green channel representing distortion on the Y axis. Values below 0.5 will result in negative distortion, whereas values above 0.5 will…
m.BaseMaterial3D.ao_enabled: If true, ambient occlusion is enabled. Ambient occlusion darkens areas based on the ao_texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.ao_light_affect: Amount that ambient occlusion affects lighting from lights. If 0, ambient occlusion only affects ambient light. If 1, ambient occlusion affects lights just as much as it affects ambient light. This can be used to impact the strength of the ambient occlusion effect, but typically looks unrealistic.
m.BaseMaterial3D.ao_on_uv2: If true, use UV2 coordinates to look up from the ao_texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.ao_texture: Texture that defines the amount of ambient occlusion for a given point on the object.
m.BaseMaterial3D.ao_texture_channel: Specifies the channel of the ao_texture in which the ambient occlusion information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.
m.BaseMaterial3D.backlight: The color used by the backlight effect. Represents the light passing through an object.
m.BaseMaterial3D.backlight_enabled: If true, the backlight effect is enabled. See also subsurf_scatter_transmittance_enabled.
m.BaseMaterial3D.backlight_texture: Texture used to control the backlight effect per-pixel. Added to backlight.
m.BaseMaterial3D.bent_normal_enabled: If true, the bent normal map is enabled. This allows for more accurate indirect lighting and specular occlusion.
m.BaseMaterial3D.bent_normal_texture: Texture that specifies the average direction of incoming ambient light at a given pixel. The bent_normal_texture only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from bent_normal_texture is oriented around the surface normal provided by the Mesh.
m.BaseMaterial3D.billboard_keep_scale: If true, the shader will keep the scale set for the mesh. Otherwise, the scale is lost when billboarding. Only applies when billboard_mode is not BILLBOARD_DISABLED.
m.BaseMaterial3D.billboard_mode: Controls how the object faces the camera.
m.BaseMaterial3D.clearcoat: Sets the strength of the clearcoat effect. Setting to 0 looks the same as disabling the clearcoat effect.
m.BaseMaterial3D.clearcoat_enabled: If true, clearcoat rendering is enabled. Adds a secondary transparent pass to the lighting calculation resulting in an added specular blob. This makes materials appear as if they have a clear layer on them that can be either glossy or rough.
m.BaseMaterial3D.clearcoat_roughness: Sets the roughness of the clearcoat pass. A higher value results in a rougher clearcoat while a lower value results in a smoother clearcoat.
m.BaseMaterial3D.clearcoat_texture: Texture that defines the strength of the clearcoat effect and the glossiness of the clearcoat. Strength is specified in the red channel while glossiness is specified in the green channel.
m.BaseMaterial3D.cull_mode: Determines which side of the triangle to cull depending on whether the triangle faces towards or away from the camera.
m.BaseMaterial3D.depth_draw_mode: Determines when depth rendering takes place. See also transparency.
m.BaseMaterial3D.depth_test: Experimental: May be affected by future rendering pipeline changes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.detail_albedo: Texture that specifies the color of the detail overlay. detail_albedo's alpha channel is used as a mask, even when the material is opaque. To use a dedicated texture as a mask, see detail_mask.
m.BaseMaterial3D.detail_blend_mode: Specifies how the detail_albedo should blend with the current ALBEDO.
m.BaseMaterial3D.detail_enabled: If true, enables the detail overlay. Detail is a second texture that gets mixed over the surface of the object based on detail_mask and detail_albedo's alpha channel. This can be used to add variation to objects, or to blend between two different albedo/normal textures.
m.BaseMaterial3D.detail_mask: Texture used to specify how the detail textures get blended with the base textures. detail_mask can be used together with detail_albedo's alpha channel (if any).
m.BaseMaterial3D.detail_normal: Texture that specifies the per-pixel normal of the detail overlay. The detail_normal texture only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from detail_normal is oriented around the surface normal provided by the Mesh.
m.BaseMaterial3D.detail_uv_layer: Specifies whether to use UV or UV2 for the detail layer.
m.BaseMaterial3D.diffuse_mode: The algorithm used for diffuse light scattering.
m.BaseMaterial3D.disable_ambient_light: If true, the object receives no ambient light.
m.BaseMaterial3D.disable_fog: If true, the object will not be affected by fog (neither volumetric nor depth fog). This is useful for unshaded or transparent materials (e.g. particles), which without this setting will be affected even if fully transparent.
m.BaseMaterial3D.disable_receive_shadows: If true, the object receives no shadow that would otherwise be cast onto it.
m.BaseMaterial3D.disable_specular_occlusio: If true, disables specular occlusion even if ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/specular_occlusion/enabled is false.
m.BaseMaterial3D.distance_fade_max_distanc: Distance at which the object appears fully opaque.
m.BaseMaterial3D.distance_fade_min_distanc: Distance at which the object starts to become visible. If the object is less than this distance away, it will be invisible.
m.BaseMaterial3D.distance_fade_mode: Specifies which type of fade to use. Can be any of the DistanceFadeModes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.emission: The emitted light's color. See emission_enabled.
m.BaseMaterial3D.emission_enabled: If true, the body emits light. Emitting light makes the object appear brighter. The object can also cast light on other objects if a VoxelGI, SDFGI, or LightmapGI is used and this object is used in baked lighting.
m.BaseMaterial3D.emission_energy_multiplie: Multiplier for emitted light. See emission_enabled.
m.BaseMaterial3D.emission_intensity: Luminance of emitted light, measured in nits (candela per square meter). Only available when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is enabled. The default is roughly equivalent to an indoor lightbulb.
m.BaseMaterial3D.emission_on_uv2: Use UV2 to read from the emission_texture.
m.BaseMaterial3D.emission_operator: Sets how emission interacts with emission_texture. Can either add or multiply.
m.BaseMaterial3D.emission_texture: Texture that specifies how much surface emits light at a given point.
m.BaseMaterial3D.fixed_size: If true, the object is rendered at the same size regardless of distance. The object's size on screen is the same as if the camera was 1.0 units away from the object's origin, regardless of the actual distance from the camera. The Camera3D's field of view (or Camera3D.size when in orthogonal/frustum mode) still affects the size the object is drawn at.
m.BaseMaterial3D.fov_override: Overrides the Camera3D's field of view angle (in degrees).
m.BaseMaterial3D.get_feature: Returns true if the specified feature is enabled.
m.BaseMaterial3D.get_flag: Returns true if the specified flag is enabled.
m.BaseMaterial3D.get_texture: Returns the Texture2D associated with the specified texture param.
m.BaseMaterial3D.grow: If true, enables the vertex grow setting. This can be used to create mesh-based outlines using a second material pass and its cull_mode set to CULL_FRONT. See also grow_amount.
m.BaseMaterial3D.grow_amount: Grows object vertices in the direction of their normals. Only effective if grow is true.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_deep_parallax: If true, uses parallax occlusion mapping to represent depth in the material instead of simple offset mapping (see heightmap_enabled). This results in a more convincing depth effect, but is much more expensive on the GPU. Only enable this on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_enabled: If true, height mapping is enabled (also called "parallax mapping" or "depth mapping"). See also normal_enabled. Height mapping is a demanding feature on the GPU, so it should only be used on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_flip_binormal: If true, flips the mesh's binormal vectors when interpreting the height map. If the heightmap effect looks strange when the camera moves (even with a reasonable heightmap_scale), try setting this to true.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_flip_tangent: If true, flips the mesh's tangent vectors when interpreting the height map. If the heightmap effect looks strange when the camera moves (even with a reasonable heightmap_scale), try setting this to true.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_flip_texture: If true, interprets the height map texture as a depth map, with brighter values appearing to be "lower" in altitude compared to darker values.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_max_layers: The number of layers to use for parallax occlusion mapping when the camera is up close to the material. Higher values result in a more convincing depth effect, especially in materials that have steep height changes. Higher values have a significant cost on the GPU, so it should only be increased on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_min_layers: The number of layers to use for parallax occlusion mapping when the camera is far away from the material. Higher values result in a more convincing depth effect, especially in materials that have steep height changes. Higher values have a significant cost on the GPU, so it should only be increased on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_scale: The heightmap scale to use for the parallax effect (see heightmap_enabled). The default value is tuned so that the highest point (value = 255) appears to be 5 cm higher than the lowest point (value = 0). Higher values result in a deeper appearance, but may result in artifacts appearing when looking at the material from oblique angles, especially when the camera moves. Negative values can be used…
m.BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_texture: The texture to use as a height map. See also heightmap_enabled.
m.BaseMaterial3D.metallic: A high value makes the material appear more like a metal. Non-metals use their albedo as the diffuse color and add diffuse to the specular reflection. With non-metals, the reflection appears on top of the albedo color. Metals use their albedo as a multiplier to the specular reflection and set the diffuse color to black resulting in a tinted reflection. Materials work better when fully metal or fu…
m.BaseMaterial3D.metallic_specular: Adjusts the strength of specular reflections. Specular reflections are composed of scene reflections and the specular lobe which is the bright spot that is reflected from light sources. When set to 0.0, no specular reflections will be visible. This differs from the SPECULAR_DISABLED SpecularMode as SPECULAR_DISABLED only applies to the specular lobe from the light source.
m.BaseMaterial3D.metallic_texture: Texture used to specify metallic for an object. This is multiplied by metallic.
m.BaseMaterial3D.metallic_texture_channel: Specifies the channel of the metallic_texture in which the metallic information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.
m.BaseMaterial3D.msdf_outline_size: The width of the shape outline.
m.BaseMaterial3D.msdf_pixel_range: The width of the range around the shape between the minimum and maximum representable signed distance.
m.BaseMaterial3D.no_depth_test: If true, depth testing is disabled and the object will be drawn in render order.
m.BaseMaterial3D.normal_enabled: If true, normal mapping is enabled. This has a slight performance cost, especially on mobile GPUs.
m.BaseMaterial3D.normal_scale: The strength of the normal map's effect.
m.BaseMaterial3D.normal_texture: Texture used to specify the normal at a given pixel. The normal_texture only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from normal_texture is oriented around the surface normal provided by the Mesh.
m.BaseMaterial3D.orm_texture: The Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic texture to use. This is a more efficient replacement of ao_texture, roughness_texture and metallic_texture in ORMMaterial3D. Ambient occlusion is stored in the red channel. Roughness map is stored in the green channel. Metallic map is stored in the blue channel. The alpha channel is ignored.
m.BaseMaterial3D.particles_anim_h_frames: The number of horizontal frames in the particle sprite sheet. Only enabled when using BILLBOARD_PARTICLES. See billboard_mode.
m.BaseMaterial3D.particles_anim_loop: If true, particle animations are looped. Only enabled when using BILLBOARD_PARTICLES. See billboard_mode.
m.BaseMaterial3D.particles_anim_v_frames: The number of vertical frames in the particle sprite sheet. Only enabled when using BILLBOARD_PARTICLES. See billboard_mode.
m.BaseMaterial3D.point_size: The point size in pixels. See use_point_size.
m.BaseMaterial3D.proximity_fade_distance: Distance over which the fade effect takes place. The larger the distance the longer it takes for an object to fade.
m.BaseMaterial3D.proximity_fade_enabled: If true, the proximity fade effect is enabled. The proximity fade effect fades out each pixel based on its distance to another object.
m.BaseMaterial3D.refraction_enabled: If true, the refraction effect is enabled. Distorts transparency based on light from behind the object.
m.BaseMaterial3D.refraction_scale: The strength of the refraction effect.
m.BaseMaterial3D.refraction_texture: Texture that controls the strength of the refraction per-pixel. Multiplied by refraction_scale.
m.BaseMaterial3D.refraction_texture_channe: Specifies the channel of the refraction_texture in which the refraction information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored refraction in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.
m.BaseMaterial3D.rim: Sets the strength of the rim lighting effect.
m.BaseMaterial3D.rim_enabled: If true, rim effect is enabled. Rim lighting increases the brightness at glancing angles on an object.
m.BaseMaterial3D.rim_texture: Texture used to set the strength of the rim lighting effect per-pixel. Multiplied by rim.
m.BaseMaterial3D.rim_tint: The amount of to blend light and albedo color when rendering rim effect. If 0 the light color is used, while 1 means albedo color is used. An intermediate value generally works best.
m.BaseMaterial3D.roughness: Surface reflection. A value of 0 represents a perfect mirror while a value of 1 completely blurs the reflection. See also metallic.
m.BaseMaterial3D.roughness_texture: Texture used to control the roughness per-pixel. Multiplied by roughness.
m.BaseMaterial3D.roughness_texture_channel: Specifies the channel of the roughness_texture in which the roughness information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.
m.BaseMaterial3D.set_feature: If enable is true, enables the specified feature. Many features that are available in BaseMaterial3D need to be enabled before use. This way, the cost for using the feature is only incurred when specified. Features can also be enabled by setting their corresponding property to true.
m.BaseMaterial3D.set_flag: If enable is true, enables the specified flag. Flags are optional behavior that can be turned on and off. Only one flag can be enabled at a time with this function, the flag enumerators cannot be bit-masked together to enable or disable multiple flags at once. Flags can also be enabled by setting their corresponding property to true.
m.BaseMaterial3D.set_texture: Sets the texture for the slot specified by param.
m.BaseMaterial3D.shading_mode: Sets whether the shading takes place, per-pixel, per-vertex or unshaded. Per-vertex lighting is faster, making it the best choice for mobile applications, however it looks considerably worse than per-pixel. Unshaded rendering is the fastest, but disables all interactions with lights.
m.BaseMaterial3D.shadow_to_opacity: If true, enables the "shadow to opacity" render mode where lighting modifies the alpha so shadowed areas are opaque and non-shadowed areas are transparent. Useful for overlaying shadows onto a camera feed in AR.
m.BaseMaterial3D.specular_mode: The method for rendering the specular blob.
m.BaseMaterial3D.stencil_color: Experimental: May be affected by future rendering pipeline changes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.stencil_compare: Experimental: May be affected by future rendering pipeline changes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.stencil_flags: Experimental: May be affected by future rendering pipeline changes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.stencil_mode: Experimental: May be affected by future rendering pipeline changes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.stencil_outline_thickness: Experimental: May be affected by future rendering pipeline changes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.stencil_reference: Experimental: May be affected by future rendering pipeline changes.
m.BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_enabled: If true, subsurface scattering is enabled. Emulates light that penetrates an object's surface, is scattered, and then emerges. Subsurface scattering quality is controlled by ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_quality.
m.BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_skin_mode: If true, subsurface scattering will use a special mode optimized for the color and density of human skin, such as boosting the intensity of the red channel in subsurface scattering.
m.BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_strength: The strength of the subsurface scattering effect. The depth of the effect is also controlled by ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_scale, which is set globally.
m.BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_texture: Texture used to control the subsurface scattering strength. Stored in the red texture channel. Multiplied by subsurf_scatter_strength.
m.BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_transmitt: The intensity of the subsurface scattering transmittance effect.
The color to multiply the subsurface scattering transmittance effect with. Ignored if subsurf_scatter_skin_mode is true.
The depth of the subsurface scattering transmittance effect.
If true, enables subsurface scattering transmittance. Only effective if subsurf_scatter_enabled is true. See also backlight_enabled.
The texture to use for multiplying the intensity of the subsurface scattering transmittance intensity. See also subsurf_scatter_texture. Ignored if subsurf_scatter_skin_mode is true.
m.BaseMaterial3D.texture_repeat: If true, the texture repeats when exceeding the texture's size. See FLAG_USE_TEXTURE_REPEAT.
m.BaseMaterial3D.transparency: The material's transparency mode. Some transparency modes will disable shadow casting. Any transparency mode other than TRANSPARENCY_DISABLED has a greater performance impact compared to opaque rendering. See also blend_mode.
m.BaseMaterial3D.use_fov_override: If true use fov_override to override the Camera3D's field of view angle.
m.BaseMaterial3D.use_particle_trails: If true, enables parts of the shader required for GPUParticles3D trails to function. This also requires using a mesh with appropriate skinning, such as RibbonTrailMesh or TubeTrailMesh. Enabling this feature outside of materials used in GPUParticles3D meshes will break material rendering.
m.BaseMaterial3D.use_point_size: If true, render point size can be changed.
m.BaseMaterial3D.use_z_clip_scale: If true use z_clip_scale to scale the object being rendered towards the camera to avoid clipping into things like walls.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv1_offset: How much to offset the UV coordinates. This amount will be added to UV in the vertex function. This can be used to offset a texture. The Z component is used when uv1_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv1_scale: How much to scale the UV coordinates. This is multiplied by UV in the vertex function. The Z component is used when uv1_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv1_triplanar: If true, instead of using UV textures will use a triplanar texture lookup to determine how to apply textures. Triplanar uses the orientation of the object's surface to blend between texture coordinates. It reads from the source texture 3 times, once for each axis and then blends between the results based on how closely the pixel aligns with each axis. This is often used for natural features to ge…
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv1_triplanar_sharpness: A lower number blends the texture more softly while a higher number blends the texture more sharply.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv1_world_triplanar: If true, triplanar mapping for UV is calculated in world space rather than object local space. See also uv1_triplanar.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv2_offset: How much to offset the UV2 coordinates. This amount will be added to UV2 in the vertex function. This can be used to offset a texture. The Z component is used when uv2_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv2_scale: How much to scale the UV2 coordinates. This is multiplied by UV2 in the vertex function. The Z component is used when uv2_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv2_triplanar: If true, instead of using UV2 textures will use a triplanar texture lookup to determine how to apply textures. Triplanar uses the orientation of the object's surface to blend between texture coordinates. It reads from the source texture 3 times, once for each axis and then blends between the results based on how closely the pixel aligns with each axis. This is often used for natural features to g…
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv2_triplanar_sharpness: A lower number blends the texture more softly while a higher number blends the texture more sharply.
m.BaseMaterial3D.uv2_world_triplanar: If true, triplanar mapping for UV2 is calculated in world space rather than object local space. See also uv2_triplanar.
m.BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_is_srgb: If true, vertex colors are considered to be stored in nonlinear sRGB encoding and are converted to linear encoding during rendering. If false, vertex colors are considered to be stored in linear encoding and are rendered as-is. See also albedo_texture_force_srgb.
m.BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albed: If true, the vertex color is used as albedo color.
m.BaseMaterial3D.z_clip_scale: Scales the object being rendered towards the camera to avoid clipping into things like walls. This is intended to be used for objects that are fixed with respect to the camera like player arms, tools, etc. Lighting and shadows will continue to work correctly when this setting is adjusted, but screen-space effects like SSAO and SSR may break with lower scales. Therefore, try to keep this setting a…
m.Basis.IDENTITY: The identity Basis. This is an orthonormal basis with no rotation, no shear, and a scale of Vector3.ONE. This also means that:
m.Basis.determinant: Returns the determinant [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant] of this basis's matrix. For advanced math, this number can be used to determine a few attributes:
m.Basis.from_euler: Constructs a new Basis that only represents rotation from the given Vector3 of Euler angles [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles], in radians.
m.Basis.from_scale: Constructs a new Basis that only represents scale, with no rotation or shear, from the given scale vector.
m.Basis.get_euler: Returns this basis's rotation as a Vector3 of Euler angles [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles], in radians. For the returned value:
m.Basis.get_rotation_quaternion: Returns this basis's rotation as a Quaternion.
m.Basis.get_scale: Returns the length of each axis of this basis, as a Vector3. If the basis is not sheared, this value is the scaling factor. It is not affected by rotation.
m.Basis.inverse: Returns the inverse of this basis's matrix [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertible_matrix].
m.Basis.is_conformal: Returns true if this basis is conformal. A conformal basis is both orthogonal (the axes are perpendicular to each other) and uniform (the axes share the same length). This method can be especially useful during physics calculations.
m.Basis.is_equal_approx: Returns true if this basis and b are approximately equal, by calling @GlobalScope.is_equal_approx() on all vector components.
m.Basis.is_finite: Returns true if this basis is finite, by calling @GlobalScope.is_finite() on all vector components.
m.Basis.is_orthonormal: Returns true if this basis is orthonormal. An orthonormal basis is both orthogonal (the axes are perpendicular to each other) and normalized (the length of every axis is 1.0). This method can be especially useful during physics calculations.
m.Basis.looking_at: Creates a new Basis with a rotation such that the forward axis (-Z) points towards the target position.
m.Basis.orthonormalized: Returns the orthonormalized version of this basis. An orthonormal basis is both orthogonal (the axes are perpendicular to each other) and normalized (the axes have a length of 1.0), which also means it can only represent a rotation.
m.Basis.rotated: Returns a copy of this basis rotated around the given axis by the given angle (in radians).
m.Basis.scaled: Returns this basis with each axis's components scaled by the given scale's components.
m.Basis.scaled_local: Returns this basis with each axis scaled by the corresponding component in the given scale.
m.Basis.slerp: Performs a spherical-linear interpolation with the to basis, given a weight. Both this basis and to should represent a rotation.
m.Basis.tdotx: Returns the transposed dot product between with and the x axis (see transposed()).
m.Basis.tdoty: Returns the transposed dot product between with and the y axis (see transposed()).
m.Basis.tdotz: Returns the transposed dot product between with and the z axis (see transposed()).
m.Basis.transposed: Returns the transposed version of this basis. This turns the basis matrix's columns into rows, and its rows into columns.
m.Basis.x: The basis's X axis, and the column 0 of the matrix.
m.Basis.y: The basis's Y axis, and the column 1 of the matrix.
m.Basis.z: The basis's Z axis, and the column 2 of the matrix.
m.BitMap.convert_to_image: Returns an image of the same size as the bitmap and with an Format of type Image.FORMAT_L8. true bits of the bitmap are being converted into white pixels, and false bits into black.
m.BitMap.create: Creates a bitmap with the specified size, filled with false.
m.BitMap.create_from_image_alpha: Creates a bitmap that matches the given image dimensions, every element of the bitmap is set to false if the alpha value of the image at that position is equal to threshold or less, and true in other case.
m.BitMap.get_bit: Returns bitmap's value at the specified position.
m.BitMap.get_bitv: Returns bitmap's value at the specified position.
m.BitMap.get_true_bit_count: Returns the number of bitmap elements that are set to true.
m.BitMap.grow_mask: Applies morphological dilation or erosion to the bitmap. If pixels is positive, dilation is applied to the bitmap. If pixels is negative, erosion is applied to the bitmap. rect defines the area where the morphological operation is applied. Pixels located outside the rect are unaffected by grow_mask().
m.BitMap.opaque_to_polygons: Creates an Array of polygons covering a rectangular portion of the bitmap. It uses a marching squares algorithm, followed by Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) reduction of the number of vertices. Each polygon is described as a PackedVector2Array of its vertices.
m.BitMap.set_bit: Sets the bitmap's element at the specified position, to the specified value.
m.BitMap.set_bit_rect: Sets a rectangular portion of the bitmap to the specified value.
m.BitMap.set_bitv: Sets the bitmap's element at the specified position, to the specified value.
m.BlitMaterial.BLEND_MODE_DISABLED: No blending mode, direct color copy.
m.BlitMaterial.BLEND_MODE_MIX: Mix blending mode. Colors are assumed to be independent of the alpha (opacity) value.
m.BlitMaterial.blend_mode: The manner in which the newly blitted texture is blended with the original DrawableTexture.
m.Bone2D.apply_rest: Resets the bone to the rest pose. This is equivalent to setting Node2D.transform to rest.
m.Bone2D.get_autocalculate_length_and_angl: Returns whether this Bone2D is going to autocalculate its length and bone angle using its first Bone2D child node, if one exists. If there are no Bone2D children, then it cannot autocalculate these values and will print a warning.
m.Bone2D.get_bone_angle: Returns the angle of the bone in the Bone2D.
m.Bone2D.get_index_in_skeleton: Returns the node's index as part of the entire skeleton. See Skeleton2D.
m.Bone2D.get_length: Returns the length of the bone in the Bone2D node.
m.Bone2D.get_skeleton_rest: Returns the node's rest Transform2D if it doesn't have a parent, or its rest pose relative to its parent.
m.Bone2D.rest: Rest transform of the bone. You can reset the node's transforms to this value using apply_rest().
m.Bone2D.set_autocalculate_length_and_angl: When set to true, the Bone2D node will attempt to automatically calculate the bone angle and length using the first child Bone2D node, if one exists. If none exist, the Bone2D cannot automatically calculate these values and will print a warning.
m.Bone2D.set_bone_angle: Sets the bone angle for the Bone2D. This is typically set to the rotation from the Bone2D to a child Bone2D node.
m.Bone2D.set_length: Sets the length of the bone in the Bone2D.
m.BoneAttachment3D.bone_idx: The index of the attached bone.
m.BoneAttachment3D.bone_name: The name of the attached bone.
m.BoneAttachment3D.external_skeleton: The NodePath to the external Skeleton3D node.
m.BoneAttachment3D.get_skeleton: Returns the parent or external Skeleton3D node if it exists, otherwise returns null.
m.BoneAttachment3D.on_skeleton_update: A function that is called automatically when the Skeleton3D is updated. This function is where the BoneAttachment3D node updates its position so it is correctly bound when it is not set to override the bone pose.
m.BoneAttachment3D.override_pose: Whether the BoneAttachment3D node will override the bone pose of the bone it is attached to. When set to true, the BoneAttachment3D node can change the pose of the bone. When set to false, the BoneAttachment3D will always be set to the bone's transform.
m.BoneAttachment3D.use_external_skeleton: Whether the BoneAttachment3D node will use an external Skeleton3D node rather than attempting to use its parent node as the Skeleton3D. When set to true, the BoneAttachment3D node will use the external Skeleton3D node set in external_skeleton.
m.BoneConstraint3D.REFERENCE_TYPE_BONE: The reference target is a bone. In this case, the reference target spaces is local space.
m.BoneConstraint3D.REFERENCE_TYPE_NODE: The reference target is a Node3D. In this case, the reference target spaces is model space.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_amount: Returns the apply amount of the setting at index.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_apply_bone: Returns the apply bone of the setting at index. This bone will be modified.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_apply_bone_name: Returns the apply bone name of the setting at index. This bone will be modified.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_reference_bone: Returns the reference bone of the setting at index.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_reference_bone_name: Returns the reference bone name of the setting at index.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_reference_node: Returns the reference node path of the setting at index.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_reference_type: Returns the reference target type of the setting at index. See also ReferenceType.
m.BoneConstraint3D.get_setting_count: Returns the number of settings in the modifier.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_amount: Sets the apply amount of the setting at index to amount.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_apply_bone: Sets the apply bone of the setting at index to bone. This bone will be modified.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_apply_bone_name: Sets the apply bone of the setting at index to bone_name. This bone will be modified.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_reference_bone: Sets the reference bone of the setting at index to bone.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_reference_bone_name: Sets the reference bone of the setting at index to bone_name.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_reference_node: Sets the reference node path of the setting at index to node.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_reference_type: Sets the reference target type of the setting at index to type. See also ReferenceType.
m.BoneConstraint3D.set_setting_count: Sets the number of settings in the modifier.
m.BoneMap.bone_map_updated: This signal is emitted when change the key value in the BoneMap. This is used to validate mapping and to update BoneMap editor.
m.BoneMap.find_profile_bone_name: Returns a profile bone name having skeleton_bone_name. If not found, an empty StringName will be returned.
m.BoneMap.get_skeleton_bone_name: Returns a skeleton bone name is mapped to profile_bone_name.
m.BoneMap.profile: A SkeletonProfile of the mapping target. Key names in the BoneMap are synchronized with it.
m.BoneMap.profile_updated: This signal is emitted when change the value in profile or change the reference of profile. This is used to update key names in the BoneMap and to redraw the BoneMap editor.
m.BoneMap.set_skeleton_bone_name: Maps a skeleton bone name to profile_bone_name.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTO: You can assign arbitrary amounts to the joint list. See also set_joint_twist_amount().
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.DISPERSE_MODE_EVEN: Assign amounts so that they monotonically increase from 0.0 to 1.0, ensuring all weights are equal. For example, with five joints, the amounts would be 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0 starting from the root bone.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.DISPERSE_MODE_WEIGH: Assign amounts so that they monotonically increase from 0.0 to 1.0, based on the length of the bones between joint segments. See also set_weight_position().
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_damping_curve: Returns the damping curve when get_disperse_mode() is DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_disperse_mode: Returns whether to use automatic amount assignment or to allow manual assignment.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_end_bone: Returns the end bone index of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_end_bone_direct: Returns the tail direction of the end bone of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_end_bone_name: Returns the end bone name of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_joint_bone: Returns the bone index at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_joint_bone_name: Returns the bone name at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_joint_count: Returns the joint count of the bone chain's joint list.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_joint_twist_amo: Returns the twist amount at joint in the bone chain's joint list when get_disperse_mode() is DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_reference_bone: Returns the reference bone to extract twist of the setting at index.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_reference_bone_: Returns the reference bone name to extract twist of the setting at index.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_root_bone: Returns the root bone index of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_root_bone_name: Returns the root bone name of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_twist_from: Returns the rotation to an arbitrary state before twisting for the current bone pose to extract the twist when is_twist_from_rest() is false.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.get_weight_position: Returns the position at which to divide the segment between joints for weight assignment when get_disperse_mode() is DISPERSE_MODE_WEIGHTED.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.is_end_bone_extende: Returns true if the end bone is extended to have a tail.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.is_twist_from_rest: Returns true if extracting the twist amount from the difference between the bone rest and the current bone pose.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.mutable_bone_axes: If true, the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone pose every frame.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_damping_curve: Sets the damping curve when get_disperse_mode() is DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_disperse_mode: Sets whether to use automatic amount assignment or to allow manual assignment.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_end_bone: Sets the end bone index of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_end_bone_direct: Sets the end bone tail direction of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_end_bone_name: Sets the end bone name of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_extend_end_bone: If enabled is true, the end bone is extended to have a tail.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_joint_twist_amo: Sets the twist amount at joint in the bone chain's joint list when get_disperse_mode() is DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_root_bone: Sets the root bone index of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_root_bone_name: Sets the root bone name of the bone chain.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_twist_from: Sets the rotation to an arbitrary state before twisting for the current bone pose to extract the twist when is_twist_from_rest() is false.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_twist_from_rest: If enabled is true, it extracts the twist amount from the difference between the bone rest and the current bone pose.
m.BoneTwistDisperser3D.set_weight_position: Sets the position at which to divide the segment between joints for weight assignment when get_disperse_mode() is DISPERSE_MODE_WEIGHTED.
m.BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_BEGIN: The child controls will be arranged at the beginning of the container, i.e. top if orientation is vertical, left if orientation is horizontal (right for RTL layout).
m.BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER: The child controls will be centered in the container.
m.BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_END: The child controls will be arranged at the end of the container, i.e. bottom if orientation is vertical, right if orientation is horizontal (left for RTL layout).
m.BoxContainer.add_spacer: Adds a Control node to the box as a spacer. If begin is true, it will insert the Control node in front of all other children.
m.BoxContainer.alignment: The alignment of the container's children (must be one of ALIGNMENT_BEGIN, ALIGNMENT_CENTER, or ALIGNMENT_END).
m.BoxContainer.vertical: If true, the BoxContainer will arrange its children vertically, rather than horizontally.
m.BoxMesh.size: The box's width, height and depth.
m.BoxMesh.subdivide_depth: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the Z axis.
m.BoxMesh.subdivide_height: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the Y axis.
m.BoxMesh.subdivide_width: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the X axis.
m.BoxShape3D.size: The box's width, height and depth.
m.Button.alignment: Text alignment policy for the button's text.
m.Button.autowrap_mode: If set to something other than TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF, the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle.
m.Button.autowrap_trim_flags: Autowrap space trimming flags. See TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_START_EDGE_SPACES and TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_END_EDGE_SPACES for more info.
m.Button.clip_text: If true, text that is too large to fit the button is clipped horizontally. If false, the button will always be wide enough to hold the text. The text is not vertically clipped, and the button's height is not affected by this property.
m.Button.expand_icon: When enabled, the button's icon will expand/shrink to fit the button's size while keeping its aspect. See also icon_max_width.
m.Button.icon: Button's icon, if text is present the icon will be placed before the text.
m.Button.icon_alignment: Specifies if the icon should be aligned horizontally to the left, right, or center of a button. Uses the same HorizontalAlignment constants as the text alignment. If centered horizontally and vertically, text will draw on top of the icon.
m.Button.language: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.Button.text: The button's text that will be displayed inside the button's area.
m.Button.text_overrun_behavior: Sets the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the node's bounding rectangle.
m.Button.vertical_icon_alignment: Specifies if the icon should be aligned vertically to the top, bottom, or center of a button. Uses the same VerticalAlignment constants as the text alignment. If centered horizontally and vertically, text will draw on top of the icon.
m.ButtonGroup.allow_unpress: If true, it is possible to unpress all buttons in this ButtonGroup.
m.ButtonGroup.get_buttons: Returns an Array of Buttons who have this as their ButtonGroup (see BaseButton.button_group).
m.ButtonGroup.pressed: Emitted when one of the buttons of the group is pressed.
m.CPUParticles2D.DRAW_ORDER_INDEX: Particles are drawn in the order emitted.
m.CPUParticles2D.DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME: Particles are drawn in order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_P: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among emission_points. Particle velocity and rotation will be set based on emission_normals. Particle color will be modulated by emission_colors.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_MAX: Represents the size of the EmissionShape enum.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_POINT: All particles will be emitted from a single point.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among emission_points. Particle color will be modulated by emission_colors.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_RECTANGLE: Particles will be emitted in the area of a rectangle.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_RING: Particles will be emitted in the area of a ring parameterized by its outer and inner radius.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE: Particles will be emitted in the volume of a sphere flattened to two dimensions.
m.CPUParticles2D.EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE_SUR: Particles will be emitted on the surface of a sphere flattened to two dimensions.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_ANGLE: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set angle properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_ANGULAR_VELOCITY: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set angular velocity properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_ANIM_OFFSET: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set animation offset properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_ANIM_SPEED: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set animation speed properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_DAMPING: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set damping properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_HUE_VARIATION: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set hue variation properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_INITIAL_LINEAR_VELO: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set initial velocity properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_LINEAR_ACCEL: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set linear acceleration properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_MAX: Represents the size of the Parameter enum.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_ORBIT_VELOCITY: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set orbital velocity properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_RADIAL_ACCEL: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set radial acceleration properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_SCALE: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set scale properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARAM_TANGENTIAL_ACCEL: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set tangential acceleration properties.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARTICLE_FLAG_ALIGN_Y_TO_: Use with set_particle_flag() to set particle_flag_align_y.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARTICLE_FLAG_DISABLE_Z: Present for consistency with 3D particle nodes, not used in 2D.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARTICLE_FLAG_MAX: Represents the size of the ParticleFlags enum.
m.CPUParticles2D.PARTICLE_FLAG_ROTATE_Y: Present for consistency with 3D particle nodes, not used in 2D.
