m.CPUParticles2D.amount: Number of particles emitted in one emission cycle.
m.CPUParticles2D.angle_curve: Each particle's rotation will be animated along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.angle_max: Maximum initial rotation applied to each particle, in degrees.
m.CPUParticles2D.angular_velocity_curve: Each particle's angular velocity will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.angular_velocity_max: Maximum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.
m.CPUParticles2D.anim_offset_curve: Each particle's animation offset will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.anim_offset_max: Maximum animation offset that corresponds to frame index in the texture. 0 is the first frame, 1 is the last one. See CanvasItemMaterial.particles_animation.
m.CPUParticles2D.anim_speed_curve: Each particle's animation speed will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.anim_speed_max: Maximum particle animation speed. Animation speed of 1 means that the particles will make full 0 to 1 offset cycle during lifetime, 2 means 2 cycles etc.
m.CPUParticles2D.color: Each particle's initial color. If texture is defined, it will be multiplied by this color.
m.CPUParticles2D.color_initial_ramp: Each particle's initial color will vary along this Gradient (multiplied with color).
m.CPUParticles2D.color_ramp: Each particle's color will vary along this Gradient over its lifetime (multiplied with color).
m.CPUParticles2D.convert_from_particles: Sets this node's properties to match a given GPUParticles2D node with an assigned ParticleProcessMaterial.
m.CPUParticles2D.damping_curve: Damping will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.damping_max: The maximum rate at which particles lose velocity. For example value of 100 means that the particle will go from 100 velocity to 0 in 1 second.
m.CPUParticles2D.direction: Unit vector specifying the particles' emission direction.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_colors: Sets the Colors to modulate particles by when using EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS or EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_normals: Sets the direction the particles will be emitted in when using EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_points: Sets the initial positions to spawn particles when using EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS or EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_rect_extents: The rectangle's extents if emission_shape is set to EMISSION_SHAPE_RECTANGLE.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_ring_inner_radiu: The ring's inner radius if emission_shape is set to EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_ring_radius: The ring's outer radius if emission_shape is set to EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_shape: Particles will be emitted inside this region.
m.CPUParticles2D.emission_sphere_radius: The sphere's radius if emission_shape is set to EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE.
m.CPUParticles2D.emitting: If true, particles are being emitted. emitting can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if one_shot is true setting emitting to true will not restart the emission cycle until after all active particles finish processing. You can use the finished signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.
m.CPUParticles2D.explosiveness: How rapidly particles in an emission cycle are emitted. If greater than 0, there will be a gap in emissions before the next cycle begins.
m.CPUParticles2D.finished: Emitted when all active particles have finished processing. When one_shot is disabled, particles will process continuously, so this is never emitted.
m.CPUParticles2D.fixed_fps: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the simulation of the particle system itself.
m.CPUParticles2D.fract_delta: If true, results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.
m.CPUParticles2D.get_param_curve: Returns the Curve of the parameter specified by Parameter.
m.CPUParticles2D.get_param_max: Returns the maximum value range for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles2D.get_param_min: Returns the minimum value range for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles2D.get_particle_flag: Returns the enabled state of the given particle flag.
m.CPUParticles2D.hue_variation_curve: Each particle's hue will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.hue_variation_max: Maximum initial hue variation applied to each particle. It will shift the particle color's hue.
m.CPUParticles2D.initial_velocity_max: Maximum initial velocity magnitude for each particle. Direction comes from direction and spread.
m.CPUParticles2D.lifetime: Amount of time each particle will exist.
m.CPUParticles2D.linear_accel_curve: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.linear_accel_max: Maximum linear acceleration applied to each particle in the direction of motion.
m.CPUParticles2D.local_coords: If true, particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the CPUParticles2D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If false, particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the CPUParticles2D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.
m.CPUParticles2D.one_shot: If true, only one emission cycle occurs. If set true during a cycle, emission will stop at the cycle's end.
m.CPUParticles2D.orbit_velocity_curve: Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.orbit_velocity_max: Maximum orbital velocity applied to each particle. Makes the particles circle around origin. Specified in number of full rotations around origin per second.
m.CPUParticles2D.particle_flag_align_y: Align Y axis of particle with the direction of its velocity.
m.CPUParticles2D.preprocess: Particle system starts as if it had already run for this many seconds.
m.CPUParticles2D.radial_accel_curve: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.radial_accel_max: Maximum radial acceleration applied to each particle. Makes particle accelerate away from the origin or towards it if negative.
m.CPUParticles2D.request_particles_process: Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
m.CPUParticles2D.scale_amount_curve: Each particle's scale will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.scale_amount_max: Maximum initial scale applied to each particle.
m.CPUParticles2D.scale_curve_x: Each particle's horizontal scale will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.scale_curve_y: Each particle's vertical scale will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.seed: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if use_fixed_seed is true.
m.CPUParticles2D.set_param_curve: Sets the Curve of the parameter specified by Parameter. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.set_param_max: Sets the maximum value for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles2D.set_param_min: Sets the minimum value for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles2D.set_particle_flag: Enables or disables the given particle flag.
m.CPUParticles2D.speed_scale: Particle system's running speed scaling ratio. A value of 0 can be used to pause the particles.
m.CPUParticles2D.split_scale: If true, the scale curve will be split into x and y components. See scale_curve_x and scale_curve_y.
m.CPUParticles2D.spread: Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees.
m.CPUParticles2D.tangential_accel_curve: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles2D.tangential_accel_max: Maximum tangential acceleration applied to each particle. Tangential acceleration is perpendicular to the particle's velocity giving the particles a swirling motion.
m.CPUParticles2D.texture: Particle texture. If null, particles will be squares.
m.CPUParticles2D.use_fixed_seed: If true, particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in seed. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.
m.CPUParticles3D.DRAW_ORDER_INDEX: Particles are drawn in the order emitted.
m.CPUParticles3D.DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME: Particles are drawn in order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.
m.CPUParticles3D.DRAW_ORDER_VIEW_DEPTH: Particles are drawn in order of depth.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_BOX: Particles will be emitted in the volume of a box.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_P: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among emission_points. Particle velocity and rotation will be set based on emission_normals. Particle color will be modulated by emission_colors.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_MAX: Represents the size of the EmissionShape enum.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_POINT: All particles will be emitted from a single point.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among emission_points. Particle color will be modulated by emission_colors.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_RING: Particles will be emitted in a ring or cylinder.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE: Particles will be emitted in the volume of a sphere.
m.CPUParticles3D.EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE_SUR: Particles will be emitted on the surface of a sphere.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_ANGLE: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set angle properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_ANGULAR_VELOCITY: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set angular velocity properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_ANIM_OFFSET: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set animation offset properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_ANIM_SPEED: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set animation speed properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_DAMPING: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set damping properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_HUE_VARIATION: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set hue variation properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_INITIAL_LINEAR_VELO: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set initial velocity properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_LINEAR_ACCEL: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set linear acceleration properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_MAX: Represents the size of the Parameter enum.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_ORBIT_VELOCITY: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set orbital velocity properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_RADIAL_ACCEL: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set radial acceleration properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_SCALE: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set scale properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARAM_TANGENTIAL_ACCEL: Use with set_param_min(), set_param_max(), and set_param_curve() to set tangential acceleration properties.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARTICLE_FLAG_ALIGN_Y_TO_: Use with set_particle_flag() to set particle_flag_align_y.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARTICLE_FLAG_DISABLE_Z: Use with set_particle_flag() to set particle_flag_disable_z.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARTICLE_FLAG_MAX: Represents the size of the ParticleFlags enum.
m.CPUParticles3D.PARTICLE_FLAG_ROTATE_Y: Use with set_particle_flag() to set particle_flag_rotate_y.
m.CPUParticles3D.amount: Number of particles emitted in one emission cycle.
m.CPUParticles3D.angle_curve: Each particle's rotation will be animated along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.angular_velocity_curve: Each particle's angular velocity (rotation speed) will vary along this Curve over its lifetime. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.angular_velocity_max: Maximum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.
m.CPUParticles3D.angular_velocity_min: Minimum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.
m.CPUParticles3D.anim_offset_curve: Each particle's animation offset will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.anim_speed_curve: Each particle's animation speed will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.capture_aabb: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box that contains all the particles that are active in the current frame.
m.CPUParticles3D.color_initial_ramp: Each particle's initial color will vary along this Gradient (multiplied with color).
m.CPUParticles3D.color_ramp: Each particle's color will vary along this Gradient over its lifetime (multiplied with color).
m.CPUParticles3D.convert_from_particles: Sets this node's properties to match a given GPUParticles3D node with an assigned ParticleProcessMaterial.
m.CPUParticles3D.damping_curve: Damping will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.direction: Unit vector specifying the particles' emission direction.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_box_extents: The rectangle's extents if emission_shape is set to EMISSION_SHAPE_BOX.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_colors: Sets the Colors to modulate particles by when using EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS or EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_normals: Sets the direction the particles will be emitted in when using EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_points: Sets the initial positions to spawn particles when using EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS or EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_ring_axis: The axis of the ring when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_ring_cone_angle: The angle of the cone when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING. The default angle of 90 degrees results in a ring, while an angle of 0 degrees results in a cone. Intermediate values will result in a ring where one end is larger than the other.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_ring_height: The height of the ring when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_ring_inner_radiu: The inner radius of the ring when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_ring_radius: The radius of the ring when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_shape: Particles will be emitted inside this region.
m.CPUParticles3D.emission_sphere_radius: The sphere's radius if EmissionShape is set to EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE.
m.CPUParticles3D.emitting: If true, particles are being emitted. emitting can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if one_shot is true setting emitting to true will not restart the emission cycle until after all active particles finish processing. You can use the finished signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.
m.CPUParticles3D.explosiveness: How rapidly particles in an emission cycle are emitted. If greater than 0, there will be a gap in emissions before the next cycle begins.
m.CPUParticles3D.finished: Emitted when all active particles have finished processing. When one_shot is disabled, particles will process continuously, so this is never emitted.
m.CPUParticles3D.fixed_fps: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the particle system itself.
m.CPUParticles3D.flatness: Amount of spread in Y/Z plane. A value of 1 restricts particles to X/Z plane.
m.CPUParticles3D.fract_delta: If true, results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.
m.CPUParticles3D.get_param_curve: Returns the Curve of the parameter specified by Parameter.
m.CPUParticles3D.get_param_max: Returns the maximum value range for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles3D.get_param_min: Returns the minimum value range for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles3D.get_particle_flag: Returns the enabled state of the given particle flag.
m.CPUParticles3D.hue_variation_curve: Each particle's hue will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.initial_velocity_max: Maximum value of the initial velocity.
m.CPUParticles3D.initial_velocity_min: Minimum value of the initial velocity.
m.CPUParticles3D.lifetime: Amount of time each particle will exist.
m.CPUParticles3D.linear_accel_curve: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.local_coords: If true, particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the CPUParticles3D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If false, particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the CPUParticles3D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.
m.CPUParticles3D.mesh: The Mesh used for each particle. If null, particles will be spheres.
m.CPUParticles3D.one_shot: If true, only one emission cycle occurs. If set true during a cycle, emission will stop at the cycle's end.
m.CPUParticles3D.orbit_velocity_curve: Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.particle_flag_align_y: Align Y axis of particle with the direction of its velocity.
m.CPUParticles3D.particle_flag_disable_z: If true, particles will not move on the Z axis.
m.CPUParticles3D.particle_flag_rotate_y: If true, particles rotate around Y axis by angle_min.
m.CPUParticles3D.preprocess: Particle system starts as if it had already run for this many seconds.
m.CPUParticles3D.radial_accel_curve: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.request_particles_process: Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
m.CPUParticles3D.scale_amount_curve: Each particle's scale will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.scale_curve_x: Curve for the scale over life, along the x axis.
m.CPUParticles3D.scale_curve_y: Curve for the scale over life, along the y axis.
m.CPUParticles3D.scale_curve_z: Curve for the scale over life, along the z axis.
m.CPUParticles3D.seed: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if use_fixed_seed is true.
m.CPUParticles3D.set_param_curve: Sets the Curve of the parameter specified by Parameter. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.set_param_max: Sets the maximum value for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles3D.set_param_min: Sets the minimum value for the given parameter.
m.CPUParticles3D.set_particle_flag: Enables or disables the given particle flag.
m.CPUParticles3D.speed_scale: Particle system's running speed scaling ratio. A value of 0 can be used to pause the particles.
m.CPUParticles3D.split_scale: If set to true, three different scale curves can be specified, one per scale axis.
m.CPUParticles3D.spread: Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees. Applied to X/Z plane and Y/Z planes.
m.CPUParticles3D.tangential_accel_curve: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this Curve. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CPUParticles3D.use_fixed_seed: If true, particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in seed. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.
m.CPUParticles3D.visibility_aabb: The AABB that determines the node's region which needs to be visible on screen for the particle system to be active.
m.CSGBox3D.material: The material used to render the box.
m.CSGBox3D.size: The box's width, height and depth.
m.CSGCylinder3D.cone: If true a cone is created, the radius will only apply to one side.
m.CSGCylinder3D.material: The material used to render the cylinder.
m.CSGCylinder3D.sides: The number of sides of the cylinder, the higher this number the more detail there will be in the cylinder.
m.CSGCylinder3D.smooth_faces: If true the normals of the cylinder are set to give a smooth effect making the cylinder seem rounded. If false the cylinder will have a flat shaded look.
m.CSGMesh3D.material: The Material used in drawing the CSG shape.
m.CSGMesh3D.mesh: The Mesh resource to use as a CSG shape.
m.CSGPolygon3D.MODE_DEPTH: The polygon shape is extruded along the negative Z axis.
m.CSGPolygon3D.MODE_PATH: The polygon shape is extruded along the Path3D specified in path_node.
m.CSGPolygon3D.MODE_SPIN: The polygon shape is extruded by rotating it around the Y axis.
m.CSGPolygon3D.PATH_INTERVAL_DISTANCE: When mode is set to MODE_PATH, path_interval will determine the distance, in meters, each interval of the path will extrude.
m.CSGPolygon3D.PATH_INTERVAL_SUBDIVIDE: When mode is set to MODE_PATH, path_interval will subdivide the polygons along the path.
m.CSGPolygon3D.PATH_ROTATION_PATH: The polygon shape is rotated along the path, but it is not rotated around the path axis.
m.CSGPolygon3D.PATH_ROTATION_PATH_FOLLOW: The polygon shape follows the path and its rotations around the path axis.
m.CSGPolygon3D.PATH_ROTATION_POLYGON: The polygon shape is not rotated.
m.CSGPolygon3D.depth: When mode is MODE_DEPTH, the depth of the extrusion.
m.CSGPolygon3D.material: Material to use for the resulting mesh. The UV maps the top half of the material to the extruded shape (U along the length of the extrusions and V around the outline of the polygon), the bottom-left quarter to the front end face, and the bottom-right quarter to the back end face.
m.CSGPolygon3D.mode: The mode used to extrude the polygon.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_continuous_u: When mode is MODE_PATH, by default, the top half of the material is stretched along the entire length of the extruded shape. If false the top half of the material is repeated every step of the extrusion.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_interval: When mode is MODE_PATH, the path interval or ratio of path points to extrusions.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_interval_type: When mode is MODE_PATH, this will determine if the interval should be by distance (PATH_INTERVAL_DISTANCE) or subdivision fractions (PATH_INTERVAL_SUBDIVIDE).
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_joined: When mode is MODE_PATH, if true the ends of the path are joined, by adding an extrusion between the last and first points of the path.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_local: When mode is MODE_PATH, if true the Transform3D of the CSGPolygon3D is used as the starting point for the extrusions, not the Transform3D of the path_node.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_node: When mode is MODE_PATH, the location of the Path3D object used to extrude the polygon.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_rotation: When mode is MODE_PATH, the path rotation method used to rotate the polygon as it is extruded.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_rotation_accurate: When mode is MODE_PATH, if true the polygon will be rotated according to the proper tangent of the path at the sampled points. If false an approximation is used, which decreases in accuracy as the number of subdivisions decreases.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_simplify_angle: When mode is MODE_PATH, extrusions that are less than this angle, will be merged together to reduce polygon count.
m.CSGPolygon3D.path_u_distance: When mode is MODE_PATH, this is the distance along the path, in meters, the texture coordinates will tile. When set to 0, texture coordinates will match geometry exactly with no tiling.
m.CSGPolygon3D.polygon: The point array that defines the 2D polygon that is extruded. This can be a convex or concave polygon with 3 or more points. The polygon must not have any intersecting edges. Otherwise, triangulation will fail and no mesh will be generated.
m.CSGPolygon3D.smooth_faces: If true, applies smooth shading to the extrusions.
m.CSGPolygon3D.spin_degrees: When mode is MODE_SPIN, the total number of degrees the polygon is rotated when extruding.
m.CSGPolygon3D.spin_sides: When mode is MODE_SPIN, the number of extrusions made.
m.CSGPrimitive3D.flip_faces: If set, the order of the vertices in each triangle are reversed resulting in the backside of the mesh being drawn.
m.CSGShape3D.OPERATION_INTERSECTION: Only intersecting geometry remains, the rest is removed.
m.CSGShape3D.OPERATION_SUBTRACTION: The second shape is subtracted from the first, leaving a dent with its shape.
m.CSGShape3D.OPERATION_UNION: Geometry of both primitives is merged, intersecting geometry is removed.
m.CSGShape3D.autosmooth: Enables automatic smoothing. This overrides any smoothing on the CSG node and instead uses smoothing_angle to calculate normals based on the angle between faces.
m.CSGShape3D.bake_collision_shape: Returns a baked physics ConcavePolygonShape3D of this node's CSG operation result. Returns an empty shape if the node is not a CSG root node or has no valid geometry.
m.CSGShape3D.bake_static_mesh: Returns a baked static ArrayMesh of this node's CSG operation result. Materials from involved CSG nodes are added as extra mesh surfaces. Returns an empty mesh if the node is not a CSG root node or has no valid geometry.
m.CSGShape3D.calculate_tangents: Calculate tangents for the CSG shape which allows the use of normal and height maps. This is only applied on the root shape, this setting is ignored on any child. Setting this to false can speed up shape generation slightly.
m.CSGShape3D.collision_layer: The physics layers this area is in.
m.CSGShape3D.collision_mask: The physics layers this CSG shape scans for collisions. Only effective if use_collision is true. See Collision layers and masks in the documentation for more information.
m.CSGShape3D.collision_priority: The priority used to solve colliding when occurring penetration. Only effective if use_collision is true. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the object will be. This can for example be used to prevent the player from breaking through the boundaries of a level.
m.CSGShape3D.get_collision_layer_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_layer is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CSGShape3D.get_collision_mask_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CSGShape3D.get_meshes: Returns an Array with two elements, the first is the Transform3D of this node and the second is the root Mesh of this node. Only works when this node is the root shape.
m.CSGShape3D.is_root_shape: Returns true if this is a root shape and is thus the object that is rendered.
m.CSGShape3D.operation: The operation that is performed on this shape. This is ignored for the first CSG child node as the operation is between this node and the previous child of this nodes parent.
m.CSGShape3D.set_collision_layer_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_layer, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CSGShape3D.set_collision_mask_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CSGShape3D.smoothing_angle: When autosmooth is enabled, faces with an angle between them greater than this will be smoothed, while faces with a smaller angle will remain sharp.
m.CSGShape3D.snap: Deprecated: The CSG library no longer uses snapping.
m.CSGShape3D.use_collision: Adds a collision shape to the physics engine for our CSG shape. This will always act like a static body. Note that the collision shape is still active even if the CSG shape itself is hidden. See also collision_mask and collision_priority.
m.CSGSphere3D.material: The material used to render the sphere.
m.CSGSphere3D.radial_segments: Number of vertical slices for the sphere.
m.CSGSphere3D.rings: Number of horizontal slices for the sphere.
m.CSGSphere3D.smooth_faces: If true the normals of the sphere are set to give a smooth effect making the sphere seem rounded. If false the sphere will have a flat shaded look.
m.CSGTorus3D.inner_radius: The inner radius of the torus.
m.CSGTorus3D.material: The material used to render the torus.
m.CSGTorus3D.outer_radius: The outer radius of the torus.
m.CSGTorus3D.ring_sides: The number of edges each ring of the torus is constructed of.
m.CSGTorus3D.sides: The number of slices the torus is constructed of.
m.CSGTorus3D.smooth_faces: If true the normals of the torus are set to give a smooth effect making the torus seem rounded. If false the torus will have a flat shaded look.
m.Callable.bind: Returns a copy of this Callable with one or more arguments bound. When called, the bound arguments are passed after the arguments supplied by call(). See also unbind().
m.Callable.bindv: Returns a copy of this Callable with one or more arguments bound, reading them from an array. When called, the bound arguments are passed after the arguments supplied by call(). See also unbind().
m.Callable.call: Calls the method represented by this Callable. Arguments can be passed and should match the method's signature.
m.Callable.call_deferred: Calls the method represented by this Callable in deferred mode, i.e. at the end of the current frame. Arguments can be passed and should match the method's signature.
m.Callable.callv: Calls the method represented by this Callable. Unlike call(), this method expects all arguments to be contained inside the arguments Array.
m.Callable.create: Creates a new Callable for the method named method in the specified variant. To represent a method of a built-in Variant type, a custom callable is used (see is_custom()). If variant is Object, then a standard callable will be created instead.
m.Callable.get_argument_count: Returns the total number of arguments this Callable should take, including optional arguments. This means that any arguments bound with bind() are subtracted from the result, and any arguments unbound with unbind() are added to the result.
m.Callable.get_bound_arguments: Returns the array of arguments bound via successive bind() or unbind() calls. These arguments will be added after the arguments passed to the call, from which get_unbound_arguments_count() arguments on the right have been previously excluded.
m.Callable.get_bound_arguments_count: Returns the total amount of arguments bound via successive bind() or unbind() calls. This is the same as the size of the array returned by get_bound_arguments(). See get_bound_arguments() for details.
m.Callable.get_method: Returns the name of the method represented by this Callable. If the callable is a GDScript lambda function, returns the function's name or "".
m.Callable.get_object: Returns the object on which this Callable is called.
m.Callable.get_object_id: Returns the ID of this Callable's object (see Object.get_instance_id()).
m.Callable.get_unbound_arguments_count: Returns the total amount of arguments unbound via successive bind() or unbind() calls. See get_bound_arguments() for details.
m.Callable.hash: Returns the 32-bit hash value of this Callable's object.
m.Callable.is_custom: Returns true if this Callable is a custom callable. Custom callables are used:
m.Callable.is_null: Returns true if this Callable has no target to call the method on. Equivalent to callable == Callable().
m.Callable.is_standard: Returns true if this Callable is a standard callable. This method is the opposite of is_custom(). Returns false if this callable is a lambda function.
m.Callable.is_valid: Returns true if the callable's object exists and has a valid method name assigned, or is a custom callable.
m.Callable.rpc: Perform an RPC (Remote Procedure Call) on all connected peers. This is used for multiplayer and is normally not available, unless the function being called has been marked as RPC (using @GDScript.@rpc or Node.rpc_config()). Calling this method on unsupported functions will result in an error. See Node.rpc().
m.Callable.rpc_id: Perform an RPC (Remote Procedure Call) on a specific peer ID (see multiplayer documentation for reference). This is used for multiplayer and is normally not available unless the function being called has been marked as RPC (using @GDScript.@rpc or Node.rpc_config()). Calling this method on unsupported functions will result in an error. See Node.rpc_id().
m.Callable.unbind: Returns a copy of this Callable with a number of arguments unbound. In other words, when the new callable is called the last few arguments supplied by the user are ignored, according to argcount. The remaining arguments are passed to the callable. This allows to use the original callable in a context that attempts to pass more arguments than this callable can handle, e.g. a signal with a fixed nu…
m.CallbackTweener.set_delay: Makes the callback call delayed by given time in seconds.
m.Camera2D.ANCHOR_MODE_DRAG_CENTER: The camera's position takes into account vertical/horizontal offsets and the screen size.
m.Camera2D.ANCHOR_MODE_FIXED_TOP_LEFT: The camera's position is fixed so that the top-left corner is always at the origin.
m.Camera2D.CAMERA2D_PROCESS_IDLE: The camera updates during process frames (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS).
m.Camera2D.CAMERA2D_PROCESS_PHYSICS: The camera updates during physics frames (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS).
m.Camera2D.align: Aligns the camera to the tracked node.
m.Camera2D.custom_viewport: The custom Viewport node attached to the Camera2D. If null or not a Viewport, uses the default viewport instead.
m.Camera2D.drag_bottom_margin: Bottom margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the bottom edge of the screen.
m.Camera2D.drag_horizontal_enabled: If true, the camera only moves when reaching the horizontal (left and right) drag margins. If false, the camera moves horizontally regardless of margins.
m.Camera2D.drag_horizontal_offset: The relative horizontal drag offset of the camera between the right (-1) and left (1) drag margins.
m.Camera2D.drag_left_margin: Left margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the left edge of the screen.
m.Camera2D.drag_right_margin: Right margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the right edge of the screen.
m.Camera2D.drag_top_margin: Top margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the top edge of the screen.
m.Camera2D.drag_vertical_enabled: If true, the camera only moves when reaching the vertical (top and bottom) drag margins. If false, the camera moves vertically regardless of the drag margins.
m.Camera2D.drag_vertical_offset: The relative vertical drag offset of the camera between the bottom (-1) and top (1) drag margins.
m.Camera2D.editor_draw_drag_margin: If true, draws the camera's drag margin rectangle in the editor.
m.Camera2D.editor_draw_limits: If true, draws the camera's limits rectangle in the editor.
m.Camera2D.editor_draw_screen: If true, draws the camera's screen rectangle in the editor.
m.Camera2D.enabled: Controls whether the camera can be active or not. If true, the Camera2D will become the main camera when it enters the scene tree and there is no active camera currently (see Viewport.get_camera_2d()).
m.Camera2D.force_update_scroll: Forces the camera to update scroll immediately.
m.Camera2D.get_drag_margin: Returns the specified Side's margin. See also drag_bottom_margin, drag_top_margin, drag_left_margin, and drag_right_margin.
m.Camera2D.get_limit: Returns the camera limit for the specified Side. See also limit_bottom, limit_top, limit_left, and limit_right.
m.Camera2D.get_screen_center_position: Returns the center of the screen from this camera's point of view, in global coordinates.
m.Camera2D.get_screen_rotation: Returns the current screen rotation from this camera's point of view.
m.Camera2D.get_target_position: Returns this camera's target position, in global coordinates.
m.Camera2D.ignore_rotation: If true, the camera's rendered view is not affected by its Node2D.rotation and Node2D.global_rotation.
m.Camera2D.is_current: Returns true if this Camera2D is the active camera (see Viewport.get_camera_2d()).
m.Camera2D.limit_bottom: Bottom scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.
m.Camera2D.limit_enabled: If true, the limits will be enabled. Disabling this will allow the camera to focus anywhere, when the four limit_* properties will not work.
m.Camera2D.limit_left: Left scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.
m.Camera2D.limit_right: Right scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.
m.Camera2D.limit_smoothed: If true, the camera smoothly stops when reaches its limits.
m.Camera2D.limit_top: Top scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.
m.Camera2D.make_current: Forces this Camera2D to become the current active one. enabled must be true.
m.Camera2D.offset: The camera's relative offset. Useful for looking around or camera shake animations. The offsetted camera can go past the limits defined in limit_top, limit_bottom, limit_left and limit_right.
m.Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled: If true, the camera's view smoothly moves towards its target position at position_smoothing_speed.
m.Camera2D.position_smoothing_speed: Speed in pixels per second of the camera's smoothing effect when position_smoothing_enabled is true.
m.Camera2D.reset_smoothing: Sets the camera's position immediately to its current smoothing destination.
m.Camera2D.rotation_smoothing_enabled: If true, the camera's view smoothly rotates, via asymptotic smoothing, to align with its target rotation at rotation_smoothing_speed.
m.Camera2D.rotation_smoothing_speed: The angular, asymptotic speed of the camera's rotation smoothing effect when rotation_smoothing_enabled is true.
m.Camera2D.set_drag_margin: Sets the specified Side's margin. See also drag_bottom_margin, drag_top_margin, drag_left_margin, and drag_right_margin.
m.Camera2D.set_limit: Sets the camera limit for the specified Side. See also limit_bottom, limit_top, limit_left, and limit_right.
m.Camera2D.zoom: The camera's zoom. Higher values are more zoomed in. For example, a zoom of Vector2(2.0, 2.0) will be twice as zoomed in on each axis (the view covers an area four times smaller). In contrast, a zoom of Vector2(0.5, 0.5) will be twice as zoomed out on each axis (the view covers an area four times larger). The X and Y components should generally always be set to the same value, unless you wish to…
m.Camera3D.DOPPLER_TRACKING_IDLE_STEP: Simulate Doppler effect [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect] by tracking positions of objects that are changed in _process. Changes in the relative velocity of this camera compared to those objects affect how audio is perceived (changing the audio's AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale).
m.Camera3D.DOPPLER_TRACKING_PHYSICS_STEP: Simulate Doppler effect [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect] by tracking positions of objects that are changed in _physics_process. Changes in the relative velocity of this camera compared to those objects affect how audio is perceived (changing the audio's AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale).
m.Camera3D.KEEP_HEIGHT: Preserves the vertical aspect ratio; also known as Hor+ scaling. This is usually the best option for projects running in landscape mode, as wider aspect ratios will automatically benefit from a wider horizontal FOV.
m.Camera3D.KEEP_WIDTH: Preserves the horizontal aspect ratio; also known as Vert- scaling. This is usually the best option for projects running in portrait mode, as taller aspect ratios will benefit from a wider vertical FOV.
m.Camera3D.PROJECTION_FRUSTUM: Frustum projection. This mode allows adjusting frustum_offset to create "tilted frustum" effects.
m.Camera3D.PROJECTION_ORTHOGONAL: Orthogonal projection, also known as orthographic projection. Objects remain the same size on the screen no matter how far away they are.
m.Camera3D.PROJECTION_PERSPECTIVE: Perspective projection. Objects on the screen becomes smaller when they are far away.
m.Camera3D.attributes: The CameraAttributes to use for this camera.
m.Camera3D.clear_current: If this is the current camera, remove it from being current. If enable_next is true, request to make the next camera current, if any.
m.Camera3D.compositor: The Compositor to use for this camera.
m.Camera3D.cull_mask: The culling mask that describes which VisualInstance3D.layers are rendered by this camera. By default, all 20 user-visible layers are rendered.
m.Camera3D.current: If true, the ancestor Viewport is currently using this camera.
m.Camera3D.doppler_tracking: If not DOPPLER_TRACKING_DISABLED, this camera will simulate the Doppler effect [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect] for objects changed in particular _process methods.
m.Camera3D.environment: The Environment to use for this camera.
m.Camera3D.far: The distance to the far culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis. Higher values allow the camera to see further away, while decreasing far can improve performance if it results in objects being partially or fully culled.
m.Camera3D.fov: The camera's field of view angle (in degrees). Only applicable in perspective mode. Since keep_aspect locks one axis, fov sets the other axis' field of view angle.
m.Camera3D.frustum_offset: The camera's frustum offset. This can be changed from the default to create "tilted frustum" effects such as Y-shearing [https://zdoom.org/wiki/Y-shearing].
m.Camera3D.get_camera_projection: Returns the projection matrix that this camera uses to render to its associated viewport. The camera must be part of the scene tree to function.
m.Camera3D.get_camera_rid: Returns the camera's RID from the RenderingServer.
m.Camera3D.get_camera_transform: Returns the transform of the camera plus the vertical (v_offset) and horizontal (h_offset) offsets; and any other adjustments made to the position and orientation of the camera by subclassed cameras such as XRCamera3D.
m.Camera3D.get_cull_mask_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the cull_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 20.
m.Camera3D.get_frustum: Returns the camera's frustum planes in world space units as an array of Planes in the following order: near, far, left, top, right, bottom. Not to be confused with frustum_offset.
m.Camera3D.get_pyramid_shape_rid: Returns the RID of a pyramid shape encompassing the camera's view frustum, ignoring the camera's near plane. The tip of the pyramid represents the position of the camera.
m.Camera3D.h_offset: The horizontal (X) offset of the camera viewport.
m.Camera3D.is_position_behind: Returns true if the given position is behind the camera (the blue part of the linked diagram). See this diagram [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-docs/master/img/camera3d_position_frustum.png] for an overview of position query methods.
m.Camera3D.is_position_in_frustum: Returns true if the given position is inside the camera's frustum (the green part of the linked diagram). See this diagram [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-docs/master/img/camera3d_position_frustum.png] for an overview of position query methods.
m.Camera3D.keep_aspect: The axis to lock during fov/size adjustments. Can be either KEEP_WIDTH or KEEP_HEIGHT.
m.Camera3D.make_current: Makes this camera the current camera for the Viewport (see class description). If the camera node is outside the scene tree, it will attempt to become current once it's added.
m.Camera3D.near: The distance to the near culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis. Lower values allow the camera to see objects more up close to its origin, at the cost of lower precision across the entire range. Values lower than the default can lead to increased Z-fighting.
m.Camera3D.project_local_ray_normal: Returns a normal vector from the screen point location directed along the camera. Orthogonal cameras are normalized. Perspective cameras account for perspective, screen width/height, etc.
m.Camera3D.project_position: Returns the 3D point in world space that maps to the given 2D coordinate in the Viewport rectangle on a plane that is the given z_depth distance into the scene away from the camera.
m.Camera3D.project_ray_normal: Returns a normal vector in world space, that is the result of projecting a point on the Viewport rectangle by the inverse camera projection. This is useful for casting rays in the form of (origin, normal) for object intersection or picking.
m.Camera3D.project_ray_origin: Returns a 3D position in world space, that is the result of projecting a point on the Viewport rectangle by the inverse camera projection. This is useful for casting rays in the form of (origin, normal) for object intersection or picking.
m.Camera3D.projection: The camera's projection mode. In PROJECTION_PERSPECTIVE mode, objects' Z distance from the camera's local space scales their perceived size.
m.Camera3D.set_cull_mask_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the cull_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 20.
m.Camera3D.set_frustum: Sets the camera projection to frustum mode (see PROJECTION_FRUSTUM), by specifying a size, an offset, and the z_near and z_far clip planes in world space units. The size parameter represents the size of the near plane, either its width or height depending on the value of keep_aspect. See also frustum_offset.
m.Camera3D.set_orthogonal: Sets the camera projection to orthogonal mode (see PROJECTION_ORTHOGONAL), by specifying a size, and the z_near and z_far clip planes in world space units.
m.Camera3D.set_perspective: Sets the camera projection to perspective mode (see PROJECTION_PERSPECTIVE), by specifying a fov (field of view) angle in degrees, and the z_near and z_far clip planes in world space units.
m.Camera3D.size: The camera's size in meters measured as the diameter of the width or height, depending on keep_aspect. Only applicable in orthogonal and frustum modes.
m.Camera3D.unproject_position: Returns the 2D coordinate in the Viewport rectangle that maps to the given 3D point in world space.
m.Camera3D.v_offset: The vertical (Y) offset of the camera viewport.
m.CameraAttributes.auto_exposure_enabled: If true, enables the tonemapping auto exposure mode of the scene renderer. If true, the renderer will automatically determine the exposure setting to adapt to the scene's illumination and the observed light.
m.CameraAttributes.auto_exposure_scale: The scale of the auto exposure effect. Affects the intensity of auto exposure.
m.CameraAttributes.auto_exposure_speed: The speed of the auto exposure effect. Affects the time needed for the camera to perform auto exposure.
m.CameraAttributes.exposure_multiplier: Multiplier for the exposure amount. A higher value results in a brighter image.
m.CameraAttributes.exposure_sensitivity: Sensitivity of camera sensors, measured in ISO. A higher sensitivity results in a brighter image.
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.auto_exposure_m: The maximum luminance (in EV100) used when calculating auto exposure. When calculating scene average luminance, color values will be clamped to at least this value. This limits the auto-exposure from exposing below a certain brightness, resulting in a cut off point where the scene will remain bright.

The minimum luminance (in EV100) used when calculating auto exposure. When calculating scene average luminance, color values will be clamped to at least this value. This limits the auto-exposure from exposing above a certain brightness, resulting in a cut off point where the scene will remain dark.
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.exposure_apertu: Size of the aperture of the camera, measured in f-stops. An f-stop is a unitless ratio between the focal length of the camera and the diameter of the aperture. A high aperture setting will result in a smaller aperture which leads to a dimmer image and sharper focus. A low aperture results in a wide aperture which lets in more light resulting in a brighter, less-focused image. Default is appropria…
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.exposure_shutte: Time for shutter to open and close, evaluated as 1 / shutter_speed seconds. A higher value will allow less light (leading to a darker image), while a lower value will allow more light (leading to a brighter image).
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.frustum_far: Override value for Camera3D.far. Used internally when calculating depth of field. When attached to a Camera3D as its Camera3D.attributes, it will override the Camera3D.far property.
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.frustum_focal_l: Distance between camera lens and camera aperture, measured in millimeters. Controls field of view and depth of field. A larger focal length will result in a smaller field of view and a narrower depth of field meaning fewer objects will be in focus. A smaller focal length will result in a wider field of view and a larger depth of field meaning more objects will be in focus. When attached to a Came…
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.frustum_focus_d: Distance from camera of object that will be in focus, measured in meters. Internally this will be clamped to be at least 1 millimeter larger than frustum_focal_length.
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.frustum_near: Override value for Camera3D.near. Used internally when calculating depth of field. When attached to a Camera3D as its Camera3D.attributes, it will override the Camera3D.near property.
m.CameraAttributesPhysical.get_fov: Returns the vertical field of view that corresponds to the frustum_focal_length. This value is calculated internally whenever frustum_focal_length is changed.
m.CameraAttributesPractical.auto_exposure_: The maximum sensitivity (in ISO) used when calculating auto exposure. When calculating scene average luminance, color values will be clamped to at least this value. This limits the auto-exposure from exposing below a certain brightness, resulting in a cut off point where the scene will remain bright.

The minimum sensitivity (in ISO) used when calculating auto exposure. When calculating scene average luminance, color values will be clamped to at least this value. This limits the auto-exposure from exposing above a certain brightness, resulting in a cut off point where the scene will remain dark.
m.CameraAttributesPractical.dof_blur_amoun: Sets the maximum amount of blur. When using physically-based blur amounts, will instead act as a multiplier. High values lead to an increased amount of blurriness, but can be much more expensive to calculate. It is best to keep this as low as possible for a given art style.
m.CameraAttributesPractical.dof_blur_far_d: Objects further from the Camera3D by this amount will be blurred by the depth of field effect. Measured in meters.
m.CameraAttributesPractical.dof_blur_far_e: Enables depth of field blur for objects further than dof_blur_far_distance. Strength of blur is controlled by dof_blur_amount and modulated by dof_blur_far_transition.
m.CameraAttributesPractical.dof_blur_far_t: When positive, distance over which (starting from dof_blur_far_distance) blur effect will scale from 0 to dof_blur_amount. When negative, uses physically-based scaling so depth of field effect will scale from 0 at dof_blur_far_distance and will increase in a physically accurate way as objects get further from the Camera3D.
m.CameraAttributesPractical.dof_blur_near_: Objects closer from the Camera3D by this amount will be blurred by the depth of field effect. Measured in meters.
Enables depth of field blur for objects closer than dof_blur_near_distance. Strength of blur is controlled by dof_blur_amount and modulated by dof_blur_near_transition.

When positive, distance over which blur effect will scale from 0 to dof_blur_amount, ending at dof_blur_near_distance. When negative, uses physically-based scaling so depth of field effect will scale from 0 at dof_blur_near_distance and will increase in a physically accurate way as objects get closer to the Camera3D.
m.CameraFeed.FEED_BACK: Camera is mounted at the back of the device.
m.CameraFeed.FEED_FRONT: Camera is mounted at the front of the device.
m.CameraFeed.FEED_NOIMAGE: No image set for the feed.
m.CameraFeed.FEED_YCBCR: Feed supplies YCbCr images that need to be converted to RGB.
m.CameraFeed.FEED_YCBCR_SEP: Feed supplies separate Y and CbCr images that need to be combined and converted to RGB.
m.CameraFeed._activate_feed: Called when the camera feed is activated.
m.CameraFeed._deactivate_feed: Called when the camera feed is deactivated.
m.CameraFeed._get_formats: Override this method to define supported formats of the camera feed.
m.CameraFeed._set_format: Override this method to set the format of the camera feed.
m.CameraFeed.feed_is_active: If true, the feed is active.
m.CameraFeed.feed_transform: The transform applied to the camera's image.
m.CameraFeed.format_changed: Emitted when the format has changed.
m.CameraFeed.formats: Formats supported by the feed. Each entry is a Dictionary describing format parameters.
m.CameraFeed.frame_changed: Emitted when a new frame is available.
m.CameraFeed.get_id: Returns the unique ID for this feed.
m.CameraFeed.get_position: Returns the position of camera on the device.
m.CameraFeed.get_texture_tex_id: Returns the texture backend ID (usable by some external libraries that need a handle to a texture to write data).
m.CameraFeed.set_external: Sets the feed as external feed provided by another library.
m.CameraFeed.set_format: Sets the feed format parameters for the given index in the formats array. Returns true on success. By default, the YUYV encoded stream is transformed to FEED_RGB. The YUYV encoded stream output format can be changed by setting parameters's output entry to one of the following:
m.CameraFeed.set_position: Sets the position of this camera.
m.CameraFeed.set_rgb_image: Sets RGB image for this feed.
m.CameraFeed.set_ycbcr_image: Sets YCbCr image for this feed.
m.CameraFeed.set_ycbcr_images: Sets Y and CbCr images for this feed.
m.CameraServer.add_feed: Adds the camera feed to the camera server.
m.CameraServer.camera_feed_added: Emitted when a CameraFeed is added (e.g. a webcam is plugged in).
m.CameraServer.camera_feed_removed: Emitted when a CameraFeed is removed (e.g. a webcam is unplugged).
m.CameraServer.camera_feeds_updated: Emitted when camera feeds are updated.
m.CameraServer.get_feed: Returns the CameraFeed corresponding to the camera with the given index.
m.CameraServer.get_feed_count: Returns the number of CameraFeeds registered.
m.CameraServer.monitoring_feeds: If true, the server is actively monitoring available camera feeds.
m.CameraTexture.camera_feed_id: The ID of the CameraFeed for which we want to display the image.
m.CameraTexture.camera_is_active: Convenience property that gives access to the active property of the CameraFeed.
m.CameraTexture.which_feed: Which image within the CameraFeed we want access to, important if the camera image is split in a Y and CbCr component.
m.CanvasGroup.clear_margin: Sets the size of the margin used to expand the clearing rect of this CanvasGroup. This expands the area of the backbuffer that will be used by the CanvasGroup. A smaller margin will reduce the area of the backbuffer used which can increase performance, however if use_mipmaps is enabled, a small margin may result in mipmap errors at the edge of the CanvasGroup. Accordingly, this should be left as…
m.CanvasGroup.fit_margin: Sets the size of a margin used to expand the drawable rect of this CanvasGroup. The size of the CanvasGroup is determined by fitting a rect around its children then expanding that rect by fit_margin. This increases both the backbuffer area used and the area covered by the CanvasGroup both of which can reduce performance. This should be kept as small as possible and should only be expanded when an…
m.CanvasGroup.use_mipmaps: If true, calculates mipmaps for the backbuffer before drawing the CanvasGroup so that mipmaps can be used in a custom ShaderMaterial attached to the CanvasGroup. Generating mipmaps has a performance cost so this should not be enabled unless required.
m.CanvasItem.CLIP_CHILDREN_AND_DRAW: This node is used as a mask and is also drawn. The mask is based on this node's alpha channel: Opaque pixels are kept, transparent pixels are discarded, and semi-transparent pixels are blended in according to their opacity. Children are clipped to the parent's drawn area.
m.CanvasItem.CLIP_CHILDREN_DISABLED: Children are drawn over this node and are not clipped.
m.CanvasItem.CLIP_CHILDREN_MAX: Represents the size of the ClipChildrenMode enum.
m.CanvasItem.CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY: This node is used as a mask and is not drawn. The mask is based on this node's alpha channel: Opaque pixels are kept, transparent pixels are discarded, and semi-transparent pixels are blended in according to their opacity. Children are clipped to this node's drawn area.
m.CanvasItem.NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGE: Notification received when this node's global transform changes, if is_transform_notification_enabled() is true. See also set_notify_transform() and get_transform().
m.CanvasItem.OVERSAMPLING_WITH_SCALE_DISAB: The oversampling is not affected by CanvasItem scale, and is equal to the Viewport oversampling.
m.CanvasItem.OVERSAMPLING_WITH_SCALE_ENABL: The oversampling is a product of CanvasItem scale and Viewport oversampling.
m.CanvasItem.OVERSAMPLING_WITH_SCALE_MAX: Represents the size of the OversamplingWithScale enum.
m.CanvasItem.OVERSAMPLING_WITH_SCALE_PAREN: The CanvasItem will inherit the oversampling mode from its parent.
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MI: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance.

The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces t…
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_MAX: Represents the size of the TextureFilter enum.
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel only. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_M: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance.

The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that…
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE: The CanvasItem will inherit the filter from its parent.
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_DISABLED: The texture does not repeat. Sampling the texture outside its extents will result in "stretching" of the edge pixels. You can avoid this by ensuring a 1-pixel fully transparent border on each side of the texture.
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_ENABLED: The texture repeats when exceeding the texture's size.
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_MAX: Represents the size of the TextureRepeat enum.
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_MIRROR: The texture repeats when the exceeding the texture's size in a "2×2 tiled mode". Repeated textures at even positions are mirrored.
m.CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_PARENT_NODE: The CanvasItem will inherit the repeat mode from its parent.
m.CanvasItem._draw: Called when CanvasItem has been requested to redraw (after queue_redraw() is called, either manually or by the engine).
m.CanvasItem.clip_children: The mode in which this node clips its children, acting as a mask.
m.CanvasItem.draw: Emitted when the CanvasItem must redraw, after the related NOTIFICATION_DRAW notification, and before _draw() is called.
m.CanvasItem.draw_animation_slice: Subsequent drawing commands will be ignored unless they fall within the specified animation slice. This is a faster way to implement animations that loop on background rather than redrawing constantly.
m.CanvasItem.draw_arc: Draws an unfilled arc between the given angles with a uniform color and width and optional antialiasing (supported only for positive width). The larger the value of point_count, the smoother the curve. center is defined in local space. For elliptical arcs, see draw_ellipse_arc(). See also draw_circle().
m.CanvasItem.draw_char: Draws a string first character using a custom font. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used. pos is defined in local space.
m.CanvasItem.draw_char_outline: Draws a string first character outline using a custom font. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used. pos is defined in local space.
m.CanvasItem.draw_circle: Draws a circle, with position defined in local space. See also draw_ellipse(), draw_arc(), draw_polyline(), and draw_polygon().
m.CanvasItem.draw_colored_polygon: Draws a colored polygon of any number of points, convex or concave. The points in the points array are defined in local space. Unlike draw_polygon(), a single color must be specified for the whole polygon.
m.CanvasItem.draw_dashed_line: Draws a dashed line from a 2D point to another, with a given color and width. The from and to positions are defined in local space. See also draw_line(), draw_multiline(), and draw_polyline().
m.CanvasItem.draw_ellipse: Draws an ellipse with semi-major axis major and semi-minor axis minor. See also draw_circle(), draw_ellipse_arc(), draw_polyline(), and draw_polygon().
m.CanvasItem.draw_ellipse_arc: Draws an unfilled elliptical arc between the given angles with a uniform color and width and optional antialiasing (supported only for positive width). The larger the value of point_count, the smoother the curve. For circular arcs, see draw_arc(). See also draw_ellipse().
m.CanvasItem.draw_end_animation: After submitting all animations slices via draw_animation_slice(), this function can be used to revert drawing to its default state (all subsequent drawing commands will be visible). If you don't care about this particular use case, usage of this function after submitting the slices is not required.
m.CanvasItem.draw_lcd_texture_rect_region: Draws a textured rectangle region of the font texture with LCD subpixel anti-aliasing at a given position, optionally modulated by a color. The rect is defined in local space.
m.CanvasItem.draw_line: Draws a line from a 2D point to another, with a given color and width. It can be optionally antialiased. The from and to positions are defined in local space. See also draw_dashed_line(), draw_multiline(), and draw_polyline().
m.CanvasItem.draw_mesh: Draws a Mesh in 2D, using the provided texture. See MeshInstance2D for related documentation. The transform is defined in local space.
m.CanvasItem.draw_msdf_texture_rect_region: Draws a textured rectangle region of the multichannel signed distance field texture at a given position, optionally modulated by a color. The rect is defined in local space. See FontFile.multichannel_signed_distance_field for more information and caveats about MSDF font rendering.
m.CanvasItem.draw_multiline: Draws multiple disconnected lines with a uniform width and color. Each line is defined by two consecutive points from points array in local space, i.e. i-th segment consists of points[2 * i], points[2 * i + 1] endpoints. When drawing large amounts of lines, this is faster than using individual draw_line() calls. To draw interconnected lines, use draw_polyline() instead.
m.CanvasItem.draw_multiline_colors: Draws multiple disconnected lines with a uniform width and segment-by-segment coloring. Each segment is defined by two consecutive points from points array in local space and a corresponding color from colors array, i.e. i-th segment consists of points[2 * i], points[2 * i + 1] endpoints and has colors[i] color. When drawing large amounts of lines, this is faster than using individual draw_line()…
m.CanvasItem.draw_multiline_string: Breaks text into lines and draws it using the specified font at the pos in local space (top-left corner). The text will have its color multiplied by modulate. If width is greater than or equal to 0, the text will be clipped if it exceeds the specified width. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
m.CanvasItem.draw_multiline_string_outline: Breaks text to the lines and draws text outline using the specified font at the pos in local space (top-left corner). The text will have its color multiplied by modulate. If width is greater than or equal to 0, the text will be clipped if it exceeds the specified width. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
m.CanvasItem.draw_multimesh: Draws a MultiMesh in 2D with the provided texture. See MultiMeshInstance2D for related documentation.
m.CanvasItem.draw_polygon: Draws a solid polygon of any number of points, convex or concave. Unlike draw_colored_polygon(), each point's color can be changed individually. The points array is defined in local space. See also draw_polyline() and draw_polyline_colors(). If you need more flexibility (such as being able to use bones), use RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_triangle_array() instead.
m.CanvasItem.draw_polyline: Draws interconnected line segments with a uniform color and width and optional antialiasing (supported only for positive width). The points array is defined in local space. When drawing large amounts of lines, this is faster than using individual draw_line() calls. To draw disconnected lines, use draw_multiline() instead. See also draw_polygon().
m.CanvasItem.draw_polyline_colors: Draws interconnected line segments with a uniform width, point-by-point coloring, and optional antialiasing (supported only for positive width). Colors assigned to line points match by index between points and colors, i.e. each line segment is filled with a gradient between the colors of the endpoints. The points array is defined in local space. When drawing large amounts of lines, this is faster…
m.CanvasItem.draw_primitive: Draws a custom primitive. 1 point for a point, 2 points for a line, 3 points for a triangle, and 4 points for a quad. If 0 points or more than 4 points are specified, nothing will be drawn and an error message will be printed. The points array is defined in local space. See also draw_line(), draw_polyline(), draw_polygon(), and draw_rect().
m.CanvasItem.draw_rect: Draws a rectangle. If filled is true, the rectangle will be filled with the color specified. If filled is false, the rectangle will be drawn as a stroke with the color and width specified. The rect is specified in local space. See also draw_texture_rect().
m.CanvasItem.draw_set_transform: Sets a custom local transform for drawing via components. Anything drawn afterwards will be transformed by this.
m.CanvasItem.draw_set_transform_matrix: Sets a custom local transform for drawing via matrix. Anything drawn afterwards will be transformed by this.
m.CanvasItem.draw_string: Draws text using the specified font at the pos in local space (bottom-left corner using the baseline of the font). The text will have its color multiplied by modulate. If width is greater than or equal to 0, the text will be clipped if it exceeds the specified width. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
m.CanvasItem.draw_string_outline: Draws text outline using the specified font at the pos in local space (bottom-left corner using the baseline of the font). The text will have its color multiplied by modulate. If width is greater than or equal to 0, the text will be clipped if it exceeds the specified width. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are…
m.CanvasItem.draw_style_box: Draws a styled rectangle. The rect is defined in local space.
m.CanvasItem.draw_texture: Draws a texture at a given position. The position is defined in local space.
m.CanvasItem.draw_texture_rect: Draws a textured rectangle at a given position, optionally modulated by a color. The rect is defined in local space. If transpose is true, the texture will have its X and Y coordinates swapped. See also draw_rect() and draw_texture_rect_region().
m.CanvasItem.draw_texture_rect_region: Draws a textured rectangle from a texture's region (specified by src_rect) at a given position in local space, optionally modulated by a color. If transpose is true, the texture will have its X and Y coordinates swapped. See also draw_texture_rect().
m.CanvasItem.force_update_transform: Forces the node's transform to update. Fails if the node is not inside the tree. See also get_transform().
m.CanvasItem.get_canvas: Returns the RID of the World2D canvas where this node is registered to, used by the RenderingServer.
m.CanvasItem.get_canvas_item: Returns the internal canvas item RID used by the RenderingServer for this node.
m.CanvasItem.get_canvas_layer_node: Returns the CanvasLayer that contains this node, or null if the node is not in any CanvasLayer.
m.CanvasItem.get_canvas_transform: Returns the transform of this node, converted from its registered canvas's coordinate system to its viewport's coordinate system. See also Node.get_viewport().
m.CanvasItem.get_global_mouse_position: Returns mouse cursor's global position relative to the CanvasLayer that contains this node.
m.CanvasItem.get_global_transform: Returns the global transform matrix of this item, i.e. the combined transform up to the topmost CanvasItem node. The topmost item is a CanvasItem that either has no parent, has non-CanvasItem parent or it has top_level enabled.
m.CanvasItem.get_global_transform_with_can: Returns the transform from the local coordinate system of this CanvasItem to the Viewports coordinate system.
m.CanvasItem.get_instance_shader_parameter: Get the value of a shader parameter as set on this instance.
m.CanvasItem.get_local_mouse_position: Returns the mouse's position in this CanvasItem using the local coordinate system of this CanvasItem.
m.CanvasItem.get_screen_transform: Returns the transform of this CanvasItem in global screen coordinates (i.e. taking window position into account). Mostly useful for editor plugins.
m.CanvasItem.get_transform: Returns the transform matrix of this CanvasItem.
m.CanvasItem.get_viewport_rect: Returns this node's viewport boundaries as a Rect2. See also Node.get_viewport().
m.CanvasItem.get_viewport_transform: Returns the transform of this node, converted from its registered canvas's coordinate system to its viewport embedder's coordinate system. See also Viewport.get_final_transform() and Node.get_viewport().
m.CanvasItem.get_visibility_layer_bit: Returns true if the layer at the given index is set in visibility_layer.
m.CanvasItem.get_world_2d: Returns the World2D this node is registered to.
m.CanvasItem.hidden: Emitted when this node becomes hidden, i.e. it's no longer visible in the tree (see is_visible_in_tree()).
m.CanvasItem.hide: Hide the CanvasItem if it's currently visible. This is equivalent to setting visible to false.
m.CanvasItem.is_local_transform_notificati: Returns true if the node receives NOTIFICATION_LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED whenever its local transform changes. This is enabled with set_notify_local_transform().
m.CanvasItem.is_transform_notification_ena: Returns true if the node receives NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED whenever its global transform changes. This is enabled with set_notify_transform().
m.CanvasItem.is_visible_in_tree: Returns true if the node is present in the SceneTree, its visible property is true and all its ancestors are also visible. If any ancestor is hidden, this node will not be visible in the scene tree, and is therefore not drawn (see _draw()).
m.CanvasItem.item_rect_changed: Emitted when the CanvasItem's boundaries (position or size) change, or when an action took place that may have affected these boundaries (e.g. changing Sprite2D.texture).
m.CanvasItem.light_mask: The rendering layers in which this CanvasItem responds to Light2D nodes.
m.CanvasItem.make_canvas_position_local: Transforms viewport_point from the viewport's coordinates to this node's local coordinates.
m.CanvasItem.make_input_local: Returns a copy of the given event with its coordinates converted from global space to this CanvasItem's local space. If not possible, returns the same InputEvent unchanged.
m.CanvasItem.material: The material applied to this CanvasItem.
m.CanvasItem.modulate: 调制颜色。乘以此颜色影响整个节点及其子节点。
m.CanvasItem.move_to_front: Moves this node below its siblings, usually causing the node to draw on top of its siblings. Does nothing if this node does not have a parent. See also Node.move_child().
m.CanvasItem.oversampling_with_scale: If enabled, oversampling for this CanvasItem is automatically adjusted with scale.
m.CanvasItem.queue_redraw: Queues the CanvasItem to redraw. During idle time, if CanvasItem is visible, NOTIFICATION_DRAW is sent and _draw() is called. This only occurs once per frame, even if this method has been called multiple times.
m.CanvasItem.self_modulate: 自身调制颜色（不影响子节点）。
m.CanvasItem.set_instance_shader_parameter: Set the value of a shader uniform for this instance only (per-instance uniform). See also ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter() to assign a uniform on all instances using the same ShaderMaterial.
m.CanvasItem.set_notify_local_transform: If true, the node will receive NOTIFICATION_LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED whenever its local transform changes.
m.CanvasItem.set_notify_transform: If true, the node will receive NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED whenever its global transform changes.
m.CanvasItem.set_visibility_layer_bit: Set/clear individual bits on the rendering visibility layer. This simplifies editing this CanvasItem's visibility layer.
m.CanvasItem.show: Show the CanvasItem if it's currently hidden. This is equivalent to setting visible to true.
m.CanvasItem.show_behind_parent: If true, this node draws behind its parent.
m.CanvasItem.texture_filter: The filtering mode used to render this CanvasItem's texture(s).
m.CanvasItem.texture_repeat: The repeating mode used to render this CanvasItem's texture(s). It affects what happens when the texture is sampled outside its extents, for example by setting a Sprite2D.region_rect that is larger than the texture or assigning Polygon2D UV points outside the texture.
m.CanvasItem.top_level: If true, this CanvasItem will not inherit its transform from parent CanvasItems. Its draw order will also be changed to make it draw on top of other CanvasItems that do not have top_level set to true. The CanvasItem will effectively act as if it was placed as a child of a bare Node.
m.CanvasItem.use_parent_material: If true, the parent CanvasItem's material is used as this node's material.
m.CanvasItem.visibility_changed: Emitted when the CanvasItem's visibility changes, either because its own visible property changed or because its visibility in the tree changed (see is_visible_in_tree()).
m.CanvasItem.visibility_layer: The rendering layer in which this CanvasItem is rendered by Viewport nodes. A Viewport will render a CanvasItem if it and all its parents share a layer with the Viewport's canvas cull mask.
m.CanvasItem.y_sort_enabled: If true, this and child CanvasItem nodes with a higher Y position are rendered in front of nodes with a lower Y position. If false, this and child CanvasItem nodes are rendered normally in scene tree order.
m.CanvasItem.z_as_relative: If true, this node's final Z index is relative to its parent's Z index.
m.CanvasItem.z_index: The order in which this node is drawn. A node with a higher Z index will display in front of others. Must be between RenderingServer.CANVAS_ITEM_Z_MIN and RenderingServer.CANVAS_ITEM_Z_MAX (inclusive).
m.CanvasItemMaterial.BLEND_MODE_MIX: Mix blending mode. Colors are assumed to be independent of the alpha (opacity) value.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.BLEND_MODE_PREMULT_AL: Mix blending mode. Colors are assumed to be premultiplied by the alpha (opacity) value.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.LIGHT_MODE_LIGHT_ONLY: Render the material as if there were only light.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.LIGHT_MODE_NORMAL: Render the material using both light and non-light sensitive material properties.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.LIGHT_MODE_UNSHADED: Render the material as if there were no light.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.blend_mode: The manner in which a material's rendering is applied to underlying textures.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.light_mode: The manner in which material reacts to lighting.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_h_fram: The number of columns in the spritesheet assigned as Texture2D for a GPUParticles2D or CPUParticles2D.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_loop: If true, the particles animation will loop.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_v_fram: The number of rows in the spritesheet assigned as Texture2D for a GPUParticles2D or CPUParticles2D.
m.CanvasItemMaterial.particles_animation: If true, enable spritesheet-based animation features when assigned to GPUParticles2D and CPUParticles2D nodes. The ParticleProcessMaterial.anim_speed_max or CPUParticles2D.anim_speed_max should also be set to a positive value for the animation to play.
m.CanvasLayer.custom_viewport: The custom Viewport node assigned to the CanvasLayer. If null, uses the default viewport instead.
m.CanvasLayer.follow_viewport_enabled: If enabled, the CanvasLayer maintains its position in world space. If disabled, the CanvasLayer stays in a fixed position on the screen.
m.CanvasLayer.follow_viewport_scale: Scales the layer when using follow_viewport_enabled. Layers moving into the foreground should have increasing scales, while layers moving into the background should have decreasing scales.
m.CanvasLayer.get_canvas: Returns the RID of the canvas used by this layer.
m.CanvasLayer.get_final_transform: Returns the transform from the CanvasLayers coordinate system to the Viewports coordinate system.
m.CanvasLayer.hide: Hides any CanvasItem under this CanvasLayer. This is equivalent to setting visible to false.
m.CanvasLayer.layer: Layer index for draw order. Lower values are drawn behind higher values.
m.CanvasLayer.show: Shows any CanvasItem under this CanvasLayer. This is equivalent to setting visible to true.
