m.CanvasLayer.visibility_changed: Emitted when visibility of the layer is changed. See visible.
m.CanvasLayer.visible: If false, any CanvasItem under this CanvasLayer will be hidden.
m.CanvasTexture.diffuse_texture: The diffuse (color) texture to use. This is the main texture you want to set in most cases.
m.CanvasTexture.normal_texture: The normal map texture to use. Only has a visible effect if Light2Ds are affecting this CanvasTexture.
m.CanvasTexture.specular_color: The multiplier for specular reflection colors. The Light2D's color is also taken into account when determining the reflection color. Only has a visible effect if Light2Ds are affecting this CanvasTexture.
m.CanvasTexture.specular_shininess: The specular exponent for Light2D specular reflections. Higher values result in a more glossy/"wet" look, with reflections becoming more localized and less visible overall. The default value of 1.0 disables specular reflections entirely. Only has a visible effect if Light2Ds are affecting this CanvasTexture.
m.CanvasTexture.specular_texture: The specular map to use for Light2D specular reflections. This should be a grayscale or colored texture, with brighter areas resulting in a higher specular_shininess value. Using a colored specular_texture allows controlling specular shininess on a per-channel basis. Only has a visible effect if Light2Ds are affecting this CanvasTexture.
m.CanvasTexture.texture_filter: The texture filtering mode to use when drawing this CanvasTexture.
m.CanvasTexture.texture_repeat: The texture repeat mode to use when drawing this CanvasTexture.
m.CapsuleMesh.height: Total height of the capsule mesh (including the hemispherical ends).
m.CapsuleMesh.radial_segments: Number of radial segments on the capsule mesh.
m.CapsuleMesh.rings: Number of rings along the height of the capsule.
m.CapsuleShape2D.height: The capsule's full height, including the semicircles.
m.CapsuleShape2D.mid_height: The capsule's height, excluding the semicircles. This is the height of the central rectangular part in the middle of the capsule, and is the distance between the centers of the two semicircles. This is a wrapper for height.
m.CapsuleShape3D.height: The capsule's full height, including the hemispheres.
m.CapsuleShape3D.mid_height: The capsule's height, excluding the hemispheres. This is the height of the central cylindrical part in the middle of the capsule, and is the distance between the centers of the two hemispheres. This is a wrapper for height.
m.CenterContainer.use_top_left: If true, centers children relative to the CenterContainer's top left corner.
m.ChainIK3D.get_end_bone: Returns the end bone index of the bone chain.
m.ChainIK3D.get_end_bone_direction: Returns the tail direction of the end bone of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.ChainIK3D.get_end_bone_length: Returns the end bone tail length of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.ChainIK3D.get_end_bone_name: Returns the end bone name of the bone chain.
m.ChainIK3D.get_joint_bone: Returns the bone index at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.ChainIK3D.get_joint_bone_name: Returns the bone name at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.ChainIK3D.get_joint_count: Returns the joint count of the bone chain's joint list.
m.ChainIK3D.get_root_bone: Returns the root bone index of the bone chain.
m.ChainIK3D.get_root_bone_name: Returns the root bone name of the bone chain.
m.ChainIK3D.is_end_bone_extended: Returns true if the end bone is extended to have a tail.
m.ChainIK3D.set_end_bone: Sets the end bone index of the bone chain.
m.ChainIK3D.set_end_bone_direction: Sets the end bone tail direction of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.ChainIK3D.set_end_bone_length: Sets the end bone tail length of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.ChainIK3D.set_end_bone_name: Sets the end bone name of the bone chain.
m.ChainIK3D.set_extend_end_bone: If enabled is true, the end bone is extended to have a tail.
m.ChainIK3D.set_root_bone: Sets the root bone index of the bone chain.
m.ChainIK3D.set_root_bone_name: Sets the root bone name of the bone chain.
m.CharFXTransform.color: The color the character will be drawn with.
m.CharFXTransform.elapsed_time: The time elapsed since the RichTextLabel was added to the scene tree (in seconds). Time stops when the RichTextLabel is paused (see Node.process_mode). Resets when the text in the RichTextLabel is changed.
m.CharFXTransform.env: Contains the arguments passed in the opening BBCode tag. By default, arguments are strings; if their contents match a type such as bool, int or float, they will be converted automatically. Color codes in the form #rrggbb or #rgb will be converted to an opaque Color. String arguments may not contain spaces, even if they're quoted. If present, quotes will also be present in the final string.
m.CharFXTransform.font: TextServer RID of the font used to render glyph, this value can be used with TextServer.font_* methods to retrieve font information.
m.CharFXTransform.glyph_count: Number of glyphs in the grapheme cluster. This value is set in the first glyph of a cluster.
m.CharFXTransform.glyph_flags: Glyph flags. See GraphemeFlag for more info.
m.CharFXTransform.glyph_index: Glyph index specific to the font. If you want to replace this glyph, use TextServer.font_get_glyph_index() with font to get a new glyph index for a single character.
m.CharFXTransform.offset: The position offset the character will be drawn with (in pixels).
m.CharFXTransform.outline: If true, FX transform is called for outline drawing.
m.CharFXTransform.range: Absolute character range in the string, corresponding to the glyph.
m.CharFXTransform.relative_index: The character offset of the glyph, relative to the current RichTextEffect custom block.
m.CharFXTransform.transform: The current transform of the current glyph. It can be overridden (for example, by driving the position and rotation from a curve). You can also alter the existing value to apply transforms on top of other effects.
m.CharFXTransform.visible: If true, the character will be drawn. If false, the character will be hidden. Characters around hidden characters will reflow to take the space of hidden characters. If this is not desired, set their color to Color(1, 1, 1, 0) instead.
m.CharacterBody2D.MOTION_MODE_FLOATING: Apply when there is no notion of floor or ceiling. All collisions will be reported as on_wall. In this mode, when you slide, the speed will always be constant. This mode is suitable for top-down games.
m.CharacterBody2D.MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED: Apply when notions of walls, ceiling and floor are relevant. In this mode the body motion will react to slopes (acceleration/slowdown). This mode is suitable for sided games like platformers.
m.CharacterBody2D.PLATFORM_ON_LEAVE_ADD_UP: Add the last platform velocity to the velocity when you leave a moving platform, but any downward motion is ignored. It's useful to keep full jump height even when the platform is moving down.
m.CharacterBody2D.PLATFORM_ON_LEAVE_ADD_VE: Add the last platform velocity to the velocity when you leave a moving platform.
m.CharacterBody2D.PLATFORM_ON_LEAVE_DO_NOT: Do nothing when leaving a platform.
m.CharacterBody2D.apply_floor_snap: Allows to manually apply a snap to the floor regardless of the body's velocity. This function does nothing when is_on_floor() returns true.
m.CharacterBody2D.floor_block_on_wall: If true, the body will be able to move on the floor only. This option avoids to be able to walk on walls, it will however allow to slide down along them.
m.CharacterBody2D.floor_constant_speed: If false (by default), the body will move faster on downward slopes and slower on upward slopes.
m.CharacterBody2D.floor_max_angle: Maximum angle (in radians) where a slope is still considered a floor (or a ceiling), rather than a wall, when calling move_and_slide(). The default value equals 45 degrees.
m.CharacterBody2D.floor_snap_length: Sets a snapping distance. When set to a value different from 0.0, the body is kept attached to slopes when calling move_and_slide(). The snapping vector is determined by the given distance along the opposite direction of the up_direction.
m.CharacterBody2D.floor_stop_on_slope: If true, the body will not slide on slopes when calling move_and_slide() when the body is standing still.
m.CharacterBody2D.get_floor_angle: Returns the floor's collision angle at the last collision point according to up_direction, which is Vector2.UP by default. This value is always positive and only valid after calling move_and_slide() and when is_on_floor() returns true.
m.CharacterBody2D.get_floor_normal: Returns the collision normal of the floor at the last collision point. Only valid after calling move_and_slide() and when is_on_floor() returns true.
m.CharacterBody2D.get_last_motion: Returns the last motion applied to the CharacterBody2D during the last call to move_and_slide(). The movement can be split into multiple motions when sliding occurs, and this method return the last one, which is useful to retrieve the current direction of the movement.
m.CharacterBody2D.get_last_slide_collision: Returns a KinematicCollision2D if a collision occurred. The returned value contains information about the latest collision that occurred during the last call to move_and_slide(). Returns null if no collision occurred. See also get_slide_collision().
m.CharacterBody2D.get_platform_velocity: Returns the linear velocity of the platform at the last collision point. Only valid after calling move_and_slide().
m.CharacterBody2D.get_position_delta: Returns the travel (position delta) that occurred during the last call to move_and_slide().
m.CharacterBody2D.get_real_velocity: Returns the current real velocity since the last call to move_and_slide(). For example, when you climb a slope, you will move diagonally even though the velocity is horizontal. This method returns the diagonal movement, as opposed to velocity which returns the requested velocity.
m.CharacterBody2D.get_slide_collision: Returns a KinematicCollision2D, which contains information about a collision that occurred during the last call to move_and_slide(). Since the body can collide several times in a single call to move_and_slide(), you must specify the index of the collision in the range 0 to (get_slide_collision_count() - 1). See also get_last_slide_collision().
m.CharacterBody2D.get_slide_collision_coun: Returns the number of times the body collided and changed direction during the last call to move_and_slide().
m.CharacterBody2D.get_wall_normal: Returns the collision normal of the wall at the last collision point. Only valid after calling move_and_slide() and when is_on_wall() returns true.
m.CharacterBody2D.is_on_ceiling: Returns true if the body collided with the ceiling on the last call of move_and_slide(). Otherwise, returns false. The up_direction and floor_max_angle are used to determine whether a surface is "ceiling" or not.
m.CharacterBody2D.is_on_ceiling_only: Returns true if the body collided only with the ceiling on the last call of move_and_slide(). Otherwise, returns false. The up_direction and floor_max_angle are used to determine whether a surface is "ceiling" or not.
m.CharacterBody2D.is_on_floor: Returns true if the body collided with the floor on the last call of move_and_slide(). Otherwise, returns false. The up_direction and floor_max_angle are used to determine whether a surface is "floor" or not.
m.CharacterBody2D.is_on_floor_only: Returns true if the body collided only with the floor on the last call of move_and_slide(). Otherwise, returns false. The up_direction and floor_max_angle are used to determine whether a surface is "floor" or not.
m.CharacterBody2D.is_on_wall: Returns true if the body collided with a wall on the last call of move_and_slide(). Otherwise, returns false. The up_direction and floor_max_angle are used to determine whether a surface is "wall" or not.
m.CharacterBody2D.is_on_wall_only: Returns true if the body collided only with a wall on the last call of move_and_slide(). Otherwise, returns false. The up_direction and floor_max_angle are used to determine whether a surface is "wall" or not.
m.CharacterBody2D.max_slides: Maximum number of times the body can change direction before it stops when calling move_and_slide(). Must be greater than zero.
m.CharacterBody2D.motion_mode: Sets the motion mode which defines the behavior of move_and_slide().
m.CharacterBody2D.move_and_slide: Moves the body based on velocity. If the body collides with another, it will slide along the other body (by default only on floor) rather than stop immediately. If the other body is a CharacterBody2D or RigidBody2D, it will also be affected by the motion of the other body. You can use this to make moving and rotating platforms, or to make nodes push other nodes.
m.CharacterBody2D.platform_floor_layers: Collision layers that will be included for detecting floor bodies that will act as moving platforms to be followed by the CharacterBody2D. By default, all floor bodies are detected and propagate their velocity.
m.CharacterBody2D.platform_on_leave: Sets the behavior to apply when you leave a moving platform. By default, to be physically accurate, when you leave the last platform velocity is applied.
m.CharacterBody2D.platform_wall_layers: Collision layers that will be included for detecting wall bodies that will act as moving platforms to be followed by the CharacterBody2D. By default, all wall bodies are ignored.
m.CharacterBody2D.safe_margin: Extra margin used for collision recovery when calling move_and_slide().
m.CharacterBody2D.slide_on_ceiling: If true, during a jump against the ceiling, the body will slide, if false it will be stopped and will fall vertically.
m.CharacterBody2D.up_direction: Vector pointing upwards, used to determine what is a wall and what is a floor (or a ceiling) when calling move_and_slide(). Defaults to Vector2.UP. As the vector will be normalized it can't be equal to Vector2.ZERO, if you want all collisions to be reported as walls, consider using MOTION_MODE_FLOATING as motion_mode.
m.CharacterBody2D.velocity: Current velocity vector in pixels per second, used and modified during calls to move_and_slide().
m.CharacterBody2D.wall_min_slide_angle: Minimum angle (in radians) where the body is allowed to slide when it encounters a wall. The default value equals 15 degrees. This property only affects movement when motion_mode is MOTION_MODE_FLOATING.
m.CharacterBody3D.MOTION_MODE_FLOATING: Apply when there is no notion of floor or ceiling. All collisions will be reported as on_wall. In this mode, when you slide, the speed will always be constant. This mode is suitable for games without ground like space games.

m.CharacterBody3D.PLATFORM_ON_LEAVE_DO_NOT: Do nothing when leaving a platform.

m.ClassDB.can_instantiate: Returns true if objects can be instantiated from the specified class, otherwise returns false.
m.ClassDB.class_call_static: Calls a static method on a class.
m.ClassDB.class_exists: Returns whether the specified class is available or not.
m.ClassDB.class_get_api_type: Returns the API type of the specified class.
m.ClassDB.class_get_enum_constants: Returns an array with all the keys in enum of class or its ancestry.
m.ClassDB.class_get_enum_list: Returns an array with all the enums of class or its ancestry.
m.ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant: Returns the value of the integer constant name of class or its ancestry. Always returns 0 when the constant could not be found.
m.ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant_enum: Returns which enum the integer constant name of class or its ancestry belongs to.
m.ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant_list: Returns an array with the names all the integer constants of class or its ancestry.
m.ClassDB.class_get_method_argument_count: Returns the number of arguments of the method method of class or its ancestry if no_inheritance is false.
m.ClassDB.class_get_method_list: Returns an array with all the methods of class or its ancestry if no_inheritance is false. Every element of the array is a Dictionary with the following keys: args, default_args, flags, id, name, return: (class_name, hint, hint_string, name, type, usage).
m.ClassDB.class_get_property: Returns the value of property of object or its ancestry.
m.ClassDB.class_get_property_default_value: Returns the default value of property of class or its ancestor classes.
m.ClassDB.class_get_property_getter: Returns the getter method name of property of class.
m.ClassDB.class_get_property_list: Returns an array with all the properties of class or its ancestry if no_inheritance is false.
m.ClassDB.class_get_property_setter: Returns the setter method name of property of class.
m.ClassDB.class_get_signal: Returns the signal data of class or its ancestry. The returned value is a Dictionary with the following keys: args, default_args, flags, id, name, return: (class_name, hint, hint_string, name, type, usage).
m.ClassDB.class_get_signal_list: Returns an array with all the signals of class or its ancestry if no_inheritance is false. Every element of the array is a Dictionary as described in class_get_signal().
m.ClassDB.class_has_enum: Returns whether class or its ancestry has an enum called name or not.
m.ClassDB.class_has_integer_constant: Returns whether class or its ancestry has an integer constant called name or not.
m.ClassDB.class_has_method: Returns whether class (or its ancestry if no_inheritance is false) has a method called method or not.
m.ClassDB.class_has_signal: Returns whether class or its ancestry has a signal called signal or not.
m.ClassDB.class_set_property: Sets property value of object to value.
m.ClassDB.get_class_list: Returns the names of all engine classes available.
m.ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class: Returns the names of all engine classes that directly or indirectly inherit from class.
m.ClassDB.get_parent_class: Returns the parent class of class.
m.ClassDB.is_class_enabled: Returns whether this class is enabled or not.
m.ClassDB.is_class_enum_bitfield: Returns whether class (or its ancestor classes if no_inheritance is false) has an enum called enum that is a bitfield.
m.ClassDB.is_parent_class: Returns whether inherits is an ancestor of class or not.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_CLASS: Marks the option as a class.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_CONSTANT: Marks the option as a constant.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_ENUM: Marks the option as an enum entry.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_FILE_PATH: Marks the option as a file path.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_FUNCTION: Marks the option as a function.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_KEYWORD: Marks the option as a keyword.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_MEMBER: Marks the option as a member.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_NODE_PATH: Marks the option as a Godot node path.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_PLAIN_TEXT: Marks the option as unclassified or plain text.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_SIGNAL: Marks the option as a Godot signal.
m.CodeEdit.KIND_VARIABLE: Marks the option as a variable.
m.CodeEdit.LOCATION_LOCAL: The option is local to the location of the code completion query - e.g. a local variable. Subsequent value of location represent options from the outer class, the exact value represent how far they are (in terms of inner classes).
m.CodeEdit.LOCATION_OTHER: The option is from other engine code, not covered by the other enum constants - e.g. built-in classes.
m.CodeEdit.LOCATION_OTHER_USER_CODE: The option is from user code which is not local and not in a derived class (e.g. Autoload Singletons).
m.CodeEdit.LOCATION_PARENT_MASK: The option is from the containing class or a parent class, relative to the location of the code completion query. Perform a bitwise OR with the class depth (e.g. 0 for the local class, 1 for the parent, 2 for the grandparent, etc.) to store the depth of an option in the class or a parent class.
m.CodeEdit._confirm_code_completion: Override this method to define how the selected entry should be inserted. If replace is true, any existing text should be replaced.
m.CodeEdit._filter_code_completion_candida: Override this method to define what items in candidates should be displayed.
m.CodeEdit._request_code_completion: Override this method to define what happens when the user requests code completion. If force is true, any checks should be bypassed.
m.CodeEdit.add_code_completion_option: Submits an item to the queue of potential candidates for the autocomplete menu. Call update_code_completion_options() to update the list.
m.CodeEdit.add_comment_delimiter: Adds a comment delimiter from start_key to end_key. Both keys should be symbols, and start_key must not be shared with other delimiters.
m.CodeEdit.add_string_delimiter: Defines a string delimiter from start_key to end_key. Both keys should be symbols, and start_key must not be shared with other delimiters.
m.CodeEdit.auto_brace_completion_enabled: If true, uses auto_brace_completion_pairs to automatically insert the closing brace when the opening brace is inserted by typing or autocompletion. Also automatically removes the closing brace when using backspace on the opening brace.
m.CodeEdit.auto_brace_completion_highlight: If true, highlights brace pairs when the caret is on either one, using auto_brace_completion_pairs. If matching, the pairs will be underlined. If a brace is unmatched, it is colored with brace_mismatch_color.
m.CodeEdit.auto_brace_completion_pairs: Sets the brace pairs to be autocompleted. For each entry in the dictionary, the key is the opening brace and the value is the closing brace that matches it. A brace is a String made of symbols. See auto_brace_completion_enabled and auto_brace_completion_highlight_matching.
m.CodeEdit.breakpoint_toggled: Emitted when a breakpoint is added or removed from a line. If the line is removed via backspace, a signal is emitted at the old line.
m.CodeEdit.can_fold_line: Returns true if the given line is foldable. A line is foldable if it is the start of a valid code region (see get_code_region_start_tag()), if it is the start of a comment or string block, or if the next non-empty line is more indented (see TextEdit.get_indent_level()).
m.CodeEdit.code_completion_enabled: If true, the ProjectSettings.input/ui_text_completion_query action requests code completion. To handle it, see _request_code_completion() or code_completion_requested.
m.CodeEdit.code_completion_prefixes: Sets prefixes that will trigger code completion.
m.CodeEdit.code_completion_requested: Emitted when the user requests code completion. This signal will not be sent if _request_code_completion() is overridden or code_completion_enabled is false.
m.CodeEdit.confirm_code_completion: Inserts the selected entry into the text. If replace is true, any existing text is replaced rather than merged.
m.CodeEdit.convert_indent: Converts the indents of lines between from_line and to_line to tabs or spaces as set by indent_use_spaces.
m.CodeEdit.create_code_region: Creates a new code region with the selection. At least one single line comment delimiter have to be defined (see add_comment_delimiter()).
m.CodeEdit.delete_lines: Deletes all lines that are selected or have a caret on them.
m.CodeEdit.delimiter_comments: Sets the comment delimiters. All existing comment delimiters will be removed.
m.CodeEdit.delimiter_strings: Sets the string delimiters. All existing string delimiters will be removed.
m.CodeEdit.do_indent: If there is no selection, indentation is inserted at the caret. Otherwise, the selected lines are indented like indent_lines(). Equivalent to the ProjectSettings.input/ui_text_indent action. The indentation characters used depend on indent_use_spaces and indent_size.
m.CodeEdit.duplicate_lines: Duplicates all lines currently selected with any caret. Duplicates the entire line beneath the current one no matter where the caret is within the line.
m.CodeEdit.duplicate_selection: Duplicates all selected text and duplicates all lines with a caret on them.
m.CodeEdit.fold_all_lines: Folds all lines that are possible to be folded (see can_fold_line()).
m.CodeEdit.fold_line: Folds the given line, if possible (see can_fold_line()).
m.CodeEdit.get_auto_brace_completion_close: Gets the matching auto brace close key for open_key.
m.CodeEdit.get_code_completion_option: Gets the completion option at index. The return Dictionary has the following key-values:
m.CodeEdit.get_code_completion_options: Gets all completion options, see get_code_completion_option() for return content.
m.CodeEdit.get_code_completion_selected_in: Gets the index of the current selected completion option.
m.CodeEdit.get_code_region_end_tag: Returns the code region end tag (without comment delimiter).
m.CodeEdit.get_code_region_start_tag: Returns the code region start tag (without comment delimiter).
m.CodeEdit.get_delimiter_end_key: Gets the end key for a string or comment region index.
m.CodeEdit.get_delimiter_end_position: If line column is in a string or comment, returns the end position of the region. If not or no end could be found, both Vector2 values will be -1.
m.CodeEdit.get_delimiter_start_key: Gets the start key for a string or comment region index.
m.CodeEdit.get_delimiter_start_position: If line column is in a string or comment, returns the start position of the region. If not or no start could be found, both Vector2 values will be -1.
m.CodeEdit.get_folded_lines: Returns all lines that are currently folded.
m.CodeEdit.get_text_for_code_completion: Returns the full text with char 0xFFFF at the caret location.
m.CodeEdit.get_text_for_symbol_lookup: Returns the full text with char 0xFFFF at the cursor location.
m.CodeEdit.get_text_with_cursor_char: Returns the full text with char 0xFFFF at the specified location.
m.CodeEdit.gutters_draw_bookmarks: If true, bookmarks are drawn in the gutter. This gutter is shared with breakpoints and executing lines. See set_line_as_bookmarked().
m.CodeEdit.gutters_draw_breakpoints_gutter: If true, breakpoints are drawn in the gutter. This gutter is shared with bookmarks and executing lines. Clicking the gutter will toggle the breakpoint for the line, see set_line_as_breakpoint().
m.CodeEdit.gutters_draw_executing_lines: If true, executing lines are marked in the gutter. This gutter is shared with breakpoints and bookmarks. See set_line_as_executing().
m.CodeEdit.gutters_draw_fold_gutter: If true, the fold gutter is drawn. In this gutter, the can_fold_code_region icon is drawn for each foldable line (see can_fold_line()) and the folded_code_region icon is drawn for each folded line (see is_line_folded()). These icons can be clicked to toggle the fold state, see toggle_foldable_line(). line_folding must be true to show icons.
m.CodeEdit.gutters_draw_line_numbers: If true, the line number gutter is drawn. Line numbers start at 1 and are incremented for each line of text. Clicking and dragging in the line number gutter will select entire lines of text.
m.CodeEdit.gutters_line_numbers_min_digits: The minimum width in digits reserved for the line number gutter.
m.CodeEdit.gutters_zero_pad_line_numbers: If true, line numbers drawn in the gutter are zero padded based on the total line count. Requires gutters_draw_line_numbers to be set to true.
m.CodeEdit.has_auto_brace_completion_close: Returns true if close key close_key exists.
m.CodeEdit.has_auto_brace_completion_open_: Returns true if open key open_key exists.
m.CodeEdit.has_comment_delimiter: Returns true if comment start_key exists.
m.CodeEdit.has_string_delimiter: Returns true if string start_key exists.
m.CodeEdit.indent_automatic: If true, an extra indent is automatically inserted when a new line is added and a prefix in indent_automatic_prefixes is found. If a brace pair opening key is found, the matching closing brace will be moved to another new line (see auto_brace_completion_pairs).
m.CodeEdit.indent_automatic_prefixes: Prefixes to trigger an automatic indent. Used when indent_automatic is set to true.
m.CodeEdit.indent_lines: Indents all lines that are selected or have a caret on them. Uses spaces or a tab depending on indent_use_spaces. See unindent_lines().
m.CodeEdit.indent_size: Size of the tabulation indent (one Tab press) in characters. If indent_use_spaces is enabled the number of spaces to use.
m.CodeEdit.indent_use_spaces: Use spaces instead of tabs for indentation.
m.CodeEdit.is_in_comment: Returns delimiter index if line column is in a comment. If column is not provided, will return delimiter index if the entire line is a comment. Otherwise -1.
m.CodeEdit.is_in_string: Returns the delimiter index if line column is in a string. If column is not provided, will return the delimiter index if the entire line is a string. Otherwise -1.
m.CodeEdit.is_line_bookmarked: Returns true if the given line is bookmarked. See set_line_as_bookmarked().
m.CodeEdit.is_line_breakpointed: Returns true if the given line is breakpointed. See set_line_as_breakpoint().
m.CodeEdit.is_line_code_region_end: Returns true if the given line is a code region end. See set_code_region_tags().
m.CodeEdit.is_line_code_region_start: Returns true if the given line is a code region start. See set_code_region_tags().
m.CodeEdit.is_line_executing: Returns true if the given line is marked as executing. See set_line_as_executing().
m.CodeEdit.is_line_folded: Returns true if the given line is folded. See fold_line().
m.CodeEdit.join_lines: Joins all selected lines or lines containing a caret with their next line. Whitespace in between will be removed. If the next line has content, the line_ending will be inserted in between.
m.CodeEdit.line_folding: If true, lines can be folded. Otherwise, line folding methods like fold_line() will not work and can_fold_line() will always return false. See gutters_draw_fold_gutter.
m.CodeEdit.line_length_guidelines: Draws vertical lines at the provided columns. The first entry is considered a main hard guideline and is drawn more prominently.
m.CodeEdit.move_lines_down: Moves all lines down that are selected or have a caret on them.
m.CodeEdit.move_lines_up: Moves all lines up that are selected or have a caret on them.
m.CodeEdit.remove_comment_delimiter: Removes the comment delimiter with start_key.
m.CodeEdit.remove_string_delimiter: Removes the string delimiter with start_key.
m.CodeEdit.request_code_completion: Emits code_completion_requested, if force is true will bypass all checks. Otherwise will check that the caret is in a word or in front of a prefix. Will ignore the request if all current options are of type file path, node path, or signal.
m.CodeEdit.set_code_completion_selected_in: Sets the current selected completion option.
m.CodeEdit.set_code_hint: Sets the code hint text. Pass an empty string to clear.
m.CodeEdit.set_code_hint_draw_below: If true, the code hint will draw below the main caret. If false, the code hint will draw above the main caret. See set_code_hint().
m.CodeEdit.set_code_region_tags: Sets the code region start and end tags (without comment delimiter).
m.CodeEdit.set_line_as_bookmarked: Sets the given line as bookmarked. If true and gutters_draw_bookmarks is true, draws the bookmark icon in the gutter for this line. See get_bookmarked_lines() and is_line_bookmarked().
m.CodeEdit.set_line_as_breakpoint: Sets the given line as a breakpoint. If true and gutters_draw_breakpoints_gutter is true, draws the breakpoint icon in the gutter for this line. See get_breakpointed_lines() and is_line_breakpointed().
m.CodeEdit.set_line_as_executing: Sets the given line as executing. If true and gutters_draw_executing_lines is true, draws the executing_line icon in the gutter for this line. See get_executing_lines() and is_line_executing().
m.CodeEdit.set_symbol_lookup_word_as_valid: Sets the symbol emitted by symbol_validate as a valid lookup.
m.CodeEdit.symbol_hovered: Emitted when the user hovers over a symbol. Unlike Control.mouse_entered, this signal is not emitted immediately, but when the cursor is over the symbol for ProjectSettings.gui/timers/tooltip_delay_sec seconds.
m.CodeEdit.symbol_lookup: Emitted when the user has clicked on a valid symbol.
m.CodeEdit.symbol_lookup_on_click: Set when a validated word from symbol_validate is clicked, the symbol_lookup should be emitted.
m.CodeEdit.symbol_tooltip_on_hover: If true, the symbol_hovered signal is emitted when hovering over a word.
m.CodeEdit.symbol_validate: Emitted when the user hovers over a symbol. The symbol should be validated and responded to, by calling set_symbol_lookup_word_as_valid().
m.CodeEdit.toggle_foldable_line: Toggle the folding of the code block at the given line.
m.CodeEdit.toggle_foldable_lines_at_carets: Toggle the folding of the code block on all lines with a caret on them.
m.CodeEdit.unfold_all_lines: Unfolds all lines that are folded.
m.CodeEdit.unfold_line: Unfolds the given line if it is folded or if it is hidden under a folded line.
m.CodeEdit.unindent_lines: Unindents all lines that are selected or have a caret on them. Uses spaces or a tab depending on indent_use_spaces. Equivalent to the ProjectSettings.input/ui_text_dedent action. See indent_lines().
m.CodeEdit.update_code_completion_options: Submits all completion options added with add_code_completion_option(). Will try to force the autocomplete menu to popup, if force is true.
m.CodeHighlighter.add_color_region: Adds a color region (such as for comments or strings) from start_key to end_key. Both keys should be symbols, and start_key must not be shared with other delimiters.
m.CodeHighlighter.add_keyword_color: Sets the color for a keyword.
m.CodeHighlighter.add_member_keyword_color: Sets the color for a member keyword.
m.CodeHighlighter.color_regions: Sets the color regions. All existing regions will be removed. The Dictionary key is the region start and end key, separated by a space. The value is the region color.
m.CodeHighlighter.function_color: Sets color for functions. A function is a non-keyword string followed by a '('.
m.CodeHighlighter.get_keyword_color: Returns the color for a keyword.
m.CodeHighlighter.get_member_keyword_color: Returns the color for a member keyword.
m.CodeHighlighter.has_color_region: Returns true if the start key exists, else false.
m.CodeHighlighter.has_keyword_color: Returns true if the keyword exists, else false.
m.CodeHighlighter.has_member_keyword_color: Returns true if the member keyword exists, else false.
m.CodeHighlighter.keyword_colors: Sets the keyword colors. All existing keywords will be removed. The Dictionary key is the keyword. The value is the keyword color.
m.CodeHighlighter.member_keyword_colors: Sets the member keyword colors. All existing member keyword will be removed. The Dictionary key is the member keyword. The value is the member keyword color.
m.CodeHighlighter.member_variable_color: Sets color for member variables. A member variable is non-keyword, non-function string proceeded with a '.'.
m.CodeHighlighter.remove_color_region: Removes the color region that uses that start key.
m.CollisionObject2D.DISABLE_MODE_KEEP_ACTI: When Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED, do not affect the physics simulation.
m.CollisionObject2D.DISABLE_MODE_MAKE_STAT: When Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED, make the body static. Doesn't affect Area2D. PhysicsBody2D can't be affected by forces or other bodies while static.
m.CollisionObject2D.DISABLE_MODE_REMOVE: When Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED, remove from the physics simulation to stop all physics interactions with this CollisionObject2D.
m.CollisionObject2D._input_event: Accepts unhandled InputEvents. shape_idx is the child index of the clicked Shape2D. Connect to input_event to easily pick up these events.
m.CollisionObject2D._mouse_enter: Called when the mouse pointer enters any of this object's shapes. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set. Note that moving between different shapes within a single CollisionObject2D won't cause this function to be called.
m.CollisionObject2D._mouse_exit: Called when the mouse pointer exits all this object's shapes. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set. Note that moving between different shapes within a single CollisionObject2D won't cause this function to be called.
m.CollisionObject2D._mouse_shape_enter: Called when the mouse pointer enters any of this object's shapes or moves from one shape to another. shape_idx is the child index of the newly entered Shape2D. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be called.
m.CollisionObject2D._mouse_shape_exit: Called when the mouse pointer exits any of this object's shapes. shape_idx is the child index of the exited Shape2D. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be called.
m.CollisionObject2D.collision_layer: The physics layers this CollisionObject2D is in. Collision objects can exist in one or more of 32 different layers. See also collision_mask.
m.CollisionObject2D.collision_mask: The physics layers this CollisionObject2D scans. Collision objects can scan one or more of 32 different layers. See also collision_layer.
m.CollisionObject2D.collision_priority: The priority used to solve colliding when occurring penetration. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the object will be. This can for example be used to prevent the player from breaking through the boundaries of a level.
m.CollisionObject2D.create_shape_owner: Creates a new shape owner for the given object. Returns owner_id of the new owner for future reference.
m.CollisionObject2D.disable_mode: Defines the behavior in physics when Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED.
m.CollisionObject2D.get_collision_layer_va: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_layer is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject2D.get_collision_mask_val: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject2D.get_shape_owner_one_wa: Returns the one_way_collision_direction of the shape owner identified by the given owner_id.
Returns the one_way_collision_margin of the shape owner identified by given owner_id.
m.CollisionObject2D.get_shape_owners: Returns an Array of owner_id identifiers. You can use these ids in other methods that take owner_id as an argument.
m.CollisionObject2D.input_event: Emitted when an input event occurs. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set. See _input_event() for details.
m.CollisionObject2D.input_pickable: If true, this object is pickable. A pickable object can detect the mouse pointer entering/leaving, and if the mouse is inside it, report input events. Requires at least one collision_layer bit to be set.
m.CollisionObject2D.is_shape_owner_disable: If true, the shape owner and its shapes are disabled.
m.CollisionObject2D.is_shape_owner_one_way: Returns true if collisions for the shape owner originating from this CollisionObject2D will not be reported to collided with CollisionObject2Ds.
m.CollisionObject2D.mouse_entered: Emitted when the mouse pointer enters any of this object's shapes. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set. Note that moving between different shapes within a single CollisionObject2D won't cause this signal to be emitted.
m.CollisionObject2D.mouse_exited: Emitted when the mouse pointer exits all this object's shapes. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set. Note that moving between different shapes within a single CollisionObject2D won't cause this signal to be emitted.
m.CollisionObject2D.mouse_shape_entered: Emitted when the mouse pointer enters any of this object's shapes or moves from one shape to another. shape_idx is the child index of the newly entered Shape2D. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set.
m.CollisionObject2D.mouse_shape_exited: Emitted when the mouse pointer exits any of this object's shapes. shape_idx is the child index of the exited Shape2D. Requires input_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set.
m.CollisionObject2D.set_collision_layer_va: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_layer, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject2D.set_collision_mask_val: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_find_owner: Returns the owner_id of the given shape.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_add_shape: Adds a Shape2D to the shape owner.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_clear_shap: Removes all shapes from the shape owner.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_get_owner: Returns the parent object of the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_get_shape: Returns the Shape2D with the given ID from the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_get_shape_: Returns the number of shapes the given shape owner contains.
Returns the child index of the Shape2D with the given ID from the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_remove_sha: Removes a shape from the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_set_disabl: If true, disables the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_set_one_wa: If enable is true, collisions for the shape owner originating from this CollisionObject2D will not be reported to collided with CollisionObject2Ds.
Sets the one_way_collision_direction of the shape owner identified by the given owner_id to direction.
Sets the one_way_collision_margin of the shape owner identified by given owner_id to margin pixels.
m.CollisionObject2D.shape_owner_set_transf: Sets the Transform2D of the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.DISABLE_MODE_KEEP_ACTI: When Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED, do not affect the physics simulation.
m.CollisionObject3D.DISABLE_MODE_MAKE_STAT: When Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED, make the body static. Doesn't affect Area3D. PhysicsBody3D can't be affected by forces or other bodies while static.
m.CollisionObject3D.DISABLE_MODE_REMOVE: When Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED, remove from the physics simulation to stop all physics interactions with this CollisionObject3D.
m.CollisionObject3D._input_event: Receives unhandled InputEvents. event_position is the location in world space of the mouse pointer on the surface of the shape with index shape_idx and normal is the normal vector of the surface at that point. Connect to the input_event signal to easily pick up these events.
m.CollisionObject3D._mouse_enter: Called when the mouse pointer enters any of this object's shapes. Requires input_ray_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set. Note that moving between different shapes within a single CollisionObject3D won't cause this function to be called.
m.CollisionObject3D._mouse_exit: Called when the mouse pointer exits all this object's shapes. Requires input_ray_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set. Note that moving between different shapes within a single CollisionObject3D won't cause this function to be called.
m.CollisionObject3D.collision_layer: The physics layers this CollisionObject3D is in. Collision objects can exist in one or more of 32 different layers. See also collision_mask.
m.CollisionObject3D.collision_mask: The physics layers this CollisionObject3D scans. Collision objects can scan one or more of 32 different layers. See also collision_layer.
m.CollisionObject3D.collision_priority: The priority used to solve colliding when occurring penetration. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the object will be. This can for example be used to prevent the player from breaking through the boundaries of a level.
m.CollisionObject3D.create_shape_owner: Creates a new shape owner for the given object. Returns owner_id of the new owner for future reference.
m.CollisionObject3D.disable_mode: Defines the behavior in physics when Node.process_mode is set to Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED.
m.CollisionObject3D.get_collision_layer_va: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_layer is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject3D.get_collision_mask_val: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject3D.get_shape_owners: Returns an Array of owner_id identifiers. You can use these ids in other methods that take owner_id as an argument.
m.CollisionObject3D.input_capture_on_drag: If true, the CollisionObject3D will continue to receive input events as the mouse is dragged across its shapes.
m.CollisionObject3D.input_event: Emitted when the object receives an unhandled InputEvent. event_position is the location in world space of the mouse pointer on the surface of the shape with index shape_idx and normal is the normal vector of the surface at that point.
m.CollisionObject3D.input_ray_pickable: If true, this object is pickable. A pickable object can detect the mouse pointer entering/leaving, and if the mouse is inside it, report input events. Requires at least one collision_layer bit to be set.
m.CollisionObject3D.is_shape_owner_disable: If true, the shape owner and its shapes are disabled.
m.CollisionObject3D.mouse_entered: Emitted when the mouse pointer enters any of this object's shapes. Requires input_ray_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set.
m.CollisionObject3D.mouse_exited: Emitted when the mouse pointer exits all this object's shapes. Requires input_ray_pickable to be true and at least one collision_layer bit to be set.
m.CollisionObject3D.set_collision_layer_va: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_layer, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject3D.set_collision_mask_val: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_find_owner: Returns the owner_id of the given shape.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_add_shape: Adds a Shape3D to the shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_clear_shap: Removes all shapes from the shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_get_owner: Returns the parent object of the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_get_shape: Returns the Shape3D with the given ID from the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_get_shape_: Returns the number of shapes the given shape owner contains.
Returns the child index of the Shape3D with the given ID from the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_remove_sha: Removes a shape from the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_set_disabl: If true, disables the given shape owner.
m.CollisionObject3D.shape_owner_set_transf: Sets the Transform3D of the given shape owner.
m.CollisionPolygon2D.BUILD_SEGMENTS: Collisions will only include the polygon edges. In this mode the node has the same effect as a single ConcavePolygonShape2D made of segments, with the restriction that each segment (after the first one) starts where the previous one ends, and the last one ends where the first one starts (forming a closed but hollow polygon).
m.CollisionPolygon2D.BUILD_SOLIDS: Collisions will include the polygon and its contained area. In this mode the node has the same effect as several ConvexPolygonShape2D nodes, one for each convex shape in the convex decomposition of the polygon (but without the overhead of multiple nodes).
m.CollisionPolygon2D.disabled: If true, no collisions will be detected. This property should be changed with Object.set_deferred().
m.CollisionPolygon2D.one_way_collision: If true, only edges that face up, relative to CollisionPolygon2D's rotation, will collide with other objects.
m.CollisionPolygon2D.one_way_collision_dir: The direction used for one-way collision.
m.CollisionPolygon2D.one_way_collision_mar: The margin used for one-way collision (in pixels). Higher values will make the shape thicker, and work better for colliders that enter the polygon at a high velocity.
m.CollisionPolygon2D.polygon: The polygon's list of vertices. Each point will be connected to the next, and the final point will be connected to the first.
m.CollisionPolygon3D.debug_color: The collision shape color that is displayed in the editor, or in the running project if Debug > Visible Collision Shapes is checked at the top of the editor.
m.CollisionPolygon3D.debug_fill: If true, when the shape is displayed, it will show a solid fill color in addition to its wireframe.
m.CollisionPolygon3D.depth: Length that the resulting collision extends in either direction perpendicular to its 2D polygon.
m.CollisionPolygon3D.disabled: If true, no collision will be produced. This property should be changed with Object.set_deferred().
m.CollisionPolygon3D.margin: The collision margin for the generated Shape3D. See Shape3D.margin for more details.
m.CollisionPolygon3D.polygon: Array of vertices which define the 2D polygon in the local XY plane.
m.CollisionShape2D.debug_color: The collision shape color that is displayed in the editor, or in the running project if Debug > Visible Collision Shapes is checked at the top of the editor.
m.CollisionShape2D.disabled: A disabled collision shape has no effect in the world. This property should be changed with Object.set_deferred().
m.CollisionShape2D.one_way_collision: Sets whether this collision shape should only detect collision on one side (top or bottom).
m.CollisionShape2D.one_way_collision_direc: The direction used for one-way collision.
m.CollisionShape2D.one_way_collision_margi: The margin used for one-way collision (in pixels). Higher values will make the shape thicker, and work better for colliders that enter the shape at a high velocity.
m.CollisionShape2D.shape: The actual shape owned by this collision shape.
m.CollisionShape3D.debug_color: The collision shape color that is displayed in the editor, or in the running project if Debug > Visible Collision Shapes is checked at the top of the editor.
m.CollisionShape3D.debug_fill: If true, when the shape is displayed, it will show a solid fill color in addition to its wireframe.
m.CollisionShape3D.disabled: A disabled collision shape has no effect in the world. This property should be changed with Object.set_deferred().
m.CollisionShape3D.make_convex_from_siblin: Sets the collision shape's shape to the addition of all its convexed MeshInstance3D siblings geometry.
m.CollisionShape3D.shape: The actual shape owned by this collision shape.
m.Color.a: 透明度。0.0 完全透明，1.0 不透明。
m.Color.a8: Wrapper for a that uses the range 0 to 255, instead of 0 to 1.
m.Color.b8: Wrapper for b that uses the range 0 to 255, instead of 0 to 1.
m.Color.blend: Returns a new color resulting from overlaying this color over the given color. In a painting program, you can imagine it as the over color painted over this color (including alpha).
m.Color.clamp: Returns a new color with all components clamped between the components of min and max, by running @GlobalScope.clamp() on each component.
m.Color.darkened: Returns a new color resulting from making this color darker by the specified amount (ratio from 0.0 to 1.0). See also lightened().
m.Color.from_hsv: Constructs a color from an HSV profile [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSL_and_HSV]. The hue (h), saturation (s), and value (v) are typically between 0.0 and 1.0.
m.Color.from_ok_hsl: Constructs a color from an OK HSL profile [https://bottosson.github.io/posts/colorpicker/]. The hue (h), saturation (s), and lightness (l) are typically between 0.0 and 1.0.
m.Color.from_rgba8: Returns a Color constructed from red (r8), green (g8), blue (b8), and optionally alpha (a8) integer channels, each divided by 255.0 for their final value.
m.Color.from_rgbe9995: Decodes a Color from an RGBE9995 format integer. See Image.FORMAT_RGBE9995.
m.Color.from_string: Creates a Color from the given string, which can be either an HTML color code or a named color (case-insensitive). Returns default if the color cannot be inferred from the string.
m.Color.g8: Wrapper for g that uses the range 0 to 255, instead of 0 to 1.
m.Color.get_luminance: Returns the light intensity of the color, as a value between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). This is useful when determining light or dark color. Colors with a luminance smaller than 0.5 can be generally considered dark.
m.Color.h: The HSV hue of this color, on the range 0 to 1.
m.Color.hex: Returns the Color associated with the provided hex integer in 32-bit RGBA format (8 bits per channel). This method is the inverse of to_rgba32().
m.Color.hex64: Returns the Color associated with the provided hex integer in 64-bit RGBA format (16 bits per channel). This method is the inverse of to_rgba64().
m.Color.html: Returns a new color from rgba, an HTML hexadecimal color string. rgba is not case-sensitive, and may be prefixed by a hash sign (#).
m.Color.html_is_valid: Returns true if color is a valid HTML hexadecimal color string. The string must be a hexadecimal value (case-insensitive) of either 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits, and may be prefixed by a hash sign (#). This method is identical to String.is_valid_html_color().
m.Color.inverted: Returns the color with its r, g, and b components inverted ((1 - r, 1 - g, 1 - b, a)).
m.Color.is_equal_approx: Returns true if this color and to are approximately equal, by running @GlobalScope.is_equal_approx() on each component.
m.Color.lerp: Returns the linear interpolation between this color's components and to's components. The interpolation factor weight should be between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). See also @GlobalScope.lerp().
m.Color.lightened: Returns a new color resulting from making this color lighter by the specified amount, which should be a ratio from 0.0 to 1.0. See also darkened().
m.Color.linear_to_srgb: Returns a copy of the color that is encoded using the nonlinear sRGB transfer function [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRGB]. This method requires the original color to use linear encoding. See also srgb_to_linear() which performs the opposite operation.
m.Color.ok_hsl_h: The OKHSL hue of this color, on the range 0 to 1.
m.Color.ok_hsl_l: The OKHSL lightness of this color, on the range 0 to 1.
m.Color.ok_hsl_s: The OKHSL saturation of this color, on the range 0 to 1.
m.Color.r8: Wrapper for r that uses the range 0 to 255, instead of 0 to 1.
m.Color.s: The HSV saturation of this color, on the range 0 to 1.
m.Color.srgb_to_linear: Returns a copy of the color that uses linear encoding. This method requires the original color to be encoded using the nonlinear sRGB transfer function [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRGB]. See also linear_to_srgb() which performs the opposite operation.
m.Color.to_abgr32: Returns the color converted to a 32-bit integer in ABGR format (each component is 8 bits). ABGR is the reversed version of the default RGBA format.
m.Color.to_abgr64: Returns the color converted to a 64-bit integer in ABGR format (each component is 16 bits). ABGR is the reversed version of the default RGBA format.
m.Color.to_argb32: Returns the color converted to a 32-bit integer in ARGB format (each component is 8 bits). ARGB is more compatible with DirectX.
m.Color.to_argb64: Returns the color converted to a 64-bit integer in ARGB format (each component is 16 bits). ARGB is more compatible with DirectX.
m.Color.to_html: Returns the color converted to an HTML hexadecimal color String in RGBA format, without the hash (#) prefix.
m.Color.to_rgba32: Returns the color converted to a 32-bit integer in RGBA format (each component is 8 bits). RGBA is Godot's default format. This method is the inverse of hex().
m.Color.to_rgba64: Returns the color converted to a 64-bit integer in RGBA format (each component is 16 bits). RGBA is Godot's default format. This method is the inverse of hex64().
m.Color.v: The HSV value (brightness) of this color, on the range 0 to 1.
m.ColorPalette.colors: A PackedColorArray containing the colors in the palette.
m.ColorPicker.MODE_HSV: Allows editing the color with Hue/Saturation/Value sliders.
m.ColorPicker.MODE_LINEAR: Allows editing the color with Red/Green/Blue sliders in linear color space.
m.ColorPicker.MODE_OKHSL: Allows editing the color with Hue/Saturation/Lightness sliders.
m.ColorPicker.MODE_RAW: Deprecated: This is replaced by MODE_LINEAR.
m.ColorPicker.MODE_RGB: Allows editing the color with Red/Green/Blue sliders in sRGB color space.
m.ColorPicker.SHAPE_HSV_RECTANGLE: HSV Color Model rectangle color space.
m.ColorPicker.SHAPE_HSV_WHEEL: HSV Color Model rectangle color space with a wheel.
m.ColorPicker.SHAPE_NONE: The color space shape and the shape select button are hidden. Can't be selected from the shapes popup.
m.ColorPicker.SHAPE_OKHSL_CIRCLE: HSL OK Color Model circle color space.
m.ColorPicker.SHAPE_OK_HL_RECTANGLE: OKHSL Color Model rectangle with constant saturation.
m.ColorPicker.SHAPE_OK_HS_RECTANGLE: OKHSL Color Model rectangle with constant lightness.
m.ColorPicker.SHAPE_VHS_CIRCLE: HSV Color Model circle color space. Use Saturation as a radius.
m.ColorPicker.add_preset: Adds the given color to a list of color presets. The presets are displayed in the color picker and the user will be able to select them.
m.ColorPicker.add_recent_preset: Adds the given color to a list of color recent presets so that it can be picked later. Recent presets are the colors that were picked recently, a new preset is automatically created and added to recent presets when you pick a new color.
m.ColorPicker.can_add_swatches: If true, it's possible to add presets under Swatches. If false, the button to add presets is disabled.
m.ColorPicker.color_changed: Emitted when the color is changed.
m.ColorPicker.color_modes_visible: If true, the color mode buttons are visible.
m.ColorPicker.deferred_mode: If true, the color will apply only after the user releases the mouse button, otherwise it will apply immediately even in mouse motion event (which can cause performance issues).
m.ColorPicker.edit_alpha: If true, shows an alpha channel slider (opacity).
m.ColorPicker.edit_intensity: If true, shows an intensity slider. The intensity is applied as follows: convert the color to linear encoding, multiply it by 2 ** intensity, and then convert it back to nonlinear sRGB encoding.
m.ColorPicker.erase_preset: Removes the given color from the list of color presets of this color picker.
m.ColorPicker.erase_recent_preset: Removes the given color from the list of color recent presets of this color picker.
m.ColorPicker.get_presets: Returns the list of colors in the presets of the color picker.
m.ColorPicker.get_recent_presets: Returns the list of colors in the recent presets of the color picker.
m.ColorPicker.hex_visible: If true, the hex color code input field is visible.
m.ColorPicker.picker_shape: The shape of the color space view.
m.ColorPicker.preset_added: Emitted when a preset is added.
m.ColorPicker.preset_removed: Emitted when a preset is removed.
m.ColorPicker.presets_visible: If true, the Swatches and Recent Colors presets are visible.
m.ColorPicker.sampler_visible: If true, the color sampler and color preview are visible.
m.ColorPicker.sliders_visible: If true, the color sliders are visible.
m.ColorPickerButton.edit_alpha: If true, the alpha channel in the displayed ColorPicker will be visible.
m.ColorPickerButton.edit_intensity: If true, the intensity slider in the displayed ColorPicker will be visible.
m.ColorPickerButton.get_picker: Returns the ColorPicker that this node toggles.
m.ColorPickerButton.get_popup: Returns the control's PopupPanel which allows you to connect to popup signals. This allows you to handle events when the ColorPicker is shown or hidden.
m.ColorPickerButton.picker_created: Emitted when the ColorPicker is created (the button is pressed for the first time).
m.ColorPickerButton.popup_closed: Emitted when the ColorPicker is closed.
m.ColorRect.color: The fill color of the rectangle.
m.Compositor.compositor_effects: The custom CompositorEffects that are applied during rendering of viewports using this compositor.
m.CompositorEffect.EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_MA: Represents the size of the EffectCallbackType enum.
m.CompositorEffect.EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PO: The callback is called after our opaque rendering pass, but before our sky is rendered.
The callback is called after our sky is rendered, but before our back buffers are created (and if enabled, before subsurface scattering and/or screen space reflections).
The callback is called after our transparent rendering pass, but before any built-in post-processing effects and output to our render target.
m.CompositorEffect.EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PR: The callback is called before our opaque rendering pass, but after depth prepass (if applicable).
The callback is called before our transparent rendering pass, but after our sky is rendered and we've created our back buffers.
m.CompositorEffect._render_callback: Implement this function with your custom rendering code. effect_callback_type should always match the effect callback type you've specified in effect_callback_type. render_data provides access to the rendering state, it is only valid during rendering and should not be stored.
m.CompositorEffect.access_resolved_color: If true and MSAA is enabled, this will trigger a color buffer resolve before the effect is run.
m.CompositorEffect.access_resolved_depth: If true and MSAA is enabled, this will trigger a depth buffer resolve before the effect is run.
m.CompositorEffect.effect_callback_type: The type of effect that is implemented, determines at what stage of rendering the callback is called.
m.CompositorEffect.enabled: If true this rendering effect is applied to any viewport it is added to.
m.CompositorEffect.needs_motion_vectors: If true this triggers motion vectors being calculated during the opaque render state.
m.CompositorEffect.needs_normal_roughness: If true this triggers normal and roughness data to be output during our depth pre-pass, only applicable for the Forward+ renderer.
m.CompositorEffect.needs_separate_specular: If true this triggers specular data being rendered to a separate buffer and combined after effects have been applied, only applicable for the Forward+ renderer.
m.CompressedTexture2D.load: Loads the texture from the specified path.
m.CompressedTexture2D.load_path: The CompressedTexture2D's file path to a .ctex file.
m.CompressedTexture3D.load: Loads the texture from the specified path.
m.CompressedTexture3D.load_path: The CompressedTexture3D's file path to a .ctex3d file.
m.CompressedTextureLayered.load_path: The path the texture should be loaded from.
m.ConcavePolygonShape2D.segments: The array of points that make up the ConcavePolygonShape2D's line segments. The array (of length divisible by two) is naturally divided into pairs (one pair for each segment); each pair consists of the starting point of a segment and the endpoint of a segment.
m.ConcavePolygonShape3D.backface_collision: If set to true, collisions occur on both sides of the concave shape faces. Otherwise they occur only along the face normals.
m.ConcavePolygonShape3D.get_faces: Returns the faces of the trimesh shape as an array of vertices. The array (of length divisible by three) is naturally divided into triples; each triple of vertices defines a triangle.
m.ConcavePolygonShape3D.set_faces: Sets the faces of the trimesh shape from an array of vertices. The faces array should be composed of triples such that each triple of vertices defines a triangle.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.PARAM_BIAS: The speed with which the swing or twist will take place.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.PARAM_MAX: Represents the size of the Param enum.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.PARAM_RELAXATION: Defines, how fast the swing- and twist-speed-difference on both sides gets synced.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.PARAM_SOFTNESS: The ease with which the joint starts to twist. If it's too low, it takes more force to start twisting the joint.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.PARAM_SWING_SPAN: Swing is rotation from side to side, around the axis perpendicular to the twist axis.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.PARAM_TWIST_SPAN: Twist is the rotation around the twist axis, this value defined how far the joint can twist.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.bias: The speed with which the swing or twist will take place.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.get_param: Returns the value of the specified parameter.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.relaxation: Defines, how fast the swing- and twist-speed-difference on both sides gets synced.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.set_param: Sets the value of the specified parameter.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.softness: The ease with which the joint starts to twist. If it's too low, it takes more force to start twisting the joint.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.swing_span: Swing is rotation from side to side, around the axis perpendicular to the twist axis.
m.ConeTwistJoint3D.twist_span: Twist is the rotation around the twist axis, this value defined how far the joint can twist.
m.ConfigFile.clear: Removes the entire contents of the config.
m.ConfigFile.encode_to_text: Obtain the text version of this config file (the same text that would be written to a file).
m.ConfigFile.erase_section: Deletes the specified section along with all the key-value pairs inside. Raises an error if the section does not exist.
m.ConfigFile.erase_section_key: Deletes the specified key in a section. Raises an error if either the section or the key do not exist.
m.ConfigFile.get_section_keys: Returns an array of all defined key identifiers in the specified section. Raises an error and returns an empty array if the section does not exist.
m.ConfigFile.get_sections: Returns an array of all defined section identifiers.
m.ConfigFile.get_value: Returns the current value for the specified section and key. If either the section or the key do not exist, the method returns the fallback default value. If default is not specified or set to null, an error is also raised.
m.ConfigFile.has_section: Returns true if the specified section exists.
m.ConfigFile.has_section_key: Returns true if the specified section-key pair exists.
m.ConfigFile.load: Loads the config file specified as a parameter. The file's contents are parsed and loaded in the ConfigFile object which the method was called on.
m.ConfigFile.load_encrypted: Loads the encrypted config file specified as a parameter, using the provided key to decrypt it. The file's contents are parsed and loaded in the ConfigFile object which the method was called on.
m.ConfigFile.load_encrypted_pass: Loads the encrypted config file specified as a parameter, using the provided password to decrypt it. The file's contents are parsed and loaded in the ConfigFile object which the method was called on.
m.ConfigFile.parse: Parses the passed string as the contents of a config file. The string is parsed and loaded in the ConfigFile object which the method was called on.
m.ConfigFile.save: Saves the contents of the ConfigFile object to the file specified as a parameter. The output file uses an INI-style structure.
m.ConfigFile.save_encrypted: Saves the contents of the ConfigFile object to the AES-256 encrypted file specified as a parameter, using the provided key to encrypt it. The output file uses an INI-style structure.
m.ConfigFile.save_encrypted_pass: Saves the contents of the ConfigFile object to the AES-256 encrypted file specified as a parameter, using the provided password to encrypt it. The output file uses an INI-style structure.
m.ConfigFile.set_value: Assigns a value to the specified key of the specified section. If either the section or the key do not exist, they are created. Passing a null value deletes the specified key if it exists, and deletes the section if it ends up empty once the key has been removed.
m.ConfirmationDialog.cancel_button_text: The text displayed by the cancel button (see get_cancel_button()).
m.Container.NOTIFICATION_PRE_SORT_CHILDREN: Notification just before children are going to be sorted, in case there's something to process beforehand.
m.Container._get_allowed_size_flags_horizo: Implement to return a list of allowed horizontal SizeFlags for child nodes. This doesn't technically prevent the usages of any other size flags, if your implementation requires that. This only limits the options available to the user in the Inspector dock.
m.Container._get_allowed_size_flags_vertic: Implement to return a list of allowed vertical SizeFlags for child nodes. This doesn't technically prevent the usages of any other size flags, if your implementation requires that. This only limits the options available to the user in the Inspector dock.
m.Container.accessibility_region: If true, this container is marked as a region for accessibility. Use Control.accessibility_name to give the region a descriptive name. Screen readers can navigate between regions using landmark navigation.
m.Container.fit_child_in_rect: Fit a child control in a given rect. This is mainly a helper for creating custom container classes.
m.Container.pre_sort_children: Emitted when children are going to be sorted.
m.Container.queue_sort: Queue resort of the contained children. This is called automatically anyway, but can be called upon request.
m.Container.sort_children: Emitted when sorting the children is needed.
m.Control.ANCHOR_BEGIN: Snaps one of the 4 anchor's sides to the origin of the node's Rect, in the top left. Use it with one of the anchor_* member variables, like anchor_left. To change all 4 anchors at once, use set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.ANCHOR_END: Snaps one of the 4 anchor's sides to the end of the node's Rect, in the bottom right. Use it with one of the anchor_* member variables, like anchor_left. To change all 4 anchors at once, use set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.CURSOR_ARROW: Show the system's arrow mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. Use with mouse_default_cursor_shape.
m.Control.CURSOR_BDIAGSIZE: Show the system's window resize mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. The cursor is a double-headed arrow that goes from the bottom left to the top right. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel both horizontally and vertically.
m.Control.CURSOR_BUSY: Show the system's busy mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. Often an arrow with a small hourglass.
m.Control.CURSOR_CAN_DROP: Show the system's drop mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. It can be an open hand. It tells the user they can drop an item they're currently grabbing, like a node in the Scene dock.
m.Control.CURSOR_CROSS: Show the system's cross mouse cursor when the user hovers the node.
m.Control.CURSOR_DRAG: Show the system's drag mouse cursor, often a closed fist or a cross symbol, when the user hovers the node. It tells the user they're currently dragging an item, like a node in the Scene dock.
m.Control.CURSOR_FDIAGSIZE: Show the system's window resize mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. The cursor is a double-headed arrow that goes from the top left to the bottom right, the opposite of CURSOR_BDIAGSIZE. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel both horizontally and vertically.
m.Control.CURSOR_FORBIDDEN: Show the system's forbidden mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. Often a crossed circle.
m.Control.CURSOR_HELP: Show the system's help mouse cursor when the user hovers the node, a question mark.
m.Control.CURSOR_HSIZE: Show the system's horizontal resize mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. A double-headed horizontal arrow. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel horizontally.
m.Control.CURSOR_HSPLIT: Show the system's horizontal split mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. On Windows, it's the same as CURSOR_HSIZE.
m.Control.CURSOR_IBEAM: Show the system's I-beam mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. The I-beam pointer has a shape similar to "I". It tells the user they can highlight or insert text.
m.Control.CURSOR_MOVE: Show the system's move mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. It shows 2 double-headed arrows at a 90 degree angle. It tells the user they can move a UI element freely.
m.Control.CURSOR_POINTING_HAND: Show the system's pointing hand mouse cursor when the user hovers the node.
m.Control.CURSOR_VSIZE: Show the system's vertical resize mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. A double-headed vertical arrow. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel vertically.
m.Control.CURSOR_VSPLIT: Show the system's vertical split mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. On Windows, it's the same as CURSOR_VSIZE.
m.Control.CURSOR_WAIT: Show the system's wait mouse cursor when the user hovers the node. Often an hourglass.
m.Control.FOCUS_ACCESSIBILITY: The node can grab focus only when screen reader is active. Use with focus_mode.
m.Control.FOCUS_ALL: The node can grab focus on mouse click, using the arrows and the Tab keys on the keyboard, or using the D-pad buttons on a gamepad. Use with focus_mode.
m.Control.FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_DISABLED: Prevents the control from getting focused. get_focus_mode_with_override() will return FOCUS_NONE.
m.Control.FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_ENABLED: Allows the control to be focused, depending on the focus_mode. This can be used to ignore the parent's focus_behavior_recursive. get_focus_mode_with_override() will return the focus_mode.
m.Control.FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_INHERITED: Inherits the focus_behavior_recursive from the parent control. If there is no parent control, this is the same as FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_ENABLED.
m.Control.FOCUS_CLICK: The node can only grab focus on mouse clicks. Use with focus_mode.
m.Control.FOCUS_NONE: The node cannot grab focus. Use with focus_mode.
m.Control.GROW_DIRECTION_BEGIN: The control will grow to the left or top to make up if its minimum size is changed to be greater than its current size on the respective axis.
m.Control.GROW_DIRECTION_BOTH: The control will grow in both directions equally to make up if its minimum size is changed to be greater than its current size.
m.Control.GROW_DIRECTION_END: The control will grow to the right or bottom to make up if its minimum size is changed to be greater than its current size on the respective axis.
m.Control.LAYOUT_DIRECTION_APPLICATION_LOC: Automatic layout direction, determined from the current locale. Right-to-left layout direction is automatically used for languages that require it such as Arabic and Hebrew, but only if a valid translation file is loaded for the given language (unless said language is configured as a fallback in ProjectSettings.internationalization/locale/fallback). For all other languages (or if no valid transla…
m.Control.LAYOUT_DIRECTION_INHERITED: Automatic layout direction, determined from the parent control layout direction.
m.Control.LAYOUT_DIRECTION_MAX: Represents the size of the LayoutDirection enum.
m.Control.LAYOUT_DIRECTION_SYSTEM_LOCALE: Automatic layout direction, determined from the system locale. Right-to-left layout direction is automatically used for languages that require it such as Arabic and Hebrew, but only if a valid translation file is loaded for the given language. For all other languages (or if no valid translation file is found by Godot), left-to-right layout direction is used. If using TextServerFallback (ProjectSe…
m.Control.MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_DISABLED: Prevents the control from receiving mouse input. get_mouse_filter_with_override() will return MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE.
m.Control.MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_ENABLED: Allows the control to receive mouse input, depending on the mouse_filter. This can be used to ignore the parent's mouse_behavior_recursive. get_mouse_filter_with_override() will return the mouse_filter.
m.Control.MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_INHERITED: Inherits the mouse_behavior_recursive from the parent control. If there is no parent control, this is the same as MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_ENABLED.
m.Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE: The control will not receive any mouse movement input events nor mouse button input events through _gui_input(). The control will also not receive the mouse_entered nor mouse_exited signals. This will not block other controls from receiving these events or firing the signals. Ignored events will not be handled automatically. If a child has MOUSE_FILTER_PASS and an event was passed to this control…
m.Control.MOUSE_FILTER_PASS: The control will receive mouse movement input events and mouse button input events if clicked on through _gui_input(). The control will also receive the mouse_entered and mouse_exited signals.
m.Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP: The control will receive mouse movement input events and mouse button input events if clicked on through _gui_input(). The control will also receive the mouse_entered and mouse_exited signals. These events are automatically marked as handled, and they will not propagate further to other controls. This also results in blocking signals in other controls.
m.Control.NOTIFICATION_RESIZED: Sent when the node changes size. Use size to get the new size.
m.Control.PRESET_BOTTOM_LEFT: Snap all 4 anchors to the bottom-left of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_BOTTOM_RIGHT: Snap all 4 anchors to the bottom-right of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_BOTTOM_WIDE: Snap all 4 anchors to the bottom edge of the parent control. The left offset becomes relative to the bottom left corner, the bottom offset relative to the bottom edge, and the right offset relative to the bottom right corner of the node's parent. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_CENTER: Snap all 4 anchors to the center of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_CENTER_BOTTOM: Snap all 4 anchors to the center of the bottom edge of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_CENTER_LEFT: Snap all 4 anchors to the center of the left edge of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_CENTER_RIGHT: Snap all 4 anchors to the center of the right edge of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_CENTER_TOP: Snap all 4 anchors to the center of the top edge of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT: Snap all 4 anchors to the respective corners of the parent control. Set all 4 offsets to 0 after you applied this preset and the Control will fit its parent control. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_HCENTER_WIDE: Snap all 4 anchors to a horizontal line that cuts the parent control in half. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_LEFT_WIDE: Snap all 4 anchors to the left edge of the parent control. The left offset becomes relative to the left edge and the top offset relative to the top left corner of the node's parent. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_MODE_KEEP_HEIGHT: The control's height will not change.
m.Control.PRESET_MODE_KEEP_SIZE: The control's size will not change.
m.Control.PRESET_MODE_KEEP_WIDTH: The control's width will not change.
m.Control.PRESET_MODE_MINSIZE: The control will be resized to its minimum size.
m.Control.PRESET_RIGHT_WIDE: Snap all 4 anchors to the right edge of the parent control. The right offset becomes relative to the right edge and the top offset relative to the top right corner of the node's parent. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_TOP_LEFT: Snap all 4 anchors to the top-left of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_TOP_RIGHT: Snap all 4 anchors to the top-right of the parent control's bounds. Use with set_anchors_preset().
