m.Control.PRESET_TOP_WIDE: Snap all 4 anchors to the top edge of the parent control. The left offset becomes relative to the top left corner, the top offset relative to the top edge, and the right offset relative to the top right corner of the node's parent. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.PRESET_VCENTER_WIDE: Snap all 4 anchors to a vertical line that cuts the parent control in half. Use with set_anchors_preset().
m.Control.SIZE_EXPAND: Tells the parent Container to let this node take all the available space on the axis you flag. If multiple neighboring nodes are set to expand, they'll share the space based on their stretch ratio. See size_flags_stretch_ratio. Use with size_flags_horizontal and size_flags_vertical.
m.Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL: Sets the node's size flags to both fill and expand. See SIZE_FILL and SIZE_EXPAND for more information.
m.Control.SIZE_FILL: Tells the parent Container to expand the bounds of this node to fill all the available space without pushing any other node. It is mutually exclusive with shrink size flags. Use with size_flags_horizontal and size_flags_vertical.
m.Control.SIZE_SHRINK_BEGIN: Tells the parent Container to align the node with its start, either the top or the left edge. It is mutually exclusive with SIZE_FILL and other shrink size flags, but can be used with SIZE_EXPAND in some containers. Use with size_flags_horizontal and size_flags_vertical.
m.Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER: Tells the parent Container to center the node in the available space. It is mutually exclusive with SIZE_FILL and other shrink size flags, but can be used with SIZE_EXPAND in some containers. Use with size_flags_horizontal and size_flags_vertical.
m.Control.SIZE_SHRINK_END: Tells the parent Container to align the node with its end, either the bottom or the right edge. It is mutually exclusive with SIZE_FILL and other shrink size flags, but can be used with SIZE_EXPAND in some containers. Use with size_flags_horizontal and size_flags_vertical.
m.Control.TEXT_DIRECTION_AUTO: Automatic text writing direction, determined from the current locale and text content.
m.Control.TEXT_DIRECTION_INHERITED: Text writing direction is the same as layout direction.
m.Control._accessibility_get_contextual_in: Return the description of the keyboard shortcuts and other contextual help for this control.
m.Control._can_drop_data: Godot calls this method to test if data from a control's _get_drag_data() can be dropped at at_position. at_position is local to this control.
m.Control._drop_data: Godot calls this method to pass you the data from a control's _get_drag_data() result. Godot first calls _can_drop_data() to test if data is allowed to drop at at_position where at_position is local to this control.
m.Control._get_accessibility_container_nam: Override this method to return a human-readable description of the position of the child node in the custom container, added to the accessibility_name.
m.Control._get_cursor_shape: Virtual method to be implemented by the user. Returns the cursor shape for the position at_position in the control's local coordinates, which will typically be used while hovering over this control. See get_cursor_shape().
m.Control._get_drag_data: Godot calls this method to get data that can be dragged and dropped onto controls that expect drop data. Returns null if there is no data to drag. Controls that want to receive drop data should implement _can_drop_data() and _drop_data(). at_position is local to this control. Drag may be forced with force_drag().
m.Control._get_maximum_size: Virtual method to be implemented by the user. Returns the maximum size for this control. Alternative to custom_maximum_size for controlling maximum size via code. The actual maximum size will be the max value of these two (in each axis separately).
m.Control._get_minimum_size: Virtual method to be implemented by the user. Returns the minimum size for this control. Alternative to custom_minimum_size for controlling minimum size via code. The actual minimum size will be the max value of these two (in each axis separately).
m.Control._get_tooltip: Virtual method to be implemented by the user. Returns the tooltip text for the position at_position in the control's local coordinates, which will typically appear when the cursor is resting over this control. See get_tooltip().
m.Control._get_tooltip_auto_translate_mode: Return the auto-translation mode at the given at_position. If not implemented, the tooltip_auto_translate_mode property will be used instead.
m.Control._gui_input: Virtual method to be implemented by the user. Override this method to handle and accept inputs on UI elements. See also accept_event().
m.Control._has_point: Virtual method to be implemented by the user. Returns whether the given point is inside this control.
m.Control._make_custom_tooltip: Virtual method to be implemented by the user. Returns a Control node that should be used as a tooltip instead of the default one. for_text is the return value of get_tooltip().
m.Control._structured_text_parser: User defined BiDi algorithm override function.
m.Control.accept_event: Marks an input event as handled. Once you accept an input event, it stops propagating, even to nodes listening to Node._unhandled_input() or Node._unhandled_key_input().
m.Control.accessibility_controls_nodes: The paths to the nodes which are controlled by this node.
m.Control.accessibility_described_by_nodes: The paths to the nodes which are describing this node.
m.Control.accessibility_description: The human-readable node description that is reported to assistive apps.
m.Control.accessibility_drag: Starts drag-and-drop operation without using a mouse.
m.Control.accessibility_drop: Ends drag-and-drop operation without using a mouse.
m.Control.accessibility_flow_to_nodes: The paths to the nodes which this node flows into.
m.Control.accessibility_labeled_by_nodes: The paths to the nodes which label this node.
m.Control.accessibility_live: The mode with which a live region updates. A live region is a Node that is updated as a result of an external event when the user's focus may be elsewhere.
m.Control.accessibility_name: The human-readable node name that is reported to assistive apps.
m.Control.add_theme_color_override: Creates a local override for a theme Color with the specified name. Local overrides always take precedence when fetching theme items for the control. An override can be removed with remove_theme_color_override().
m.Control.add_theme_constant_override: Creates a local override for a theme constant with the specified name. Local overrides always take precedence when fetching theme items for the control. An override can be removed with remove_theme_constant_override().
m.Control.add_theme_font_override: Creates a local override for a theme Font with the specified name. Local overrides always take precedence when fetching theme items for the control. An override can be removed with remove_theme_font_override().
m.Control.add_theme_font_size_override: Creates a local override for a theme font size with the specified name. Local overrides always take precedence when fetching theme items for the control. An override can be removed with remove_theme_font_size_override().
m.Control.add_theme_icon_override: Creates a local override for a theme icon with the specified name. Local overrides always take precedence when fetching theme items for the control. An override can be removed with remove_theme_icon_override().
m.Control.add_theme_stylebox_override: Creates a local override for a theme StyleBox with the specified name. Local overrides always take precedence when fetching theme items for the control. An override can be removed with remove_theme_stylebox_override().
m.Control.anchor_bottom: Anchors the bottom edge of the node to the origin, the center, or the end of its parent control. It changes how the bottom offset updates when the node moves or changes size. You can use one of the Anchor constants for convenience.
m.Control.anchor_left: Anchors the left edge of the node to the origin, the center or the end of its parent control. It changes how the left offset updates when the node moves or changes size. You can use one of the Anchor constants for convenience.
m.Control.anchor_right: Anchors the right edge of the node to the origin, the center or the end of its parent control. It changes how the right offset updates when the node moves or changes size. You can use one of the Anchor constants for convenience.
m.Control.anchor_top: Anchors the top edge of the node to the origin, the center or the end of its parent control. It changes how the top offset updates when the node moves or changes size. You can use one of the Anchor constants for convenience.
m.Control.auto_translate: Deprecated: Use Node.auto_translate_mode and Node.can_auto_translate() instead.
m.Control.begin_bulk_theme_override: Prevents *_theme_*_override methods from emitting NOTIFICATION_THEME_CHANGED until end_bulk_theme_override() is called.
m.Control.clip_contents: Enables whether rendering of CanvasItem based children should be clipped to this control's rectangle. If true, parts of a child which would be visibly outside of this control's rectangle will not be rendered and won't receive input.
m.Control.custom_maximum_size: The maximum size of this Control's bounding rectangle. If set to a value greater than or equal to (0, 0), the node's bounding rectangle will never exceed this size. A value below (0, 0) means there is no maximum size.
m.Control.custom_minimum_size: The minimum size of the node's bounding rectangle. If you set it to a value greater than (0, 0), the node's bounding rectangle will always have at least this size. Note that Control nodes have their internal minimum size returned by get_minimum_size(). It depends on the control's contents, like text, textures, or style boxes. The actual minimum size is the maximum value of this property and the i…
m.Control.end_bulk_theme_override: Ends a bulk theme override update. See begin_bulk_theme_override().
m.Control.find_next_valid_focus: Finds the next (below in the tree) Control that can receive the focus.
m.Control.find_prev_valid_focus: Finds the previous (above in the tree) Control that can receive the focus.
m.Control.find_valid_focus_neighbor: Finds the next Control that can receive the focus on the specified Side.
m.Control.focus_behavior_recursive: Determines which controls can be focused together with focus_mode. See get_focus_mode_with_override(). Since the default behavior is FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_INHERITED, this can be used to prevent all children controls from getting focused.
m.Control.focus_entered: Emitted when the node gains focus.
m.Control.focus_exited: Emitted when the node loses focus.
m.Control.focus_mode: Determines which controls can be focused. Only one control can be focused at a time, and the focused control will receive keyboard, gamepad, and mouse events in _gui_input(). Use get_focus_mode_with_override() to determine if a control can grab focus, since focus_behavior_recursive also affects it. See also grab_focus().
m.Control.focus_neighbor_bottom: Tells Godot which node it should give focus to if the user presses the down arrow on the keyboard or down on a gamepad by default. You can change the key by editing the ProjectSettings.input/ui_down input action. The node must be a Control. If this property is not set, Godot will give focus to the closest Control to the bottom of this one.
m.Control.focus_neighbor_left: Tells Godot which node it should give focus to if the user presses the left arrow on the keyboard or left on a gamepad by default. You can change the key by editing the ProjectSettings.input/ui_left input action. The node must be a Control. If this property is not set, Godot will give focus to the closest Control to the left of this one.
m.Control.focus_neighbor_right: Tells Godot which node it should give focus to if the user presses the right arrow on the keyboard or right on a gamepad by default. You can change the key by editing the ProjectSettings.input/ui_right input action. The node must be a Control. If this property is not set, Godot will give focus to the closest Control to the right of this one.
m.Control.focus_neighbor_top: Tells Godot which node it should give focus to if the user presses the top arrow on the keyboard or top on a gamepad by default. You can change the key by editing the ProjectSettings.input/ui_up input action. The node must be a Control. If this property is not set, Godot will give focus to the closest Control to the top of this one.
m.Control.focus_next: Tells Godot which node it should give focus to if the user presses Tab on a keyboard by default. You can change the key by editing the ProjectSettings.input/ui_focus_next input action.
m.Control.focus_previous: Tells Godot which node it should give focus to if the user presses Shift + Tab on a keyboard by default. You can change the key by editing the ProjectSettings.input/ui_focus_prev input action.
m.Control.force_drag: Forces drag and bypasses _get_drag_data() and set_drag_preview() by passing data and preview. Drag will start even if the mouse is neither over nor pressed on this control.
m.Control.get_anchor: Returns the anchor for the specified Side. A getter method for anchor_bottom, anchor_left, anchor_right and anchor_top.
m.Control.get_begin: Returns offset_left and offset_top. See also position.
m.Control.get_bound_minimum_size: Returns the bound value of get_combined_minimum_size() by get_combined_maximum_size().
m.Control.get_combined_maximum_size: Returns the combined maximum size from custom_maximum_size and get_maximum_size(), as well as the custom_maximum_size of this node's parent if it is a Control node with propagate_maximum_size set to true.
m.Control.get_combined_minimum_size: Returns the combined minimum size from custom_minimum_size and get_minimum_size().
m.Control.get_combined_pivot_offset: Returns the combined value of pivot_offset and pivot_offset_ratio, in pixels. The ratio is multiplied by the control's size.
m.Control.get_cursor_shape: Returns the mouse cursor shape for this control when hovered over at_position in local coordinates. For most controls, this is the same as mouse_default_cursor_shape, but some built-in controls implement more complex logic.
m.Control.get_focus_mode_with_override: Returns the focus_mode, but takes the focus_behavior_recursive into account. If focus_behavior_recursive is set to FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_DISABLED, or it is set to FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_INHERITED and its ancestor is set to FOCUS_BEHAVIOR_DISABLED, then this returns FOCUS_NONE.
m.Control.get_focus_neighbor: Returns the focus neighbor for the specified Side. A getter method for focus_neighbor_bottom, focus_neighbor_left, focus_neighbor_right and focus_neighbor_top.
m.Control.get_global_rect: Returns the position and size of the control relative to the containing canvas. See global_position and size.
m.Control.get_maximum_size: Returns the maximum size for this control. See custom_maximum_size.
m.Control.get_minimum_size: Returns the minimum size for this control. See custom_minimum_size.
m.Control.get_mouse_filter_with_override: Returns the mouse_filter, but takes the mouse_behavior_recursive into account. If mouse_behavior_recursive is set to MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_DISABLED, or it is set to MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_INHERITED and its ancestor is set to MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_DISABLED, then this returns MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE.
m.Control.get_offset: Returns the offset for the specified Side. A getter method for offset_bottom, offset_left, offset_right and offset_top.
m.Control.get_parent_area_size: Returns the width/height occupied in the parent control.
m.Control.get_rect: Returns the position and size of the control in the coordinate system of the containing node. See position, scale and size.
m.Control.get_screen_position: Returns the position of this Control in global screen coordinates (i.e. taking window position into account). Mostly useful for editor plugins.
m.Control.get_theme_color: Returns a Color from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a color item with the specified name and theme_type. If theme_type is omitted the class name of the current control is used as the type, or theme_type_variation if it is defined. If the type is a class name its parent classes are also checked, in order of inheritance. If the type is a variation its base types are checked,…
m.Control.get_theme_constant: Returns a constant from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a constant item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.get_theme_default_base_scale: Returns the default base scale value from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a valid Theme.default_base_scale value.
m.Control.get_theme_default_font: Returns the default font from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a valid Theme.default_font value.
m.Control.get_theme_default_font_size: Returns the default font size value from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a valid Theme.default_font_size value.
m.Control.get_theme_font: Returns a Font from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a font item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.get_theme_font_size: Returns a font size from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a font size item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.get_theme_icon: Returns an icon from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has an icon item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.get_theme_stylebox: Returns a StyleBox from the first matching Theme in the tree if that Theme has a stylebox item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.get_tooltip: Returns the tooltip text for the position at_position in the control's local coordinates, which will typically appear when the cursor is resting over this control. By default, it returns tooltip_text.
m.Control.global_position: The node's global position, relative to the world (usually to the CanvasLayer).
m.Control.grab_click_focus: Creates an InputEventMouseButton that attempts to click the control. If the event is received, the control gains focus.
m.Control.grab_focus: Steal the focus from another control and become the focused control (see focus_mode).
m.Control.grow_horizontal: Controls the direction on the horizontal axis in which the control should grow if its horizontal minimum size is changed to be greater than its current size, as the control always has to be at least the minimum size.
m.Control.grow_vertical: Controls the direction on the vertical axis in which the control should grow if its vertical minimum size is changed to be greater than its current size, as the control always has to be at least the minimum size.
m.Control.gui_input: Emitted when the node receives an InputEvent.
m.Control.has_focus: Returns true if this is the current focused control. See focus_mode.
m.Control.has_theme_color: Returns true if there is a matching Theme in the tree that has a color item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.has_theme_color_override: Returns true if there is a local override for a theme Color with the specified name in this Control node.
m.Control.has_theme_constant: Returns true if there is a matching Theme in the tree that has a constant item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.has_theme_constant_override: Returns true if there is a local override for a theme constant with the specified name in this Control node.
m.Control.has_theme_font: Returns true if there is a matching Theme in the tree that has a font item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.has_theme_font_override: Returns true if there is a local override for a theme Font with the specified name in this Control node.
m.Control.has_theme_font_size: Returns true if there is a matching Theme in the tree that has a font size item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.has_theme_font_size_override: Returns true if there is a local override for a theme font size with the specified name in this Control node.
m.Control.has_theme_icon: Returns true if there is a matching Theme in the tree that has an icon item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.has_theme_icon_override: Returns true if there is a local override for a theme icon with the specified name in this Control node.
m.Control.has_theme_stylebox: Returns true if there is a matching Theme in the tree that has a stylebox item with the specified name and theme_type.
m.Control.has_theme_stylebox_override: Returns true if there is a local override for a theme StyleBox with the specified name in this Control node.
m.Control.is_drag_successful: Returns true if a drag operation is successful. Alternative to Viewport.gui_is_drag_successful().
m.Control.is_layout_rtl: Returns true if the layout is right-to-left. See also layout_direction.
m.Control.layout_direction: Controls layout direction and text writing direction. Right-to-left layouts are necessary for certain languages (e.g. Arabic and Hebrew). See also is_layout_rtl().
m.Control.localize_numeral_system: If true, automatically converts code line numbers, list indices, SpinBox and ProgressBar values from the Western Arabic (0..9) to the numeral systems used in current locale.
m.Control.maximum_size_changed: Emitted when the node's maximum size changes.
m.Control.minimum_size_changed: Emitted when the node's minimum size changes.
m.Control.mouse_behavior_recursive: Determines which controls can receive mouse input together with mouse_filter. See get_mouse_filter_with_override(). Since the default behavior is MOUSE_BEHAVIOR_INHERITED, this can be used to prevent all children controls from receiving mouse input.
m.Control.mouse_default_cursor_shape: The default cursor shape for this control. Useful for Godot plugins and applications or games that use the system's mouse cursors.
m.Control.mouse_entered: Emitted when the mouse cursor enters the control's (or any child control's) visible area, that is not occluded behind other Controls or Windows, provided its mouse_filter lets the event reach it and regardless if it's currently focused or not.
m.Control.mouse_exited: Emitted when the mouse cursor leaves the control's (and all child control's) visible area, that is not occluded behind other Controls or Windows, provided its mouse_filter lets the event reach it and regardless if it's currently focused or not.
m.Control.mouse_force_pass_scroll_events: When enabled, scroll wheel events processed by _gui_input() will be passed to the parent control even if mouse_filter is set to MOUSE_FILTER_STOP.
m.Control.offset_bottom: Distance between the node's bottom edge and its parent control, based on anchor_bottom.
m.Control.offset_left: Distance between the node's left edge and its parent control, based on anchor_left.
m.Control.offset_right: Distance between the node's right edge and its parent control, based on anchor_right.
m.Control.offset_top: Distance between the node's top edge and its parent control, based on anchor_top.
m.Control.offset_transform_enabled: If true, applies all offset transform properties. Otherwise, no offset transform is applied and the properties have no effect.
m.Control.offset_transform_pivot: Pivot used by offset_transform_rotation and offset_transform_scale in absolute units.
m.Control.offset_transform_pivot_ratio: Same as offset_transform_pivot but expressed in units relative to the Control size where Vector2(0, 0) is the top-left corner of this control, and Vector2(1, 1) is its bottom-right corner.
m.Control.offset_transform_position: Position offset in absolute units. The final offset is the combined value of this property and offset_transform_position_ratio.
m.Control.offset_transform_position_ratio: Same as offset_transform_position but expressed in units relative to the Control size where Vector2(0, 0) is the top-left corner of this control, and Vector2(1, 1) is its bottom-right corner.
m.Control.offset_transform_rotation: Rotation offset. The rotation pivot is defined by offset_transform_pivot and offset_transform_pivot_ratio.
m.Control.offset_transform_scale: Scale offset. The scale pivot is defined by offset_transform_pivot and offset_transform_pivot_ratio.
m.Control.offset_transform_visual_only: If true, the offset transforms is only applied visually and does not affect input. In other words, this Control will still receive input events at its original location before the offset transform is applied.
m.Control.pivot_offset: By default, the node's pivot is its top-left corner. When you change its rotation or scale, it will rotate or scale around this pivot.
m.Control.pivot_offset_ratio: Same as pivot_offset, but expressed as uniform vector, where Vector2(0, 0) is the top-left corner of this control, and Vector2(1, 1) is its bottom-right corner. Set this property to Vector2(0.5, 0.5) to pivot around this control's center.
m.Control.position: 控件位置（父容器坐标系）。
m.Control.propagate_maximum_size: If true, this Control's children will use the value returned by get_combined_maximum_size() in their own size calculations.
m.Control.release_focus: Give up the focus. No other control will be able to receive input.
m.Control.remove_theme_color_override: Removes a local override for a theme Color with the specified name previously added by add_theme_color_override() or via the Inspector dock.
m.Control.remove_theme_constant_override: Removes a local override for a theme constant with the specified name previously added by add_theme_constant_override() or via the Inspector dock.
m.Control.remove_theme_font_override: Removes a local override for a theme Font with the specified name previously added by add_theme_font_override() or via the Inspector dock.
m.Control.remove_theme_font_size_override: Removes a local override for a theme font size with the specified name previously added by add_theme_font_size_override() or via the Inspector dock.
m.Control.remove_theme_icon_override: Removes a local override for a theme icon with the specified name previously added by add_theme_icon_override() or via the Inspector dock.
m.Control.remove_theme_stylebox_override: Removes a local override for a theme StyleBox with the specified name previously added by add_theme_stylebox_override() or via the Inspector dock.
m.Control.reset_size: Resets the size to get_combined_minimum_size(). This is equivalent to calling set_size(Vector2()) (or any size below the minimum).
m.Control.resized: Emitted when the control changes size.
m.Control.rotation: The node's rotation around its pivot, in radians. See pivot_offset to change the pivot's position.
m.Control.rotation_degrees: Helper property to access rotation in degrees instead of radians.
m.Control.scale: The node's scale, relative to its size. Change this property to scale the node around its pivot_offset. The Control's tooltip will also scale according to this value.
m.Control.set_anchor: Sets the anchor for the specified Side to anchor. A setter method for anchor_bottom, anchor_left, anchor_right and anchor_top.
m.Control.set_anchor_and_offset: Works the same as set_anchor(), but instead of keep_offset argument and automatic update of offset, it allows to set the offset yourself (see set_offset()).
m.Control.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset: Sets both anchor preset and offset preset. See set_anchors_preset() and set_offsets_preset().
m.Control.set_anchors_preset: Sets the anchors to a preset from LayoutPreset enum. This is the code equivalent to using the Layout menu in the 2D editor.
m.Control.set_begin: Sets offset_left and offset_top at the same time. Equivalent of changing position.
m.Control.set_drag_forwarding: Sets the given callables to be used instead of the control's own drag-and-drop virtual methods. If a callable is empty, its respective virtual method is used as normal.
m.Control.set_drag_preview: Shows the given control at the mouse pointer. A good time to call this method is in _get_drag_data(). The control must not be in the scene tree. You should not free the control, and you should not keep a reference to the control beyond the duration of the drag. It will be deleted automatically after the drag has ended.
m.Control.set_end: Sets offset_right and offset_bottom at the same time.
m.Control.set_focus_neighbor: Sets the focus neighbor for the specified Side to the Control at neighbor node path. A setter method for focus_neighbor_bottom, focus_neighbor_left, focus_neighbor_right and focus_neighbor_top.
m.Control.set_global_position: Sets the global_position to given position.
m.Control.set_offset: Sets the offset for the specified Side to offset. A setter method for offset_bottom, offset_left, offset_right and offset_top.
m.Control.set_offsets_preset: Sets the offsets to a preset from LayoutPreset enum. This is the code equivalent to using the Layout menu in the 2D editor.
m.Control.set_position: Sets the position to given position.
m.Control.shortcut_context: The Node which must be a parent of the focused Control for the shortcut to be activated. If null, the shortcut can be activated when any control is focused (a global shortcut). This allows shortcuts to be accepted only when the user has a certain area of the GUI focused.
m.Control.size_flags_changed: Emitted when one of the size flags changes. See size_flags_horizontal and size_flags_vertical.
m.Control.size_flags_horizontal: Tells the parent Container nodes how they should resize and place the node on the X axis. Use a combination of the SizeFlags constants to change the flags. See the constants to learn what each does.
m.Control.size_flags_stretch_ratio: If the node and at least one of its neighbors uses the SIZE_EXPAND size flag, the parent Container will let it take more or less space depending on this property. If this node has a stretch ratio of 2 and its neighbor a ratio of 1, this node will take two thirds of the available space.
m.Control.size_flags_vertical: Tells the parent Container nodes how they should resize and place the node on the Y axis. Use a combination of the SizeFlags constants to change the flags. See the constants to learn what each does.
m.Control.theme: The Theme resource this node and all its Control and Window children use. If a child node has its own Theme resource set, theme items are merged with child's definitions having higher priority.
m.Control.theme_changed: Emitted when the NOTIFICATION_THEME_CHANGED notification is sent.
m.Control.theme_type_variation: The name of a theme type variation used by this Control to look up its own theme items. When empty, the class name of the node is used (e.g. Button for the Button control), as well as the class names of all parent classes (in order of inheritance).
m.Control.tooltip_auto_translate_mode: Defines if tooltip text should automatically change to its translated version depending on the current locale. Uses the same auto translate mode as this control when set to Node.AUTO_TRANSLATE_MODE_INHERIT.
m.Control.tooltip_text: The default tooltip text. The tooltip appears when the user's mouse cursor stays idle over this control for a few moments, provided that the mouse_filter property is not MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE. The time required for the tooltip to appear can be changed with the ProjectSettings.gui/timers/tooltip_delay_sec setting.
m.Control.translation_context: The translation context used when translating this control's displayed text, if it has any. Also used when generating translation templates.
m.Control.update_maximum_size: Invalidates the maximum size cache in this node and in parent nodes up to top level. Intended to be used with get_maximum_size() when the return value is changed. Setting custom_maximum_size directly calls this method automatically.
m.Control.update_minimum_size: Invalidates the minimum size cache in this node and in parent nodes up to top level. Intended to be used with get_minimum_size() when the return value is changed. Setting custom_minimum_size directly calls this method automatically.
m.Control.warp_mouse: Moves the mouse cursor to position, relative to position of this Control.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.TRANSFORM_MOD: Convert with position. Transfer the difference.
Convert with rotation. The angle is the roll for the specified axis.
Convert with scale. Transfers the ratio, not the difference.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.get_apply_axi: Returns the axis of the remapping destination transform.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.get_apply_ran: Returns the maximum value of the remapping destination range.
Returns the minimum value of the remapping destination range.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.get_apply_tra: Returns the operation of the remapping destination transform.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.get_reference: Returns the axis of the remapping source transform.
Returns the maximum value of the remapping source range.
Returns the minimum value of the remapping source range.
Returns the operation of the remapping source transform.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.is_additive: Returns true if the additive option is enabled in the setting at index.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.is_relative: Returns true if the relative option is enabled in the setting at index.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.set_additive: Sets additive option in the setting at index to enabled. This mainly affects the process of applying transform to the BoneConstraint3D.set_apply_bone().
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.set_apply_axi: Sets the axis of the remapping destination transform.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.set_apply_ran: Sets the maximum value of the remapping destination range.
Sets the minimum value of the remapping destination range.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.set_apply_tra: Sets the operation of the remapping destination transform.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.set_reference: Sets the axis of the remapping source transform.
Sets the maximum value of the remapping source range.
Sets the minimum value of the remapping source range.
Sets the operation of the remapping source transform.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.set_relative: Sets relative option in the setting at index to enabled.
m.ConvertTransformModifier3D.setting_count: The number of settings in the modifier.
m.ConvexPolygonShape2D.points: The polygon's list of vertices that form a convex hull. Can be in either clockwise or counterclockwise order.
m.ConvexPolygonShape2D.set_point_cloud: Based on the set of points provided, this assigns the points property using the convex hull algorithm, removing all unneeded points. See Geometry2D.convex_hull() for details.
m.ConvexPolygonShape3D.points: The list of 3D points forming the convex polygon shape.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.get_axis_flags: Returns the axis flags of the setting at index.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.get_copy_flags: Returns the copy flags of the setting at index.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.get_invert_flags: Returns the invert flags of the setting at index.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_additive: Returns true if the additive option is enabled in the setting at index.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_axis_x_enable: Returns true if the enable flags has the flag for the X-axis in the setting at index. See also set_axis_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_axis_x_invert: Returns true if the invert flags has the flag for the X-axis in the setting at index. See also set_invert_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_axis_y_enable: Returns true if the enable flags has the flag for the Y-axis in the setting at index. See also set_axis_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_axis_y_invert: Returns true if the invert flags has the flag for the Y-axis in the setting at index. See also set_invert_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_axis_z_enable: Returns true if the enable flags has the flag for the Z-axis in the setting at index. See also set_axis_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_axis_z_invert: Returns true if the invert flags has the flag for the Z-axis in the setting at index. See also set_invert_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_position_copy: Returns true if the copy flags has the flag for the position in the setting at index. See also set_copy_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_relative: Returns true if the relative option is enabled in the setting at index.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_rotation_copy: Returns true if the copy flags has the flag for the rotation in the setting at index. See also set_copy_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.is_scale_copying: Returns true if the copy flags has the flag for the scale in the setting at index. See also set_copy_flags().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_additive: Sets additive option in the setting at index to enabled. This mainly affects the process of applying transform to the BoneConstraint3D.set_apply_bone().
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_axis_flags: Sets the flags to copy axes. If the flag is valid, the axis is copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_axis_x_enabl: If sets enabled to true, the X-axis will be copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_axis_x_inver: If sets enabled to true, the X-axis will be inverted.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_axis_y_enabl: If sets enabled to true, the Y-axis will be copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_axis_y_inver: If sets enabled to true, the Y-axis will be inverted.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_axis_z_enabl: If sets enabled to true, the Z-axis will be copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_axis_z_inver: If sets enabled to true, the Z-axis will be inverted.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_copy_flags: Sets the flags to process the transform operations. If the flag is valid, the transform operation is processed.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_copy_positio: If sets enabled to true, the position will be copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_copy_rotatio: If sets enabled to true, the rotation will be copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_copy_scale: If sets enabled to true, the scale will be copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_invert_flags: Sets the flags to inverte axes. If the flag is valid, the axis is copied.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.set_relative: Sets relative option in the setting at index to enabled.
m.CopyTransformModifier3D.setting_count: The number of settings in the modifier.
m.Crypto.constant_time_compare: Compares two PackedByteArrays for equality without leaking timing information in order to prevent timing attacks.
m.Crypto.decrypt: Decrypt the given ciphertext with the provided private key.
m.Crypto.encrypt: Encrypt the given plaintext with the provided public key.
m.Crypto.generate_random_bytes: Generates a PackedByteArray of cryptographically secure random bytes with given size.
m.Crypto.generate_rsa: Generates an RSA CryptoKey that can be used for creating self-signed certificates and passed to StreamPeerTLS.accept_stream().
m.Crypto.generate_self_signed_certificate: Generates a self-signed X509Certificate from the given CryptoKey and issuer_name. The certificate validity will be defined by not_before and not_after (first valid date and last valid date). The issuer_name must contain at least "CN=" (common name, i.e. the domain name), "O=" (organization, i.e. your company name), "C=" (country, i.e. 2 lettered ISO-3166 code of the country the organization is ba…
m.Crypto.hmac_digest: Generates an HMAC [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMAC] digest of msg using key. The hash_type parameter is the hashing algorithm that is used for the inner and outer hashes.
m.Crypto.sign: Sign a given hash of type hash_type with the provided private key.
m.Crypto.verify: Verify that a given signature for hash of type hash_type against the provided public key.
m.CryptoKey.is_public_only: Returns true if this CryptoKey only has the public part, and not the private one.
m.CryptoKey.load: Loads a key from path. If public_only is true, only the public key will be loaded.
m.CryptoKey.load_from_string: Loads a key from the given string_key. If public_only is true, only the public key will be loaded.
m.CryptoKey.save: Saves a key to the given path. If public_only is true, only the public key will be saved.
m.CryptoKey.save_to_string: Returns a string containing the key in PEM format. If public_only is true, only the public key will be included.
m.Cubemap.create_placeholder: Creates a placeholder version of this resource (PlaceholderCubemap).
m.CubemapArray.create_placeholder: Creates a placeholder version of this resource (PlaceholderCubemapArray).
m.Curve.TANGENT_FREE: The tangent on this side of the point is user-defined.
m.Curve.TANGENT_LINEAR: The curve calculates the tangent on this side of the point as the slope halfway towards the adjacent point.
m.Curve.TANGENT_MODE_COUNT: The total number of available tangent modes.
m.Curve.Vector2: The position of the point at index.
m.Curve.add_point: Adds a point to the curve. For each side, if the *_mode is TANGENT_LINEAR, the *_tangent angle (in degrees) uses the slope of the curve halfway to the adjacent point. Allows custom assignments to the *_tangent angle if *_mode is set to TANGENT_FREE.
m.Curve.bake: Recomputes the baked cache of points for the curve.
m.Curve.bake_resolution: The number of points to include in the baked (i.e. cached) curve data.
m.Curve.clean_dupes: Removes duplicate points, i.e. points that are less than 0.00001 units (engine epsilon value) away from their neighbor on the curve.
m.Curve.clear_points: Removes all points from the curve.
m.Curve.domain_changed: Emitted when max_domain or min_domain is changed.
m.Curve.get_domain_range: Returns the difference between min_domain and max_domain.
m.Curve.get_point_left_mode: Returns the left TangentMode for the point at index.
m.Curve.get_point_left_tangent: Returns the left tangent angle (in degrees) for the point at index.
m.Curve.get_point_position: Returns the curve coordinates for the point at index.
m.Curve.get_point_right_mode: Returns the right TangentMode for the point at index.
m.Curve.get_point_right_tangent: Returns the right tangent angle (in degrees) for the point at index.
m.Curve.get_value_range: Returns the difference between min_value and max_value.
m.Curve.max_domain: The maximum domain (x-coordinate) that points can have.
m.Curve.max_value: The maximum value (y-coordinate) that points can have. Tangents can cause higher values between points.
m.Curve.min_domain: The minimum domain (x-coordinate) that points can have.
m.Curve.min_value: The minimum value (y-coordinate) that points can have. Tangents can cause lower values between points.
m.Curve.point_count: The number of points describing the curve.
m.Curve.range_changed: Emitted when max_value or min_value is changed.
m.Curve.remove_point: Removes the point at index from the curve.
m.Curve.sample: Returns the Y value for the point that would exist at the X position offset along the curve.
m.Curve.sample_baked: Returns the Y value for the point that would exist at the X position offset along the curve using the baked cache. Bakes the curve's points if not already baked.
m.Curve.set_point_left_mode: Sets the left TangentMode for the point at index to mode.
m.Curve.set_point_left_tangent: Sets the left tangent angle for the point at index to tangent.
m.Curve.set_point_offset: Assigns the horizontal position offset to the point at index.
m.Curve.set_point_right_mode: Sets the right TangentMode for the point at index to mode.
m.Curve.set_point_right_tangent: Sets the right tangent angle for the point at index to tangent.
m.Curve.set_point_value: Assigns the vertical position y to the point at index.
m.Curve2D.Vector2: The position of the control point leading to the vertex at index.
m.Curve2D.add_point: Adds a point with the specified position relative to the curve's own position, with control points in and out. Appends the new point at the end of the point list.
m.Curve2D.bake_interval: The distance in pixels between two adjacent cached points. Changing it forces the cache to be recomputed the next time the get_baked_points() or get_baked_length() function is called. The smaller the distance, the more points in the cache and the more memory it will consume, so use with care.
m.Curve2D.clear_points: Removes all points from the curve.
m.Curve2D.get_baked_length: Returns the total length of the curve, based on the cached points. Given enough density (see bake_interval), it should be approximate enough.
m.Curve2D.get_baked_points: Returns the cache of points as a PackedVector2Array.
m.Curve2D.get_closest_offset: Returns the closest offset to to_point. This offset is meant to be used in sample_baked().
m.Curve2D.get_closest_point: Returns the closest point on baked segments (in curve's local space) to to_point.
m.Curve2D.get_point_in: Returns the position of the control point leading to the vertex idx. The returned position is relative to the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console, and returns (0, 0).
m.Curve2D.get_point_out: Returns the position of the control point leading out of the vertex idx. The returned position is relative to the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console, and returns (0, 0).
m.Curve2D.get_point_position: Returns the position of the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console, and returns (0, 0).
m.Curve2D.point_count: The number of points describing the curve.
m.Curve2D.remove_point: Deletes the point idx from the curve. Sends an error to the console if idx is out of bounds.
m.Curve2D.sample: Returns the position between the vertex idx and the vertex idx + 1, where t controls if the point is the first vertex (t = 0.0), the last vertex (t = 1.0), or in between. Values of t outside the range (0.0 <= t <= 1.0) give strange, but predictable results.
m.Curve2D.sample_baked: Returns a point within the curve at position offset, where offset is measured as a pixel distance along the curve.
m.Curve2D.sample_baked_with_rotation: Similar to sample_baked(), but returns Transform2D that includes a rotation along the curve, with Transform2D.origin as the point position and the Transform2D.x vector pointing in the direction of the path at that point. Returns an empty transform if the length of the curve is 0.
m.Curve2D.samplef: Returns the position at the vertex fofs. It calls sample() using the integer part of fofs as idx, and its fractional part as t.
m.Curve2D.set_point_in: Sets the position of the control point leading to the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console. The position is relative to the vertex.
m.Curve2D.set_point_out: Sets the position of the control point leading out of the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console. The position is relative to the vertex.
m.Curve2D.set_point_position: Sets the position for the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console.
m.Curve2D.tessellate: Returns a list of points along the curve, with a curvature controlled point density. That is, the curvier parts will have more points than the straighter parts.
m.Curve2D.tessellate_even_length: Returns a list of points along the curve, with almost uniform density. max_stages controls how many subdivisions a curve segment may face before it is considered approximate enough. Each subdivision splits the segment in half, so the default 5 stages may mean up to 32 subdivisions per curve segment. Increase with care!
m.Curve3D.Vector3: The position of the control point leading to the vertex at index.
m.Curve3D.add_point: Adds a point with the specified position relative to the curve's own position, with control points in and out. Appends the new point at the end of the point list.
m.Curve3D.bake_interval: The distance in meters between two adjacent cached points. Changing it forces the cache to be recomputed the next time the get_baked_points() or get_baked_length() function is called. The smaller the distance, the more points in the cache and the more memory it will consume, so use with care.
m.Curve3D.clear_points: Removes all points from the curve.
m.Curve3D.closed: If true, and the curve has more than 2 control points, the last point and the first one will be connected in a loop.
m.Curve3D.get_baked_length: Returns the total length of the curve, based on the cached points. Given enough density (see bake_interval), it should be approximate enough.
m.Curve3D.get_baked_points: Returns the cache of points as a PackedVector3Array.
m.Curve3D.get_baked_tilts: Returns the cache of tilts as a PackedFloat32Array.
m.Curve3D.get_baked_up_vectors: Returns the cache of up vectors as a PackedVector3Array.
m.Curve3D.get_closest_offset: Returns the closest offset to to_point. This offset is meant to be used in sample_baked() or sample_baked_up_vector().
m.Curve3D.get_closest_point: Returns the closest point on baked segments (in curve's local space) to to_point.
m.Curve3D.get_point_in: Returns the position of the control point leading to the vertex idx. The returned position is relative to the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console, and returns (0, 0, 0).
m.Curve3D.get_point_out: Returns the position of the control point leading out of the vertex idx. The returned position is relative to the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console, and returns (0, 0, 0).
m.Curve3D.get_point_position: Returns the position of the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console, and returns (0, 0, 0).
m.Curve3D.get_point_tilt: Returns the tilt angle in radians for the point idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console, and returns 0.
m.Curve3D.point_count: The number of points describing the curve.
m.Curve3D.remove_point: Deletes the point idx from the curve. Sends an error to the console if idx is out of bounds.
m.Curve3D.sample: Returns the position between the vertex idx and the vertex idx + 1, where t controls if the point is the first vertex (t = 0.0), the last vertex (t = 1.0), or in between. Values of t outside the range (0.0 >= t <=1) give strange, but predictable results.
m.Curve3D.sample_baked: Returns a point within the curve at position offset, where offset is measured as a distance in 3D units along the curve. To do that, it finds the two cached points where the offset lies between, then interpolates the values. This interpolation is cubic if cubic is set to true, or linear if set to false.
m.Curve3D.sample_baked_up_vector: Returns an up vector within the curve at position offset, where offset is measured as a distance in 3D units along the curve. To do that, it finds the two cached up vectors where the offset lies between, then interpolates the values. If apply_tilt is true, an interpolated tilt is applied to the interpolated up vector.
m.Curve3D.sample_baked_with_rotation: Returns a Transform3D with origin as point position, basis.x as sideway vector, basis.y as up vector, basis.z as forward vector. When the curve length is 0, there is no reasonable way to calculate the rotation, all vectors aligned with global space axes. See also sample_baked().
m.Curve3D.samplef: Returns the position at the vertex fofs. It calls sample() using the integer part of fofs as idx, and its fractional part as t.
m.Curve3D.set_point_in: Sets the position of the control point leading to the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console. The position is relative to the vertex.
m.Curve3D.set_point_out: Sets the position of the control point leading out of the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console. The position is relative to the vertex.
m.Curve3D.set_point_position: Sets the position for the vertex idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console.
m.Curve3D.set_point_tilt: Sets the tilt angle in radians for the point idx. If the index is out of bounds, the function sends an error to the console.
m.Curve3D.tessellate: Returns a list of points along the curve, with a curvature controlled point density. That is, the curvier parts will have more points than the straighter parts.
m.Curve3D.tessellate_even_length: Returns a list of points along the curve, with almost uniform density. max_stages controls how many subdivisions a curve segment may face before it is considered approximate enough. Each subdivision splits the segment in half, so the default 5 stages may mean up to 32 subdivisions per curve segment. Increase with care!
m.Curve3D.up_vector_enabled: If true, the curve will bake up vectors used for orientation. This is used when PathFollow3D.rotation_mode is set to PathFollow3D.ROTATION_ORIENTED. Changing it forces the cache to be recomputed.
m.CurveTexture.TEXTURE_MODE_RED: Store the curve only in the red channel. This saves video memory, but some custom shaders may not be able to work with this.
m.CurveTexture.TEXTURE_MODE_RGB: Store the curve equally across the red, green and blue channels. This uses more video memory, but is more compatible with shaders that only read the green and blue values.
m.CurveTexture.curve: The Curve that is rendered onto the texture. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CurveTexture.texture_mode: The format the texture should be generated with. When passing a CurveTexture as an input to a Shader, this may need to be adjusted.
m.CurveTexture.width: The width of the texture (in pixels). Higher values make it possible to represent high-frequency data better (such as sudden direction changes), at the cost of increased generation time and memory usage.
m.CurveXYZTexture.curve_x: The Curve that is rendered onto the texture's red channel. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CurveXYZTexture.curve_y: The Curve that is rendered onto the texture's green channel. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CurveXYZTexture.curve_z: The Curve that is rendered onto the texture's blue channel. Should be a unit Curve.
m.CurveXYZTexture.width: The width of the texture (in pixels). Higher values make it possible to represent high-frequency data better (such as sudden direction changes), at the cost of increased generation time and memory usage.
m.CylinderMesh.bottom_radius: Bottom radius of the cylinder. If set to 0.0, the bottom faces will not be generated, resulting in a conic shape. See also cap_bottom.
m.CylinderMesh.cap_bottom: If true, generates a cap at the bottom of the cylinder. This can be set to false to speed up generation and rendering when the cap is never seen by the camera. See also bottom_radius.
m.CylinderMesh.cap_top: If true, generates a cap at the top of the cylinder. This can be set to false to speed up generation and rendering when the cap is never seen by the camera. See also top_radius.
m.CylinderMesh.radial_segments: Number of radial segments on the cylinder. Higher values result in a more detailed cylinder/cone at the cost of performance.
m.CylinderMesh.rings: Number of edge rings along the height of the cylinder. Changing rings does not have any visual impact unless a shader or procedural mesh tool is used to alter the vertex data. Higher values result in more subdivisions, which can be used to create smoother-looking effects with shaders or procedural mesh tools (at the cost of performance). When not altering the vertex data using a shader or procedu…
m.CylinderMesh.top_radius: Top radius of the cylinder. If set to 0.0, the top faces will not be generated, resulting in a conic shape. See also cap_top.
m.DPITexture.base_scale: Texture scale. 1.0 is the original SVG size. Higher values result in a larger image.
m.DPITexture.color_map: If set, remaps texture colors according to Color-Color map.
m.DPITexture.create_from_string: Creates a new DPITexture and initializes it by allocating and setting the SVG data to source.
m.DPITexture.fix_alpha_border: If true, puts pixels of the same surrounding color in transition from transparent to opaque areas. For textures displayed with bilinear filtering, this helps to reduce the outline effect when exporting images from an image editor.
m.DPITexture.get_scaled_rid: Returns the RID of the texture rasterized to match the oversampling of the currently drawn canvas item.
m.DPITexture.get_source: Returns this SVG texture's source code.
m.DPITexture.premult_alpha: An alternative to fixing darkened borders with fix_alpha_border is to use premultiplied alpha. By enabling this option, the texture will be converted to this format. A premultiplied alpha texture requires specific materials to be displayed correctly:
m.DPITexture.set_size_override: Resizes the texture to the specified dimensions.
m.DPITexture.set_source: Sets this SVG texture's source code.
m.DTLSServer.setup: Setup the DTLS server to use the given server_options. See TLSOptions.server().
m.DTLSServer.take_connection: Try to initiate the DTLS handshake with the given udp_peer which must be already connected (see PacketPeerUDP.connect_to_host()).
m.DampedSpringJoint2D.damping: The spring joint's damping ratio. A value between 0 and 1. When the two bodies move into different directions the system tries to align them to the spring axis again. A high damping value forces the attached bodies to align faster.
m.DampedSpringJoint2D.length: The spring joint's maximum length. The two attached bodies cannot stretch it past this value.
m.DampedSpringJoint2D.rest_length: When the bodies attached to the spring joint move they stretch or squash it. The joint always tries to resize towards this length.
m.DampedSpringJoint2D.stiffness: The higher the value, the less the bodies attached to the joint will deform it. The joint applies an opposing force to the bodies, the product of the stiffness multiplied by the size difference from its resting length.
m.Decal.albedo_mix: Blends the albedo Color of the decal with albedo Color of the underlying mesh. This can be set to 0.0 to create a decal that only affects normal or ORM. In this case, an albedo texture is still required as its alpha channel will determine where the normal and ORM will be overridden. See also modulate.
m.Decal.cull_mask: Specifies which VisualInstance3D.layers this decal will project on. By default, Decals affect all layers. This is used so you can specify which types of objects receive the Decal and which do not. This is especially useful so you can ensure that dynamic objects don't accidentally receive a Decal intended for the terrain under them.
m.Decal.distance_fade_begin: The distance from the camera at which the Decal begins to fade away (in 3D units).
m.Decal.distance_fade_enabled: If true, decals will smoothly fade away when far from the active Camera3D starting at distance_fade_begin. The Decal will fade out over distance_fade_begin + distance_fade_length, after which it will be culled and not sent to the shader at all. Use this to reduce the number of active Decals in a scene and thus improve performance.
m.Decal.distance_fade_length: The distance over which the Decal fades (in 3D units). The Decal becomes slowly more transparent over this distance and is completely invisible at the end. Higher values result in a smoother fade-out transition, which is more suited when the camera moves fast.
m.Decal.emission_energy: Energy multiplier for the emission texture. This will make the decal emit light at a higher or lower intensity, independently of the albedo color. See also modulate.
m.Decal.get_texture: Returns the Texture2D associated with the specified DecalTexture. This is a convenience method, in most cases you should access the texture directly.
m.Decal.lower_fade: Sets the curve over which the decal will fade as the surface gets further from the center of the AABB. Only positive values are valid (negative values will be clamped to 0.0). See also upper_fade.
m.Decal.modulate: Changes the Color of the Decal by multiplying the albedo and emission colors with this value. The alpha component is only taken into account when multiplying the albedo color, not the emission color. See also emission_energy and albedo_mix to change the emission and albedo intensity independently of each other.
m.Decal.normal_fade: Fades the Decal if the angle between the Decal's AABB and the target surface becomes too large. A value of 0 projects the Decal regardless of angle, a value of 1 limits the Decal to surfaces that are nearly perpendicular.
m.Decal.set_texture: Sets the Texture2D associated with the specified DecalTexture. This is a convenience method, in most cases you should access the texture directly.
m.Decal.size: Sets the size of the AABB used by the decal. All dimensions must be set to a value greater than zero (they will be clamped to 0.001 if this is not the case). The AABB goes from -size/2 to size/2.
m.Decal.texture_albedo: Texture2D with the base Color of the Decal. Either this or the texture_emission must be set for the Decal to be visible. Use the alpha channel like a mask to smoothly blend the edges of the decal with the underlying object.
m.Decal.texture_emission: Texture2D with the emission Color of the Decal. Either this or the texture_albedo must be set for the Decal to be visible. Use the alpha channel like a mask to smoothly blend the edges of the decal with the underlying object.
m.Decal.texture_normal: Texture2D with the per-pixel normal map for the decal. Use this to add extra detail to decals.
m.Decal.texture_orm: Texture2D storing ambient occlusion, roughness, and metallic for the decal. Use this to add extra detail to decals.
m.Decal.upper_fade: Sets the curve over which the decal will fade as the surface gets further from the center of the AABB. Only positive values are valid (negative values will be clamped to 0.0). See also lower_fade.
m.Dictionary.assign: Assigns elements of another dictionary into the dictionary. Resizes the dictionary to match dictionary. Performs type conversions if the dictionary is typed.
m.Dictionary.clear: Clears the dictionary, removing all entries from it.
m.Dictionary.duplicate: Returns a new copy of the dictionary.
m.Dictionary.duplicate_deep: Duplicates this dictionary, deeply, like duplicate() when passing true, with extra control over how subresources are handled.
m.Dictionary.erase: Removes the dictionary entry by key, if it exists. Returns true if the given key existed in the dictionary, otherwise false.
m.Dictionary.find_key: Finds and returns the first key whose associated value is equal to value, or null if it is not found.
m.Dictionary.get: Returns the corresponding value for the given key in the dictionary. If the key does not exist, returns default, or null if the parameter is omitted.
m.Dictionary.get_or_add: Gets a value and ensures the key is set. If the key exists in the dictionary, this behaves like get(). Otherwise, the default value is inserted into the dictionary and returned.
m.Dictionary.get_typed_key_builtin: Returns the built-in Variant type of the typed dictionary's keys as a Variant.Type constant. If the keys are not typed, returns @GlobalScope.TYPE_NIL. See also is_typed_key().
m.Dictionary.get_typed_key_class_name: Returns the built-in class name of the typed dictionary's keys, if the built-in Variant type is @GlobalScope.TYPE_OBJECT. Otherwise, returns an empty StringName. See also is_typed_key() and Object.get_class().
m.Dictionary.get_typed_key_script: Returns the Script instance associated with this typed dictionary's keys, or null if it does not exist. See also is_typed_key().
m.Dictionary.get_typed_value_builtin: Returns the built-in Variant type of the typed dictionary's values as a Variant.Type constant. If the values are not typed, returns @GlobalScope.TYPE_NIL. See also is_typed_value().
m.Dictionary.get_typed_value_class_name: Returns the built-in class name of the typed dictionary's values, if the built-in Variant type is @GlobalScope.TYPE_OBJECT. Otherwise, returns an empty StringName. See also is_typed_value() and Object.get_class().
m.Dictionary.get_typed_value_script: Returns the Script instance associated with this typed dictionary's values, or null if it does not exist. See also is_typed_value().
m.Dictionary.has_all: Returns true if the dictionary contains all keys in the given keys array.
m.Dictionary.hash: Returns a hashed 32-bit integer value representing the dictionary contents.
m.Dictionary.is_empty: Returns true if the dictionary is empty (its size is 0). See also size().
m.Dictionary.is_read_only: Returns true if the dictionary is read-only. See make_read_only(). Dictionaries are automatically read-only if declared with const keyword.
m.Dictionary.is_same_typed: Returns true if the dictionary is typed the same as dictionary.
m.Dictionary.is_same_typed_key: Returns true if the dictionary's keys are typed the same as dictionary's keys.
m.Dictionary.is_same_typed_value: Returns true if the dictionary's values are typed the same as dictionary's values.
m.Dictionary.is_typed: Returns true if the dictionary is typed. Typed dictionaries can only store keys/values of their associated type and provide type safety for the [] operator. Methods of typed dictionary still return Variant.
m.Dictionary.is_typed_key: Returns true if the dictionary's keys are typed.
m.Dictionary.is_typed_value: Returns true if the dictionary's values are typed.
m.Dictionary.make_read_only: Makes the dictionary read-only, i.e. disables modification of the dictionary's contents. Does not apply to nested content, e.g. content of nested dictionaries.
m.Dictionary.merge: Adds entries from dictionary to this dictionary. By default, duplicate keys are not copied over, unless overwrite is true.
m.Dictionary.merged: Returns a copy of this dictionary merged with the other dictionary. By default, duplicate keys are not copied over, unless overwrite is true. See also merge().
m.Dictionary.recursive_equal: Returns true if the two dictionaries contain the same keys and values, inner Dictionary and Array keys and values are compared recursively.
m.Dictionary.set: Sets the value of the element at the given key to the given value. Returns true if the value is set successfully. Fails and returns false if the dictionary is read-only, or if key and value don't match the dictionary's types. This is the same as using the [] operator (dict[key] = value).
m.Dictionary.size: Returns the number of entries in the dictionary. Empty dictionaries ({ }) always return 0. See also is_empty().
m.Dictionary.sort: Sorts the dictionary in ascending order, by key. The final order is dependent on the "less than" (<) comparison between keys.
m.DirAccess.change_dir: Changes the currently opened directory to the one passed as an argument. The argument can be relative to the current directory (e.g. newdir or ../newdir), or an absolute path (e.g. /tmp/newdir or res://somedir/newdir).
m.DirAccess.copy: Copies the from file to the to destination. Both arguments should be paths to files, either relative or absolute. If the destination file exists and is not access-protected, it will be overwritten.
m.DirAccess.copy_absolute: Static version of copy(). Supports only absolute paths.
m.DirAccess.create_link: Creates symbolic link between files or folders.
m.DirAccess.create_temp: Creates a temporary directory. This directory will be freed when the returned DirAccess is freed.
m.DirAccess.current_is_dir: Returns whether the current item processed with the last get_next() call is a directory (. and .. are considered directories).
m.DirAccess.dir_exists: Returns whether the target directory exists. The argument can be relative to the current directory, or an absolute path.
m.DirAccess.dir_exists_absolute: Static version of dir_exists(). Supports only absolute paths.
m.DirAccess.file_exists: Returns whether the target file exists. The argument can be relative to the current directory, or an absolute path.
m.DirAccess.get_current_dir: Returns the absolute path to the currently opened directory (e.g. res://folder or C:\tmp\folder).
m.DirAccess.get_current_drive: Returns the currently opened directory's drive index. See get_drive_name() to convert returned index to the name of the drive.
m.DirAccess.get_directories: Returns a PackedStringArray containing filenames of the directory contents, excluding files. The array is sorted alphabetically.
m.DirAccess.get_directories_at: Returns a PackedStringArray containing filenames of the directory contents, excluding files, at the given path. The array is sorted alphabetically.
m.DirAccess.get_drive_count: On Windows, returns the number of drives (partitions) mounted on the current filesystem.
m.DirAccess.get_drive_label: On Windows, returns the label of the drive (partition) passed as an argument.
m.DirAccess.get_drive_name: On Windows, returns the name of the drive (partition) passed as an argument (e.g. C:).
m.DirAccess.get_files: Returns a PackedStringArray containing filenames of the directory contents, excluding directories. The array is sorted alphabetically.
m.DirAccess.get_files_at: Returns a PackedStringArray containing filenames of the directory contents, excluding directories, at the given path. The array is sorted alphabetically.
m.DirAccess.get_filesystem_type: Returns file system type name of the current directory's disk. Returned values are uppercase strings like NTFS, FAT32, EXFAT, APFS, EXT4, BTRFS, and so on.
m.DirAccess.get_next: Returns the next element (file or directory) in the current directory.
m.DirAccess.get_open_error: Returns the result of the last open() call in the current thread.
m.DirAccess.get_space_left: Returns the available space on the current directory's disk, in bytes. Returns 0 if the platform-specific method to query the available space fails.
m.DirAccess.include_hidden: If true, hidden files are included when navigating the directory.
m.DirAccess.include_navigational: If true, . and .. are included when navigating the directory.
m.DirAccess.is_bundle: Returns true if the directory is a macOS bundle.
m.DirAccess.is_case_sensitive: Returns true if the file system or directory use case sensitive file names.
m.DirAccess.is_equivalent: Returns true if paths path_a and path_b resolve to the same file system object. Returns false otherwise, even if the files are bit-for-bit identical (e.g., identical copies of the file that are not symbolic links).
m.DirAccess.is_link: Returns true if the file or directory is a symbolic link, directory junction, or other reparse point.
m.DirAccess.list_dir_begin: Initializes the stream used to list all files and directories using the get_next() function, closing the currently opened stream if needed. Once the stream has been processed, it should typically be closed with list_dir_end().
m.DirAccess.list_dir_end: Closes the current stream opened with list_dir_begin() (whether it has been fully processed with get_next() does not matter).
m.DirAccess.make_dir: Creates a directory. The argument can be relative to the current directory, or an absolute path. The target directory should be placed in an already existing directory (to create the full path recursively, see make_dir_recursive()).
m.DirAccess.make_dir_absolute: Static version of make_dir(). Supports only absolute paths.
m.DirAccess.make_dir_recursive: Creates a target directory and all necessary intermediate directories in its path, by calling make_dir() recursively. The argument can be relative to the current directory, or an absolute path.
m.DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute: Static version of make_dir_recursive(). Supports only absolute paths.
m.DirAccess.open: Creates a new DirAccess object and opens an existing directory of the filesystem. The path argument can be within the project tree (res://folder), the user directory (user://folder) or an absolute path of the user filesystem (e.g. /tmp/folder or C:\tmp\folder).
m.DirAccess.read_link: Returns target of the symbolic link.
m.DirAccess.remove: Permanently deletes the target file or an empty directory. The argument can be relative to the current directory, or an absolute path. If the target directory is not empty, the operation will fail.
m.DirAccess.remove_absolute: Static version of remove(). Supports only absolute paths.
m.DirAccess.rename: Renames (move) the from file or directory to the to destination. Both arguments should be paths to files or directories, either relative or absolute. If the destination file or directory exists and is not access-protected, it will be overwritten.
m.DirAccess.rename_absolute: Static version of rename(). Supports only absolute paths.
m.DirectionalLight2D.height: The height of the light. Used with 2D normal mapping. Ranges from 0 (parallel to the plane) to 1 (perpendicular to the plane).
m.DirectionalLight2D.max_distance: The maximum distance from the camera center objects can be before their shadows are culled (in pixels). Decreasing this value can prevent objects located outside the camera from casting shadows (while also improving performance). Camera2D.zoom is not taken into account by max_distance, which means that at higher zoom values, shadows will appear to fade out sooner when zooming onto a given point.
m.DirectionalLight3D.SHADOW_ORTHOGONAL: Renders the entire scene's shadow map from an orthogonal point of view. This is the fastest directional shadow mode. May result in blurrier shadows on close objects.
m.DirectionalLight3D.SHADOW_PARALLEL_2_SPL: Splits the view frustum in 2 areas, each with its own shadow map. This shadow mode is a compromise between SHADOW_ORTHOGONAL and SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS in terms of performance.
m.DirectionalLight3D.SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPL: Splits the view frustum in 4 areas, each with its own shadow map. This is the slowest directional shadow mode.
m.DirectionalLight3D.SKY_MODE_LIGHT_AND_SK: Makes the light visible in both scene lighting and sky rendering.
m.DirectionalLight3D.SKY_MODE_LIGHT_ONLY: Makes the light visible in scene lighting only (including direct lighting and global illumination). When using this mode, the light will not be visible from sky shaders.
m.DirectionalLight3D.SKY_MODE_SKY_ONLY: Makes the light visible to sky shaders only. When using this mode the light will not cast light into the scene (either through direct lighting or through global illumination), but can be accessed through sky shaders. This can be useful, for example, when you want to control sky effects without illuminating the scene (during a night cycle, for example).
m.DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_bl: If true, shadow detail is sacrificed in exchange for smoother transitions between splits. Enabling shadow blend splitting also has a moderate performance cost. This is ignored when directional_shadow_mode is SHADOW_ORTHOGONAL.
m.DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_fa: Proportion of directional_shadow_max_distance at which point the shadow starts to fade. At directional_shadow_max_distance, the shadow will disappear. The default value is a balance between smooth fading and distant shadow visibility. If the camera moves fast and the directional_shadow_max_distance is low, consider lowering directional_shadow_fade_start below 0.8 to make shadow transitions less n…
m.DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_ma: The maximum distance for shadow splits. Increasing this value will make directional shadows visible from further away, at the cost of lower overall shadow detail and performance (since more objects need to be included in the directional shadow rendering).
m.DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_pa: Sets the size of the directional shadow pancake. The pancake offsets the start of the shadow's camera frustum to provide a higher effective depth resolution for the shadow. However, a high pancake size can cause artifacts in the shadows of large objects that are close to the edge of the frustum. Reducing the pancake size can help. Setting the size to 0 turns off the pancaking effect.
m.DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_sp: The distance from camera to shadow split 1. Relative to directional_shadow_max_distance. Only used when directional_shadow_mode is SHADOW_PARALLEL_2_SPLITS or SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS.
The distance from shadow split 1 to split 2. Relative to directional_shadow_max_distance. Only used when directional_shadow_mode is SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS.
The distance from shadow split 2 to split 3. Relative to directional_shadow_max_distance. Only used when directional_shadow_mode is SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS.
m.DirectionalLight3D.sky_mode: Whether this DirectionalLight3D is visible in the sky, in the scene, or both in the sky and in the scene.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_ARROW: Arrow cursor shape. This is the default when not pointing anything that overrides the mouse cursor, such as a LineEdit or TextEdit.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_BDIAGSIZE: Secondary diagonal resize cursor (top-right/bottom-left). Intended to be displayed when the hovered Control can be resized on both axes at once using the mouse.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_BUSY: Wait cursor. On most cursor themes, this replaces the arrow with a spinning icon. Intended to be used for blocking operations (when the user can't do anything else at the moment). See also CURSOR_WAIT.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_CAN_DROP: "Can drop" cursor. This is displayed during drag-and-drop operations if hovering over a Control that can accept the drag-and-drop event. On most cursor themes, this displays a dragging hand with an arrow symbol besides it. See also CURSOR_DRAG.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_CROSS: Crosshair cursor. This is intended to be displayed when the user needs precise aim over an element, such as a rectangle selection tool or a color picker.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_DRAG: Dragging hand cursor. This is displayed during drag-and-drop operations. See also CURSOR_CAN_DROP.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_FDIAGSIZE: Main diagonal resize cursor (top-left/bottom-right). Intended to be displayed when the hovered Control can be resized on both axes at once using the mouse.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_FORBIDDEN: Forbidden cursor. This is displayed during drag-and-drop operations if the hovered Control can't accept the drag-and-drop event.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_HELP: Help cursor. On most cursor themes, this displays a question mark icon instead of the mouse cursor. Intended to be used when the user has requested help on the next element that will be clicked.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_HSIZE: Horizontal resize cursor. Intended to be displayed when the hovered Control can be horizontally resized using the mouse. See also CURSOR_HSPLIT.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_HSPLIT: Horizontal split cursor. This is displayed when hovering a Control with splits that can be horizontally resized using the mouse, such as HSplitContainer. On some cursor themes, this cursor may have the same appearance as CURSOR_HSIZE.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_IBEAM: I-beam cursor shape. This is used by default when hovering a control that accepts text input, such as LineEdit or TextEdit.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_MAX: Represents the size of the CursorShape enum.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_MOVE: Move cursor. Intended to be displayed when the hovered Control can be moved using the mouse.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_POINTING_HAND: Pointing hand cursor shape. This is used by default when hovering a LinkButton or a URL tag in a RichTextLabel.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_VSIZE: Vertical resize cursor. Intended to be displayed when the hovered Control can be vertically resized using the mouse. See also CURSOR_VSPLIT.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_VSPLIT: Vertical split cursor. This is displayed when hovering a Control with splits that can be vertically resized using the mouse, such as VSplitContainer. On some cursor themes, this cursor may have the same appearance as CURSOR_VSIZE.
m.DisplayServer.CURSOR_WAIT: Wait cursor. On most cursor themes, this displays a spinning icon besides the arrow. Intended to be used for non-blocking operations (when the user can do something else at the moment). See also CURSOR_BUSY.
