m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_ACCESSIBILITY_SCRE: Display server supports interaction with screen reader or Braille display. Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS, Windows
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_CLIPBOARD: Display server supports setting and getting clipboard data. See also FEATURE_CLIPBOARD_PRIMARY. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), Android, iOS, Web
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_CLIPBOARD_PRIMARY: Display server supports Primary clipboard can be used. This is a different clipboard from FEATURE_CLIPBOARD. Linux (X11/Wayland)
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_CURSOR_SHAPE: Display server supports setting the mouse cursor shape to be different from the default. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), Android, Web
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_CUSTOM_CURSOR_SHAP: Display server supports setting the mouse cursor shape to a custom image. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), Web
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_EMOJI_AND_SYMBOL_P: Display server supports system emoji and symbol picker. Windows, macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_EXTEND_TO_TITLE: Display server supports expanding window content to the title. See WINDOW_FLAG_EXTEND_TO_TITLE. macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_GLOBAL_MENU: Deprecated: Use NativeMenu or PopupMenu instead.
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_HDR_OUTPUT: Display server supports HDR output. Linux (Wayland), macOS, iOS, visionOS, Windows
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_HIDPI: Display server supports querying the operating system's display scale factor. This allows automatically detecting the hiDPI display reliably, instead of guessing based on the screen resolution and the display's reported DPI (which might be unreliable due to broken monitor EDID). Windows, Linux (Wayland), macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_ICON: Display server supports changing the window icon (usually displayed in the top-left corner). Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland)
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_IME: Display server supports Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method], which is commonly used for inputting Chinese/Japanese/Korean text. This is handled by the operating system, rather than by Godot. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11)
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_MOUSE: Display server supports mouse input. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), Android, Web
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_MOUSE_WARP: Display server supports warping mouse coordinates to keep the mouse cursor constrained within an area, but looping when one of the edges is reached. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland)
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_NATIVE_COLOR_PICKE: Display server supports native color picker. Linux (X11/Wayland)
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_NATIVE_DIALOG: Display server supports spawning text dialogs using the operating system's native look-and-feel. See dialog_show(). Windows, macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_NATIVE_DIALOG_FILE: Display server supports spawning dialogs for selecting files or directories using the operating system's native look-and-feel. See file_dialog_show(). Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), Android

The display server supports all features of FEATURE_NATIVE_DIALOG_FILE, with the added functionality of Options and native dialog file access to res:// and user:// paths. See file_dialog_show() and file_dialog_with_options_show(). Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland)
Native file selection dialog supports MIME types as filters.
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_NATIVE_DIALOG_INPU: Display server supports spawning text input dialogs using the operating system's native look-and-feel. See dialog_input_text(). Windows, macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_NATIVE_HELP: Display server supports native help system search callbacks. See help_set_search_callbacks().
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_NATIVE_ICON: Display server supports changing the window icon (usually displayed in the top-left corner). Windows, macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_ORIENTATION: Display server supports changing the screen orientation. Android, iOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_PIP_MODE: Display server supports putting the application in picture-in-picture mode. Android
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_SCREEN_CAPTURE: Display server supports reading screen pixels. See screen_get_pixel().
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_SCREEN_EXCLUDE_FRO: Display server supports WINDOW_FLAG_EXCLUDE_FROM_CAPTURE window flag. Windows, macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_SELF_FITTING_WINDO: Display server automatically fits popups according to the screen boundaries. Window nodes should not attempt to do that themselves.
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_STATUS_INDICATOR: Display server supports application status indicators.
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_SUBWINDOWS: Display server supports multiple windows that can be moved outside of the main window. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11)
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_SWAP_BUFFERS: Display server supports V-Sync status can be changed from the default (which is forced to be enabled platforms not supporting this feature). Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland)
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_TEXT_TO_SPEECH: Display server supports text-to-speech. See tts_* methods. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), Android, iOS, Web
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_TOUCHSCREEN: Display server supports touchscreen input. Windows, Linux (X11/Wayland), Android, iOS, Web
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_VIRTUAL_KEYBOARD: Display server supports popping up a virtual keyboard when requested to input text without a physical keyboard. Android, iOS, Web
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_WINDOW_DRAG: The display server supports initiating window drag and resize operations on demand. See window_start_drag() and window_start_resize().
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_WINDOW_EMBEDDING: Display server supports embedding a window from another process. Windows, Linux (X11), macOS
m.DisplayServer.FEATURE_WINDOW_TRANSPARENC: Display server supports windows can use per-pixel transparency to make windows behind them partially or fully visible. Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), Android
m.DisplayServer.FILE_DIALOG_MODE_OPEN_ANY: The native file dialog allows selecting one file or directory.
m.DisplayServer.FILE_DIALOG_MODE_OPEN_DIR: The native file dialog only allows selecting a directory, disallowing the selection of any file.
m.DisplayServer.FILE_DIALOG_MODE_OPEN_FILE: The native file dialog allows selecting one, and only one file.
The native file dialog allows selecting multiple files.
m.DisplayServer.FILE_DIALOG_MODE_SAVE_FILE: The native file dialog will warn when a file exists.
m.DisplayServer.GLX_VISUALID: The GLX VisualID for the window.
m.DisplayServer.INVALID_SCREEN: The ID that refers to a screen that does not exist. This is returned by some DisplayServer methods if no screen matches the requested result.
m.DisplayServer.KEYBOARD_TYPE_EMAIL_ADDRES: Virtual keyboard with additional keys to assist with typing email addresses.
m.DisplayServer.KEYBOARD_TYPE_NUMBER: Virtual number keypad, useful for PIN entry.
m.DisplayServer.KEYBOARD_TYPE_NUMBER_DECIM: Virtual number keypad, useful for entering fractional numbers.
m.DisplayServer.KEYBOARD_TYPE_PASSWORD: Virtual keyboard for entering a password. On most platforms, this should disable autocomplete and autocapitalization.
m.DisplayServer.KEYBOARD_TYPE_URL: Virtual keyboard with additional keys to assist with typing URLs.
m.DisplayServer.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED: Captures the mouse. The mouse will be hidden and its position locked at the center of the window manager's window.
m.DisplayServer.MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED: Confines the mouse cursor to the game window, and make it visible.
m.DisplayServer.MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN: Confines the mouse cursor to the game window, and make it hidden.
m.DisplayServer.MOUSE_MODE_HIDDEN: Makes the mouse cursor hidden if it is visible.
m.DisplayServer.MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE: Makes the mouse cursor visible if it is hidden.
m.DisplayServer.OPENGL_CONTEXT: OpenGL context (only with the Compatibility renderer):
m.DisplayServer.PROGRESS_STATE_ERROR: The progress indicator shows that an error has occurred.
m.DisplayServer.PROGRESS_STATE_INDETERMINA: The progress indicator shows an indeterminate progress.
m.DisplayServer.PROGRESS_STATE_NOPROGRESS: Stops displaying progress and returns the button to its normal state.
m.DisplayServer.PROGRESS_STATE_NORMAL: The progress indicator shows progress normally.
m.DisplayServer.PROGRESS_STATE_PAUSED: The progress indicator shows it was paused.
m.DisplayServer.SCREEN_SENSOR: Automatic landscape or portrait orientation (default or reverse depending on sensor).
m.DisplayServer.SCREEN_SENSOR_LANDSCAPE: Automatic landscape orientation (default or reverse depending on sensor).
m.DisplayServer.SCREEN_SENSOR_PORTRAIT: Automatic portrait orientation (default or reverse depending on sensor).
m.DisplayServer.TTS_UTTERANCE_BOUNDARY: Utterance reached a word or sentence boundary.
m.DisplayServer.TTS_UTTERANCE_CANCELED: Utterance was canceled, or TTS service was unable to process it.
m.DisplayServer.TTS_UTTERANCE_STARTED: Utterance has begun to be spoken.
m.DisplayServer.VSYNC_ADAPTIVE: Behaves like VSYNC_DISABLED when the framerate drops below the screen's refresh rate to reduce stuttering (tearing may be visible). Otherwise, vertical synchronization is enabled to avoid tearing. Framerate is limited by the monitor refresh rate (regardless of Engine.max_fps). Behaves like VSYNC_ENABLED when using the Compatibility rendering method.
m.DisplayServer.VSYNC_DISABLED: No vertical synchronization, which means the engine will display frames as fast as possible (tearing may be visible). Framerate is unlimited (regardless of Engine.max_fps).
m.DisplayServer.VSYNC_ENABLED: Default vertical synchronization mode, the image is displayed only on vertical blanking intervals (no tearing is visible). Framerate is limited by the monitor refresh rate (regardless of Engine.max_fps).
m.DisplayServer.VSYNC_MAILBOX: Displays the most recent image in the queue on vertical blanking intervals, while rendering to the other images (no tearing is visible). Framerate is unlimited (regardless of Engine.max_fps).
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EDGE_MAX: Represents the size of the WindowResizeEdge enum.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_CLOSE_REQUEST: Sent when the user has attempted to close the window (e.g. close button is pressed).
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_DPI_CHANGE: Sent when the window is moved to the display with different DPI, or display DPI is changed.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_FOCUS_IN: Sent when the window grabs focus.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_FOCUS_OUT: Sent when the window loses focus.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_FORCE_CLOSE: Sent when the window has been forcibly closed by the display server. The window will immediately hide and clean any internal rendering references.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_GO_BACK_REQUE: Sent when the device "Back" button is pressed.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_MOUSE_ENTER: Sent when the mouse pointer enters the window.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_MOUSE_EXIT: Sent when the mouse pointer exits the window.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_OUTPUT_MAX_LI: Sent when the output max linear value returned by Window.get_output_max_linear_value() has changed.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_EVENT_TITLEBAR_CHAN: Sent when the window title bar decoration is changed (e.g. WINDOW_FLAG_EXTEND_TO_TITLE is set or window entered/exited full screen mode).
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_ALWAYS_ON_TOP: The window is floating on top of all other windows. This flag is ignored for full-screen windows.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_BORDERLESS: The window do not have native title bar and other decorations. This flag is ignored for full-screen windows.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_EXCLUDE_FROM_C: Window is excluded from screenshots taken by screen_get_image(), screen_get_image_rect(), and screen_get_pixel().
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_EXTEND_TO_TITL: Window content is expanded to the full size of the window. Unlike borderless window, the frame is left intact and can be used to resize the window, title bar is transparent, but have minimize/maximize/close buttons.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_MAX: Represents the size of the WindowFlags enum.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_MOUSE_PASSTHRO: All mouse events are passed to the underlying window of the same application.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_NO_FOCUS: The window can't be focused. No-focus window will ignore all input, except mouse clicks.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_POPUP: Window is part of menu or OptionButton dropdown. This flag can't be changed when the window is visible. An active popup window will exclusively receive all input, without stealing focus from its parent. Popup windows are automatically closed when uses click outside it, or when an application is switched. Popup window must have transient parent set (see window_set_transient()).
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_POPUP_WM_HINT: Signals the window manager that this window is supposed to be an implementation-defined "popup" (usually a floating, borderless, untileable and immovable child window).
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_RESIZE_DISABLE: The window can't be resized by dragging its resize grip. It's still possible to resize the window using window_set_size(). This flag is ignored for full screen windows.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_SHARP_CORNERS: Window style is overridden, forcing sharp corners.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_TRANSPARENT: The window background can be transparent.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_EXCLUSIVE_FULL: A single window full screen mode. This mode has less overhead, but only one window can be open on a given screen at a time (opening a child window or application switching will trigger a full screen transition).
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN: Full screen mode with full multi-window support.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_MAXIMIZED: Maximized window mode, i.e. Window will occupy whole screen area except task bar and still display its borders. Normally happens when the maximize button is pressed.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_MINIMIZED: Minimized window mode, i.e. Window is not visible and available on window manager's window list. Normally happens when the minimize button is pressed.
m.DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED: Windowed mode, i.e. Window doesn't occupy the whole screen (unless set to the size of the screen).
m.DisplayServer.accessibility_screen_reade: Returns 1 if a screen reader, Braille display or other assistive app is active, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
m.DisplayServer.accessibility_should_incre: Returns 1 if a high-contrast user interface theme should be used, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
m.DisplayServer.accessibility_should_reduc: Returns 1 if flashing, blinking, and other moving content that can cause seizures in users with photosensitive epilepsy should be disabled, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
Returns 1 if background images, transparency, and other features that can reduce the contrast between the foreground and background should be disabled, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
m.DisplayServer.beep: Plays the beep sound from the operative system, if possible. Because it comes from the OS, the beep sound will be audible even if the application is muted. It may also be disabled for the entire OS by the user.
m.DisplayServer.clipboard_get: Returns the user's clipboard as a string if possible.
m.DisplayServer.clipboard_get_image: Returns the user's clipboard as an image if possible.
m.DisplayServer.clipboard_get_primary: Returns the user's primary [https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/139191/whats-the-difference-between-primary-selection-and-clipboard-buffer] clipboard as a string if possible. This is the clipboard that is set when the user selects text in any application, rather than when pressing Ctrl + C. The clipboard data can then be pasted by clicking the middle mouse button in any application that supp…
m.DisplayServer.clipboard_has: Returns true if there is a text content on the user's clipboard.
m.DisplayServer.clipboard_has_image: Returns true if there is an image content on the user's clipboard.
m.DisplayServer.clipboard_set: Sets the user's clipboard content to the given string.
m.DisplayServer.clipboard_set_primary: Sets the user's primary [https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/139191/whats-the-difference-between-primary-selection-and-clipboard-buffer] clipboard content to the given string. This is the clipboard that is set when the user selects text in any application, rather than when pressing Ctrl + C. The clipboard data can then be pasted by clicking the middle mouse button in any application that sup…
m.DisplayServer.create_status_indicator: Creates a new application status indicator with the specified icon, tooltip, and activation callback.
m.DisplayServer.cursor_get_shape: Returns the default mouse cursor shape set by cursor_set_shape().
m.DisplayServer.cursor_set_custom_image: Sets a custom mouse cursor image for the given shape. This means the user's operating system and mouse cursor theme will no longer influence the mouse cursor's appearance.
m.DisplayServer.cursor_set_shape: Sets the default mouse cursor shape. The cursor's appearance will vary depending on the user's operating system and mouse cursor theme. See also cursor_get_shape() and cursor_set_custom_image().
m.DisplayServer.dialog_input_text: Shows a text input dialog which uses the operating system's native look-and-feel. callback should accept a single String parameter which contains the text field's contents.
m.DisplayServer.dialog_show: Shows a text dialog which uses the operating system's native look-and-feel. callback should accept a single int parameter which corresponds to the index of the pressed button.
m.DisplayServer.enable_for_stealing_focus: Allows the process_id PID to steal focus from this window. In other words, this disables the operating system's focus stealing protection for the specified PID.
m.DisplayServer.file_dialog_show: Displays OS native dialog for selecting files or directories in the file system.
m.DisplayServer.file_dialog_with_options_s: Displays OS native dialog for selecting files or directories in the file system with additional user selectable options.
m.DisplayServer.force_process_and_drop_eve: Forces window manager processing while ignoring all InputEvents. See also process_events().
m.DisplayServer.get_accent_color: Returns OS theme accent color. Returns Color(0, 0, 0, 0), if accent color is unknown.
m.DisplayServer.get_base_color: Returns the OS theme base color (default control background). Returns Color(0, 0, 0, 0) if the base color is unknown.
m.DisplayServer.get_display_cutouts: Returns an Array of Rect2, each of which is the bounding rectangle for a display cutout or notch. These are non-functional areas on edge-to-edge screens used by cameras and sensors. Returns an empty array if the device does not have cutouts. See also get_display_safe_area().
m.DisplayServer.get_display_safe_area: Returns the unobscured area of the display where interactive controls should be rendered. See also get_display_cutouts().
m.DisplayServer.get_keyboard_focus_screen: Returns the index of the screen containing the window with the keyboard focus, or the primary screen if there's no focused window.
m.DisplayServer.get_name: Returns the name of the DisplayServer currently in use. Most operating systems only have a single DisplayServer, but Linux has access to more than one DisplayServer (currently X11 and Wayland).
m.DisplayServer.get_primary_screen: Returns the index of the primary screen.
m.DisplayServer.get_screen_count: Returns the number of displays available.
m.DisplayServer.get_screen_from_rect: Returns the index of the screen that overlaps the most with the given rectangle. Returns INVALID_SCREEN if the rectangle doesn't overlap with any screen or has no area.
m.DisplayServer.get_swap_cancel_ok: Returns true if positions of OK and Cancel buttons are swapped in dialogs. This is enabled by default on Windows to follow interface conventions, and be toggled by changing ProjectSettings.gui/common/swap_cancel_ok.
m.DisplayServer.get_window_at_screen_posit: Returns the ID of the window at the specified screen position (in pixels). On multi-monitor setups, the screen position is relative to the virtual desktop area. m.DisplayServer.get_window_list: Returns the list of Godot window IDs belonging to this process.

m.DisplayServer.has_additional_outputs: Returns true if any additional outputs have been registered via register_additional_output().
m.DisplayServer.has_feature: Returns true if the specified feature is supported by the current DisplayServer, false otherwise.
m.DisplayServer.has_hardware_keyboard: Returns true if a hardware keyboard is connected.
m.DisplayServer.help_set_search_callbacks: Sets native help system search callbacks.
m.DisplayServer.ime_get_selection: Returns the text selection in the Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method] composition string, with the Vector2i's x component being the caret position and y being the length of the selection.
m.DisplayServer.ime_get_text: Returns the composition string contained within the Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method] window.
m.DisplayServer.is_dark_mode: Returns true if OS is using dark mode.
m.DisplayServer.is_dark_mode_supported: Returns true if OS supports dark mode.
m.DisplayServer.is_in_pip_mode: Returns true if the application is in picture-in-picture mode.
m.DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available: Returns true if touch events are available (Android or iOS), the capability is detected on the Web platform or if ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse is true.
m.DisplayServer.is_window_transparency_ava: Returns true if the window background can be made transparent. This method returns false if ProjectSettings.display/window/per_pixel_transparency/allowed is set to false, or if transparency is not supported by the renderer or OS compositor.
m.DisplayServer.keyboard_get_keycode_from_: Converts a physical (US QWERTY) keycode to one in the active keyboard layout.
m.DisplayServer.keyboard_get_label_from_ph: Converts a physical (US QWERTY) keycode to localized label printed on the key in the active keyboard layout.
m.DisplayServer.keyboard_get_layout_count: Returns the number of keyboard layouts.
m.DisplayServer.keyboard_get_layout_langua: Returns the ISO-639/BCP-47 language code of the keyboard layout at position index.
m.DisplayServer.keyboard_get_layout_name: Returns the localized name of the keyboard layout at position index.
m.DisplayServer.mouse_get_button_state: Returns the current state of mouse buttons (whether each button is pressed) as a bitmask. If multiple mouse buttons are pressed at the same time, the bits are added together. Equivalent to Input.get_mouse_button_mask().
m.DisplayServer.mouse_get_mode: Returns the current mouse mode. See also mouse_set_mode().
m.DisplayServer.mouse_get_position: Returns the mouse cursor's current position in screen coordinates.
m.DisplayServer.mouse_set_mode: Sets the current mouse mode. See also mouse_get_mode().
m.DisplayServer.orientation_changed: Emitted when the device orientation changes. orientation is the new orientation.
m.DisplayServer.pip_mode_set_aspect_ratio: Specifies the aspect ratio for picture-in-picture mode.
m.DisplayServer.pip_mode_set_auto_enter_on: Specifies whether picture-in-picture mode should be entered automatically when the application goes in the background.
m.DisplayServer.process_events: Perform window manager processing, including input flushing. See also force_process_and_drop_events(), Input.flush_buffered_events() and Input.use_accumulated_input.
m.DisplayServer.register_additional_output: Registers an Object which represents an additional output that will be rendered too, beyond normal windows. The Object is only used as an identifier, which can be later passed to unregister_additional_output().
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi: Returns the dots per inch density of the specified screen. Returns platform specific default value if screen is invalid.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_image: Returns a screenshot of the screen. Returns null if screen is invalid or the DisplayServer fails to capture screenshot.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_image_rect: Returns a screenshot of the screen region defined by rect. Returns null if rect is outside screen bounds or the DisplayServer fails to capture screenshot.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_max_scale: Returns the greatest scale factor of all screens.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_orientation: Returns the screen's current orientation. See also screen_set_orientation(). Returns SCREEN_LANDSCAPE if screen is invalid.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_pixel: Returns the color of the pixel at the given screen position. On multi-monitor setups, the screen position is relative to the virtual desktop area.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_position: Returns the screen's top-left corner position in pixels. Returns Vector2i.ZERO if screen is invalid. On multi-monitor setups, the screen position is relative to the virtual desktop area. On multi-monitor setups with different screen resolutions or orientations, the origin might be located outside any display like this:
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_refresh_rate: Returns the current refresh rate of the specified screen. When V-Sync is enabled, this returns the maximum framerate the project can effectively reach. Returns -1.0 if screen is invalid or the DisplayServer fails to find the refresh rate for the specified screen.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_scale: Returns the scale factor of the specified screen by index. Returns 1.0 if screen is invalid.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_size: Returns the screen's size in pixels. See also screen_get_position() and screen_get_usable_rect(). Returns Vector2i.ZERO if screen is invalid.
m.DisplayServer.screen_get_usable_rect: Returns the portion of the screen that is not obstructed by a status bar in pixels. See also screen_get_size().
m.DisplayServer.screen_is_kept_on: Returns true if the screen should never be turned off by the operating system's power-saving measures. See also screen_set_keep_on().
m.DisplayServer.screen_set_keep_on: Sets whether the screen should never be turned off by the operating system's power-saving measures. See also screen_is_kept_on().
m.DisplayServer.screen_set_orientation: Sets the screen's orientation. See also screen_get_orientation().
m.DisplayServer.set_hardware_keyboard_conn: Sets the callback that should be called when a hardware keyboard is connected or disconnected. callable should accept a single bool argument indicating whether the keyboard has been connected (true) or disconnected (false).
m.DisplayServer.set_icon: Sets the application icon and icons of all windows with an Image. To use icons in the operating system's native format, use set_native_icon() instead.
m.DisplayServer.set_native_icon: Sets the window icon (usually displayed in the top-left corner) in the operating system's native format. The file at filename must be in .ico format on Windows or .icns on macOS. By using specially crafted .ico or .icns icons, set_native_icon() allows specifying different icons depending on the size the icon is displayed at. This size is determined by the operating system and user preferences (in…
m.DisplayServer.set_system_theme_change_ca: Sets the callback that should be called when the system's theme settings are changed. callable should accept zero arguments.
m.DisplayServer.show_emoji_and_symbol_pick: Opens system emoji and symbol picker.
m.DisplayServer.status_indicator_get_rect: Returns the rectangle for the given status indicator id in screen coordinates. If the status indicator is not visible, returns an empty Rect2.
m.DisplayServer.status_indicator_set_callb: Sets the application status indicator activation callback. callback should take two arguments: int mouse button index (one of MouseButton values) and Vector2i click position in screen coordinates.
m.DisplayServer.status_indicator_set_icon: Sets the application status indicator icon.
m.DisplayServer.status_indicator_set_menu: Sets the application status indicator native popup menu.
m.DisplayServer.status_indicator_set_toolt: Sets the application status indicator tooltip.
m.DisplayServer.tablet_get_current_driver: Returns current active tablet driver name.
m.DisplayServer.tablet_get_driver_count: Returns the total number of available tablet drivers.
m.DisplayServer.tablet_get_driver_name: Returns the tablet driver name for the given index.
m.DisplayServer.tts_get_voices: Returns an Array of voice information dictionaries.
m.DisplayServer.tts_get_voices_for_languag: Returns a PackedStringArray of voice identifiers for the language.
m.DisplayServer.tts_is_paused: Returns true if the synthesizer is in a paused state.
m.DisplayServer.tts_is_speaking: Returns true if the synthesizer is generating speech, or have utterance waiting in the queue.
m.DisplayServer.tts_pause: Puts the synthesizer into a paused state.
m.DisplayServer.tts_resume: Resumes the synthesizer if it was paused.
m.DisplayServer.tts_set_utterance_callback: Adds a callback, which is called when the utterance has started, finished, canceled or reached a text boundary.
m.DisplayServer.tts_speak: Adds an utterance to the queue. If interrupt is true, the queue is cleared first.
m.DisplayServer.tts_stop: Stops synthesis in progress and removes all utterances from the queue.
m.DisplayServer.unregister_additional_outp: Unregisters an Object representing an additional output, that was registered via register_additional_output().
m.DisplayServer.virtual_keyboard_get_heigh: Returns the on-screen keyboard's height in pixels. Returns 0 if there is no keyboard or if it is currently hidden.
m.DisplayServer.virtual_keyboard_hide: Hides the virtual keyboard if it is shown, does nothing otherwise.
m.DisplayServer.virtual_keyboard_show: Shows the virtual keyboard if the platform has one.
m.DisplayServer.warp_mouse: Sets the mouse cursor position to the given position relative to an origin at the upper left corner of the currently focused game Window Manager window.
m.DisplayServer.window_can_draw: Returns true if anything can be drawn in the window specified by window_id, false otherwise. Using the --disable-render-loop command line argument or a headless build will return false.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_active_popup: Returns ID of the active popup window, or INVALID_WINDOW_ID if there is none.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_attached_instan: Returns the Object.get_instance_id() of the Window the window_id is attached to.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_current_screen: Returns the screen the window specified by window_id is currently positioned on. If the screen overlaps multiple displays, the screen where the window's center is located is returned. See also window_set_current_screen(). Returns INVALID_SCREEN if window_id is invalid.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_flag: Returns the current value of the given window's flag.
