m.DisplayServer.window_get_hdr_output_max_: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_hdr_output_refe: Returns the reference white luminance in nits (cd/m²) set for HDR output by the window specified by window_id. Negative values indicate that the value is being automatically adjusted to match the operating system brightness. See also window_get_hdr_output_current_reference_luminance().
m.DisplayServer.window_get_max_size: Returns the window's maximum size (in pixels). See also window_set_max_size().
m.DisplayServer.window_get_min_size: Returns the window's minimum size (in pixels). See also window_set_min_size().
m.DisplayServer.window_get_mode: Returns the mode of the given window.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_native_handle: Returns internal structure pointers for use in plugins.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_output_max_line: Returns the maximum value for linear color components that can be displayed for the window specified by window_id, regardless of SDR or HDR output. Returns 1.0 if HDR is not enabled or not supported. When HDR output is enabled, this is calculated based on window_get_hdr_output_current_reference_luminance() and window_get_hdr_output_current_max_luminance(). The Window.output_max_linear_value_chang…
m.DisplayServer.window_get_popup_safe_rect: Returns the bounding box of control, or menu item that was used to open the popup window, in the screen coordinate system.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_position: Returns the position of the client area of the given window on the screen.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_position_with_d: Returns the position of the given window on the screen including the borders drawn by the operating system. See also window_get_position().
m.DisplayServer.window_get_safe_title_marg: Returns left margins (x), right margins (y) and height (z) of the title that are safe to use (contains no buttons or other elements) when WINDOW_FLAG_EXTEND_TO_TITLE flag is set.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_size: Returns the size of the window specified by window_id (in pixels), excluding the borders drawn by the operating system. This is also called the "client area". See also window_get_size_with_decorations(), window_set_size() and window_get_position().
m.DisplayServer.window_get_size_with_decor: Returns the size of the window specified by window_id (in pixels), including the borders drawn by the operating system. See also window_get_size().
m.DisplayServer.window_get_title_size: Returns the estimated window title bar size (including text and window buttons) for the window specified by window_id (in pixels). This method does not change the window title.
m.DisplayServer.window_get_vsync_mode: Returns the V-Sync mode of the given window.
m.DisplayServer.window_is_focused: Returns true if the window specified by window_id is focused.
m.DisplayServer.window_is_hdr_output_enabl: Returns true if HDR output is currently enabled for the window specified by window_id. The returned value may change dynamically based on system settings, screen capabilities, and which screen the window is currently on.
m.DisplayServer.window_is_hdr_output_reque: Returns true if HDR output is requested for the window specified by window_id. Corresponds to Window.hdr_output_requested.
m.DisplayServer.window_is_hdr_output_suppo: Returns true if the window specified by window_id supports HDR output. This depends on the platform, screen capabilities, system settings, and the screen the window is currently on.
m.DisplayServer.window_is_maximize_allowed: Returns true if the given window can be maximized (the maximize button is enabled).
m.DisplayServer.window_maximize_on_title_d: Returns true if double-clicking on a window's title should maximize it.
m.DisplayServer.window_minimize_on_title_d: Returns true if double-clicking on a window's title should minimize it.
m.DisplayServer.window_move_to_foreground: Moves the window specified by window_id to the foreground, so that it is visible over other windows.
m.DisplayServer.window_request_attention: Makes the window specified by window_id request attention, which is materialized by the window title and taskbar entry blinking until the window is focused. This usually has no visible effect if the window is currently focused. The exact behavior varies depending on the operating system.
m.DisplayServer.window_request_hdr_output: If enable is true, HDR output is requested for the window specified by window_id. The window will automatically switch between HDR and SDR if it is moved between screens, screen capabilities change, or system settings are modified. This will internally force Viewport.use_hdr_2d to be enabled on the main Viewport. All other SubViewport of the Window must have their Viewport.use_hdr_2d property ena…
m.DisplayServer.window_set_color: Sets the background color of the root window.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_current_screen: Moves the window specified by window_id to the specified screen. See also window_get_current_screen().
m.DisplayServer.window_set_drop_files_call: Sets the callback that should be called when files are dropped from the operating system's file manager to the window specified by window_id. callback should take one PackedStringArray argument, which is the list of dropped files.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_exclusive: If set to true, this window will always stay on top of its parent window, parent window will ignore input while this window is opened.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_flag: Enables or disables the given window's given flag.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_hdr_output_max_: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_hdr_output_refe: Sets the reference white luminance in nits (cd/m²) for HDR output by the window specified by window_id. If reference_luminance is negative, the window automatically adjusts to the brightness set by the operating system. By default, this luminance is set to -1.0 for every window. Typically this property should be left at this default value, but may optionally be exposed as an "HDR Brightness" in-g…
m.DisplayServer.window_set_icon: Sets the window icon (usually displayed in the top-left corner) for the window specified by window_id.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_ime_active: Sets whether Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method] should be enabled for the window specified by window_id. See also window_set_ime_position().
m.DisplayServer.window_set_ime_position: Sets the position of the Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method] popup for the specified window_id. Only effective if window_set_ime_active() was set to true for the specified window_id.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_input_event_cal: Sets the callback that should be called when any InputEvent is sent to the window specified by window_id.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_input_text_call: Sets the callback that should be called when text is entered using the virtual keyboard to the window specified by window_id.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_max_size: Sets the maximum size of the window specified by window_id in pixels. Normally, the user will not be able to drag the window to make it larger than the specified size. See also window_get_max_size().
m.DisplayServer.window_set_min_size: Sets the minimum size for the given window to min_size in pixels. Normally, the user will not be able to drag the window to make it smaller than the specified size. See also window_get_min_size().
m.DisplayServer.window_set_mode: Sets window mode for the given window to mode.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_mouse_passthrou: Sets a polygonal region of the window which accepts mouse events. Mouse events outside the region will be passed through.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_popup_safe_rect: Sets the bounding box of control, or menu item that was used to open the popup window, in the screen coordinate system. Clicking this area will not auto-close this popup.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_position: Sets the position of the given window to position. On multi-monitor setups, the screen position is relative to the virtual desktop area. On multi-monitor setups with different screen resolutions or orientations, the origin may be located outside any display like this:
m.DisplayServer.window_set_rect_changed_ca: Sets the callback that will be called when the window specified by window_id is moved or resized.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_size: Sets the size of the given window to size (in pixels). See also window_get_size() and window_get_position().
m.DisplayServer.window_set_taskbar_progres: Sets the type and state of the progress bar on the taskbar/dock icon of the window specified by window_id. See ProgressState for possible values and how each mode behaves.
Creates a progress bar on the taskbar/dock icon of the window specified by window_id if it does not exist, sets the progress of the icon.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_title: Sets the title of the given window to title.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_transient: Sets window transient parent. Transient window will be destroyed with its transient parent and will return focus to their parent when closed. The transient window is displayed on top of a non-exclusive full-screen parent window. Transient windows can't enter full-screen mode.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_vsync_mode: Sets the V-Sync mode of the given window. See also ProjectSettings.display/window/vsync/vsync_mode.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_window_buttons_: When WINDOW_FLAG_EXTEND_TO_TITLE flag is set, set offset to the center of the first titlebar button.
m.DisplayServer.window_set_window_event_ca: Sets the callback that will be called when an event occurs in the window specified by window_id.
m.DisplayServer.window_start_drag: Starts an interactive drag operation on the window with the given window_id, using the current mouse position. Call this method when handling a mouse button being pressed to simulate a pressed event on the window's title bar. Using this method allows the window to participate in space switching, tiling, and other system features.
m.DisplayServer.window_start_resize: Starts an interactive resize operation on the window with the given window_id, using the current mouse position. Call this method when handling a mouse button being pressed to simulate a pressed event on the window's edge.
m.DrawableTexture2D.DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBA8: OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 8.
m.DrawableTexture2D.DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBA8_: OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 8.
m.DrawableTexture2D.DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBAF: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA32F where there are four components, each a 32-bit floating-point value.
m.DrawableTexture2D.DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBAH: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA16F where there are four components, each a 16-bit "half-precision" floating-point value.
m.DrawableTexture2D.blit_rect: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.DrawableTexture2D.blit_rect_multi: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.DrawableTexture2D.generate_mipmaps: Re-calculates the mipmaps for this texture on demand.
m.DrawableTexture2D.get_use_mipmaps: Returns true if mipmaps are set to be used on this DrawableTexture.
m.DrawableTexture2D.set_format: Sets the format of this DrawableTexture.
m.DrawableTexture2D.set_use_mipmaps: Sets if mipmaps should be used on this DrawableTexture.
m.DrawableTexture2D.setup: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.ENetConnection.COMPRESS_FASTLZ: FastLZ [https://fastlz.org/] compression. This option uses less CPU resources compared to COMPRESS_ZLIB, at the expense of using more bandwidth.
m.ENetConnection.COMPRESS_NONE: No compression. This uses the most bandwidth, but has the upside of requiring the fewest CPU resources. This option may also be used to make network debugging using tools like Wireshark easier.
m.ENetConnection.COMPRESS_RANGE_CODER: ENet's built-in range encoding. Works well on small packets, but is not the most efficient algorithm on packets larger than 4 KB.
m.ENetConnection.COMPRESS_ZLIB: Zlib [https://www.zlib.net/] compression. This option uses less bandwidth compared to COMPRESS_FASTLZ, at the expense of using more CPU resources.
m.ENetConnection.COMPRESS_ZSTD: Zstandard [https://facebook.github.io/zstd/] compression. Note that this algorithm is not very efficient on packets smaller than 4 KB. Therefore, it's recommended to use other compression algorithms in most cases.
m.ENetConnection.EVENT_CONNECT: A connection request initiated by enet_host_connect has completed. The array will contain the peer which successfully connected.
m.ENetConnection.EVENT_DISCONNECT: A peer has disconnected. This event is generated on a successful completion of a disconnect initiated by ENetPacketPeer.peer_disconnect(), if a peer has timed out, or if a connection request initialized by connect_to_host() has timed out. The array will contain the peer which disconnected. The data field contains user supplied data describing the disconnection, or 0, if none is available.
m.ENetConnection.EVENT_ERROR: An error occurred during service(). You will likely need to destroy() the host and recreate it.
m.ENetConnection.EVENT_NONE: No event occurred within the specified time limit.
m.ENetConnection.EVENT_RECEIVE: A packet has been received from a peer. The array will contain the peer which sent the packet and the channel number upon which the packet was received. The received packet will be queued to the associated ENetPacketPeer.
m.ENetConnection.bandwidth_limit: Adjusts the bandwidth limits of a host.
m.ENetConnection.broadcast: Queues a packet to be sent to all peers associated with the host over the specified channel. See ENetPacketPeer FLAG_* constants for available packet flags.
m.ENetConnection.channel_limit: Limits the maximum allowed channels of future incoming connections.
m.ENetConnection.compress: Sets the compression method used for network packets. These have different tradeoffs of compression speed versus bandwidth, you may need to test which one works best for your use case if you use compression at all.
m.ENetConnection.connect_to_host: Initiates a connection to a foreign address using the specified port and allocating the requested channels. Optional data can be passed during connection in the form of a 32 bit integer.
m.ENetConnection.create_host: Creates an ENetHost that allows up to max_peers connected peers, each allocating up to max_channels channels, optionally limiting bandwidth to in_bandwidth and out_bandwidth (if greater than zero).
m.ENetConnection.create_host_bound: Creates an ENetHost bound to the given bind_address and bind_port that allows up to max_peers connected peers, each allocating up to max_channels channels, optionally limiting bandwidth to in_bandwidth and out_bandwidth (if greater than zero).
m.ENetConnection.destroy: Destroys the host and all resources associated with it.
m.ENetConnection.dtls_client_setup: Configure this ENetHost to use the custom Godot extension allowing DTLS encryption for ENet clients. Call this before connect_to_host() to have ENet connect using DTLS validating the server certificate against hostname. You can pass the optional client_options parameter to customize the trusted certification authorities, or disable the common name verification. See TLSOptions.client() and TLSOpti…
m.ENetConnection.dtls_server_setup: Configure this ENetHost to use the custom Godot extension allowing DTLS encryption for ENet servers. Call this right after create_host_bound() to have ENet expect peers to connect using DTLS. See TLSOptions.server().
m.ENetConnection.flush: Sends any queued packets on the host specified to its designated peers.
m.ENetConnection.get_local_port: Returns the local port to which this peer is bound.
m.ENetConnection.get_max_channels: Returns the maximum number of channels allowed for connected peers.
m.ENetConnection.get_peers: Returns the list of peers associated with this host.
m.ENetConnection.refuse_new_connections: Configures the DTLS server to automatically drop new connections.
m.ENetConnection.service: Waits for events on this connection and shuttles packets between the host and its peers, with the given timeout (in milliseconds). The returned Array will have 4 elements. An EventType, the ENetPacketPeer which generated the event, the event associated data (if any), the event associated channel (if any). If the generated event is EVENT_RECEIVE, the received packet will be queued to the associate…
m.ENetConnection.socket_send: Sends a packet toward a destination from the address and port currently bound by this ENetConnection instance.
m.ENetMultiplayerPeer.add_mesh_peer: Add a new remote peer with the given peer_id connected to the given host.
m.ENetMultiplayerPeer.create_client: Create client that connects to a server at address using specified port. The given address needs to be either a fully qualified domain name (e.g. "www.example.com") or an IP address in IPv4 or IPv6 format (e.g. "192.168.1.1"). The port is the port the server is listening on. The channel_count parameter can be used to specify the number of ENet channels allocated for the connection. The in_bandwid…
m.ENetMultiplayerPeer.create_mesh: Initialize this MultiplayerPeer in mesh mode. The provided unique_id will be used as the local peer network unique ID once assigned as the MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer. In the mesh configuration you will need to set up each new peer manually using ENetConnection before calling add_mesh_peer(). While this technique is more advanced, it allows for better control over the connection process (e.g.…
m.ENetMultiplayerPeer.create_server: Create server that listens to connections via port. The port needs to be an available, unused port between 0 and 65535. Note that ports below 1024 are privileged and may require elevated permissions depending on the platform. To change the interface the server listens on, use set_bind_ip(). The default IP is the wildcard "*", which listens on all available interfaces. max_clients is the maximum n…
m.ENetMultiplayerPeer.get_peer: Returns the ENetPacketPeer associated to the given id.
m.ENetMultiplayerPeer.host: The underlying ENetConnection created after create_client() and create_server().
m.ENetMultiplayerPeer.set_bind_ip: The IP used when creating a server. This is set to the wildcard "*" by default, which binds to all available interfaces. The given IP needs to be in IPv4 or IPv6 address format, for example: "192.168.1.1".
m.ENetPacketPeer.PACKET_LOSS_SCALE: The reference scale for packet loss. See get_statistic() and PEER_PACKET_LOSS.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_LAST_ROUND_TRIP_TIME: Last recorded round trip time for a reliable packet.
Variance of the last trip time recorded.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_LOSS: Mean packet loss of reliable packets as a ratio with respect to the PACKET_LOSS_SCALE.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_LOSS_EPOCH: The time at which packet loss statistics were last updated (in milliseconds since the connection started). The interval for packet loss statistics updates is 10 seconds, and at least one packet must have been sent since the last statistics update.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_ACCE: The throttle's acceleration factor. Higher values will make ENet adapt to fluctuating network conditions faster, causing unrelaible packets to be sent more often. The default value is 2.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_COUN: Internal value used to increment the packet throttle counter. The value is hardcoded to 7 and cannot be changed. You probably want to look at PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_ACCELERATION instead.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_DECE: The throttle's deceleration factor. Higher values will make ENet adapt to fluctuating network conditions faster, causing unrelaible packets to be sent less often. The default value is 2.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_EPOC: The time at which throttle statistics were last updated (in milliseconds since the connection started). The interval for throttle statistics updates is PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_INTERVAL.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_INTE: The interval over which the lowest mean round trip time should be measured for use by the throttle mechanism (in milliseconds). The default value is 5000.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_PACKET_THROTTLE_LIMI: The maximum number of unreliable packets that should not be dropped. This value is always greater than or equal to 1. The initial value is equal to PACKET_THROTTLE_SCALE.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_ROUND_TRIP_TIME: Mean packet round trip time for reliable packets.
m.ENetPacketPeer.PEER_ROUND_TRIP_TIME_VARI: Variance of the mean round trip time.
m.ENetPacketPeer.STATE_ACKNOWLEDGING_CONNE: The peer has acknowledged the connection request.
m.ENetPacketPeer.STATE_ACKNOWLEDGING_DISCO: The peer has acknowledged the disconnection request.
m.ENetPacketPeer.STATE_CONNECTED: The peer is currently connected and ready to communicate with.
m.ENetPacketPeer.STATE_CONNECTING: The peer is currently attempting to connect.
m.ENetPacketPeer.STATE_CONNECTION_SUCCEEDE: The peer has successfully connected, but is not ready to communicate with yet (STATE_CONNECTED).
m.ENetPacketPeer.STATE_DISCONNECT_LATER: The peer is expected to disconnect after it has no more outgoing packets to send.
m.ENetPacketPeer.STATE_ZOMBIE: The peer has lost connection, but is not considered truly disconnected (as the peer didn't acknowledge the disconnection request).
m.ENetPacketPeer.get_channels: Returns the number of channels allocated for communication with peer.
m.ENetPacketPeer.get_packet_flags: Returns the ENet flags of the next packet in the received queue. See FLAG_* constants for available packet flags. Note that not all flags are replicated from the sending peer to the receiving peer.
m.ENetPacketPeer.get_remote_address: Returns the IP address of this peer.
m.ENetPacketPeer.get_remote_port: Returns the remote port of this peer.
m.ENetPacketPeer.get_statistic: Returns the requested statistic for this peer.
m.ENetPacketPeer.is_active: Returns true if the peer is currently active (i.e. the associated ENetConnection is still valid).
m.ENetPacketPeer.peer_disconnect: Request a disconnection from a peer. An ENetConnection.EVENT_DISCONNECT will be generated during ENetConnection.service() once the disconnection is complete.
m.ENetPacketPeer.peer_disconnect_later: Request a disconnection from a peer, but only after all queued outgoing packets are sent. An ENetConnection.EVENT_DISCONNECT will be generated during ENetConnection.service() once the disconnection is complete.
m.ENetPacketPeer.peer_disconnect_now: Force an immediate disconnection from a peer. No ENetConnection.EVENT_DISCONNECT will be generated. The foreign peer is not guaranteed to receive the disconnect notification, and is reset immediately upon return from this function.
m.ENetPacketPeer.ping: Sends a ping request to a peer. ENet automatically pings all connected peers at regular intervals, however, this function may be called to ensure more frequent ping requests.
m.ENetPacketPeer.ping_interval: Sets the ping_interval in milliseconds at which pings will be sent to a peer. Pings are used both to monitor the liveness of the connection and also to dynamically adjust the throttle during periods of low traffic so that the throttle has reasonable responsiveness during traffic spikes. The default ping interval is 500 milliseconds.
m.ENetPacketPeer.reset: Forcefully disconnects a peer. The foreign host represented by the peer is not notified of the disconnection and will timeout on its connection to the local host.
m.ENetPacketPeer.send: Queues a packet to be sent over the specified channel. See FLAG_* constants for available packet flags.
m.ENetPacketPeer.set_timeout: Sets the timeout parameters for a peer. The timeout parameters control how and when a peer will timeout from a failure to acknowledge reliable traffic. Timeout values are expressed in milliseconds.
m.ENetPacketPeer.throttle_configure: Configures throttle parameter for a peer.
m.EditorCommandPalette.add_command: Adds a custom command to EditorCommandPalette.
m.EditorCommandPalette.remove_command: Removes the custom command from EditorCommandPalette.
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.CONTEXT_SLOT_2D_: Context menu of 2D editor's basic right-click menu. _popup_menu() will be called with paths to all CanvasItem nodes under the cursor. You can fetch them using this code:
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.CONTEXT_SLOT_FIL: Context menu of FileSystem dock. _popup_menu() and option callback will be called with list of paths of the currently selected files.

The "Create..." submenu of FileSystem dock's context menu, or the "New" section of the main context menu when empty space is clicked. _popup_menu() and option callback will be called with the path of the currently selected folder. When clicking the empty space, the list of paths for popup method will be empty.
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.CONTEXT_SLOT_INS: Context menu of the inspectors right-click menu. _popup_menu() will be called with an array of two items: The first will be the object's ID, the second will be the property name. An object can be retrieved from it's ID via @GlobalScope.instance_from_id() after converting it to an int. The option callback will receive the EditorProperty directly.
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.CONTEXT_SLOT_SCE: Context menu of scene tabs. _popup_menu() will be called with the path of the clicked scene, or empty PackedStringArray if the menu was opened on empty space. The option callback will receive the path of the clicked scene, or empty String if none was clicked.
Context menu of Scene dock. _popup_menu() will be called with a list of paths to currently selected nodes, while option callback will receive the list of currently selected nodes.
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.CONTEXT_SLOT_SCR: Context menu of Script editor's script tabs. _popup_menu() will be called with the path to the currently edited script, while option callback will receive reference to that script.
Context menu of Script editor's code editor. _popup_menu() will be called with the path to the CodeEdit node. You can fetch it using this code:
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin._popup_menu: Called when creating a context menu, custom options can be added by using the add_context_menu_item() or add_context_menu_item_from_shortcut() functions. paths contains currently selected paths (depending on menu), which can be used to conditionally add options.
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.add_context_menu: Add custom option to the context menu of the plugin's specified slot. When the option is activated, callback will be called. Callback should take single Array argument; array contents depend on context menu slot.

Add custom option to the context menu of the plugin's specified slot. The option will have the shortcut assigned and reuse its callback. The shortcut has to be registered beforehand with add_menu_shortcut().
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.add_context_subm: Add a submenu to the context menu of the plugin's specified slot. The submenu is not automatically handled, you need to connect to its signals yourself. Also the submenu is freed on every popup, so provide a new PopupMenu every time.
m.EditorContextMenuPlugin.add_menu_shortcu: Registers a shortcut associated with the plugin's context menu. This method should be called once (e.g. in plugin's Object._init()). callback will be called when user presses the specified shortcut while the menu's context is in effect (e.g. FileSystem dock is focused). Callback should take single Array argument; array contents depend on context menu slot.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin._breakpoint_set_in_: Override this method to be notified when a breakpoint is set in the editor.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin._breakpoints_cleare: Override this method to be notified when all breakpoints are cleared in the editor.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin._capture: Override this method to process incoming messages. The session_id is the ID of the EditorDebuggerSession that received the message. Use get_session() to retrieve the session. This method should return true if the message is recognized.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin._goto_script_line: Override this method to be notified when a breakpoint line has been clicked in the debugger breakpoint panel.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin._has_capture: Override this method to enable receiving messages from the debugger. If capture is "my_message" then messages starting with "my_message:" will be passed to the _capture() method.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin._setup_session: Override this method to be notified whenever a new EditorDebuggerSession is created. Note that the session may be inactive during this stage.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin.get_session: Returns the EditorDebuggerSession with the given id.
m.EditorDebuggerPlugin.get_sessions: Returns an array of EditorDebuggerSession currently available to this debugger plugin.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.add_session_tab: Adds the given control to the debug session UI in the debugger bottom panel. The control's node name will be used as the tab title.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.breaked: Emitted when the attached remote instance enters a break state. If can_debug is true, the remote instance will enter the debug loop.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.continued: Emitted when the attached remote instance exits a break state.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.is_active: Returns true if the debug session is currently attached to a remote instance.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.is_breaked: Returns true if the attached remote instance is currently in the debug loop.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.is_debuggable: Returns true if the attached remote instance can be debugged.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.remove_session_tab: Removes the given control from the debug session UI in the debugger bottom panel.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.send_message: Sends the given message to the attached remote instance, optionally passing additionally data. See EngineDebugger for how to retrieve those messages.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.set_breakpoint: Enables or disables a specific breakpoint based on enabled, updating the Editor Breakpoint Panel accordingly.
m.EditorDebuggerSession.started: Emitted when a remote instance is attached to this session (i.e. the session becomes active).
m.EditorDebuggerSession.stopped: Emitted when a remote instance is detached from this session (i.e. the session becomes inactive).
m.EditorDebuggerSession.toggle_profiler: Toggle the given profiler on the attached remote instance, optionally passing additionally data. See EngineProfiler for more details.
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_BOTTOM_L: Dock slot at the bottom, below bottom panel, on the left side.
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_BOTTOM_R: Dock slot at the bottom, below bottom panel, on the right side.
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_BL: Dock slot, left side, bottom-left (empty in default layout).
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_BR: Dock slot, left side, bottom-right (in default layout includes FileSystem and History docks).
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_UL: Dock slot, left side, upper-left (empty in default layout).
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_UR: Dock slot, left side, upper-right (in default layout includes Scene and Import docks).
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_MAX: Represents the size of the DockSlot enum.
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_BL: Dock slot, right side, bottom-left (empty in default layout).
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_BR: Dock slot, right side, bottom-right (empty in default layout).
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_UL: Dock slot, right side, upper-left (in default layout includes Inspector, Signal, and Group docks).
m.EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_UR: Dock slot, right side, upper-right (empty in default layout).
m.EditorDock._load_layout_from_config: Implement this method to handle loading this dock's layout. It's equivalent to EditorPlugin._set_window_layout(). section is a unique section based on layout_key.
m.EditorDock._save_layout_to_config: Implement this method to handle saving this dock's layout. It's equivalent to EditorPlugin._get_window_layout(). section is a unique section based on layout_key.
m.EditorDock._update_layout: Implement this method to handle the layout switching for this dock. layout is one of the DockLayout constants.
m.EditorDock.available_layouts: The available layouts for this dock, as a bitmask. By default, the dock allows vertical and floating layouts.
m.EditorDock.closable: If true, the dock can be closed with the Close button in the context popup. Docks with global enabled are always closable.
m.EditorDock.close: Closes the dock, making its tab hidden.
m.EditorDock.closed: Emitted when the dock is closed with the Close button in the context popup, before it's removed from its parent. See closable.
m.EditorDock.default_slot: The default dock slot used when adding the dock with EditorPlugin.add_dock().
m.EditorDock.dock_icon: The icon for the dock, as a texture. If specified, it will override icon_name.
m.EditorDock.dock_shortcut: The shortcut used to open the dock.
m.EditorDock.force_show_icon: If true, the dock will always display an icon, regardless of EditorSettings.interface/editor/docks/dock_tab_style or EditorSettings.interface/editor/docks/bottom_dock_tab_style.
m.EditorDock.global: If true, the dock appears in the Editor > Editor Docks menu and can be closed. Non-global docks can still be closed using close() or when closable is true.
m.EditorDock.icon_name: The icon for the dock, as a name from the EditorIcons theme type in the editor theme. You can find the list of available icons here [https://godot-editor-icons.github.io/].
m.EditorDock.layout_key: The key representing this dock in the editor's layout file. If empty, the dock's displayed name will be used instead.
m.EditorDock.make_visible: Focuses the dock's tab (or window if it's floating). If the dock was closed, it will be opened. If it's a bottom dock, makes the bottom panel visible.
m.EditorDock.open: Opens the dock. It will appear in the last used dock slot. If the dock has no default slot, it will be opened floating.
m.EditorDock.opened: Emitted when the dock is opened via the Editor > Editor Docks menu, before it's made visible.
m.EditorDock.title: The title of the dock's tab. If empty, the dock's Node.name will be used. If the name is auto-generated (contains @), the first child's name will be used instead.
m.EditorDock.title_color: The color of the dock tab's title. If its alpha is 0.0, the default font color will be used.
m.EditorDock.transient: If true, the dock is not automatically opened or closed when loading an editor layout, only moved. It also can't be opened using a shortcut. This is meant for docks that are opened and closed in specific cases, such as when selecting a TileMap or AnimationTree node.
m.EditorExportPlatform.DEBUG_FLAG_DUMB_CLI: Flag is set if the remotely debugged project is expected to use the remote file system. If set, gen_export_flags() will append --remote-fs and --remote-fs-password (if EditorSettings.filesystem/file_server/password is defined) command line arguments to the returned list.
m.EditorExportPlatform.DEBUG_FLAG_REMOTE_D: Flag is set if remote debug is enabled. If set, gen_export_flags() will append --remote-debug and --breakpoints (if breakpoints are selected in the script editor or added by the plugin) command line arguments to the returned list.
Flag is set if remotely debugged project is running on the localhost. If set, gen_export_flags() will use localhost instead of EditorSettings.network/debug/remote_host as remote debugger host.
m.EditorExportPlatform.DEBUG_FLAG_VIEW_COL: Flag is set if the "Visible Collision Shapes" remote debug option is enabled. If set, gen_export_flags() will append the --debug-collisions command line argument to the returned list.
m.EditorExportPlatform.DEBUG_FLAG_VIEW_NAV: Flag is set if the "Visible Navigation" remote debug option is enabled. If set, gen_export_flags() will append the --debug-navigation command line argument to the returned list.
m.EditorExportPlatform.EXPORT_MESSAGE_ERRO: Message type for error messages that must be addressed and fail the export.
m.EditorExportPlatform.EXPORT_MESSAGE_INFO: Message type for informational messages that have no effect on the export.
m.EditorExportPlatform.EXPORT_MESSAGE_NONE: Invalid message type used as the default value when no type is specified.
m.EditorExportPlatform.EXPORT_MESSAGE_WARN: Message type for warning messages that should be addressed but still allow to complete the export.
m.EditorExportPlatform.add_message: Adds a message to the export log that will be displayed when exporting ends.
m.EditorExportPlatform.create_preset: Create a new preset for this platform.
m.EditorExportPlatform.export_pack: Creates a PCK archive at path for the specified preset.
m.EditorExportPlatform.export_pack_patch: Creates a patch PCK archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
m.EditorExportPlatform.export_project: Creates a full project at path for the specified preset. If notify is true, plugins using EditorExportPlugin._export_begin() will be called during the process.
m.EditorExportPlatform.export_project_file: Exports project files for the specified preset. This method can be used to implement custom export format, other than PCK and ZIP. One of the callbacks is called for each exported file.
m.EditorExportPlatform.export_zip: Create a ZIP archive at path for the specified preset.
m.EditorExportPlatform.export_zip_patch: Create a patch ZIP archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
m.EditorExportPlatform.find_export_templat: Locates export template for the platform, and returns Dictionary with the following keys: path: String and error: String. This method is provided for convenience and custom export platforms aren't required to use it or keep export templates stored in the same way official templates are.
m.EditorExportPlatform.gen_export_flags: Generates array of command line arguments for the default export templates for the debug flags and editor settings.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_current_presets: Returns array of EditorExportPresets for this platform.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_forced_export_f: Returns array of core file names that always should be exported regardless of preset config.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_internal_export: Returns additional files that should always be exported regardless of preset configuration, and are not part of the project source. The returned Dictionary contains filename keys (String) and their corresponding raw data (PackedByteArray).
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_message_categor: Returns the message category for the message with the given index.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_message_count: Returns the number of messages in the export log.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_message_text: Returns the text for the message with the given index.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_message_type: Returns the type for the message with the given index.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_os_name: Returns the name of the export operating system handled by this EditorExportPlatform class, as a friendly string. Possible return values are Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS, and Web.
m.EditorExportPlatform.get_worst_message_t: Returns most severe message type currently present in the export log.
m.EditorExportPlatform.save_pack: Saves PCK archive and returns Dictionary with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).
m.EditorExportPlatform.save_pack_patch: Saves patch PCK archive and returns Dictionary with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).
m.EditorExportPlatform.save_zip: Saves ZIP archive and returns Dictionary with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).
m.EditorExportPlatform.save_zip_patch: Saves patch ZIP archive and returns Dictionary with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).
m.EditorExportPlatform.ssh_push_to_remote: Uploads specified file over SCP protocol to the remote host.
m.EditorExportPlatform.ssh_run_on_remote: Executes specified command on the remote host via SSH protocol and returns command output in the output.
m.EditorExportPlatform.ssh_run_on_remote_n: Executes specified command on the remote host via SSH protocol and returns process ID (on the remote host) without waiting for command to finish.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._can_expor: Returns true if the specified preset is valid and can be exported. Use set_config_error() and set_config_missing_templates() to set error details.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._cleanup: Called by the editor before platform is unregistered.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._export_pa: Creates a PCK archive at path for the specified preset.
Creates a patch PCK archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._export_pr: Creates a full project at path for the specified preset.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._export_zi: Create a ZIP archive at path for the specified preset.
Create a ZIP archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_binar: Returns array of supported binary extensions for the full project export.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_debug: Returns protocol used for remote debugging. Default implementation return tcp://.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_devic: Returns device architecture for one-click deploy.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_expor: Validates option and returns visibility for the specified preset. Default implementation return true for all options.
Validates option and returns warning message for the specified preset. Default implementation return empty string for all options.
Returns a property list, as an Array of dictionaries. Each Dictionary must at least contain the name: StringName and type: Variant.Type entries.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_logo: Returns the platform logo displayed in the export dialog. The logo should be 32×32 pixels, adjusted for the current editor scale (see EditorInterface.get_editor_scale()).
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_optio: Returns the item icon for the specified device in the one-click deploy menu. The icon should be 16×16 pixels, adjusted for the current editor scale (see EditorInterface.get_editor_scale()).
Returns one-click deploy menu item label for the specified device.
Returns one-click deploy menu item tooltip for the specified device.
Returns the number of devices (or other options) available in the one-click deploy menu.
Returns tooltip of the one-click deploy menu button.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_platf: Returns array of platform specific features.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_prese: Returns array of platform specific features for the specified preset.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._get_run_i: Returns the icon of the one-click deploy menu button. The icon should be 16×16 pixels, adjusted for the current editor scale (see EditorInterface.get_editor_scale()).
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._has_valid: Returns true if export configuration is valid.
Returns true if project configuration is valid.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._initializ: Initializes the plugin. Called by the editor when platform is registered.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._is_execut: Returns true if specified file is a valid executable (native executable or script) for the target platform.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._poll_expo: Returns true if one-click deploy options are changed and editor interface should be updated.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._run: This method is called when device one-click deploy menu option is selected.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension._should_up: Returns true if export options list is changed and presets should be updated.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension.get_config: Returns current configuration error message text. This method should be called only from the _can_export(), _has_valid_export_configuration(), or _has_valid_project_configuration() implementations.

Returns true is export templates are missing from the current configuration. This method should be called only from the _can_export(), _has_valid_export_configuration(), or _has_valid_project_configuration() implementations.
m.EditorExportPlatformExtension.set_config: Sets current configuration error message text. This method should be called only from the _can_export(), _has_valid_export_configuration(), or _has_valid_project_configuration() implementations.

Set to true is export templates are missing from the current configuration. This method should be called only from the _can_export(), _has_valid_export_configuration(), or _has_valid_project_configuration() implementations.
m.EditorExportPlugin._begin_customize_reso: Return true if this plugin will customize resources based on the platform and features used.
m.EditorExportPlugin._begin_customize_scen: Return true if this plugin will customize scenes based on the platform and features used.
m.EditorExportPlugin._customize_resource: Customize a resource. If changes are made to it, return the same or a new resource. Otherwise, return null. When a new resource is returned, resource will be replaced by a copy of the new resource.
m.EditorExportPlugin._customize_scene: Customize a scene. If changes are made to it, return the same or a new scene. Otherwise, return null. If a new scene is returned, it is up to you to dispose of the old one.
m.EditorExportPlugin._end_customize_resour: This is called when the customization process for resources ends.
m.EditorExportPlugin._end_customize_scenes: This is called when the customization process for scenes ends.
m.EditorExportPlugin._end_generate_apple_e: This is called after Xcode project generation, but before it is built.
m.EditorExportPlugin._export_begin: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. It is called when the export starts and provides all information about the export. features is the list of features for the export, is_debug is true for debug builds, path is the target path for the exported project. flags is only used when running a runnable profile, e.g. when using native run on Android.
m.EditorExportPlugin._export_end: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. Called when the export is finished.
m.EditorExportPlugin._export_file: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. Called for each exported file before _customize_resource() and _customize_scene(). The arguments can be used to identify the file. path is the path of the file, type is the Resource represented by the file (e.g. PackedScene), and features is the list of features for the export.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_android_dependen: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is called to retrieve the set of Android dependencies provided by this plugin. Each returned Android dependency should have the format of an Android remote binary dependency: org.godot.example:my-plugin:0.0.0
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is called to retrieve the URLs of Maven repositories for the set of Android dependencies provided by this plugin.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_android_librarie: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is called to retrieve the local paths of the Android libraries archive (AAR) files provided by this plugin.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_android_manifest: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is used at export time to update the contents of the activity element in the generated Android manifest.
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is used at export time to update the contents of the application element in the generated Android manifest.
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is used at export time to update the contents of the manifest element in the generated Android manifest.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_customization_co: Return a hash based on the configuration passed (for both scenes and resources). This helps keep separate caches for separate export configurations.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_export_features: Return a PackedStringArray of additional features this preset, for the given platform, should have.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_export_option_vi: Validates option and returns the visibility for the specified platform. The default implementation returns true for all options.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_export_option_wa: Check the requirements for the given option and return a non-empty warning string if they are not met.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_export_options: Return a list of export options that can be configured for this export plugin.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_export_options_o: Return a Dictionary of override values for export options, that will be used instead of user-provided values. Overridden options will be hidden from the user interface.
m.EditorExportPlugin._get_name: Return the name identifier of this plugin (for future identification by the exporter). The plugins are sorted by name before exporting.
m.EditorExportPlugin._should_update_export: Return true if the result of _get_export_options() has changed and the export options of the preset corresponding to platform should be updated.
m.EditorExportPlugin._supports_platform: Return true if the plugin supports the given platform.
m.EditorExportPlugin._update_android_prebu: Provide access to the Android prebuilt manifest and allows the plugin to modify it if needed.
m.EditorExportPlugin.add_apple_embedded_pl: Adds an Apple embedded platform bundle file from the given path to the exported project.
Adds C++ code to the Apple embedded platform export. The final code is created from the code appended by each active export plugin.
Adds a dynamic library (*.dylib, *.framework) to the Linking Phase in the Apple embedded platform's Xcode project and embeds it into the resulting binary.
Adds a static library (*.a) or a dynamic library (*.dylib, *.framework) to the Linking Phase to the Apple embedded platform's Xcode project.
Adds linker flags for the Apple embedded platform export.
Adds additional fields to the Apple embedded platform's project Info.plist file.
Adds a static library from the given path to the Apple embedded platform project.
m.EditorExportPlugin.add_file: Adds a custom file to be exported. path is the virtual path that can be used to load the file, file is the binary data of the file.
m.EditorExportPlugin.add_macos_plugin_file: Adds file or directory matching path to PlugIns directory of macOS app bundle.
m.EditorExportPlugin.add_shared_object: Adds a shared object or a directory containing only shared objects with the given tags and destination path.
m.EditorExportPlugin.get_option: Returns the current value of an export option supplied by _get_export_options().
m.EditorExportPlugin.skip: To be called inside _export_file(). Skips the current file, so it's not included in the export.

m.EditorExportPreset.get_custom_features: Returns a comma-separated list of custom features added to this preset, as a string. See Feature tags in the documentation for more information.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_customized_files: Returns a dictionary of files selected in the "Resources" tab of the export dialog. The dictionary's keys are file paths, and its values are the corresponding export modes: "strip", "keep", or "remove". See also get_file_export_mode().
m.EditorExportPreset.get_customized_files_: Returns the number of files selected in the "Resources" tab of the export dialog.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_encrypt_directory: Returns true if PCK directory encryption is enabled in the export dialog.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_encrypt_pck: Returns true if PCK encryption is enabled in the export dialog.

m.EditorExportPreset.get_encryption_in_fil: Returns file filters to include during PCK encryption.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_exclude_filter: Returns file filters to exclude during export.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_export_filter: Returns export file filter mode selected in the "Resources" tab of the export dialog.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_file_export_mode: Returns file export mode for the specified file.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_files_to_export: Returns array of files to export.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_include_filter: Returns file filters to include during export.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_or_env: Returns export option value or value of environment variable if it is set.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_patches: Returns the list of packs on which to base a patch export on.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_project_setting: Returns the value of the setting identified by name using export preset feature tag overrides instead of current OS features.
m.EditorExportPreset.get_script_export_mod: Returns the export mode used by GDScript files. 0 for "Text", 1 for "Binary tokens", and 2 for "Compressed binary tokens (smaller files)".
