m.EditorExportPreset.has: Returns true if the preset has the property named property.
m.EditorExportPreset.has_export_file: Returns true if the file at the specified path will be exported.
m.EditorExportPreset.is_dedicated_server: Returns true if the dedicated server export mode is selected in the export dialog.
m.EditorExportPreset.is_runnable: Returns true if the "Runnable" toggle is enabled in the export dialog.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_3D: The 3D editor. If this feature is disabled, the 3D editor won't display but 3D nodes will still display in the Create New Node dialog.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_ASSET_LIB: The Asset Store tab. If this feature is disabled, the Asset Store tab won't display.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_FILESYSTEM_: The FileSystem dock. If this feature is disabled, the FileSystem dock won't be visible.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_GAME: The Game tab, which allows embedding the game window and selecting nodes by clicking inside of it. If this feature is disabled, the Game tab won't display.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_GROUPS_DOCK: The Groups dock. If this feature is disabled, groups won't be visible and modifiable from the editor.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_HISTORY_DOC: The History dock. If this feature is disabled, the History dock won't be visible.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_IMPORT_DOCK: The Import dock. If this feature is disabled, the Import dock won't be visible.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_MAX: Represents the size of the Feature enum.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_NODE_DOCK: Deprecated: Replaced by the Signals and Groups docks.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_SCENE_TREE: Scene tree editing. If this feature is disabled, the Scene tree dock will still be visible but will be read-only.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_SCRIPT: The Script tab, which contains the script editor and class reference browser. If this feature is disabled, the Script tab won't display.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.FEATURE_SIGNALS_DOC: The Signals dock. If this feature is disabled, signals won't be visible and modifiable from the editor.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.get_feature_name: Returns the specified feature's human-readable name.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.is_class_disabled: Returns true if the class specified by class_name is disabled. When disabled, the class won't appear in the Create New Node dialog.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.is_class_editor_dis: Returns true if editing for the class specified by class_name is disabled. When disabled, the class will still appear in the Create New Node dialog but the Inspector will be read-only when selecting a node that extends the class.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.is_class_property_d: Returns true if property is disabled in the class specified by class_name. When a property is disabled, it won't appear in the Inspector when selecting a node that extends the class specified by class_name.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.is_feature_disabled: Returns true if the feature is disabled. When a feature is disabled, it will disappear from the editor entirely.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.load_from_file: Loads an editor feature profile from a file. The file must follow the JSON format obtained by using the feature profile manager's Export button or the save_to_file() method.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.save_to_file: Saves the editor feature profile to a file in JSON format. It can then be imported using the feature profile manager's Import button or the load_from_file() method.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.set_disable_class: If disable is true, disables the class specified by class_name. When disabled, the class won't appear in the Create New Node dialog.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.set_disable_class_e: If disable is true, disables editing for the class specified by class_name. When disabled, the class will still appear in the Create New Node dialog but the Inspector will be read-only when selecting a node that extends the class.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.set_disable_class_p: If disable is true, disables editing for property in the class specified by class_name. When a property is disabled, it won't appear in the Inspector when selecting a node that extends the class specified by class_name.
m.EditorFeatureProfile.set_disable_feature: If disable is true, disables the editor feature specified in feature. When a feature is disabled, it will disappear from the editor entirely.
m.EditorFileDialog.add_side_menu: Deprecated: This feature is no longer supported.
m.EditorFileSystem.get_file_type: Returns the resource type of the file, given the full path. This returns a string such as "Resource" or "GDScript", not a file extension such as ".gd".
m.EditorFileSystem.get_filesystem_path: Returns a view into the filesystem at path.
m.EditorFileSystem.get_scanning_progress: Returns the scan progress for 0 to 1 if the FS is being scanned.
m.EditorFileSystem.is_importing: Returns true if resources are currently being imported.
m.EditorFileSystem.is_scanning: Returns true if the filesystem is being scanned.
m.EditorFileSystem.reimport_files: Reimports a set of files. Call this if these files or their .import files were directly edited by script or an external program.
m.EditorFileSystem.resources_reimported: Emitted if a resource is reimported.
m.EditorFileSystem.resources_reimporting: Emitted before a resource is reimported.
m.EditorFileSystem.resources_reload: Emitted if at least one resource is reloaded when the filesystem is scanned.
m.EditorFileSystem.scan_sources: Check if the source of any imported resource changed.
m.EditorFileSystem.script_classes_updated: Emitted when the list of global script classes gets updated.
m.EditorFileSystem.sources_changed: Emitted if the source of any imported file changed.
m.EditorFileSystem.update_file: Add a file in an existing directory, or schedule file information to be updated on editor restart. Can be used to update text files saved by an external program.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.find_dir_index: Returns the index of the directory with name name or -1 if not found.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.find_file_inde: Returns the index of the file with name name or -1 if not found.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_file: Returns the name of the file at index idx.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_file_count: Returns the number of files in this directory.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_file_impor: Returns true if the file at index idx imported properly.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_file_path: Returns the path to the file at index idx.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_file_scrip: Returns the base class of the script class defined in the file at index idx. If the file doesn't define a script class using the class_name syntax, this will return an empty string.
Returns the name of the script class defined in the file at index idx. If the file doesn't define a script class using the class_name syntax, this will return an empty string.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_file_type: Returns the resource type of the file at index idx. This returns a string such as "Resource" or "GDScript", not a file extension such as ".gd".
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_name: Returns the name of this directory.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_parent: Returns the parent directory for this directory or null if called on a directory at res:// or user://.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_path: Returns the path to this directory.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_subdir: Returns the subdirectory at index idx.
m.EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_subdir_cou: Returns the number of subdirectories in this directory.
m.EditorFileSystemImportFormatSupportQuery: Return whether this importer is active.
Query support. Return false if import must not continue.
m.EditorImportPlugin._can_import_threaded: Tells whether this importer can be run in parallel on threads, or, on the contrary, it's only safe for the editor to call it from the main thread, for one file at a time.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_format_version: Gets the format version of this importer. Increment this version when making incompatible changes to the format of the imported resources.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_import_options: Gets the options and default values for the preset at this index. Returns an Array of Dictionaries with the following keys: name, default_value, property_hint (optional), hint_string (optional), usage (optional).
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_import_order: Gets the order of this importer to be run when importing resources. Importers with lower import orders will be called first, and higher values will be called later. Use this to ensure the importer runs after the dependencies are already imported. The default import order is 0 unless overridden by a specific importer. See ImportOrder for some predefined values.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_importer_name: Gets the unique name of the importer.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_option_visibilit: Gets whether the import option specified by option_name should be visible in the Import dock. The default implementation always returns true, making all options visible. This is mainly useful for hiding options that depend on others if one of them is disabled.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_preset_count: Gets the number of initial presets defined by the plugin. Use _get_import_options() to get the default options for the preset and _get_preset_name() to get the name of the preset.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_preset_name: Gets the name of the options preset at this index.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_priority: Gets the priority of this plugin for the recognized extension. Higher priority plugins will be preferred. The default priority is 1.0.
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_recognized_exten: Gets the list of file extensions to associate with this loader (case-insensitive). e.g. ["obj"].
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_resource_type: Gets the Godot resource type associated with this loader. e.g. "Mesh" or "Animation".
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_save_extension: Gets the extension used to save this resource in the .godot/imported directory (see ProjectSettings.application/config/use_hidden_project_data_directory).
m.EditorImportPlugin._get_visible_name: Gets the name to display in the import window. You should choose this name as a continuation to "Import as", e.g. "Import as Special Mesh".
m.EditorImportPlugin._import: Imports source_file with the import options specified. Should return @GlobalScope.OK if the import is successful, other values indicate failure.
m.EditorImportPlugin.append_import_externa: This function can only be called during the _import() callback and it allows manually importing resources from it. This is useful when the imported file generates external resources that require importing (as example, images). Custom parameters for the ".import" file can be passed via the custom_options. Additionally, in cases where multiple importers can handle a file, the custom_importer can be…
m.EditorInspector.create_default_inspector: Creates an inspector with the same configuration as the one used in the editor's Inspector dock. When passing a LineEdit into filter_line_edit, the inspector will filter its properties based on LineEdit.text whenever LineEdit.text_changed is emitted.
m.EditorInspector.edit: Shows the properties of the given object in this inspector for editing. To clear the inspector, call this method with null.
m.EditorInspector.edited_object_changed: Emitted when the object being edited by the inspector has changed.
m.EditorInspector.expand_revertable: Expands only the foldable sections that contain a revertable (i.e. non-default) property.
m.EditorInspector.get_edited_object: Returns the object currently selected in this inspector.
m.EditorInspector.get_selected_path: Gets the path of the currently selected property.
m.EditorInspector.instantiate_property_edi: Creates a property editor that can be used by plugin UI to edit the specified property of an object.
m.EditorInspector.object_id_selected: Emitted when the Edit button of an Object has been pressed in the inspector. This is mainly used in the remote scene tree Inspector.
m.EditorInspector.property_deleted: Emitted when a property is removed from the inspector.
m.EditorInspector.property_edited: Emitted when a property is edited in the inspector.
m.EditorInspector.property_keyed: Emitted when a property is keyed in the inspector. Properties can be keyed by clicking the "key" icon next to a property when the Animation panel is toggled.
m.EditorInspector.property_selected: Emitted when a property is selected in the inspector.
m.EditorInspector.property_toggled: Emitted when a boolean property is toggled in the inspector.
m.EditorInspector.resource_selected: Emitted when a resource is selected in the inspector.
m.EditorInspector.restart_requested: Emitted when a property that requires a restart to be applied is edited in the inspector. This is only used in the Project Settings and Editor Settings.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin._can_handle: Returns true if this object can be handled by this plugin.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin._parse_begin: Called to allow adding controls at the beginning of the property list for object.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin._parse_category: Called to allow adding controls at the beginning of a category in the property list for object.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin._parse_end: Called to allow adding controls at the end of the property list for object.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin._parse_group: Called to allow adding controls at the beginning of a group or a sub-group in the property list for object.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin._parse_property: Called to allow adding property-specific editors to the property list for object. The added editor control must extend EditorProperty. Returning true removes the built-in editor for this property, otherwise allows to insert a custom editor before the built-in one.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin.add_custom_control: Adds a custom control, which is not necessarily a property editor.
m.EditorInspectorPlugin.add_property_edito: Adds a property editor for an individual property. The editor control must extend EditorProperty.
Adds an editor that allows modifying multiple properties. The editor control must extend EditorProperty.
m.EditorInterface.add_root_node: Makes node root of the currently opened scene. Only works if the scene is empty. If the node is a scene instance, an inheriting scene will be created.
m.EditorInterface.close_scene: Closes the currently active scene, discarding any pending changes in the process. Returns @GlobalScope.OK on success or @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST if there is no scene to close.
m.EditorInterface.distraction_free_mode: If true, enables distraction-free mode which hides side docks to increase the space available for the main view.
m.EditorInterface.edit_node: Edits the given Node. The node will be also selected if it's inside the scene tree.
m.EditorInterface.edit_resource: Edits the given Resource. If the resource is a Script you can also edit it with edit_script() to specify the line and column position.
m.EditorInterface.edit_script: Edits the given Script. The line and column on which to open the script can also be specified. The script will be open with the user-configured editor for the script's language which may be an external editor.
m.EditorInterface.get_base_control: Returns the main container of Godot editor's window. For example, you can use it to retrieve the size of the container and place your controls accordingly.
m.EditorInterface.get_current_directory: Returns the current directory being viewed in the FileSystemDock. If a file is selected, its base directory will be returned using String.get_base_dir() instead.
m.EditorInterface.get_current_feature_prof: Returns the name of the currently activated feature profile. If the default profile is currently active, an empty string is returned instead.
m.EditorInterface.get_current_path: Returns the current path being viewed in the FileSystemDock.
m.EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root: Returns the edited (current) scene's root Node.
m.EditorInterface.get_editor_language: Returns the language currently used for the editor interface.
m.EditorInterface.get_editor_main_screen: Returns the editor control responsible for main screen plugins and tools. Use it with plugins that implement EditorPlugin._has_main_screen().
m.EditorInterface.get_editor_scale: Returns the actual scale of the editor UI (1.0 being 100% scale). This can be used to adjust position and dimensions of the UI added by plugins.
m.EditorInterface.get_editor_viewport_2d: Returns the 2D editor SubViewport. It does not have a camera. Instead, the view transforms are done directly and can be accessed with Viewport.global_canvas_transform.
m.EditorInterface.get_editor_viewport_3d: Returns the specified 3D editor SubViewport, from 0 to 3. The viewport can be used to access the active editor cameras with Viewport.get_camera_3d().
m.EditorInterface.get_node_3d_rotate_snap: Returns the amount of degrees the 3D editor's rotational snapping is set to.
m.EditorInterface.get_node_3d_scale_snap: Returns the amount of units the 3D editor's scale snapping is set to.
m.EditorInterface.get_node_3d_translate_sn: Returns the amount of units the 3D editor's translation snapping is set to.
m.EditorInterface.get_open_scene_roots: Returns an array with references to the root nodes of the currently opened scenes.
m.EditorInterface.get_open_scenes: Returns an array with the file paths of the currently opened scenes.
m.EditorInterface.get_playing_scene: Returns the name of the scene that is being played. If no scene is currently being played, returns an empty string.
m.EditorInterface.get_selected_paths: Returns an array containing the paths of the currently selected files (and directories) in the FileSystemDock.
m.EditorInterface.get_unsaved_scenes: Returns an array of file paths of currently unsaved scenes.
m.EditorInterface.inspect_object: Shows the given property on the given object in the editor's Inspector dock. If inspector_only is true, plugins will not attempt to edit object.
m.EditorInterface.is_multi_window_enabled: Returns true if multiple window support is enabled in the editor. Multiple window support is enabled if all of these statements are true:
m.EditorInterface.is_node_3d_snap_enabled: Returns true if the 3D editor currently has snapping mode enabled, and false otherwise.
m.EditorInterface.is_object_edited: Returns true if the object has been marked as edited through set_object_edited().
m.EditorInterface.is_playing_scene: Returns true if a scene is currently being played, false otherwise. Paused scenes are considered as being played.
m.EditorInterface.is_plugin_enabled: Returns true if the specified plugin is enabled. The plugin name is the same as its directory name.
m.EditorInterface.make_mesh_previews: Returns mesh previews rendered at the given size as an Array of Texture2Ds.
m.EditorInterface.mark_scene_as_unsaved: Marks the current scene tab as unsaved.
m.EditorInterface.movie_maker_enabled: If true, the Movie Maker mode is enabled in the editor. See MovieWriter for more information.
m.EditorInterface.open_scene_from_path: Opens the scene at the given path. If set_inherited is true, creates a new inherited scene.
m.EditorInterface.play_custom_scene: Plays the scene specified by its filepath.
m.EditorInterface.popup_create_dialog: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.EditorInterface.popup_dialog: Pops up the dialog in the editor UI with Window.popup_exclusive(). The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
m.EditorInterface.popup_dialog_centered: Pops up the dialog in the editor UI with Window.popup_exclusive_centered(). The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
m.EditorInterface.popup_dialog_centered_cl: Pops up the dialog in the editor UI with Window.popup_exclusive_centered_clamped(). The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
m.EditorInterface.popup_dialog_centered_ra: Pops up the dialog in the editor UI with Window.popup_exclusive_centered_ratio(). The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
m.EditorInterface.popup_method_selector: Pops up an editor dialog for selecting a method from object. The callback must take a single argument of type String which will contain the name of the selected method or be empty if the dialog is canceled. If current_value is provided, the method will be selected automatically in the method list, if it exists.
m.EditorInterface.popup_node_selector: Pops up an editor dialog for selecting a Node from the edited scene. The callback must take a single argument of type NodePath. It is called on the selected NodePath or the empty path ^"" if the dialog is canceled. If valid_types is provided, the dialog will only show Nodes that match one of the listed Node types. If current_value is provided, the Node will be automatically selected in the tree,…
m.EditorInterface.popup_property_selector: Pops up an editor dialog for selecting properties from object. The callback must take a single argument of type NodePath. It is called on the selected property path (see NodePath.get_as_property_path()) or the empty path ^"" if the dialog is canceled. If type_filter is provided, the dialog will only show properties that match one of the listed Variant.Type values. If current_value is provided, th…
m.EditorInterface.popup_quick_open: Pops up an editor dialog for quick selecting a resource file. The callback must take a single argument of type String which will contain the path of the selected resource or be empty if the dialog is canceled. If base_types is provided, the dialog will only show resources that match these types. Only types deriving from Resource are supported.
m.EditorInterface.reload_scene_from_path: Reloads the scene at the given path. Fails if the scene is not open.
m.EditorInterface.restart_editor: Restarts the editor. This closes the editor and then opens the same project. If save is true, the project will be saved before restarting.
m.EditorInterface.save_all_scenes: Saves all opened scenes in the editor.
m.EditorInterface.save_scene: Saves the currently active scene. Returns either @GlobalScope.OK or @GlobalScope.ERR_CANT_CREATE.
m.EditorInterface.save_scene_as: Saves the currently active scene as a file at path.
m.EditorInterface.select_file: Selects the file, with the path provided by file, in the FileSystem dock.
m.EditorInterface.set_current_feature_prof: Selects and activates the specified feature profile with the given profile_name. Set profile_name to an empty string to reset to the default feature profile.
m.EditorInterface.set_main_screen_editor: Sets the editor's current main screen to the one specified in name. name must match the title of the tab in question exactly (e.g. 2D, 3D, Script, Game, or Asset Store for default tabs).
m.EditorInterface.set_object_edited: If edited is true, the object is marked as edited.
m.EditorInterface.set_plugin_enabled: Sets the enabled status of a plugin. The plugin name is the same as its directory name.
m.EditorInterface.stop_playing_scene: Stops the scene that is currently playing.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._begin_handle_action: There is currently no description for this method. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._commit_handle: Override this method to commit a handle being edited (handles must have been previously added by add_handles()). This usually means creating an UndoRedo action for the change, using the current handle value as "do" and the restore argument as "undo".
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._commit_subgizmos: Override this method to commit a group of subgizmos being edited (see _subgizmos_intersect_ray() and _subgizmos_intersect_frustum()). This usually means creating an UndoRedo action for the change, using the current transforms as "do" and the restores transforms as "undo".
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._get_handle_name: Override this method to return the name of an edited handle (handles must have been previously added by add_handles()). Handles can be named for reference to the user when editing.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._get_handle_value: Override this method to return the current value of a handle. This value will be requested at the start of an edit and used as the restore argument in _commit_handle().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._get_subgizmo_transfor: Override this method to return the current transform of a subgizmo. This transform will be requested at the start of an edit and used as the restore argument in _commit_subgizmos().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._is_handle_highlighted: Override this method to return true whenever the given handle should be highlighted in the editor.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._redraw: Override this method to add all the gizmo elements whenever a gizmo update is requested. It's common to call clear() at the beginning of this method and then add visual elements depending on the node's properties.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._set_handle: Override this method to update the node properties when the user drags a gizmo handle (previously added with add_handles()). The provided point is the mouse position in screen coordinates and the camera can be used to convert it to raycasts.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._set_subgizmo_transfor: Override this method to update the node properties during subgizmo editing (see _subgizmos_intersect_ray() and _subgizmos_intersect_frustum()). The transform is given in the Node3D's local coordinate system.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._subgizmos_intersect_f: Override this method to allow selecting subgizmos using mouse drag box selection. Given a camera and a frustum, this method should return which subgizmos are contained within the frustum. The frustum argument consists of an array with all the Planes that make up the selection frustum. The returned value should contain a list of unique subgizmo identifiers, which can have any non-negative value an…
m.EditorNode3DGizmo._subgizmos_intersect_r: Override this method to allow selecting subgizmos using mouse clicks. Given a camera and a point in screen coordinates, this method should return which subgizmo should be selected. The returned value should be a unique subgizmo identifier, which can have any non-negative value and will be used in other virtual methods like _get_subgizmo_transform() or _commit_subgizmos().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.add_collision_segments: Adds the specified segments to the gizmo's collision shape for picking. Call this method during _redraw().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.add_collision_triangle: Adds collision triangles to the gizmo for picking. A TriangleMesh can be generated from a regular Mesh too. Call this method during _redraw().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.add_handles: Adds a list of handles (points) which can be used to edit the properties of the gizmo's Node3D. The ids argument can be used to specify a custom identifier for each handle, if an empty array is passed, the ids will be assigned automatically from the handles argument order.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.add_lines: Adds lines to the gizmo (as sets of 2 points), with a given material. The lines are used for visualizing the gizmo. Call this method during _redraw().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.add_mesh: Adds a mesh to the gizmo with the specified material, local transform and skeleton. Call this method during _redraw().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.add_unscaled_billboard: Adds an unscaled billboard for visualization and selection. Call this method during _redraw().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.clear: Removes everything in the gizmo including meshes, collisions and handles.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.get_node_3d: Returns the Node3D node associated with this gizmo.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.get_plugin: Returns the EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin that owns this gizmo. It's useful to retrieve materials using EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin.get_material().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.get_subgizmo_selection: Returns a list of the currently selected subgizmos. Can be used to highlight selected elements during _redraw().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.is_subgizmo_selected: Returns true if the given subgizmo is currently selected. Can be used to highlight selected elements during _redraw().
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.set_hidden: Sets the gizmo's hidden state. If true, the gizmo will be hidden. If false, it will be shown.
m.EditorNode3DGizmo.set_node_3d: Sets the reference Node3D node for the gizmo. node must inherit from Node3D.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._begin_handle_ac: There is currently no description for this method. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._can_be_hidden: Override this method to define whether the gizmos handled by this plugin can be hidden or not. Returns true if not overridden.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._can_commit_hand: Override this method to define whether the gizmos should commit when the final handle position is the same as the initial one. Returns false if not overridden.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._commit_handle: Override this method to commit a handle being edited (handles must have been previously added by EditorNode3DGizmo.add_handles() during _redraw()). This usually means creating an UndoRedo action for the change, using the current handle value as "do" and the restore argument as "undo".
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._commit_subgizmo: Override this method to commit a group of subgizmos being edited (see _subgizmos_intersect_ray() and _subgizmos_intersect_frustum()). This usually means creating an UndoRedo action for the change, using the current transforms as "do" and the restores transforms as "undo".
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._create_gizmo: Override this method to return a custom EditorNode3DGizmo for the 3D nodes of your choice, return null for the rest of nodes. See also _has_gizmo().
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._get_gizmo_name: Override this method to provide the name that will appear in the gizmo visibility menu.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._get_handle_name: Override this method to provide gizmo's handle names. The secondary argument is true when the requested handle is secondary (see EditorNode3DGizmo.add_handles() for more information). Called for this plugin's active gizmos.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._get_handle_valu: Override this method to return the current value of a handle. This value will be requested at the start of an edit and used as the restore argument in _commit_handle().
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._get_priority: Override this method to set the gizmo's priority. Gizmos with higher priority will have precedence when processing inputs like handles or subgizmos selection.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._get_subgizmo_tr: Override this method to return the current transform of a subgizmo. As with all subgizmo methods, the transform should be in local space respect to the gizmo's Node3D. This transform will be requested at the start of an edit and used in the restore argument in _commit_subgizmos(). Called for this plugin's active gizmos.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._has_gizmo: Override this method to define which Node3D nodes have a gizmo from this plugin. Whenever a Node3D node is added to a scene this method is called, if it returns true the node gets a generic EditorNode3DGizmo assigned and is added to this plugin's list of active gizmos.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._is_handle_highl: Override this method to return true whenever to given handle should be highlighted in the editor. The secondary argument is true when the requested handle is secondary (see EditorNode3DGizmo.add_handles() for more information). Called for this plugin's active gizmos.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._is_selectable_w: Override this method to define whether Node3D with this gizmo should be selectable even when the gizmo is hidden.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._redraw: Override this method to add all the gizmo elements whenever a gizmo update is requested. It's common to call EditorNode3DGizmo.clear() at the beginning of this method and then add visual elements depending on the node's properties.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._set_handle: Override this method to update the node's properties when the user drags a gizmo handle (previously added with EditorNode3DGizmo.add_handles()). The provided screen_pos is the mouse position in screen coordinates and the camera can be used to convert it to raycasts.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._set_subgizmo_tr: Override this method to update the node properties during subgizmo editing (see _subgizmos_intersect_ray() and _subgizmos_intersect_frustum()). The transform is given in the Node3D's local coordinate system. Called for this plugin's active gizmos.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin._subgizmos_inter: Override this method to allow selecting subgizmos using mouse drag box selection. Given a camera and frustum_planes, this method should return which subgizmos are contained within the frustums. The frustum_planes argument consists of an array with all the Planes that make up the selection frustum. The returned value should contain a list of unique subgizmo identifiers, these identifiers can have…

Called for this plu…
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin.add_material: Adds a new material to the internal material list for the plugin. It can then be accessed with get_material(). Should not be overridden.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin.create_handle_ma: Creates a handle material with its variants (selected and/or editable) and adds them to the internal material list. They can then be accessed with get_material() and used in EditorNode3DGizmo.add_handles(). Should not be overridden.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin.create_icon_mate: Creates an icon material with its variants (selected and/or editable) and adds them to the internal material list. They can then be accessed with get_material() and used in EditorNode3DGizmo.add_unscaled_billboard(). Should not be overridden.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin.create_material: Creates an unshaded material with its variants (selected and/or editable) and adds them to the internal material list. They can then be accessed with get_material() and used in EditorNode3DGizmo.add_mesh() and EditorNode3DGizmo.add_lines(). Should not be overridden.
m.EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin.get_material: Gets material from the internal list of materials. If an EditorNode3DGizmo is provided, it will try to get the corresponding variant (selected and/or editable).
m.EditorPaths.get_cache_dir: Returns the absolute path to the user's cache folder. This folder should be used for temporary data that can be removed safely whenever the editor is closed (such as generated resource thumbnails).
m.EditorPaths.get_config_dir: Returns the absolute path to the user's configuration folder. This folder should be used for persistent user configuration files.
m.EditorPaths.get_data_dir: Returns the absolute path to the user's data folder. This folder should be used for persistent user data files such as installed export templates.
m.EditorPaths.get_project_settings_dir: Returns the relative path to the editor settings for this project. This is usually "res://.godot/editor". Projects all have a unique subdirectory inside the settings path where project-specific editor settings are saved.
m.EditorPaths.get_self_contained_file: Returns the absolute path to the self-contained file that makes the current Godot editor instance be considered as self-contained. Returns an empty string if the current Godot editor instance isn't self-contained. See also is_self_contained().
m.EditorPaths.is_self_contained: Returns true if the editor is marked as self-contained, false otherwise. When self-contained mode is enabled, user configuration, data and cache files are saved in an editor_data/ folder next to the editor binary. This makes portable usage easier and ensures the Godot editor minimizes file writes outside its own folder. Self-contained mode is not available for exported projects.
m.EditorPlugin.AFTER_GUI_INPUT_CUSTOM: Pass the InputEvent to other editor plugins except the main Node3D one. This can be used to prevent node selection changes and work with sub-gizmos instead.
m.EditorPlugin.AFTER_GUI_INPUT_PASS: Forwards the InputEvent to other EditorPlugins.
m.EditorPlugin.AFTER_GUI_INPUT_STOP: Prevents the InputEvent from reaching other Editor classes.
m.EditorPlugin.CONTAINER_CANVAS_EDITOR_MEN: The toolbar that appears when 2D editor is active.
m.EditorPlugin.CONTAINER_PROJECT_SETTING_T: Tab of Project Settings dialog, to the left of other tabs.
Tab of Project Settings dialog, to the right of other tabs.
m.EditorPlugin.CONTAINER_SPATIAL_EDITOR_ME: The toolbar that appears when 3D editor is active.
m.EditorPlugin.CONTAINER_TOOLBAR: Main editor toolbar, next to play buttons.
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_BL: Dock slot, left side, bottom-left (empty in default layout).
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_BR: Dock slot, left side, bottom-right (in default layout includes FileSystem dock).
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_UL: Dock slot, left side, upper-left (empty in default layout).
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_UR: Dock slot, left side, upper-right (in default layout includes Scene and Import docks).
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_MAX: Represents the size of the DockSlot enum.
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_BL: Dock slot, right side, bottom-left (empty in default layout).
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_BR: Dock slot, right side, bottom-right (empty in default layout).
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_UL: Dock slot, right side, upper-left (in default layout includes Inspector, Node, and History docks).
m.EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_UR: Dock slot, right side, upper-right (empty in default layout).
m.EditorPlugin._apply_changes: This method is called when the editor is about to save the project, switch to another tab, etc. It asks the plugin to apply any pending state changes to ensure consistency.
m.EditorPlugin._build: This method is called when the editor is about to run the project. The plugin can then perform required operations before the project runs.
m.EditorPlugin._clear: Clear all the state and reset the object being edited to zero. This ensures your plugin does not keep editing a currently existing node, or a node from the wrong scene.
m.EditorPlugin._disable_plugin: Called by the engine when the user disables the EditorPlugin in the Plugin tab of the project settings window.
m.EditorPlugin._edit: This function is used for plugins that edit specific object types (nodes or resources). It requests the editor to edit the given object.
m.EditorPlugin._enable_plugin: Called by the engine when the user enables the EditorPlugin in the Plugin tab of the project settings window.
m.EditorPlugin._forward_3d_draw_over_viewp: Called by the engine when the 3D editor's viewport is updated. viewport_control is an overlay on top of the viewport and it can be used for drawing. You can update the viewport manually by calling update_overlays().
m.EditorPlugin._forward_3d_force_draw_over: This method is the same as _forward_3d_draw_over_viewport(), except it draws on top of everything. Useful when you need an extra layer that shows over anything else.
m.EditorPlugin._forward_3d_gui_input: Called when there is a root node in the current edited scene, _handles() is implemented, and an InputEvent happens in the 3D viewport. The return value decides whether the InputEvent is consumed or forwarded to other EditorPlugins. See AfterGUIInput for options.
m.EditorPlugin._forward_canvas_draw_over_v: Called by the engine when the 2D editor's viewport is updated. viewport_control is an overlay on top of the viewport and it can be used for drawing. You can update the viewport manually by calling update_overlays().
m.EditorPlugin._forward_canvas_force_draw_: This method is the same as _forward_canvas_draw_over_viewport(), except it draws on top of everything. Useful when you need an extra layer that shows over anything else.
m.EditorPlugin._forward_canvas_gui_input: Called when there is a root node in the current edited scene, _handles() is implemented, and an InputEvent happens in the 2D viewport. If this method returns true, event is intercepted by this EditorPlugin, otherwise event is forwarded to other Editor classes.
m.EditorPlugin._get_breakpoints: This is for editors that edit script-based objects. You can return a list of breakpoints in the format (script:line), for example: res://path_to_script.gd:25.
m.EditorPlugin._get_plugin_icon: Override this method in your plugin to return a Texture2D in order to give it an icon.
m.EditorPlugin._get_plugin_name: Override this method in your plugin to provide the name of the plugin when displayed in the Godot editor.
m.EditorPlugin._get_state: Override this method to provide a state data you want to be saved, like view position, grid settings, folding, etc. This is used when saving the scene (so state is kept when opening it again) and for switching tabs (so state can be restored when the tab returns). This data is automatically saved for each scene in an editstate file in the editor metadata folder. If you want to store global (scene-…
m.EditorPlugin._get_unsaved_status: Override this method to provide a custom message that lists unsaved changes. The editor will call this method when exiting or when closing a scene, and display the returned string in a confirmation dialog. Return empty string if the plugin has no unsaved changes.
m.EditorPlugin._get_window_layout: Override this method to provide the GUI layout of the plugin or any other data you want to be stored. This is used to save the project's editor layout when queue_save_layout() is called or the editor layout was changed (for example changing the position of a dock). The data is stored in the editor_layout.cfg file in the editor metadata directory.
m.EditorPlugin._handles: Implement this function if your plugin edits a specific type of object (Resource or Node). If you return true, then you will get the functions _edit() and _make_visible() called when the editor requests them. If you have declared the methods _forward_canvas_gui_input() and _forward_3d_gui_input() these will be called too.
m.EditorPlugin._has_main_screen: Returns true if this is a main screen editor plugin (it goes in the workspace selector together with 2D, 3D, Script, Game, and Asset Store).
m.EditorPlugin._make_visible: This function will be called when the editor is requested to become visible. It is used for plugins that edit a specific object type.
m.EditorPlugin._run_scene: This function is called when an individual scene is about to be played in the editor. args is a list of command line arguments that will be passed to the new Godot instance, which will be replaced by the list returned by this function.
m.EditorPlugin._save_external_data: This method is called after the editor saves the project or when it's closed. It asks the plugin to save edited external scenes/resources.
m.EditorPlugin._set_state: Restore the state saved by _get_state(). This method is called when the current scene tab is changed in the editor.
m.EditorPlugin._set_window_layout: Restore the plugin GUI layout and data saved by _get_window_layout(). This method is called for every plugin on editor startup. Use the provided configuration file to read your saved data.
m.EditorPlugin.add_autoload_singleton: Adds a script at path to the Autoload list as name.
m.EditorPlugin.add_context_menu_plugin: Adds a plugin to the context menu. slot is the context menu where the plugin will be added.
m.EditorPlugin.add_control_to_bottom_panel: Deprecated: Use add_dock() instead, with EditorDock.default_slot set to DOCK_SLOT_BOTTOM.
m.EditorPlugin.add_control_to_container: Adds a custom control to a container in the editor UI.
m.EditorPlugin.add_custom_type: Adds a custom type, which will appear in the list of nodes or resources.
m.EditorPlugin.add_debugger_plugin: Adds a Script as debugger plugin to the Debugger. The script must extend EditorDebuggerPlugin.
m.EditorPlugin.add_export_platform: Registers a new EditorExportPlatform. Export platforms provides functionality of exporting to the specific platform.
m.EditorPlugin.add_export_plugin: Registers a new EditorExportPlugin. Export plugins are used to perform tasks when the project is being exported.
m.EditorPlugin.add_import_plugin: Registers a new EditorImportPlugin. Import plugins are used to import custom and unsupported assets as a custom Resource type.
m.EditorPlugin.add_inspector_plugin: Registers a new EditorInspectorPlugin. Inspector plugins are used to extend EditorInspector and provide custom configuration tools for your object's properties.
m.EditorPlugin.add_node_3d_gizmo_plugin: Registers a new EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin. Gizmo plugins are used to add custom gizmos to the 3D preview viewport for a Node3D.
m.EditorPlugin.add_resource_conversion_plu: Registers a new EditorResourceConversionPlugin. Resource conversion plugins are used to add custom resource converters to the editor inspector.
m.EditorPlugin.add_scene_format_importer_p: Registers a new EditorSceneFormatImporter. Scene importers are used to import custom 3D asset formats as scenes.
m.EditorPlugin.add_scene_post_import_plugi: Add an EditorScenePostImportPlugin. These plugins allow customizing the import process of 3D assets by adding new options to the import dialogs.
m.EditorPlugin.add_tool_menu_item: Adds a custom menu item to Project > Tools named name. When clicked, the provided callable will be called.
m.EditorPlugin.add_tool_submenu_item: Adds a custom PopupMenu submenu under Project > Tools > name. Use remove_tool_menu_item() on plugin clean up to remove the menu.
m.EditorPlugin.add_translation_parser_plug: Registers a custom translation parser plugin for extracting translatable strings from custom files.
m.EditorPlugin.add_undo_redo_inspector_hoo: Hooks a callback into the undo/redo action creation when a property is modified in the inspector. This allows, for example, to save other properties that may be lost when a given property is modified.
m.EditorPlugin.get_editor_interface: Deprecated: EditorInterface is a global singleton and can be accessed directly by its name.
m.EditorPlugin.get_export_as_menu: Returns the PopupMenu under Scene > Export As....
m.EditorPlugin.get_plugin_version: Provide the version of the plugin declared in the plugin.cfg config file.
m.EditorPlugin.get_script_create_dialog: Gets the Editor's dialog used for making scripts.
m.EditorPlugin.get_undo_redo: Gets the undo/redo object. Most actions in the editor can be undoable, so use this object to make sure this happens when it's worth it.
m.EditorPlugin.main_screen_changed: Emitted when user changes the workspace (2D, 3D, Script, Game, Asset Store). Also works with custom screens defined by plugins.
m.EditorPlugin.make_bottom_panel_item_visi: Makes a specific item in the bottom panel visible.
m.EditorPlugin.queue_save_layout: Queue save the project's editor layout.
m.EditorPlugin.remove_autoload_singleton: Removes an Autoload name from the list.
m.EditorPlugin.remove_context_menu_plugin: Removes the specified context menu plugin.
m.EditorPlugin.remove_control_from_contain: Removes the control from the specified container. You have to manually Node.queue_free() the control.
m.EditorPlugin.remove_custom_type: Removes a custom type added by add_custom_type().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_debugger_plugin: Removes the debugger plugin with given script from the Debugger.
m.EditorPlugin.remove_dock: Removes dock from the available docks. You should manually call Node.queue_free() to free it.
m.EditorPlugin.remove_export_platform: Removes an export platform registered by add_export_platform().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_export_plugin: Removes an export plugin registered by add_export_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_import_plugin: Removes an import plugin registered by add_import_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_inspector_plugin: Removes an inspector plugin registered by add_inspector_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_node_3d_gizmo_plugin: Removes a gizmo plugin registered by add_node_3d_gizmo_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_resource_conversion_: Removes a resource conversion plugin registered by add_resource_conversion_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_scene_format_importe: Removes a scene format importer registered by add_scene_format_importer_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_scene_post_import_pl: Remove the EditorScenePostImportPlugin, added with add_scene_post_import_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_tool_menu_item: Removes a menu name from Project > Tools.
m.EditorPlugin.remove_translation_parser_p: Removes a custom translation parser plugin registered by add_translation_parser_plugin().
m.EditorPlugin.remove_undo_redo_inspector_: Removes a callback previously added by add_undo_redo_inspector_hook_callback().
m.EditorPlugin.resource_saved: Emitted when the given resource was saved on disc. See also scene_saved.
m.EditorPlugin.scene_changed: Emitted when the scene is changed in the editor. The argument will return the root node of the scene that has just become active. If this scene is new and empty, the argument will be null.
m.EditorPlugin.scene_closed: Emitted when user closes a scene. The argument is a file path to the closed scene.
m.EditorPlugin.scene_saved: Emitted when a scene was saved on disc. The argument is a file path to the saved scene. See also resource_saved.
m.EditorPlugin.set_force_draw_over_forward: Enables calling of _forward_canvas_force_draw_over_viewport() for the 2D editor and _forward_3d_force_draw_over_viewport() for the 3D editor when their viewports are updated. You need to call this method only once and it will work permanently for this plugin.
m.EditorPlugin.set_input_event_forwarding_: Use this method if you always want to receive inputs from 3D view screen inside _forward_3d_gui_input(). It might be especially usable if your plugin will want to use raycast in the scene.
m.EditorPlugin.update_overlays: Updates the overlays of the 2D and 3D editor viewport. Causes methods _forward_canvas_draw_over_viewport(), _forward_canvas_force_draw_over_viewport(), _forward_3d_draw_over_viewport() and _forward_3d_force_draw_over_viewport() to be called.
m.EditorProperty._set_read_only: Called when the read-only status of the property is changed. It may be used to change custom controls into a read-only or modifiable state.
m.EditorProperty._update_property: When this virtual function is called, you must update your editor.
m.EditorProperty.add_focusable: If any of the controls added can gain keyboard focus, add it here. This ensures that focus will be restored if the inspector is refreshed.
m.EditorProperty.checkable: Used by the inspector, set to true when the property is checkable.

m.EditorProperty.property_deleted: Emitted when a property was deleted. Used internally.
m.EditorProperty.property_favorited: Emit it if you want to mark a property as favorited, making it appear at the top of the inspector.
m.EditorProperty.property_keyed: Emit it if you want to add this value as an animation key (check for keying being enabled first).
m.EditorProperty.property_keyed_with_value: Emit it if you want to key a property with a single value.
m.EditorProperty.property_overridden: Emitted when a setting override for the current project is requested.
m.EditorProperty.property_pinned: Emit it if you want to mark (or unmark) the value of a property for being saved regardless of being equal to the default value.
m.EditorProperty.read_only: Used by the inspector, set to true when the property is read-only.
m.EditorProperty.resource_selected: If you want a sub-resource to be edited, emit this signal with the resource.
m.EditorProperty.select: Draw property as selected. Used by the inspector.
m.EditorProperty.selectable: Used by the inspector, set to true when the property is selectable.

m.EditorProperty.set_label_reference: Used by the inspector, set to a control that will be used as a reference to calculate the size of the label.
m.EditorProperty.set_object_and_property: Assigns object and property to edit.
m.EditorProperty.update_property: Forces a refresh of the property display.
m.EditorProperty.use_folding: Used by the inspector, set to true when the property is using folding.

m.EditorSettings.set_setting: Sets the value of the setting specified by name. This is equivalent to using Object.set() on the EditorSettings instance.
m.EditorSettings.settings_changed: Emitted after any editor setting has changed.

m.EditorTranslationParserPlugin._parse_fil: Override this method to define a custom parsing logic to extract the translatable strings.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.GLOBAL_HISTORY: Global history not associated with any scene, but with external resources etc.

m.EditorUndoRedoManager.REMOTE_HISTORY: History associated with remote inspector. Used when live editing a running project.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.add_do_method: Register a method that will be called when the action is committed (i.e. the "do" action).
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.add_do_property: Register a property value change for "do".
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.add_do_reference: Register a reference for "do" that will be erased if the "do" history is lost. This is useful mostly for new nodes created for the "do" call. Do not use for resources.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.add_undo_method: Register a method that will be called when the action is undone (i.e. the "undo" action).
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.add_undo_property: Register a property value change for "undo".
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.add_undo_reference: Register a reference for "undo" that will be erased if the "undo" history is lost. This is useful mostly for nodes removed with the "do" call (not the "undo" call!).
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.clear_history: Clears the given undo history. You can clear history for a specific scene, global history, or for all histories at once (except REMOTE_HISTORY) if id is INVALID_HISTORY.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.commit_action: Commits the action. If execute is true (default), all "do" methods/properties are called/set when this function is called.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.create_action: Create a new action. After this is called, do all your calls to add_do_method(), add_undo_method(), add_do_property(), and add_undo_property(), then commit the action with commit_action().
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.force_fixed_histor: Forces the next operation (e.g. add_do_method()) to use the action's history rather than guessing it from the object. This is sometimes needed when a history can't be correctly determined, like for a nested resource that doesn't have a path yet.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.get_history_undo_r: Returns the UndoRedo object associated with the given history id.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.get_object_history: Returns the history ID deduced from the given object. It can be used with get_history_undo_redo().
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.history_changed: Emitted when the list of actions in any history has changed, either when an action is committed or a history is cleared.
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.is_committing_acti: Returns true if the EditorUndoRedoManager is currently committing the action, i.e. running its "do" method or property change (see commit_action()).
m.EditorUndoRedoManager.version_changed: Emitted when the version of any history has changed as a result of undo or redo call.

m.EditorVCSInterface._allow_amends: Returns whether or not the plugin allows commit amends.

m.EditorVCSInterface._discard_file: Discards the changes made in a file present at file_path.
m.EditorVCSInterface._fetch: Fetches new changes from the remote, but doesn't write changes to the current working directory. Equivalent to git fetch.
m.EditorVCSInterface._get_branch_list: Gets an instance of an Array of Strings containing available branch names in the VCS.
m.EditorVCSInterface._get_current_branch_n: Gets the current branch name defined in the VCS.
m.EditorVCSInterface._get_diff: Returns an array of Dictionary items (see create_diff_file(), create_diff_hunk(), create_diff_line(), add_line_diffs_into_diff_hunk() and add_diff_hunks_into_diff_file()), each containing information about a diff. m.EditorVCSInterface._get_remotes: Returns an Array of Strings, each containing the name of a remote configured in the VCS.
m.EditorVCSInterface._get_vcs_name: Returns the name of the underlying VCS provider.

m.EditorVCSInterface._pull: Pulls changes from the remote. This can give rise to merge conflicts.

m.EditorVCSInterface._remove_branch: Remove a branch from the local VCS.
m.EditorVCSInterface._remove_remote: Remove a remote from the local VCS.

m.EditorVCSInterface._unstage_file: Unstages the file present at file_path from the staged area to the unstaged area.

m.EditorVCSInterface.create_status_file: Helper function to create a Dictionary used by editor to read the status of a file.

m.Engine.capture_script_backtraces: Captures and returns backtraces from all registered script languages.

m.Engine.get_frames_per_second: Returns the average frames rendered every second (FPS), also known as the framerate.

m.Engine.get_license_text: Returns the full Godot license text.

m.Engine.get_script_language_count: Returns the number of available script languages. Use with get_script_language().
