m.Engine.get_singleton_list: Returns a list of names of all available global singletons. See also get_singleton().
m.Engine.get_version_info: Returns the current engine version information as a Dictionary containing the following entries:
m.Engine.get_write_movie_path: Returns the path to the MovieWriter's output file, or an empty string if the engine wasn't started in Movie Maker mode. The default path can be changed in ProjectSettings.editor/movie_writer/movie_file.
m.Engine.has_singleton: Returns true if a singleton with the given name exists in the global scope. See also get_singleton().
m.Engine.is_editor_hint: Returns true if the script is currently running inside the editor, otherwise returns false. This is useful for @tool scripts to conditionally draw editor helpers, or prevent accidentally running "game" code that would affect the scene state while in the editor:
m.Engine.is_embedded_in_editor: Returns true if the engine is running embedded in the editor. This is useful to prevent attempting to update window mode or window flags that are not supported when running the project embedded in the editor.
m.Engine.is_in_physics_frame: Returns true if the engine is inside the fixed physics process step of the main loop.
m.Engine.max_fps: The maximum number of frames that can be rendered every second (FPS). A value of 0 means the framerate is uncapped.
m.Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame: The maximum number of physics steps that can be simulated each rendered frame.
m.Engine.physics_jitter_fix: How much physics ticks are synchronized with real time. If 0 or less, the ticks are fully synchronized. Higher values cause the in-game clock to deviate more from the real clock, but they smooth out framerate jitters.
m.Engine.physics_ticks_per_second: The number of fixed iterations per second. This controls how often physics simulation and the Node._physics_process() method are run.
m.Engine.print_error_messages: If false, stops printing error and warning messages to the console and editor Output log. This can be used to hide error and warning messages during unit test suite runs. This property is equivalent to the ProjectSettings.application/run/disable_stderr project setting.
m.Engine.print_to_stdout: If false, stops printing messages (for example using @GlobalScope.print()) to the console, log files, and editor Output log. This property is equivalent to the ProjectSettings.application/run/disable_stdout project setting.
m.Engine.register_script_language: Registers a ScriptLanguage instance to be available with ScriptServer.
m.Engine.register_singleton: Registers the given Object instance as a singleton, available globally under name. Useful for plugins.
m.Engine.time_scale: The speed multiplier at which the in-game clock updates, compared to real time. For example, if set to 2.0 the game runs twice as fast, and if set to 0.5 the game runs half as fast.
m.Engine.unregister_script_language: Unregisters the ScriptLanguage instance from ScriptServer.
m.Engine.unregister_singleton: Removes the singleton registered under name. The singleton object is not freed. Only works with user-defined singletons registered with register_singleton().
m.EngineDebugger.debug: Starts a debug break in script execution, optionally specifying whether the program can continue based on can_continue and whether the break was due to a breakpoint.
m.EngineDebugger.get_depth: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.EngineDebugger.get_lines_left: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.EngineDebugger.has_capture: Returns true if a capture with the given name is present otherwise false.
m.EngineDebugger.has_profiler: Returns true if a profiler with the given name is present otherwise false.
m.EngineDebugger.insert_breakpoint: Inserts a new breakpoint with the given source and line.
m.EngineDebugger.is_active: Returns true if the debugger is active otherwise false.
m.EngineDebugger.is_breakpoint: Returns true if the given source and line represent an existing breakpoint.
m.EngineDebugger.is_profiling: Returns true if a profiler with the given name is present and active otherwise false.
m.EngineDebugger.is_skipping_breakpoints: Returns true if the debugger is skipping breakpoints otherwise false.
m.EngineDebugger.line_poll: Forces a processing loop of debugger events. The purpose of this method is just processing events every now and then when the script might get too busy, so that bugs like infinite loops can be caught.
m.EngineDebugger.profiler_add_frame_data: Calls the add callable of the profiler with given name and data.
m.EngineDebugger.profiler_enable: Calls the toggle callable of the profiler with given name and arguments. Enables/Disables the same profiler depending on enable argument.
m.EngineDebugger.register_message_capture: Registers a message capture with given name. If name is "my_message" then messages starting with "my_message:" will be called with the given callable.
m.EngineDebugger.register_profiler: Registers a profiler with the given name. See EngineProfiler for more information.
m.EngineDebugger.remove_breakpoint: Removes a breakpoint with the given source and line.
m.EngineDebugger.script_debug: Starts a debug break in script execution, optionally specifying whether the program can continue based on can_continue and whether the break was due to a breakpoint.
m.EngineDebugger.send_message: Sends a message with given message and data array.
m.EngineDebugger.set_depth: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.EngineDebugger.set_lines_left: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.EngineDebugger.unregister_message_captur: Unregisters the message capture with given name.
m.EngineDebugger.unregister_profiler: Unregisters a profiler with given name.
m.EngineProfiler._add_frame: Called when data is added to profiler using EngineDebugger.profiler_add_frame_data().
m.EngineProfiler._tick: Called once every engine iteration when the profiler is active with information about the current frame. All time values are in seconds. Lower values represent faster processing times and are therefore considered better.
m.EngineProfiler._toggle: Called when the profiler is enabled/disabled, along with a set of options.
m.Environment.AMBIENT_SOURCE_BG: Gather ambient light from whichever source is specified as the background.
m.Environment.AMBIENT_SOURCE_COLOR: Specify a specific Color for ambient light. This provides a slight performance boost over AMBIENT_SOURCE_SKY.
m.Environment.AMBIENT_SOURCE_DISABLED: Disable ambient light. This provides a slight performance boost over AMBIENT_SOURCE_SKY.
m.Environment.AMBIENT_SOURCE_SKY: Gather ambient light from the Sky regardless of what the background is.
m.Environment.BG_CAMERA_FEED: Displays a camera feed in the background.
m.Environment.BG_CANVAS: Displays a CanvasLayer in the background.
m.Environment.BG_CLEAR_COLOR: Clears the background using the clear color defined in ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color.
m.Environment.BG_COLOR: Clears the background using a custom clear color.
m.Environment.BG_KEEP: Keeps on screen every pixel drawn in the background. This is the fastest background mode, but it can only be safely used in fully-interior scenes (no visible sky or sky reflections). If enabled in a scene where the background is visible, "ghost trail" artifacts will be visible when moving the camera.
m.Environment.BG_MAX: Represents the size of the BGMode enum.
m.Environment.BG_SKY: Displays a user-defined sky in the background.
m.Environment.FOG_MODE_DEPTH: Use a simple fog model defined by start and end positions and a custom curve. While not physically accurate, this model can be useful when you need more artistic control.
m.Environment.FOG_MODE_EXPONENTIAL: Use a physically-based fog model defined primarily by fog density.
m.Environment.GLOW_BLEND_MODE_ADDITIVE: Adds the glow effect to the scene.
m.Environment.GLOW_BLEND_MODE_MIX: Mixes the glow image with the scene image. Best used with glow_bloom to avoid darkening the scene.
m.Environment.GLOW_BLEND_MODE_REPLACE: Replaces all pixels' color by the glow effect. This can be used to simulate a full-screen blur effect by tweaking the glow parameters to match the original image's brightness or to preview glow configuration in the editor.
m.Environment.GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SCREEN: Adds the glow effect to the scene after modifying the glow influence based on the scene value; dark values will be highly influenced by glow and bright values will not be influenced by glow. This approach avoids bright values becoming overly bright from the glow effect. tonemap_white is used to determine the maximum scene value where the glow should have no influence. When tonemap_mode is set to…
m.Environment.GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SOFTLIGHT: Adds the glow effect to the tonemapped image after modifying the glow influence based on the image value; dark values and bright values will not be influenced by glow and mid-range values will be highly influenced by glow. This approach avoids bright values becoming overly bright from the glow effect. The glow will have the largest influence on image values of 0.25 and will have no influence when…
m.Environment.REFLECTION_SOURCE_DISABLED: Disable reflections. This provides a slight performance boost over other options.
m.Environment.REFLECTION_SOURCE_SKY: Use the Sky for reflections regardless of what the background is.
m.Environment.SDFGI_Y_SCALE_100_PERCENT: Use 100% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. SDFGI cells will be as tall as they are wide. This is usually the best choice for highly vertical scenes. The downside is that light leaking may become more noticeable with thin floors and ceilings.
m.Environment.SDFGI_Y_SCALE_50_PERCENT: Use 50% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. SDFGI cells will be twice as short as they are wide. This allows providing increased GI detail and reduced light leaking with thin floors and ceilings. This is usually the best choice for scenes that don't feature much verticality.
m.Environment.SDFGI_Y_SCALE_75_PERCENT: Use 75% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. This is a balance between the 50% and 100% SDFGI Y scales.
m.Environment.TONE_MAPPER_ACES: Uses a high-contrast film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Slightly slower than TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC.
m.Environment.TONE_MAPPER_AGX: Uses an adjustable film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Better than other tonemappers at maintaining the hue of colors as they become brighter. The slowest tonemapping option.
m.Environment.TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC: Uses a film-like tonemapping curve to prevent clipping of bright values and provide better contrast than TONE_MAPPER_REINHARDT. Slightly slower than TONE_MAPPER_REINHARDT.
m.Environment.TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR: Does not modify color data, resulting in a linear tonemapping curve which unnaturally clips bright values, causing bright lighting to look blown out. The simplest and fastest tonemapper.
m.Environment.TONE_MAPPER_REINHARDT: A simple tonemapping curve that rolls off bright values to prevent clipping. This results in an image that can appear dull and low contrast. Slower than TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR.
m.Environment.adjustment_brightness: Applies a simple brightness adjustment to the rendered image after tonemaping. To adjust scene brightness use tonemap_exposure instead, which is applied before tonemapping and thus less prone to issues with bright colors. Effective only if adjustment_enabled is true.
m.Environment.adjustment_color_correction: The Texture2D or Texture3D lookup table (LUT) to use for the built-in post-process color grading. Can use a GradientTexture1D for a 1-dimensional LUT, or a Texture3D for a more complex LUT. Effective only if adjustment_enabled is true.
m.Environment.adjustment_contrast: Increasing adjustment_contrast will make dark values darker and bright values brighter. This simple adjustment is applied to the rendered image after tonemaping. When set to a value greater than 1.0, adjustment_contrast is prone to clipping colors that become too bright or too dark. Effective only if adjustment_enabled is true.
m.Environment.adjustment_enabled: If true, enables the adjustment_* properties provided by this resource. If false, modifications to the adjustment_* properties will have no effect on the rendered scene.
m.Environment.adjustment_saturation: Applies a simple saturation adjustment to the rendered image after tonemaping. When adjustment_saturation is set to 0.0, the rendered image will be fully converted to a grayscale image. Effective only if adjustment_enabled is true.
m.Environment.ambient_light_color: The ambient light's Color. Only effective if ambient_light_sky_contribution is lower than 1.0 (exclusive).
m.Environment.ambient_light_energy: The ambient light's energy. The higher the value, the stronger the light. Only effective if ambient_light_sky_contribution is lower than 1.0 (exclusive).
m.Environment.ambient_light_sky_contributi: Defines the amount of light that the sky brings on the scene. A value of 0.0 means that the sky's light emission has no effect on the scene illumination, thus all ambient illumination is provided by the ambient light. On the contrary, a value of 1.0 means that all the light that affects the scene is provided by the sky, thus the ambient light parameter has no effect on the scene.
m.Environment.ambient_light_source: The ambient light source to use for rendering materials and global illumination.
m.Environment.background_camera_feed_id: The ID of the camera feed to show in the background.
m.Environment.background_canvas_max_layer: The maximum layer ID to display. Only effective when using the BG_CANVAS background mode.
m.Environment.background_color: The Color displayed for clear areas of the scene. Only effective when using the BG_COLOR background mode.
m.Environment.background_energy_multiplier: Multiplier for background energy. Increase to make background brighter, decrease to make background dimmer.
m.Environment.background_intensity: Luminance of background measured in nits (candela per square meter). Only used when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is enabled. The default value is roughly equivalent to the sky at midday.
m.Environment.fog_aerial_perspective: If set above 0.0 (exclusive), blends between the fog's color and the color of the background Sky, as read from the radiance cubemap. This has a small performance cost when set above 0.0. Must have background_mode set to BG_SKY.
m.Environment.fog_density: The fog density to be used. This is demonstrated in different ways depending on the fog_mode mode chosen:
m.Environment.fog_depth_begin: The fog's depth starting distance from the camera. Only available when fog_mode is set to FOG_MODE_DEPTH.
m.Environment.fog_depth_curve: The fog depth's intensity curve. A number of presets are available in the Inspector by right-clicking the curve. Only available when fog_mode is set to FOG_MODE_DEPTH.
m.Environment.fog_depth_end: The fog's depth end distance from the camera. If this value is set to 0, it will be equal to the current camera's Camera3D.far value. Only available when fog_mode is set to FOG_MODE_DEPTH.
m.Environment.fog_enabled: If true, fog effects are enabled.
m.Environment.fog_height: The height at which the height fog effect begins.
m.Environment.fog_height_density: The density used to increase fog as height decreases. To make fog increase as height increases, use a negative value.
m.Environment.fog_light_energy: The fog's brightness. Higher values result in brighter fog.
m.Environment.fog_sky_affect: The factor to use when affecting the sky with non-volumetric fog. 1.0 means that fog can fully obscure the sky. Lower values reduce the impact of fog on sky rendering, with 0.0 not affecting sky rendering at all.
m.Environment.fog_sun_scatter: If set above 0.0, renders the scene's directional light(s) in the fog color depending on the view angle. This can be used to give the impression that the sun is "piercing" through the fog.
m.Environment.get_glow_level: Returns the intensity of the glow level idx.
m.Environment.glow_bloom: The bloom's intensity. If set to a value higher than 0, this will make glow visible in areas darker than the glow_hdr_threshold.
m.Environment.glow_enabled: If true, the glow effect is enabled. This simulates real world atmosphere and eye/camera behavior by causing bright pixels to bleed onto surrounding pixels.
m.Environment.glow_hdr_luminance_cap: The higher threshold of the HDR glow. Areas brighter than this threshold will be clamped for the purposes of the glow effect.
m.Environment.glow_hdr_scale: Smooths the transition between values that are below and above glow_hdr_threshold by reducing the amount of glow generated by values that are close to glow_hdr_threshold. Values above glow_hdr_threshold + glow_hdr_scale will not have glow reduced in this way.
m.Environment.glow_hdr_threshold: The lower threshold of the HDR glow. When using the Mobile rendering method (which only supports a lower dynamic range up to 2.0), this may need to be below 1.0 for glow to be visible. A value of 0.9 works well in this case. This value also needs to be decreased below 1.0 when using glow in 2D, as 2D rendering is performed in SDR.
m.Environment.glow_intensity: The overall brightness multiplier that is applied to the glow effect just before it is blended with the scene. When using the Mobile rendering method (which only supports a lower dynamic range up to 2.0), this should be increased to 1.5 to compensate.
m.Environment.glow_map: The texture that should be used as a glow map to multiply the resulting glow color according to glow_map_strength. This can be used to create a "lens dirt" effect. The texture's RGB color channels are used for modulation, but the alpha channel is ignored.
m.Environment.glow_map_strength: How strong of an influence the glow_map should have on the overall glow effect. A strength of 0.0 means the glow map has no influence, while a strength of 1.0 means the glow map has full influence.
m.Environment.glow_mix: When using the GLOW_BLEND_MODE_MIX glow_blend_mode, this controls how much the source image is blended with the glow layer. A value of 0.0 makes the glow rendering invisible, while a value of 1.0 is equivalent to GLOW_BLEND_MODE_REPLACE.
m.Environment.glow_normalized: If true, glow levels will be normalized so that summed together their intensities equal 1.0.
m.Environment.glow_strength: The strength that is used when blurring across the screen to generate the glow effect. This affects the distance and intensity of the blur. When using the Mobile rendering method, this should be increased to compensate for the lower dynamic range.
m.Environment.sdfgi_bounce_feedback: The energy multiplier applied to light every time it bounces from a surface when using SDFGI. Values greater than 0.0 will simulate multiple bounces, resulting in a more realistic appearance. Increasing sdfgi_bounce_feedback generally has no performance impact. See also sdfgi_energy.
m.Environment.sdfgi_cascade0_distance: Note: This property is linked to sdfgi_min_cell_size and sdfgi_max_distance. Changing its value will automatically change those properties as well.
m.Environment.sdfgi_cascades: The number of cascades to use for SDFGI (between 1 and 8). A higher number of cascades allows displaying SDFGI further away while preserving detail up close, at the cost of performance. When using SDFGI on small-scale levels, sdfgi_cascades can often be decreased between 1 and 4 to improve performance.
m.Environment.sdfgi_enabled: If true, enables signed distance field global illumination for meshes that have their GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode set to GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_STATIC. SDFGI is a real-time global illumination technique that works well with procedurally generated and user-built levels, including in situations where geometry is created during gameplay. The signed distance field is automatically generated around…
m.Environment.sdfgi_energy: The energy multiplier to use for SDFGI. Higher values will result in brighter indirect lighting and reflections. See also sdfgi_bounce_feedback.
m.Environment.sdfgi_max_distance: The maximum distance at which SDFGI is visible. Beyond this distance, environment lighting or other sources of GI such as ReflectionProbe will be used as a fallback.
m.Environment.sdfgi_min_cell_size: The cell size to use for the closest SDFGI cascade (in 3D units). Lower values allow SDFGI to be more precise up close, at the cost of making SDFGI updates more demanding. This can cause stuttering when the camera moves fast. Higher values allow SDFGI to cover more ground, while also reducing the performance impact of SDFGI updates.
m.Environment.sdfgi_normal_bias: The normal bias to use for SDFGI probes. Increasing this value can reduce visible streaking artifacts on sloped surfaces, at the cost of increased light leaking.
m.Environment.sdfgi_probe_bias: The constant bias to use for SDFGI probes. Increasing this value can reduce visible streaking artifacts on sloped surfaces, at the cost of increased light leaking.
m.Environment.sdfgi_read_sky_light: If true, SDFGI takes the environment lighting into account. This should be set to false for interior scenes.
m.Environment.sdfgi_use_occlusion: If true, SDFGI uses an occlusion detection approach to reduce light leaking. Occlusion may however introduce dark blotches in certain spots, which may be undesired in mostly outdoor scenes. sdfgi_use_occlusion has a performance impact and should only be enabled when needed.
m.Environment.sdfgi_y_scale: The Y scale to use for SDFGI cells. Lower values will result in SDFGI cells being packed together more closely on the Y axis. This is used to balance between quality and covering a lot of vertical ground. sdfgi_y_scale should be set depending on how vertical your scene is (and how fast your camera may move on the Y axis).
m.Environment.set_glow_level: Sets the intensity of the glow level idx. A value above 0.0 enables the level. Each level relies on the previous level. This means that enabling higher glow levels will slow down the glow effect rendering, even if previous levels aren't enabled.
m.Environment.sky: The Sky resource used for this Environment.
m.Environment.sky_custom_fov: If set to a value greater than 0.0, overrides the field of view to use for sky rendering. If set to 0.0, the same FOV as the current Camera3D is used for sky rendering.
m.Environment.sky_rotation: The rotation to use for sky rendering.
m.Environment.ssao_ao_channel_affect: The screen-space ambient occlusion intensity on materials that have an AO texture defined. Values higher than 0 will make the SSAO effect visible in areas darkened by AO textures.
m.Environment.ssao_detail: Sets the strength of the additional level of detail for the screen-space ambient occlusion effect. A high value makes the detail pass more prominent, but it may contribute to aliasing in your final image.
m.Environment.ssao_enabled: If true, the screen-space ambient occlusion effect is enabled. This darkens objects' corners and cavities to simulate ambient light not reaching the entire object as in real life. This works well for small, dynamic objects, but baked lighting or ambient occlusion textures will do a better job at displaying ambient occlusion on large static objects. Godot uses a form of SSAO called Adaptive Screen…
m.Environment.ssao_horizon: The threshold for considering whether a given point on a surface is occluded or not represented as an angle from the horizon mapped into the 0.0-1.0 range. A value of 1.0 results in no occlusion.
m.Environment.ssao_intensity: The primary screen-space ambient occlusion intensity. Acts as a multiplier for the screen-space ambient occlusion effect. A higher value results in darker occlusion.
m.Environment.ssao_light_affect: The screen-space ambient occlusion intensity in direct light. In real life, ambient occlusion only applies to indirect light, which means its effects can't be seen in direct light. Values higher than 0 will make the SSAO effect visible in direct light.
m.Environment.ssao_power: The distribution of occlusion. A higher value results in darker occlusion, similar to ssao_intensity, but with a sharper falloff.
m.Environment.ssao_radius: The distance at which objects can occlude each other when calculating screen-space ambient occlusion. Higher values will result in occlusion over a greater distance at the cost of performance and quality.
m.Environment.ssao_sharpness: The amount that the screen-space ambient occlusion effect is allowed to blur over the edges of objects. Setting too high will result in aliasing around the edges of objects. Setting too low will make object edges appear blurry.
m.Environment.ssil_enabled: If true, the screen-space indirect lighting effect is enabled. Screen space indirect lighting is a form of indirect lighting that allows diffuse light to bounce between nearby objects. Screen-space indirect lighting works very similarly to screen-space ambient occlusion, in that it only affects a limited range. It is intended to be used along with a form of proper global illumination like SDFGI o…
m.Environment.ssil_intensity: The brightness multiplier for the screen-space indirect lighting effect. A higher value will result in brighter light.
m.Environment.ssil_normal_rejection: Amount of normal rejection used when calculating screen-space indirect lighting. Normal rejection uses the normal of a given sample point to reject samples that are facing away from the current pixel. Normal rejection is necessary to avoid light leaking when only one side of an object is illuminated. However, normal rejection can be disabled if light leaking is desirable, such as when the scene m…
m.Environment.ssil_radius: The distance that bounced lighting can travel when using the screen space indirect lighting effect. A larger value will result in light bouncing further in a scene, but may result in under-sampling artifacts which look like long spikes surrounding light sources.
m.Environment.ssil_sharpness: The amount that the screen-space indirect lighting effect is allowed to blur over the edges of objects. Setting too high will result in aliasing around the edges of objects. Setting too low will make object edges appear blurry.
m.Environment.ssr_depth_tolerance: The depth tolerance for screen-space reflections.
m.Environment.ssr_enabled: If true, screen-space reflections are enabled. Screen-space reflections are more accurate than reflections from VoxelGIs or ReflectionProbes, but are slower and can't reflect surfaces occluded by others.
m.Environment.ssr_fade_in: The fade-in distance for screen-space reflections. Affects the area from the reflected material to the screen-space reflection. Only positive values are valid (negative values will be clamped to 0.0).
m.Environment.ssr_fade_out: The fade-out distance for screen-space reflections. Affects the area from the screen-space reflection to the "global" reflection. Only positive values are valid (negative values will be clamped to 0.0).
m.Environment.ssr_max_steps: The maximum number of steps for screen-space reflections. Higher values are slower.
m.Environment.tonemap_agx_contrast: Increasing tonemap_agx_contrast will make dark values darker and bright values brighter. Produces a higher quality result than adjustment_contrast without any additional performance cost, but is only available when using the TONE_MAPPER_AGX tonemapper.
m.Environment.tonemap_agx_white: The white reference value for tonemapping, which indicates where bright white is located in the scale of values provided to the tonemapper. For photorealistic lighting, it is recommended to set tonemap_agx_white to at least 6.0. Higher values result in less blown out highlights, but may make the scene appear lower contrast. tonemap_agx_white is the same as tonemap_white, but is only effective wit…
m.Environment.tonemap_exposure: Adjusts the brightness of values before they are provided to the tonemapper. Higher tonemap_exposure values result in a brighter image. See also tonemap_white.
m.Environment.tonemap_mode: The tonemapping mode to use. Tonemapping is the process that "converts" HDR values to be suitable for rendering on an LDR display. (Godot doesn't support rendering on HDR displays yet.)
m.Environment.tonemap_white: The white reference value for tonemapping, which indicates where bright white is located in the scale of values provided to the tonemapper. For photorealistic lighting, it is recommended to set tonemap_white to at least 6.0. Higher values result in less blown out highlights, but may make the scene appear lower contrast. tonemap_agx_white will be used instead when using the TONE_MAPPER_AGX tonemap…
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_albedo: The Color of the volumetric fog when interacting with lights. Mist and fog have an albedo close to Color(1, 1, 1, 1) while smoke has a darker albedo.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_ambient_injec: Scales the strength of ambient light used in the volumetric fog. A value of 0.0 means that ambient light will not impact the volumetric fog. volumetric_fog_ambient_inject has a small performance cost when set above 0.0.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_anisotropy: The direction of scattered light as it goes through the volumetric fog. A value close to 1.0 means almost all light is scattered forward. A value close to 0.0 means light is scattered equally in all directions. A value close to -1.0 means light is scattered mostly backward. Fog and mist scatter light slightly forward, while smoke scatters light equally in all directions.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_density: The base exponential density of the volumetric fog. Set this to the lowest density you want to have globally. FogVolumes can be used to add to or subtract from this density in specific areas. Fog rendering is exponential as in real life.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_detail_spread: The distribution of size down the length of the froxel buffer. A higher value compresses the froxels closer to the camera and places more detail closer to the camera.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_emission: The emitted light from the volumetric fog. Even with emission, volumetric fog will not cast light onto other surfaces. Emission is useful to establish an ambient color. As the volumetric fog effect uses single-scattering only, fog tends to need a little bit of emission to soften the harsh shadows.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_emission_ener: The brightness of the emitted light from the volumetric fog.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_enabled: Enables the volumetric fog effect. Volumetric fog uses a screen-aligned froxel buffer to calculate accurate volumetric scattering in the short to medium range. Volumetric fog interacts with FogVolumes and lights to calculate localized and global fog. Volumetric fog uses a PBR single-scattering model based on extinction, scattering, and emission which it exposes to users as density, albedo, and em…
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_gi_inject: Scales the strength of Global Illumination used in the volumetric fog's albedo color. A value of 0.0 means that Global Illumination will not impact the volumetric fog. volumetric_fog_gi_inject has a small performance cost when set above 0.0.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_length: The distance over which the volumetric fog is computed. Increase to compute fog over a greater range, decrease to add more detail when a long range is not needed. For best quality fog, keep this as low as possible. See also ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/volumetric_fog/volume_depth.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_sky_affect: The factor to use when affecting the sky with volumetric fog. 1.0 means that volumetric fog can fully obscure the sky. Lower values reduce the impact of volumetric fog on sky rendering, with 0.0 not affecting sky rendering at all.
m.Environment.volumetric_fog_temporal_repr: The amount by which to blend the last frame with the current frame. A higher number results in smoother volumetric fog, but makes "ghosting" much worse. A lower value reduces ghosting but can result in the per-frame temporal jitter becoming visible.

Enables temporal reprojection in the volumetric fog. Temporal reprojection blends the current frame's volumetric fog with the last frame's volumetric fog to smooth out jagged edges. The performance cost is minimal; however, it leads to moving FogVolumes and Light3Ds "ghosting" and leaving a trail behind them. When temporal reprojection is enabled, try to avoid moving FogVolumes or Light3Ds too fa…
m.Expression.execute: Executes the expression that was previously parsed by parse() and returns the result. Before you use the returned object, you should check if the method failed by calling has_execute_failed().
m.Expression.get_error_text: Returns the error text if parse() or execute() has failed.
m.Expression.has_execute_failed: Returns true if execute() has failed.
m.Expression.parse: Parses the expression and returns an Error code.
m.FBXState.allow_geometry_helper_nodes: If true, the import process used auxiliary nodes called geometry helper nodes. These nodes help preserve the pivots and transformations of the original 3D model during import.
m.FastNoiseLite.DISTANCE_EUCLIDEAN: Euclidean distance to the nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.DISTANCE_EUCLIDEAN_SQUARED: Squared Euclidean distance to the nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.DISTANCE_HYBRID: Blend of DISTANCE_EUCLIDEAN and DISTANCE_MANHATTAN to give curved cell boundaries.
m.FastNoiseLite.DISTANCE_MANHATTAN: Manhattan distance (taxicab metric) to the nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.DOMAIN_WARP_BASIC_GRID: The domain is warped using a simple noise grid (not as smooth as the other methods, but more performant).
m.FastNoiseLite.DOMAIN_WARP_FRACTAL_INDEPE: Warping the space independently for each octave, resulting in a more chaotic distortion.
m.FastNoiseLite.DOMAIN_WARP_FRACTAL_NONE: No fractal noise for warping the space.
m.FastNoiseLite.DOMAIN_WARP_FRACTAL_PROGRE: Warping the space progressively, octave for octave, resulting in a more "liquified" distortion.
m.FastNoiseLite.DOMAIN_WARP_SIMPLEX: The domain is warped using the simplex noise algorithm.
m.FastNoiseLite.DOMAIN_WARP_SIMPLEX_REDUCE: The domain is warped using a simplified version of the simplex noise algorithm.
m.FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_FBM: Method using Fractional Brownian Motion to combine octaves into a fractal.
m.FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_PING_PONG: Method of combining octaves into a fractal with a ping pong effect.
m.FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_RIDGED: Method of combining octaves into a fractal resulting in a "ridged" look.
m.FastNoiseLite.RETURN_CELL_VALUE: The cellular distance function will return the same value for all points within a cell.
m.FastNoiseLite.RETURN_DISTANCE: The cellular distance function will return a value determined by the distance to the nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.RETURN_DISTANCE2: The cellular distance function returns the distance to the second-nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.RETURN_DISTANCE2_ADD: The distance to the nearest point is added to the distance to the second-nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.RETURN_DISTANCE2_DIV: The distance to the nearest point is divided by the distance to the second-nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.RETURN_DISTANCE2_MUL: The distance to the nearest point is multiplied with the distance to the second-nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.RETURN_DISTANCE2_SUB: The distance to the nearest point is subtracted from the distance to the second-nearest point.
m.FastNoiseLite.TYPE_CELLULAR: Cellular includes both Worley noise and Voronoi diagrams which creates various regions of the same value.
m.FastNoiseLite.TYPE_PERLIN: A lattice of random gradients. Their dot products are interpolated to obtain values in between the lattices.
m.FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX: As opposed to TYPE_PERLIN, gradients exist in a simplex lattice rather than a grid lattice, avoiding directional artifacts. Internally uses FastNoiseLite's OpenSimplex2 noise type.
m.FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH: Modified, higher quality version of TYPE_SIMPLEX, but slower. Internally uses FastNoiseLite's OpenSimplex2S noise type.
m.FastNoiseLite.TYPE_VALUE: A lattice of points are assigned random values then interpolated based on neighboring values.
m.FastNoiseLite.TYPE_VALUE_CUBIC: Similar to value noise (TYPE_VALUE), but slower. Has more variance in peaks and valleys.
m.FastNoiseLite.cellular_distance_function: Determines how the distance to the nearest/second-nearest point is computed.
m.FastNoiseLite.cellular_jitter: Maximum distance a point can move off of its grid position. Set to 0 for an even grid.
m.FastNoiseLite.cellular_return_type: Return type from cellular noise calculations.
m.FastNoiseLite.domain_warp_amplitude: Sets the maximum warp distance from the origin.
m.FastNoiseLite.domain_warp_enabled: If enabled, another FastNoiseLite instance is used to warp the space, resulting in a distortion of the noise.
m.FastNoiseLite.domain_warp_fractal_gain: Determines the strength of each subsequent layer of the noise which is used to warp the space.
m.FastNoiseLite.domain_warp_fractal_lacuna: The change in frequency between octaves, also known as "lacunarity", of the fractal noise which warps the space. Increasing this value results in higher octaves, producing noise with finer details and a rougher appearance.
m.FastNoiseLite.domain_warp_fractal_octave: The number of noise layers that are sampled to get the final value for the fractal noise which warps the space.
m.FastNoiseLite.domain_warp_fractal_type: The method for combining octaves into a fractal which is used to warp the space.
m.FastNoiseLite.domain_warp_frequency: Frequency of the noise which warps the space. Low frequency results in smooth noise while high frequency results in rougher, more granular noise.
m.FastNoiseLite.fractal_gain: Determines the strength of each subsequent layer of noise in fractal noise.
m.FastNoiseLite.fractal_lacunarity: Frequency multiplier between subsequent octaves. Increasing this value results in higher octaves producing noise with finer details and a rougher appearance.
m.FastNoiseLite.fractal_octaves: The number of noise layers that are sampled to get the final value for fractal noise types.
m.FastNoiseLite.fractal_ping_pong_strength: Sets the strength of the fractal ping pong type.
m.FastNoiseLite.fractal_type: The method for combining octaves into a fractal.
m.FastNoiseLite.fractal_weighted_strength: Higher weighting means higher octaves have less impact if lower octaves have a large impact.
m.FastNoiseLite.frequency: The frequency for all noise types. Low frequency results in smooth noise while high frequency results in rougher, more granular noise.
m.FastNoiseLite.offset: Translate the noise input coordinates by the given Vector3.
m.FastNoiseLite.seed: The random number seed for all noise types.
m.FileAccess.COMPRESSION_BROTLI: Uses the brotli [https://github.com/google/brotli] compression method (only decompression is supported).
m.FileAccess.READ: Opens the file for read operations. The file cursor is positioned at the beginning of the file.
m.FileAccess.READ_WRITE: Opens the file for read and write operations. Does not truncate the file. The file cursor is positioned at the beginning of the file.
m.FileAccess.UNIX_SET_GROUP_ID: Set group id on execution bit.
m.FileAccess.UNIX_SET_USER_ID: Set user id on execution bit.
m.FileAccess.WRITE: Opens the file for write operations. If the file exists, it is truncated to zero length and its contents are cleared. Otherwise, it is created.
m.FileAccess.WRITE_READ: Opens the file for read and write operations. If the file exists, it is truncated to zero length and its contents are cleared. Otherwise, it is created. The file cursor is positioned at the beginning of the file.
m.FileAccess.big_endian: If true, the file is read with big-endian endianness [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endianness]. If false, the file is read with little-endian endianness. If in doubt, leave this to false as most files are written with little-endian endianness.
m.FileAccess.close: Closes the currently opened file and prevents subsequent read/write operations. Use flush() to persist the data to disk without closing the file.
m.FileAccess.create_temp: Creates a temporary file. This file will be freed when the returned FileAccess is freed.
m.FileAccess.eof_reached: Returns true if the file cursor has already read past the end of the file.
m.FileAccess.file_exists: Returns true if the file exists in the given path.
m.FileAccess.flush: Writes the file's buffer to disk. Flushing is automatically performed when the file is closed. This means you don't need to call flush() manually before closing a file. Still, calling flush() can be used to ensure the data is safe even if the project crashes instead of being closed gracefully.
m.FileAccess.get_16: Returns the next 16 bits from the file as an integer. This advances the file cursor by 2 bytes. See store_16() for details on what values can be stored and retrieved this way.
m.FileAccess.get_32: Returns the next 32 bits from the file as an integer. This advances the file cursor by 4 bytes. See store_32() for details on what values can be stored and retrieved this way.
m.FileAccess.get_64: Returns the next 64 bits from the file as an integer. This advances the file cursor by 8 bytes. See store_64() for details on what values can be stored and retrieved this way.
m.FileAccess.get_8: Returns the next 8 bits from the file as an integer. This advances the file cursor by 1 byte. See store_8() for details on what values can be stored and retrieved this way.
m.FileAccess.get_access_time: Returns the last time the file was accessed in Unix timestamp format, or 0 on error. This Unix timestamp can be converted to another format using the Time singleton.
m.FileAccess.get_as_text: Returns the whole file as a String. Text is interpreted as being UTF-8 encoded. This ignores the file cursor and does not affect it.
m.FileAccess.get_buffer: Returns next length bytes of the file as a PackedByteArray. This advances the file cursor by length bytes.
m.FileAccess.get_csv_line: Returns the next value of the file in CSV (Comma-Separated Values) format. You can pass a different delimiter delim to use other than the default "," (comma). This delimiter must be one-character long, and cannot be a double quotation mark.
m.FileAccess.get_double: Returns the next 64 bits from the file as a floating-point number. This advances the file cursor by 8 bytes.
m.FileAccess.get_error: Returns the last error that happened when trying to perform operations. Compare with the ERR_FILE_* constants from Error.
m.FileAccess.get_extended_attribute: Reads the file extended attribute with name attribute_name as a byte array.
m.FileAccess.get_extended_attribute_string: Reads the file extended attribute with name attribute_name as a UTF-8 encoded string.
m.FileAccess.get_extended_attributes_list: Returns a list of file extended attributes.
m.FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes: Returns the whole path file contents as a PackedByteArray without any decoding.
m.FileAccess.get_file_as_string: Returns the whole path file contents as a String. Text is interpreted as being UTF-8 encoded.
m.FileAccess.get_float: Returns the next 32 bits from the file as a floating-point number. This advances the file cursor by 4 bytes.
m.FileAccess.get_half: Returns the next 16 bits from the file as a half-precision floating-point number. This advances the file cursor by 2 bytes.
m.FileAccess.get_hidden_attribute: Returns true if the hidden attribute is set on the file at the given path.
m.FileAccess.get_length: Returns the size of the file in bytes. For a pipe, returns the number of bytes available for reading from the pipe.
m.FileAccess.get_line: Returns the next line of the file as a String. The returned string doesn't include newline (\n) or carriage return (\r) characters, but does include any other leading or trailing whitespace. This advances the file cursor to after the newline character at the end of the line.
m.FileAccess.get_md5: Returns an MD5 String representing the file at the given path or an empty String on failure.
m.FileAccess.get_modified_time: Returns the last time the file was modified in Unix timestamp format, or 0 on error. This Unix timestamp can be converted to another format using the Time singleton.
m.FileAccess.get_open_error: Returns the result of the last open() call in the current thread.
m.FileAccess.get_pascal_string: Returns a String saved in Pascal format from the file, meaning that the length of the string is explicitly stored at the start. See store_pascal_string(). This may include newline characters. The file cursor is advanced after the bytes read.
m.FileAccess.get_path: Returns the path as a String for the current open file.
m.FileAccess.get_path_absolute: Returns the absolute path as a String for the current open file.
m.FileAccess.get_position: Returns the file cursor's position in bytes from the beginning of the file. This is the file reading/writing cursor set by seek() or seek_end() and advanced by read/write operations.
m.FileAccess.get_read_only_attribute: Returns true if the read only attribute is set on the file at the given path.
m.FileAccess.get_real: Returns the next bits from the file as a floating-point number. This advances the file cursor by either 4 or 8 bytes, depending on the precision used by the Godot build that saved the file.
m.FileAccess.get_sha256: Returns an SHA-256 String representing the file at the given path or an empty String on failure.
m.FileAccess.get_size: Returns the size of the file at the given path, in bytes, or -1 on error.
m.FileAccess.get_unix_permissions: Returns the UNIX permissions of the file at the given path.
m.FileAccess.get_var: Returns the next Variant value from the file. If allow_objects is true, decoding objects is allowed. This advances the file cursor by the number of bytes read.
m.FileAccess.is_open: Returns true if the file is currently opened.
m.FileAccess.open: Creates a new FileAccess object and opens the file for writing or reading, depending on the flags.
m.FileAccess.open_compressed: Creates a new FileAccess object and opens a compressed file for reading or writing.
m.FileAccess.open_encrypted: Creates a new FileAccess object and opens an encrypted file in write or read mode. You need to pass a binary key to encrypt/decrypt it.
m.FileAccess.open_encrypted_with_pass: Creates a new FileAccess object and opens an encrypted file in write or read mode. You need to pass a password to encrypt/decrypt it.
m.FileAccess.remove_extended_attribute: Removes file extended attribute with name attribute_name.
m.FileAccess.resize: Resizes the file to a specified length. The file must be open in a mode that permits writing. If the file is extended, NUL characters are appended. If the file is truncated, all data from the end file to the original length of the file is lost.
m.FileAccess.seek: Sets the file cursor to the specified position in bytes, from the beginning of the file. This changes the value returned by get_position().
m.FileAccess.seek_end: Sets the file cursor to the specified position in bytes, from the end of the file. This changes the value returned by get_position().
m.FileAccess.set_extended_attribute: Writes file extended attribute with name attribute_name as a byte array.
m.FileAccess.set_extended_attribute_string: Writes file extended attribute with name attribute_name as a UTF-8 encoded string.
m.FileAccess.store_16: Stores an integer as 16 bits in the file. This advances the file cursor by 2 bytes. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_32: Stores an integer as 32 bits in the file. This advances the file cursor by 4 bytes. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_64: Stores an integer as 64 bits in the file. This advances the file cursor by 8 bytes. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_8: Stores an integer as 8 bits in the file. This advances the file cursor by 1 byte. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_buffer: Stores the given array of bytes in the file. This advances the file cursor by the number of bytes written. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_csv_line: Stores the given PackedStringArray in the file as a line formatted in the CSV (Comma-Separated Values) format. You can pass a different delimiter delim to use other than the default "," (comma). This delimiter must be one-character long.
m.FileAccess.store_double: Stores a floating-point number as 64 bits in the file. This advances the file cursor by 8 bytes. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_float: Stores a floating-point number as 32 bits in the file. This advances the file cursor by 4 bytes. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_half: Stores a half-precision floating-point number as 16 bits in the file. This advances the file cursor by 2 bytes. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_line: Stores line in the file followed by a newline character (\n), encoding the text as UTF-8. This advances the file cursor by the length of the line, after the newline character. The amount of bytes written depends on the UTF-8 encoded bytes, which may be different from String.length() which counts the number of UTF-32 codepoints. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_pascal_string: Stores the given String as a line in the file in Pascal format (i.e. also store the length of the string). Text will be encoded as UTF-8. This advances the file cursor by the number of bytes written depending on the UTF-8 encoded bytes, which may be different from String.length() which counts the number of UTF-32 codepoints. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_real: Stores a floating-point number in the file. This advances the file cursor by either 4 or 8 bytes, depending on the precision used by the current Godot build.
m.FileAccess.store_string: Stores string in the file without a newline character (\n), encoding the text as UTF-8. This advances the file cursor by the length of the string in UTF-8 encoded bytes, which may be different from String.length() which counts the number of UTF-32 codepoints. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileAccess.store_var: Stores any Variant value in the file. If full_objects is true, encoding objects is allowed (and can potentially include code). This advances the file cursor by the number of bytes written. Returns true if the operation is successful.
m.FileDialog.ACCESS_FILESYSTEM: The dialog allows accessing files on the whole file system.
m.FileDialog.ACCESS_RESOURCES: The dialog only allows accessing files under the Resource path (res://).
m.FileDialog.ACCESS_USERDATA: The dialog only allows accessing files under user data path (user://).
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_CREATE_FOLDER: If enabled, shows the button for creating new directories (when using FILE_MODE_OPEN_DIR, FILE_MODE_OPEN_ANY, or FILE_MODE_SAVE_FILE).
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_DELETE: If enabled, the context menu will show the "Delete" option, which allows moving files and folders to trash.
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_FAVORITES: If enabled, shows the toggle favorite button and favorite list on the left side of the dialog.
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_FILE_FILTER: If enabled, shows the toggle file filter button.
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_FILE_SORT: If enabled, shows the file sorting options button.
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_HIDDEN_FILES: Toggles visibility of the favorite button, and the favorite list on the left side of the dialog.
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_LAYOUT: If enabled, shows the layout switch buttons (list/thumbnails).
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_OVERWRITE_WARNI: If enabled, the FileDialog will warn the user before overwriting files in save mode.
m.FileDialog.CUSTOMIZATION_RECENT: If enabled, shows the recent directories list on the left side of the dialog.
m.FileDialog.DISPLAY_LIST: The dialog displays files as a list of filenames.
m.FileDialog.DISPLAY_THUMBNAILS: The dialog displays files as a grid of thumbnails. Use thumbnail_size to adjust their size.
m.FileDialog.FILE_MODE_OPEN_ANY: The dialog allows selecting one file or directory.
m.FileDialog.FILE_MODE_OPEN_DIR: The dialog only allows selecting a directory, disallowing the selection of any file.
m.FileDialog.FILE_MODE_OPEN_FILE: The dialog allows selecting one, and only one file.
m.FileDialog.FILE_MODE_OPEN_FILES: The dialog allows selecting multiple files.
m.FileDialog.FILE_MODE_SAVE_FILE: The dialog will warn when a file exists.
m.FileDialog.PackedStringArray: The list of values for the option at index.
m.FileDialog.add_filter: Adds a comma-separated file extension filter and comma-separated MIME type mime_type option to the FileDialog with an optional description, which restricts what files can be picked.
m.FileDialog.add_option: Adds an additional OptionButton to the file dialog. If values is empty, a CheckBox is added instead.
m.FileDialog.clear_filename_filter: Clear the filter for file names.
m.FileDialog.clear_filters: Clear all the added filters in the dialog.
m.FileDialog.current_dir: The current working directory of the file dialog.
m.FileDialog.current_file: The currently selected file of the file dialog.
m.FileDialog.current_path: The currently selected file path of the file dialog.
m.FileDialog.deleting_enabled: If true, the context menu will show the "Delete" option, which allows moving files and folders to trash.
m.FileDialog.deselect_all: Clear all currently selected items in the dialog.
m.FileDialog.dir_selected: Emitted when the user selects a directory.
m.FileDialog.display_mode: Display mode of the dialog's file list.
m.FileDialog.favorites_enabled: If true, shows the toggle favorite button and favorite list on the left side of the dialog.
m.FileDialog.file_filter_toggle_enabled: If true, shows the toggle file filter button.
m.FileDialog.file_mode: The dialog's open or save mode, which affects the selection behavior.
m.FileDialog.file_selected: Emitted when the user selects a file by double-clicking it or pressing the OK button.
m.FileDialog.file_sort_options_enabled: If true, shows the file sorting options button.
m.FileDialog.filename_filter: The filter for file names (case-insensitive). When set to a non-empty string, only files that contains the substring will be shown. filename_filter can be edited by the user with the filter button at the top of the file dialog.
m.FileDialog.filename_filter_changed: Emitted when the filter for file names changes.
m.FileDialog.files_selected: Emitted when the user selects multiple files.
m.FileDialog.filters: The available file type filters. Each filter string in the array should be formatted like this: *.png,*.jpg,*.jpeg;Image Files;image/png,image/jpeg. The description text of the filter is optional and can be omitted. Both file extensions and MIME type should be always set.
m.FileDialog.folder_creation_enabled: If true, shows the button for creating new directories (when using FILE_MODE_OPEN_DIR, FILE_MODE_OPEN_ANY, or FILE_MODE_SAVE_FILE), and the context menu will have the "New Folder..." option.
m.FileDialog.get_favorite_list: Returns the list of favorite directories, which is shared by all FileDialog nodes. Useful to store the list of favorites between project sessions. This method can be called only from the main thread.
m.FileDialog.get_line_edit: Returns the LineEdit for the selected file.
m.FileDialog.get_option_default: Returns the default value index of the OptionButton or CheckBox with index option.
m.FileDialog.get_option_name: Returns the name of the OptionButton or CheckBox with index option.
m.FileDialog.get_option_values: Returns an array of values of the OptionButton with index option.
m.FileDialog.get_recent_list: Returns the list of recent directories, which is shared by all FileDialog nodes. Useful to store the list of recents between project sessions. This method can be called only from the main thread.
m.FileDialog.get_selected_options: Returns a Dictionary with the selected values of the additional OptionButtons and/or CheckBoxes. Dictionary keys are names and values are selected value indices.
m.FileDialog.get_vbox: Returns the vertical box container of the dialog, custom controls can be added to it.
m.FileDialog.hidden_files_toggle_enabled: If true, shows the toggle hidden files button.
m.FileDialog.invalidate: Invalidates and updates this dialog's content list.
m.FileDialog.is_customization_flag_enabled: Returns true if the provided flag is enabled.
m.FileDialog.layout_toggle_enabled: If true, shows the layout switch buttons (list/thumbnails).
m.FileDialog.mode_overrides_title: If true, changing the file_mode property will set the window title accordingly (e.g. setting file_mode to FILE_MODE_OPEN_FILE will change the window title to "Open a File").
m.FileDialog.option_count: The number of additional OptionButtons and CheckBoxes in the dialog.
m.FileDialog.overwrite_warning_enabled: If true, the FileDialog will warn the user before overwriting files in save mode.
m.FileDialog.popup_file_dialog: Shows the FileDialog using the default size and position for file dialogs, and selects the file name if there is a current file.
m.FileDialog.recent_list_enabled: If true, shows the recent directories list on the left side of the dialog.
m.FileDialog.root_subfolder: If non-empty, the given sub-folder will be "root" of this FileDialog, i.e. user won't be able to go to its parent directory.
m.FileDialog.set_customization_flag_enable: Sets the specified customization flag, allowing to customize the features available in this FileDialog.
m.FileDialog.set_favorite_list: Sets the list of favorite directories, which is shared by all FileDialog nodes. Useful to restore the list of favorites saved with get_favorite_list(). This method can be called only from the main thread.
m.FileDialog.set_get_icon_callback: Sets the callback used by the FileDialog nodes to get a file icon, when DISPLAY_LIST mode is used. The callback should take a single String argument (file path), and return a Texture2D. If an invalid texture is returned, the file icon will be used instead.
m.FileDialog.set_get_thumbnail_callback: Sets the callback used by the FileDialog nodes to get a file icon, when DISPLAY_THUMBNAILS mode is used. The callback should take a single String argument (file path), and return a Texture2D. If an invalid texture is returned, the file_thumbnail icon will be used instead.
m.FileDialog.set_option_default: Sets the default value index of the OptionButton or CheckBox with index option.
m.FileDialog.set_option_name: Sets the name of the OptionButton or CheckBox with index option.
m.FileDialog.set_option_values: Sets the option values of the OptionButton with index option.
m.FileDialog.set_recent_list: Sets the list of recent directories, which is shared by all FileDialog nodes. Useful to restore the list of recents saved with set_recent_list(). This method can be called only from the main thread.
m.FileDialog.show_hidden_files: If true, the dialog will show hidden files.
m.FileDialog.use_native_dialog: If true, and if supported by the current DisplayServer, OS native dialog will be used instead of custom one.
m.FileSystemDock.display_mode_changed: Emitted when the user switches file display mode or split mode.
m.FileSystemDock.file_removed: Emitted when the given file was removed.
m.FileSystemDock.files_moved: Emitted when a file is moved from old_file path to new_file path.
m.FileSystemDock.folder_moved: Emitted when a folder is moved from old_folder path to new_folder path.
m.FileSystemDock.folder_removed: Emitted when the given folder was removed.
m.FileSystemDock.inherit: Emitted when a new scene is created that inherits the scene at file path.
m.FileSystemDock.instantiate: Emitted when the given scenes are being instantiated in the editor.
m.FileSystemDock.navigate_to_path: Sets the given path as currently selected, ensuring that the selected file/directory is visible.
m.FileSystemDock.remove_resource_tooltip_p: Removes an EditorResourceTooltipPlugin. Fails if the plugin wasn't previously added.
m.FileSystemDock.resource_removed: Emitted when an external resource had its file removed.
m.FileSystemDock.selection_changed: Emitted when the selection changes. Use EditorInterface.get_selected_paths() in the connected method to get the selected paths.
m.FlowContainer.ALIGNMENT_BEGIN: The child controls will be arranged at the beginning of the container, i.e. top if orientation is vertical, left if orientation is horizontal (right for RTL layout).
m.FlowContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER: The child controls will be centered in the container.
m.FlowContainer.ALIGNMENT_END: The child controls will be arranged at the end of the container, i.e. bottom if orientation is vertical, right if orientation is horizontal (left for RTL layout).
m.FlowContainer.LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_BEGIN: The last partially filled row or column will wrap aligned to the beginning of the previous row or column.
m.FlowContainer.LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_CENTER: The last partially filled row or column will wrap aligned to the center of the previous row or column.
m.FlowContainer.LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_END: The last partially filled row or column will wrap aligned to the end of the previous row or column.
m.FlowContainer.LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_INHERI: The last partially filled row or column will wrap aligned to the previous row or column in accordance with alignment.
m.FlowContainer.alignment: The alignment of the container's children (must be one of ALIGNMENT_BEGIN, ALIGNMENT_CENTER, or ALIGNMENT_END).
m.FlowContainer.last_wrap_alignment: The wrap behavior of the last, partially filled row or column (must be one of LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_INHERIT, LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_BEGIN, LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_CENTER, or LAST_WRAP_ALIGNMENT_END).
m.FlowContainer.reverse_fill: If true, reverses fill direction. Horizontal FlowContainers will fill rows bottom to top, vertical FlowContainers will fill columns right to left.
m.FlowContainer.vertical: If true, the FlowContainer will arrange its children vertically, rather than horizontally.
m.FogMaterial.albedo: The single-scattering Color of the FogVolume. Internally, albedo is converted into single-scattering, which is additively blended with other FogVolumes and the Environment.volumetric_fog_albedo.
m.FogMaterial.density: The density of the FogVolume. Denser objects are more opaque, but may suffer from under-sampling artifacts that look like stripes. Negative values can be used to subtract fog from other FogVolumes or global volumetric fog.
m.FogMaterial.density_texture: The 3D texture that is used to scale the density of the FogVolume. This can be used to vary fog density within the FogVolume with any kind of static pattern. For animated effects, consider using a custom fog shader.
m.FogMaterial.edge_fade: The hardness of the edges of the FogVolume. A higher value will result in softer edges, while a lower value will result in harder edges.
m.FogMaterial.emission: The Color of the light emitted by the FogVolume. Emitted light will not cast light or shadows on other objects, but can be useful for modulating the Color of the FogVolume independently from light sources.
m.FogMaterial.height_falloff: The rate by which the height-based fog decreases in density as height increases in world space. A high falloff will result in a sharp transition, while a low falloff will result in a smoother transition. A value of 0.0 results in uniform-density fog. The height threshold is determined by the height of the associated FogVolume.
m.FogVolume.material: The Material used by the FogVolume. Can be either a built-in FogMaterial or a custom ShaderMaterial.
m.FogVolume.shape: The shape of the FogVolume. This can be set to either RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_ELLIPSOID, RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CONE, RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CYLINDER, RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_BOX or RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_WORLD.
m.FogVolume.size: The size of the FogVolume when shape is RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_ELLIPSOID, RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CONE, RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CYLINDER or RenderingServer.FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_BOX.
m.FoldableContainer.POSITION_BOTTOM: Makes the title appear at the bottom of the container. Also makes all StyleBoxes flipped vertically.
m.FoldableContainer.POSITION_TOP: Makes the title appear at the top of the container.
m.FoldableContainer.add_title_bar_control: Adds a Control that will be placed next to the container's title, obscuring the clickable area. Prime usage is adding Button nodes, but it can be any Control.
m.FoldableContainer.expand: Expands the container and emits folding_changed.
m.FoldableContainer.fold: Folds the container and emits folding_changed.
m.FoldableContainer.foldable_group: The FoldableGroup associated with the container. When multiple FoldableContainer nodes share the same group, only one of them is allowed to be unfolded.
m.FoldableContainer.folded: If true, the container will become folded and will hide all its children.
m.FoldableContainer.folding_changed: Emitted when the container is folded/expanded.
m.FoldableContainer.language: Language code used for text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.FoldableContainer.remove_title_bar_contr: Removes a Control added with add_title_bar_control(). The node is not freed automatically, you need to use Node.queue_free().
m.FoldableContainer.title: The container's title text.
m.FoldableContainer.title_text_overrun_beh: Defines the behavior of the title when the text is longer than the available space.
m.FoldableGroup.allow_folding_all: If true, it is possible to fold all containers in this FoldableGroup.
m.FoldableGroup.expanded: Emitted when one of the containers of the group is expanded.
m.FoldableGroup.get_containers: Returns an Array of FoldableContainers that have this as their FoldableGroup (see FoldableContainer.foldable_group). This is equivalent to ButtonGroup but for FoldableContainers.
m.Font.draw_char: Draw a single Unicode character char into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
m.Font.draw_char_outline: Draw a single Unicode character char outline into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color and size outline size. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
m.Font.draw_multiline_string: Breaks text into lines using rules specified by brk_flags and draws it into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color, optionally clipping the width and aligning horizontally. pos specifies the baseline of the first line, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor,…
