To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is…
m.Font.draw_string: Draw text into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color, optionally clipping the width and aligning horizontally. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
m.Font.draw_string_outline: Draw text outline into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color and size outline size, optionally clipping the width and aligning horizontally. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are use…
m.Font.fallbacks: Array of fallback Fonts to use as a substitute if a glyph is not found in this current Font.
m.Font.find_variation: Returns TextServer RID of the font cache for specific variation.
m.Font.get_ascent: Returns the maximum font ascent (number of pixels above the baseline) of this font and all fallback fonts.
m.Font.get_char_size: Returns the size of a character. Does not take kerning into account.
m.Font.get_descent: Returns the maximum font descent (number of pixels below the baseline) of this font and all fallback fonts.
m.Font.get_face_count: Returns number of faces in the TrueType / OpenType collection.
m.Font.get_font_stretch: Returns font stretch amount, compared to a normal width. A percentage value between 50% and 200%.
m.Font.get_font_weight: Returns weight (boldness) of the font. A value in the 100...999 range, normal font weight is 400, bold font weight is 700.
m.Font.get_height: Returns the total average font height (ascent plus descent) in pixels.
m.Font.get_multiline_string_size: Returns the size of a bounding box of a string broken into the lines, taking kerning and advance into account.
m.Font.get_opentype_features: Returns a set of OpenType feature tags. More info: OpenType feature tags [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/featuretags].
m.Font.get_ot_name_strings: Returns Dictionary with OpenType font name strings (localized font names, version, description, license information, sample text, etc.).
m.Font.get_palette_colors: Returns the array in the predefined color palette at index. Palette contains all colors used to render font glyphs. Each palette has the same number of colors. Colors can be overridden using FontVariation.
m.Font.get_palette_count: Returns the number of predefined color palettes. Palette contains all colors used to render font glyphs. Each palette has the same number of colors.
m.Font.get_palette_name: Returns the name of the predefined color palette at index. Palette contains all colors used to render font glyphs. Each palette has the same number of colors.
m.Font.get_rids: Returns Array of valid Font RIDs, which can be passed to the TextServer methods.
m.Font.get_spacing: Returns the amount of spacing for the given spacing type.
m.Font.get_string_size: Returns the size of a bounding box of a single-line string, taking kerning, advance and subpixel positioning into account. See also get_multiline_string_size() and draw_string().
m.Font.get_supported_chars: Returns a string containing all the characters available in the font.
m.Font.get_supported_feature_list: Returns list of OpenType features supported by font.
m.Font.get_supported_variation_list: Returns list of supported variation coordinates [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/dvaraxisreg], each coordinate is returned as tag: Vector3i(min_value,max_value,default_value).
m.Font.get_underline_position: Returns average pixel offset of the underline below the baseline.
m.Font.get_underline_thickness: Returns average thickness of the underline.
m.Font.has_char: Returns true if a Unicode char is available in the font.
m.Font.is_language_supported: Returns true if the font supports the given language (as a ISO 639 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_639-1] code).
m.Font.is_script_supported: Returns true if the font supports the given script (as a ISO 15924 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_15924] code).
m.Font.set_cache_capacity: Sets LRU cache capacity for draw_* methods.
m.FontFile.allow_system_fallback: If set to true, system fonts can be automatically used as fallbacks.
m.FontFile.clear_glyphs: Removes all rendered glyph information from the cache entry.
m.FontFile.clear_size_cache: Removes all font sizes from the cache entry.
m.FontFile.clear_textures: Removes all textures from font cache entry.
m.FontFile.data: Contents of the dynamic font source file.
m.FontFile.disable_embedded_bitmaps: If set to true, embedded font bitmap loading is disabled (bitmap-only and color fonts ignore this property).
m.FontFile.fixed_size: Font size, used only for the bitmap fonts.
m.FontFile.fixed_size_scale_mode: Scaling mode, used only for the bitmap fonts with fixed_size greater than zero.
m.FontFile.font_stretch: Font stretch amount, compared to a normal width. A percentage value between 50% and 200%.
m.FontFile.font_weight: Weight (boldness) of the font. A value in the 100...999 range, normal font weight is 400, bold font weight is 700.
m.FontFile.force_autohinter: If set to true, auto-hinting is supported and preferred over font built-in hinting. Used by dynamic fonts only (MSDF fonts don't support hinting).
m.FontFile.generate_mipmaps: If set to true, generate mipmaps for the font textures.
m.FontFile.get_cache_ascent: Returns the font ascent (number of pixels above the baseline).
m.FontFile.get_cache_count: Returns number of the font cache entries.
m.FontFile.get_cache_descent: Returns the font descent (number of pixels below the baseline).
m.FontFile.get_cache_scale: Returns scaling factor of the color bitmap font.
m.FontFile.get_cache_underline_position: Returns pixel offset of the underline below the baseline.
m.FontFile.get_cache_underline_thickness: Returns thickness of the underline in pixels.
m.FontFile.get_char_from_glyph_index: Returns character code associated with glyph_index, or 0 if glyph_index is invalid. See get_glyph_index().
m.FontFile.get_embolden: Returns embolden strength, if is not equal to zero, emboldens the font outlines. Negative values reduce the outline thickness.
m.FontFile.get_extra_baseline_offset: Returns extra baseline offset (as a fraction of font height).
m.FontFile.get_extra_spacing: Returns spacing for spacing in pixels (not relative to the font size).
m.FontFile.get_face_index: Returns an active face index in the TrueType / OpenType collection.
m.FontFile.get_glyph_advance: Returns glyph advance (offset of the next glyph).
m.FontFile.get_glyph_index: Returns the glyph index of a char, optionally modified by the variation_selector.
m.FontFile.get_glyph_list: Returns list of rendered glyphs in the cache entry.
m.FontFile.get_glyph_offset: Returns glyph offset from the baseline.
m.FontFile.get_glyph_texture_idx: Returns index of the cache texture containing the glyph.
m.FontFile.get_glyph_uv_rect: Returns rectangle in the cache texture containing the glyph.
m.FontFile.get_kerning: Returns kerning for the pair of glyphs.
m.FontFile.get_kerning_list: Returns list of the kerning overrides.
m.FontFile.get_language_support_override: Returns true if support override is enabled for the language.
m.FontFile.get_language_support_overrides: Returns list of language support overrides.
m.FontFile.get_script_support_override: Returns true if support override is enabled for the script.
m.FontFile.get_script_support_overrides: Returns list of script support overrides.
m.FontFile.get_size_cache_list: Returns list of the font sizes in the cache. Each size is Vector2i with font size and outline size.
m.FontFile.get_texture_count: Returns number of textures used by font cache entry.
m.FontFile.get_texture_image: Returns a copy of the font cache texture image.
m.FontFile.get_texture_offsets: Returns a copy of the array containing glyph packing data.
m.FontFile.get_transform: Returns 2D transform, applied to the font outlines, can be used for slanting, flipping and rotating glyphs.
m.FontFile.get_variation_coordinates: Returns variation coordinates for the specified font cache entry. See Font.get_supported_variation_list() for more info.
m.FontFile.hinting: Font hinting mode. Used by dynamic fonts only.
m.FontFile.keep_rounding_remainders: If set to true, when aligning glyphs to the pixel boundaries rounding remainders are accumulated to ensure more uniform glyph distribution. This setting has no effect if subpixel positioning is enabled.
m.FontFile.load_bitmap_font: Loads an AngelCode BMFont (.fnt, .font) bitmap font from file path.
m.FontFile.load_dynamic_font: Loads a TrueType (.ttf), OpenType (.otf), WOFF (.woff), WOFF2 (.woff2) or Type 1 (.pfb, .pfm) dynamic font from file path.
m.FontFile.modulate_color_glyphs: If set to true, color modulation is applied when drawing colored glyphs, otherwise it's applied to the monochrome glyphs only.
m.FontFile.msdf_pixel_range: The width of the range around the shape between the minimum and maximum representable signed distance. If using font outlines, msdf_pixel_range must be set to at least twice the size of the largest font outline. The default msdf_pixel_range value of 16 allows outline sizes up to 8 to look correct.
m.FontFile.msdf_size: Source font size used to generate MSDF textures. Higher values allow for more precision, but are slower to render and require more memory. Only increase this value if you notice a visible lack of precision in glyph rendering.
m.FontFile.multichannel_signed_distance_fi: If set to true, glyphs of all sizes are rendered using single multichannel signed distance field (MSDF) generated from the dynamic font vector data. Since this approach does not rely on rasterizing the font every time its size changes, this allows for resizing the font in real-time without any performance penalty. Text will also not look grainy for Controls that are scaled down (or for Label3Ds v…
m.FontFile.oversampling: If set to a positive value, overrides the oversampling factor of the viewport this font is used in. See Viewport.oversampling. This value doesn't override the oversampling parameter of draw_* methods.
m.FontFile.remove_glyph: Removes specified rendered glyph information from the cache entry.
m.FontFile.remove_kerning: Removes kerning override for the pair of glyphs.
m.FontFile.remove_size_cache: Removes specified font size from the cache entry.
m.FontFile.remove_texture: Removes specified texture from the cache entry.
m.FontFile.render_glyph: Renders specified glyph to the font cache texture.
m.FontFile.render_range: Renders the range of characters to the font cache texture.
m.FontFile.set_cache_ascent: Sets the font ascent (number of pixels above the baseline).
m.FontFile.set_cache_descent: Sets the font descent (number of pixels below the baseline).
m.FontFile.set_cache_scale: Sets scaling factor of the color bitmap font.
m.FontFile.set_cache_underline_position: Sets pixel offset of the underline below the baseline.
m.FontFile.set_cache_underline_thickness: Sets thickness of the underline in pixels.
m.FontFile.set_embolden: Sets embolden strength, if is not equal to zero, emboldens the font outlines. Negative values reduce the outline thickness.
m.FontFile.set_extra_baseline_offset: Sets extra baseline offset (as a fraction of font height).
m.FontFile.set_extra_spacing: Sets the spacing for spacing to value in pixels (not relative to the font size).
m.FontFile.set_face_index: Sets an active face index in the TrueType / OpenType collection.
m.FontFile.set_glyph_advance: Sets glyph advance (offset of the next glyph).
m.FontFile.set_glyph_offset: Sets glyph offset from the baseline.
m.FontFile.set_glyph_texture_idx: Sets index of the cache texture containing the glyph.
m.FontFile.set_glyph_uv_rect: Sets rectangle in the cache texture containing the glyph.
m.FontFile.set_kerning: Sets kerning for the pair of glyphs.
m.FontFile.set_texture_offsets: Sets array containing glyph packing data.
m.FontFile.set_transform: Sets 2D transform, applied to the font outlines, can be used for slanting, flipping, and rotating glyphs.
m.FontFile.set_variation_coordinates: Sets variation coordinates for the specified font cache entry. See Font.get_supported_variation_list() for more info.
m.FontFile.subpixel_positioning: Font glyph subpixel positioning mode. Subpixel positioning provides shaper text and better kerning for smaller font sizes, at the cost of higher memory usage and lower font rasterization speed. Use TextServer.SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_AUTO to automatically enable it based on the font size.
m.FontVariation.base_font: Base font used to create a variation. If not set, default Theme font is used.
m.FontVariation.baseline_offset: Extra baseline offset (as a fraction of font height).
m.FontVariation.opentype_features: A set of OpenType feature tags. More info: OpenType feature tags [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/featuretags].
m.FontVariation.palette_custom_colors: An array of colors to override predefined palette. Use Color(0, 0, 0, 0), to keep predefined palette color at specific position.
m.FontVariation.set_spacing: Sets the spacing for spacing to value in pixels (not relative to the font size).
m.FontVariation.spacing_bottom: Extra spacing at the bottom of the line in pixels.
m.FontVariation.spacing_space: Extra width of the space glyphs.
m.FontVariation.spacing_top: Extra spacing at the top of the line in pixels.
m.FontVariation.variation_embolden: If is not equal to zero, emboldens the font outlines. Negative values reduce the outline thickness.
m.FontVariation.variation_face_index: Active face index in the TrueType / OpenType collection file.
m.FontVariation.variation_opentype: Font OpenType variation coordinates. More info: OpenType variation tags [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/dvaraxisreg].
m.FontVariation.variation_transform: 2D transform, applied to the font outlines, can be used for slanting, flipping and rotating glyphs.

m.GDExtensionManager.get_loaded_extensions: Returns the file paths of all currently loaded extensions.
m.GDExtensionManager.is_extension_loaded: Returns true if the extension at the given file path has already been loaded successfully. See also get_loaded_extensions().

m.GDExtensionManager.load_extension_from_f: Loads the extension already in address space via the given path and initialization function. The path needs to be unique and start with "libgodot://". Returns LOAD_STATUS_OK if successful.

m.GDExtensionManager.unload_extension: Unloads an extension by file path. The path needs to point to an already loaded GDExtension, otherwise this method returns LOAD_STATUS_NOT_LOADED.

m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_DOUBLE_FLOAT: Component type "DOUBLE". The value is 0x140A which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 8-byte or 64-bit floating-point numbers. This is NOT a core part of the glTF specification, and may not be supported by all glTF importers. May be used by some extensions including KHR_interactivity.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_HALF_FLOAT: Component type "HALF_FLOAT". The value is 0x140B which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 2-byte or 16-bit floating-point numbers. This is NOT a core part of the glTF specification, and may not be supported by all glTF importers. May be used by some extensions including KHR_interactivity.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_NONE: Component type "NONE". This is not a valid component type, and is used to indicate that the component type is not set.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_SIGNED_BYTE: Component type "BYTE". The value is 0x1400 which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 1-byte or 8-bit signed integers. This is a core part of the glTF specification.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_SIGNED_INT: Component type "INT". The value is 0x1404 which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 4-byte or 32-bit signed integers. This is NOT a core part of the glTF specification, and may not be supported by all glTF importers. May be used by some extensions including KHR_interactivity.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_SIGNED_LONG: Component type "LONG". The value is 0x140E which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 8-byte or 64-bit signed integers. This is NOT a core part of the glTF specification, and may not be supported by all glTF importers. May be used by some extensions including KHR_interactivity.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_SIGNED_SHORT: Component type "SHORT". The value is 0x1402 which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 2-byte or 16-bit signed integers. This is a core part of the glTF specification.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_SINGLE_FLOAT: Component type "FLOAT". The value is 0x1406 which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 4-byte or 32-bit floating-point numbers. This is a core part of the glTF specification.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_UNSIGNED_BYT: Component type "UNSIGNED_BYTE". The value is 0x1401 which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 1-byte or 8-bit unsigned integers. This is a core part of the glTF specification.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT: Component type "UNSIGNED_INT". The value is 0x1405 which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 4-byte or 32-bit unsigned integers. This is a core part of the glTF specification.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LON: Component type "UNSIGNED_LONG". The value is 0x140F which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 8-byte or 64-bit unsigned integers. This is NOT a core part of the glTF specification, and may not be supported by all glTF importers. May be used by some extensions including KHR_interactivity.
m.GLTFAccessor.COMPONENT_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHO: Component type "UNSIGNED_SHORT". The value is 0x1403 which comes from OpenGL. This indicates data is stored in 2-byte or 16-bit unsigned integers. This is a core part of the glTF specification.
m.GLTFAccessor.TYPE_MAT2: Accessor type "MAT2". For the glTF object model, this maps to "float2x2", represented in the glTF JSON as an array of four floats.
m.GLTFAccessor.TYPE_MAT3: Accessor type "MAT3". For the glTF object model, this maps to "float3x3", represented in the glTF JSON as an array of nine floats.
m.GLTFAccessor.TYPE_MAT4: Accessor type "MAT4". For the glTF object model, this maps to "float4x4", represented in the glTF JSON as an array of sixteen floats.
m.GLTFAccessor.TYPE_SCALAR: Accessor type "SCALAR". For the glTF object model, this can be used to map to a single float, int, or bool value, or a float array.
m.GLTFAccessor.TYPE_VEC2: Accessor type "VEC2". For the glTF object model, this maps to "float2", represented in the glTF JSON as an array of two floats.
m.GLTFAccessor.TYPE_VEC3: Accessor type "VEC3". For the glTF object model, this maps to "float3", represented in the glTF JSON as an array of three floats.
m.GLTFAccessor.TYPE_VEC4: Accessor type "VEC4". For the glTF object model, this maps to "float4", represented in the glTF JSON as an array of four floats.
m.GLTFAccessor.accessor_type: The glTF accessor type, as an enum.
m.GLTFAccessor.buffer_view: The index of the buffer view this accessor is referencing. If -1, this accessor is not referencing any buffer view.
m.GLTFAccessor.byte_offset: The offset relative to the start of the buffer view in bytes.
m.GLTFAccessor.component_type: The glTF component type as an enum. See GLTFComponentType for possible values. Within the core glTF specification, a value of 5125 or "UNSIGNED_INT" must not be used for any accessor that is not referenced by mesh.primitive.indices.
m.GLTFAccessor.count: The number of elements referenced by this accessor.
m.GLTFAccessor.from_dictionary: Creates a new GLTFAccessor instance by parsing the given Dictionary.
m.GLTFAccessor.max: Maximum value of each component in this accessor.
m.GLTFAccessor.min: Minimum value of each component in this accessor.
m.GLTFAccessor.normalized: Specifies whether integer data values are normalized before usage.
m.GLTFAccessor.sparse_count: Number of deviating accessor values stored in the sparse array.
m.GLTFAccessor.sparse_indices_buffer_view: The index of the buffer view with sparse indices. The referenced buffer view MUST NOT have its target or byteStride properties defined. The buffer view and the optional byteOffset MUST be aligned to the componentType byte length.
m.GLTFAccessor.sparse_indices_byte_offset: The offset relative to the start of the buffer view in bytes.
m.GLTFAccessor.sparse_indices_component_ty: The indices component data type as an enum. Possible values are 5121 for "UNSIGNED_BYTE", 5123 for "UNSIGNED_SHORT", and 5125 for "UNSIGNED_INT".
m.GLTFAccessor.sparse_values_buffer_view: The index of the bufferView with sparse values. The referenced buffer view MUST NOT have its target or byteStride properties defined.
m.GLTFAccessor.sparse_values_byte_offset: The offset relative to the start of the bufferView in bytes.
m.GLTFAccessor.to_dictionary: Serializes this GLTFAccessor instance into a Dictionary.
m.GLTFAnimation.get_additional_data: Gets additional arbitrary data in this GLTFAnimation instance. This can be used to keep per-node state data in GLTFDocumentExtension classes, which is important because they are stateless.
m.GLTFAnimation.loop: There is currently no description for this property. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.GLTFAnimation.original_name: The original name of the animation.
m.GLTFAnimation.set_additional_data: Sets additional arbitrary data in this GLTFAnimation instance. This can be used to keep per-node state data in GLTFDocumentExtension classes, which is important because they are stateless.
m.GLTFBufferView.buffer: The index of the buffer this buffer view is referencing. If -1, this buffer view is not referencing any buffer.
m.GLTFBufferView.byte_length: The length, in bytes, of this buffer view. If 0, this buffer view is empty.
m.GLTFBufferView.byte_offset: The offset, in bytes, from the start of the buffer to the start of this buffer view.
m.GLTFBufferView.byte_stride: The stride, in bytes, between interleaved data. If -1, this buffer view is not interleaved.
m.GLTFBufferView.from_dictionary: Creates a new GLTFBufferView instance by parsing the given Dictionary.
m.GLTFBufferView.indices: true if the GLTFBufferView's OpenGL GPU buffer type is an ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER used for vertex indices (integer constant 34963). false if the buffer type is any other value. See Buffers, BufferViews, and Accessors [https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Tutorials/blob/master/gltfTutorial/gltfTutorial_005_BuffersBufferViewsAccessors.md] for possible values. This property is set on import and used on…
m.GLTFBufferView.load_buffer_view_data: Loads the buffer view data from the buffer referenced by this buffer view in the given GLTFState. Interleaved data with a byte stride is not yet supported by this method. The data is returned as a PackedByteArray.
m.GLTFBufferView.to_dictionary: Serializes this GLTFBufferView instance into a Dictionary.
m.GLTFBufferView.vertex_attributes: true if the GLTFBufferView's OpenGL GPU buffer type is an ARRAY_BUFFER used for vertex attributes (integer constant 34962). false if the buffer type is any other value. See Buffers, BufferViews, and Accessors [https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Tutorials/blob/master/gltfTutorial/gltfTutorial_005_BuffersBufferViewsAccessors.md] for possible values. This property is set on import and used on expo…
m.GLTFCamera.depth_far: The distance to the far culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis, in meters. This maps to glTF's zfar property.
m.GLTFCamera.depth_near: The distance to the near culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis, in meters. This maps to glTF's znear property.
m.GLTFCamera.fov: The FOV of the camera. This class and glTF define the camera FOV in radians, while Godot uses degrees. This maps to glTF's yfov property. This value is only used for perspective cameras, when perspective is true.
m.GLTFCamera.from_dictionary: Creates a new GLTFCamera instance by parsing the given Dictionary.
m.GLTFCamera.from_node: Create a new GLTFCamera instance from the given Godot Camera3D node.
m.GLTFCamera.perspective: If true, the camera is in perspective mode. Otherwise, the camera is in orthographic/orthogonal mode. This maps to glTF's camera type property. See Camera3D.projection and the glTF spec for more information.
m.GLTFCamera.size_mag: The size of the camera. This class and glTF define the camera size magnitude as a radius in meters, while Godot defines it as a diameter in meters. This maps to glTF's ymag property. This value is only used for orthographic/orthogonal cameras, when perspective is false.
m.GLTFCamera.to_dictionary: Serializes this GLTFCamera instance into a Dictionary.
m.GLTFCamera.to_node: Converts this GLTFCamera instance into a Godot Camera3D node.
m.GLTFDocument.IMPORT_FLAG_DISCARD_MESHES_: Ignore meshes and materials on import. When importing a scene as an AnimationLibrary, this flag is always enabled.
m.GLTFDocument.IMPORT_FLAG_FORCE_DISABLE_M: If true, mesh compression will not be used. Consider enabling if you notice blocky artifacts in your mesh normals or UVs, or if you have meshes that are larger than a few thousand meters in each direction.
m.GLTFDocument.IMPORT_FLAG_GENERATE_TANGEN: If true, generate vertex tangents using Mikktspace [http://www.mikktspace.com/] if the input meshes don't have tangent data. When possible, it's recommended to let the 3D modeling software generate tangents on export instead of relying on this option. Tangents are required for correct display of normal and height maps, along with any material/shader features that require tangents.
m.GLTFDocument.IMPORT_FLAG_USE_NAMED_SKIN_: If checked, use named Skins for animation. The MeshInstance3D node contains 3 properties of relevance here: a skeleton NodePath pointing to the Skeleton3D node (usually ..), a mesh, and a skin:
m.GLTFDocument.ROOT_NODE_MODE_KEEP_ROOT: Treat the Godot scene's root node as the root node of the glTF file, but do not mark it as anything special. An extra root node will be generated when importing into Godot. This uses only vanilla glTF features. This is equivalent to the behavior in Godot 4.1 and earlier.
m.GLTFDocument.ROOT_NODE_MODE_MULTI_ROOT: Treat the Godot scene's root node as the name of the glTF scene, and add all of its children as root nodes of the glTF file. This uses only vanilla glTF features. This avoids an extra root node, but only the name of the Godot scene's root node will be preserved, as it will not be saved as a node.
m.GLTFDocument.ROOT_NODE_MODE_SINGLE_ROOT: Treat the Godot scene's root node as the root node of the glTF file, and mark it as the single root node via the GODOT_single_root glTF extension. This will be parsed the same as ROOT_NODE_MODE_KEEP_ROOT if the implementation does not support GODOT_single_root.
m.GLTFDocument.TEXTURE_MAP_MODE_DO_NOT_REM: Import the texture maps in the glTF file as they are, without trying to fit them into specific texture slots suitable for Godot's built-in materials. This may be desirable if using the glTF file with custom shaders, but may not display correctly with Godot's built-in materials. This is equivalent to the behavior in Godot 4.6 and earlier.
m.GLTFDocument.TEXTURE_MAP_MODE_REMAP_TO_S: Import the texture maps in the glTF file remapped to the most suitable texture slots based on Godot's StandardMaterial3D class. This is the default behavior.
m.GLTFDocument.VISIBILITY_MODE_EXCLUDE: If the scene contains any non-visible nodes, do not include them in the export. This is the same as the behavior in Godot 4.4 and earlier. Downside: Invisible nodes will not exist in the exported file.
m.GLTFDocument.VISIBILITY_MODE_INCLUDE_OPT: If the scene contains any non-visible nodes, include them, mark them as non-visible with KHR_node_visibility, and do not impose any requirements on importers. Downside: If the importer does not support KHR_node_visibility, invisible objects will be visible.
m.GLTFDocument.VISIBILITY_MODE_INCLUDE_REQ: If the scene contains any non-visible nodes, include them, mark them as non-visible with KHR_node_visibility, and require that importers respect their non-visibility. Downside: If the importer does not support KHR_node_visibility, the file cannot be imported.
m.GLTFDocument.append_from_buffer: Takes a PackedByteArray defining a glTF and imports the data to the given GLTFState object through the state parameter.
m.GLTFDocument.append_from_file: Takes a path to a glTF file and imports the data at that file path to the given GLTFState object through the state parameter.
m.GLTFDocument.append_from_scene: Takes a Godot Engine scene node and exports it and its descendants to the given GLTFState object through the state parameter.
m.GLTFDocument.export_object_model_propert: Determines a mapping between the given Godot node_path and the corresponding glTF Object Model JSON pointer(s) in the generated glTF file. The details of this mapping are returned in a GLTFObjectModelProperty object. Additional mappings can be supplied via the GLTFDocumentExtension._import_object_model_property() callback method.
m.GLTFDocument.fallback_image_format: The user-friendly name of the fallback image format. This is used when exporting the glTF file, including writing to a file and writing to a byte array.
m.GLTFDocument.fallback_image_quality: The quality of the fallback image, if any. For PNG files, this downscales the image on both dimensions by this factor. For JPEG files, this is the lossy quality of the image. A low value is recommended, since including multiple high quality images in a glTF file defeats the file size gains of using a more efficient image format.
m.GLTFDocument.generate_buffer: Takes a GLTFState object through the state parameter and returns a glTF PackedByteArray.
m.GLTFDocument.generate_scene: Takes a GLTFState object through the state parameter and returns a Godot Engine scene node.
m.GLTFDocument.get_supported_gltf_extensio: Returns a list of all support glTF extensions, including extensions supported directly by the engine, and extensions supported by user plugins registering GLTFDocumentExtension classes.
m.GLTFDocument.image_format: The user-friendly name of the export image format. This is used when exporting the glTF file, including writing to a file and writing to a byte array.
m.GLTFDocument.import_object_model_propert: Determines a mapping between the given glTF Object Model json_pointer and the corresponding Godot node path(s) in the generated Godot scene. The details of this mapping are returned in a GLTFObjectModelProperty object. Additional mappings can be supplied via the GLTFDocumentExtension._export_object_model_property() callback method.
m.GLTFDocument.lossy_quality: If image_format is a lossy image format, this determines the lossy quality of the image. On a range of 0.0 to 1.0, where 0.0 is the lowest quality and 1.0 is the highest quality. A lossy quality of 1.0 is not the same as lossless.
m.GLTFDocument.register_gltf_document_exte: Registers the given GLTFDocumentExtension instance with GLTFDocument. If first_priority is true, this extension will be run first. Otherwise, it will be run last.
m.GLTFDocument.root_node_mode: How to process the root node during export. The default and recommended value is ROOT_NODE_MODE_SINGLE_ROOT.
m.GLTFDocument.texture_map_mode: How to handle texture maps during import. The default and recommended value is TEXTURE_MAP_MODE_REMAP_TO_STANDARD_MATERIAL, which automatically remaps from glTF's flexible texture map system to the more specific texture map slots in Godot's StandardMaterial3D class. Alternatively, TEXTURE_MAP_MODE_DO_NOT_REMAP can be used to preserve the original texture maps from the glTF file, which may be desi…
m.GLTFDocument.visibility_mode: How to deal with node visibility during export. This setting does nothing if all nodes are visible. The default and recommended value is VISIBILITY_MODE_INCLUDE_REQUIRED, which uses the KHR_node_visibility extension.
m.GLTFDocument.write_to_filesystem: Takes a GLTFState object through the state parameter and writes a glTF file to the filesystem.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._convert_scene_nod: Part of the export process. This method is run after _export_preflight() and before _export_post_convert().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._export_get_proper: Runs prior to the export process. This method is run before _export_preflight() when exporting a scene from the editor, or it may not be run at all in other situations.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._export_node: Part of the export process. This method is run after _get_saveable_image_formats() and before _export_post(). If this GLTFDocumentExtension is used for exporting images, this runs after _serialize_texture_json().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._export_object_mod: Part of the export process. Allows GLTFDocumentExtension classes to provide mappings for properties of nodes in the Godot scene tree, to JSON pointers to glTF properties, as defined by the glTF object model.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._export_post: Part of the export process. This method is run last, after all other parts of the export process.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._export_post_conve: Part of the export process. This method is run after _convert_scene_node() and before _export_preserialize().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._export_preflight: Part of the export process. This method is run first, before all other parts of the export process.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._export_preseriali: Part of the export process. This method is run after _export_post_convert() and before _get_saveable_image_formats().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._generate_scene_no: Part of the import process. This method is run after _import_pre_generate() and before _import_node().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._get_image_file_ex: Returns the file extension to use for saving image data into, for example, ".png". If defined, when this extension is used to handle images, and the images are saved to a separate file, the image bytes will be copied to a file with this extension. If this is set, there should be a ResourceImporter class able to import the file. If not defined or empty, Godot will save the image into a PNG file.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._get_saveable_imag: Part of the export process. This method is run after _convert_scene_node() and before _export_node().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._get_supported_ext: Part of the import process. This method is run after _import_preflight() and before _parse_node_extensions().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._import_node: Part of the import process. This method is run after _generate_scene_node() and before _import_post().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._import_object_mod: Part of the import process. Allows GLTFDocumentExtension classes to provide mappings for JSON pointers to glTF properties, as defined by the glTF object model, to properties of nodes in the Godot scene tree.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._import_post: Part of the import process. This method is run last, after all other parts of the import process.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._import_post_parse: Part of the import process. This method is run after _parse_node_extensions() and before _import_pre_generate().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._import_pre_genera: Part of the import process. This method is run after _import_post_parse() and before _generate_scene_node().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._import_preflight: Part of the import process. This method is run first, before all other parts of the import process.
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._parse_image_data: Part of the import process. This method is run after _parse_node_extensions() and before _parse_texture_json().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._parse_node_extens: Part of the import process. This method is run after _get_supported_extensions() and before _import_post_parse().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._parse_texture_jso: Part of the import process. This method is run after _parse_image_data() and before _generate_scene_node().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._save_image_at_pat: Part of the export process. This method is run after _get_saveable_image_formats() and before _serialize_texture_json().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._serialize_image_t: Part of the export process. This method is run after _get_saveable_image_formats() and before _serialize_texture_json().
m.GLTFDocumentExtension._serialize_texture: Part of the export process. This method is run after _save_image_at_path() or _serialize_image_to_bytes(), and before _export_node(). Note that this method only runs when this GLTFDocumentExtension is selected as the image exporter.
m.GLTFLight.color: The Color of the light in linear space. Defaults to white. A black color causes the light to have no effect.
m.GLTFLight.from_dictionary: Creates a new GLTFLight instance by parsing the given Dictionary.
m.GLTFLight.from_node: Create a new GLTFLight instance from the given Godot Light3D node.
m.GLTFLight.get_additional_data: There is currently no description for this method. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.GLTFLight.inner_cone_angle: The inner angle of the cone in a spotlight. Must be less than or equal to the outer cone angle.
m.GLTFLight.intensity: The intensity of the light. This is expressed in candelas (lumens per steradian) for point and spot lights, and lux (lumens per m²) for directional lights. When creating a Godot light, this value is converted to a unitless multiplier.
m.GLTFLight.light_type: The type of the light. The values accepted by Godot are "point", "spot", and "directional", which correspond to Godot's OmniLight3D, SpotLight3D, and DirectionalLight3D respectively.
m.GLTFLight.outer_cone_angle: The outer angle of the cone in a spotlight. Must be greater than or equal to the inner angle.
m.GLTFLight.range: The range of the light, beyond which the light has no effect. glTF lights with no range defined behave like physical lights (which have infinite range). When creating a Godot light, the range is clamped to 4096.0.
m.GLTFLight.set_additional_data: There is currently no description for this method. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.GLTFLight.to_dictionary: Serializes this GLTFLight instance into a Dictionary.
m.GLTFLight.to_node: Converts this GLTFLight instance into a Godot Light3D node.
m.GLTFMesh.blend_weights: An array of floats representing the blend weights of the mesh.
m.GLTFMesh.get_additional_data: Gets additional arbitrary data in this GLTFMesh instance. This can be used to keep per-node state data in GLTFDocumentExtension classes, which is important because they are stateless.
m.GLTFMesh.instance_materials: An array of Material objects representing the materials used in the mesh.
m.GLTFMesh.mesh: The ImporterMesh object representing the mesh itself.
m.GLTFMesh.original_name: The original name of the mesh.
m.GLTFMesh.set_additional_data: Sets additional arbitrary data in this GLTFMesh instance. This can be used to keep per-node state data in GLTFDocumentExtension classes, which is important because they are stateless.
m.GLTFNode.append_child_index: Appends the given child node index to the children array.
m.GLTFNode.camera: If this glTF node is a camera, the index of the GLTFCamera in the GLTFState that describes the camera's properties. If -1, this node is not a camera.
m.GLTFNode.children: The indices of the child nodes in the GLTFState. If this glTF node has no children, this will be an empty array.
m.GLTFNode.get_additional_data: Gets additional arbitrary data in this GLTFNode instance. This can be used to keep per-node state data in GLTFDocumentExtension classes, which is important because they are stateless.
m.GLTFNode.get_scene_node_path: Returns the NodePath that this GLTF node will have in the Godot scene tree after being imported. This is useful when importing glTF object model pointers with GLTFObjectModelProperty, for handling extensions such as KHR_animation_pointer or KHR_interactivity.
m.GLTFNode.height: How deep into the node hierarchy this node is. A root node will have a height of 0, its children will have a height of 1, and so on. If -1, the height has not been calculated.
m.GLTFNode.light: If this glTF node is a light, the index of the GLTFLight in the GLTFState that describes the light's properties. If -1, this node is not a light.
m.GLTFNode.mesh: If this glTF node is a mesh, the index of the GLTFMesh in the GLTFState that describes the mesh's properties. If -1, this node is not a mesh.
m.GLTFNode.original_name: The original name of the node.
m.GLTFNode.parent: The index of the parent node in the GLTFState. If -1, this node is a root node.
m.GLTFNode.position: The position of the glTF node relative to its parent.
m.GLTFNode.rotation: The rotation of the glTF node relative to its parent.
m.GLTFNode.scale: The scale of the glTF node relative to its parent.
m.GLTFNode.set_additional_data: Sets additional arbitrary data in this GLTFNode instance. This can be used to keep per-node state data in GLTFDocumentExtension classes, which is important because they are stateless.
m.GLTFNode.skeleton: If this glTF node has a skeleton, the index of the GLTFSkeleton in the GLTFState that describes the skeleton's properties. If -1, this node does not have a skeleton.
m.GLTFNode.skin: If this glTF node has a skin, the index of the GLTFSkin in the GLTFState that describes the skin's properties. If -1, this node does not have a skin.
m.GLTFNode.visible: If true, the GLTF node is visible. If false, the GLTF node is not visible. This is converted to the Node3D.visible property in the Godot scene, and is exported to KHR_node_visibility when false.
m.GLTFNode.xform: The transform of the glTF node relative to its parent. This property is usually unused since the position, rotation, and scale properties are preferred.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.GLTF_OBJECT_MODE: Object model type "bool". Represented in the glTF JSON as a boolean, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "SCALAR". When encoded in an accessor, a value of 0 is false, and any other value is true.
Object model type "float". Represented in the glTF JSON as a number, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "SCALAR".
Object model type "float2". Represented in the glTF JSON as an array of two numbers, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "VEC2".
Object model type "float2x2". Represented in the glTF JSON as an array of four numbers, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "MAT2".
Object model type "float3". Represented in the glTF JSON as an array of three numbers, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "VEC3".
Object model type "float3x3". Represented in the glTF JSON as an array of nine numbers, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "MAT3".
Object model type "float4". Represented in the glTF JSON as an array of four numbers, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "VEC4".
Object model type "float4x4". Represented in the glTF JSON as an array of sixteen numbers, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "MAT4".
Object model type "float[]". Represented in the glTF JSON as an array of numbers, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "SCALAR".

Object model type "int". Represented in the glTF JSON as a number, and encoded in a GLTFAccessor as "SCALAR". The range of values is limited to signed integers. For KHR_interactivity, only 32-bit integers are supported.
Unknown or not set object model type. If the object model type is set to this value, the real type still needs to be determined.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.append_node_path: Appends a NodePath to node_paths. This can be used by GLTFDocumentExtension classes to define how a glTF object model property maps to a Godot property, or multiple Godot properties. Prefer using append_path_to_property() for simple cases. Be sure to also call set_types() once (the order does not matter).
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.append_path_to_p: High-level wrapper over append_node_path() that handles the most common cases. It constructs a new NodePath using node_path as a base and appends prop_name to the subpath. Be sure to also call set_types() once (the order does not matter).
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.get_accessor_typ: The GLTF accessor type associated with this property's object_model_type. See GLTFAccessor.accessor_type for possible values, and see GLTFObjectModelType for how the object model type maps to accessor types.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.gltf_to_godot_ex: If set, this Expression will be used to convert the property value from the glTF object model to the value expected by the Godot property. This is useful when the glTF object model uses a different unit system, or when the data needs to be transformed in some way. If null, the value will be copied as-is.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.godot_to_gltf_ex: If set, this Expression will be used to convert the property value from the Godot property to the value expected by the glTF object model. This is useful when the glTF object model uses a different unit system, or when the data needs to be transformed in some way. If null, the value will be copied as-is.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.has_json_pointer: Returns true if json_pointers is not empty. This is used during export to determine if a GLTFObjectModelProperty can handle converting a Godot property to a glTF object model property.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.has_node_paths: Returns true if node_paths is not empty. This is used during import to determine if a GLTFObjectModelProperty can handle converting a glTF object model property to a Godot property.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.json_pointers: The glTF object model JSON pointers used to identify the property in the glTF object model. In most cases, there will be only one item in this array, but specific cases may require multiple pointers. The items are themselves arrays which represent the JSON pointer split into its components.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.node_paths: An array of NodePaths that point to a property, or multiple properties, in the Godot scene tree. On import, this will either be set by GLTFDocument, or by a GLTFDocumentExtension class. For simple cases, use append_path_to_property() to add properties to this array.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.object_model_typ: The type of data stored in the glTF file as defined by the object model. This is a superset of the available accessor types, and determines the accessor type.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.set_types: Sets the variant_type and object_model_type properties. This is a convenience method to set both properties at once, since they are almost always known at the same time. This method should be called once. Calling it again with the same values will have no effect.
m.GLTFObjectModelProperty.variant_type: The type of data stored in the Godot property. This is the type of the property that the node_paths point to.
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.angular_velocity: The angular velocity of the physics body, in radians per second. This is only used when the body type is "rigid" or "vehicle".
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.center_of_mass: The center of mass of the body, in meters. This is in local space relative to the body. By default, the center of the mass is the body's origin.
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.from_dictionary: Creates a new GLTFPhysicsBody instance by parsing the given Dictionary in the OMI_physics_body glTF extension format.
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.from_node: Creates a new GLTFPhysicsBody instance from the given Godot CollisionObject3D node.
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.inertia_diagonal: The inertia strength of the physics body, in kilogram meter squared (kg⋅m²). This represents the inertia around the principle axes, the diagonal of the inertia tensor matrix. This is only used when the body type is "rigid" or "vehicle".
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.inertia_orientation: The inertia orientation of the physics body. This defines the rotation of the inertia's principle axes relative to the object's local axes. This is only used when the body type is "rigid" or "vehicle" and inertia_diagonal is set to a non-zero value.
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.inertia_tensor: Deprecated: This property may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.linear_velocity: The linear velocity of the physics body, in meters per second. This is only used when the body type is "rigid" or "vehicle".
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.mass: The mass of the physics body, in kilograms. This is only used when the body type is "rigid" or "vehicle".
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.to_dictionary: Serializes this GLTFPhysicsBody instance into a Dictionary. It will be in the format expected by the OMI_physics_body glTF extension.
m.GLTFPhysicsBody.to_node: Converts this GLTFPhysicsBody instance into a Godot CollisionObject3D node.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.from_dictionary: Creates a new GLTFPhysicsShape instance by parsing the given Dictionary.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.from_node: Creates a new GLTFPhysicsShape instance from the given Godot CollisionShape3D node.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.from_resource: Creates a new GLTFPhysicsShape instance from the given Godot Shape3D resource.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.height: The height of the shape, in meters. This is only used when the shape type is "capsule" or "cylinder". This value should not be negative, and for "capsule" it should be at least twice the radius.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.importer_mesh: The ImporterMesh resource of the shape. This is only used when the shape type is "hull" (convex hull) or "trimesh" (concave trimesh).
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.is_trigger: If true, indicates that this shape is a trigger. For Godot, this means that the shape should be a child of an Area3D node.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.mesh_index: The index of the shape's mesh in the glTF file. This is only used when the shape type is "hull" (convex hull) or "trimesh" (concave trimesh).
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.radius: The radius of the shape, in meters. This is only used when the shape type is "capsule", "cylinder", or "sphere". This value should not be negative.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.shape_type: The type of shape this shape represents. Valid values are "box", "capsule", "cylinder", "sphere", "hull", and "trimesh".
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.size: The size of the shape, in meters. This is only used when the shape type is "box", and it represents the "diameter" of the box. This value should not be negative.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.to_dictionary: Serializes this GLTFPhysicsShape instance into a Dictionary in the format defined by OMI_physics_shape.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.to_node: Converts this GLTFPhysicsShape instance into a Godot CollisionShape3D node.
m.GLTFPhysicsShape.to_resource: Converts this GLTFPhysicsShape instance into a Godot Shape3D resource.

m.GLTFSpecGloss.diffuse_factor: The reflected diffuse factor of the material.
m.GLTFSpecGloss.gloss_factor: The glossiness or smoothness of the material.
m.GLTFSpecGloss.specular_factor: The specular RGB color of the material. The alpha channel is unused.
m.GLTFState.HANDLE_BINARY_IMAGE_MODE_DISCA: When importing a glTF file with embedded binary images, discards all images and uses untextured materials in their place. Images stored as separate files in the res:// folder are not affected by this; those will be used as Godot imported them.
m.GLTFState.HANDLE_BINARY_IMAGE_MODE_EMBED: When importing a glTF file with embedded binary images, embeds textures VRAM compressed with Basis Universal into the generated scene. Images stored as separate files in the res:// folder are not affected by this; those will be used as Godot imported them.

When importing a glTF file with embedded binary images, embeds textures compressed losslessly into the generated scene. Images stored as separate files in the res:// folder are not affected by this; those will be used as Godot imported them.
m.GLTFState.HANDLE_BINARY_IMAGE_MODE_EXTRA: When importing a glTF file with embedded binary images, extracts them and saves them to their own files. This allows the image to be imported by Godot's image importer, which can then have their import options customized by the user, including optionally compressing the image to VRAM texture formats.
m.GLTFState.add_used_extension: Appends an extension to the list of extensions used by this glTF file during serialization. If required is true, the extension will also be added to the list of required extensions. Do not run this in GLTFDocumentExtension._export_post(), as that stage is too late to add extensions. The final list is sorted alphabetically.
m.GLTFState.append_data_to_buffers: Appends the given byte array data to the buffers and creates a GLTFBufferView for it. The index of the destination GLTFBufferView is returned. If deduplication is true, the buffers are first searched for duplicate data, otherwise new bytes are always appended.
m.GLTFState.append_gltf_node: Appends the given GLTFNode to the state, and returns its new index. This can be used to export one Godot node as multiple glTF nodes, or inject new glTF nodes at import time. On import, this must be called before GLTFDocumentExtension._generate_scene_node() finishes for the parent node. On export, this must be called before GLTFDocumentExtension._export_node() runs for the parent node.
m.GLTFState.bake_fps: The baking fps of the animation for either import or export.
m.GLTFState.base_path: The folder path associated with this glTF data. This is used to find other files the glTF file references, like images or binary buffers. This will be set during import when appending from a file, and will be set during export when writing to a file.

m.GLTFState.copyright: The copyright string in the asset header of the glTF file. This is set during import if present and export if non-empty. See the glTF asset header documentation for more information.

This will be set during import when appending from a file, and will be set during export when writing to a file. If writing to a buffer, this will be an empty string.

m.GLTFState.get_images: Gets the images of the glTF file as an array of Texture2Ds. These are the images that the GLTFTexture.src_image index refers to.
m.GLTFState.get_lights: Returns an array of all GLTFLights in the glTF file. These are the lights that the GLTFNode.light index refers to.

m.GLTFState.get_node_index: Returns the index of the GLTFNode corresponding to this Godot scene node. This is the inverse of get_scene_node(). Useful during the export process.
m.GLTFState.get_nodes: Returns an array of all GLTFNodes in the glTF file. These are the nodes that GLTFNode.children and root_nodes refer to. This includes nodes that may not be generated in the Godot scene, or nodes that may generate multiple Godot scene nodes.
m.GLTFState.get_scene_node: Returns the Godot scene node that corresponds to the same index as the GLTFNode it was generated from. This is the inverse of get_node_index(). Useful during the import process.
m.GLTFState.get_skeletons: Returns an array of all GLTFSkeletons in the glTF file. These are the skeletons that the GLTFNode.skeleton index refers to.
m.GLTFState.get_skins: Returns an array of all GLTFSkins in the glTF file. These are the skins that the GLTFNode.skin index refers to.

m.GLTFState.get_unique_names: Returns an array of unique node names. This is used in both the import process and export process.
m.GLTFState.glb_data: The binary buffer attached to a .glb file.
m.GLTFState.handle_binary_image_mode: When importing a glTF file with unimported raw binary images embedded inside of binary blob buffers, in data URIs, or separate files not imported by Godot, this controls how the images are handled. m.GPUParticles2D.DRAW_ORDER_INDEX: Particles are drawn in the order emitted.
m.GPUParticles2D.DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME: Particles are drawn in order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.
m.GPUParticles2D.DRAW_ORDER_REVERSE_LIFETI: Particles are drawn in reverse order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the lowest lifetime is drawn at the front.
m.GPUParticles2D.EMIT_FLAG_CUSTOM: Particle starts with specified CUSTOM data.
m.GPUParticles2D.EMIT_FLAG_POSITION: Particle starts at the specified position.
m.GPUParticles2D.EMIT_FLAG_ROTATION_SCALE: Particle starts with specified rotation and scale.
m.GPUParticles2D.EMIT_FLAG_VELOCITY: Particle starts with the specified velocity vector, which defines the emission direction and speed.
m.GPUParticles2D.amount: The number of particles to emit in one emission cycle. The effective emission rate is (amount * amount_ratio) / lifetime particles per second. Higher values will increase GPU requirements, even if not all particles are visible at a given time or if amount_ratio is decreased.
m.GPUParticles2D.amount_ratio: The ratio of particles that should actually be emitted. If set to a value lower than 1.0, this will set the amount of emitted particles throughout the lifetime to amount * amount_ratio. Unlike changing amount, changing amount_ratio while emitting does not affect already-emitted particles and doesn't cause the particle system to restart. amount_ratio can be used to create effects that make the num…
m.GPUParticles2D.capture_rect: Returns a rectangle containing the positions of all existing particles.
m.GPUParticles2D.collision_base_size: Multiplier for particle's collision radius. 1.0 corresponds to the size of the sprite. If particles appear to sink into the ground when colliding, increase this value. If particles appear to float when colliding, decrease this value. Only effective if ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode is ParticleProcessMaterial.COLLISION_RIGID or ParticleProcessMaterial.COLLISION_HIDE_ON_CONTACT.
m.GPUParticles2D.convert_from_particles: Sets this node's properties to match a given CPUParticles2D node.
m.GPUParticles2D.emit_particle: Emits a single particle. Whether xform, velocity, color and custom are applied depends on the value of flags. See EmitFlags.
m.GPUParticles2D.emitting: If true, particles are being emitted. emitting can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if one_shot is true setting emitting to true will not restart the emission cycle unless all active particles have finished processing. Use the finished signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.
m.GPUParticles2D.explosiveness: How rapidly particles in an emission cycle are emitted. If greater than 0, there will be a gap in emissions before the next cycle begins.
m.GPUParticles2D.finished: Emitted when all active particles have finished processing. To immediately restart the emission cycle, call restart().
m.GPUParticles2D.fixed_fps: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the simulation of the particle system itself.
m.GPUParticles2D.fract_delta: If true, results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.
m.GPUParticles2D.interp_to_end: Causes all the particles in this node to interpolate towards the end of their lifetime.
m.GPUParticles2D.interpolate: Enables particle interpolation, which makes the particle movement smoother when their fixed_fps is lower than the screen refresh rate.
m.GPUParticles2D.lifetime: The amount of time each particle will exist (in seconds). The effective emission rate is (amount * amount_ratio) / lifetime particles per second.
m.GPUParticles2D.local_coords: If true, particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the GPUParticles2D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If false, particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the GPUParticles2D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.
m.GPUParticles2D.one_shot: If true, only one emission cycle occurs. If set true during a cycle, emission will stop at the cycle's end.
m.GPUParticles2D.preprocess: Particle system starts as if it had already run for this many seconds.
m.GPUParticles2D.process_material: Material for processing particles. Can be a ParticleProcessMaterial or a ShaderMaterial.
m.GPUParticles2D.request_particles_process: Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
m.GPUParticles2D.restart: Restarts the particle emission cycle, clearing existing particles. To avoid particles vanishing from the viewport, wait for the finished signal before calling.
m.GPUParticles2D.seed: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if use_fixed_seed is true.
m.GPUParticles2D.speed_scale: Particle system's running speed scaling ratio. A value of 0 can be used to pause the particles.
m.GPUParticles2D.sub_emitter: Path to another GPUParticles2D node that will be used as a subemitter (see ParticleProcessMaterial.sub_emitter_mode). Subemitters can be used to achieve effects such as fireworks, sparks on collision, bubbles popping into water drops, and more.
m.GPUParticles2D.texture: Particle texture. If null, particles will be squares with a size of 1×1 pixels.
m.GPUParticles2D.trail_enabled: If true, enables particle trails using a mesh skinning system.
m.GPUParticles2D.trail_lifetime: The amount of time the particle's trail should represent (in seconds). Only effective if trail_enabled is true.
m.GPUParticles2D.trail_section_subdivision: The number of subdivisions to use for the particle trail rendering. Higher values can result in smoother trail curves, at the cost of performance due to increased mesh complexity. See also trail_sections. Only effective if trail_enabled is true.
m.GPUParticles2D.trail_sections: The number of sections to use for the particle trail rendering. Higher values can result in smoother trail curves, at the cost of performance due to increased mesh complexity. See also trail_section_subdivisions. Only effective if trail_enabled is true.
m.GPUParticles2D.use_fixed_seed: If true, particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in seed. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.
m.GPUParticles2D.visibility_rect: The Rect2 that determines the node's region which needs to be visible on screen for the particle system to be active.
m.GPUParticles3D.DRAW_ORDER_INDEX: Particles are drawn in the order emitted.
m.GPUParticles3D.DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME: Particles are drawn in order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.
m.GPUParticles3D.DRAW_ORDER_REVERSE_LIFETI: Particles are drawn in reverse order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the lowest lifetime is drawn at the front.
m.GPUParticles3D.DRAW_ORDER_VIEW_DEPTH: Particles are drawn in order of depth.
m.GPUParticles3D.EMIT_FLAG_CUSTOM: Particle starts with specified CUSTOM data.
m.GPUParticles3D.EMIT_FLAG_POSITION: Particle starts at the specified position.
m.GPUParticles3D.EMIT_FLAG_ROTATION_SCALE: Particle starts with specified rotation and scale.
m.GPUParticles3D.EMIT_FLAG_VELOCITY: Particle starts with the specified velocity vector, which defines the emission direction and speed.
m.GPUParticles3D.MAX_DRAW_PASSES: Maximum number of draw passes supported.
m.GPUParticles3D.TRANSFORM_ALIGN_DISABLED: Do not align particle transforms relative to the camera or velocity.
m.GPUParticles3D.TRANSFORM_ALIGN_LOCAL_BIL: Align each particle's Z axis to face the camera, while preserving a given axis (X or Y).
m.GPUParticles3D.TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Y_TO_VELO: Align each particle's Y axis to the velocity vector.
m.GPUParticles3D.TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Z_BILLBOA: Align each particle's Z axis to face the camera.
Align each particle's Z axis to face the camera and Y axis to the velocity vector.
m.GPUParticles3D.amount: The number of particles to emit in one emission cycle. The effective emission rate is (amount * amount_ratio) / lifetime particles per second. Higher values will increase GPU requirements, even if not all particles are visible at a given time or if amount_ratio is decreased.
m.GPUParticles3D.amount_ratio: The ratio of particles that should actually be emitted. If set to a value lower than 1.0, this will set the amount of emitted particles throughout the lifetime to amount * amount_ratio. Unlike changing amount, changing amount_ratio while emitting does not affect already-emitted particles and doesn't cause the particle system to restart. amount_ratio can be used to create effects that make the num…
m.GPUParticles3D.capture_aabb: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box that contains all the particles that are active in the current frame.
m.GPUParticles3D.collision_base_size: The base diameter for particle collision in meters. If particles appear to sink into the ground when colliding, increase this value. If particles appear to float when colliding, decrease this value. Only effective if ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode is ParticleProcessMaterial.COLLISION_RIGID or ParticleProcessMaterial.COLLISION_HIDE_ON_CONTACT.
m.GPUParticles3D.convert_from_particles: Sets this node's properties to match a given CPUParticles3D node.
m.GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_1: Mesh that is drawn for the first draw pass.
m.GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_2: Mesh that is drawn for the second draw pass.
m.GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_3: Mesh that is drawn for the third draw pass.
m.GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_4: Mesh that is drawn for the fourth draw pass.
m.GPUParticles3D.draw_passes: The number of draw passes when rendering particles.
m.GPUParticles3D.draw_skin: There is currently no description for this property. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.GPUParticles3D.emit_particle: Emits a single particle. Whether xform, velocity, color and custom are applied depends on the value of flags. See EmitFlags.
m.GPUParticles3D.emitting: If true, particles are being emitted. emitting can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if one_shot is true setting emitting to true will not restart the emission cycle unless all active particles have finished processing. Use the finished signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.
m.GPUParticles3D.explosiveness: Time ratio between each emission. If 0, particles are emitted continuously. If 1, all particles are emitted simultaneously.
m.GPUParticles3D.finished: Emitted when all active particles have finished processing. To immediately restart the emission cycle, call restart().
m.GPUParticles3D.fixed_fps: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the simulation of the particle system itself.
m.GPUParticles3D.fract_delta: If true, results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.
m.GPUParticles3D.get_draw_pass_mesh: Returns the Mesh that is drawn at index pass.
m.GPUParticles3D.interp_to_end: Causes all the particles in this node to interpolate towards the end of their lifetime.
m.GPUParticles3D.interpolate: Enables particle interpolation, which makes the particle movement smoother when their fixed_fps is lower than the screen refresh rate.
m.GPUParticles3D.lifetime: The amount of time each particle will exist (in seconds). The effective emission rate is (amount * amount_ratio) / lifetime particles per second.
m.GPUParticles3D.local_coords: If true, particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the GPUParticles3D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If false, particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the GPUParticles3D node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.
m.GPUParticles3D.one_shot: If true, only the number of particles equal to amount will be emitted.
m.GPUParticles3D.preprocess: Amount of time to preprocess the particles before animation starts. Lets you start the animation some time after particles have started emitting.
m.GPUParticles3D.process_material: Material for processing particles. Can be a ParticleProcessMaterial or a ShaderMaterial.
m.GPUParticles3D.request_particles_process: Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
m.GPUParticles3D.restart: Restarts the particle emission cycle, clearing existing particles. To avoid particles vanishing from the viewport, wait for the finished signal before calling.
m.GPUParticles3D.seed: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if use_fixed_seed is true.
m.GPUParticles3D.set_draw_pass_mesh: Sets the Mesh that is drawn at index pass.
m.GPUParticles3D.speed_scale: Speed scaling ratio. A value of 0 can be used to pause the particles.
m.GPUParticles3D.sub_emitter: Path to another GPUParticles3D node that will be used as a subemitter (see ParticleProcessMaterial.sub_emitter_mode). Subemitters can be used to achieve effects such as fireworks, sparks on collision, bubbles popping into water drops, and more.
m.GPUParticles3D.trail_enabled: If true, enables particle trails using a mesh skinning system. Designed to work with RibbonTrailMesh and TubeTrailMesh.
m.GPUParticles3D.trail_lifetime: The amount of time the particle's trail should represent (in seconds). Only effective if trail_enabled is true.
m.GPUParticles3D.transform_align: The alignment of particles. Use this for billboarding and aligning to velocity.
m.GPUParticles3D.transform_align_axis: When using transform align local billboard, which axis to use for the billboarding. Supports only X or Y.
m.GPUParticles3D.transform_align_channel_f: In the case of billboarded particles, which custom channel to read from to calculate their angle.
m.GPUParticles3D.use_fixed_seed: If true, particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in seed. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.
m.GPUParticles3D.visibility_aabb: The AABB that determines the node's region which needs to be visible on screen for the particle system to be active. GeometryInstance3D.extra_cull_margin is added on each of the AABB's axes. Particle collisions and attraction will only occur within this area.
m.GPUParticlesAttractor3D.attenuation: The particle attractor's attenuation. Higher values result in more gradual pushing of particles as they come closer to the attractor's origin. Zero or negative values will cause particles to be pushed very fast as soon as the touch the attractor's edges.
m.GPUParticlesAttractor3D.cull_mask: The particle rendering layers (VisualInstance3D.layers) that will be affected by the attractor. By default, all particles are affected by an attractor.
m.GPUParticlesAttractor3D.directionality: Adjusts how directional the attractor is. At 0.0, the attractor is not directional at all: it will attract particles towards its center. At 1.0, the attractor is fully directional: particles will always be pushed towards local -Z (or +Z if strength is negative).
m.GPUParticlesAttractor3D.strength: Adjusts the strength of the attractor. If strength is negative, particles will be pushed in the opposite direction. Particles will be pushed away from the attractor's origin if directionality is 0.0, or towards local +Z if directionality is greater than 0.0.
m.GPUParticlesAttractorBox3D.size: The attractor box's size in 3D units.
m.GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D.radius: The attractor sphere's radius in 3D units.
m.GPUParticlesAttractorVectorField3D.size: The size of the vector field box in 3D units.
m.GPUParticlesAttractorVectorField3D.textu: The 3D texture to be used. Values are linearly interpolated between the texture's pixels.
m.GPUParticlesCollision3D.cull_mask: The particle rendering layers (VisualInstance3D.layers) that will be affected by the collision shape. By default, all particles that have ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode set to ParticleProcessMaterial.COLLISION_RIGID or ParticleProcessMaterial.COLLISION_HIDE_ON_CONTACT will be affected by a collision shape.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D.size: The collision box's size in 3D units.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.RESOL: Generate a 1024×1024 heightmap. Intended for large scenes with distant particles.
Generate a 2048×2048 heightmap. Intended for very large scenes with distant particles.
Generate a 256×256 heightmap. Intended for small-scale scenes, or larger scenes with no distant particles.
Generate a 4096×4096 heightmap. Intended for huge scenes with distant particles.
Generate a 512×512 heightmap. Intended for medium-scale scenes, or larger scenes with no distant particles.
Generate a 8192×8192 heightmap. Intended for gigantic scenes with distant particles.
Represents the size of the Resolution enum.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.UPDAT: Update the heightmap every frame. This has a significant performance cost. This update should only be used when geometry that particles can collide with changes significantly during gameplay.

Only update the heightmap when the GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D node is moved, or when the camera moves if follow_camera_enabled is true. An update can be forced by slightly moving the GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D in any direction, or by calling RenderingServer.particles_collision_height_field_update().
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.follo: If true, the GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D will follow the current camera in global space. The GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D does not need to be a child of the Camera3D node for this to work.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.get_h: Returns true if the specified layer of the heightfield_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 20, inclusive.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.heigh: The visual layers to account for when updating the heightmap. Only MeshInstance3Ds whose VisualInstance3D.layers match with this heightfield_mask will be included in the heightmap collision update. By default, all 20 user-visible layers are taken into account for updating the heightmap collision.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.resol: Higher resolutions can represent small details more accurately in large scenes, at the cost of lower performance. If update_mode is UPDATE_MODE_ALWAYS, consider using the lowest resolution possible.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.set_h: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the heightfield_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 20, inclusive.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.size: The collision heightmap's size in 3D units. To improve heightmap quality, size should be set as small as possible while covering the parts of the scene you need.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.updat: The update policy to use for the generated heightmap.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.RESOLUTION_16: Bake a 16×16×16 signed distance field. This is the fastest option, but also the least precise.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.RESOLUTION_51: Bake a 512×512×512 signed distance field. This is the slowest option, but also the most precise.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.RESOLUTION_MA: Represents the size of the Resolution enum.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.bake_mask: The visual layers to account for when baking the particle collision SDF. Only MeshInstance3Ds whose VisualInstance3D.layers match with this bake_mask will be included in the generated particle collision SDF. By default, all objects are taken into account for the particle collision SDF baking.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.get_bake_mask: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the bake_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.resolution: The bake resolution to use for the signed distance field texture. The texture must be baked again for changes to the resolution property to be effective. Higher resolutions have a greater performance cost and take more time to bake. Higher resolutions also result in larger baked textures, leading to increased VRAM and storage space requirements. To improve performance and reduce bake times, use t…
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.set_bake_mask: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the bake_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.size: The collision SDF's size in 3D units. To improve SDF quality, the size should be set as small as possible while covering the parts of the scene you need.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.texture: The 3D texture representing the signed distance field.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.thickness: The collision shape's thickness. Unlike other particle colliders, GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D is actually hollow on the inside. thickness can be increased to prevent particles from tunneling through the collision shape at high speeds, or when the GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D is moved.
m.GPUParticlesCollisionSphere3D.radius: The collision sphere's radius in 3D units.

m.Generic6DOFJoint3D.PARAM_ANGULAR_ERP: When rotating across the axes, this error tolerance factor defines how much the correction gets slowed down. The lower, the slower.
m.Generic6DOFJoint3D.PARAM_ANGULAR_FORCE_L: The maximum amount of force that can occur, when rotating around the axes.
m.Generic6DOFJoint3D.PARAM_ANGULAR_LIMIT_S: The speed of all rotations across the axes.

m.Generic6DOFJoint3D.PARAM_ANGULAR_RESTITU: The amount of rotational restitution across the axes. The lower, the more restitution occurs.

m.Geometry2D.END_BUTT: Endpoints are squared off with no extension.
m.Geometry2D.END_JOINED: Endpoints are joined using the PolyJoinType value and the path filled as a polyline.
m.Geometry2D.END_POLYGON: Endpoints are joined using the PolyJoinType value and the path filled as a polygon.
m.Geometry2D.END_ROUND: Endpoints are rounded off and extended by delta units.
m.Geometry2D.END_SQUARE: Endpoints are squared off and extended by delta units.
m.Geometry2D.JOIN_MITER: There's a necessary limit to mitered joins since offsetting edges that join at very acute angles will produce excessively long and narrow "spikes". For any given edge join, when miter offsetting would exceed that maximum distance, "square" joining is applied.
m.Geometry2D.JOIN_ROUND: While flattened paths can never perfectly trace an arc, they are approximated by a series of arc chords.
m.Geometry2D.JOIN_SQUARE: Squaring is applied uniformally at all convex edge joins at 1 * delta.
m.Geometry2D.OPERATION_DIFFERENCE: Create regions where subject polygons are filled except where clip polygons are filled.
m.Geometry2D.OPERATION_INTERSECTION: Create regions where both subject and clip polygons are filled.
m.Geometry2D.OPERATION_UNION: Create regions where either subject or clip polygons (or both) are filled.
m.Geometry2D.OPERATION_XOR: Create regions where either subject or clip polygons are filled but not where both are filled.
m.Geometry2D.bresenham_line: Returns the Bresenham line [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bresenham%27s_line_algorithm] between the from and to points. A Bresenham line is a series of pixels that draws a line and is always 1-pixel thick on every row and column of the drawing (never more, never less).
m.Geometry2D.clip_polygons: Clips polygon_a against polygon_b and returns an array of clipped polygons. This performs OPERATION_DIFFERENCE between polygons. Returns an empty array if polygon_b completely overlaps polygon_a.
