m.Geometry2D.clip_polyline_with_polygon: Clips polyline against polygon and returns an array of clipped polylines. This performs OPERATION_DIFFERENCE between the polyline and the polygon. This operation can be thought of as cutting a line with a closed shape.
m.Geometry2D.convex_hull: Given an array of Vector2s, returns the convex hull as a list of points in counterclockwise order. The last point is the same as the first one.
m.Geometry2D.decompose_polygon_in_convex: Decomposes the polygon into multiple convex hulls and returns an array of PackedVector2Array.
m.Geometry2D.exclude_polygons: Mutually excludes common area defined by intersection of polygon_a and polygon_b (see intersect_polygons()) and returns an array of excluded polygons. This performs OPERATION_XOR between polygons. In other words, returns all but common area between polygons.
m.Geometry2D.get_closest_point_to_segment: Returns the 2D point on the 2D segment (s1, s2) that is closest to point. The returned point will always be inside the specified segment.
m.Geometry2D.get_closest_point_to_segment_: Returns the 2D point on the 2D line defined by (s1, s2) that is closest to point. The returned point can be inside the segment (s1, s2) or outside of it, i.e. somewhere on the line extending from the segment.
m.Geometry2D.get_closest_points_between_se: Given the two 2D segments (p1, q1) and (p2, q2), finds those two points on the two segments that are closest to each other. Returns a PackedVector2Array that contains this point on (p1, q1) as well the accompanying point on (p2, q2).
m.Geometry2D.intersect_polygons: Intersects polygon_a with polygon_b and returns an array of intersected polygons. This performs OPERATION_INTERSECTION between polygons. In other words, returns common area shared by polygons. Returns an empty array if no intersection occurs.
m.Geometry2D.intersect_polyline_with_polyg: Intersects polyline with polygon and returns an array of intersected polylines. This performs OPERATION_INTERSECTION between the polyline and the polygon. This operation can be thought of as chopping a line with a closed shape.
m.Geometry2D.is_point_in_circle: Returns true if point is inside the circle or if it's located exactly on the circle's boundary, otherwise returns false.
m.Geometry2D.is_point_in_polygon: Returns true if point is inside polygon or if it's located exactly on polygon's boundary, otherwise returns false.
m.Geometry2D.is_polygon_clockwise: Returns true if polygon's vertices are ordered in clockwise order, otherwise returns false.
m.Geometry2D.line_intersects_line: Returns the point of intersection between the two lines (from_a, dir_a) and (from_b, dir_b). Returns a Vector2, or null if the lines are parallel.
m.Geometry2D.make_atlas: Given an array of Vector2s representing tiles, builds an atlas. The returned dictionary has two keys: points is a PackedVector2Array that specifies the positions of each tile, size contains the overall size of the whole atlas as Vector2i.
m.Geometry2D.merge_polygons: Merges (combines) polygon_a and polygon_b and returns an array of merged polygons. This performs OPERATION_UNION between polygons.
m.Geometry2D.offset_polygon: Inflates or deflates polygon by delta units (pixels). If delta is positive, makes the polygon grow outward. If delta is negative, shrinks the polygon inward. Returns an array of polygons because inflating/deflating may result in multiple discrete polygons. Returns an empty array if delta is negative and the absolute value of it approximately exceeds the minimum bounding rectangle dimensions of th…
m.Geometry2D.offset_polyline: Inflates or deflates polyline by delta units (pixels), producing polygons. If delta is positive, makes the polyline grow outward. Returns an array of polygons because inflating/deflating may result in multiple discrete polygons. If delta is negative, returns an empty array.
m.Geometry2D.point_is_inside_triangle: Returns if point is inside the triangle specified by a, b and c.
m.Geometry2D.segment_intersects_circle: Given the 2D segment (segment_from, segment_to), returns the position on the segment (as a number between 0 and 1) at which the segment hits the circle that is located at position circle_position and has radius circle_radius. If the segment does not intersect the circle, -1 is returned (this is also the case if the line extending the segment would intersect the circle, but the segment does not).
m.Geometry2D.segment_intersects_segment: Checks if two line segments intersect, with line a between from_a and to_a and line b between from_b and to_b. If the line segments intersect, the point of intersection is returned as a Vector2. If no intersection takes place, null is returned.
m.Geometry2D.triangulate_delaunay: Triangulates the area specified by discrete set of points such that no point is inside the circumcircle of any resulting triangle. Returns a PackedInt32Array where each triangle consists of three consecutive point indices into points (i.e. the returned array will have n * 3 elements, with n being the number of found triangles). If the triangulation did not succeed, an empty PackedInt32Array is re…
m.Geometry2D.triangulate_polygon: Triangulates the polygon specified by the points in polygon. Returns a PackedInt32Array where each triangle consists of three consecutive point indices into polygon (i.e. the returned array will have n * 3 elements, with n being the number of found triangles). Output triangles will always be counter clockwise, and the contour will be flipped if it's clockwise. If the triangulation did not succeed…
m.Geometry3D.build_box_planes: Returns an array with 6 Planes that describe the sides of a box centered at the origin. The box size is defined by extents, which represents one (positive) corner of the box (i.e. half its actual size).
m.Geometry3D.build_capsule_planes: Returns an array of Planes closely bounding a faceted capsule centered at the origin with radius radius and height height. The parameter sides defines how many planes will be generated for the side part of the capsule, whereas lats gives the number of latitudinal steps at the bottom and top of the capsule. The parameter axis describes the axis along which the capsule is oriented (0 for X, 1 for Y…
m.Geometry3D.build_cylinder_planes: Returns an array of Planes closely bounding a faceted cylinder centered at the origin with radius radius and height height. The parameter sides defines how many planes will be generated for the round part of the cylinder. The parameter axis describes the axis along which the cylinder is oriented (0 for X, 1 for Y, 2 for Z).
m.Geometry3D.clip_polygon: Clips the polygon defined by the points in points against the plane and returns the points of the clipped polygon.
m.Geometry3D.compute_convex_mesh_points: Calculates and returns all the vertex points of a convex shape defined by an array of planes.
m.Geometry3D.get_closest_point_to_segment: Returns the 3D point on the 3D segment (s1, s2) that is closest to point. The returned point will always be inside the specified segment.
m.Geometry3D.get_closest_point_to_segment_: Returns the 3D point on the 3D line defined by (s1, s2) that is closest to point. The returned point can be inside the segment (s1, s2) or outside of it, i.e. somewhere on the line extending from the segment.
m.Geometry3D.get_closest_points_between_se: Given the two 3D segments (p1, p2) and (q1, q2), finds those two points on the two segments that are closest to each other. Returns a PackedVector3Array that contains this point on (p1, p2) as well the accompanying point on (q1, q2).
m.Geometry3D.get_triangle_barycentric_coor: Returns a Vector3 containing weights based on how close a 3D position (point) is to a triangle's different vertices (a, b and c). This is useful for interpolating between the data of different vertices in a triangle. One example use case is using this to smoothly rotate over a mesh instead of relying solely on face normals.
m.Geometry3D.ray_intersects_triangle: Tests if the 3D ray starting at from with the direction of dir intersects the triangle specified by a, b and c. If yes, returns the point of intersection as Vector3. If no intersection takes place, returns null.
m.Geometry3D.segment_intersects_convex: Given a convex hull defined though the Planes in the array planes, tests if the segment (from, to) intersects with that hull. If an intersection is found, returns a PackedVector3Array containing the point the intersection and the hull's normal. Otherwise, returns an empty array.
m.Geometry3D.segment_intersects_cylinder: Checks if the segment (from, to) intersects the cylinder with height height that is centered at the origin and has radius radius. If no, returns an empty PackedVector3Array. If an intersection takes place, the returned array contains the point of intersection and the cylinder's normal at the point of intersection.
m.Geometry3D.segment_intersects_sphere: Checks if the segment (from, to) intersects the sphere that is located at sphere_position and has radius sphere_radius. If no, returns an empty PackedVector3Array. If yes, returns a PackedVector3Array containing the point of intersection and the sphere's normal at the point of intersection.
m.Geometry3D.segment_intersects_triangle: Tests if the segment (from, to) intersects the triangle a, b, c. If yes, returns the point of intersection as Vector3. If no intersection takes place, returns null.
m.Geometry3D.tetrahedralize_delaunay: Tetrahedralizes the volume specified by a discrete set of points in 3D space, ensuring that no point lies within the circumsphere of any resulting tetrahedron. The method returns a PackedInt32Array where each tetrahedron consists of four consecutive point indices into the points array (resulting in an array with n * 4 elements, where n is the number of tetrahedra found). If the tetrahedralization…
m.GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_DISABLED: Disabled global illumination mode. Use for dynamic objects that do not contribute to global illumination (such as characters). When using VoxelGI and SDFGI, the geometry will receive indirect lighting and reflections but the geometry will not be considered in GI baking.
m.GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_DYNAMIC: Dynamic global illumination mode. Use for dynamic objects that contribute to global illumination. This GI mode is only effective when using VoxelGI, but it has a higher performance impact than GI_MODE_STATIC. When using other GI methods, this will act the same as GI_MODE_DISABLED. When using LightmapGI, the object will receive indirect lighting using lightmap probes instead of using the baked lig…
m.GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_STATIC: Baked global illumination mode. Use for static objects that contribute to global illumination (such as level geometry). This GI mode is effective when using VoxelGI, SDFGI and LightmapGI.
m.GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTIN: Will cast shadows from all visible faces in the GeometryInstance3D.
Will not cast any shadows. Use this to improve performance for small geometry that is unlikely to cast noticeable shadows (such as debris).
Will cast shadows from all visible faces in the GeometryInstance3D.
Will only show the shadows casted from this object.
m.GeometryInstance3D.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE: Will fade-in its visibility dependencies (see Node3D.visibility_parent) when reaching the limits of its own visibility range. This is slower than VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DISABLED, but it can provide smoother transitions. The fading range is determined by visibility_range_begin_margin and visibility_range_end_margin.

Will not fade itself nor its visibility dependencies, hysteresis will be used instead. This is the fastest approach to manual LOD, but it can result in noticeable LOD transitions depending on how the LOD meshes are authored. See visibility_range_begin and Node3D.visibility_parent for more information.

Will fade-out itself when reaching the limits of its own visibility range. This is slower than VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DISABLED, but it can provide smoother transitions. The fading range is determined by visibility_range_begin_margin and visibility_range_end_margin.
m.GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow: The mode used to cast shadows from this instance.
m.GeometryInstance3D.custom_aabb: Overrides the bounding box of this node with a custom one. This can be used to avoid the expensive AABB recalculation that happens when a skeleton is used with a MeshInstance3D or to have precise control over the MeshInstance3D's bounding box. To use the default AABB, set value to an AABB with all fields set to 0.0. To avoid frustum culling, set custom_aabb to a very large AABB that covers your e…
m.GeometryInstance3D.extra_cull_margin: The extra distance added to the GeometryInstance3D's bounding box (AABB) to increase its cull box.
m.GeometryInstance3D.get_instance_shader_p: Get the value of a shader parameter as set on this instance.
m.GeometryInstance3D.gi_lightmap_texel_sca: The texel density to use for lightmapping in LightmapGI. Greater scale values provide higher resolution in the lightmap, which can result in sharper shadows for lights that have both direct and indirect light baked. However, greater scale values will also increase the space taken by the mesh in the lightmap texture, which increases the memory, storage, and bake time requirements. When using a sin…
m.GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode: The global illumination mode to use for the whole geometry. To avoid inconsistent results, use a mode that matches the purpose of the mesh during gameplay (static/dynamic).
m.GeometryInstance3D.ignore_occlusion_cull: If true, disables occlusion culling for this instance. Useful for gizmos that must be rendered even when occlusion culling is in use.
m.GeometryInstance3D.lod_bias: Changes how quickly the mesh transitions to a lower level of detail. A value of 0 will force the mesh to its lowest level of detail, a value of 1 will use the default settings, and larger values will keep the mesh in a higher level of detail at farther distances.
m.GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay: The material overlay for the whole geometry.
m.GeometryInstance3D.material_override: The material override for the whole geometry.
m.GeometryInstance3D.set_instance_shader_p: Set the value of a shader uniform for this instance only (per-instance uniform). See also ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter() to assign a uniform on all instances using the same ShaderMaterial.
m.GeometryInstance3D.transparency: The transparency applied to the whole geometry (as a multiplier of the materials' existing transparency). 0.0 is fully opaque, while 1.0 is fully transparent. Values greater than 0.0 (exclusive) will force the geometry's materials to go through the transparent pipeline, which is slower to render and can exhibit rendering issues due to incorrect transparency sorting. However, unlike using a transp…
m.GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begi: Starting distance from which the GeometryInstance3D will be visible, taking visibility_range_begin_margin into account as well. The default value of 0 is used to disable the range check.
Margin for the visibility_range_begin threshold. The GeometryInstance3D will only change its visibility state when it goes over or under the visibility_range_begin threshold by this amount.
m.GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end: Distance from which the GeometryInstance3D will be hidden, taking visibility_range_end_margin into account as well. The default value of 0 is used to disable the range check.
m.GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end_: Margin for the visibility_range_end threshold. The GeometryInstance3D will only change its visibility state when it goes over or under the visibility_range_end threshold by this amount.
m.GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_fade: Controls which instances will be faded when approaching the limits of the visibility range.
m.GodotInstance.focus_in: Notifies the instance that it is now in focus.
m.GodotInstance.focus_out: Notifies the instance that it is now not in focus.
m.GodotInstance.is_started: Returns true if this instance has been fully started.
m.GodotInstance.iteration: Runs a single iteration of the main loop. Returns true if the engine is attempting to quit.
m.GodotInstance.pause: Notifies the instance that it is going to be paused.
m.GodotInstance.resume: Notifies the instance that it is being resumed.
m.GodotInstance.start: Finishes this instance's startup sequence. Returns true on success.
m.Gradient.GRADIENT_COLOR_SPACE_OKLAB: Oklab [https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/] color space. This color space provides a smooth and uniform-looking transition between colors.
m.Gradient.GRADIENT_INTERPOLATE_CONSTANT: Constant interpolation, color changes abruptly at each point and stays uniform between. This might cause visible aliasing when used for a gradient texture in some cases.
m.Gradient.add_point: Adds the specified color to the gradient, with the specified offset.
m.Gradient.get_color: Returns the color of the gradient color at index point.
m.Gradient.get_offset: Returns the offset of the gradient color at index point.
m.Gradient.get_point_count: Returns the number of colors in the gradient.
m.Gradient.interpolation_color_space: The color space used to interpolate between points of the gradient. It does not affect the returned colors, which will always use nonlinear sRGB encoding.
m.Gradient.interpolation_mode: The algorithm used to interpolate between points of the gradient.
m.Gradient.remove_point: Removes the color at index point.
m.Gradient.sample: Returns the interpolated color specified by offset. offset should be between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). Using a value lower than 0.0 will return the same color as 0.0, and using a value higher than 1.0 will return the same color as 1.0. If your input value is not within this range, consider using @GlobalScope.remap() on the input value with output values set to 0.0 and 1.0.
m.Gradient.set_color: Sets the color of the gradient color at index point.
m.Gradient.set_offset: Sets the offset for the gradient color at index point.
m.GradientTexture1D.gradient: The Gradient used to fill the texture.
m.GradientTexture1D.use_hdr: If true, the generated texture will support high dynamic range (Image.FORMAT_RGBAF format). This allows for glow effects to work if Environment.glow_enabled is true. If false, the generated texture will use low dynamic range; overbright colors will be clamped (Image.FORMAT_RGBA8 format).
m.GradientTexture1D.width: The number of color samples that will be obtained from the Gradient.
m.GradientTexture2D.FILL_CONIC: The colors are linearly interpolated in a cone pattern.
m.GradientTexture2D.FILL_LINEAR: The colors are linearly interpolated in a straight line.
m.GradientTexture2D.FILL_RADIAL: The colors are linearly interpolated in a circular pattern.
m.GradientTexture2D.FILL_SQUARE: The colors are linearly interpolated in a square pattern.
m.GradientTexture2D.REPEAT: The texture is filled starting from fill_from to fill_to offsets, repeating the same pattern in both directions.
m.GradientTexture2D.REPEAT_MIRROR: The texture is filled starting from fill_from to fill_to offsets, mirroring the pattern in both directions.
m.GradientTexture2D.REPEAT_NONE: The gradient fill is restricted to the range defined by fill_from to fill_to offsets.
m.GradientTexture2D.fill_from: The initial offset used to fill the texture specified in UV coordinates.
m.GradientTexture2D.fill_to: The final offset used to fill the texture specified in UV coordinates.
m.GradientTexture2D.gradient: The Gradient used to fill the texture.
m.GradientTexture2D.height: The number of vertical color samples that will be obtained from the Gradient, which also represents the texture's height.
m.GradientTexture2D.use_hdr: If true, the generated texture will support high dynamic range (Image.FORMAT_RGBAF format). This allows for glow effects to work if Environment.glow_enabled is true. If false, the generated texture will use low dynamic range; overbright colors will be clamped (Image.FORMAT_RGBA8 format).
m.GradientTexture2D.width: The number of horizontal color samples that will be obtained from the Gradient, which also represents the texture's width.
m.GraphEdit.GRID_PATTERN_LINES: Draw the grid using solid lines.
m.GraphEdit.SCROLL_PANS: Mouse Wheel will move the view, Ctrl + Mouse Wheel will zoom.
m.GraphEdit.SCROLL_ZOOMS: Mouse Wheel will zoom, Ctrl + Mouse Wheel will move the view.
m.GraphEdit._get_connection_line: Virtual method which can be overridden to customize how connections are drawn.
m.GraphEdit._is_in_input_hotzone: Returns whether the mouse_position is in the input hot zone.
m.GraphEdit._is_in_output_hotzone: Returns whether the mouse_position is in the output hot zone. For more information on hot zones, see _is_in_input_hotzone().
m.GraphEdit._is_node_hover_valid: This virtual method can be used to insert additional error detection while the user is dragging a connection over a valid port.
m.GraphEdit.add_valid_connection_type: Allows the connection between two different port types. The port type is defined individually for the left and the right port of each slot with the GraphNode.set_slot() method.
m.GraphEdit.add_valid_left_disconnect_type: Allows to disconnect nodes when dragging from the left port of the GraphNode's slot if it has the specified type. See also remove_valid_left_disconnect_type().
m.GraphEdit.add_valid_right_disconnect_typ: Allows to disconnect nodes when dragging from the right port of the GraphNode's slot if it has the specified type. See also remove_valid_right_disconnect_type().
m.GraphEdit.arrange_nodes: Rearranges selected nodes in a layout with minimum crossings between connections and uniform horizontal and vertical gap between nodes.
m.GraphEdit.attach_graph_element_to_frame: Attaches the element GraphElement to the frame GraphFrame.
m.GraphEdit.begin_node_move: Emitted at the beginning of a GraphElement's movement.
m.GraphEdit.connect_node: Create a connection between the from_port of the from_node GraphNode and the to_port of the to_node GraphNode. If the connection already exists, no connection is created.
m.GraphEdit.connection_drag_ended: Emitted at the end of a connection drag.
m.GraphEdit.connection_drag_started: Emitted at the beginning of a connection drag.
m.GraphEdit.connection_from_empty: Emitted when user drags a connection from an input port into the empty space of the graph.
m.GraphEdit.connection_lines_antialiased: If true, the lines between nodes will use antialiasing.
m.GraphEdit.connection_lines_curvature: The curvature of the lines between the nodes. 0 results in straight lines.
m.GraphEdit.connection_lines_thickness: The thickness of the lines between the nodes.
m.GraphEdit.connection_request: Emitted to the GraphEdit when the connection between the from_port of the from_node GraphNode and the to_port of the to_node GraphNode is attempted to be created.
m.GraphEdit.connection_to_empty: Emitted when user drags a connection from an output port into the empty space of the graph.
m.GraphEdit.copy_nodes_request: Emitted when this GraphEdit captures a ui_copy action (Ctrl + C by default). In general, this signal indicates that the selected GraphElements should be copied.
m.GraphEdit.cut_nodes_request: Emitted when this GraphEdit captures a ui_cut action (Ctrl + X by default). In general, this signal indicates that the selected GraphElements should be cut.
m.GraphEdit.delete_nodes_request: Emitted when this GraphEdit captures a ui_graph_delete action (Delete by default).
m.GraphEdit.detach_graph_element_from_fram: Detaches the element GraphElement from the GraphFrame it is currently attached to.
m.GraphEdit.disconnect_node: Removes the connection between the from_port of the from_node GraphNode and the to_port of the to_node GraphNode. If the connection does not exist, no connection is removed.
m.GraphEdit.disconnection_request: Emitted to the GraphEdit when the connection between from_port of from_node GraphNode and to_port of to_node GraphNode is attempted to be removed.
m.GraphEdit.duplicate_nodes_request: Emitted when this GraphEdit captures a ui_graph_duplicate action (Ctrl + D by default). In general, this signal indicates that the selected GraphElements should be duplicated.
m.GraphEdit.end_node_move: Emitted at the end of a GraphElement's movement.
m.GraphEdit.force_connection_drag_end: Ends the creation of the current connection. In other words, if you are dragging a connection you can use this method to abort the process and remove the line that followed your cursor.
m.GraphEdit.frame_rect_changed: Emitted when the GraphFrame frame is resized to new_rect.
m.GraphEdit.get_attached_nodes_of_frame: Returns an array of node names that are attached to the GraphFrame with the given name.
m.GraphEdit.get_closest_connection_at_poin: Returns the closest connection to the given point in screen space. If no connection is found within max_distance pixels, an empty Dictionary is returned.
m.GraphEdit.get_connection_count: Returns the number of connections from from_port of from_node.
m.GraphEdit.get_connection_line: Returns the points which would make up a connection between from_node and to_node.
m.GraphEdit.get_connection_list_from_node: Returns an Array containing a list of all connections for node.
m.GraphEdit.get_connections_intersecting_w: Returns an Array containing the list of connections that intersect with the given Rect2.
m.GraphEdit.get_element_frame: Returns the GraphFrame that contains the GraphElement with the given name.
m.GraphEdit.get_menu_hbox: Gets the HBoxContainer that contains the zooming and grid snap controls in the top left of the graph. You can use this method to reposition the toolbar or to add your own custom controls to it.
m.GraphEdit.graph_elements_linked_to_frame: Emitted when one or more GraphElements are dropped onto the GraphFrame named frame, when they were not previously attached to any other one.
m.GraphEdit.grid_pattern: The pattern used for drawing the grid.
m.GraphEdit.is_node_connected: Returns true if the from_port of the from_node GraphNode is connected to the to_port of the to_node GraphNode.
m.GraphEdit.is_valid_connection_type: Returns whether it's possible to make a connection between two different port types. The port type is defined individually for the left and the right port of each slot with the GraphNode.set_slot() method.
m.GraphEdit.minimap_enabled: If true, the minimap is visible.
m.GraphEdit.minimap_opacity: The opacity of the minimap rectangle.
m.GraphEdit.minimap_size: The size of the minimap rectangle. The map itself is based on the size of the grid area and is scaled to fit this rectangle.
m.GraphEdit.node_deselected: Emitted when the given GraphElement node is deselected.
m.GraphEdit.node_selected: Emitted when the given GraphElement node is selected.
m.GraphEdit.panning_scheme: Defines the control scheme for panning with mouse wheel.
m.GraphEdit.paste_nodes_request: Emitted when this GraphEdit captures a ui_paste action (Ctrl + V by default). In general, this signal indicates that previously copied GraphElements should be pasted.
m.GraphEdit.popup_request: Emitted when a popup is requested. Happens on right-clicking in the GraphEdit. at_position is the position of the mouse pointer when the signal is sent.
m.GraphEdit.remove_valid_connection_type: Disallows the connection between two different port types previously allowed by add_valid_connection_type(). The port type is defined individually for the left and the right port of each slot with the GraphNode.set_slot() method.
m.GraphEdit.remove_valid_left_disconnect_t: Disallows to disconnect nodes when dragging from the left port of the GraphNode's slot if it has the specified type. Use this to disable a disconnection previously allowed with add_valid_left_disconnect_type().
m.GraphEdit.remove_valid_right_disconnect_: Disallows to disconnect nodes when dragging from the right port of the GraphNode's slot if it has the specified type. Use this to disable a disconnection previously allowed with add_valid_right_disconnect_type().
m.GraphEdit.right_disconnects: If true, enables disconnection of existing connections in the GraphEdit by dragging the right end.
m.GraphEdit.scroll_offset_changed: Emitted when the scroll offset is changed by the user. It will not be emitted when changed in code.
m.GraphEdit.set_connection_activity: Sets the coloration of the connection between from_node's from_port and to_node's to_port with the color provided in the activity theme property. The color is linearly interpolated between the connection color and the activity color using amount as weight.
m.GraphEdit.set_selected: Sets the specified node as the one selected.
m.GraphEdit.show_arrange_button: If true, the button to automatically arrange graph nodes is visible.
m.GraphEdit.show_grid: If true, the grid is visible.
m.GraphEdit.show_grid_buttons: If true, buttons that allow to configure grid and snapping options are visible.
m.GraphEdit.show_menu: If true, the menu toolbar is visible.
m.GraphEdit.show_minimap_button: If true, the button to toggle the minimap is visible.
m.GraphEdit.show_zoom_buttons: If true, buttons that allow to change and reset the zoom level are visible.
m.GraphEdit.show_zoom_label: If true, the label with the current zoom level is visible. The zoom level is displayed in percents.
m.GraphEdit.snapping_distance: The snapping distance in pixels, also determines the grid line distance.
m.GraphEdit.type_names: Dictionary of human-readable port type names.
m.GraphEdit.zoom_step: The step of each zoom level.
m.GraphElement.delete_request: Emitted when removing the GraphElement is requested.
m.GraphElement.draggable: If true, the user can drag the GraphElement.
m.GraphElement.dragged: Emitted when the GraphElement is dragged.
m.GraphElement.node_deselected: Emitted when the GraphElement is deselected.
m.GraphElement.node_selected: Emitted when the GraphElement is selected.
m.GraphElement.position_offset: The offset of the GraphElement, relative to the scroll offset of the GraphEdit.
m.GraphElement.position_offset_changed: Emitted when the GraphElement is moved.
m.GraphElement.raise_request: Emitted when displaying the GraphElement over other ones is requested. Happens on focusing (clicking into) the GraphElement.
m.GraphElement.resizable: If true, the user can resize the GraphElement.
m.GraphElement.resize_end: Emitted when releasing the mouse button after dragging the resizer handle (see resizable).
m.GraphElement.resize_request: Emitted when resizing the GraphElement is requested. Happens on dragging the resizer handle (see resizable).
m.GraphElement.scaling_menus: If true, PopupMenus that are descendants of the GraphElement are scaled with the GraphEdit zoom.
m.GraphElement.selectable: If true, the user can select the GraphElement.
m.GraphElement.selected: If true, the GraphElement is selected.
m.GraphFrame.autoshrink_changed: Emitted when autoshrink_enabled or autoshrink_margin changes.
m.GraphFrame.autoshrink_enabled: If true, the frame's rect will be adjusted automatically to enclose all attached GraphElements.
m.GraphFrame.autoshrink_margin: The margin around the attached nodes that is used to calculate the size of the frame when autoshrink_enabled is true.
m.GraphFrame.drag_margin: The margin inside the frame that can be used to drag the frame.
m.GraphFrame.get_titlebar_hbox: Returns the HBoxContainer used for the title bar, only containing a Label for displaying the title by default.
m.GraphFrame.tint_color: The color of the frame when tint_color_enabled is true.
m.GraphFrame.tint_color_enabled: If true, the tint color will be used to tint the frame.
m.GraphFrame.title: Title of the frame.
m.GraphNode._draw_port: There is currently no description for this method. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.GraphNode.clear_all_slots: Disables all slots of the GraphNode. This will remove all input/output ports from the GraphNode.
m.GraphNode.clear_slot: Disables the slot with the given slot_index. This will remove the corresponding input and output port from the GraphNode.
m.GraphNode.get_input_port_color: Returns the Color of the input port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_input_port_count: Returns the number of slots with an enabled input port.
m.GraphNode.get_input_port_position: Returns the position of the input port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_input_port_slot: Returns the corresponding slot index of the input port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_input_port_type: Returns the type of the input port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_output_port_color: Returns the Color of the output port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_output_port_count: Returns the number of slots with an enabled output port.
m.GraphNode.get_output_port_position: Returns the position of the output port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_output_port_slot: Returns the corresponding slot index of the output port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_output_port_type: Returns the type of the output port with the given port_idx.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_color_left: Returns the left (input) Color of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_color_right: Returns the right (output) Color of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_custom_icon_left: Returns the left (input) custom Texture2D of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_custom_icon_right: Returns the right (output) custom Texture2D of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_metadata_left: Returns the left (input) metadata of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_metadata_right: Returns the right (output) metadata of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_type_left: Returns the left (input) type of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_slot_type_right: Returns the right (output) type of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.get_titlebar_hbox: Returns the HBoxContainer used for the title bar, only containing a Label for displaying the title by default. This can be used to add custom controls to the title bar such as option or close buttons.
m.GraphNode.ignore_invalid_connection_type: If true, you can connect ports with different types, even if the connection was not explicitly allowed in the parent GraphEdit.
m.GraphNode.is_slot_draw_stylebox: Returns true if the background StyleBox of the slot with the given slot_index is drawn.
m.GraphNode.is_slot_enabled_left: Returns true if left (input) side of the slot with the given slot_index is enabled.
m.GraphNode.is_slot_enabled_right: Returns true if right (output) side of the slot with the given slot_index is enabled.
m.GraphNode.set_slot: Sets properties of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_color_left: Sets the Color of the left (input) side of the slot with the given slot_index to color.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_color_right: Sets the Color of the right (output) side of the slot with the given slot_index to color.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_custom_icon_left: Sets the custom Texture2D of the left (input) side of the slot with the given slot_index to custom_icon.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_custom_icon_right: Sets the custom Texture2D of the right (output) side of the slot with the given slot_index to custom_icon.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_draw_stylebox: Toggles the background StyleBox of the slot with the given slot_index.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_enabled_left: Toggles the left (input) side of the slot with the given slot_index. If enable is true, a port will appear on the left side and the slot will be able to be connected from this side.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_enabled_right: Toggles the right (output) side of the slot with the given slot_index. If enable is true, a port will appear on the right side and the slot will be able to be connected from this side.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_metadata_left: Sets the custom metadata for the left (input) side of the slot with the given slot_index to value.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_metadata_right: Sets the custom metadata for the right (output) side of the slot with the given slot_index to value.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_type_left: Sets the left (input) type of the slot with the given slot_index to type. If the value is negative, all connections will be disallowed to be created via user inputs.
m.GraphNode.set_slot_type_right: Sets the right (output) type of the slot with the given slot_index to type. If the value is negative, all connections will be disallowed to be created via user inputs.
m.GraphNode.slot_sizes_changed: Emitted when any slot's size might have changed.
m.GraphNode.slot_updated: Emitted when any GraphNode's slot is updated.
m.GraphNode.slots_focus_mode: Determines how connection slots can be focused.
m.GraphNode.title: The text displayed in the GraphNode's title bar.
m.GridContainer.columns: The number of columns in the GridContainer. If modified, GridContainer reorders its Control-derived children to accommodate the new layout.
m.GridMap.DEBUG_VISIBILITY_MODE_DEFAULT: Hide the collisions debug shapes in the editor, and use the debug settings to determine their visibility in game (i.e. SceneTree.debug_collisions_hint or SceneTree.debug_navigation_hint).
m.GridMap.DEBUG_VISIBILITY_MODE_FORCE_HIDE: Always hide the collisions debug shapes.
m.GridMap.DEBUG_VISIBILITY_MODE_FORCE_SHOW: Always show the collisions debug shapes.
m.GridMap.INVALID_CELL_ITEM: Invalid cell item that can be used in set_cell_item() to clear cells (or represent an empty cell in get_cell_item()).
m.GridMap.bake_navigation: If true, this GridMap creates a navigation region for each cell that uses a mesh_library item with a navigation mesh. The created navigation region will use the navigation layers bitmask assigned to the MeshLibrary's item.
m.GridMap.cell_center_x: If true, grid items are centered on the X axis.
m.GridMap.cell_center_y: If true, grid items are centered on the Y axis.
m.GridMap.cell_center_z: If true, grid items are centered on the Z axis.
m.GridMap.cell_octant_size: The size of each octant measured in number of cells. This applies to all three axis.
m.GridMap.cell_scale: The scale of the cell items.
m.GridMap.cell_size: The dimensions of the grid's cells.
m.GridMap.changed: Emitted when the MeshLibrary of this GridMap changes.
m.GridMap.clear_baked_meshes: Clears all baked meshes. See make_baked_meshes().
m.GridMap.collision_layer: The physics layers this GridMap is in.
m.GridMap.collision_mask: The physics layers this GridMap detects collisions in. See Collision layers and masks in the documentation for more information.
m.GridMap.collision_priority: The priority used to solve colliding when occurring penetration. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the object will be. This can for example be used to prevent the player from breaking through the boundaries of a level.
m.GridMap.collision_visibility_mode: Show or hide the GridMap's collision shapes. If set to DEBUG_VISIBILITY_MODE_DEFAULT, this depends on the show collision debug settings.
m.GridMap.get_bake_mesh_instance: Returns RID of a baked mesh with the given idx.
m.GridMap.get_bake_meshes: Returns an array of ArrayMeshes and Transform3D references of all bake meshes that exist within the current GridMap. Even indices contain ArrayMeshes, while odd indices contain Transform3Ds that are always equal to Transform3D.IDENTITY.
m.GridMap.get_basis_with_orthogonal_index: Returns one of 24 possible rotations that lie along the vectors (x,y,z) with each component being either -1, 0, or 1. For further details, refer to the Godot source code.
m.GridMap.get_cell_item: The MeshLibrary item index located at the given grid coordinates. If the cell is empty, INVALID_CELL_ITEM will be returned.
m.GridMap.get_cell_item_basis: Returns the basis that gives the specified cell its orientation.
m.GridMap.get_cell_item_orientation: The orientation of the cell at the given grid coordinates. -1 is returned if the cell is empty.
m.GridMap.get_collision_layer_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_layer is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.GridMap.get_collision_mask_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.GridMap.get_meshes: Returns an array of Transform3D and Mesh references corresponding to the non-empty cells in the grid. The transforms are specified in local space. Even indices contain Transform3Ds, while odd indices contain Meshes related to the Transform3D in the index preceding it.
m.GridMap.get_navigation_map: Returns the RID of the navigation map this GridMap node uses for its cell baked navigation meshes.
m.GridMap.get_octant_coords_from_cell_coor: Returns the Vector3i octant coordinates of the octant that the cell at cell_coords belongs to.
m.GridMap.get_octants_in_bounds: Returns an array of Vector3i octant coordinates that are inside the given bounds, including octants that have no cells in use.
m.GridMap.get_orthogonal_index_from_basis: This function considers a discretization of rotations into 24 points on unit sphere, lying along the vectors (x,y,z) with each component being either -1, 0, or 1, and returns the index (in the range from 0 to 23) of the point best representing the orientation of the object. For further details, refer to the Godot source code.
m.GridMap.get_used_cells: Returns an array of Vector3 with the non-empty cell coordinates in the grid map.
m.GridMap.get_used_cells_by_item: Returns an array of all cells with the given item index specified in item.
m.GridMap.get_used_cells_in_octant: Returns an array of Vector3is with the cell coordinates of non-empty cells inside the octant at octant_coords.
m.GridMap.get_used_cells_in_octant_by_item: Returns an array of Vector3is with the cell coordinates of cells inside the octant at octant_coords that use the specified cell item.
m.GridMap.get_used_octants: Returns an array of Vector3is with the octant coordinates of the non-empty octants in the grid map.
m.GridMap.get_used_octants_by_item: Returns an array of Vector3is with the octant coordinates of the octants that use the specified item in the grid map.
m.GridMap.get_used_octants_in_bounds: Returns an array of Vector3is with the octant coordinates of non-empty octants that are inside the local bounds.
m.GridMap.local_to_map: Returns the map coordinates of the cell containing the given local_position. If local_position is in global coordinates, consider using Node3D.to_local() before passing it to this method. See also map_to_local().
m.GridMap.make_baked_meshes: Generates a baked mesh that represents all meshes in the assigned MeshLibrary for use with LightmapGI. If gen_lightmap_uv is true, UV2 data will be generated for each mesh currently used in the GridMap. Otherwise, only meshes that already have UV2 data present will be able to use baked lightmaps. When generating UV2, lightmap_uv_texel_size controls the texel density for lightmaps, with lower valu…
m.GridMap.map_to_local: Returns the position of a grid cell in the GridMap's local coordinate space. To convert the returned value into global coordinates, use Node3D.to_global(). See also local_to_map().
m.GridMap.physics_material: Overrides the default friction and bounce physics properties for the whole GridMap.
m.GridMap.set_cell_item: Sets the mesh index for the cell referenced by its grid coordinates.
m.GridMap.set_collision_layer_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_layer, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.GridMap.set_collision_mask_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.GridMap.set_navigation_map: Sets the RID of the navigation map this GridMap node should use for its cell baked navigation meshes.
m.GridMapEditorPlugin.get_current_grid_map: Returns the GridMap node currently edited by the grid map editor.
m.GridMapEditorPlugin.get_selected_cells: Returns an array of Vector3is with the selected cells' coordinates.
m.GridMapEditorPlugin.get_selected_palette: Returns the index of the selected MeshLibrary item in the grid map editor's palette or -1 if no item is selected.
m.GridMapEditorPlugin.get_selection: Returns the cell coordinate bounds of the current selection. Use has_selection() to check if there is an active selection.
m.GridMapEditorPlugin.has_selection: Returns true if there are selected cells.
m.GridMapEditorPlugin.set_selected_palette: Selects the MeshLibrary item with the given index in the grid map editor's palette. If a negative index is given, no item will be selected. If a value greater than the last index is given, the last item will be selected.
m.GridMapEditorPlugin.set_selection: Selects the cells inside the given bounds from begin to end.
m.GrooveJoint2D.initial_offset: The body B's initial anchor position defined by the joint's origin and a local offset initial_offset along the joint's Y axis (along the groove).
m.GrooveJoint2D.length: The groove's length. The groove is from the joint's origin towards length along the joint's local Y axis.
m.HMACContext.finish: Returns the resulting HMAC. If the HMAC failed, an empty PackedByteArray is returned.
m.HMACContext.start: Initializes the HMACContext. This method cannot be called again on the same HMACContext until finish() has been called.
m.HMACContext.update: Updates the message to be HMACed. This can be called multiple times before finish() is called to append data to the message, but cannot be called until start() has been called.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_CONNECT: HTTP CONNECT method. The CONNECT method establishes a tunnel to the server identified by the target resource. Rarely used.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_DELETE: HTTP DELETE method. The DELETE method requests to delete the specified resource.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_GET: HTTP GET method. The GET method requests a representation of the specified resource. Requests using GET should only retrieve data.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_HEAD: HTTP HEAD method. The HEAD method asks for a response identical to that of a GET request, but without the response body. This is useful to request metadata like HTTP headers or to check if a resource exists.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_MAX: Represents the size of the Method enum.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_OPTIONS: HTTP OPTIONS method. The OPTIONS method asks for a description of the communication options for the target resource. Rarely used.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_PATCH: HTTP PATCH method. The PATCH method is used to apply partial modifications to a resource.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_POST: HTTP POST method. The POST method is used to submit an entity to the specified resource, often causing a change in state or side effects on the server. This is often used for forms and submitting data or uploading files.
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_PUT: HTTP PUT method. The PUT method asks to replace all current representations of the target resource with the request payload. (You can think of POST as "create or update" and PUT as "update", although many services tend to not make a clear distinction or change their meaning).
m.HTTPClient.METHOD_TRACE: HTTP TRACE method. The TRACE method performs a message loop-back test along the path to the target resource. Returns the entire HTTP request received in the response body. Rarely used.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_ACCEPTED: HTTP status code 202 Accepted. The request has been received but not yet acted upon. It is non-committal, meaning that there is no way in HTTP to later send an asynchronous response indicating the outcome of processing the request. It is intended for cases where another process or server handles the request, or for batch processing.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_ALREADY_REPORTED: HTTP status code 208 Already Reported (WebDAV). Used inside a DAV: propstat response element to avoid enumerating the internal members of multiple bindings to the same collection repeatedly.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_BAD_GATEWAY: HTTP status code 502 Bad Gateway. The server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from an inbound server it accessed while attempting to fulfill the request. Usually returned by load balancers or proxies.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_BAD_REQUEST: HTTP status code 400 Bad Request. The request was invalid. The server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing, invalid request contents, or deceptive request routing).
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_CONFLICT: HTTP status code 409 Conflict. The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource. This code is used in situations where the user might be able to resolve the conflict and resubmit the request.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_CONTINUE: HTTP status code 100 Continue. Interim response that indicates everything so far is OK and that the client should continue with the request (or ignore this status if already finished).
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_CREATED: HTTP status code 201 Created. The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result of it. This is typically the response sent after a PUT request.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_EXPECTATION_FAILED: HTTP status code 417 Expectation Failed. The expectation given in the request's Expect header field could not be met by at least one of the inbound servers.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_FAILED_DEPENDENCY: HTTP status code 424 Failed Dependency (WebDAV). The method could not be performed on the resource because the requested action depended on another action and that action failed.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_FORBIDDEN: HTTP status code 403 Forbidden. The client does not have access rights to the content, i.e. they are unauthorized, so server is rejecting to give proper response. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_FOUND: HTTP status code 302 Found. Temporary redirection. This response code means the URI of requested resource has been changed temporarily. New changes in the URI might be made in the future. Therefore, this same URI should be used by the client in future requests.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT: HTTP status code 504 Gateway Timeout. The server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, did not receive a timely response from an upstream server it needed to access in order to complete the request. Usually returned by load balancers or proxies.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_GONE: HTTP status code 410 Gone. The target resource is no longer available at the origin server and this condition is likely permanent.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_HTTP_VERSION_NOT_SUP: HTTP status code 505 HTTP Version Not Supported. The server does not support, or refuses to support, the major version of HTTP that was used in the request message.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_IM_A_TEAPOT: HTTP status code 418 I'm A Teapot. Any attempt to brew coffee with a teapot should result in the error code "418 I'm a teapot". The resulting entity body MAY be short and stout.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_IM_USED: HTTP status code 226 IM Used (WebDAV). The server has fulfilled a GET request for the resource, and the response is a representation of the result of one or more instance-manipulations applied to the current instance.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE: HTTP status code 507 Insufficient Storage. The method could not be performed on the resource because the server is unable to store the representation needed to successfully complete the request.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERRO: HTTP status code 500 Internal Server Error. The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_LENGTH_REQUIRED: HTTP status code 411 Length Required. The server refuses to accept the request without a defined Content-Length header.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_LOCKED: HTTP status code 423 Locked (WebDAV). The source or destination resource of a method is locked.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_LOOP_DETECTED: HTTP status code 508 Loop Detected. The server terminated an operation because it encountered an infinite loop while processing a request with "Depth: infinity". This status indicates that the entire operation failed.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: HTTP status code 405 Method Not Allowed. The request's HTTP method is known by the server but has been disabled and cannot be used. For example, an API may forbid DELETE-ing a resource. The two mandatory methods, GET and HEAD, must never be disabled and should not return this error code.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_MISDIRECTED_REQUEST: HTTP status code 421 Misdirected Request. The request was directed at a server that is not able to produce a response. This can be sent by a server that is not configured to produce responses for the combination of scheme and authority that are included in the request URI.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_MOVED_PERMANENTLY: HTTP status code 301 Moved Permanently. Redirection. This response code means the URI of requested resource has been changed. The new URI is usually included in the response.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_MULTIPLE_CHOICES: HTTP status code 300 Multiple Choice. The request has more than one possible responses and there is no standardized way to choose one of the responses. User-agent or user should choose one of them.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_MULTI_STATUS: HTTP status code 207 Multi-Status (WebDAV). A Multi-Status response conveys information about multiple resources in situations where multiple status codes might be appropriate.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NETWORK_AUTH_REQUIRE: HTTP status code 511 Network Authentication Required. The client needs to authenticate to gain network access.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NON_AUTHORITATIVE_IN: HTTP status code 203 Non-Authoritative Information. This response code means returned meta-information set is not exact set as available from the origin server, but collected from a local or a third party copy. Except this condition, 200 OK response should be preferred instead of this response.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NOT_ACCEPTABLE: HTTP status code 406 Not Acceptable. The target resource does not have a current representation that would be acceptable to the user agent, according to the proactive negotiation header fields received in the request. Used when negotiation content.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NOT_EXTENDED: HTTP status code 510 Not Extended. The policy for accessing the resource has not been met in the request. The server should send back all the information necessary for the client to issue an extended request.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND: HTTP status code 404 Not Found. The server can not find requested resource. Either the URL is not recognized or the endpoint is valid but the resource itself does not exist. May also be sent instead of 403 to hide existence of a resource if the client is not authorized.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: HTTP status code 501 Not Implemented. The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NOT_MODIFIED: HTTP status code 304 Not Modified. A conditional GET or HEAD request has been received and would have resulted in a 200 OK response if it were not for the fact that the condition evaluated to false.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_NO_CONTENT: HTTP status code 204 No Content. There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful. The user-agent may update its cached headers for this resource with the new ones.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_OK: HTTP status code 200 OK. The request has succeeded. Default response for successful requests. Meaning varies depending on the request:
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_PARTIAL_CONTENT: HTTP status code 206 Partial Content. This response code is used because of a range header sent by the client to separate download into multiple streams.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_PAYMENT_REQUIRED: HTTP status code 402 Payment Required. This response code is reserved for future use. Initial aim for creating this code was using it for digital payment systems, however this is not currently used.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_PERMANENT_REDIRECT: HTTP status code 308 Permanent Redirect. The target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI and any future references to this resource ought to use one of the enclosed URIs.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_PRECONDITION_FAILED: HTTP status code 412 Precondition Failed. One or more conditions given in the request header fields evaluated to false when tested on the server.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_PRECONDITION_REQUIRE: HTTP status code 428 Precondition Required. The origin server requires the request to be conditional.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_PROCESSING: HTTP status code 102 Processing (WebDAV). Indicates that the server has received and is processing the request, but no response is available yet.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION: HTTP status code 407 Proxy Authentication Required. Similar to 401 Unauthorized, but it indicates that the client needs to authenticate itself in order to use a proxy.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_REQUESTED_RANGE_NOT_: HTTP status code 416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable. None of the ranges in the request's Range header field overlap the current extent of the selected resource or the set of ranges requested has been rejected due to invalid ranges or an excessive request of small or overlapping ranges.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_L: HTTP status code 413 Entity Too Large. The server is refusing to process a request because the request payload is larger than the server is willing or able to process.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_REQUEST_HEADER_FIELD: HTTP status code 431 Request Header Fields Too Large. The server is unwilling to process the request because its header fields are too large. The request MAY be resubmitted after reducing the size of the request header fields.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: HTTP status code 408 Request Timeout. The server did not receive a complete request message within the time that it was prepared to wait.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_REQUEST_URI_TOO_LONG: HTTP status code 414 Request-URI Too Long. The server is refusing to service the request because the request-target is longer than the server is willing to interpret.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_RESET_CONTENT: HTTP status code 205 Reset Content. The server has fulfilled the request and desires that the client resets the "document view" that caused the request to be sent to its original state as received from the origin server.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_SEE_OTHER: HTTP status code 303 See Other. The server is redirecting the user agent to a different resource, as indicated by a URI in the Location header field, which is intended to provide an indirect response to the original request.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: HTTP status code 503 Service Unavailable. The server is currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance, which will likely be alleviated after some delay. Try again later.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_SWITCHING_PROTOCOLS: HTTP status code 101 Switching Protocol. Sent in response to an Upgrade request header by the client. Indicates the protocol the server is switching to.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_SWITCH_PROXY: Deprecated: Many clients ignore this response code for security reasons. It is also deprecated by the HTTP standard.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_TEMPORARY_REDIRECT: HTTP status code 307 Temporary Redirect. The target resource resides temporarily under a different URI and the user agent MUST NOT change the request method if it performs an automatic redirection to that URI.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS: HTTP status code 429 Too Many Requests. The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time (see "rate limiting"). Back off and increase time between requests or try again later.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_UNAUTHORIZED: HTTP status code 401 Unauthorized. Credentials required. The request has not been applied because it lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_UNAVAILABLE_FOR_LEGA: HTTP status code 451 Response Unavailable For Legal Reasons. The server is denying access to the resource as a consequence of a legal demand.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY: HTTP status code 422 Unprocessable Entity (WebDAV). The server understands the content type of the request entity (hence a 415 Unsupported Media Type status code is inappropriate), and the syntax of the request entity is correct (thus a 400 Bad Request status code is inappropriate) but was unable to process the contained instructions.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TY: HTTP status code 415 Unsupported Media Type. The origin server is refusing to service the request because the payload is in a format not supported by this method on the target resource.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_UPGRADE_REQUIRED: HTTP status code 426 Upgrade Required. The server refuses to perform the request using the current protocol but might be willing to do so after the client upgrades to a different protocol.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_USE_PROXY: Deprecated: Many clients ignore this response code for security reasons. It is also deprecated by the HTTP standard.
m.HTTPClient.RESPONSE_VARIANT_ALSO_NEGOTIA: HTTP status code 506 Variant Also Negotiates. The server has an internal configuration error: the chosen variant resource is configured to engage in transparent content negotiation itself, and is therefore not a proper end point in the negotiation process.
m.HTTPClient.STATUS_CANT_CONNECT: Status: Can't connect to the server.
m.HTTPClient.STATUS_CANT_RESOLVE: Status: DNS failure: Can't resolve the hostname for the given URL.
m.HTTPClient.STATUS_RESOLVING: Status: Currently resolving the hostname for the given URL into an IP.
m.HTTPClient.blocking_mode_enabled: If true, execution will block until all data is read from the response.
m.HTTPClient.close: Closes the current connection, allowing reuse of this HTTPClient.
m.HTTPClient.connect_to_host: Connects to a host. This needs to be done before any requests are sent.
m.HTTPClient.connection: The connection to use for this client.
m.HTTPClient.get_response_code: Returns the response's HTTP status code.
m.HTTPClient.get_response_headers_as_dicti: Returns all response headers as a Dictionary. Each entry is composed by the header name, and a String containing the values separated by "; ". The casing is kept the same as the headers were received.
m.HTTPClient.get_status: Returns a Status constant. Need to call poll() in order to get status updates.
m.HTTPClient.has_response: If true, this HTTPClient has a response available.
m.HTTPClient.is_response_chunked: If true, this HTTPClient has a response that is chunked.
m.HTTPClient.poll: This needs to be called in order to have any request processed. Check results with get_status().
m.HTTPClient.query_string_from_dict: Generates a GET/POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded style query string from a provided dictionary, e.g.:
m.HTTPClient.read_chunk_size: The size of the buffer used and maximum bytes to read per iteration. See read_response_body_chunk().
m.HTTPClient.read_response_body_chunk: Reads one chunk from the response.
m.HTTPClient.request: Sends an HTTP request to the connected host with the given method.
m.HTTPClient.request_raw: Sends a raw HTTP request to the connected host with the given method.
m.HTTPClient.set_http_proxy: Sets the proxy server for HTTP requests.
m.HTTPClient.set_https_proxy: Sets the proxy server for HTTPS requests.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_BODY_DECOMPRESS_FAILE: Request failed due to an error while decompressing the response body. Possible causes include unsupported or incorrect compression format, corrupted data, or incomplete transfer.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_BODY_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEE: Request exceeded its maximum size limit, see body_size_limit.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_CHUNKED_BODY_SIZE_MIS: Request failed due to a mismatch between the expected and actual chunked body size during transfer. Possible causes include network errors, server misconfiguration, or issues with chunked encoding.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_CONNECTION_ERROR: Request failed due to connection (read/write) error.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_DOWNLOAD_FILE_CANT_OP: HTTPRequest couldn't open the download file.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_DOWNLOAD_FILE_WRITE_E: HTTPRequest couldn't write to the download file.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_NO_RESPONSE: Request does not have a response (yet).
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_REDIRECT_LIMIT_REACHE: Request reached its maximum redirect limit, see max_redirects.
m.HTTPRequest.RESULT_TIMEOUT: Request failed due to a timeout. If you expect requests to take a long time, try increasing the value of timeout or setting it to 0.0 to remove the timeout completely.
m.HTTPRequest.accept_gzip: If true, this header will be added to each request: Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate telling servers that it's okay to compress response bodies.
m.HTTPRequest.body_size_limit: Maximum allowed size for response bodies. If the response body is compressed, this will be used as the maximum allowed size for the decompressed body.
m.HTTPRequest.download_chunk_size: The size of the buffer used and maximum bytes to read per iteration. See HTTPClient.read_chunk_size.
m.HTTPRequest.download_file: The file to download into. Will output any received file into it.
m.HTTPRequest.get_downloaded_bytes: Returns the number of bytes this HTTPRequest downloaded.
m.HTTPRequest.get_http_client_status: Returns the current status of the underlying HTTPClient.
m.HTTPRequest.request: Creates request on the underlying HTTPClient. If there is no configuration errors, it tries to connect using HTTPClient.connect_to_host() and passes parameters onto HTTPClient.request().
m.HTTPRequest.request_completed: Emitted when a request is completed.
m.HTTPRequest.request_raw: Creates request on the underlying HTTPClient using a raw array of bytes for the request body. If there is no configuration errors, it tries to connect using HTTPClient.connect_to_host() and passes parameters onto HTTPClient.request().
m.HTTPRequest.set_http_proxy: Sets the proxy server for HTTP requests.
m.HTTPRequest.set_https_proxy: Sets the proxy server for HTTPS requests.
m.HTTPRequest.set_tls_options: Sets the TLSOptions to be used when connecting to an HTTPS server. See TLSOptions.client().
m.HTTPRequest.timeout: The duration to wait before a request times out, in seconds (independent of Engine.time_scale). If timeout is set to 0.0, the request will never time out.
m.HTTPRequest.use_threads: If true, multithreading is used to improve performance.
m.HashingContext.finish: Closes the current context, and return the computed hash.
m.HashingContext.start: Starts a new hash computation of the given type (e.g. HASH_SHA256 to start computation of an SHA-256).
m.HashingContext.update: Updates the computation with the given chunk of data.
m.HeightMapShape3D.get_max_height: Returns the largest height value found in map_data. Recalculates only when map_data changes.
m.HeightMapShape3D.get_min_height: Returns the smallest height value found in map_data. Recalculates only when map_data changes.
m.HeightMapShape3D.map_data: Heightmap data. The array's size must be equal to map_width multiplied by map_depth.
m.HeightMapShape3D.map_depth: Number of vertices in the depth of the heightmap. Changing this will resize the map_data.
m.HeightMapShape3D.map_width: Number of vertices in the width of the heightmap. Changing this will resize the map_data.
m.HeightMapShape3D.update_map_data_from_im: Updates map_data with data read from an Image reference. Automatically resizes heightmap map_width and map_depth to fit the full image width and height.
m.HingeJoint3D.FLAG_ENABLE_MOTOR: When activated, a motor turns the hinge.
m.HingeJoint3D.FLAG_MAX: Represents the size of the Flag enum.
m.HingeJoint3D.FLAG_USE_LIMIT: If true, the hinges maximum and minimum rotation, defined by angular_limit/lower and angular_limit/upper has effects.
m.HingeJoint3D.PARAM_BIAS: The speed with which the two bodies get pulled together when they move in different directions.
m.HingeJoint3D.PARAM_LIMIT_BIAS: The speed with which the rotation across the axis perpendicular to the hinge gets corrected.
m.HingeJoint3D.PARAM_LIMIT_LOWER: The minimum rotation. Only active if angular_limit/enable is true.
m.HingeJoint3D.PARAM_LIMIT_RELAXATION: The lower this value, the more the rotation gets slowed down.
m.HingeJoint3D.PARAM_LIMIT_SOFTNESS: Deprecated: This property is never used by the engine and is kept for compatibility purpose.
m.HingeJoint3D.PARAM_LIMIT_UPPER: The maximum rotation. Only active if angular_limit/enable is true.
m.HingeJoint3D.PARAM_MAX: Represents the size of the Param enum.
m.HingeJoint3D.get_flag: Returns the value of the specified flag.
m.HingeJoint3D.get_param: Returns the value of the specified parameter.
m.HingeJoint3D.set_flag: If true, enables the specified flag.
m.HingeJoint3D.set_param: Sets the value of the specified parameter.
m.IKModifier3D.mutable_bone_axes: If true, the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone pose every frame.
m.IKModifier3D.reset: Resets a state with respect to the current bone pose.
m.IP.RESOLVER_MAX_QUERIES: Maximum number of concurrent DNS resolver queries allowed, RESOLVER_INVALID_ID is returned if exceeded.
m.IP.RESOLVER_STATUS_NONE: DNS hostname resolver status: No status.
m.IP.clear_cache: Removes all of a hostname's cached references. If no hostname is given, all cached IP addresses are removed.
m.IP.erase_resolve_item: Removes a given item id from the queue. This should be used to free a queue after it has completed to enable more queries to happen.
m.IP.get_local_addresses: Returns all the user's current IPv4 and IPv6 addresses as an array.
m.IP.get_local_interfaces: Returns all network adapters as an array.
m.IP.get_resolve_item_address: Returns a queued hostname's IP address, given its queue id. Returns an empty string on error or if resolution hasn't happened yet (see get_resolve_item_status()).
m.IP.get_resolve_item_addresses: Returns resolved addresses, or an empty array if an error happened or resolution didn't happen yet (see get_resolve_item_status()).
m.IP.get_resolve_item_status: Returns a queued hostname's status as a ResolverStatus constant, given its queue id.
m.IP.resolve_hostname: Returns a given hostname's IPv4 or IPv6 address when resolved (blocking-type method). The address type returned depends on the Type constant given as ip_type.
m.IP.resolve_hostname_addresses: Resolves a given hostname in a blocking way. Addresses are returned as an Array of IPv4 or IPv6 addresses depending on ip_type.
m.IP.resolve_hostname_queue_item: Creates a queue item to resolve a hostname to an IPv4 or IPv6 address depending on the Type constant given as ip_type. Returns the queue ID if successful, or RESOLVER_INVALID_ID on error.
m.Image.ALPHA_BIT: Image stores either fully opaque or fully transparent pixels. Also known as punchthrough alpha.
m.Image.ALPHA_BLEND: Image stores alpha data with values varying between 0.0 and 1.0.
m.Image.ALPHA_NONE: Image is fully opaque. It does not store alpha data.
m.Image.ASTC_FORMAT_4x4: Hint to indicate that the high quality 4×4 ASTC compression format should be used.
m.Image.ASTC_FORMAT_8x8: Hint to indicate that the low quality 8×8 ASTC compression format should be used.
m.Image.COMPRESS_MAX: Represents the size of the CompressMode enum.
m.Image.COMPRESS_SOURCE_GENERIC: Source texture (before compression) is a regular texture. Default for all textures.
m.Image.COMPRESS_SOURCE_NORMAL: Source texture (before compression) is a normal texture (e.g. it can be compressed into two channels).
m.Image.COMPRESS_SOURCE_SRGB: Source texture (before compression) uses nonlinear sRGB encoding.
m.Image.FORMAT_ASTC_4x4: Adaptive Scalable Texture Compression [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptive_scalable_texture_compression]. This implements the 4×4 (high quality) mode.
m.Image.FORMAT_ASTC_4x4_HDR: Same format as FORMAT_ASTC_4x4, but with the hint to let the GPU know it is used for HDR.
m.Image.FORMAT_ASTC_8x8: Adaptive Scalable Texture Compression [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptive_scalable_texture_compression]. This implements the 8×8 (low quality) mode.
m.Image.FORMAT_ASTC_8x8_HDR: Same format as FORMAT_ASTC_8x8, but with the hint to let the GPU know it is used for HDR.
m.Image.FORMAT_BPTC_RGBA: Texture format that uses BPTC [https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/BPTC_Texture_Compression] compression with unsigned normalized RGBA components.
m.Image.FORMAT_BPTC_RGBF: Texture format that uses BPTC [https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/BPTC_Texture_Compression] compression with signed floating-point RGB components.
m.Image.FORMAT_BPTC_RGBFU: Texture format that uses BPTC [https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/BPTC_Texture_Compression] compression with unsigned floating-point RGB components.
m.Image.FORMAT_DXT1: The S3TC [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S3_Texture_Compression] texture format that uses Block Compression 1, and is the smallest variation of S3TC, only providing 1 bit of alpha and color data being premultiplied with alpha.
m.Image.FORMAT_DXT3: The S3TC [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S3_Texture_Compression] texture format that uses Block Compression 2, and color data is interpreted as not having been premultiplied by alpha. Well suited for images with sharp alpha transitions between translucent and opaque areas.
m.Image.FORMAT_DXT5: The S3TC [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S3_Texture_Compression] texture format also known as Block Compression 3 or BC3 that contains 64 bits of alpha channel data followed by 64 bits of DXT1-encoded color data. Color data is not premultiplied by alpha, same as DXT3. DXT5 generally produces superior results for transparent gradients compared to DXT3.
m.Image.FORMAT_DXT5_RA_AS_RG: The S3TC [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S3_Texture_Compression] texture format also known as Block Compression 3 or BC3, which compresses RA data and interprets it as two channels (red and green). See also FORMAT_DXT5.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC: Ericsson Texture Compression format 1 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC1], also referred to as "ETC1", and is part of the OpenGL ES graphics standard. This format cannot store an alpha channel.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_R11: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (R11_EAC variant), which provides one channel of unsigned data.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_R11S: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (SIGNED_R11_EAC variant), which provides one channel of signed data.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_RA_AS_RG: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (RGBA8 variant), which compresses RA data and interprets it as two channels (red and green). See also FORMAT_ETC2_RGBA8.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_RG11: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (RG11_EAC variant), which provides two channels of unsigned data.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_RG11S: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (SIGNED_RG11_EAC variant), which provides two channels of signed data.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_RGB8: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (RGB8 variant), which is a follow-up of ETC1 and compresses RGB888 data.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_RGB8A1: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (RGB8_PUNCHTHROUGH_ALPHA1 variant), which compresses RGBA data to make alpha either fully transparent or fully opaque.
m.Image.FORMAT_ETC2_RGBA8: Ericsson Texture Compression format 2 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ericsson_Texture_Compression#ETC2_and_EAC] (RGBA8variant), which compresses RGBA8888 data with full alpha support.
m.Image.FORMAT_L8: Texture format with a single 8-bit depth representing luminance.
m.Image.FORMAT_LA8: OpenGL texture format with two values, luminance and alpha each stored with 8 bits.
m.Image.FORMAT_MAX: Represents the size of the Format enum.
m.Image.FORMAT_R16: OpenGL texture format GL_R16 where there's one component, a 16-bit unsigned normalized integer value. Since the value is normalized, each component is clamped between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_R16I: OpenGL texture format GL_R16UI where there's one component, a 16-bit unsigned integer value. Each component is clamped between 0 and 65535 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_R8: OpenGL texture format RED with a single component and a bitdepth of 8.
m.Image.FORMAT_RF: OpenGL texture format GL_R32F where there's one component, a 32-bit floating-point value.
m.Image.FORMAT_RG16: OpenGL texture format GL_RG16 where there are two components, each a 16-bit unsigned normalized integer value. Since the value is normalized, each component is clamped between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_RG16I: OpenGL texture format GL_RG16UI where there are two components, each a 16-bit unsigned integer value. Each component is clamped between 0 and 65535 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_RG8: OpenGL texture format RG with two components and a bitdepth of 8 for each.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGB16: OpenGL texture format GL_RGB16 where there are three components, each a 16-bit unsigned normalized integer value. Since the value is normalized, each component is clamped between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_RGB16I: OpenGL texture format GL_RGB16UI where there are three components, each a 16-bit unsigned integer value. Each component is clamped between 0 and 65535 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_RGB565: OpenGL texture format RGB with three components. Red and blue have a bitdepth of 5, and green has a bitdepth of 6.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGB8: OpenGL texture format RGB with three components, each with a bitdepth of 8.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBA16: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA16 where there are four components, each a 16-bit unsigned normalized integer value. Since the value is normalized, each component is clamped between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBA16I: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA16UI where there are four components, each a 16-bit unsigned integer value. Each component is clamped between 0 and 65535 (inclusive).
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBA4444: OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 4.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBA8: OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 8.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBAF: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA32F where there are four components, each a 32-bit floating-point values.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBAH: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA16F where there are four components, each a 16-bit "half-precision" floating-point value.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBE9995: A special OpenGL texture format where the three color components have 9 bits of precision and all three share a single 5-bit exponent.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBF: OpenGL texture format GL_RGB32F where there are three components, each a 32-bit floating-point values.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGBH: OpenGL texture format GL_RGB16F where there are three components, each a 16-bit "half-precision" floating-point value.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGF: OpenGL texture format GL_RG32F where there are two components, each a 32-bit floating-point values.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGH: OpenGL texture format GL_RG16F where there are two components, each a 16-bit "half-precision" floating-point value.
