m.Image.FORMAT_RGTC_R: Texture format that uses Red Green Texture Compression [https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Red_Green_Texture_Compression], normalizing the red channel data using the same compression algorithm that DXT5 uses for the alpha channel.
m.Image.FORMAT_RGTC_RG: Texture format that uses Red Green Texture Compression [https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Red_Green_Texture_Compression], normalizing the red and green channel data using the same compression algorithm that DXT5 uses for the alpha channel.
m.Image.FORMAT_RH: OpenGL texture format GL_R16F where there's one component, a 16-bit "half-precision" floating-point value.
m.Image.INTERPOLATE_BILINEAR: Performs bilinear interpolation. If the image is resized, it will be blurry. This mode is faster than INTERPOLATE_CUBIC, but it results in lower quality.
m.Image.INTERPOLATE_CUBIC: Performs cubic interpolation. If the image is resized, it will be blurry. This mode often gives better results compared to INTERPOLATE_BILINEAR, at the cost of being slower.
m.Image.INTERPOLATE_LANCZOS: Performs Lanczos interpolation. This is the slowest image resizing mode, but it typically gives the best results, especially when downscaling images.
m.Image.INTERPOLATE_NEAREST: Performs nearest-neighbor interpolation. If the image is resized, it will be pixelated.
m.Image.INTERPOLATE_TRILINEAR: Performs bilinear separately on the two most-suited mipmap levels, then linearly interpolates between them.
m.Image.MAX_WIDTH: The maximal width allowed for Image resources.
m.Image.USED_CHANNELS_L: The image only uses one channel for luminance (grayscale).
m.Image.USED_CHANNELS_LA: The image uses two channels for luminance and alpha, respectively.
m.Image.USED_CHANNELS_R: The image only uses the red channel.
m.Image.USED_CHANNELS_RG: The image uses two channels for red and green.
m.Image.USED_CHANNELS_RGB: The image uses three channels for red, green, and blue.
m.Image.USED_CHANNELS_RGBA: The image uses four channels for red, green, blue, and alpha.
m.Image.adjust_bcs: Adjusts this image's brightness, contrast, and saturation by the given values. Does not work if the image is compressed (see is_compressed()).
m.Image.blend_rect: Alpha-blends src_rect from src image to this image at coordinates dst, clipped accordingly to both image bounds. This image and src image must have the same format. src_rect with non-positive size is treated as empty.
m.Image.blend_rect_mask: Alpha-blends src_rect from src image to this image using mask image at coordinates dst, clipped accordingly to both image bounds. Alpha channels are required for both src and mask. dst pixels and src pixels will blend if the corresponding mask pixel's alpha value is not 0. This image and src image must have the same format. src image and mask image must have the same size (width and height) but t…
m.Image.blit_rect: Copies src_rect from src image to this image at coordinates dst, clipped accordingly to both image bounds. This image and src image must have the same format. src_rect with non-positive size is treated as empty.
m.Image.blit_rect_mask: Blits src_rect area from src image to this image at the coordinates given by dst, clipped accordingly to both image bounds. src pixel is copied onto dst if the corresponding mask pixel's alpha value is not 0. This image and src image must have the same format. src image and mask image must have the same size (width and height) but they can have different formats. src_rect with non-positive size i…
m.Image.bump_map_to_normal_map: Converts a bump map to a normal map. A bump map provides a height offset per-pixel, while a normal map provides a normal direction per pixel.
m.Image.compress: Compresses the image with a VRAM-compressed format to use less memory. Can not directly access pixel data while the image is compressed. Returns error if the chosen compression mode is not available.
m.Image.compress_from_channels: Compresses the image with a VRAM-compressed format to use less memory. Can not directly access pixel data while the image is compressed. Returns error if the chosen compression mode is not available.
m.Image.compute_image_metrics: Compute image metrics on the current image and the compared image. This can be used to calculate the similarity between two images.
m.Image.convert: Converts this image's format to the given format.
m.Image.copy_from: Copies src image to this image.
m.Image.create_empty: Creates an empty image of the given size and format. If use_mipmaps is true, generates mipmaps for this image (see generate_mipmaps()).
m.Image.create_from_data: Creates a new image of the given size and format. Fills the image with the given raw data. If use_mipmaps is true, loads the mipmaps for this image from data. See generate_mipmaps().
m.Image.crop: Crops the image to the given width and height. If the specified size is larger than the current size, the extra area is filled with black pixels.
m.Image.data: Holds all the image's color data in a given format. See Format constants.
m.Image.decompress: Decompresses the image if it is VRAM-compressed in a supported format. This increases memory utilization, but allows modifying the image. Returns @GlobalScope.OK if the format is supported, otherwise @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE. All VRAM-compressed formats supported by Godot can be decompressed with this method, except FORMAT_ETC2_R11S, FORMAT_ETC2_RG11S, and FORMAT_ETC2_RGB8A1.
m.Image.detect_alpha: Returns ALPHA_BLEND if the image has data for alpha values. Returns ALPHA_BIT if all the alpha values are stored in a single bit. Returns ALPHA_NONE if no data for alpha values is found.
m.Image.detect_used_channels: Returns the color channels used by this image. If the image is compressed, the original source must be specified.
m.Image.fix_alpha_edges: Blends low-alpha pixels with nearby pixels.
m.Image.generate_mipmaps: Generates mipmaps for the image. Mipmaps are precalculated lower-resolution copies of the image that are automatically used if the image needs to be scaled down when rendered. They help improve image quality and performance when rendering. This method returns an error if the image is compressed, in a custom format, or if the image's width/height is 0. Enabling renormalize when generating mipmaps…
m.Image.get_data: Returns a copy of the image's raw data.
m.Image.get_data_size: Returns size (in bytes) of the image's raw data.
m.Image.get_mipmap_count: Returns the number of mipmap levels or 0 if the image has no mipmaps. The largest main level image is not counted as a mipmap level by this method, so if you want to include it you can add 1 to this count.
m.Image.get_mipmap_offset: Returns the offset where the image's mipmap with index mipmap is stored in the data dictionary.
m.Image.get_pixel: Returns the color of the pixel at (x, y).
m.Image.get_pixelv: Returns the color of the pixel at point.
m.Image.get_region: Returns a new Image that is a copy of this Image's area specified with region.
m.Image.get_size: Returns the image's size (width and height).
m.Image.get_used_rect: Returns a Rect2i enclosing the visible portion of the image, considering each pixel with a non-zero alpha channel as visible.
m.Image.has_mipmaps: Returns true if the image has generated mipmaps.
m.Image.is_compressed: Returns true if the image is compressed.
m.Image.is_empty: Returns true if the image has no data.
m.Image.is_invisible: Returns true if all the image's pixels have an alpha value of 0. Returns false if any pixel has an alpha value higher than 0.
m.Image.linear_to_srgb: Converts the entire image from linear encoding to nonlinear sRGB encoding by using a lookup table. Only works on images with FORMAT_RGB8 or FORMAT_RGBA8 formats.
m.Image.load: Loads an image from file path. See Supported image formats for a list of supported image formats and limitations.
m.Image.load_bmp_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of a BMP file.
m.Image.load_dds_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of a DDS file.
m.Image.load_exr_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of an OpenEXR file.
m.Image.load_from_file: Creates a new Image and loads data from the specified file.
m.Image.load_jpg_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of a JPEG file.
m.Image.load_ktx_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of a KTX [https://github.com/KhronosGroup/KTX-Software] file. Unlike most image formats, KTX can store VRAM-compressed data and embed mipmaps.
m.Image.load_png_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of a PNG file.
m.Image.load_svg_from_buffer: Loads an image from the UTF-8 binary contents of an uncompressed SVG file (.svg).
m.Image.load_svg_from_string: Loads an image from the string contents of an SVG file (.svg).
m.Image.load_tga_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of a TGA file.
m.Image.load_webp_from_buffer: Loads an image from the binary contents of a WebP file.
m.Image.normal_map_to_xy: Converts the image's data to represent coordinates on a 3D plane. This is used when the image represents a normal map. A normal map can add lots of detail to a 3D surface without increasing the polygon count.
m.Image.premultiply_alpha: Multiplies color values with alpha values. Resulting color values for a pixel are (color * alpha)/256. See also CanvasItemMaterial.blend_mode.
m.Image.resize: Resizes the image to the given width and height. New pixels are calculated using the interpolation mode defined via Interpolation constants.
m.Image.resize_to_po2: Resizes the image to the nearest power of 2 for the width and height. If square is true, sets width and height to be the same. New pixels are calculated using the interpolation mode defined via Interpolation constants.
m.Image.rgbe_to_srgb: Converts a standard linear RGBE (Red Green Blue Exponent) image to an image that uses nonlinear sRGB encoding.
m.Image.rotate_180: Rotates the image by 180 degrees. The width and height of the image must be greater than 1.
m.Image.rotate_90: Rotates the image in the specified direction by 90 degrees. The width and height of the image must be greater than 1. If the width and height are not equal, the image will be resized.
m.Image.save_dds: Saves the image as a DDS (DirectDraw Surface) file to path. DDS is a container format that can store textures in various compression formats, such as DXT1, DXT5, or BC7. This function will return @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE if Godot was compiled without the DDS module.
m.Image.save_dds_to_buffer: Saves the image as a DDS (DirectDraw Surface) file to a byte array. DDS is a container format that can store textures in various compression formats, such as DXT1, DXT5, or BC7. This function will return an empty byte array if Godot was compiled without the DDS module.
m.Image.save_exr: Saves the image as an EXR file to path. If grayscale is true and the image has only one channel, it will be saved explicitly as monochrome rather than one red channel. Set color_image to true when saving a color image, such as a screenshot. Negative values will be included when color_image is false, which may be useful for saving raw floating point data such as a lightmap that includes negative l…
m.Image.save_exr_to_buffer: Saves the image as an EXR file to a byte array. If grayscale is true and the image has only one channel, it will be saved explicitly as monochrome rather than one red channel. Set color_image to true when saving a color image, such as a screenshot. Negative values will be included when color_image is false, which may be useful for saving raw floating point data such as a lightmap that includes ne…
m.Image.save_jpg: Saves the image as a JPEG file to path with the specified quality between 0.01 and 1.0 (inclusive). Higher quality values result in better-looking output at the cost of larger file sizes. Recommended quality values are between 0.75 and 0.90. Even at quality 1.00, JPEG compression remains lossy.
m.Image.save_jpg_to_buffer: Saves the image as a JPEG file to a byte array with the specified quality between 0.01 and 1.0 (inclusive). Higher quality values result in better-looking output at the cost of larger byte array sizes (and therefore memory usage). Recommended quality values are between 0.75 and 0.90. Even at quality 1.00, JPEG compression remains lossy.
m.Image.save_png: Saves the image as a PNG file to the file at path.
m.Image.save_png_to_buffer: Saves the image as a PNG file to a byte array.
m.Image.save_webp: Saves the image as a WebP (Web Picture) file to the file at path. By default it will save lossless. If lossy is true, the image will be saved lossy, using the quality setting between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). Lossless WebP offers more efficient compression than PNG.
m.Image.save_webp_to_buffer: Saves the image as a WebP (Web Picture) file to a byte array. By default it will save lossless. If lossy is true, the image will be saved lossy, using the quality setting between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). Lossless WebP offers more efficient compression than PNG.
m.Image.set_data: Overwrites data of an existing Image. Non-static equivalent of create_from_data().
m.Image.set_pixel: Sets the Color of the pixel at (x, y) to color.
m.Image.set_pixelv: Sets the Color of the pixel at point to color.
m.Image.shrink_x2: Shrinks the image by a factor of 2 on each axis (this divides the pixel count by 4).
m.Image.srgb_to_linear: Converts the raw data from nonlinear sRGB encoding to linear encoding using a lookup table. Only works on images with FORMAT_RGB8 or FORMAT_RGBA8 formats.
m.ImageFormatLoaderExtension._get_recogniz: Returns the list of file extensions for this image format. Files with the given extensions will be treated as image file and loaded using this class.
m.ImageFormatLoaderExtension._load_image: Loads the content of fileaccess into the provided image.
m.ImageFormatLoaderExtension.add_format_lo: Add this format loader to the engine, allowing it to recognize the file extensions returned by _get_recognized_extensions().
m.ImageFormatLoaderExtension.remove_format: Remove this format loader from the engine.
m.ImageTexture.create_from_image: Creates a new ImageTexture and initializes it by allocating and setting the data from an Image.
m.ImageTexture.set_image: Replaces the texture's data with a new Image. This will re-allocate new memory for the texture.
m.ImageTexture.set_size_override: Resizes the texture to the specified dimensions.
m.ImageTexture.update: Replaces the texture's data with a new Image.
m.ImageTexture3D.create: Creates the ImageTexture3D with specified format, width, height, and depth. If use_mipmaps is true, generates mipmaps for the ImageTexture3D.
m.ImageTexture3D.update: Replaces the texture's existing data with the layers specified in data. The size of data must match the parameters that were used for create(). In other words, the texture cannot be resized or have its format changed by calling update().
m.ImageTextureLayered.create_from_images: Creates an ImageTextureLayered from an array of Images. See Image.create() for the expected data format. The first image decides the width, height, image format and mipmapping setting. The other images must have the same width, height, image format and mipmapping setting.
m.ImageTextureLayered.update_layer: Replaces the existing Image data at the given layer with this new image.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_add_vertex: Add a 3D vertex using the current attributes previously set.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_add_vertex_2d: Add a 2D vertex using the current attributes previously set.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_end: End and commit current surface. Note that surface being created will not be visible until this function is called.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_set_color: Set the color attribute that will be pushed with the next vertex.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_set_normal: Set the normal attribute that will be pushed with the next vertex.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_set_tangent: Set the tangent attribute that will be pushed with the next vertex.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_set_uv: Set the UV attribute that will be pushed with the next vertex.
m.ImmediateMesh.surface_set_uv2: Set the UV2 attribute that will be pushed with the next vertex.
m.ImporterMesh.add_blend_shape: Adds name for a blend shape that will be added with add_surface(). Must be called before surface is added.
m.ImporterMesh.add_surface: Creates a new surface. Mesh.get_surface_count() will become the surf_idx for this new surface.
m.ImporterMesh.clear: Removes all surfaces and blend shapes from this ImporterMesh.
m.ImporterMesh.from_mesh: Converts the given Mesh into an ImporterMesh by copying all its surfaces, blend shapes, materials, and metadata into a new ImporterMesh object.
m.ImporterMesh.generate_lods: Generates all lods for this ImporterMesh.
m.ImporterMesh.get_blend_shape_count: Returns the number of blend shapes that the mesh holds.
m.ImporterMesh.get_blend_shape_mode: Returns the blend shape mode for this Mesh.
m.ImporterMesh.get_blend_shape_name: Returns the name of the blend shape at this index.
m.ImporterMesh.get_lightmap_size_hint: Returns the size hint of this mesh for lightmap-unwrapping in UV-space.
m.ImporterMesh.get_mesh: Returns the mesh data represented by this ImporterMesh as a usable ArrayMesh.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_arrays: Returns the arrays for the vertices, normals, UVs, etc. that make up the requested surface. See add_surface().
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_blend_shape_arr: Returns a single set of blend shape arrays for the requested blend shape index for a surface.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_count: Returns the number of surfaces that the mesh holds.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_format: Returns the format of the surface that the mesh holds.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_lod_count: Returns the number of lods that the mesh holds on a given surface.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_lod_indices: Returns the index buffer of a lod for a surface.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_lod_size: Returns the screen ratio which activates a lod for a surface.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_material: Returns a Material in a given surface. Surface is rendered using this material.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_name: Gets the name assigned to this surface.
m.ImporterMesh.get_surface_primitive_type: Returns the primitive type of the requested surface (see add_surface()).
m.ImporterMesh.merge_importer_meshes: Merges multiple ImporterMeshes into a single ImporterMesh. Each input mesh is transformed by the corresponding Transform3D in the relative_transforms array, which must be the same size as importer_meshes. Negative scales are supported, and the winding order in the mesh data will be corrected to account for this.
m.ImporterMesh.set_lightmap_size_hint: Sets the size hint of this mesh for lightmap-unwrapping in UV-space.

m.Input.CURSOR_ARROW: Arrow cursor. Standard, default pointing cursor.
m.Input.CURSOR_BDIAGSIZE: Window resize mouse cursor. The cursor is a double-headed arrow that goes from the bottom left to the top right. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel both horizontally and vertically.
m.Input.CURSOR_BUSY: Busy cursor. Indicates that the application is busy performing an operation, and that it is still usable during the operation.
m.Input.CURSOR_CAN_DROP: Can drop cursor. Usually displayed when dragging something to indicate that it can be dropped at the current position.
m.Input.CURSOR_CROSS: Cross cursor. Typically appears over regions in which a drawing operation can be performed or for selections.
m.Input.CURSOR_DRAG: Drag cursor. Usually displayed when dragging something.
m.Input.CURSOR_FDIAGSIZE: Window resize mouse cursor. The cursor is a double-headed arrow that goes from the top left to the bottom right, the opposite of CURSOR_BDIAGSIZE. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel both horizontally and vertically.
m.Input.CURSOR_FORBIDDEN: Forbidden cursor. Indicates that the current action is forbidden (for example, when dragging something) or that the control at a position is disabled.
m.Input.CURSOR_HELP: Help cursor. Usually a question mark.
m.Input.CURSOR_HSIZE: Horizontal resize mouse cursor. A double-headed horizontal arrow. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel horizontally.
m.Input.CURSOR_HSPLIT: Horizontal split mouse cursor. On Windows, it's the same as CURSOR_HSIZE.
m.Input.CURSOR_IBEAM: I-beam cursor. Usually used to show where the text cursor will appear when the mouse is clicked.
m.Input.CURSOR_MOVE: Move cursor. Indicates that something can be moved.
m.Input.CURSOR_POINTING_HAND: Pointing hand cursor. Usually used to indicate the pointer is over a link or other interactable item.
m.Input.CURSOR_VSIZE: Vertical resize mouse cursor. A double-headed vertical arrow. It tells the user they can resize the window or the panel vertically.
m.Input.CURSOR_VSPLIT: Vertical split mouse cursor. On Windows, it's the same as CURSOR_VSIZE.
m.Input.CURSOR_WAIT: Wait cursor. Indicates that the application is busy performing an operation, and that it cannot be used during the operation (e.g. something is blocking its main thread).
m.Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED: Captures the mouse. The mouse will be hidden and its position locked at the center of the window manager's window.
m.Input.MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED: Confines the mouse cursor to the game window, and make it visible.
m.Input.MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN: Confines the mouse cursor to the game window, and make it hidden.
m.Input.MOUSE_MODE_HIDDEN: Makes the mouse cursor hidden if it is visible.
m.Input.MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE: Makes the mouse cursor visible if it is hidden.
m.Input.action_press: This will simulate pressing the specified action.
m.Input.action_release: If the specified action is already pressed, this will release it.
m.Input.add_joy_mapping: Adds a new mapping entry (in SDL2 format) to the mapping database. Optionally update already connected devices.
m.Input.clear_joy_motion_sensors_calibrati: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.emulate_mouse_from_touch: If true, sends mouse input events when tapping or swiping on the touchscreen. See also ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch.
m.Input.emulate_touch_from_mouse: If true, sends touch input events when clicking or dragging the mouse. See also ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse.
m.Input.flush_buffered_events: Sends all input events which are in the current buffer to the game loop. These events may have been buffered as a result of accumulated input (use_accumulated_input) or agile input flushing (ProjectSettings.input_devices/buffering/agile_event_flushing).
m.Input.get_accelerometer: Returns the acceleration in m/s² of the device's accelerometer sensor, if the device has one. Otherwise, the method returns Vector3.ZERO.
m.Input.get_action_raw_strength: Returns a value between 0 and 1 representing the raw intensity of the given action, ignoring the action's deadzone. In most cases, you should use get_action_strength() instead.
m.Input.get_action_strength: Returns a value between 0 and 1 representing the intensity of the given action. In a joypad, for example, the further away the axis (analog sticks or L2, R2 triggers) is from the dead zone, the closer the value will be to 1. If the action is mapped to a control that has no axis such as the keyboard, the value returned will be 0 or 1.
m.Input.get_axis: 返回两个动作之间的差值（如左右移动）。
m.Input.get_connected_joypads: Returns an Array containing the device IDs of all currently connected joypads.
m.Input.get_current_cursor_shape: Returns the currently assigned cursor shape.
m.Input.get_gravity: Returns the gravity in m/s² of the device's accelerometer sensor, if the device has one. Otherwise, the method returns Vector3.ZERO.
m.Input.get_gyroscope: Returns the rotation rate in rad/s around a device's X, Y, and Z axes of the gyroscope sensor, if the device has one. Otherwise, the method returns Vector3.ZERO.
m.Input.get_joy_accelerometer: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.get_joy_axis: Returns the current value of the joypad axis at index axis.
m.Input.get_joy_gravity: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.get_joy_guid: Returns an SDL-compatible device GUID on platforms that use gamepad remapping, e.g. 030000004c050000c405000000010000. Returns an empty string if it cannot be found. Godot uses SDL's internal mappings, supplemented by community-contributed mappings, to determine gamepad names and mappings based on this GUID.
m.Input.get_joy_gyroscope: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.get_joy_info: Returns a dictionary with extra platform-specific information about the device, e.g. the raw gamepad name from the OS or the Steam Input index.
m.Input.get_joy_motion_sensors_calibration: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.get_joy_motion_sensors_rate: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.get_joy_name: Returns the name of the joypad at the specified device index, e.g. PS4 Controller. Godot uses the SDL2 game controller database [https://github.com/gabomdq/SDL_GameControllerDB] to determine gamepad names.
m.Input.get_joy_vibration_duration: Returns the duration of the current vibration effect in seconds.
m.Input.get_joy_vibration_remaining_durati: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.get_joy_vibration_strength: Returns the strength of the joypad vibration: x is the strength of the weak motor, and y is the strength of the strong motor.
m.Input.get_last_mouse_screen_velocity: Returns the last mouse velocity in screen coordinates. To provide a precise and jitter-free velocity, mouse velocity is only calculated every 0.1s. Therefore, mouse velocity will lag mouse movements.
m.Input.get_last_mouse_velocity: Returns the last mouse velocity. To provide a precise and jitter-free velocity, mouse velocity is only calculated every 0.1s. Therefore, mouse velocity will lag mouse movements.
m.Input.get_magnetometer: Returns the magnetic field strength in micro-Tesla for all axes of the device's magnetometer sensor, if the device has one. Otherwise, the method returns Vector3.ZERO.
m.Input.get_mouse_button_mask: Returns mouse buttons as a bitmask. If multiple mouse buttons are pressed at the same time, the bits are added together. Equivalent to DisplayServer.mouse_get_button_state().
m.Input.has_joy_light: Returns true if the joypad has an LED light that can change colors and/or brightness. See also set_joy_light().
m.Input.has_joy_motion_sensors: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.has_joy_vibration: Returns true if the joypad supports vibration. See also start_joy_vibration().
m.Input.ignore_joypad_on_unfocused_applica: If true, joypad input (including motion sensors) and LED light changes will be ignored and joypad vibration will be stopped when the application is not focused.
m.Input.is_action_just_pressed: Returns true when the user has started pressing the action event in the current frame or physics tick. It will only return true on the frame or tick that the user pressed down the button.
m.Input.is_action_just_pressed_by_event: Returns true when the user has started pressing the action event in the current frame or physics tick, and the first event that triggered action press in the current frame/physics tick was event. It will only return true on the frame or tick that the user pressed down the button.
m.Input.is_action_just_released: Returns true when the user stops pressing the action event in the current frame or physics tick. It will only return true on the frame or tick that the user releases the button.
m.Input.is_action_just_released_by_event: Returns true when the user stops pressing the action event in the current frame or physics tick, and the first event that triggered action release in the current frame/physics tick was event. It will only return true on the frame or tick that the user releases the button.
m.Input.is_action_pressed: 判断动作是否被按下。动作在项目设置→输入映射中定义。
m.Input.is_anything_pressed: Returns true if any action, key, joypad button, or mouse button is being pressed. This will also return true if any action is simulated via code by calling action_press().
m.Input.is_joy_button_pressed: Returns true if you are pressing the joypad button at index button.
m.Input.is_joy_known: Returns true if the system knows the specified device. This means that it sets all button and axis indices. Unknown joypads are not expected to match these constants, but you can still retrieve events from them.
m.Input.is_joy_motion_sensors_calibrated: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.is_joy_motion_sensors_calibrating: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.is_joy_motion_sensors_enabled: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.is_joy_vibrating: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.is_key_label_pressed: Returns true if you are pressing the key with the keycode printed on it. You can pass a Key constant or any Unicode character code.
m.Input.is_key_pressed: 判断键盘按键是否按下。
m.Input.is_mouse_button_pressed: Returns true if you are pressing the mouse button specified with MouseButton.
m.Input.is_physical_key_pressed: Returns true if you are pressing the key in the physical location on the 101/102-key US QWERTY keyboard. You can pass a Key constant.
m.Input.joy_connection_changed: Emitted when a joypad device has been connected or disconnected.
m.Input.parse_input_event: Feeds an InputEvent to the game. Can be used to artificially trigger input events from code. Also generates Node._input() calls.
m.Input.remove_joy_mapping: Removes all mappings from the internal database that match the given GUID. All currently connected joypads that use this GUID will become unmapped.
m.Input.set_accelerometer: Sets the acceleration value of the accelerometer sensor. Can be used for debugging on devices without a hardware sensor, for example in an editor on a PC.
m.Input.set_custom_mouse_cursor: Sets a custom mouse cursor image, which is only visible inside the game window, for the given mouse shape. The hotspot can also be specified. Passing null to the image parameter resets to the system cursor.
m.Input.set_default_cursor_shape: Sets the default cursor shape to be used in the viewport instead of CURSOR_ARROW.
m.Input.set_gravity: Sets the gravity value of the accelerometer sensor. Can be used for debugging on devices without a hardware sensor, for example in an editor on a PC.
m.Input.set_gyroscope: Sets the value of the rotation rate of the gyroscope sensor. Can be used for debugging on devices without a hardware sensor, for example in an editor on a PC.
m.Input.set_joy_light: Sets the joypad's LED light, if available, to the specified color. See also has_joy_light().
m.Input.set_joy_motion_sensors_calibration: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.set_joy_motion_sensors_enabled: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.set_magnetometer: Sets the value of the magnetic field of the magnetometer sensor. Can be used for debugging on devices without a hardware sensor, for example in an editor on a PC.
m.Input.should_ignore_device: Queries whether an input device should be ignored or not. Devices can be ignored by setting the environment variable SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_IGNORE_DEVICES. Read the SDL documentation [https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL2] for more information.
m.Input.start_joy_motion_sensors_calibrati: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.start_joy_vibration: Starts to vibrate the joypad. See also has_joy_vibration() and is_joy_vibrating().
m.Input.stop_joy_motion_sensors_calibratio: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.Input.stop_joy_vibration: Stops the vibration of the joypad started with start_joy_vibration().
m.Input.use_accumulated_input: If true, similar input events sent by the operating system are accumulated. When input accumulation is enabled, all input events generated during a frame will be merged and emitted when the frame is done rendering. Therefore, this limits the number of input method calls per second to the rendering FPS.
m.Input.vibrate_handheld: Vibrate the handheld device for the specified duration in milliseconds.
m.Input.warp_mouse: Sets the mouse position to the specified vector, provided in pixels and relative to an origin at the upper left corner of the currently focused Window Manager game window.
m.InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_EMULATION: Device ID used for emulated mouse input from a touchscreen, or for emulated touch input from a mouse. This can be used to distinguish emulated mouse input from physical mouse input, or emulated touch input from physical touch input.
m.InputEvent.accumulate: Returns true if the given input event and this input event can be added together (only for events of type InputEventMouseMotion).
m.InputEvent.as_text: Returns a String representation of the event.
m.InputEvent.get_action_strength: Returns a value between 0.0 and 1.0 depending on the given actions' state. Useful for getting the value of events of type InputEventJoypadMotion.
m.InputEvent.is_action: Returns true if this input event matches a pre-defined action of any type.
m.InputEvent.is_action_pressed: Returns true if the given action matches this event and is being pressed (and is not an echo event for InputEventKey events, unless allow_echo is true). Not relevant for events of type InputEventMouseMotion or InputEventScreenDrag.
m.InputEvent.is_action_released: Returns true if the given action matches this event and is released (i.e. not pressed). Not relevant for events of type InputEventMouseMotion or InputEventScreenDrag.
m.InputEvent.is_action_type: Returns true if this input event's type is one that can be assigned to an input action: InputEventKey, InputEventMouseButton, InputEventJoypadButton, InputEventJoypadMotion, InputEventAction. Returns false for all other input event types.
m.InputEvent.is_canceled: Returns true if this input event has been canceled.
m.InputEvent.is_echo: Returns true if this input event is an echo event (only for events of type InputEventKey). An echo event is a repeated key event sent when the user is holding down the key. Any other event type returns false.
m.InputEvent.is_match: Returns true if the specified event matches this event. Only valid for action events, which include key (InputEventKey), button (InputEventMouseButton or InputEventJoypadButton), axis InputEventJoypadMotion, and action (InputEventAction) events.
m.InputEvent.is_pressed: Returns true if this input event is pressed. Not relevant for events of type InputEventMouseMotion or InputEventScreenDrag.
m.InputEvent.is_released: Returns true if this input event is released. Not relevant for events of type InputEventMouseMotion or InputEventScreenDrag.
m.InputEvent.xformed_by: Returns a copy of the given input event which has been offset by local_ofs and transformed by xform. Relevant for events of type InputEventMouseButton, InputEventMouseMotion, InputEventScreenTouch, InputEventScreenDrag, InputEventMagnifyGesture and InputEventPanGesture.
m.InputEventAction.action: The action's name. This is usually the name of an existing action in the InputMap which you want this custom event to match.
m.InputEventAction.event_index: The real event index in action this event corresponds to (from events defined for this action in the InputMap). If -1, a unique ID will be used and actions pressed with this ID will need to be released with another InputEventAction.
m.InputEventAction.pressed: If true, the action's state is pressed. If false, the action's state is released.
m.InputEventAction.strength: The action's strength between 0 and 1. This value is considered as equal to 0 if pressed is false. The event strength allows faking analog joypad motion events, by specifying how strongly the joypad axis is bent or pressed.
m.InputEventFromWindow.window_id: The ID of a Window that received this event.
m.InputEventGesture.position: The local gesture position relative to the Viewport. If used in Control._gui_input(), the position is relative to the current Control that received this gesture.
m.InputEventJoypadButton.button_index: Button identifier. One of the JoyButton button constants.
m.InputEventJoypadButton.pressed: If true, the button's state is pressed. If false, the button's state is released.
m.InputEventJoypadButton.pressure: Deprecated: This property is never set by the engine and is always 0.
m.InputEventJoypadMotion.axis_value: Current position of the joystick on the given axis. The value ranges from -1.0 to 1.0. A value of 0 means the axis is in its resting position.
m.InputEventKey.as_text_key_label: Returns a String representation of the event's key_label and modifiers.
m.InputEventKey.as_text_keycode: Returns a String representation of the event's keycode and modifiers.
m.InputEventKey.as_text_location: Returns a String representation of the event's location. This will be a blank string if the event is not specific to a location.
m.InputEventKey.as_text_physical_keycode: Returns a String representation of the event's physical_keycode and modifiers.
m.InputEventKey.echo: If true, the key was already pressed before this event. An echo event is a repeated key event sent when the user is holding down the key.
m.InputEventKey.get_key_label_with_modifie: Returns the localized key label combined with modifier keys such as Shift or Alt. See also InputEventWithModifiers.
m.InputEventKey.get_keycode_with_modifiers: Returns the Latin keycode combined with modifier keys such as Shift or Alt. See also InputEventWithModifiers.
m.InputEventKey.get_physical_keycode_with_: Returns the physical keycode combined with modifier keys such as Shift or Alt. See also InputEventWithModifiers.
m.InputEventKey.key_label: Represents the localized label printed on the key in the current keyboard layout, which corresponds to one of the Key constants or any valid Unicode character. Key labels are meant for key prompts.
m.InputEventKey.keycode: Latin label printed on the key in the current keyboard layout, which corresponds to one of the Key constants. Key codes are meant for shortcuts expressed with a standard Latin keyboard, such as Ctrl + S for a "Save" shortcut.
m.InputEventKey.location: Represents the location of a key which has both left and right versions, such as Shift or Alt.
m.InputEventKey.physical_keycode: Represents the physical location of a key on the 101/102-key US QWERTY keyboard, which corresponds to one of the Key constants. Physical key codes meant for game input, such as WASD movement, where only the location of the keys is important.
m.InputEventKey.pressed: If true, the key's state is pressed. If false, the key's state is released.
m.InputEventKey.unicode: The key Unicode character code (when relevant), shifted by modifier keys. Unicode character codes for composite characters and complex scripts may not be available unless IME input mode is active. See Window.set_ime_active() for more information. Unicode character codes are meant for text input.
m.InputEventMIDI.channel: The MIDI channel of this message, ranging from 0 to 15. MIDI channel 9 is reserved for percussion instruments.
m.InputEventMIDI.controller_number: The unique number of the controller, if message is @GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_CONTROL_CHANGE, otherwise this is 0. This value can be used to identify sliders for volume, balance, and panning, as well as switches and pedals on the MIDI device. See the General MIDI specification [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_MIDI#Controller_events] for a small list.
m.InputEventMIDI.controller_value: The value applied to the controller. If message is @GlobalScope.MIDI_MESSAGE_CONTROL_CHANGE, this value ranges from 0 to 127, otherwise it is 0. See also controller_value.
m.InputEventMIDI.instrument: The instrument (also called program or preset) used on this MIDI message. This value ranges from 0 to 127.
m.InputEventMIDI.message: Represents the type of MIDI message (see the MIDIMessage enum).
m.InputEventMIDI.pitch: The pitch index number of this MIDI message. This value ranges from 0 to 127.
m.InputEventMIDI.pressure: The strength of the key being pressed. This value ranges from 0 to 127.
m.InputEventMIDI.velocity: The velocity of the MIDI message. This value ranges from 0 to 127. For a musical keyboard, this corresponds to how quickly the key was pressed, and is rarely above 110 in practice.
m.InputEventMagnifyGesture.factor: The amount (or delta) of the event. This value is closer to 1.0 the slower the gesture is performed.
m.InputEventMouse.button_mask: The mouse button mask identifier, one of or a bitwise combination of the MouseButton button masks.
m.InputEventMouse.global_position: When received in Node._input() or Node._unhandled_input(), returns the mouse's position in the root Viewport using the coordinate system of the root Viewport.
m.InputEventMouse.position: When received in Node._input() or Node._unhandled_input(), returns the mouse's position in the Viewport this Node is in using the coordinate system of this Viewport.
m.InputEventMouseButton.button_index: The mouse button identifier, one of the MouseButton button or button wheel constants.
m.InputEventMouseButton.canceled: If true, the mouse button event has been canceled.
m.InputEventMouseButton.double_click: If true, the mouse button's state is a double-click.
m.InputEventMouseButton.factor: The amount (or delta) of the event. When used for high-precision scroll events, this indicates the scroll amount (vertical or horizontal). This is only supported on some platforms; the reported sensitivity varies depending on the platform. May be 0 if not supported.
m.InputEventMouseButton.pressed: If true, the mouse button's state is pressed. If false, the mouse button's state is released.
m.InputEventMouseMotion.pen_inverted: Returns true when using the eraser end of a stylus pen.
m.InputEventMouseMotion.pressure: Represents the pressure the user puts on the pen. Ranges from 0.0 to 1.0.
m.InputEventMouseMotion.relative: The mouse position relative to the previous position (position at the last frame).
m.InputEventMouseMotion.screen_relative: The unscaled mouse position relative to the previous position in the coordinate system of the screen (position at the last frame).
m.InputEventMouseMotion.screen_velocity: The unscaled mouse velocity in pixels per second in screen coordinates. This velocity is not scaled according to the content scale factor or calls to InputEvent.xformed_by().
m.InputEventMouseMotion.tilt: Represents the angles of tilt of the pen. Positive X-coordinate value indicates a tilt to the right. Positive Y-coordinate value indicates a tilt toward the user. Ranges from -1.0 to 1.0 for both axes.
m.InputEventMouseMotion.velocity: The mouse velocity in pixels per second.
m.InputEventPanGesture.delta: Panning amount since last pan event.
m.InputEventScreenDrag.index: The drag event index in the case of a multi-drag event.
m.InputEventScreenDrag.pen_inverted: Returns true when using the eraser end of a stylus pen.
m.InputEventScreenDrag.position: The drag position in the viewport the node is in, using the coordinate system of this viewport.
m.InputEventScreenDrag.pressure: Represents the pressure the user puts on the pen. Ranges from 0.0 to 1.0.
m.InputEventScreenDrag.relative: The drag position relative to the previous position (position at the last frame).
m.InputEventScreenDrag.screen_relative: The unscaled drag position relative to the previous position in screen coordinates (position at the last frame). This position is not scaled according to the content scale factor or calls to InputEvent.xformed_by(). This should be preferred over relative for touch aiming regardless of the project's stretch mode.
m.InputEventScreenDrag.screen_velocity: The unscaled drag velocity in pixels per second in screen coordinates. This velocity is not scaled according to the content scale factor or calls to InputEvent.xformed_by(). This should be preferred over velocity for touch aiming regardless of the project's stretch mode.
m.InputEventScreenDrag.tilt: Represents the angles of tilt of the pen. Positive X-coordinate value indicates a tilt to the right. Positive Y-coordinate value indicates a tilt toward the user. Ranges from -1.0 to 1.0 for both axes.
m.InputEventScreenTouch.canceled: If true, the touch event has been canceled.
m.InputEventScreenTouch.double_tap: If true, the touch's state is a double tap.
m.InputEventScreenTouch.index: The touch index in the case of a multi-touch event. One index = one finger.
m.InputEventScreenTouch.position: The touch position in the viewport the node is in, using the coordinate system of this viewport.
m.InputEventScreenTouch.pressed: If true, the touch's state is pressed. If false, the touch's state is released.
m.InputEventShortcut.shortcut: The Shortcut represented by this event. Its Shortcut.matches_event() method will always return true for this event.
m.InputEventWithModifiers.command_or_contr: Automatically use Meta (Cmd) on macOS and Ctrl on other platforms. If true, ctrl_pressed and meta_pressed cannot be set.
m.InputEventWithModifiers.get_modifiers_ma: Returns the keycode combination of modifier keys.
m.InputEventWithModifiers.is_command_or_co: On macOS, returns true if Meta (Cmd) is pressed.
m.InputEventWithModifiers.meta_pressed: State of the Meta modifier. On Windows and Linux, this represents the Windows key (sometimes called "meta" or "super" on Linux). On macOS, this represents the Command key.
m.InputMap.action_add_event: Adds an InputEvent to an action. This InputEvent will trigger the action.
m.InputMap.action_erase_event: Removes an InputEvent from an action.
m.InputMap.action_erase_events: Removes all events from an action.
m.InputMap.action_get_deadzone: Returns a deadzone value for the action.
m.InputMap.action_get_events: Returns an array of InputEvents associated with a given action.
m.InputMap.action_has_event: Returns true if the action has the given InputEvent associated with it.
m.InputMap.action_set_deadzone: Sets a deadzone value for the action.
m.InputMap.add_action: Adds an empty action to the InputMap with a configurable deadzone.
m.InputMap.erase_action: Removes an action from the InputMap.
m.InputMap.event_is_action: Returns true if the given event is part of an existing action. This method ignores keyboard modifiers if the given InputEvent is not pressed (for proper release detection). See action_has_event() if you don't want this behavior.
m.InputMap.get_action_description: Returns the human-readable description of the given action.
m.InputMap.get_actions: Returns an array of all actions in the InputMap.
m.InputMap.has_action: Returns true if the InputMap has a registered action with the given name.
m.InputMap.load_from_project_settings: Clears all InputEventAction in the InputMap and load it anew from ProjectSettings.
m.InputMap.project_settings_loaded: Emitted when the ProjectSettings InputMap has been loaded.
m.InstancePlaceholder.create_instance: Call this method to actually load in the node. The created node will be placed as a sibling above the InstancePlaceholder in the scene tree. The Node's reference is also returned for convenience.
m.InstancePlaceholder.get_instance_path: Gets the path to the PackedScene resource file that is loaded by default when calling create_instance(). Not thread-safe. Use Object.call_deferred() if calling from a thread.
m.InstancePlaceholder.get_stored_values: Returns the list of properties that will be applied to the node when create_instance() is called.
m.ItemList.ICON_MODE_LEFT: Icon is drawn to the left of the text.
m.ItemList.ICON_MODE_TOP: Icon is drawn above the text.
m.ItemList.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_BOTH: Scroll hints will be shown at the top and bottom.
m.ItemList.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_BOTTOM: Only the bottom scroll hint will be shown.
m.ItemList.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_DISABLED: Scroll hints will never be shown.
m.ItemList.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_TOP: Only the top scroll hint will be shown.
m.ItemList.SELECT_MULTI: Allows selecting multiple items by holding Ctrl or Shift.
m.ItemList.SELECT_SINGLE: Only allow selecting a single item.
m.ItemList.SELECT_TOGGLE: Allows selecting multiple items by toggling them on and off.
m.ItemList.add_icon_item: Adds an item to the item list with no text, only an icon. Returns the index of an added item.
m.ItemList.add_item: Adds an item to the item list with specified text. Returns the index of an added item.
m.ItemList.allow_reselect: If true, the currently selected item can be selected again.
m.ItemList.allow_rmb_select: If true, right mouse button click can select items.
m.ItemList.allow_search: If true, allows navigating the ItemList with letter keys through incremental search.
m.ItemList.auto_height: If true, the control will automatically resize the height to fit its content.
m.ItemList.auto_width: If true, the control will automatically resize the width to fit its content.
m.ItemList.center_on_current: Ensures the currently selected item (the first selected item if multiple selection is enabled) is visible, adjusting the scroll position as necessary to place the item at the center of the list if possible. See also ensure_current_is_visible().
m.ItemList.clear: Removes all items from the list.
m.ItemList.deselect: Ensures the item associated with the specified index is not selected.
m.ItemList.deselect_all: Ensures there are no items selected.
m.ItemList.empty_clicked: Emitted when any mouse click is issued within the rect of the list but on empty space.
m.ItemList.ensure_current_is_visible: Ensures the currently selected item (the first selected item if multiple selection is enabled) is visible, adjusting the scroll position as necessary. See also center_on_current().
m.ItemList.fixed_column_width: The width all columns will be adjusted to.
m.ItemList.fixed_icon_size: The size all icons will be adjusted to.
m.ItemList.force_update_list_size: Forces an update to the list size based on its items. This happens automatically whenever size of the items, or other relevant settings like auto_height, change. The method can be used to trigger the update ahead of next drawing pass.
m.ItemList.get_item_at_position: Returns the item index at the given position.
m.ItemList.get_item_custom_bg_color: Returns the custom background color of the item specified by idx index.
m.ItemList.get_item_custom_fg_color: Returns the custom foreground color of the item specified by idx index.
m.ItemList.get_item_icon: Returns the icon associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.get_item_icon_modulate: Returns a Color modulating item's icon at the specified index.
m.ItemList.get_item_icon_region: Returns the region of item's icon used. The whole icon will be used if the region has no area.
m.ItemList.get_item_metadata: Returns the metadata value of the specified index.
m.ItemList.get_item_rect: Returns the position and size of the item with the specified index, in the coordinate system of the ItemList node. If expand is true the last column expands to fill the rest of the row.
m.ItemList.get_item_text: Returns the text associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.get_item_text_direction: Returns item's text base writing direction.
m.ItemList.get_item_tooltip: Returns the tooltip hint associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.get_selected_items: Returns an array with the indexes of the selected items.
m.ItemList.icon_mode: The icon position, whether above or to the left of the text. See the IconMode constants.
m.ItemList.icon_scale: The scale of icon applied after fixed_icon_size and transposing takes effect.
m.ItemList.is_anything_selected: Returns true if one or more items are selected.
m.ItemList.is_item_disabled: Returns true if the item at the specified index is disabled.
m.ItemList.is_item_icon_transposed: Returns true if the item icon will be drawn transposed, i.e. the X and Y axes are swapped.
m.ItemList.is_item_selectable: Returns true if the item at the specified index is selectable.
m.ItemList.is_item_tooltip_enabled: Returns true if the tooltip is enabled for specified item index.
m.ItemList.is_selected: Returns true if the item at the specified index is currently selected.
m.ItemList.item_activated: Emitted when specified list item is activated via double-clicking or by pressing Enter.
m.ItemList.item_clicked: Emitted when specified list item has been clicked with any mouse button.
m.ItemList.item_count: The number of items currently in the list.
m.ItemList.item_selected: Emitted when specified item has been selected. Only applicable in single selection mode.
m.ItemList.max_columns: Maximum columns the list will have.
m.ItemList.max_text_lines: Maximum lines of text allowed in each item. Space will be reserved even when there is not enough lines of text to display.
m.ItemList.move_item: Moves item from index from_idx to to_idx.
m.ItemList.multi_selected: Emitted when a multiple selection is altered on a list allowing multiple selection.
m.ItemList.remove_item: Removes the item specified by idx index from the list.
m.ItemList.same_column_width: Whether all columns will have the same width.
m.ItemList.scroll_hint_mode: The way which scroll hints (indicators that show that the content can still be scrolled in a certain direction) will be shown.
m.ItemList.select: Selects the item at the specified index.
m.ItemList.select_mode: Allows single or multiple item selection. See the SelectMode constants.
m.ItemList.set_item_auto_translate_mode: Sets the auto translate mode of the item associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_custom_bg_color: Sets the background color of the item specified by idx index to the specified Color.
m.ItemList.set_item_custom_fg_color: Sets the foreground color of the item specified by idx index to the specified Color.
m.ItemList.set_item_disabled: Disables (or enables) the item at the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_icon: Sets (or replaces) the icon's Texture2D associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_icon_modulate: Sets a modulating Color of the item associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_icon_region: Sets the region of item's icon used. The whole icon will be used if the region has no area.
m.ItemList.set_item_icon_transposed: Sets whether the item icon will be drawn transposed.
m.ItemList.set_item_language: Sets the language code of the text for the item at the given index to language. This is used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If language is empty, the current locale is used.
m.ItemList.set_item_metadata: Sets a value (of any type) to be stored with the item associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_selectable: Allows or disallows selection of the item associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_text: Sets text of the item associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_text_direction: Sets item's text base writing direction.
m.ItemList.set_item_tooltip: Sets the tooltip hint for the item associated with the specified index.
m.ItemList.set_item_tooltip_enabled: Sets whether the tooltip hint is enabled for specified item index.
m.ItemList.sort_items_by_text: Sorts items in the list by their text.
m.ItemList.text_overrun_behavior: The clipping behavior when the text exceeds an item's bounding rectangle.
m.ItemList.tile_scroll_hint: If true, the scroll hint texture will be tiled instead of stretched. See scroll_hint_mode.
m.ItemList.wraparound_items: If true, the control will automatically move items into a new row to fit its content. See also HFlowContainer for this behavior.
m.IterateIK3D.angular_delta_limit: The maximum amount each bone can rotate in a single iteration.
m.IterateIK3D.deterministic: If false, the result is calculated from the previous frame's IterateIK3D result as the initial state.
m.IterateIK3D.get_joint_limitation: Returns the joint limitation at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.get_joint_limitation_right_a: Returns the joint limitation right axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
Returns the joint limitation right axis vector at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.get_joint_limitation_rotatio: Returns the joint limitation rotation offset at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.get_joint_rotation_axis: Returns the rotation axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.get_joint_rotation_axis_vect: Returns the rotation axis vector for the specified joint in the bone chain. This vector represents the axis around which the joint can rotate. It is determined based on the rotation axis set for the joint.
m.IterateIK3D.get_target_node: Returns the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.
m.IterateIK3D.max_iterations: The number of iteration loops used by the IK solver to produce more accurate results.
m.IterateIK3D.min_distance: The minimum distance between the end bone and the target. If the distance is below this value, the IK solver stops any further iterations.
m.IterateIK3D.set_joint_limitation: Sets the joint limitation at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.set_joint_limitation_right_a: Sets the joint limitation right axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
Sets the optional joint limitation right axis vector at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.set_joint_limitation_rotatio: Sets the joint limitation rotation offset at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.set_joint_rotation_axis: Sets the rotation axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
m.IterateIK3D.set_joint_rotation_axis_vect: Sets the rotation axis vector for the specified joint in the bone chain.
m.IterateIK3D.set_target_node: Sets the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.
m.JNISingleton.has_java_method: Returns true if the given method name exists in the JNISingleton's Java methods.
m.JSON.data: Contains the parsed JSON data in Variant form.
m.JSON.from_native: Converts a native engine type to a JSON-compliant value.
m.JSON.get_error_line: Returns 0 if the last call to parse() was successful, or the line number where the parse failed.
m.JSON.get_error_message: Returns an empty string if the last call to parse() was successful, or the error message if it failed.
m.JSON.get_parsed_text: Return the text parsed by parse() (requires passing keep_text to parse()).
m.JSON.parse: Attempts to parse the json_text provided.
m.JSON.parse_string: Attempts to parse the json_string provided and returns the parsed data. Returns null if parse failed.
m.JSON.stringify: Converts a Variant var to JSON text and returns the result. Useful for serializing data to store or send over the network.
m.JSONRPC.INTERNAL_ERROR: An internal error occurred while processing the request. Not used by the built-in JSONRPC.
m.JSONRPC.INVALID_PARAMS: A method call was requested but the given method parameters are not valid. Not used by the built-in JSONRPC.
m.JSONRPC.INVALID_REQUEST: A method call was requested but the request's format is not valid.
m.JSONRPC.METHOD_NOT_FOUND: A method call was requested but no function of that name existed in the JSONRPC subclass.
m.JSONRPC.PARSE_ERROR: The request could not be parsed as it was not valid by JSON standard (JSON.parse() failed).
m.JSONRPC.make_notification: Returns a dictionary in the form of a JSON-RPC notification. Notifications are one-shot messages which do not expect a response.
m.JSONRPC.make_request: Returns a dictionary in the form of a JSON-RPC request. Requests are sent to a server with the expectation of a response. The ID field is used for the server to specify which exact request it is responding to.
m.JSONRPC.make_response: When a server has received and processed a request, it is expected to send a response. If you did not want a response then you need to have sent a Notification instead.
m.JSONRPC.make_response_error: Creates a response which indicates a previous reply has failed in some way.
m.JSONRPC.process_action: Given a Dictionary which takes the form of a JSON-RPC request: unpack the request and run it. Methods are resolved by looking at the field called "method" and looking for an equivalently named function in the JSONRPC object. If one is found that method is called.
m.JSONRPC.process_string: There is currently no description for this method. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.JSONRPC.set_method: Registers a callback for the given method name.
m.JavaClass.get_java_method_list: Returns the object's Java methods and their signatures as an Array of dictionaries, in the same format as Object.get_method_list().
m.JavaClass.get_java_parent_class: Returns a JavaClass representing the Java parent class of this class.
m.JavaClass.has_java_method: Returns true if the given method name exists in the object's Java methods.
m.JavaClassWrapper.create_proxy: Creates a JavaObject implementing the given Java interfaces using the given Object as the implementation.
m.JavaClassWrapper.create_sam_callback: Creates a JavaObject implementing the Java Single Abstract Method (SAM) interface using the Godot Callable as the implementation.
m.JavaClassWrapper.get_exception: Returns the Java exception from the last call into a Java class. If there was no exception, it will return null.
m.JavaClassWrapper.wrap: Wraps a class defined in Java, and returns it as a JavaClass Object type that Godot can interact with.
m.JavaObject.get_java_class: Returns the JavaClass that this object is an instance of.
m.JavaObject.has_java_method: Returns true if the given method name exists in the object's Java methods.
m.JavaScriptBridge.create_callback: Creates a reference to a Callable that can be used as a callback by JavaScript. The reference must be kept until the callback happens, or it won't be called at all. See JavaScriptObject for usage.
m.JavaScriptBridge.create_object: Creates a new JavaScript object using the new constructor. The object must a valid property of the JavaScript window. See JavaScriptObject for usage.
m.JavaScriptBridge.download_buffer: Prompts the user to download a file containing the specified buffer. The file will have the given name and mime type.
m.JavaScriptBridge.eval: Execute the string code as JavaScript code within the browser window. This is a call to the actual global JavaScript function eval().
m.JavaScriptBridge.force_fs_sync: Force synchronization of the persistent file system (when enabled).
m.JavaScriptBridge.get_interface: Returns an interface to a JavaScript object that can be used by scripts. The interface must be a valid property of the JavaScript window. The callback must accept a single Array argument, which will contain the JavaScript arguments. See JavaScriptObject for usage.
m.JavaScriptBridge.is_js_buffer: Returns true if the given javascript_object is of type ArrayBuffer [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/ArrayBuffer], DataView [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/DataView], or one of the many typed array objects [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypedArray].
m.JavaScriptBridge.js_buffer_to_packed_byt: Returns a copy of javascript_buffer's contents as a PackedByteArray. See also is_js_buffer().
m.JavaScriptBridge.pwa_needs_update: Returns true if a new version of the progressive web app is waiting to be activated.
m.JavaScriptBridge.pwa_update: Performs the live update of the progressive web app. Forcing the new version to be installed and the page to be reloaded.
m.JavaScriptBridge.pwa_update_available: Emitted when an update for this progressive web app has been detected but is waiting to be activated because a previous version is active. See pwa_update() to force the update to take place immediately.
m.Joint2D.bias: When node_a and node_b move in different directions the bias controls how fast the joint pulls them back to their original position. The lower the bias the more the two bodies can pull on the joint.
m.Joint2D.disable_collision: If true, the two bodies bound together do not collide with each other.
m.Joint2D.get_rid: Returns the joint's internal RID from the PhysicsServer2D.
m.Joint2D.node_a: Path to the first body (A) attached to the joint. The node must inherit PhysicsBody2D.
m.Joint2D.node_b: Path to the second body (B) attached to the joint. The node must inherit PhysicsBody2D.
m.Joint3D.exclude_nodes_from_collision: If true, the two bodies bound together do not collide with each other.
m.Joint3D.get_rid: Returns the joint's internal RID from the PhysicsServer3D.
m.Joint3D.node_a: Path to the first node (A) attached to the joint. The node must inherit PhysicsBody3D.
m.Joint3D.node_b: Path to the second node (B) attached to the joint. The node must inherit PhysicsBody3D.
m.Joint3D.solver_priority: The priority used to define which solver is executed first for multiple joints. The lower the value, the higher the priority.
m.JointLimitationCone3D.angle: The radius range of the hole made by the cone.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_angle: Returns the collision angle according to up_direction, which is Vector2.UP by default. This value is always positive.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_collider: Returns the colliding body's attached Object.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_collider_id: Returns the unique instance ID of the colliding body's attached Object. See Object.get_instance_id().
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_collider_rid: Returns the colliding body's RID used by the PhysicsServer2D.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_collider_shape_: Returns the colliding body's shape index. See CollisionObject2D.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_depth: Returns the colliding body's length of overlap along the collision normal.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_local_shape: Returns the moving object's colliding shape.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_normal: Returns the colliding body's shape's normal at the point of collision.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_position: Returns the point of collision in global coordinates.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_remainder: Returns the moving object's remaining movement vector.
m.KinematicCollision2D.get_travel: Returns the moving object's travel before collision.
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_angle: Returns the collision angle according to up_direction, which is Vector3.UP by default. This value is always positive.
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_collider: Returns the colliding body's attached Object given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_collider_id: Returns the unique instance ID of the colliding body's attached Object given a collision index (the deepest collision by default). See Object.get_instance_id().
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_collider_rid: Returns the colliding body's RID used by the PhysicsServer3D given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_collider_shape: Returns the colliding body's shape given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_collider_shape_: Returns the colliding body's shape index given a collision index (the deepest collision by default). See CollisionObject3D.
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_collider_veloci: Returns the colliding body's velocity given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_collision_count: Returns the number of detected collisions.
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_depth: Returns the colliding body's length of overlap along the collision normal.
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_local_shape: Returns the moving object's colliding shape given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_normal: Returns the colliding body's shape's normal at the point of collision given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_position: Returns the point of collision in global coordinates given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_remainder: Returns the moving object's remaining movement vector.
m.KinematicCollision3D.get_travel: Returns the moving object's travel before collision.
m.Label.autowrap_mode: If set to something other than TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF, the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle. If you resize the node, it will change its height automatically to show all the text.
m.Label.autowrap_trim_flags: Autowrap space trimming flags. See TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_START_EDGE_SPACES and TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_END_EDGE_SPACES for more info.
m.Label.clip_text: If true, the Label only shows the text that fits inside its bounding rectangle and will clip text horizontally.
m.Label.ellipsis_char: Ellipsis character used for text clipping.
m.Label.get_character_bounds: Returns the bounding rectangle of the character at position pos in the label's local coordinate system. If the character is a non-visual character or pos is outside the valid range, an empty Rect2 is returned. If the character is a part of a composite grapheme, the bounding rectangle of the whole grapheme is returned.
m.Label.get_line_count: Returns the number of lines of text the Label has.
m.Label.get_line_height: Returns the height of the line line.
m.Label.get_total_character_count: Returns the total number of printable characters in the text (excluding spaces and newlines).
m.Label.get_visible_line_count: Returns the number of lines shown. Useful if the Label's height cannot currently display all lines.
m.Label.horizontal_alignment: Controls the text's horizontal alignment. Supports left, center, right, and fill (also known as justify).
m.Label.label_settings: A LabelSettings resource that can be shared between multiple Label nodes. Takes priority over theme properties.
m.Label.language: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.Label.lines_skipped: The number of the lines ignored and not displayed from the start of the text value.
m.Label.max_lines_visible: Limits the lines of text the node shows on screen.
m.Label.paragraph_separator: String used as a paragraph separator. Each paragraph is processed independently, in its own BiDi context.
m.Label.structured_text_bidi_override: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.
m.Label.structured_text_bidi_override_opti: Set additional options for BiDi override.
m.Label.tab_stops: Aligns text to the given tab-stops.
m.Label.text: The text to display on screen.
m.Label.text_overrun_behavior: The clipping behavior when the text exceeds the node's bounding rectangle.
m.Label.uppercase: If true, all the text displays as UPPERCASE.
m.Label.vertical_alignment: Controls the text's vertical alignment. Supports top, center, bottom, and fill.
m.Label.visible_characters: The number of characters to display. If set to -1, all characters are displayed. This can be useful when animating the text appearing in a dialog box.
m.Label.visible_characters_behavior: The clipping behavior when visible_characters or visible_ratio is set.
m.Label.visible_ratio: The fraction of characters to display, relative to the total number of characters (see get_total_character_count()). If set to 1.0, all characters are displayed. If set to 0.5, only half of the characters will be displayed. This can be useful when animating the text appearing in a dialog box.
m.Label3D.ALPHA_CUT_DISABLED: This mode performs standard alpha blending. It can display translucent areas, but transparency sorting issues may be visible when multiple transparent materials are overlapping. GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow has no effect when this transparency mode is used; the Label3D will never cast shadows.
m.Label3D.ALPHA_CUT_DISCARD: This mode only allows fully transparent or fully opaque pixels. Harsh edges will be visible unless some form of screen-space antialiasing is enabled (see ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/screen_space_aa). This mode is also known as alpha testing or 1-bit transparency.
m.Label3D.ALPHA_CUT_HASH: This mode draws cuts off all values below a spatially-deterministic threshold, the rest will remain opaque.
m.Label3D.ALPHA_CUT_OPAQUE_PREPASS: This mode draws fully opaque pixels in the depth prepass. This is slower than ALPHA_CUT_DISABLED or ALPHA_CUT_DISCARD, but it allows displaying translucent areas and smooth edges while using proper sorting.
m.Label3D.FLAG_DISABLE_DEPTH_TEST: Disables the depth test, so this object is drawn on top of all others. However, objects drawn after it in the draw order may cover it.
m.Label3D.FLAG_DOUBLE_SIDED: If set, text can be seen from the back as well. If not, the text is invisible when looking at it from behind.
m.Label3D.FLAG_FIXED_SIZE: Label is scaled by depth so that it always appears the same size on screen.
m.Label3D.FLAG_MAX: Represents the size of the DrawFlags enum.
m.Label3D.FLAG_SHADED: If set, lights in the environment affect the label.
m.Label3D.alpha_antialiasing_edge: Threshold at which antialiasing will be applied on the alpha channel.
m.Label3D.alpha_antialiasing_mode: The type of alpha antialiasing to apply.
m.Label3D.alpha_cut: The alpha cutting mode to use for the sprite.
m.Label3D.alpha_hash_scale: The hashing scale for Alpha Hash. Recommended values between 0 and 2.
m.Label3D.alpha_scissor_threshold: Threshold at which the alpha scissor will discard values.
m.Label3D.autowrap_mode: If set to something other than TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF, the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle. If you resize the node, it will change its height automatically to show all the text.
m.Label3D.autowrap_trim_flags: Autowrap space trimming flags. See TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_START_EDGE_SPACES and TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_END_EDGE_SPACES for more info.
m.Label3D.billboard: The billboard mode to use for the label.
m.Label3D.double_sided: If true, text can be seen from the back as well, if false, it is invisible when looking at it from behind.
m.Label3D.fixed_size: If true, the label is rendered at the same size regardless of distance. The label's size on screen is the same as if the camera was 1.0 units away from the label's origin, regardless of the actual distance from the camera. The Camera3D's field of view (or Camera3D.size when in orthogonal/frustum mode) still affects the size the label is drawn at.
m.Label3D.font: Font configuration used to display text.
m.Label3D.font_size: Font size of the Label3D's text. To make the font look more detailed when up close, increase font_size while decreasing pixel_size at the same time.
m.Label3D.generate_triangle_mesh: Returns a TriangleMesh with the label's vertices following its current configuration (such as its pixel_size).
m.Label3D.get_draw_flag: Returns the value of the specified flag.
m.Label3D.horizontal_alignment: Controls the text's horizontal alignment. Supports left, center, right, and fill (also known as justify).
m.Label3D.language: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.Label3D.line_spacing: Additional vertical spacing between lines (in pixels), spacing is added to line descent. This value can be negative.
m.Label3D.no_depth_test: If true, depth testing is disabled and the object will be drawn in render order.
m.Label3D.outline_render_priority: Sets the render priority for the text outline. Higher priority objects will be sorted in front of lower priority objects.
m.Label3D.pixel_size: The size of one pixel's width on the label to scale it in 3D. To make the font look more detailed when up close, increase font_size while decreasing pixel_size at the same time.
m.Label3D.render_priority: Sets the render priority for the text. Higher priority objects will be sorted in front of lower priority objects.
m.Label3D.set_draw_flag: If true, the specified flag will be enabled.
m.Label3D.shaded: If true, the Light3D in the Environment has effects on the label.
m.Label3D.structured_text_bidi_override: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.
m.Label3D.structured_text_bidi_override_op: Set additional options for BiDi override.
m.Label3D.text: The text to display on screen.
m.Label3D.uppercase: If true, all the text displays as UPPERCASE.
m.Label3D.vertical_alignment: Controls the text's vertical alignment. Supports top, center, and bottom.
m.Label3D.width: Text width (in pixels), used for autowrap and fill alignment.
m.LabelSettings.Color: The color of the outline at index.
m.LabelSettings.Vector2: The offset of the shadow at index.
m.LabelSettings.add_stacked_outline: Adds a new stacked outline to the label at the given index. If index is -1, the new stacked outline will be added at the end of the list.
m.LabelSettings.add_stacked_shadow: Adds a new stacked shadow to the label at the given index. If index is -1, the new stacked shadow will be added at the end of the list.
m.LabelSettings.get_stacked_outline_color: Returns the color of the stacked outline at index.
m.LabelSettings.get_stacked_outline_size: Returns the size of the stacked outline at index.
m.LabelSettings.get_stacked_shadow_color: Returns the color of the stacked shadow at index.
m.LabelSettings.get_stacked_shadow_offset: Returns the offset of the stacked shadow at index.
m.LabelSettings.get_stacked_shadow_outline: Returns the outline size of the stacked shadow at index.
m.LabelSettings.line_spacing: Additional vertical spacing between lines (in pixels), spacing is added to line descent. This value can be negative.
m.LabelSettings.move_stacked_outline: Moves the stacked outline at index from_index to the given position to_position in the array.
m.LabelSettings.move_stacked_shadow: Moves the stacked shadow at index from_index to the given position to_position in the array.
m.LabelSettings.paragraph_spacing: Vertical space between paragraphs. Added on top of line_spacing.
m.LabelSettings.remove_stacked_outline: Removes the stacked outline at index index.
m.LabelSettings.remove_stacked_shadow: Removes the stacked shadow at index index.
m.LabelSettings.set_stacked_outline_color: Sets the color of the stacked outline identified by the given index to color.
m.LabelSettings.set_stacked_outline_size: Sets the size of the stacked outline identified by the given index to size.
m.LabelSettings.set_stacked_shadow_color: Sets the color of the stacked shadow identified by the given index to color.
m.LabelSettings.set_stacked_shadow_offset: Sets the offset of the stacked shadow identified by the given index to offset.
m.LabelSettings.set_stacked_shadow_outline: Sets the outline size of the stacked shadow identified by the given index to size.
m.LabelSettings.shadow_color: Color of the shadow effect. If alpha is 0, no shadow will be drawn.
m.LabelSettings.shadow_offset: Offset of the shadow effect, in pixels.
m.Light2D.BLEND_MODE_ADD: Adds the value of pixels corresponding to the Light2D to the values of pixels under it. This is the common behavior of a light.
m.Light2D.BLEND_MODE_MIX: Mix the value of pixels corresponding to the Light2D to the values of pixels under it by linear interpolation.
m.Light2D.BLEND_MODE_SUB: Subtracts the value of pixels corresponding to the Light2D to the values of pixels under it, resulting in inversed light effect.
m.Light2D.SHADOW_FILTER_NONE: No filter applies to the shadow map. This provides hard shadow edges and is the fastest to render. See shadow_filter.
