m.Light2D.SHADOW_FILTER_PCF13: Percentage closer filtering (13 samples) applies to the shadow map. This is the slowest shadow filtering mode, and should be used sparingly. See shadow_filter.
m.Light2D.SHADOW_FILTER_PCF5: Percentage closer filtering (5 samples) applies to the shadow map. This is slower compared to hard shadow rendering. See shadow_filter.
m.Light2D.editor_only: If true, Light2D will only appear when editing the scene.
m.Light2D.enabled: If true, Light2D will emit light.
m.Light2D.energy: The Light2D's energy value. The larger the value, the stronger the light.
m.Light2D.get_height: Returns the light's height, which is used in 2D normal mapping. See PointLight2D.height and DirectionalLight2D.height.
m.Light2D.range_item_cull_mask: The layer mask. Only objects with a matching CanvasItem.light_mask will be affected by the Light2D. See also shadow_item_cull_mask, which affects which objects can cast shadows.
m.Light2D.range_layer_max: Maximum layer value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.
m.Light2D.range_layer_min: Minimum layer value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.
m.Light2D.range_z_max: Maximum z value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.
m.Light2D.range_z_min: Minimum z value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.
m.Light2D.set_height: Sets the light's height, which is used in 2D normal mapping. See PointLight2D.height and DirectionalLight2D.height.
m.Light2D.shadow_color: Color of shadows cast by the Light2D.
m.Light2D.shadow_enabled: If true, the Light2D will cast shadows.
m.Light2D.shadow_filter_smooth: Smoothing value for shadows. Higher values will result in softer shadows, at the cost of visible streaks that can appear in shadow rendering. shadow_filter_smooth only has an effect if shadow_filter is SHADOW_FILTER_PCF5 or SHADOW_FILTER_PCF13.
m.Light2D.shadow_item_cull_mask: The shadow mask. Used with LightOccluder2D to cast shadows. Only occluders with a matching CanvasItem.light_mask will cast shadows. See also range_item_cull_mask, which affects which objects can receive the light.
m.Light3D.BAKE_DISABLED: Light is ignored when baking. This is the fastest mode, but the light will not be taken into account when baking global illumination. This mode should generally be used for dynamic lights that change quickly, as the effect of global illumination is less noticeable on those lights.
m.Light3D.BAKE_DYNAMIC: Light is taken into account in dynamic baking (VoxelGI and SDFGI (Environment.sdfgi_enabled) only). The light can be moved around or modified with global illumination updating in real-time. The light's global illumination appearance will be slightly different compared to BAKE_STATIC. This has a greater performance cost compared to BAKE_STATIC. When using SDFGI, the update speed of dynamic lights…
m.Light3D.BAKE_STATIC: Light is taken into account in static baking (VoxelGI, LightmapGI, SDFGI (Environment.sdfgi_enabled)). The light can be moved around or modified, but its global illumination will not update in real-time. This is suitable for subtle changes (such as flickering torches), but generally not large changes such as toggling a light on and off.
m.Light3D.PARAM_ATTENUATION: Constant for accessing OmniLight3D.omni_attenuation or SpotLight3D.spot_attenuation.
m.Light3D.PARAM_INTENSITY: Constant for accessing light_intensity_lumens and light_intensity_lux. Only used when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is true.
m.Light3D.PARAM_MAX: Represents the size of the Param enum.
m.Light3D.PARAM_RANGE: Constant for accessing OmniLight3D.omni_range or SpotLight3D.spot_range.
m.Light3D.distance_fade_begin: The distance from the camera at which the light begins to fade away (in 3D units).
m.Light3D.distance_fade_enabled: If true, the light will smoothly fade away when far from the active Camera3D starting at distance_fade_begin. This acts as a form of level of detail (LOD). The light will fade out over distance_fade_begin + distance_fade_length, after which it will be culled and not sent to the shader at all. Use this to reduce the number of active lights in a scene and thus improve performance.
m.Light3D.distance_fade_length: Distance over which the light and its shadow fades. The light's energy and shadow's opacity is progressively reduced over this distance and is completely invisible at the end.
m.Light3D.distance_fade_shadow: The distance from the camera at which the light's shadow cuts off (in 3D units). Set this to a value lower than distance_fade_begin + distance_fade_length to further improve performance, as shadow rendering is often more expensive than light rendering itself.
m.Light3D.editor_only: If true, the light only appears in the editor and will not be visible at runtime. If true, the light will never be baked in LightmapGI regardless of its light_bake_mode.
m.Light3D.get_correlated_color: Returns the Color of an idealized blackbody at the given light_temperature. This value is calculated internally based on the light_temperature. This Color is multiplied by light_color before being sent to the RenderingServer.
m.Light3D.get_param: Returns the value of the specified Param parameter.
m.Light3D.light_angular_distance: The light's angular size in degrees. Increasing this will make shadows softer at greater distances (also called percentage-closer soft shadows, or PCSS). Only available for DirectionalLight3Ds. For reference, the Sun from the Earth is approximately 0.5. Increasing this value above 0.0 for lights with shadows enabled will have a noticeable performance cost due to PCSS.
m.Light3D.light_bake_mode: The light's bake mode. This will affect the global illumination techniques that have an effect on the light's rendering.
m.Light3D.light_color: The light's color in nonlinear sRGB encoding. An overbright color can be used to achieve a result equivalent to increasing the light's light_energy.
m.Light3D.light_cull_mask: The light will affect objects in the selected layers.
m.Light3D.light_energy: The light's strength multiplier (this is not a physical unit). For OmniLight3D and SpotLight3D, changing this value will only change the light color's intensity, not the light's radius.
m.Light3D.light_indirect_energy: Secondary multiplier used with indirect light (light bounces). Used with VoxelGI and SDFGI (see Environment.sdfgi_enabled).
m.Light3D.light_intensity_lumens: Used by positional lights (OmniLight3D and SpotLight3D) when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is true. Sets the intensity of the light source measured in Lumens. Lumens are a measure of luminous flux, which is the total amount of visible light emitted by a light source per unit of time.
m.Light3D.light_intensity_lux: Used by DirectionalLight3Ds when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is true. Sets the intensity of the light source measured in Lux. Lux is a measure of luminous flux per unit area, it is equal to one lumen per square meter. Lux is the measure of how much light hits a surface at a given time.
m.Light3D.light_negative: If true, the light's effect is reversed, darkening areas and casting bright shadows.
m.Light3D.light_projector: Texture2D projected by light. shadow_enabled must be on for the projector to work. Light projectors make the light appear as if it is shining through a colored but transparent object, almost like light shining through stained-glass.
m.Light3D.light_size: The simulated size of the light in Godot units, affecting shading and shadows. For OmniLight3Ds and SpotLight3Ds, increasing this value simulates a spherical area light, expanding the size of specular highlights. If shadows are enabled, a penumbra is rendered, making shadows appear blurrier. For AreaLight3Ds, only the shadows are affected. Penumbras are simulated with percentage-closer soft shado…
m.Light3D.light_specular: The intensity of the specular blob in objects affected by the light. At 0, the light becomes a pure diffuse light. When not baking emission, this can be used to avoid unrealistic reflections when placing lights above an emissive surface.
m.Light3D.light_temperature: Sets the color temperature of the light source, measured in Kelvin. This is used to calculate a correlated color temperature which tints the light_color.
m.Light3D.light_volumetric_fog_energy: Secondary multiplier multiplied with light_energy then used with the Environment's volumetric fog (if enabled). If set to 0.0, computing volumetric fog will be skipped for this light, which can improve performance for large amounts of lights when volumetric fog is enabled.
m.Light3D.set_param: Sets the value of the specified Param parameter.
m.Light3D.shadow_bias: Used to adjust shadow appearance. Too small a value results in self-shadowing ("shadow acne"), while too large a value causes shadows to separate from casters ("peter-panning"). Adjust as needed.
m.Light3D.shadow_blur: Blurs the edges of the shadow. Can be used to hide pixel artifacts in low-resolution shadow maps. A high value can impact performance, make shadows appear grainy and can cause other unwanted artifacts. Try to keep as near default as possible.
m.Light3D.shadow_caster_mask: The light will only cast shadows using objects in the selected layers.
m.Light3D.shadow_enabled: If true, the light will cast real-time shadows. This has a significant performance cost. Only enable shadow rendering when it makes a noticeable difference in the scene's appearance, and consider using distance_fade_enabled to hide the light when far away from the Camera3D.
m.Light3D.shadow_normal_bias: Offsets the lookup into the shadow map by the object's normal. This can be used to reduce self-shadowing artifacts without using shadow_bias. In practice, this value should be tweaked along with shadow_bias to reduce artifacts as much as possible.
m.Light3D.shadow_opacity: The opacity to use when rendering the light's shadow map. Values lower than 1.0 make the light appear through shadows. This can be used to fake global illumination at a low performance cost.
m.Light3D.shadow_reverse_cull_face: If true, reverses the backface culling of the mesh. This can be useful when you have a flat mesh that has a light behind it. If you need to cast a shadow on both sides of the mesh, set the mesh to use double-sided shadows with GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_DOUBLE_SIDED.
m.Light3D.shadow_transmittance_bias: There is currently no description for this property. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.LightOccluder2D.occluder: The OccluderPolygon2D used to compute the shadow.
m.LightOccluder2D.occluder_light_mask: The LightOccluder2D's occluder light mask. The LightOccluder2D will cast shadows only from Light2D(s) that have the same light mask(s).
m.LightOccluder2D.sdf_collision: If enabled, the occluder will be part of a real-time generated signed distance field that can be used in custom shaders.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_ATLAS_TOO_SMALL: Lightmap baking failed as the lightmap was unable to fit into an atlas.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_CANT_CREATE_IMAGE: Lightmap baking failed as the resulting image couldn't be saved or imported by Godot after it was saved.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_FOREIGN_DATA: Lightmap baking failed as the lightmap data resource is embedded in a foreign resource.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_LIGHTMAP_TOO_SMALL: Lightmap baking failed as the lightmap is too small.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_MESHES_INVALID: Lightmap baking failed as the lightmapper failed to analyze some of the meshes marked as static for baking.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_NO_LIGHTMAPPER: Lightmap baking failed as there is no lightmapper available in this Godot build.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_NO_MESHES: Lightmap baking failed as there are no meshes whose GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode is GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_STATIC and with valid UV2 mapping in the current scene. You may need to select 3D scenes in the Import dock and change their global illumination mode accordingly.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_NO_SAVE_PATH: Lightmap baking failed as the LightmapGIData save path isn't configured in the resource.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_NO_SCENE_ROOT: Lightmap baking failed because the root node for the edited scene could not be accessed.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_TEXTURE_SIZE_TOO_S: Lightmap baking failed as the maximum texture size is too small to fit some of the meshes marked for baking.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_ERROR_USER_ABORTED: The user aborted the lightmap baking operation (typically by clicking the Cancel button in the progress dialog).
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_QUALITY_HIGH: High bake quality (slow bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/high_quality_ray_count and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/high_quality_probe_ray_count.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_QUALITY_LOW: Low bake quality (fastest bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/low_quality_ray_count and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/low_quality_probe_ray_count.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_QUALITY_MEDIUM: Medium bake quality (fast bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/medium_quality_ray_count and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/medium_quality_probe_ray_count.
m.LightmapGI.BAKE_QUALITY_ULTRA: Highest bake quality (slowest bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/ultra_quality_ray_count and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/ultra_quality_probe_ray_count.
m.LightmapGI.ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_COLOR: Use environment_custom_color multiplied by environment_custom_energy as a constant source of environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
m.LightmapGI.ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_SKY: Use environment_custom_sky as a source of environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
m.LightmapGI.ENVIRONMENT_MODE_DISABLED: Ignore environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
m.LightmapGI.ENVIRONMENT_MODE_SCENE: Use the scene's environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
m.LightmapGI.GENERATE_PROBES_DISABLED: Don't generate lightmap probes for lighting dynamic objects.
m.LightmapGI.GENERATE_PROBES_SUBDIV_16: High level of subdivision (slow bake times, large file sizes).
m.LightmapGI.GENERATE_PROBES_SUBDIV_32: Highest level of subdivision (slowest bake times, largest file sizes).
m.LightmapGI.GENERATE_PROBES_SUBDIV_4: Lowest level of subdivision (fastest bake times, smallest file sizes).
m.LightmapGI.GENERATE_PROBES_SUBDIV_8: Low level of subdivision (fast bake times, small file sizes).
m.LightmapGI.bias: The bias to use when computing shadows. Increasing bias can fix shadow acne on the resulting baked lightmap, but can introduce peter-panning (shadows not connecting to their casters). Real-time Light3D shadows are not affected by this bias property.
m.LightmapGI.bounce_indirect_energy: The energy multiplier for each bounce. Higher values will make indirect lighting brighter. A value of 1.0 represents physically accurate behavior, but higher values can be used to make indirect lighting propagate more visibly when using a low number of bounces. This can be used to speed up bake times by lowering the number of bounces then increasing bounce_indirect_energy.
m.LightmapGI.bounces: Number of light bounces that are taken into account during baking. Higher values result in brighter, more realistic lighting, at the cost of longer bake times. If set to 0, only environment lighting, direct light and emissive lighting is baked.
m.LightmapGI.camera_attributes: The CameraAttributes resource that specifies exposure levels to bake at. Auto-exposure and non exposure properties will be ignored. Exposure settings should be used to reduce the dynamic range present when baking. If exposure is too high, the LightmapGI will have banding artifacts or may have over-exposure artifacts.
m.LightmapGI.denoiser_range: The distance in pixels from which the denoiser samples. Lower values preserve more details, but may give blotchy results if the lightmap quality is not high enough. Only effective if use_denoiser is true and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/denoising/denoiser is set to JNLM.
m.LightmapGI.denoiser_strength: The strength of denoising step applied to the generated lightmaps. Only effective if use_denoiser is true and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/denoising/denoiser is set to JNLM.
m.LightmapGI.directional: If true, bakes lightmaps to contain directional information as spherical harmonics. This results in more realistic lighting appearance, especially with normal mapped materials and for lights that have their direct light baked (Light3D.light_bake_mode set to Light3D.BAKE_STATIC and with Light3D.editor_only set to false). The directional information is also used to provide rough reflections for sta…
m.LightmapGI.environment_custom_color: The color to use for environment lighting. Only effective if environment_mode is ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_COLOR.
m.LightmapGI.environment_custom_energy: The color multiplier to use for environment lighting. Only effective if environment_mode is ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_COLOR.
m.LightmapGI.environment_custom_sky: The sky to use as a source of environment lighting. Only effective if environment_mode is ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_SKY.
m.LightmapGI.environment_mode: The environment mode to use when baking lightmaps.
m.LightmapGI.generate_probes_subdiv: The level of subdivision to use when automatically generating LightmapProbes for dynamic object lighting. Higher values result in more accurate indirect lighting on dynamic objects, at the cost of longer bake times and larger file sizes.
m.LightmapGI.interior: If true, ignore environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
m.LightmapGI.light_data: The LightmapGIData associated to this LightmapGI node. This resource is automatically created after baking, and is not meant to be created manually.
m.LightmapGI.max_texture_size: The maximum texture size for the generated texture atlas. Higher values will result in fewer slices being generated, but may not work on all hardware as a result of hardware limitations on texture sizes. Leave max_texture_size at its default value of 16384 if unsure.
m.LightmapGI.quality: The quality preset to use when baking lightmaps. This affects bake times, but output file sizes remain mostly identical across quality levels.
m.LightmapGI.shadowmask_mode: Experimental: This property may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.LightmapGI.supersampling: If true, lightmaps are baked with the texel scale multiplied with supersampling_factor and downsampled before saving the lightmap (so the effective texel density is identical to having supersampling disabled).
m.LightmapGI.supersampling_factor: The factor by which the texel density is multiplied for supersampling. For best results, use an integer value. While fractional values are allowed, they can result in increased light leaking and a blurry lightmap.
m.LightmapGI.texel_scale: Scales the lightmap texel density of all meshes for the current bake. This is a multiplier that builds upon the existing lightmap texel size defined in each imported 3D scene, along with the per-mesh density multiplier (which is designed to be used when the same mesh is used at different scales). Lower values will result in faster bake times.
m.LightmapGI.use_denoiser: If true, uses a GPU-based denoising algorithm on the generated lightmap. This eliminates most noise within the generated lightmap at the cost of longer bake times. File sizes are generally not impacted significantly by the use of a denoiser, although lossless compression may do a better job at compressing a denoised image.
m.LightmapGI.use_texture_for_bounces: If true, a texture with the lighting information will be generated to speed up the generation of indirect lighting at the cost of some accuracy. The geometry might exhibit extra light leak artifacts when using low resolution lightmaps or UVs that stretch the lightmap significantly across surfaces. Leave use_texture_for_bounces at its default value of true if unsure.
m.LightmapGIData.SHADOWMASK_MODE_NONE: Shadowmasking is disabled. No shadowmask texture will be created when baking lightmaps. Existing shadowmask textures will be removed during baking.
m.LightmapGIData.SHADOWMASK_MODE_OVERLAY: Shadowmasking is enabled. Directional shadows will be rendered with real-time shadows overlaid on top of the shadowmask texture. This mode makes for smoother shadow transitions when the camera moves fast, at the cost of a potential smearing effect for directional shadows that are up close (due to the real-time shadow being mixed with a low-resolution shadowmask). Objects that only have shadows ba…
m.LightmapGIData.SHADOWMASK_MODE_REPLACE: Shadowmasking is enabled. Directional shadows that are outside the DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_max_distance will be rendered using the shadowmask texture. Shadows that are inside the range will be rendered using real-time shadows exclusively. This mode allows for more precise real-time shadows up close, without the potential "smearing" effect that can occur when using lightmaps with a h…
m.LightmapGIData.add_user: Adds an object that is considered baked within this LightmapGIData.
m.LightmapGIData.clear_users: Clear all objects that are considered baked within this LightmapGIData.
m.LightmapGIData.get_user_count: Returns the number of objects that are considered baked within this LightmapGIData.
m.LightmapGIData.get_user_path: Returns the NodePath of the baked object at index user_idx.
m.LightmapGIData.is_using_spherical_harmon: If true, lightmaps were baked with directional information. See also LightmapGI.directional.
m.LightmapGIData.light_texture: Deprecated: The lightmap atlas can now contain multiple textures. See lightmap_textures.
m.LightmapGIData.lightmap_textures: The lightmap atlas textures generated by the lightmapper.
m.LightmapGIData.set_uses_spherical_harmon: If uses_spherical_harmonics is true, tells the engine to treat the lightmap data as if it was baked with directional information.
m.LightmapGIData.shadowmask_textures: The shadowmask atlas textures generated by the lightmapper.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.exclude: If true, the modifier processes bones not included in the bone list.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.get_end_b: Returns the end bone index of the bone chain.
Returns the end bone name of the bone chain.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.get_root_: Returns the root bone index of the bone chain.
Returns the root bone name of the bone chain.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.joint_cou: The number of joints in the list which created by chains dynamically.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.max_angul: The maximum angular velocity per second.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.reset: Sets the reference pose for angle comparison to the current pose with the influence of constraints removed. This function is automatically triggered when joints change or upon activation.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.set_end_b: Sets the end bone index of the bone chain.
Sets the end bone name of the bone chain.
m.LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.set_root_: Sets the root bone index of the bone chain.
Sets the root bone name of the bone chain.
m.Line2D.LINE_CAP_BOX: Draws the line cap as a box, slightly extending the first/last segment.
m.Line2D.LINE_CAP_ROUND: Draws the line cap as a semicircle attached to the first/last segment.
m.Line2D.LINE_JOINT_BEVEL: Makes the polyline's joints bevelled/chamfered, connecting the sides of the two segments with a simple line.
m.Line2D.LINE_JOINT_ROUND: Makes the polyline's joints rounded, connecting the sides of the two segments with an arc. The detail of this arc depends on round_precision.
m.Line2D.LINE_JOINT_SHARP: Makes the polyline's joints pointy, connecting the sides of the two segments by extending them until they intersect. If the rotation of a joint is too big (based on sharp_limit), the joint falls back to LINE_JOINT_BEVEL to prevent very long miters.
m.Line2D.LINE_TEXTURE_NONE: Takes the left pixels of the texture and renders them over the whole polyline.
m.Line2D.LINE_TEXTURE_STRETCH: Stretches the texture across the polyline. CanvasItem.texture_repeat of the Line2D node must be CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_DISABLED for best results.
m.Line2D.LINE_TEXTURE_TILE: Tiles the texture over the polyline. CanvasItem.texture_repeat of the Line2D node must be CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_ENABLED or CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_MIRROR for it to work properly.
m.Line2D.add_point: Adds a point with the specified position relative to the polyline's own position. If no index is provided, the new point will be added to the end of the points array.
m.Line2D.antialiased: If true, the polyline's border will be anti-aliased.
m.Line2D.begin_cap_mode: The style of the beginning of the polyline, if closed is false.
m.Line2D.clear_points: Removes all points from the polyline, making it empty.
m.Line2D.closed: If true and the polyline has more than 2 points, the last point and the first one will be connected by a segment.
m.Line2D.default_color: The color of the polyline. Will not be used if a gradient is set.
m.Line2D.end_cap_mode: The style of the end of the polyline, if closed is false.
m.Line2D.get_point_count: Returns the number of points in the polyline.
m.Line2D.get_point_position: Returns the position of the point at index index.
m.Line2D.gradient: The gradient is drawn through the whole line from start to finish. The default_color will not be used if this property is set.
m.Line2D.joint_mode: The style of the connections between segments of the polyline.
m.Line2D.points: The points of the polyline, interpreted in local 2D coordinates. Segments are drawn between the adjacent points in this array.
m.Line2D.remove_point: Removes the point at index index from the polyline.
m.Line2D.round_precision: The smoothness used for rounded joints and caps. Higher values result in smoother corners, but are more demanding to render and update.
m.Line2D.set_point_position: Overwrites the position of the point at the given index with the supplied position.
m.Line2D.sharp_limit: Determines the miter limit of the polyline. Normally, when joint_mode is set to LINE_JOINT_SHARP, sharp angles fall back to using the logic of LINE_JOINT_BEVEL joints to prevent very long miters. Higher values of this property mean that the fallback to a bevel joint will happen at sharper angles.
m.Line2D.texture: The texture used for the polyline. Uses texture_mode for drawing style.
m.Line2D.texture_mode: The style to render the texture of the polyline.
m.Line2D.width_curve: The polyline's width curve. The width of the polyline over its length will be equivalent to the value of the width curve over its domain. The width curve should be a unit Curve.
m.LineEdit.EXPAND_MODE_FIT_TO_LINE_EDIT: Scale the right icon to fit the LineEdit.
m.LineEdit.EXPAND_MODE_FIT_TO_TEXT: Scale the right icon's size to match the size of the text.
m.LineEdit.EXPAND_MODE_ORIGINAL_SIZE: Use the original size for the right icon.
m.LineEdit.KEYBOARD_TYPE_EMAIL_ADDRESS: Virtual keyboard with additional keys to assist with typing email addresses.
m.LineEdit.KEYBOARD_TYPE_NUMBER: Virtual number keypad, useful for PIN entry.
m.LineEdit.KEYBOARD_TYPE_NUMBER_DECIMAL: Virtual number keypad, useful for entering fractional numbers.
m.LineEdit.KEYBOARD_TYPE_PASSWORD: Virtual keyboard for entering a password. On most platforms, this should disable autocomplete and autocapitalization.
m.LineEdit.KEYBOARD_TYPE_URL: Virtual keyboard with additional keys to assist with typing URLs.
m.LineEdit.MENU_CUT: Cuts (copies and clears) the selected text.
m.LineEdit.MENU_EMOJI_AND_SYMBOL: Opens system emoji and symbol picker.
m.LineEdit.MENU_INSERT_LRE: Inserts start of left-to-right embedding (LRE) character.
m.LineEdit.MENU_INSERT_LRO: Inserts start of left-to-right override (LRO) character.
m.LineEdit.MENU_INSERT_RLE: Inserts start of right-to-left embedding (RLE) character.
m.LineEdit.MENU_INSERT_RLO: Inserts start of right-to-left override (RLO) character.
m.LineEdit.MENU_MAX: Represents the size of the MenuItems enum.
m.LineEdit.MENU_PASTE: Pastes the clipboard text over the selected text (or at the caret's position).
m.LineEdit.apply_ime: Applies text from the Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method] (IME) and closes the IME if it is open.
m.LineEdit.backspace_deletes_composite_cha: If true and caret_mid_grapheme is false, backspace deletes an entire composite character such as ❤️‍🩹, instead of deleting part of the composite character.
m.LineEdit.cancel_ime: Closes the Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method] (IME) if it is open. Any text in the IME will be lost.
m.LineEdit.caret_blink: If true, makes the caret blink.
m.LineEdit.caret_blink_interval: The interval at which the caret blinks (in seconds).
m.LineEdit.caret_column: The caret's column position inside the LineEdit. When set, the text may scroll to accommodate it.
m.LineEdit.caret_force_displayed: If true, the LineEdit will always show the caret, even if not editing or focus is lost.
m.LineEdit.caret_mid_grapheme: Allow moving caret, selecting and removing the individual composite character components.
m.LineEdit.clear_button_enabled: If true, the LineEdit will show a clear button if text is not empty, which can be used to clear the text quickly.
m.LineEdit.context_menu_enabled: If true, the context menu will appear when right-clicked.
m.LineEdit.delete_char_at_caret: Deletes one character at the caret's current position (equivalent to pressing Delete).
m.LineEdit.delete_text: Deletes a section of the text going from position from_column to to_column. Both parameters should be within the text's length.
m.LineEdit.deselect_on_focus_loss_enabled: If true, the selected text will be deselected when focus is lost.
m.LineEdit.drag_and_drop_selection_enabled: If true, allow drag and drop of selected text.
m.LineEdit.draw_control_chars: If true, control characters are displayed.
m.LineEdit.edit: Allows entering edit mode whether the LineEdit is focused or not. If hide_focus is true, the focused state will not be shown (see Control.grab_focus()).
m.LineEdit.editable: If false, existing text cannot be modified and new text cannot be added.
m.LineEdit.editing_toggled: Emitted when the LineEdit switches in or out of edit mode.
m.LineEdit.emoji_menu_enabled: If true, "Emoji and Symbols" menu is enabled.
m.LineEdit.expand_to_text_length: If true, the LineEdit width will increase to stay longer than the text. It will not compress if the text is shortened.
m.LineEdit.flat: If true, the LineEdit doesn't display decoration.
m.LineEdit.get_menu: Returns the PopupMenu of this LineEdit. By default, this menu is displayed when right-clicking on the LineEdit.
m.LineEdit.get_next_composite_character_co: Returns the correct column at the end of a composite character like ❤️‍🩹 (mending heart; Unicode: U+2764 U+FE0F U+200D U+1FA79) which is comprised of more than one Unicode code point, if the caret is at the start of the composite character. Also returns the correct column with the caret at mid grapheme and for non-composite characters.
m.LineEdit.get_previous_composite_characte: Returns the correct column at the start of a composite character like ❤️‍🩹 (mending heart; Unicode: U+2764 U+FE0F U+200D U+1FA79) which is comprised of more than one Unicode code point, if the caret is at the end of the composite character. Also returns the correct column with the caret at mid grapheme and for non-composite characters.
m.LineEdit.get_scroll_offset: Returns the scroll offset due to caret_column, as a number of characters.
m.LineEdit.get_selected_text: Returns the text inside the selection.
m.LineEdit.has_ime_text: Returns true if the user has text in the Input Method Editor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_method] (IME).
m.LineEdit.has_redo: Returns true if a "redo" action is available.
m.LineEdit.has_selection: Returns true if the user has selected text.
m.LineEdit.has_undo: Returns true if an "undo" action is available.
m.LineEdit.icon_expand_mode: Define the scaling behavior of the right_icon.
m.LineEdit.insert_text_at_caret: Inserts text at the caret. If the resulting value is longer than max_length, nothing happens.
m.LineEdit.is_editing: Returns whether the LineEdit is being edited.
m.LineEdit.is_menu_visible: Returns whether the menu is visible. Use this instead of get_menu().visible to improve performance (so the creation of the menu is avoided).
m.LineEdit.keep_editing_on_text_submit: If true, the LineEdit will not exit edit mode when text is submitted by pressing ui_text_submit action (by default: Enter or Kp Enter).
m.LineEdit.language: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.LineEdit.max_length: Maximum number of characters that can be entered inside the LineEdit. If 0, there is no limit.
m.LineEdit.menu_option: Executes a given action as defined in the MenuItems enum.
m.LineEdit.middle_mouse_paste_enabled: If false, using middle mouse button to paste clipboard will be disabled.
m.LineEdit.placeholder_text: Text shown when the LineEdit is empty. It is not the LineEdit's default value (see text).
m.LineEdit.right_icon: Sets the icon that will appear in the right end of the LineEdit if there's no text, or always, if clear_button_enabled is set to false.
m.LineEdit.right_icon_scale: Scale ratio of the icon when icon_expand_mode is set to EXPAND_MODE_FIT_TO_LINE_EDIT.
m.LineEdit.secret: If true, every character is replaced with the secret character (see secret_character).
m.LineEdit.secret_character: The character to use to mask secret input. Only a single character can be used as the secret character. If it is longer than one character, only the first one will be used. If it is empty, a space will be used instead.
m.LineEdit.select: Selects characters inside LineEdit between from and to. By default, from is at the beginning and to at the end.
m.LineEdit.select_all_on_focus: If true, the LineEdit will select the whole text when it gains focus.
m.LineEdit.selecting_enabled: If false, it's impossible to select the text using mouse nor keyboard.
m.LineEdit.shortcut_keys_enabled: If true, shortcut keys for context menu items are enabled, even if the context menu is disabled.
m.LineEdit.structured_text_bidi_override: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.
m.LineEdit.structured_text_bidi_override_o: Set additional options for BiDi override.
m.LineEdit.text_change_rejected: Emitted when appending text that overflows the max_length. The appended text is truncated to fit max_length, and the part that couldn't fit is passed as the rejected_substring argument.
m.LineEdit.text_submitted: Emitted when the user presses the ui_text_submit action (by default: Enter or Kp Enter) while the LineEdit has focus.
m.LineEdit.unedit: Allows exiting edit mode while preserving focus.
m.LineEdit.virtual_keyboard_enabled: If true, the native virtual keyboard is enabled on platforms that support it.
m.LineEdit.virtual_keyboard_show_on_focus: If true, the native virtual keyboard is shown on focus events on platforms that support it.
m.LineEdit.virtual_keyboard_type: Specifies the type of virtual keyboard to show.
m.LinkButton.UNDERLINE_MODE_ALWAYS: The LinkButton will always show an underline at the bottom of its text.
m.LinkButton.UNDERLINE_MODE_NEVER: The LinkButton will never show an underline at the bottom of its text.
m.LinkButton.UNDERLINE_MODE_ON_HOVER: The LinkButton will show an underline at the bottom of its text when the mouse cursor is over it.
m.LinkButton.ellipsis_char: Ellipsis character used for text clipping.
m.LinkButton.language: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.LinkButton.structured_text_bidi_override: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.
Set additional options for BiDi override.
m.LinkButton.text: The button's text that will be displayed inside the button's area.
m.LinkButton.text_overrun_behavior: Sets the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the node's bounding rectangle.
m.LinkButton.underline: The underline mode to use for the text.
m.LinkButton.uri: The URI [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Identifier] for this LinkButton. If set to a valid URI, pressing the button opens the URI using the operating system's default program for the protocol (via OS.shell_open()). HTTP and HTTPS URLs open the default web browser.
m.Logger.ERROR_TYPE_ERROR: The message received is an error.
m.Logger.ERROR_TYPE_SCRIPT: The message received is a script error.
m.Logger.ERROR_TYPE_SHADER: The message received is a shader error.
m.Logger.ERROR_TYPE_WARNING: The message received is a warning.
m.Logger._log_error: Called when an error is logged. The error provides the function, file, and line that it originated from, as well as either the code that generated the error or a rationale.
m.Logger._log_message: Called when a message is logged. If error is true, then this message was meant to be sent to stderr.
m.LookAtModifier3D.ORIGIN_FROM_EXTERNAL_NO: The global position of the Node3D specified in origin_external_node is used as origin.
m.LookAtModifier3D.ORIGIN_FROM_SELF: The bone rest position of the bone specified in bone is used as origin.
m.LookAtModifier3D.ORIGIN_FROM_SPECIFIC_BO: The bone global pose position of the bone specified in origin_bone is used as origin.
m.LookAtModifier3D.bone: Index of the bone_name in the parent Skeleton3D.
m.LookAtModifier3D.bone_name: The bone name of the Skeleton3D that the modification will operate on.
m.LookAtModifier3D.duration: The duration of the time-based interpolation. Interpolation is triggered at the following cases:
m.LookAtModifier3D.ease_type: The ease type of the time-based interpolation. See also EaseType.
m.LookAtModifier3D.forward_axis: The forward axis of the bone. This SkeletonModifier3D modifies the bone so that this axis points toward the target_node.
m.LookAtModifier3D.get_interpolation_remai: Returns the remaining seconds of the time-based interpolation.
m.LookAtModifier3D.is_interpolating: Returns true if time-based interpolation is running. If true, it is equivalent to get_interpolation_remaining() returning 0.0.
m.LookAtModifier3D.is_target_within_limita: Returns whether the target is within the angle limitations. It is useful for unsetting the target_node when the target is outside of the angle limitations.
m.LookAtModifier3D.origin_bone: Index of the origin_bone_name in the parent Skeleton3D.
m.LookAtModifier3D.origin_bone_name: If origin_from is ORIGIN_FROM_SPECIFIC_BONE, the bone global pose position specified for this is used as origin.
m.LookAtModifier3D.origin_external_node: If origin_from is ORIGIN_FROM_EXTERNAL_NODE, the global position of the Node3D specified for this is used as origin.
m.LookAtModifier3D.origin_from: This value determines from what origin is retrieved for use in the calculation of the forward vector.
m.LookAtModifier3D.origin_offset: The offset of the bone pose origin. Matching the origins by offset is useful for cases where multiple bones must always face the same direction, such as the eyes.
m.LookAtModifier3D.origin_safe_margin: If the target passes through too close to the origin than this value, time-based interpolation is used even if the target is within the angular limitations, to prevent the angular velocity from becoming too high.
m.LookAtModifier3D.primary_damp_threshold: The threshold to start damping for primary_limit_angle. It provides non-linear (b-spline) interpolation, let it feel more resistance the more it rotate to the edge limit. This is useful for simulating the limits of human motion.
m.LookAtModifier3D.primary_limit_angle: The limit angle of the primary rotation when symmetry_limitation is true, in radians.
m.LookAtModifier3D.primary_negative_damp_t: The threshold to start damping for primary_negative_limit_angle.
m.LookAtModifier3D.primary_negative_limit_: The limit angle of negative side of the primary rotation when symmetry_limitation is false, in radians.
m.LookAtModifier3D.primary_positive_damp_t: The threshold to start damping for primary_positive_limit_angle.
m.LookAtModifier3D.primary_positive_limit_: The limit angle of positive side of the primary rotation when symmetry_limitation is false, in radians.
m.LookAtModifier3D.primary_rotation_axis: The axis of the first rotation. This SkeletonModifier3D works by compositing the rotation by Euler angles to prevent to rotate the forward_axis.
m.LookAtModifier3D.relative: The relative option. If true, the rotation is applied relative to the pose. If false, the rotation is applied relative to the rest. It means to replace the current pose with the LookAtModifier3D's result.
m.LookAtModifier3D.secondary_damp_threshol: The threshold to start damping for secondary_limit_angle.
m.LookAtModifier3D.secondary_limit_angle: The limit angle of the secondary rotation when symmetry_limitation is true, in radians.
m.LookAtModifier3D.secondary_negative_damp: The threshold to start damping for secondary_negative_limit_angle.
m.LookAtModifier3D.secondary_negative_limi: The limit angle of negative side of the secondary rotation when symmetry_limitation is false, in radians.
m.LookAtModifier3D.secondary_positive_damp: The threshold to start damping for secondary_positive_limit_angle.
m.LookAtModifier3D.secondary_positive_limi: The limit angle of positive side of the secondary rotation when symmetry_limitation is false, in radians.
m.LookAtModifier3D.symmetry_limitation: If true, the limitations are spread from the bone symmetrically.
m.LookAtModifier3D.target_node: The NodePath to the node that is the target for the look at modification. This node is what the modification will rotate the bone to.
m.LookAtModifier3D.transition_type: The transition type of the time-based interpolation. See also TransitionType.
m.LookAtModifier3D.use_angle_limitation: If true, limits the amount of rotation. For example, this helps to prevent a character's neck from rotating 360 degrees.
m.LookAtModifier3D.use_secondary_rotation: If true, provides rotation by two axes.
m.MainLoop.NOTIFICATION_OS_MEMORY_WARNING: Notification received from the OS when the application is exceeding its allocated memory.
m.MainLoop._physics_process: Called each physics tick. delta is the logical time between physics ticks in seconds and is equal to Engine.time_scale / Engine.physics_ticks_per_second. Equivalent to Node._physics_process().
m.MainLoop._process: Called on each idle frame, prior to rendering, and after physics ticks have been processed. delta is the time between frames in seconds. Equivalent to Node._process().
m.MainLoop.on_request_permissions_result: Emitted when a user responds to a permission request.
m.Marker2D.gizmo_extents: Size of the gizmo cross that appears in the editor.
m.Marker3D.gizmo_extents: Size of the gizmo cross that appears in the editor.
m.Marshalls.base64_to_raw: Returns a decoded PackedByteArray corresponding to the Base64-encoded string base64_str.
m.Marshalls.base64_to_utf8: Returns a decoded string corresponding to the Base64-encoded string base64_str.
m.Marshalls.base64_to_variant: Returns a decoded Variant corresponding to the Base64-encoded string base64_str. If allow_objects is true, decoding objects is allowed.
m.Marshalls.raw_to_base64: Returns a Base64-encoded string of a given PackedByteArray.
m.Marshalls.utf8_to_base64: Returns a Base64-encoded string of the UTF-8 string utf8_str.
m.Marshalls.variant_to_base64: Returns a Base64-encoded string of the Variant variant. If full_objects is true, encoding objects is allowed (and can potentially include code).
m.Material.RENDER_PRIORITY_MAX: Maximum value for the render_priority parameter.
m.Material._can_do_next_pass: Only exposed for the purpose of overriding. You cannot call this function directly. Used internally to determine if next_pass should be shown in the editor or not.
m.Material._can_use_render_priority: Only exposed for the purpose of overriding. You cannot call this function directly. Used internally to determine if render_priority should be shown in the editor or not.
m.Material._get_shader_mode: Only exposed for the purpose of overriding. You cannot call this function directly. Used internally by various editor tools.
m.Material._get_shader_rid: Only exposed for the purpose of overriding. You cannot call this function directly. Used internally by various editor tools. Used to access the RID of the Material's Shader.
m.Material.create_placeholder: Creates a placeholder version of this resource (PlaceholderMaterial).
m.Material.inspect_native_shader_code: Only available when running in the editor. Opens a popup that visualizes the generated shader code, including all variants and internal shader code. See also Shader.inspect_native_shader_code().
m.Material.next_pass: Sets the Material to be used for the next pass. This renders the object again using a different material.
m.Material.render_priority: Sets the render priority for objects in 3D scenes. Higher priority objects will be sorted in front of lower priority objects. In other words, all objects with render_priority 1 will render on top of all objects with render_priority 0.
m.MenuBar.flat: Flat MenuBar don't display item decoration.
m.MenuBar.get_menu_popup: Returns PopupMenu associated with menu item.
m.MenuBar.is_menu_disabled: Returns true if the menu item is disabled.
m.MenuBar.is_menu_hidden: Returns true if the menu item is hidden.
m.MenuBar.is_native_menu: Returns true if the current system's global menu is supported and used by this MenuBar.
m.MenuBar.language: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.MenuBar.prefer_global_menu: If true, MenuBar will use system global menu when supported.
m.MenuBar.set_disable_shortcuts: If true, shortcuts are disabled and cannot be used to trigger the button.
m.MenuBar.set_menu_disabled: If true, menu item is disabled.
m.MenuBar.set_menu_hidden: If true, menu item is hidden.
m.MenuBar.start_index: Position order in the global menu to insert MenuBar items at. All menu items in the MenuBar are always inserted as a continuous range. Menus with lower start_index are inserted first. Menus with start_index equal to -1 are inserted last.
m.MenuBar.switch_on_hover: If true, when the cursor hovers above menu item, it will close the current PopupMenu and open the other one.
m.MenuButton.about_to_popup: Emitted when the PopupMenu of this MenuButton is about to show.
m.MenuButton.get_popup: Returns the PopupMenu contained in this button.
m.MenuButton.item_count: The number of items currently in the list.
m.MenuButton.set_disable_shortcuts: If true, shortcuts are disabled and cannot be used to trigger the button.
m.MenuButton.show_popup: Adjusts popup position and sizing for the MenuButton, then shows the PopupMenu. Prefer this over using get_popup().popup().
m.MenuButton.switch_on_hover: If true, when the cursor hovers above another MenuButton within the same parent which also has switch_on_hover enabled, it will close the current MenuButton and open the other one.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_BONES: PackedFloat32Array or PackedInt32Array of bone indices. Contains either 4 or 8 numbers per vertex depending on the presence of the ARRAY_FLAG_USE_8_BONE_WEIGHTS flag.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_COMPRESS_FLAGS_BASE: Shift of first compress flag. Compress flags should be passed to ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays() and SurfaceTool.commit().
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM0: Contains custom color channel 0. PackedByteArray if (format >> Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM0_SHIFT) & Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_MASK is ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF, or ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF. PackedFloat32Array otherwise.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM1: Contains custom color channel 1. PackedByteArray if (format >> Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM1_SHIFT) & Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_MASK is ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF, or ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF. PackedFloat32Array otherwise.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM2: Contains custom color channel 2. PackedByteArray if (format >> Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM2_SHIFT) & Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_MASK is ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF, or ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF. PackedFloat32Array otherwise.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM3: Contains custom color channel 3. PackedByteArray if (format >> Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM3_SHIFT) & Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_MASK is ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM, ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF, or ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF. PackedFloat32Array otherwise.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_MAX: Represents the size of the ArrayCustomFormat enum.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM: Indicates this custom channel contains signed normalized byte colors from -1 to 1, encoded as PackedByteArray.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM: Indicates this custom channel contains unsigned normalized byte colors from 0 to 1, encoded as PackedByteArray.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_FLOAT: Indicates this custom channel contains full float colors, in a PackedFloat32Array.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF: Indicates this custom channel contains half precision float colors, encoded as PackedByteArray.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGB_FLOAT: Indicates this custom channel contains full float colors, in a PackedFloat32Array. Only red, green and blue channels are used.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_FLOAT: Indicates this custom channel contains full float colors, in a PackedFloat32Array. Only red and green channels are used.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF: Indicates this custom channel contains half precision float colors, encoded as PackedByteArray. Only red and green channels are used.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_R_FLOAT: Indicates this custom channel contains full float colors, in a PackedFloat32Array. Only the red channel is used.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FLAG_COMPRESS_ATTRIBUTES: Flag used to mark that a mesh is using compressed attributes (vertices, normals, tangents, UVs). When this form of compression is enabled, vertex positions will be packed into an RGBA16UNORM attribute and scaled in the vertex shader. The normal and tangent will be packed into an RG16UNORM representing an axis, and a 16-bit float stored in the A-channel of the vertex. UVs will use 16-bit normalize…
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FLAG_USES_EMPTY_VERTEX_ARRAY: Flag used to mark that the mesh intentionally contains no vertex array.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FLAG_USE_2D_VERTICES: Flag used to mark that the array contains 2D vertices.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FLAG_USE_8_BONE_WEIGHTS: Flag used to mark that the mesh contains up to 8 bone influences per vertex. This flag indicates that ARRAY_BONES and ARRAY_WEIGHTS elements will have double length.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FLAG_USE_DYNAMIC_UPDATE: Flag used to mark that the mesh data will use GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW on GLES. Unused on Vulkan.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_BLEND_SHAPE_MASK: Mask of mesh channels permitted in blend shapes.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM0: Mesh array contains custom channel index 0.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM0_SHIFT: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 0.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM1: Mesh array contains custom channel index 1.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM1_SHIFT: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 1.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM2: Mesh array contains custom channel index 2.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM2_SHIFT: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 2.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM3: Mesh array contains custom channel index 3.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM3_SHIFT: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 3.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_BITS: Number of format bits per custom channel. See ArrayCustomFormat.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_MASK: Mask of custom format bits per custom channel. Must be shifted by one of the SHIFT constants. See ArrayCustomFormat.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_VERTEX: Mesh array contains vertices. All meshes require a vertex array so this should always be present.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX: PackedInt32Array of integers used as indices referencing vertices, colors, normals, tangents, and textures. All of those arrays must have the same number of elements as the vertex array. No index can be beyond the vertex array size. When this index array is present, it puts the function into "index mode," where the index selects the i'th vertex, normal, tangent, color, UV, etc. This means if you…
m.Mesh.ARRAY_MAX: Represents the size of the ArrayType enum.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_TANGENT: PackedFloat32Array of vertex tangents. Each element in groups of 4 floats, first 3 floats determine the tangent, and the last the binormal direction as -1 or 1.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX: PackedVector3Array, PackedVector2Array, or Array of vertex positions.
m.Mesh.ARRAY_WEIGHTS: PackedFloat32Array or PackedFloat64Array of bone weights in the range 0.0 to 1.0 (inclusive). Contains either 4 or 8 numbers per vertex depending on the presence of the ARRAY_FLAG_USE_8_BONE_WEIGHTS flag.
m.Mesh.BLEND_SHAPE_MODE_RELATIVE: Blend shapes are relative to base weight.
m.Mesh.PRIMITIVE_LINES: Render array as lines (every two vertices a line is created).
m.Mesh.PRIMITIVE_POINTS: Render array as points (one vertex equals one point).
m.Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES: Render array as triangles (every three vertices a triangle is created).
m.Mesh._get_aabb: Virtual method to override the AABB for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._get_blend_shape_count: Virtual method to override the number of blend shapes for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._get_blend_shape_name: Virtual method to override the retrieval of blend shape names for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._get_surface_count: Virtual method to override the surface count for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._set_blend_shape_name: Virtual method to override the names of blend shapes for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_array_index_len: Virtual method to override the surface array index length for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_array_len: Virtual method to override the surface array length for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_arrays: Virtual method to override the surface arrays for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_blend_shape_arrays: Virtual method to override the blend shape arrays for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_format: Virtual method to override the surface format for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_lods: Virtual method to override the surface LODs for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_material: Virtual method to override the surface material for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_get_primitive_type: Virtual method to override the surface primitive type for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh._surface_set_material: Virtual method to override the setting of a material at the given index for a custom class extending Mesh.
m.Mesh.create_convex_shape: Calculate a ConvexPolygonShape3D from the mesh.
m.Mesh.create_outline: Calculate an outline mesh at a defined offset (margin) from the original mesh.
m.Mesh.create_placeholder: Creates a placeholder version of this resource (PlaceholderMesh).
m.Mesh.create_trimesh_shape: Calculate a ConcavePolygonShape3D from the mesh.
m.Mesh.generate_triangle_mesh: Generate a TriangleMesh from the mesh. Considers only surfaces using one of these primitive types: PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIP.
m.Mesh.get_aabb: Returns the smallest AABB enclosing this mesh in local space. Not affected by custom_aabb.
m.Mesh.get_faces: Returns all the vertices that make up the faces of the mesh. Each three vertices represent one triangle.
m.Mesh.get_surface_count: Returns the number of surfaces that the Mesh holds. This is equivalent to MeshInstance3D.get_surface_override_material_count().
m.Mesh.lightmap_size_hint: Sets a hint to be used for lightmap resolution.
m.Mesh.surface_get_arrays: Returns the arrays for the vertices, normals, UVs, etc. that make up the requested surface (see ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays()).
m.Mesh.surface_get_blend_shape_arrays: Returns the blend shape arrays for the requested surface.
m.Mesh.surface_get_material: Returns a Material in a given surface. Surface is rendered using this material.
m.Mesh.surface_set_material: Sets a Material for a given surface. Surface will be rendered using this material.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.CONVEX_D: Constant for tetrahedron-based approximate convex decomposition.
Constant for voxel-based approximate convex decomposition.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.convex_h: If true, uses approximation for computing convex hulls.
Controls the precision of the convex-hull generation process during the clipping plane selection stage. Ranges from 1 to 16.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.max_conv: The maximum number of convex hulls to produce from the merge operation.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.max_num_: Controls the maximum number of triangles per convex-hull. Ranges from 4 to 1024.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.min_volu: Controls the adaptive sampling of the generated convex-hulls. Ranges from 0.0 to 0.01.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.mode: Mode for the approximate convex decomposition.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.normaliz: If true, normalizes the mesh before applying the convex decomposition.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.plane_do: Controls the granularity of the search for the "best" clipping plane. Ranges from 1 to 16.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.project_: If true, projects output convex hull vertices onto the original source mesh to increase floating-point accuracy of the results.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.resoluti: Maximum number of voxels generated during the voxelization stage.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.revoluti: Controls the bias toward clipping along revolution axes. Ranges from 0.0 to 1.0.
m.MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.symmetry: Controls the bias toward clipping along symmetry planes. Ranges from 0.0 to 1.0.
m.MeshDataTool.clear: Clears all data currently in MeshDataTool.
m.MeshDataTool.commit_to_surface: Adds a new surface to specified Mesh with edited data.
m.MeshDataTool.create_from_surface: Uses specified surface of given Mesh to populate data for MeshDataTool.
m.MeshDataTool.get_edge_count: Returns the number of edges in this Mesh.
m.MeshDataTool.get_edge_faces: Returns array of faces that touch given edge.
m.MeshDataTool.get_edge_meta: Returns meta information assigned to given edge.
m.MeshDataTool.get_edge_vertex: Returns the index of the specified vertex connected to the edge at index idx.
m.MeshDataTool.get_face_count: Returns the number of faces in this Mesh.
m.MeshDataTool.get_face_edge: Returns the edge associated with the face at index idx.
m.MeshDataTool.get_face_meta: Returns the metadata associated with the given face.
m.MeshDataTool.get_face_normal: Calculates and returns the face normal of the given face.
m.MeshDataTool.get_face_vertex: Returns the specified vertex index of the given face.
m.MeshDataTool.get_format: Returns the Mesh's format as a combination of the ArrayFormat flags. For example, a mesh containing both vertices and normals would return a format of 3 because Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_VERTEX is 1 and Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_NORMAL is 2.
m.MeshDataTool.get_material: Returns the material assigned to the Mesh.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex: Returns the position of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_bones: Returns the bones of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_color: Returns the color of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_count: Returns the total number of vertices in Mesh.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_edges: Returns an array of edges that share the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_faces: Returns an array of faces that share the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_meta: Returns the metadata associated with the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_normal: Returns the normal of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_tangent: Returns the tangent of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_uv: Returns the UV of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_uv2: Returns the UV2 of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.get_vertex_weights: Returns bone weights of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_edge_meta: Sets the metadata of the given edge.
m.MeshDataTool.set_face_meta: Sets the metadata of the given face.
m.MeshDataTool.set_material: Sets the material to be used by newly-constructed Mesh.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex: Sets the position of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_bones: Sets the bones of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_color: Sets the color of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_meta: Sets the metadata associated with the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_normal: Sets the normal of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_tangent: Sets the tangent of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_uv: Sets the UV of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_uv2: Sets the UV2 of the given vertex.
m.MeshDataTool.set_vertex_weights: Sets the bone weights of the given vertex.
m.MeshInstance2D.mesh: The Mesh that will be drawn by the MeshInstance2D.
m.MeshInstance2D.texture: The Texture2D that will be used if using the default CanvasItemMaterial. Can be accessed as TEXTURE in CanvasItem shader.
m.MeshInstance2D.texture_changed: Emitted when the texture is changed.
m.MeshInstance3D.bake_mesh_from_current_bl: Takes a snapshot from the current ArrayMesh with all blend shapes applied according to their current weights and bakes it to the provided existing mesh. If no existing mesh is provided a new ArrayMesh is created, baked and returned. Mesh surface materials are not copied.
m.MeshInstance3D.bake_mesh_from_current_sk: Takes a snapshot of the current animated skeleton pose of the skinned mesh and bakes it to the provided existing mesh. If no existing mesh is provided a new ArrayMesh is created, baked, and returned. Requires a skeleton with a registered skin to work. Blendshapes are ignored. Mesh surface materials are not copied.
m.MeshInstance3D.create_convex_collision: This helper creates a StaticBody3D child node with a ConvexPolygonShape3D collision shape calculated from the mesh geometry. It's mainly used for testing.
m.MeshInstance3D.create_debug_tangents: This helper creates a MeshInstance3D child node with gizmos at every vertex calculated from the mesh geometry. It's mainly used for testing.
m.MeshInstance3D.create_multiple_convex_co: This helper creates a StaticBody3D child node with multiple ConvexPolygonShape3D collision shapes calculated from the mesh geometry via convex decomposition. The convex decomposition operation can be controlled with parameters from the optional settings.
m.MeshInstance3D.create_trimesh_collision: This helper creates a StaticBody3D child node with a ConcavePolygonShape3D collision shape calculated from the mesh geometry. It's mainly used for testing.
m.MeshInstance3D.find_blend_shape_by_name: Returns the index of the blend shape with the given name. Returns -1 if no blend shape with this name exists, including when mesh is null.
m.MeshInstance3D.get_active_material: Returns the Material that will be used by the Mesh when drawing. This can return the GeometryInstance3D.material_override, the surface override Material defined in this MeshInstance3D, or the surface Material defined in the mesh. For example, if GeometryInstance3D.material_override is used, all surfaces will return the override material.
m.MeshInstance3D.get_blend_shape_count: Returns the number of blend shapes available. Produces an error if mesh is null.
m.MeshInstance3D.get_blend_shape_value: Returns the value of the blend shape at the given blend_shape_idx. Returns 0.0 and produces an error if mesh is null or doesn't have a blend shape at that index.
m.MeshInstance3D.get_skin_reference: Returns the internal SkinReference containing the skeleton's RID attached to this RID. See also Resource.get_rid(), SkinReference.get_skeleton(), and RenderingServer.instance_attach_skeleton().
m.MeshInstance3D.get_surface_override_mate: Returns the override Material for the specified surface of the Mesh resource. See also get_surface_override_material_count().
Returns the number of surface override materials. This is equivalent to Mesh.get_surface_count(). See also get_surface_override_material().
m.MeshInstance3D.mesh: The Mesh resource for the instance.
m.MeshInstance3D.set_blend_shape_value: Sets the value of the blend shape at blend_shape_idx to value. Produces an error if mesh is null or doesn't have a blend shape at that index.
m.MeshInstance3D.set_surface_override_mate: Sets the override material for the specified surface of the Mesh resource. This material is associated with this MeshInstance3D rather than with mesh.
m.MeshInstance3D.skeleton: NodePath to the Skeleton3D associated with the instance.
m.MeshInstance3D.skin: The Skin to be used by this instance.
m.MeshLibrary.create_item: Creates a new item in the library with the given ID.
m.MeshLibrary.find_item_by_name: Returns the first item with the given name, or -1 if no item is found.
m.MeshLibrary.get_item_count: Returns the number of items present in the library.
m.MeshLibrary.get_item_list: Returns the list of item IDs in use.
m.MeshLibrary.get_item_mesh_cast_shadow: Returns the item's shadow casting mode.
m.MeshLibrary.get_item_mesh_transform: Returns the transform applied to the item's mesh.
m.MeshLibrary.get_item_navigation_layers: Returns the item's navigation layers bitmask.
m.MeshLibrary.get_item_navigation_mesh_tra: Returns the transform applied to the item's navigation mesh.
m.MeshLibrary.get_item_preview: When running in the editor, returns a generated item preview (a 3D rendering in isometric perspective). When used in a running project, returns the manually-defined item preview which can be set using set_item_preview(). Returns an empty Texture2D if no preview was manually set in a running project.
m.MeshLibrary.get_last_unused_item_id: Gets an unused ID for a new item.
m.MeshLibrary.set_item_mesh_cast_shadow: Sets the item's shadow casting mode to shadow_casting_setting.
m.MeshLibrary.set_item_mesh_transform: Sets the transform to apply to the item's mesh.
m.MeshLibrary.set_item_navigation_layers: Sets the item's navigation layers bitmask.
m.MeshLibrary.set_item_navigation_mesh_tra: Sets the transform to apply to the item's navigation mesh.
m.MeshLibrary.set_item_preview: Sets a texture to use as the item's preview icon in the editor.
m.MeshTexture.base_texture: Sets the base texture that the Mesh will use to draw.
m.MeshTexture.image_size: Sets the size of the image, needed for reference.
m.MeshTexture.mesh: Sets the mesh used to draw. It must be a mesh using 2D vertices.
m.MethodTweener.set_delay: Sets the time in seconds after which the MethodTweener will start interpolating. By default there's no delay.
m.MethodTweener.set_ease: Sets the type of used easing from EaseType. If not set, the default easing is used from the Tween that contains this Tweener.
m.MethodTweener.set_trans: Sets the type of used transition from TransitionType. If not set, the default transition is used from the Tween that contains this Tweener.
m.MissingNode.original_class: The name of the class this node was supposed to be (see Object.get_class()).
m.MissingNode.original_scene: Returns the path of the scene this node was instance of originally.
m.MissingNode.recording_properties: If true, allows new properties to be set along with existing ones. If false, only existing properties' values can be set, and new properties cannot be added.
m.MissingNode.recording_signals: If true, allows new signals to be connected to along with existing ones. If false, only existing signals can be connected to, and new signals cannot be added.
m.MissingResource.original_class: The name of the class this resource was supposed to be (see Object.get_class()).
m.MissingResource.recording_properties: If set to true, allows new properties to be added on top of the existing ones with Object.set().
m.MobileVRInterface.display_to_lens: The distance between the display and the lenses inside of the device in centimeters.
m.MobileVRInterface.display_width: The width of the display in centimeters.
m.MobileVRInterface.eye_height: The height at which the camera is placed in relation to the ground (i.e. XROrigin3D node).
m.MobileVRInterface.iod: The interocular distance, also known as the interpupillary distance. The distance between the pupils of the left and right eye.
m.MobileVRInterface.k1: The k1 lens factor is one of the two constants that define the strength of the lens used and directly influences the lens distortion effect.
m.MobileVRInterface.k2: The k2 lens factor, see k1.
m.MobileVRInterface.offset_rect: Set the offset rect relative to the area being rendered. A length of 1 represents the whole rendering area on that axis.
m.MobileVRInterface.oversample: The oversample setting. Because of the lens distortion we have to render our buffers at a higher resolution then the screen can natively handle. A value between 1.5 and 2.0 often provides good results but at the cost of performance.
m.MobileVRInterface.vrs_min_radius: The minimum radius around the focal point where full quality is guaranteed if VRS is used as a percentage of screen size.
m.MobileVRInterface.vrs_strength: The strength used to calculate the VRS density map. The greater this value, the more noticeable VRS is. This improves performance at the cost of quality.
m.ModifierBoneTarget3D.bone: The index of the attached bone.
m.ModifierBoneTarget3D.bone_name: The name of the attached bone.
m.MovieWriter._get_audio_mix_rate: Called when the audio sample rate used for recording the audio is requested by the engine. The value returned must be specified in Hz. Defaults to 48000 Hz if _get_audio_mix_rate() is not overridden.
m.MovieWriter._get_audio_speaker_mode: Called when the audio speaker mode used for recording the audio is requested by the engine. This can affect the number of output channels in the resulting audio file/stream. Defaults to AudioServer.SPEAKER_MODE_STEREO if _get_audio_speaker_mode() is not overridden.
m.MovieWriter._get_supported_extensions: Returns the list of supported filename extensions for movies written with this MovieWriter.
m.MovieWriter._handles_file: Called when the engine determines whether this MovieWriter is able to handle the file at path. Must return true if this MovieWriter is able to handle the given file path, false otherwise. Typically, _handles_file() is overridden as follows to allow the user to record a file at any path with a given file extension:
m.MovieWriter._write_begin: Called once before the engine starts writing video and audio data. movie_size is the width and height of the video to save. fps is the number of frames per second specified in the project settings or using the --fixed-fps  command line argument.
m.MovieWriter._write_end: Called when the engine finishes writing. This occurs when the engine quits by pressing the window manager's close button, or when SceneTree.quit() is called.
m.MovieWriter._write_frame: Called at the end of every rendered frame. The frame_image and audio_frame_block function arguments should be written to.
m.MovieWriter.add_writer: Adds a writer to be usable by the engine. The supported file extensions can be set by overriding _handles_file().
m.MultiMesh.INTERP_QUALITY_FAST: Always interpolate using Basis lerping, which can produce warping artifacts in some situations.
m.MultiMesh.INTERP_QUALITY_HIGH: Attempt to interpolate using Basis slerping (spherical linear interpolation) where possible, otherwise fall back to lerping.
m.MultiMesh.buffer: There is currently no description for this property. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.MultiMesh.color_array: Deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use set_instance_color() and get_instance_color() instead.
m.MultiMesh.custom_aabb: Custom AABB for this MultiMesh resource. Setting this manually prevents costly runtime AABB recalculations.
m.MultiMesh.custom_data_array: Deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use set_instance_custom_data() and get_instance_custom_data() instead.
m.MultiMesh.get_aabb: Returns the visibility axis-aligned bounding box in local space.
m.MultiMesh.get_instance_color: Gets a specific instance's color multiplier.
m.MultiMesh.get_instance_custom_data: Returns the custom data that has been set for a specific instance.
m.MultiMesh.get_instance_transform: Returns the Transform3D of a specific instance.
m.MultiMesh.get_instance_transform_2d: Returns the Transform2D of a specific instance.
m.MultiMesh.instance_count: Number of instances that will get drawn. This clears and (re)sizes the buffers. Setting data format or flags afterwards will have no effect.
m.MultiMesh.physics_interpolation_quality: Choose whether to use an interpolation method that favors speed or quality.
m.MultiMesh.reset_instance_physics_interpo: When using physics interpolation, this function allows you to prevent interpolation on an instance in the current physics tick.
m.MultiMesh.reset_instances_physics_interp: When using physics interpolation, this function allows you to prevent interpolation for all instances in the current physics tick.
m.MultiMesh.set_buffer_interpolated: An alternative to setting the buffer property, which can be used with physics interpolation. This method takes two arrays, and can set the data for the current and previous tick in one go. The renderer will automatically interpolate the data at each frame.
m.MultiMesh.set_instance_color: Sets the color of a specific instance by multiplying the mesh's existing vertex colors. This allows for different color tinting per instance.
m.MultiMesh.set_instance_custom_data: Sets custom data for a specific instance. custom_data is a Color type only to contain 4 floating-point numbers.
m.MultiMesh.set_instance_transform: Sets the Transform3D for a specific instance.
m.MultiMesh.set_instance_transform_2d: Sets the Transform2D for a specific instance.
m.MultiMesh.transform_2d_array: Deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use set_instance_transform_2d() and get_instance_transform_2d() instead.
m.MultiMesh.transform_array: Deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use set_instance_transform() and get_instance_transform() instead.
m.MultiMesh.transform_format: Format of transform used to transform mesh, either 2D or 3D.
m.MultiMesh.use_colors: If true, the MultiMesh will use color data (see set_instance_color()). Can only be set when instance_count is 0 or less. This means that you need to call this method before setting the instance count, or temporarily reset it to 0.
m.MultiMesh.use_custom_data: If true, the MultiMesh will use custom data (see set_instance_custom_data()). Can only be set when instance_count is 0 or less. This means that you need to call this method before setting the instance count, or temporarily reset it to 0.
m.MultiMesh.visible_instance_count: Limits the number of instances drawn, -1 draws all instances. Changing this does not change the sizes of the buffers.
m.MultiMeshInstance2D.multimesh: The MultiMesh that will be drawn by the MultiMeshInstance2D.
m.MultiMeshInstance2D.texture: The Texture2D that will be used if using the default CanvasItemMaterial. Can be accessed as TEXTURE in CanvasItem shader.
m.MultiMeshInstance2D.texture_changed: Emitted when the texture is changed.
m.MultiMeshInstance3D.multimesh: The MultiMesh resource that will be used and shared among all instances of the MultiMeshInstance3D.
m.MultiplayerAPI.RPC_MODE_ANY_PEER: Used with Node.rpc_config() to set a method to be callable remotely by any peer. Analogous to the @rpc("any_peer") annotation. Calls are accepted from all remote peers, no matter if they are node's authority or not.
m.MultiplayerAPI.RPC_MODE_AUTHORITY: Used with Node.rpc_config() to set a method to be callable remotely only by the current multiplayer authority (which is the server by default). Analogous to the @rpc("authority") annotation. See Node.set_multiplayer_authority().
m.MultiplayerAPI.RPC_MODE_DISABLED: Used with Node.rpc_config() to disable a method or property for all RPC calls, making it unavailable. Default for all methods.
m.MultiplayerAPI.connected_to_server: Emitted when this MultiplayerAPI's multiplayer_peer successfully connected to a server. Only emitted on clients.
m.MultiplayerAPI.connection_failed: Emitted when this MultiplayerAPI's multiplayer_peer fails to establish a connection to a server. Only emitted on clients.
m.MultiplayerAPI.create_default_interface: Returns a new instance of the default MultiplayerAPI.
m.MultiplayerAPI.get_default_interface: Returns the default MultiplayerAPI implementation class name. This is usually "SceneMultiplayer" when SceneMultiplayer is available. See set_default_interface().
m.MultiplayerAPI.get_peers: Returns the peer IDs of all connected peers of this MultiplayerAPI's multiplayer_peer.
m.MultiplayerAPI.get_remote_sender_id: Returns the sender's peer ID for the RPC currently being executed.
m.MultiplayerAPI.get_unique_id: Returns the unique peer ID of this MultiplayerAPI's multiplayer_peer.
m.MultiplayerAPI.has_multiplayer_peer: Returns true if there is a multiplayer_peer set.
m.MultiplayerAPI.is_server: Returns true if this MultiplayerAPI's multiplayer_peer is valid and in server mode (listening for connections).
m.MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer: The peer object to handle the RPC system (effectively enabling networking when set). Depending on the peer itself, the MultiplayerAPI will become a network server (check with is_server()) and will set root node's network mode to authority, or it will become a regular client peer. All child nodes are set to inherit the network mode by default. Handling of networking-related events (connection, dis…
m.MultiplayerAPI.object_configuration_add: Notifies the MultiplayerAPI of a new configuration for the given object. This method is used internally by SceneTree to configure the root path for this MultiplayerAPI (passing null and a valid NodePath as configuration). This method can be further used by MultiplayerAPI implementations to provide additional features, refer to specific implementation (e.g. SceneMultiplayer) for details on how the…
m.MultiplayerAPI.object_configuration_remo: Notifies the MultiplayerAPI to remove a configuration for the given object. This method is used internally by SceneTree to configure the root path for this MultiplayerAPI (passing null and an empty NodePath as configuration). This method can be further used by MultiplayerAPI implementations to provide additional features, refer to specific implementation (e.g. SceneMultiplayer) for details on how…
m.MultiplayerAPI.peer_connected: Emitted when this MultiplayerAPI's multiplayer_peer connects with a new peer. ID is the peer ID of the new peer. Clients get notified when other clients connect to the same server. Upon connecting to a server, a client also receives this signal for the server (with ID being 1).
m.MultiplayerAPI.peer_disconnected: Emitted when this MultiplayerAPI's multiplayer_peer disconnects from a peer. Clients get notified when other clients disconnect from the same server.
