m.Node3D.set_notify_local_transform: If true, the node will receive NOTIFICATION_LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED whenever transform changes.
m.Node3D.set_notify_transform: If true, the node will receive NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED whenever global_transform changes.
m.Node3D.set_subgizmo_selection: Selects the gizmo's subgizmo with the given id and sets its transform. Only works in the editor.
m.Node3D.show: Allows this node to be rendered. Equivalent to setting visible to true. This is the opposite of hide().
m.Node3D.to_global: Returns the local_point converted from this node's local space to global space. This is the opposite of to_local().
m.Node3D.to_local: Returns the global_point converted from global space to this node's local space. This is the opposite of to_global().
m.Node3D.top_level: If true, the node does not inherit its transformations from its parent. As such, node transformations will only be in global space, which also means that global_transform and transform will be identical.
m.Node3D.transform: The local transformation of this node, in parent space (relative to the parent node). Contains and represents this node's position, rotation, and scale.
m.Node3D.translate: Adds the given translation offset to the node's position, in local space (relative to this node).
m.Node3D.translate_object_local: Adds the given translation offset to the node's position, in local space (relative to this node).
m.Node3D.update_gizmos: Updates all the EditorNode3DGizmo objects attached to this node. Only works in the editor.
m.Node3D.visibility_changed: Emitted when this node's visibility changes (see visible and is_visible_in_tree()).
m.Node3D.visibility_parent: Path to the visibility range parent for this node and its descendants. The visibility parent must be a GeometryInstance3D.
m.Node3D.visible: If true, this node can be visible. The node is only rendered when all of its ancestors are visible, as well. That means is_visible_in_tree() must return true.
m.NodePath.get_as_property_path: Returns a copy of this node path with a colon character (:) prefixed, transforming it to a pure property path with no node names (relative to the current node).
m.NodePath.get_concatenated_names: Returns all node names concatenated with a slash character (/) as a single StringName.
m.NodePath.get_concatenated_subnames: Returns all property subnames concatenated with a colon character (:) as a single StringName.
m.NodePath.get_name: Returns the node name indicated by idx, starting from 0. If idx is out of bounds, an error is generated. See also get_subname_count() and get_name_count().
m.NodePath.get_name_count: Returns the number of node names in the path. Property subnames are not included.
m.NodePath.get_subname: Returns the property name indicated by idx, starting from 0. If idx is out of bounds, an error is generated. See also get_subname_count().
m.NodePath.get_subname_count: Returns the number of property names ("subnames") in the path. Each subname in the node path is listed after a colon character (:).
m.NodePath.hash: Returns the 32-bit hash value representing the node path's contents.
m.NodePath.is_absolute: Returns true if the node path is absolute. Unlike a relative path, an absolute path is represented by a leading slash character (/) and always begins from the SceneTree. It can be used to reliably access nodes from the root node (e.g. "/root/Global" if an autoload named "Global" exists).
m.NodePath.is_empty: Returns true if the node path has been constructed from an empty String ("").
m.NodePath.slice: Returns the slice of the NodePath, from begin (inclusive) to end (exclusive), as a new NodePath.
m.Noise.get_image: Returns an Image containing 2D noise values.
m.Noise.get_image_3d: Returns an Array of Images containing 3D noise values for use with ImageTexture3D.create().
m.Noise.get_noise_1d: Returns the 1D noise value at the given (x) coordinate.
m.Noise.get_noise_2d: Returns the 2D noise value at the given position.
m.Noise.get_noise_2dv: Returns the 2D noise value at the given position.
m.Noise.get_noise_3d: Returns the 3D noise value at the given position.
m.Noise.get_noise_3dv: Returns the 3D noise value at the given position.
m.Noise.get_seamless_image: Returns an Image containing seamless 2D noise values.
m.Noise.get_seamless_image_3d: Returns an Array of Images containing seamless 3D noise values for use with ImageTexture3D.create().
m.NoiseTexture2D.as_normal_map: If true, the resulting texture contains a normal map created from the original noise interpreted as a bump map.
m.NoiseTexture2D.bump_strength: Strength of the bump maps used in this texture. A higher value will make the bump maps appear larger while a lower value will make them appear softer.
m.NoiseTexture2D.color_ramp: A Gradient which is used to map the luminance of each pixel to a color value.
m.NoiseTexture2D.generate_mipmaps: Determines whether mipmaps are generated for this texture. Enabling this results in less texture aliasing in the distance, at the cost of increasing memory usage by roughly 33% and making the noise texture generation take longer.
m.NoiseTexture2D.height: Height of the generated texture (in pixels).
m.NoiseTexture2D.in_3d_space: Determines whether the noise image is calculated in 3D space. May result in reduced contrast.
m.NoiseTexture2D.invert: If true, inverts the noise texture. White becomes black, black becomes white.
m.NoiseTexture2D.noise: The instance of the Noise object.
m.NoiseTexture2D.normalize: If true, the noise image coming from the noise generator is normalized to the range 0.0 to 1.0.
m.NoiseTexture2D.seamless: If true, a seamless texture is requested from the Noise resource.
m.NoiseTexture2D.seamless_blend_skirt: Used for the default/fallback implementation of the seamless texture generation. It determines the distance over which the seams are blended. High values may result in less details and contrast. See Noise for further details.
m.NoiseTexture2D.width: Width of the generated texture (in pixels).
m.NoiseTexture3D.color_ramp: A Gradient which is used to map the luminance of each pixel to a color value.
m.NoiseTexture3D.depth: Depth of the generated texture (in pixels).
m.NoiseTexture3D.height: Height of the generated texture (in pixels).
m.NoiseTexture3D.invert: If true, inverts the noise texture. White becomes black, black becomes white.
m.NoiseTexture3D.noise: The instance of the Noise object.
m.NoiseTexture3D.normalize: If true, the noise image coming from the noise generator is normalized to the range 0.0 to 1.0.
m.NoiseTexture3D.seamless: If true, a seamless texture is requested from the Noise resource.
m.NoiseTexture3D.seamless_blend_skirt: Used for the default/fallback implementation of the seamless texture generation. It determines the distance over which the seams are blended. High values may result in less details and contrast. See Noise for further details.
m.NoiseTexture3D.width: Width of the generated texture (in pixels).
m.OS.RENDERING_DRIVER_D3D12: The Direct3D 12 rendering driver. It requires the 12_0 feature level and Shader Model 6.0 support.
m.OS.RENDERING_DRIVER_OPENGL3: The OpenGL 3 rendering driver. It uses OpenGL 3.3 Core Profile on desktop platforms, OpenGL ES 3.0 on mobile devices, and WebGL 2.0 on Web.
m.OS.RENDERING_DRIVER_VULKAN: The Vulkan rendering driver. It requires Vulkan 1.0 support and automatically uses features from Vulkan 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3 if available.
m.OS.STD_HANDLE_CONSOLE: Standard I/O device is a console. This typically occurs when Godot is run from a terminal with no redirection. This is also used for all standard I/O devices when running Godot from the editor, at least on desktop platforms.
m.OS.STD_HANDLE_FILE: Standard I/O device is a regular file. This typically occurs with redirection from a terminal, e.g. godot > stdout.txt, godot < stdin.txt or godot > stdout_stderr.txt 2>&1.
m.OS.STD_HANDLE_INVALID: Standard I/O device is invalid. No data can be received from or sent to these standard I/O devices.
m.OS.STD_HANDLE_PIPE: Standard I/O device is a FIFO/pipe. This typically occurs with pipe usage from a terminal, e.g. echo "Hello" | godot.
m.OS.STD_HANDLE_UNKNOWN: Standard I/O device type is unknown.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_DCIM: Refers to the DCIM (Digital Camera Images) directory path.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_DESKTOP: Refers to the Desktop directory path.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_DOCUMENTS: Refers to the Documents directory path.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_DOWNLOADS: Refers to the Downloads directory path.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_MOVIES: Refers to the Movies (or Videos) directory path.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_MUSIC: Refers to the Music directory path.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_PICTURES: Refers to the Pictures directory path.
m.OS.SYSTEM_DIR_RINGTONES: Refers to the Ringtones directory path.
m.OS.add_logger: Add a custom logger to intercept the internal message stream.
m.OS.alert: Displays a modal dialog box using the host platform's implementation. The engine execution is blocked until the dialog is closed.
m.OS.close_midi_inputs: Shuts down the system MIDI driver. Godot will no longer receive InputEventMIDI. See also open_midi_inputs() and get_connected_midi_inputs().
m.OS.crash: Crashes the engine (or the editor if called within a @tool script). See also kill().
m.OS.create_instance: Creates a new instance of Godot that runs independently. The arguments are used in the given order and separated by a space.
m.OS.create_process: Creates a new process that runs independently of Godot. It will not terminate when Godot terminates. The path specified in path must exist and be an executable file or macOS .app bundle. The path is resolved based on the current platform. The arguments are used in the given order and separated by a space.
m.OS.delay_msec: Delays execution of the current thread by msec milliseconds. msec must be greater than or equal to 0. Otherwise, delay_msec() does nothing and prints an error message.
m.OS.delay_usec: Delays execution of the current thread by usec microseconds. usec must be greater than or equal to 0. Otherwise, delay_usec() does nothing and prints an error message.
m.OS.delta_smoothing: If true, the engine filters the time delta measured between each frame, and attempts to compensate for random variation. This only works on systems where V-Sync is active.
m.OS.execute: Executes the given process in a blocking way. The file specified in path must exist and be executable. The system path resolution will be used. The arguments are used in the given order, separated by spaces, and wrapped in quotes.
m.OS.execute_with_pipe: Creates a new process that runs independently of Godot with redirected IO. It will not terminate when Godot terminates. The path specified in path must exist and be an executable file or macOS .app bundle. The path is resolved based on the current platform. The arguments are used in the given order and separated by a space.
m.OS.find_keycode_from_string: Finds the keycode for the given string. The returned values are equivalent to the Key constants.
m.OS.get_cache_dir: Returns the global cache data directory according to the operating system's standards.
m.OS.get_cmdline_args: Returns the command-line arguments passed to the engine, excluding arguments processed by the engine, such as --headless and --fullscreen.
m.OS.get_cmdline_user_args: Returns the command-line user arguments passed to the engine. User arguments are ignored by the engine and reserved for the user. They are passed after the double dash -- argument. ++ may be used when -- is intercepted by another program (such as startx).
m.OS.get_config_dir: Returns the global user configuration directory according to the operating system's standards.
m.OS.get_connected_midi_inputs: Returns an array of connected MIDI device names, if they exist. Returns an empty array if the system MIDI driver has not previously been initialized with open_midi_inputs(). See also close_midi_inputs().
m.OS.get_data_dir: Returns the global user data directory according to the operating system's standards.
m.OS.get_distribution_name: Returns the name of the distribution for Linux and BSD platforms (e.g. "Ubuntu", "Manjaro", "OpenBSD", etc.).
m.OS.get_entropy: Generates a PackedByteArray of cryptographically secure random bytes with given size.
m.OS.get_environment: Returns the value of the given environment variable, or an empty string if variable doesn't exist.
m.OS.get_executable_path: Returns the file path to the current engine executable.
m.OS.get_granted_permissions: On Android devices: Returns the list of dangerous permissions that have been granted.
m.OS.get_keycode_string: Returns the given keycode as a String.
m.OS.get_locale: Returns the host OS locale as a String of the form language_Script_COUNTRY_VARIANT@extra. Every substring after language is optional and may not exist.
m.OS.get_locale_language: Returns the host OS locale's 2 or 3-letter language code [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes] as a string which should be consistent on all platforms. This is equivalent to extracting the language part of the get_locale() string.
m.OS.get_main_thread_id: Returns the ID of the main thread. See get_thread_caller_id().
m.OS.get_memory_info: Returns a Dictionary containing information about the current memory with the following entries:
m.OS.get_model_name: Returns the model name of the current device.
m.OS.get_name: Returns the name of the host platform.
m.OS.get_process_exit_code: Returns the exit code of a spawned process once it has finished running (see is_process_running()).
m.OS.get_process_id: Returns the number used by the host machine to uniquely identify this application.
m.OS.get_processor_count: Returns the number of logical CPU cores available on the host machine. On CPUs with HyperThreading enabled, this number will be greater than the number of physical CPU cores.
m.OS.get_processor_name: Returns the full name of the CPU model on the host machine (e.g. "Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700K CPU @ 4.00GHz").
m.OS.get_restart_on_exit_arguments: Returns the list of command line arguments that will be used when the project automatically restarts using set_restart_on_exit(). See also is_restart_on_exit_set().
m.OS.get_static_memory_peak_usage: Returns the maximum amount of static memory used. Only works in debug builds.
m.OS.get_static_memory_usage: Returns the amount of static memory being used by the program in bytes. Only works in debug builds.
m.OS.get_stderr_type: Returns the type of the standard error device.
m.OS.get_stdin_type: Returns the type of the standard input device.
m.OS.get_stdout_type: Returns the type of the standard output device.
m.OS.get_system_ca_certificates: Returns the list of certification authorities trusted by the operating system as a string of concatenated certificates in PEM format.
m.OS.get_system_dir: Returns the path to commonly used folders across different platforms, as defined by dir. See the SystemDir constants for available locations.
m.OS.get_system_font_path: Returns the path to the system font file with font_name and style. Returns an empty string if no matching fonts found.
m.OS.get_system_font_path_for_text: Returns an array of the system substitute font file paths, which are similar to the font with font_name and style for the specified text, locale, and script. Returns an empty array if no matching fonts found.
m.OS.get_system_fonts: Returns the list of font family names available.
m.OS.get_temp_dir: Returns the global temporary data directory according to the operating system's standards.
m.OS.get_thread_caller_id: Returns the ID of the current thread. This can be used in logs to ease debugging of multi-threaded applications.
m.OS.get_unique_id: Returns a string that is unique to the device.
m.OS.get_user_data_dir: Returns the absolute directory path where user data is written (the user:// directory in Godot). The path depends on the project name and ProjectSettings.application/config/use_custom_user_dir.
m.OS.get_version: Returns the exact production and build version of the operating system. This is different from the branded version used in marketing. This helps to distinguish between different releases of operating systems, including minor versions, and insider and custom builds.
m.OS.get_version_alias: Returns the branded version used in marketing, followed by the build number (on Windows), the version number (on macOS), or the SDK version and incremental build number (on Android). Examples include 11 (build 22000), Sequoia (15.0.0), and 15 (SDK 35 build abc528-11988f).
m.OS.get_video_adapter_driver_info: Returns the video adapter driver name and version for the user's currently active graphics card, as a PackedStringArray. See also RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_api_version().
m.OS.has_environment: Returns true if the environment variable with the name variable exists.
m.OS.has_feature: Returns true if the feature for the given feature tag is supported in the currently running instance, depending on the platform, build, etc. Can be used to check whether you're currently running a debug build, on a certain platform or arch, etc. Refer to the Feature Tags documentation for more details.
m.OS.is_debug_build: Returns true if the Godot binary used to run the project is a debug export template, or when running in the editor.
m.OS.is_keycode_unicode: Returns true if the input keycode corresponds to a Unicode character. For a list of codes, see the Key constants.
m.OS.is_process_running: Returns true if the child process ID (pid) is still running or false if it has terminated. pid must be a valid ID generated from create_process().
m.OS.is_restart_on_exit_set: Returns true if the project will automatically restart when it exits for any reason, false otherwise. See also set_restart_on_exit() and get_restart_on_exit_arguments().
m.OS.is_sandboxed: Returns true if the application is running in the sandbox.
m.OS.is_stdout_verbose: Returns true if the engine was executed with the --verbose or -v command line argument, or if ProjectSettings.debug/settings/stdout/verbose_stdout is true. See also @GlobalScope.print_verbose().
m.OS.is_userfs_persistent: Returns true if the user:// file system is persistent, that is, its state is the same after a player quits and starts the game again. Relevant to the Web platform, where this persistence may be unavailable.
m.OS.kill: Kill (terminate) the process identified by the given process ID (pid), such as the ID returned by execute() in non-blocking mode. See also crash().
m.OS.low_processor_usage_mode: If true, the engine optimizes for low processor usage by only refreshing the screen if needed. Can improve battery consumption on mobile.
m.OS.low_processor_usage_mode_sleep_usec: The amount of sleeping between frames when the low-processor usage mode is enabled, in microseconds. Higher values will result in lower CPU usage. See also low_processor_usage_mode.
m.OS.move_to_trash: Moves the file or directory at the given path to the system's recycle bin. See also DirAccess.remove().
m.OS.open_midi_inputs: Initializes the singleton for the system MIDI driver, allowing Godot to receive InputEventMIDI. See also get_connected_midi_inputs() and close_midi_inputs().
m.OS.open_with_program: Opens one or more files/directories with the specified application. The program_path specifies the path to the application to use for opening the files, and paths contains an array of file/directory paths to open.
m.OS.read_buffer_from_stdin: Reads a user input as raw data from the standard input. This operation can be blocking, which causes the window to freeze if read_buffer_from_stdin() is called on the main thread.
m.OS.read_string_from_stdin: Reads a user input as a UTF-8 encoded string from the standard input. This operation can be blocking, which causes the window to freeze if read_string_from_stdin() is called on the main thread.
m.OS.remove_logger: Remove a custom logger added by add_logger().
m.OS.request_permission: Requests permission from the OS for the given name. Returns true if the permission has already been granted. See also MainLoop.on_request_permissions_result.
m.OS.request_permissions: Requests dangerous permissions from the OS. Returns true if permissions have already been granted. See also MainLoop.on_request_permissions_result.
m.OS.revoke_granted_permissions: On macOS (sandboxed applications only), this function clears list of user selected folders accessible to the application.
m.OS.set_environment: Sets the value of the environment variable variable to value. The environment variable will be set for the Godot process and any process executed with execute() after running set_environment(). The environment variable will not persist to processes run after the Godot process was terminated.
m.OS.set_restart_on_exit: If restart is true, restarts the project automatically when it is exited with SceneTree.quit() or Node.NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST. Command-line arguments can be supplied. To restart the project with the same command line arguments as originally used to run the project, pass get_cmdline_args() as the value for arguments.
m.OS.set_thread_name: Assigns the given name to the current thread. Returns @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE if unavailable on the current platform.
m.OS.set_use_file_access_save_and_swap: If enabled is true, when opening a file for writing, a temporary file is used in its place. When closed, it is automatically applied to the target file.
m.OS.shell_open: Requests the OS to open a resource identified by uri with the most appropriate program. For example:
m.OS.shell_show_in_file_manager: Requests the OS to open the file manager, navigate to the given file_or_dir_path and select the target file or folder.
m.OS.unset_environment: Removes the given environment variable from the current environment, if it exists. The variable name cannot be empty or include the = character. The environment variable will be removed for the Godot process and any process executed with execute() after running unset_environment(). The removal of the environment variable will not persist to processes run after the Godot process was terminated.
m.Object.NOTIFICATION_POSTINITIALIZE: Notification received when the object is initialized, before its script is attached. Used internally.
m.Object._get: Override this method to customize the behavior of get(). Should return the given property's value, or null if the property should be handled normally.
m.Object._get_property_list: Override this method to provide a custom list of additional properties to handle by the engine.
m.Object._init: Called when the object's script is instantiated, oftentimes after the object is initialized in memory (through Object.new() in GDScript, or new GodotObject in C#). It can be also defined to take in parameters. This method is similar to a constructor in most programming languages.
m.Object._iter_get: Returns the current iterable value. iter stores the iteration state, but unlike _iter_init() and _iter_next() the state is supposed to be read-only, so there is no Array wrapper.
m.Object._iter_init: Initializes the iterator. iter stores the iteration state. Since GDScript does not support passing arguments by reference, a single-element array is used as a wrapper. Returns true so long as the iterator has not reached the end.
m.Object._iter_next: Moves the iterator to the next iteration. iter stores the iteration state. Since GDScript does not support passing arguments by reference, a single-element array is used as a wrapper. Returns true so long as the iterator has not reached the end.
m.Object._notification: Called when the object receives a notification, which can be identified in what by comparing it with a constant. See also notification().
m.Object._property_can_revert: Override this method to customize the given property's revert behavior. Should return true if the property has a custom default value and is revertible in the Inspector dock. Use _property_get_revert() to specify the property's default value.
m.Object._property_get_revert: Override this method to customize the given property's revert behavior. Should return the default value for the property. If the default value differs from the property's current value, a revert icon is displayed in the Inspector dock.
m.Object._set: Override this method to customize the behavior of set(). Should set the property to value and return true, or false if the property should be handled normally. The exact way to set the property is up to this method's implementation.
m.Object._to_string: Override this method to customize the return value of to_string(), and therefore the object's representation as a String.
m.Object._validate_property: Override this method to customize existing properties. Every property info goes through this method, except properties added with _get_property_list(). The dictionary contents is the same as in _get_property_list().
m.Object.add_user_signal: Adds a user-defined signal named signal. Optional arguments for the signal can be added as an Array of dictionaries, each defining a name String and a type int (see Variant.Type). See also has_user_signal() and remove_user_signal().
m.Object.call: Calls the method on the object and returns the result. This method supports a variable number of arguments, so parameters can be passed as a comma separated list.
m.Object.call_deferred: Calls the method on the object during idle time. Always returns null, not the method's result.
m.Object.callv: Calls the method on the object and returns the result. Unlike call(), this method expects all parameters to be contained inside arg_array.
m.Object.can_translate_messages: Returns true if the object is allowed to translate messages with tr() and tr_n(). See also set_message_translation().
m.Object.cancel_free: If this method is called during NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE, this object will reject being freed and will remain allocated. This is mostly an internal function used for error handling to avoid the user from freeing objects when they are not intended to.
m.Object.connect: Connects a signal by name to a callable. Optional flags can be also added to configure the connection's behavior (see ConnectFlags constants).
m.Object.disconnect: Disconnects a signal by name from a given callable. If the connection does not exist, generates an error. Use is_connected() to make sure that the connection exists.
m.Object.emit_signal: Emits the given signal by name. The signal must exist, so it should be a built-in signal of this class or one of its inherited classes, or a user-defined signal (see add_user_signal()). This method supports a variable number of arguments, so parameters can be passed as a comma separated list.
m.Object.free: 立即销毁对象。危险，推荐 queue_free()。
m.Object.get_class: Returns the object's built-in class name, as a String. See also is_class().
m.Object.get_incoming_connections: Returns an Array of signal connections received by this object. Each connection is represented as a Dictionary that contains three entries:
m.Object.get_indexed: Gets the object's property indexed by the given property_path. The path should be a NodePath relative to the current object and can use the colon character (:) to access nested properties.
m.Object.get_instance_id: Returns the object's unique instance ID. This ID can be saved in EncodedObjectAsID, and can be used to retrieve this object instance with @GlobalScope.instance_from_id().
m.Object.get_meta: Returns the object's metadata value for the given entry name. If the entry does not exist, returns default. If default is null, an error is also generated.
m.Object.get_meta_list: Returns the object's metadata entry names as an Array of StringNames.
m.Object.get_method_argument_count: Returns the number of arguments of the given method by name.
m.Object.get_method_list: Returns this object's methods and their signatures as an Array of dictionaries. Each Dictionary contains the following entries:
m.Object.get_property_list: Returns the object's property list as an Array of dictionaries. Each Dictionary contains the following entries:
m.Object.get_script: Returns the object's Script instance, or null if no script is attached.
m.Object.get_signal_connection_list: Returns an Array of connections for the given signal name. Each connection is represented as a Dictionary that contains three entries:
m.Object.get_signal_list: Returns the list of existing signals as an Array of dictionaries.
m.Object.get_translation_domain: Returns the name of the translation domain used by tr() and tr_n(). See also TranslationServer.
m.Object.has_connections: Returns true if any connection exists on the given signal name.
m.Object.has_meta: Returns true if a metadata entry is found with the given name. See also get_meta(), set_meta() and remove_meta().
m.Object.has_method: Returns true if the given method name exists in the object.
m.Object.has_signal: Returns true if the given signal name exists in the object.
m.Object.has_user_signal: Returns true if the given user-defined signal name exists. Only signals added with add_user_signal() are included. See also remove_user_signal().
m.Object.is_blocking_signals: Returns true if the object is blocking its signals from being emitted. See set_block_signals().
m.Object.is_class: Returns true if the object inherits from the given class. See also get_class().
m.Object.is_connected: Returns true if a connection exists between the given signal name and callable.
m.Object.is_queued_for_deletion: Returns true if the methods Node.queue_free() or SceneTree.queue_delete() was called for the object.
m.Object.notification: Sends the given what notification to all classes inherited by the object, triggering calls to _notification(), starting from the highest ancestor (the Object class) and going down to the object's script.
m.Object.notify_property_list_changed: Emits the property_list_changed signal. This is mainly used to refresh the editor, so that the Inspector and editor plugins are properly updated.
m.Object.property_can_revert: Returns true if the given property has a custom default value. Use property_get_revert() to get the property's default value.
m.Object.property_get_revert: Returns the custom default value of the given property. Use property_can_revert() to check if the property has a custom default value.
m.Object.remove_meta: Removes the given entry name from the object's metadata. See also has_meta(), get_meta() and set_meta().
m.Object.remove_user_signal: Removes the given user signal signal from the object. See also add_user_signal() and has_user_signal().
m.Object.script_changed: Emitted when the object's script is changed.
m.Object.set_block_signals: If set to true, the object becomes unable to emit signals. As such, emit_signal() and signal connections will not work, until it is set to false.
m.Object.set_deferred: Assigns value to the given property, at the end of the current frame. This is equivalent to calling set() through call_deferred().
m.Object.set_indexed: Assigns a new value to the property identified by the property_path. The path should be a NodePath relative to this object, and can use the colon character (:) to access nested properties.
m.Object.set_message_translation: If set to true, allows the object to translate messages with tr() and tr_n(). Enabled by default. See also can_translate_messages().
m.Object.set_meta: Adds or changes the entry name inside the object's metadata. The metadata value can be any Variant, although some types cannot be serialized correctly.
m.Object.set_script: Attaches script to the object, and instantiates it. As a result, the script's _init() is called. A Script is used to extend the object's functionality.
m.Object.set_translation_domain: Sets the name of the translation domain used by tr() and tr_n(). See also TranslationServer.
m.Object.to_string: Returns a String representing the object. Defaults to "". Override _to_string() to customize the string representation of the object.
m.Object.tr: Translates a message, using the translation catalogs configured in the Project Settings. Further context can be specified to help with the translation. Note that most Control nodes automatically translate their strings, so this method is mostly useful for formatted strings or custom drawn text.
m.Object.tr_n: Translates a message or plural_message, using the translation catalogs configured in the Project Settings. Further context can be specified to help with the translation.
m.Occluder3D.get_indices: Returns the occluder shape's vertex indices.
m.Occluder3D.get_vertices: Returns the occluder shape's vertex positions.
m.OccluderInstance3D.bake_mask: The visual layers to account for when baking for occluders. Only MeshInstance3Ds whose VisualInstance3D.layers match with this bake_mask will be included in the generated occluder mesh. By default, all objects with opaque materials are taken into account for the occluder baking.
m.OccluderInstance3D.bake_simplification_d: The simplification distance to use for simplifying the generated occluder polygon (in 3D units). Higher values result in a less detailed occluder mesh, which improves performance but reduces culling accuracy.
m.OccluderInstance3D.get_bake_mask_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the bake_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.OccluderInstance3D.occluder: The occluder resource for this OccluderInstance3D. You can generate an occluder resource by selecting an OccluderInstance3D node then using the Bake Occluders button at the top of the editor.
m.OccluderInstance3D.set_bake_mask_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the bake_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.OccluderPolygon2D.CULL_CLOCKWISE: Culling is performed in the clockwise direction. See cull_mode.
m.OccluderPolygon2D.CULL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE: Culling is performed in the counterclockwise direction. See cull_mode.
m.OccluderPolygon2D.closed: If true, closes the polygon. A closed OccluderPolygon2D occludes the light coming from any direction. An opened OccluderPolygon2D occludes the light only at its outline's direction.
m.OccluderPolygon2D.polygon: A Vector2 array with the index for polygon's vertices positions.
m.OggPacketSequence.get_length: The length of this stream, in seconds.
m.OggPacketSequence.granule_positions: Contains the granule positions for each page in this packet sequence.
m.OggPacketSequence.packet_data: Contains the raw packets that make up this OggPacketSequence.
m.OggPacketSequence.sampling_rate: Holds sample rate information about this sequence. Must be set by another class that actually understands the codec.
m.OmniLight3D.SHADOW_CUBE: Shadows are rendered to a cubemap. Slower than SHADOW_DUAL_PARABOLOID, but higher-quality.
m.OmniLight3D.SHADOW_DUAL_PARABOLOID: Shadows are rendered to a dual-paraboloid texture. Faster than SHADOW_CUBE, but lower-quality.
m.OmniLight3D.omni_attenuation: Controls the distance attenuation function for omnilights.
m.OmniLight3D.omni_range: The light's radius. Note that the effectively lit area may appear to be smaller depending on the omni_attenuation in use. No matter the omni_attenuation in use, the light will never reach anything outside this radius.
m.OmniLight3D.omni_shadow_mode: There is currently no description for this property. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.OPENXR_ALPHA_BLEND_MO: Means that XRInterface.XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_ALPHA_BLEND isn't supported at all.
Means that XRInterface.XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_ALPHA_BLEND is really supported.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.action_get_handle: Returns the corresponding XrAction OpenXR handle for the given action RID.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.begin_debug_label_reg: Begins a new debug label region, this label will be reported in debug messages for any calls following this until end_debug_label_region() is called. Debug labels can be stacked.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.can_render: Returns true if OpenXR is initialized for rendering with an XR viewport.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.end_debug_label_regio: Marks the end of a debug label region. Removes the latest debug label region added by calling begin_debug_label_region().
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.find_action: Returns the RID corresponding to an Action of a matching name, optionally limited to a specified action set.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_error_string: Returns an error string for the given XrResult [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrResult.html].
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_hand_tracker: Returns the corresponding XRHandTrackerEXT handle for the given hand index value.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_instance: Returns the XrInstance [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrInstance.html] created during the initialization of the OpenXR API.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_instance_proc_add: Returns the function pointer of the OpenXR function with the specified name, cast to an integer. If the function with the given name does not exist, the method returns 0.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_next_frame_time: Returns the predicted display timing for the next frame.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_openxr_version: Returns the version of OpenXR that was initialized. Only valid after the OpenXR instance has been created. See XR_MAKE_VERSION [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#XR_MAKE_VERSION] for how the version is calculated.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_play_space: Returns the play space, which is an XrSpace [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrSpace.html] cast to an integer.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_predicted_display: Returns the predicted display timing for the current frame.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_projection_layer: Returns a pointer to the render state's XrCompositionLayerProjection struct.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_render_state_z_fa: Returns the far boundary value of the camera frustum.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_render_state_z_ne: Returns the near boundary value of the camera frustum.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_session: Returns the OpenXR session, which is an XrSession [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrSession.html] cast to an integer.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_supported_swapcha: Returns an array of supported swapchain formats.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_swapchain_format_: Returns the name of the specified swapchain format.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_system_id: Returns the ID of the system, which is an XrSystemId [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrSystemId.html] cast to an integer.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_view_configuratio: Returns the view configuration type, which is an XrViewConfigurationType [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrViewConfigurationType.html] cast to an integer.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.get_view_count: Returns the number of views. It is usually two, one for each eye, but may differ with different view configurations.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.insert_debug_label: Inserts a debug label, this label is reported in any debug message resulting from the OpenXR calls that follows, until any of begin_debug_label_region(), end_debug_label_region(), or insert_debug_label() is called.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.is_environment_blend_: Returns OpenXRAlphaBlendModeSupport denoting if XRInterface.XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_ALPHA_BLEND is really supported, emulated or not supported at all.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.is_initialized: Returns true if OpenXR is initialized.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.is_running: Returns true if OpenXR is running (xrBeginSession [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/xrBeginSession.html] was successfully called and the swapchains were created).
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.openxr_is_enabled: Returns true if OpenXR is enabled.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.openxr_swapchain_acqu: Acquires the image of the provided swapchain.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.openxr_swapchain_crea: Returns a pointer to a new swapchain created using the provided parameters.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.openxr_swapchain_free: Destroys the provided swapchain and frees it from memory.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.openxr_swapchain_get_: Returns the RID of the provided swapchain's image.
Returns the XrSwapchain handle of the provided swapchain.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.openxr_swapchain_rele: Releases the image of the provided swapchain.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.register_composition_: Registers the given extension as a composition layer provider.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.register_frame_info_e: Registers the given extension as modifying frame info via the OpenXRExtensionWrapper._set_frame_wait_info_and_get_next_pointer(), OpenXRExtensionWrapper._set_view_locate_info_and_get_next_pointer(), or OpenXRExtensionWrapper._set_frame_end_info_and_get_next_pointer() virtual methods.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.register_projection_l: Registers the given extension as modifying XrCompositionLayerProjection via the OpenXRExtensionWrapper._set_projection_layer_and_get_next_pointer() virtual method.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.register_projection_v: Registers the given extension as a provider of additional data structures to projections views.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.set_custom_play_space: Sets the reference space used by OpenXR to the given XrSpace [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrSpace.html] (cast to a void *).
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.set_emulate_environme: If set to true, an OpenXR extension is loaded which is capable of emulating the XRInterface.XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_ALPHA_BLEND blend mode.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.set_object_name: Set the object name of an OpenXR object, used for debug output. object_type must be a valid OpenXR XrObjectType enum and object_handle must be a valid OpenXR object handle.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.set_render_region: Sets the render region to render_region, overriding the normal render target's rect.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.set_velocity_depth_te: Sets the render target of the velocity depth texture.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.set_velocity_target_s: Sets the target size of the velocity and velocity depth textures.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.set_velocity_texture: Sets the render target of the velocity texture.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.transform_from_pose: Creates a Transform3D from an XrPosef [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrPosef.html].
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.unregister_compositio: Unregisters the given extension as a composition layer provider.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.unregister_frame_info: Unregisters the given extension as modifying frame info.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.unregister_projection: Unregisters the given extension as modifying XrCompositionLayerProjection.
Unregisters the given extension as a provider of additional data structures to projections views.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.update_main_swapchain: Request the recommended resolution from the OpenXR runtime and update the main swapchain size if it has changed.
m.OpenXRAPIExtension.xr_result: Returns true if the provided XrResult [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrResult.html] (cast to an integer) is successful. Otherwise returns false and prints the XrResult [https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/man/html/XrResult.html] converted to a string, with the specified additional information.
m.OpenXRAction.OPENXR_ACTION_BOOL: This action provides a boolean value.
m.OpenXRAction.OPENXR_ACTION_FLOAT: This action provides a float value between 0.0 and 1.0 for any analog input such as triggers.
m.OpenXRAction.OPENXR_ACTION_POSE: There is currently no description for this enum. Please help us by contributing one [https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/class_reference.html]!
m.OpenXRAction.OPENXR_ACTION_VECTOR2: This action provides a Vector2 value and can be bound to embedded trackpads and joysticks.
m.OpenXRAction.localized_name: The localized description of this action.
m.OpenXRAction.toplevel_paths: A collections of toplevel paths to which this action can be bound.
m.OpenXRActionMap.action_sets: Collection of OpenXRActionSets that are part of this action map.
m.OpenXRActionMap.create_default_action_se: Setup this action set with our default actions.
m.OpenXRActionMap.find_action_set: Retrieve an action set by name.
m.OpenXRActionMap.find_interaction_profile: Find an interaction profile by its name (path).
m.OpenXRActionMap.get_action_set: Retrieve the action set at this index.
m.OpenXRActionMap.get_action_set_count: Retrieve the number of actions sets in our action map.
m.OpenXRActionMap.get_interaction_profile: Get the interaction profile at this index.
m.OpenXRActionMap.get_interaction_profile_: Retrieve the number of interaction profiles in our action map.
m.OpenXRActionMap.interaction_profiles: Collection of OpenXRInteractionProfiles that are part of this action map.
m.OpenXRActionSet.actions: Collection of actions for this action set.
m.OpenXRActionSet.add_action: Add an action to this action set.
m.OpenXRActionSet.get_action_count: Retrieve the number of actions in our action set.
m.OpenXRActionSet.localized_name: The localized name of this action set.
m.OpenXRActionSet.priority: The priority for this action set.
m.OpenXRActionSet.remove_action: Remove an action from this action set.
m.OpenXRAnalogThresholdModifier.off_haptic: Haptic pulse to emit when the user releases the input.
m.OpenXRAnalogThresholdModifier.off_thresh: When our input value falls below this, our output becomes false.
m.OpenXRAnalogThresholdModifier.on_haptic: Haptic pulse to emit when the user presses the input.
m.OpenXRAnalogThresholdModifier.on_thresho: When our input value is equal or larger than this value, our output becomes true. It stays true until it falls under the off_threshold value.
m.OpenXRAnchorTracker.has_uuid: Returns true if a non-zero UUID is set.
m.OpenXRAnchorTracker.uuid: The UUID provided for persistent anchors.
m.OpenXRAnchorTracker.uuid_changed: Emitted when the UUID for this anchor was changed.
m.OpenXRAndroidThreadSettingsExtension.THR: Hints to the XR runtime that the thread is doing time critical CPU tasks.
Hints to the XR runtime that the thread is doing background CPU tasks.
Hints to the XR runtime that the thread is doing time critical graphics device tasks.
Hints to the XR runtime that the thread is doing background graphics device tasks.
m.OpenXRAndroidThreadSettingsExtension.set: Sets the thread type of the given thread, so that the XR runtime can adjust its scheduling priority accordingly.
m.OpenXRBindingModifier._get_description: Return the description of this class that is used for the title bar of the binding modifier editor.
m.OpenXRBindingModifier._get_ip_modificati: Returns the data that is sent to OpenXR when submitting the suggested interacting bindings this modifier is a part of.
m.OpenXRBindingModifierEditor.binding_modi: Signal emitted when the user presses the delete binding modifier button for this modifier.
m.OpenXRBindingModifierEditor.get_binding_: Returns the OpenXRBindingModifier currently being edited.
m.OpenXRBindingModifierEditor.setup: Setup this editor for the provided action_map and binding_modifier.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.EYE_VISIBILITY_BO: The layer is visible to both the left and right eyes.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.EYE_VISIBILITY_LE: The layer is visible only to the left eye.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.EYE_VISIBILITY_RI: The layer is visible only to the right eye.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.FILTER_CUBIC: Perform cubic filtering when sampling the texture.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.FILTER_LINEAR: Perform linear filtering when sampling the texture.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.FILTER_NEAREST: Perform nearest-neighbor filtering when sampling the texture.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.MIPMAP_MODE_LINEA: Use linear interpolation of the two mipmaps of the nearest resolution.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.MIPMAP_MODE_NEARE: Use the mipmap of the nearest resolution.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.SWIZZLE_ALPHA: Maps a color channel to the value of the alpha channel.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.SWIZZLE_BLUE: Maps a color channel to the value of the blue channel.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.SWIZZLE_GREEN: Maps a color channel to the value of the green channel.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.SWIZZLE_ONE: Maps a color channel to the value of one.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.SWIZZLE_RED: Maps a color channel to the value of the red channel.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.SWIZZLE_ZERO: Maps a color channel to the value of zero.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.WRAP_CLAMP_TO_BOR: Clamp the texture to its specified border color.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.WRAP_CLAMP_TO_EDG: Clamp the texture to its edge color.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.WRAP_MIRRORED_REP: Repeat the texture infinitely, mirroring it on each repeat.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.WRAP_MIRROR_CLAMP: Mirror the texture once and then clamp the texture to its edge color.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.alpha_blend: Enables the blending the layer using its alpha channel.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.android_surface_s: The size of the Android surface to create if use_android_surface is enabled.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.enable_hole_punch: Enables a technique called "hole punching", which allows putting the composition layer behind the main projection layer (i.e. setting sort_order to a negative value) while "punching a hole" through everything rendered by Godot so that the layer is still visible.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.eye_visibility: The eye(s) the composition layer is visible to.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.get_android_surfa: Returns a JavaObject representing an android.view.Surface if use_android_surface is enabled and OpenXR has created the surface. Otherwise, this will return null.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.intersects_ray: Returns UV coordinates where the given ray intersects with the composition layer. origin and direction must be in global space.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.is_natively_suppo: Returns true if the OpenXR runtime natively supports this composition layer type.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.layer_viewport: The SubViewport to render on the composition layer.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.protected_content: If enabled, the OpenXR swapchain will be created with the XR_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_PROTECTED_CONTENT_BIT flag, which will protect its contents from CPU access.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.sort_order: The sort order for this composition layer. Higher numbers will be shown in front of lower numbers.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.swapchain_state_a: The swizzle value for the alpha channel of the swapchain state.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.swapchain_state_b: The swizzle value for the blue channel of the swapchain state.
The border color of the swapchain state that is used when the wrap mode clamps to the border.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.swapchain_state_g: The swizzle value for the green channel of the swapchain state.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.swapchain_state_h: The horizontal wrap mode of the swapchain state.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.swapchain_state_m: The magnification filter of the swapchain state.
The max anisotropy of the swapchain state.
The minification filter of the swapchain state.
The mipmap mode of the swapchain state.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.swapchain_state_r: The swizzle value for the red channel of the swapchain state.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.swapchain_state_v: The vertical wrap mode of the swapchain state.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayer.use_android_surfa: If enabled, an Android surface will be created (with the dimensions from android_surface_size) which will provide the 2D content for the composition layer, rather than using layer_viewport.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayerCylinder.aspect_ra: The aspect ratio of the slice. Used to set the height relative to the width.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayerCylinder.central_a: The central angle of the cylinder. Used to set the width.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayerCylinder.fallback_: The number of segments to use in the fallback mesh.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayerEquirect.central_h: The central horizontal angle of the sphere. Used to set the width.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayerEquirect.fallback_: The number of segments to use in the fallback mesh.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayerEquirect.lower_ver: The lower vertical angle of the sphere. Used (together with upper_vertical_angle) to set the height.
m.OpenXRCompositionLayerEquirect.upper_ver: The upper vertical angle of the sphere. Used (together with lower_vertical_angle) to set the height.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.action_set: Action set for which this dpad binding modifier is active.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.center_region: Center region in which our center position of our dpad return true.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.input_path: Input path for this dpad binding modifier.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.is_sticky: If false, when the joystick enters a new dpad zone this becomes true.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.off_haptic: Haptic pulse to emit when the user releases the input.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.on_haptic: Haptic pulse to emit when the user presses the input.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.threshold: When our input value is equal or larger than this value, our dpad in that direction becomes true. It stays true until it falls under the threshold_released value.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.threshold_rele: When our input value falls below this, our output becomes false.
m.OpenXRDpadBindingModifier.wedge_angle: The angle of each wedge that identifies the 4 directions of the emulated dpad.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._get_composition_: Returns a pointer to an XrCompositionLayerBaseHeader struct to provide the given composition layer.
Returns the number of composition layers this extension wrapper provides via _get_composition_layer().

Returns an integer that will be used to sort the given composition layer provided via _get_composition_layer(). Lower numbers will move the layer to the front of the list, and higher numbers to the end. The default projection layer has an order of 0, so layers provided by this method should probably be above or below (but not exactly) 0.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._get_requested_ex: Returns a Dictionary of OpenXR extensions related to this extension. xr_version specifies the OpenXR version we're instantiating. This will be zero if the editor requests this list to flag supported features. The Dictionary should contain the name of the extension, mapped to a bool * cast to an integer:
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._get_suggested_tr: Returns a PackedStringArray of positional tracker names that are used within the extension wrapper.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._get_viewport_com: Gets an array of Dictionarys that represent properties, just like Object._get_property_list(), that will be added to OpenXRCompositionLayer nodes.
Gets a Dictionary containing the default values for the properties returned by _get_viewport_composition_layer_extension_properties().
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_before_instan: Called before the OpenXR instance is created.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_event_polled: Called when there is an OpenXR event to process. When implementing, return true if the event was handled, return false otherwise.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_instance_crea: Called right after the OpenXR instance is created.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_instance_dest: Called right before the OpenXR instance is destroyed.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_main_swapchai: Called right after the main swapchains are (re)created.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_post_draw_vie: Called right after the given viewport is rendered.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_pre_draw_view: Called right before the given viewport is rendered.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_pre_render: Called right before the XR viewports begin their rendering step.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_process: Called as part of the OpenXR process handling. This happens right before general and physics processing steps of the main loop. During this step controller data is queried and made available to game logic.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_register_meta: Allows extensions to register additional controller metadata. This function is called even when the OpenXR API is not constructed as the metadata needs to be available to the editor.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_session_creat: Called right after the OpenXR session is created.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_session_destr: Called right before the OpenXR session is destroyed.
m.OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_state_exiting: Called when the OpenXR session state is changed to exiting.

m.OpenXRInterface.PERF_SETTINGS_LEVEL_BOOS: The application has entered a section with very high complexity, during which the XR Runtime is allowed to step up beyond the thermally sustainable range.
m.OpenXRInterface.PERF_SETTINGS_LEVEL_POWE: The application has entered a non-XR section (head-locked / static screen), during which power savings are to be prioritized.
m.OpenXRInterface.PERF_SETTINGS_LEVEL_SUST: The application has entered a high or dynamic complexity section, during which the XR Runtime strives for consistent XR compositing and frame rendering within a thermally sustainable range.
The application has entered a low and stable complexity section, during which reducing power is more important than occasional late rendering frames.

The sub-domain has reached an early warning level where the application should start proactive mitigation actions.
m.OpenXRInterface.PERF_SETTINGS_SUB_DOMAIN: The compositing performance within the runtime has reached a new level.

m.OpenXRInterface.SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED: The application has synched its frame loop with the runtime, we're rendering output to the user and we're receiving XR input. session_focussed is emitted when we change to this state.
m.OpenXRInterface.SESSION_STATE_IDLE: The initial state after the OpenXR session is created or after the session is destroyed.
m.OpenXRInterface.SESSION_STATE_LOSS_PENDI: The session is about to be lost. session_loss_pending is emitted when we change to this state.

m.OpenXRInterface.SESSION_STATE_UNKNOWN: The state of the session is unknown, we haven't tried setting up OpenXR yet.
m.OpenXRInterface.SESSION_STATE_VISIBLE: The application has synched its frame loop with the runtime and we're rendering output to the user, however we receive no user input. session_visible is emitted when we change to this state.

m.OpenXRSpatialAnchorCapability.PERSISTENC: Persistence operations and data access is limited to spatial anchors, on the same device, for the same user and same app (using persist_anchor() and unpersist_anchor() functions)

Provides the application with read-only access (i.e. application cannot modify this scope) to spatial entities persisted and managed by the system. The application can use the UUID in the persistence component for this scope to correlate entities across spatial contexts and device reboots.

m.OptionButton.add_icon_item: Adds an item, with a texture icon, text label and (optionally) id. If no id is passed, the item index will be used as the item's ID. New items are appended at the end.
m.OptionButton.add_item: Adds an item, with text label and (optionally) id. If no id is passed, the item index will be used as the item's ID. New items are appended at the end.
m.OptionButton.add_separator: Adds a separator to the list of items. Separators help to group items, and can optionally be given a text header. A separator also gets an index assigned, and is appended at the end of the item list.
m.OptionButton.allow_reselect: If true, the currently selected item can be selected again.
m.OptionButton.clear: Clears all the items in the OptionButton.
m.OptionButton.fit_to_longest_item: If true, minimum size will be determined by the longest item's text, instead of the currently selected one's.
m.OptionButton.get_item_auto_translate_mod: Returns the auto translate mode of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.get_item_icon: Returns the icon of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.get_item_id: Returns the ID of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.get_item_index: Returns the index of the item with the given id.
m.OptionButton.get_item_metadata: Retrieves the metadata of an item. Metadata may be any type and can be used to store extra information about an item, such as an external string ID.
m.OptionButton.get_item_text: Returns the text of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.get_item_tooltip: Returns the tooltip of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.get_popup: Returns the PopupMenu contained in this button.
m.OptionButton.get_selectable_item: Returns the index of the first item which is not disabled, or marked as a separator. If from_last is true, the items will be searched in reverse order.
m.OptionButton.get_selected_id: Returns the ID of the selected item, or -1 if no item is selected.
m.OptionButton.get_selected_metadata: Gets the metadata of the selected item. Metadata for items can be set using set_item_metadata().
m.OptionButton.has_selectable_items: Returns true if this button contains at least one item which is not disabled, or marked as a separator.
m.OptionButton.is_item_disabled: Returns true if the item at index idx is disabled.
m.OptionButton.is_item_separator: Returns true if the item at index idx is marked as a separator.
m.OptionButton.item_count: The number of items to select from.
m.OptionButton.item_focused: Emitted when the user navigates to an item using the ProjectSettings.input/ui_up or ProjectSettings.input/ui_down input actions. The index of the item focused is passed as argument.
m.OptionButton.item_selected: Emitted when the current item has been changed by the user. The index of the item selected is passed as argument.
m.OptionButton.remove_item: Removes the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.search_bar_enabled: If true, shows a search bar at the top of the PopupMenu for filtering items. See search_bar_min_item_count for dynamically controlling its visibility based on the number of items.
m.OptionButton.search_bar_fuzzy_search_ena: If true, enables fuzzy searching in the PopupMenu search bar. This allows the search results to include items that almost match the search query, as well items that match the individual characters of the search query, but not in sequence.
m.OptionButton.search_bar_fuzzy_search_max: Sets the maximum number of mismatches allowed in each search result when fuzzy searching is enabled for the PopupMenu search bar. Any item with more mismatches will be hidden from the search results.
m.OptionButton.search_bar_min_item_count: Sets the minimum number of items required for the PopupMenu search bar to be visible. search_bar_enabled must be true for this to have any effect.
m.OptionButton.select: Selects an item by index and makes it the current item. This will work even if the item is disabled.
m.OptionButton.selected: The index of the currently selected item, or -1 if no item is selected.
m.OptionButton.set_disable_shortcuts: If true, shortcuts are disabled and cannot be used to trigger the button.
m.OptionButton.set_item_auto_translate_mod: Sets the auto translate mode of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.set_item_disabled: Sets whether the item at index idx is disabled.
m.OptionButton.set_item_icon: Sets the icon of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.set_item_id: Sets the ID of the item at index idx.
m.OptionButton.set_item_metadata: Sets the metadata of an item. Metadata may be of any type and can be used to store extra information about an item, such as an external string ID.
m.OptionButton.set_item_text: Sets the text of the item at index idx.
