m.PCKPacker.add_file: Adds the source_path file to the current PCK package at the target_path internal path. The res:// prefix for target_path is optional and stripped internally. File content is immediately written to the PCK.
m.PCKPacker.add_file_from_buffer: Adds the data to the current PCK package at the target_path internal path. The res:// prefix for target_path is optional and stripped internally. File content is immediately written to the PCK.
m.PCKPacker.add_file_removal: Registers a file removal of the target_path internal path to the PCK. This is mainly used for patches. If the file at this path has been loaded from a previous PCK, it will be removed. The res:// prefix for target_path is optional and stripped internally.
m.PCKPacker.flush: Writes the file directory and closes the PCK. If verbose is true, a list of files added will be printed to the console for easier debugging.
m.PCKPacker.pck_start: Creates a new PCK file at the file path pck_path. The .pck file extension isn't added automatically, so it should be part of pck_path (even though it's not required).
m.PackedByteArray.append: Appends an element at the end of the array (alias of push_back()).
m.PackedByteArray.append_array: Appends a PackedByteArray at the end of this array.
m.PackedByteArray.bsearch: Finds the index of an existing value (or the insertion index that maintains sorting order, if the value is not yet present in the array) using binary search. Optionally, a before specifier can be passed. If false, the returned index comes after all existing entries of the value in the array.
m.PackedByteArray.bswap16: Swaps the byte order of count 16-bit segments of the array starting at offset. Swap is done in-place. If count is less than zero, all segments to the end of array are processed, if processed data size is not a multiple of 2, the byte after the last processed 16-bit segment is not modified.
m.PackedByteArray.bswap32: Swaps the byte order of count 32-bit segments of the array starting at offset. Swap is done in-place. If count is less than zero, all segments to the end of array are processed, if processed data size is not a multiple of 4, bytes after the last processed 32-bit segment are not modified.
m.PackedByteArray.bswap64: Swaps the byte order of count 64-bit segments of the array starting at offset. Swap is done in-place. If count is less than zero, all segments to the end of array are processed, if processed data size is not a multiple of 8, bytes after the last processed 64-bit segment are not modified.
m.PackedByteArray.clear: Clears the array. This is equivalent to using resize() with a size of 0.
m.PackedByteArray.compress: Returns a new PackedByteArray with the data compressed. Set the compression mode using one of CompressionMode's constants.
m.PackedByteArray.count: Returns the number of times an element is in the array.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_double: Decodes a 64-bit floating-point number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0.0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_float: Decodes a 32-bit floating-point number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0.0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_half: Decodes a 16-bit floating-point number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0.0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_s16: Decodes a 16-bit signed integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_s32: Decodes a 32-bit signed integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_s64: Decodes a 64-bit signed integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_s8: Decodes a 8-bit signed integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_u16: Decodes a 16-bit unsigned integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_u32: Decodes a 32-bit unsigned integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_u64: Decodes a 64-bit unsigned integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_u8: Decodes a 8-bit unsigned integer number from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Fails if the byte count is insufficient. Returns 0 if a valid number can't be decoded.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_var: Decodes a Variant from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Returns null if a valid variant can't be decoded or the value is Object-derived and allow_objects is false.
m.PackedByteArray.decode_var_size: Decodes a size of a Variant from the bytes starting at byte_offset. Requires at least 4 bytes of data starting at the offset, otherwise fails.
m.PackedByteArray.decompress: Returns a new PackedByteArray with the data decompressed. Set buffer_size to the size of the uncompressed data. Set the compression mode using one of CompressionMode's constants.
m.PackedByteArray.decompress_dynamic: Returns a new PackedByteArray with the data decompressed. Set the compression mode using one of CompressionMode's constants. This method only accepts brotli, gzip, and deflate compression modes.
m.PackedByteArray.duplicate: Creates a copy of the array, and returns it.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_double: Encodes a 64-bit floating-point number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 8 bytes of allocated space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_float: Encodes a 32-bit floating-point number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 4 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_half: Encodes a 16-bit floating-point number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 2 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_s16: Encodes a 16-bit signed integer number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 2 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_s32: Encodes a 32-bit signed integer number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 4 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_s64: Encodes a 64-bit signed integer number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 8 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_s8: Encodes a 8-bit signed integer number (signed byte) at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 1 byte of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_u16: Encodes a 16-bit unsigned integer number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 2 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_u32: Encodes a 32-bit unsigned integer number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 4 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_u64: Encodes a 64-bit unsigned integer number as bytes at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 8 bytes of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_u8: Encodes a 8-bit unsigned integer number (byte) at the index of byte_offset bytes. The array must have at least 1 byte of space, starting at the offset.
m.PackedByteArray.encode_var: Encodes a Variant at the index of byte_offset bytes. A sufficient space must be allocated, depending on the encoded variant's size. If allow_objects is false, Object-derived values are not permitted and will instead be serialized as ID-only.
m.PackedByteArray.erase: Removes the first occurrence of a value from the array and returns true. If the value does not exist in the array, nothing happens and false is returned. To remove an element by index, use remove_at() instead.
m.PackedByteArray.fill: Assigns the given value to all elements in the array. This can typically be used together with resize() to create an array with a given size and initialized elements.
m.PackedByteArray.find: Searches the array for a value and returns its index or -1 if not found. Optionally, the initial search index can be passed.
m.PackedByteArray.get: Returns the byte at the given index in the array. If index is out-of-bounds or negative, this method fails and returns 0.
m.PackedByteArray.get_string_from_ascii: Converts ASCII/Latin-1 encoded array to String. Fast alternative to get_string_from_utf8() if the content is ASCII/Latin-1 only. Unlike the UTF-8 function this function maps every byte to a character in the array. Multibyte sequences will not be interpreted correctly. For parsing user input always use get_string_from_utf8(). This is the inverse of String.to_ascii_buffer().
m.PackedByteArray.get_string_from_multibyt: Converts system multibyte code page encoded array to String. If conversion fails, empty string is returned. This is the inverse of String.to_multibyte_char_buffer().
m.PackedByteArray.get_string_from_utf16: Converts UTF-16 encoded array to String. If the BOM is missing, little-endianness is assumed. Returns empty string if source array is not valid UTF-16 string. This is the inverse of String.to_utf16_buffer().
m.PackedByteArray.get_string_from_utf32: Converts UTF-32 encoded array to String. Returns empty string if source array is not valid UTF-32 string. This is the inverse of String.to_utf32_buffer().
m.PackedByteArray.get_string_from_utf8: Converts UTF-8 encoded array to String. Slower than get_string_from_ascii() but supports UTF-8 encoded data. Use this function if you are unsure about the source of the data. For user input this function should always be preferred. Returns empty string if source array is not valid UTF-8 string. This is the inverse of String.to_utf8_buffer().
m.PackedByteArray.get_string_from_wchar: Converts wide character (wchar_t, UTF-16 on Windows, UTF-32 on other platforms) encoded array to String. Returns empty string if source array is not valid wide string. This is the inverse of String.to_wchar_buffer().
m.PackedByteArray.has: Returns true if the array contains value.
m.PackedByteArray.has_encoded_var: Returns true if a valid Variant value can be decoded at the byte_offset. Returns false otherwise or when the value is Object-derived and allow_objects is false.
m.PackedByteArray.hex_encode: Returns a hexadecimal representation of this array as a String.
m.PackedByteArray.insert: Inserts a new element at a given position in the array. The position must be valid, or at the end of the array (idx == size()).
m.PackedByteArray.is_empty: Returns true if the array is empty.
m.PackedByteArray.push_back: Appends an element at the end of the array.
m.PackedByteArray.remove_at: Removes an element from the array by index.
m.PackedByteArray.resize: Sets the size of the array. If the array is grown, reserves elements at the end of the array. If the array is shrunk, truncates the array to the new size. Calling resize() once and assigning the new values is faster than adding new elements one by one.
m.PackedByteArray.reverse: Reverses the order of the elements in the array.
m.PackedByteArray.rfind: Searches the array in reverse order. Optionally, a start search index can be passed. If negative, the start index is considered relative to the end of the array.
m.PackedByteArray.set: Changes the byte at the given index.
m.PackedByteArray.size: Returns the number of elements in the array.
m.PackedByteArray.slice: Returns the slice of the PackedByteArray, from begin (inclusive) to end (exclusive), as a new PackedByteArray.
m.PackedByteArray.sort: Sorts the elements of the array in ascending order.
m.PackedByteArray.to_color_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedColorArray, where each block of 16 bytes has been converted to a Color variant.
m.PackedByteArray.to_float32_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedFloat32Array, where each block of 4 bytes has been converted to a 32-bit float (C++ float).
m.PackedByteArray.to_float64_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedFloat64Array, where each block of 8 bytes has been converted to a 64-bit float (C++ double, Godot float).
m.PackedByteArray.to_int32_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedInt32Array, where each block of 4 bytes has been converted to a signed 32-bit integer (C++ int32_t).
m.PackedByteArray.to_int64_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedInt64Array, where each block of 8 bytes has been converted to a signed 64-bit integer (C++ int64_t, Godot int).
m.PackedByteArray.to_vector2_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedVector2Array, where each block of 8 bytes or 16 bytes (32-bit or 64-bit) has been converted to a Vector2 variant.
m.PackedByteArray.to_vector3_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedVector3Array, where each block of 12 or 24 bytes (32-bit or 64-bit) has been converted to a Vector3 variant.
m.PackedByteArray.to_vector4_array: Returns a copy of the data converted to a PackedVector4Array, where each block of 16 or 32 bytes (32-bit or 64-bit) has been converted to a Vector4 variant.
m.PackedColorArray.append: Appends an element at the end of the array (alias of push_back()).
m.PackedColorArray.append_array: Appends a PackedColorArray at the end of this array.
m.PackedColorArray.bsearch: Finds the index of an existing value (or the insertion index that maintains sorting order, if the value is not yet present in the array) using binary search. Optionally, a before specifier can be passed. If false, the returned index comes after all existing entries of the value in the array.
m.PackedColorArray.clear: Clears the array. This is equivalent to using resize() with a size of 0.
m.PackedColorArray.count: Returns the number of times an element is in the array.
m.PackedColorArray.duplicate: Creates a copy of the array, and returns it.
m.PackedColorArray.erase: Removes the first occurrence of a value from the array and returns true. If the value does not exist in the array, nothing happens and false is returned. To remove an element by index, use remove_at() instead.
m.PackedColorArray.fill: Assigns the given value to all elements in the array. This can typically be used together with resize() to create an array with a given size and initialized elements.
m.PackedColorArray.find: Searches the array for a value and returns its index or -1 if not found. Optionally, the initial search index can be passed.
m.PackedColorArray.get: Returns the Color at the given index in the array. If index is out-of-bounds or negative, this method fails and returns Color(0, 0, 0, 1).
m.PackedColorArray.has: Returns true if the array contains value.
m.PackedColorArray.insert: Inserts a new element at a given position in the array. The position must be valid, or at the end of the array (idx == size()).
m.PackedColorArray.is_empty: Returns true if the array is empty.
m.PackedColorArray.push_back: Appends a value to the array.
m.PackedColorArray.remove_at: Removes an element from the array by index.
m.PackedColorArray.resize: Sets the size of the array. If the array is grown, reserves elements at the end of the array. If the array is shrunk, truncates the array to the new size. Calling resize() once and assigning the new values is faster than adding new elements one by one.
m.PackedColorArray.reverse: Reverses the order of the elements in the array.
m.PackedColorArray.rfind: Searches the array in reverse order. Optionally, a start search index can be passed. If negative, the start index is considered relative to the end of the array.
m.PackedColorArray.set: Changes the Color at the given index.
m.PackedColorArray.size: Returns the number of elements in the array.
m.PackedColorArray.slice: Returns the slice of the PackedColorArray, from begin (inclusive) to end (exclusive), as a new PackedColorArray.
m.PackedColorArray.sort: Sorts the elements of the array in ascending order.
m.PackedColorArray.to_byte_array: Returns a PackedByteArray with each color encoded as bytes.

m.PacketPeer.encode_buffer_max_size: Maximum buffer size allowed when encoding Variants. Raise this value to support heavier memory allocations.
m.PacketPeer.get_available_packet_count: Returns the number of packets currently available in the ring-buffer.
m.PacketPeer.get_packet_error: Returns the error state of the last packet received (via get_packet() and get_var()).
m.PacketPeer.get_var: Gets a Variant. If allow_objects is true, decoding objects is allowed.
m.PacketPeer.put_var: Sends a Variant as a packet. If full_objects is true, encoding objects is allowed (and can potentially include code).
m.PacketPeerDTLS.STATUS_CONNECTED: A status representing a PacketPeerDTLS that is connected to a remote peer.
m.PacketPeerDTLS.STATUS_DISCONNECTED: A status representing a PacketPeerDTLS that is disconnected.
m.PacketPeerDTLS.STATUS_ERROR: A status representing a PacketPeerDTLS in a generic error state.
m.PacketPeerDTLS.STATUS_ERROR_HOSTNAME_MIS: An error status that shows a mismatch in the DTLS certificate domain presented by the host and the domain requested for validation.
m.PacketPeerDTLS.STATUS_HANDSHAKING: A status representing a PacketPeerDTLS that is currently performing the handshake with a remote peer.
m.PacketPeerDTLS.connect_to_peer: Connects a packet_peer beginning the DTLS handshake using the underlying PacketPeerUDP which must be connected (see PacketPeerUDP.connect_to_host()). You can optionally specify the client_options to be used while verifying the TLS connections. See TLSOptions.client() and TLSOptions.client_unsafe().
m.PacketPeerDTLS.disconnect_from_peer: Disconnects this peer, terminating the DTLS session.

m.PacketPeerDTLS.poll: Poll the connection to check for incoming packets. Call this frequently to update the status and keep the connection working.

m.PacketPeerUDP.bind: Binds this PacketPeerUDP to the specified port and bind_address with a buffer size recv_buf_size, allowing it to receive incoming packets.
m.PacketPeerUDP.close: Closes the PacketPeerUDP's underlying UDP socket.
m.PacketPeerUDP.connect_to_host: Calling this method connects this UDP peer to the given host/port pair. UDP is in reality connectionless, so this option only means that incoming packets from different addresses are automatically discarded, and that outgoing packets are always sent to the connected address (future calls to set_dest_address() are not allowed). This method does not send any data to the remote peer, to do that, use…
m.PacketPeerUDP.get_local_port: Returns the local port to which this peer is bound.
m.PacketPeerUDP.get_packet_ip: Returns the IP of the remote peer that sent the last packet(that was received with PacketPeer.get_packet() or PacketPeer.get_var()).
m.PacketPeerUDP.get_packet_port: Returns the port of the remote peer that sent the last packet(that was received with PacketPeer.get_packet() or PacketPeer.get_var()).
m.PacketPeerUDP.is_bound: Returns whether this PacketPeerUDP is bound to an address and can receive packets.
m.PacketPeerUDP.is_socket_connected: Returns true if the UDP socket is open and has been connected to a remote address. See connect_to_host().
m.PacketPeerUDP.join_multicast_group: Joins the multicast group specified by multicast_address using the interface identified by interface_name.
m.PacketPeerUDP.leave_multicast_group: Removes the interface identified by interface_name from the multicast group specified by multicast_address.
m.PacketPeerUDP.set_broadcast_enabled: Enable or disable sending of broadcast packets (e.g. set_dest_address("255.255.255.255", 4343). This option is disabled by default.
m.PacketPeerUDP.set_dest_address: Sets the destination address and port for sending packets and variables. A hostname will be resolved using DNS if needed.
m.PacketPeerUDP.wait: Waits for a packet to arrive on the bound address. See bind().
m.PanoramaSkyMaterial.energy_multiplier: The sky's overall brightness multiplier. Higher values result in a brighter sky.
m.PanoramaSkyMaterial.filter: A boolean value to determine if the background texture should be filtered or not.

m.Parallax2D.autoscroll: Velocity at which the offset scrolls automatically, in pixels per second.
m.Parallax2D.follow_viewport: If true, this Parallax2D is offset by the current camera's position. If the Parallax2D is in a CanvasLayer separate from the current camera, it may be desired to match the value with CanvasLayer.follow_viewport_enabled.
m.Parallax2D.ignore_camera_scroll: If true, Parallax2D's position is not affected by the position of the camera.
m.Parallax2D.limit_begin: Top-left limits for scrolling to begin. If the camera is outside of this limit, the Parallax2D stops scrolling. Must be lower than limit_end minus the viewport size to work.
m.Parallax2D.limit_end: Bottom-right limits for scrolling to end. If the camera is outside of this limit, the Parallax2D will stop scrolling. Must be higher than limit_begin and the viewport size combined to work.
m.Parallax2D.repeat_size: Repeats the Texture2D of each of this node's children and offsets them by this value. When scrolling, the node's position loops, giving the illusion of an infinite scrolling background if the values are larger than the screen size. If an axis is set to 0, the Texture2D will not be repeated.
m.Parallax2D.repeat_times: Overrides the amount of times the texture repeats. Each texture copy spreads evenly from the original by repeat_size. Useful for when zooming out with a camera.
m.Parallax2D.screen_offset: Offset used to scroll this Parallax2D. This value is updated automatically unless ignore_camera_scroll is true.
m.Parallax2D.scroll_offset: The Parallax2D's offset. Similar to screen_offset and Node2D.position, but will not be overridden.
m.Parallax2D.scroll_scale: Multiplier to the final Parallax2D's offset. Can be used to simulate distance from the camera.
m.ParallaxBackground.scroll_base_offset: The base position offset for all ParallaxLayer children.
m.ParallaxBackground.scroll_base_scale: The base motion scale for all ParallaxLayer children.
m.ParallaxBackground.scroll_ignore_camera_: If true, elements in ParallaxLayer child aren't affected by the zoom level of the camera.
m.ParallaxBackground.scroll_limit_begin: Top-left limits for scrolling to begin. If the camera is outside of this limit, the background will stop scrolling. Must be lower than scroll_limit_end to work.
m.ParallaxBackground.scroll_limit_end: Bottom-right limits for scrolling to end. If the camera is outside of this limit, the background will stop scrolling. Must be higher than scroll_limit_begin to work.
m.ParallaxBackground.scroll_offset: The ParallaxBackground's scroll value. Calculated automatically when using a Camera2D, but can be used to manually manage scrolling when no camera is present.
m.ParallaxLayer.motion_mirroring: The interval, in pixels, at which the ParallaxLayer is drawn repeatedly. Useful for creating an infinitely scrolling background. If an axis is set to 0, the ParallaxLayer will be drawn only once along that direction.
m.ParallaxLayer.motion_offset: The ParallaxLayer's offset relative to the parent ParallaxBackground's ParallaxBackground.scroll_offset.
m.ParallaxLayer.motion_scale: Multiplies the ParallaxLayer's motion. If an axis is set to 0, it will not scroll.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.color_initial_ra: Each particle's initial color will vary along this GradientTexture1D (multiplied with color).
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.color_ramp: Each particle's color will vary along this GradientTexture1D over its lifetime (multiplied with color).

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.damping_max: The maximum rate at which particles lose velocity. For example value of 100 means that the particle will go from 100 velocity to 0 in 1 second.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.direction: Unit vector specifying the particles' emission direction.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.directional_velo: A curve that specifies the velocity along each of the axes of the particle system along its lifetime.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_curve: Each particle's color will be multiplied by this CurveTexture over its lifetime.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_point_t: Particles will be emitted at positions determined by sampling this texture at a random position. m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_ring_he: The height of the ring when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_ring_in: The inner radius of the ring when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_ring_ra: The radius of the ring when using the emitter EMISSION_SHAPE_RING.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_shape: Particles will be emitted inside this region.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_shape_c: Emitted when this material's emission shape is changed in any way. This includes changes to emission_shape, emission_shape_scale, or emission_sphere_radius, and any other property that affects the emission shape's offset, size, scale, or orientation.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_shape_o: The offset for the emission_shape, in local space.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_shape_s: The scale of the emission_shape, in local space.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.emission_sphere_: The sphere's radius if emission_shape is set to EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.flatness: Amount of spread along the Y axis.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.get_param_max: Returns the maximum value range for the given parameter.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.get_param_min: Returns the minimum value range for the given parameter.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.get_param_textur: Returns the Texture2D used by the specified parameter.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.get_particle_fla: Returns true if the specified particle flag is enabled.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.hue_variation_cu: Each particle's hue will vary along this CurveTexture.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.hue_variation_ma: Maximum initial hue variation applied to each particle. It will shift the particle color's hue.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.inherit_velocity: Percentage of the velocity of the respective GPUParticles2D or GPUParticles3D inherited by each particle when spawning.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.initial_velocity: Maximum initial velocity magnitude for each particle. Direction comes from direction and spread.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.lifetime_randomn: Particle lifetime randomness ratio. The equation for the lifetime of a particle is lifetime * (1.0 - randf() * lifetime_randomness). For example, a lifetime_randomness of 0.4 scales the lifetime between 0.6 to 1.0 of its original value.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.linear_accel_cur: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this CurveTexture.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.linear_accel_max: Maximum linear acceleration applied to each particle in the direction of motion.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.orbit_velocity_c: Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this CurveTexture.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.orbit_velocity_m: Maximum orbital velocity applied to each particle. Makes the particles circle around origin. Specified in number of full rotations around origin per second.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.particle_flag_al: Align Y axis of particle with the direction of its velocity.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.particle_flag_da: Changes the behavior of the damping properties from a linear deceleration to a deceleration based on speed percentage.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.particle_flag_di: If true, particles will not move on the z axis.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.particle_flag_in: If true, particles will inherit the scale of the emitter.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.particle_flag_ro: If true, particles rotate around Y axis by angle_min.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.radial_accel_cur: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this CurveTexture.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.radial_accel_max: Maximum radial acceleration applied to each particle. Makes particle accelerate away from the origin or towards it if negative.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.radial_velocity_: A CurveTexture that defines the velocity over the particle's lifetime away (or toward) the velocity_pivot.

Minimum radial velocity applied to each particle. Makes particles move away from the velocity_pivot, or toward it if negative.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.rotation_3d_max: The maximum 3D orientation, in degrees. Works only in 3D and if use_rotation_3d is enabled.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.rotation_3d_min: The minimum 3D orientation, in degrees. Works only in 3D and if use_rotation_3d is enabled.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.rotation_velocit: Rotation velocity curve over lifetime, per-axis. Enable use_rotation_velocity_3d to use this.
Maximum 3D rotation velocity on the particle's local axis. Enable use_rotation_velocity_3d to use this.
Minimum 3D rotation velocity on the particle's local axis. Enable use_rotation_velocity_3d to use this.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.scale_3d_max: The maximum value of the random scale vector for each particle.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.scale_3d_min: The minimum value of the random scale vector for each particle.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.scale_curve: Each particle's scale will vary along this CurveTexture over its lifetime. If a CurveXYZTexture is supplied instead, the scale will be separated per-axis.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.scale_max: Maximum initial scale applied to each particle.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.scale_over_veloc: Either a CurveTexture or a CurveXYZTexture that scales each particle based on its velocity.
Maximum velocity value reference for scale_over_velocity_curve.
Minimum velocity value reference for scale_over_velocity_curve.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.set_param_min: Sets the minimum value range for the given parameter.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.set_param_textur: Sets the Texture2D for the specified Parameter.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.spread: Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees.

The amount of particles to spawn from the subemitter node when the particle spawns.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.tangential_accel: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this CurveTexture.
Maximum tangential acceleration applied to each particle. Tangential acceleration is perpendicular to the particle's velocity giving the particles a swirling motion.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.turbulence_influ: Maximum turbulence influence on each particle.
Minimum turbulence influence on each particle.
Each particle's amount of turbulence will be influenced along this CurveTexture over its life time.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.turbulence_initi: Maximum displacement of each particle's spawn position by the turbulence.
Minimum displacement of each particle's spawn position by the turbulence.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.turbulence_noise: This value controls the overall scale/frequency of the turbulence noise pattern.

The in-place rate of change of the turbulence field. This defines how quickly the noise pattern varies over time.

m.ParticleProcessMaterial.use_scale_3d: Enable the usage of scale_3d_min and scale_3d_max.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.velocity_limit_c: A CurveTexture that defines the maximum velocity of a particle during its lifetime.
m.ParticleProcessMaterial.velocity_pivot: A pivot point used to calculate radial and orbital velocity of particles.

m.PathFollow2D.cubic_interp: If true, the position between two cached points is interpolated cubically, and linearly otherwise.

m.PathFollow2D.loop: If true, any offset outside the path's length will wrap around, instead of stopping at the ends. Use it for cyclic paths.

m.PathFollow2D.v_offset: The node's offset perpendicular to the curve.
m.PathFollow3D.ROTATION_ORIENTED: Uses the up vector information in a Curve3D to enforce orientation. This rotation mode requires the Path3D's Curve3D.up_vector_enabled property to be set to true.
m.PathFollow3D.ROTATION_XY: Allows the PathFollow3D to rotate in both the X, and Y axes.
m.PathFollow3D.ROTATION_XYZ: Allows the PathFollow3D to rotate in any axis.
m.PathFollow3D.ROTATION_Y: Allows the PathFollow3D to rotate in the Y axis only.
m.PathFollow3D.correct_posture: Correct the transform. rotation_mode implicitly specifies how posture (forward, up and sideway direction) is calculated.
m.PathFollow3D.cubic_interp: If true, the position between two cached points is interpolated cubically, and linearly otherwise.
m.PathFollow3D.h_offset: The node's offset along the curve.
m.PathFollow3D.loop: If true, any offset outside the path's length will wrap around, instead of stopping at the ends. Use it for cyclic paths.

m.PathFollow3D.v_offset: The node's offset perpendicular to the curve.

m.PhysicalBone2D.get_joint: Returns the first Joint2D child node, if one exists. This is mainly a helper function to make it easier to get the Joint2D that the PhysicalBone2D is autoconfiguring.
m.PhysicalBone2D.is_simulating_physics: Returns a boolean that indicates whether the PhysicalBone2D is running and simulating using the Godot 2D physics engine. When true, the PhysicalBone2D node is using physics.
m.PhysicalBone2D.simulate_physics: If true, the PhysicalBone2D will start simulating using physics. If false, the PhysicalBone2D will follow the transform of the Bone2D node.
m.PhysicalBone3D.DAMP_MODE_COMBINE: In this mode, the body's damping value is added to any value set in areas or the default value.
m.PhysicalBone3D.DAMP_MODE_REPLACE: In this mode, the body's damping value replaces any value set in areas or the default value.
m.PhysicalBone3D.JOINT_TYPE_6DOF: A 6 degrees of freedom joint is applied to the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D.JOINT_TYPE_CONE: A cone joint is applied to the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D.JOINT_TYPE_HINGE: A hinge joint is applied to the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D.JOINT_TYPE_NONE: No joint is applied to the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D.JOINT_TYPE_PIN: A pin joint is applied to the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D.JOINT_TYPE_SLIDER: A slider joint is applied to the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D._integrate_forces: Called during physics processing, allowing you to read and safely modify the simulation state for the object. By default, it is called before the standard force integration, but the custom_integrator property allows you to disable the standard force integration and do fully custom force integration for a body.
m.PhysicalBone3D.angular_damp: Damps the body's rotation. By default, the body will use the ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_angular_damp project setting or any value override set by an Area3D the body is in. Depending on angular_damp_mode, you can set angular_damp to be added to or to replace the body's damping value.
m.PhysicalBone3D.angular_velocity: The PhysicalBone3D's rotational velocity in radians per second.
m.PhysicalBone3D.apply_central_impulse: Applies a directional impulse without affecting rotation.
m.PhysicalBone3D.apply_impulse: Applies a positioned impulse to the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D.bounce: The body's bounciness. Values range from 0 (no bounce) to 1 (full bounciness).
m.PhysicalBone3D.can_sleep: If true, the body is deactivated when there is no movement, so it will not take part in the simulation until it is awakened by an external force.
m.PhysicalBone3D.custom_integrator: If true, the standard force integration (like gravity or damping) will be disabled for this body. Other than collision response, the body will only move as determined by the _integrate_forces() method, if that virtual method is overridden.
m.PhysicalBone3D.friction: The body's friction, from 0 (frictionless) to 1 (max friction).
m.PhysicalBone3D.get_bone_id: Returns the unique identifier of the PhysicsBone3D.
m.PhysicalBone3D.get_simulate_physics: Returns true if the PhysicsBone3D is allowed to simulate physics.
m.PhysicalBone3D.gravity_scale: This is multiplied by ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_gravity to produce this body's gravity. For example, a value of 1.0 will apply normal gravity, 2.0 will apply double the gravity, and 0.5 will apply half the gravity to this body.
m.PhysicalBone3D.is_simulating_physics: Returns true if the PhysicsBone3D is currently simulating physics.
m.PhysicalBone3D.joint_rotation: Sets the joint's rotation in radians.
m.PhysicalBone3D.linear_damp: Damps the body's movement. By default, the body will use ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_linear_damp or any value override set by an Area3D the body is in. Depending on linear_damp_mode, linear_damp may be added to or replace the body's damping value.
m.PhysicalBone3D.linear_velocity: The body's linear velocity in units per second. Can be used sporadically, but don't set this every frame, because physics may run in another thread and runs at a different granularity. Use _integrate_forces() as your process loop for precise control of the body state.
m.PhysicalBoneSimulator3D.is_simulating_ph: Returns a boolean that indicates whether the PhysicalBoneSimulator3D is running and simulating.
m.PhysicalBoneSimulator3D.physical_bones_a: Adds a collision exception to the physical bone.
m.PhysicalBoneSimulator3D.physical_bones_r: Removes a collision exception to the physical bone.
m.PhysicalBoneSimulator3D.physical_bones_s: Tells the PhysicalBone3D nodes in the Skeleton to start simulating and reacting to the physics world.
Tells the PhysicalBone3D nodes in the Skeleton to stop simulating.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.energy_multiplier: The sky's overall brightness multiplier. Higher values result in a brighter sky.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.ground_color: Modulates the Color on the bottom half of the sky to represent the ground.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.mie_coefficient: Controls the strength of Mie scattering [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mie_scattering] for the sky. Mie scattering results from light colliding with larger particles (like water). On earth, Mie scattering results in a whitish color around the sun and horizon.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.mie_color: Controls the Color of the Mie scattering [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mie_scattering] effect. While not physically accurate, this allows for the creation of alien-looking planets.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.mie_eccentricity: Controls the direction of the Mie scattering [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mie_scattering]. A value of 1 means that when light hits a particle it's passing through straight forward. A value of -1 means that all light is scatter backwards.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.night_sky: Texture2D for the night sky. This is added to the sky, so if it is bright enough, it may be visible during the day.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.rayleigh_coefficient: Controls the strength of the Rayleigh scattering [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayleigh_scattering]. Rayleigh scattering results from light colliding with small particles. It is responsible for the blue color of the sky.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.rayleigh_color: Controls the Color of the Rayleigh scattering [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayleigh_scattering]. While not physically accurate, this allows for the creation of alien-looking planets. For example, setting this to a red Color results in a Mars-looking atmosphere with a corresponding blue sunset.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.sun_disk_scale: Sets the size of the sun disk. Default value is based on Sol's perceived size from Earth.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.turbidity: Sets the thickness of the atmosphere. High turbidity creates a foggy-looking atmosphere, while a low turbidity results in a clearer atmosphere.
m.PhysicalSkyMaterial.use_debanding: If true, enables debanding. Debanding adds a small amount of noise which helps reduce banding that appears from the smooth changes in color in the sky.
m.PhysicsBody2D.add_collision_exception_wi: Adds a body to the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.
m.PhysicsBody2D.get_collision_exceptions: Returns an array of nodes that were added as collision exceptions for this body.
m.PhysicsBody2D.get_gravity: Returns the gravity vector computed from all sources that can affect the body, including all gravity overrides from Area2D nodes and the global world gravity.
m.PhysicsBody2D.move_and_collide: Moves the body along the vector motion. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process() or Node._process(), motion should be computed using delta.
m.PhysicsBody2D.remove_collision_exception: Removes a body from the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.
m.PhysicsBody2D.test_move: Checks for collisions without moving the body. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process() or Node._process(), motion should be computed using delta.
m.PhysicsBody3D.add_collision_exception_wi: Adds a body to the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.
m.PhysicsBody3D.axis_lock_angular_x: Lock the body's rotation in the X axis.
m.PhysicsBody3D.axis_lock_angular_y: Lock the body's rotation in the Y axis.
m.PhysicsBody3D.axis_lock_angular_z: Lock the body's rotation in the Z axis.
m.PhysicsBody3D.axis_lock_linear_x: Lock the body's linear movement in the X axis.
m.PhysicsBody3D.axis_lock_linear_y: Lock the body's linear movement in the Y axis.
m.PhysicsBody3D.axis_lock_linear_z: Lock the body's linear movement in the Z axis.
m.PhysicsBody3D.get_axis_lock: Returns true if the specified linear or rotational axis is locked.
m.PhysicsBody3D.get_collision_exceptions: Returns an array of nodes that were added as collision exceptions for this body.
m.PhysicsBody3D.get_gravity: Returns the gravity vector computed from all sources that can affect the body, including all gravity overrides from Area3D nodes and the global world gravity.
m.PhysicsBody3D.move_and_collide: Moves the body along the vector motion. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process() or Node._process(), motion should be computed using delta.
m.PhysicsBody3D.remove_collision_exception: Removes a body from the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.
m.PhysicsBody3D.set_axis_lock: Locks or unlocks the specified linear or rotational axis depending on the value of lock.
m.PhysicsBody3D.test_move: Checks for collisions without moving the body. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process() or Node._process(), motion should be computed using delta.

m.PhysicsDirectBodyState2D.add_constant_fo: Adds a constant positioned force to the body that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_force = Vector2(0, 0).
m.PhysicsDirectBodyState2D.add_constant_to: Adds a constant rotational force without affecting position that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_torque = 0.
m.PhysicsDirectBodyState2D.angular_velocit: The body's rotational velocity in radians per second.
