m.PortableCompressedTexture2D.create_from_: Initializes the compressed texture from a base image. The compression mode must be provided.
m.PortableCompressedTexture2D.get_compress: Return the compression mode used (valid after initialized).
m.PortableCompressedTexture2D.is_keeping_a: Returns true if the flag is overridden for all textures of this type.
m.PortableCompressedTexture2D.keep_compres: If true, when running in the editor, this texture will keep the source-compressed data in memory, allowing the data to persist after loading. Otherwise, the source-compressed data is lost after loading and the texture can't be re-saved.
m.PortableCompressedTexture2D.set_basisu_c: Sets the compressor parameters for Basis Universal compression. See also the settings in ResourceImporterTexture.
m.PortableCompressedTexture2D.set_keep_all: If keep is true, overrides the flag globally for all textures of this type. This is used primarily by the editor.
m.PortableCompressedTexture2D.size_overrid: Allows overriding the texture's size (for 2D only).
m.PrimitiveMesh._create_mesh_array: Override this method to customize how this primitive mesh should be generated. Should return an Array where each element is another Array of values required for the mesh (see the ArrayType constants).
m.PrimitiveMesh.add_uv2: If set, generates UV2 UV coordinates applying a padding using the uv2_padding setting. UV2 is needed for lightmapping.
m.PrimitiveMesh.custom_aabb: Overrides the AABB with one defined by user for use with frustum culling. Especially useful to avoid unexpected culling when using a shader to offset vertices.
m.PrimitiveMesh.flip_faces: If true, the order of the vertices in each triangle is reversed, resulting in the backside of the mesh being drawn.
m.PrimitiveMesh.get_mesh_arrays: Returns the mesh arrays used to make up the surface of this primitive mesh.
m.PrimitiveMesh.material: The current Material of the primitive mesh.
m.PrimitiveMesh.request_update: Request an update of this primitive mesh based on its properties.
m.PrimitiveMesh.uv2_padding: If add_uv2 is set, specifies the padding in pixels applied along seams of the mesh. Lower padding values allow making better use of the lightmap texture (resulting in higher texel density), but may introduce visible lightmap bleeding along edges.
m.PrismMesh.left_to_right: Displacement of the upper edge along the X axis. 0.0 positions edge straight above the bottom-left edge.
m.PrismMesh.subdivide_depth: Number of added edge loops along the Z axis.
m.PrismMesh.subdivide_height: Number of added edge loops along the Y axis.
m.PrismMesh.subdivide_width: Number of added edge loops along the X axis.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.energy_multiplier: The sky's overall brightness multiplier. Higher values result in a brighter sky.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.ground_bottom_colo: Color of the ground at the bottom. Blends with ground_horizon_color.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.ground_curve: How quickly the ground_horizon_color fades into the ground_bottom_color.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.ground_energy_mult: Multiplier for ground color. A higher value will make the ground brighter.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.ground_horizon_col: Color of the ground at the horizon. Blends with ground_bottom_color.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sky_cover: The sky cover texture to use. This texture must use an equirectangular projection (similar to PanoramaSkyMaterial). The texture's colors will be added to the existing sky color, and will be multiplied by sky_energy_multiplier and sky_cover_modulate. This is mainly suited to displaying stars at night, but it can also be used to display clouds at day or night (with a non-physically-accurate look).
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sky_cover_modulate: The tint to apply to the sky_cover texture. This can be used to change the sky cover's colors or opacity independently of the sky energy, which is useful for day/night or weather transitions. Only effective if a texture is defined in sky_cover.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sky_curve: How quickly the sky_horizon_color fades into the sky_top_color.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sky_energy_multipl: Multiplier for sky color. A higher value will make the sky brighter.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sky_horizon_color: Color of the sky at the horizon. Blends with sky_top_color.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sky_top_color: Color of the sky at the top. Blends with sky_horizon_color.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sun_angle_max: Distance from center of sun where it fades out completely.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.sun_curve: How quickly the sun fades away between the edge of the sun disk and sun_angle_max.
m.ProceduralSkyMaterial.use_debanding: If true, enables debanding. Debanding adds a small amount of noise which helps reduce banding that appears from the smooth changes in color in the sky.
m.ProgressBar.FILL_BEGIN_TO_END: The progress bar fills from begin to end horizontally, according to the language direction. If Control.is_layout_rtl() returns false, it fills from left to right, and if it returns true, it fills from right to left.
m.ProgressBar.FILL_BOTTOM_TO_TOP: The progress fills from bottom to top.
m.ProgressBar.FILL_END_TO_BEGIN: The progress bar fills from end to begin horizontally, according to the language direction. If Control.is_layout_rtl() returns false, it fills from right to left, and if it returns true, it fills from left to right.
m.ProgressBar.FILL_TOP_TO_BOTTOM: The progress fills from top to bottom.
m.ProgressBar.editor_preview_indeterminate: If false, the indeterminate animation will be paused in the editor.
m.ProgressBar.fill_mode: The fill direction. See FillMode for possible values.
m.ProgressBar.indeterminate: When set to true, the progress bar indicates that something is happening with an animation, but does not show the fill percentage or value.
m.ProgressBar.show_percentage: If true, the fill percentage is displayed on the bar.
m.ProjectSettings.Color: Background color for the boot splash.
m.ProjectSettings.Vector2: Hotspot for the custom mouse cursor image.
m.ProjectSettings.Vector2i: Main window initial position (in virtual desktop coordinates), this setting is used only if display/window/size/initial_position_type is set to "Absolute" (0).
m.ProjectSettings.Vector3: Default up orientation for 3D navigation maps. See NavigationServer3D.map_set_up().
m.ProjectSettings.add_property_info: Adds a custom property info to a property. The dictionary must contain:
m.ProjectSettings.check_changed_settings_i: Checks if any settings with the prefix setting_prefix exist in the set of changed settings. See also get_changed_settings().
m.ProjectSettings.clear: Clears the whole configuration (not recommended, may break things).
m.ProjectSettings.get_changed_settings: Gets an array of the settings which have been changed since the last save. Note that internally changed_settings is cleared after a successful save, so generally the most appropriate place to use this method is when processing settings_changed.
m.ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list: Returns an Array of registered global classes. Each global class is represented as a Dictionary that contains the following entries:
m.ProjectSettings.get_order: Returns the order of a configuration value (influences when saved to the config file).
m.ProjectSettings.get_setting: Returns the value of the setting identified by name. If the setting doesn't exist and default_value is specified, the value of default_value is returned. Otherwise, null is returned.
m.ProjectSettings.get_setting_with_overrid: Similar to get_setting(), but applies feature tag overrides if any exists and is valid.
Similar to get_setting_with_override(), but applies feature tag overrides instead of current OS features.
m.ProjectSettings.globalize_path: Returns the absolute, native OS path corresponding to the localized path (starting with res:// or user://). The returned path will vary depending on the operating system and user preferences. See File paths in Godot projects to see what those paths convert to. See also localize_path().
m.ProjectSettings.has_setting: Returns true if a configuration value is present.
m.ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack: Loads the contents of the .pck or .zip file specified by pack into the resource filesystem (res://). Returns true on success.
m.ProjectSettings.localize_path: Returns the localized path (starting with res://) corresponding to the absolute, native OS path. See also globalize_path().
m.ProjectSettings.save: Saves the configuration to the project.godot file.
m.ProjectSettings.save_custom: Saves the configuration to a custom file. The file extension must be .godot (to save in text-based ConfigFile format) or .binary (to save in binary format). You can also save an override.cfg file, which is also text, but can be used in exported projects unlike other formats.
m.ProjectSettings.set_as_basic: Defines if the specified setting is considered basic or advanced. Basic settings will always be shown in the project settings. Advanced settings will only be shown if the user enables the "Advanced Settings" option.
m.ProjectSettings.set_as_internal: Defines if the specified setting is considered internal. An internal setting won't show up in the Project Settings dialog. This is mostly useful for addons that need to store their own internal settings without exposing them directly to the user.
m.ProjectSettings.set_initial_value: Sets the specified setting's initial value. This is the value the setting reverts to. The setting should already exist before calling this method. Note that project settings equal to their default value are not saved, so your code needs to account for that.
m.ProjectSettings.set_order: Sets the order of a configuration value (influences when saved to the config file).
m.ProjectSettings.set_restart_if_changed: Sets whether a setting requires restarting the editor to properly take effect.
m.ProjectSettings.set_setting: Sets the value of a setting.
m.ProjectSettings.settings_changed: Emitted when any setting is changed, up to once per process frame.
m.Projection.IDENTITY: A Projection with no transformation defined. When applied to other data structures, no transformation is performed.
m.Projection.PLANE_BOTTOM: The index value of the projection bottom clipping plane.
m.Projection.PLANE_FAR: The index value of the projection's far clipping plane.
m.Projection.PLANE_LEFT: The index value of the projection's left clipping plane.
m.Projection.PLANE_NEAR: The index value of the projection's near clipping plane.
m.Projection.PLANE_RIGHT: The index value of the projection's right clipping plane.
m.Projection.PLANE_TOP: The index value of the projection's top clipping plane.
m.Projection.create_depth_correction: Creates a new Projection that projects positions from a depth range of -1 to 1 to one that ranges from 0 to 1, and flips the projected positions vertically, according to flip_y.
m.Projection.create_fit_aabb: Creates a new Projection that scales a given projection to fit around a given AABB in projection space.
m.Projection.create_for_hmd: Creates a new Projection for projecting positions onto a head-mounted display with the given X:Y aspect ratio, distance between eyes, display width, distance to lens, oversampling factor, and depth clipping planes.
m.Projection.create_frustum: Creates a new Projection that projects positions in a frustum with the given clipping planes.
m.Projection.create_frustum_aspect: Creates a new Projection that projects positions in a frustum with the given size, X:Y aspect ratio, offset, and clipping planes.
m.Projection.create_light_atlas_rect: Creates a new Projection that projects positions into the given Rect2.
m.Projection.create_orthogonal: Creates a new Projection that projects positions using an orthogonal projection with the given clipping planes.
m.Projection.create_orthogonal_aspect: Creates a new Projection that projects positions using an orthogonal projection with the given size, X:Y aspect ratio, and clipping planes.
m.Projection.create_perspective: Creates a new Projection that projects positions using a perspective projection with the given Y-axis field of view (in degrees), X:Y aspect ratio, and clipping planes.
m.Projection.create_perspective_hmd: Creates a new Projection that projects positions using a perspective projection with the given Y-axis field of view (in degrees), X:Y aspect ratio, and clipping distances. The projection is adjusted for a head-mounted display with the given distance between eyes and distance to a point that can be focused on.
m.Projection.determinant: Returns a scalar value that is the signed factor by which areas are scaled by this matrix. If the sign is negative, the matrix flips the orientation of the area.
m.Projection.flipped_y: Returns a copy of this Projection with the signs of the values of the Y column flipped.
m.Projection.get_aspect: Returns the X:Y aspect ratio of this Projection's viewport.
m.Projection.get_far_plane_half_extents: Returns the dimensions of the far clipping plane of the projection, divided by two.
m.Projection.get_fov: Returns the horizontal field of view of the projection (in degrees).
m.Projection.get_fovy: Returns the vertical field of view of the projection (in degrees) associated with the given horizontal field of view (in degrees) and aspect ratio.
m.Projection.get_lod_multiplier: Returns the factor by which the visible level of detail is scaled by this Projection.
m.Projection.get_pixels_per_meter: Returns for_pixel_width divided by the viewport's width measured in meters on the near plane, after this Projection is applied.
m.Projection.get_projection_plane: Returns the clipping plane of this Projection whose index is given by plane.
m.Projection.get_viewport_half_extents: Returns the dimensions of the viewport plane that this Projection projects positions onto, divided by two.
m.Projection.get_z_far: Returns the distance for this Projection beyond which positions are clipped.
m.Projection.get_z_near: Returns the distance for this Projection before which positions are clipped.
m.Projection.inverse: Returns a Projection that performs the inverse of this Projection's projective transformation.
m.Projection.is_orthogonal: Returns true if this Projection performs an orthogonal projection.
m.Projection.jitter_offseted: Returns a Projection with the X and Y values from the given Vector2 added to the first and second values of the final column respectively.
m.Projection.perspective_znear_adjusted: Returns a Projection with the near clipping distance adjusted to be new_znear.
m.Projection.w: The projection matrix's W vector (column 3). Equivalent to array index 3.
m.Projection.x: The projection matrix's X vector (column 0). Equivalent to array index 0.
m.Projection.y: The projection matrix's Y vector (column 1). Equivalent to array index 1.
m.Projection.z: The projection matrix's Z vector (column 2). Equivalent to array index 2.
m.PropertyTweener.as_relative: When called, the final value will be used as a relative value instead.
m.PropertyTweener.from: Sets a custom initial value to the PropertyTweener.
m.PropertyTweener.from_current: Makes the PropertyTweener use the current property value (i.e. at the time of creating this PropertyTweener) as a starting point. This is equivalent of using from() with the current value. These two calls will do the same:
m.PropertyTweener.set_custom_interpolator: Allows interpolating the value with a custom easing function. The provided interpolator_method will be called with a value ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 and is expected to return a value within the same range (values outside the range can be used for overshoot). The return value of the method is then used for interpolation between initial and final value. Note that the parameter passed to the method is…
m.PropertyTweener.set_delay: Sets the time in seconds after which the PropertyTweener will start interpolating. By default there's no delay.
m.PropertyTweener.set_ease: Sets the type of used easing from EaseType. If not set, the default easing is used from the Tween that contains this Tweener.
m.PropertyTweener.set_trans: Sets the type of used transition from TransitionType. If not set, the default transition is used from the Tween that contains this Tweener.
m.Quaternion.IDENTITY: The identity quaternion, representing no rotation. This has the same rotation as Basis.IDENTITY.
m.Quaternion.angle_to: Returns the angle between this quaternion and to. This is the magnitude of the angle you would need to rotate by to get from one to the other.
m.Quaternion.dot: Returns the dot product between this quaternion and with.
m.Quaternion.exp: Returns the exponential of this quaternion. The rotation axis of the result is the normalized rotation axis of this quaternion, the angle of the result is the length of the vector part of this quaternion.
m.Quaternion.from_euler: Constructs a new Quaternion from the given Vector3 of Euler angles [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles], in radians. In Godot, Euler angles always use intrinsic order. This method always uses the intrinsic YXZ convention (@GlobalScope.EULER_ORDER_YXZ).
m.Quaternion.get_angle: Returns the angle of the rotation represented by this quaternion.
m.Quaternion.get_axis: Returns the rotation axis of the rotation represented by this quaternion.
m.Quaternion.get_euler: Returns this quaternion's rotation as a Vector3 of Euler angles [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles], in radians.
m.Quaternion.inverse: Returns the inverse version of this quaternion, inverting the sign of every component except w.
m.Quaternion.is_equal_approx: Returns true if this quaternion and to are approximately equal, by calling @GlobalScope.is_equal_approx() on each component.
m.Quaternion.is_finite: Returns true if this quaternion is finite, by calling @GlobalScope.is_finite() on each component.
m.Quaternion.is_normalized: Returns true if this quaternion is normalized. See also normalized().
m.Quaternion.length: Returns this quaternion's length, also called magnitude.
m.Quaternion.log: Returns the logarithm of this quaternion. Multiplies this quaternion's rotation axis by its rotation angle, and stores the result in the returned quaternion's vector part (x, y, and z). The returned quaternion's real part (w) is always 0.0.
m.Quaternion.normalized: Returns a copy of this quaternion, normalized so that its length is 1.0. See also is_normalized().
m.Quaternion.slerp: Performs a spherical-linear interpolation with the to quaternion, given a weight and returns the result. Both this quaternion and to must be normalized.
m.Quaternion.slerpni: Performs a spherical-linear interpolation with the to quaternion, given a weight and returns the result. Unlike slerp(), this method does not check if the rotation path is smaller than 90 degrees. Both this quaternion and to must be normalized.
m.Quaternion.spherical_cubic_interpolate: Performs a spherical cubic interpolation between quaternions pre_a, this vector, b, and post_b, by the given amount weight.
m.Quaternion.spherical_cubic_interpolate_i: Performs a spherical cubic interpolation between quaternions pre_a, this vector, b, and post_b, by the given amount weight.
m.Quaternion.w: W component of the quaternion. This is the "real" part.
m.Quaternion.x: X component of the quaternion. This is the value along the "imaginary" i axis.
m.Quaternion.y: Y component of the quaternion. This is the value along the "imaginary" j axis.
m.Quaternion.z: Z component of the quaternion. This is the value along the "imaginary" k axis.
m.RDAccelerationStructureGeometry.index_bu: Buffer containing vertex indices. If null, triangles are non-indexed.
m.RDAccelerationStructureGeometry.index_co: Number of indices used by this geometry in index_buffer.
m.RDAccelerationStructureGeometry.index_of: Byte offset of the first index in index_buffer.
m.RDAccelerationStructureGeometry.vertex_c: Number of vertices used by this geometry in vertex_buffer.
m.RDAccelerationStructureGeometry.vertex_f: Format of the vertices in vertex_buffer.
m.RDAccelerationStructureGeometry.vertex_o: Byte offset of the first vertex in vertex_buffer.
m.RDAccelerationStructureGeometry.vertex_s: Number of bytes between each vertex in vertex_buffer.
m.RDAccelerationStructureInstance.blas: The BLAS referenced by this instance. If null, the instance is treated as a placeholder but still contributes to gl_InstanceIndex in GLSL.
m.RDAccelerationStructureInstance.hit_sbt_: Hit shader binding table range used for this instance, allocated using the RenderingDevice.hit_sbt_range_alloc() method.
m.RDAccelerationStructureInstance.id: Custom instance ID that can be accessed in GLSL using gl_InstanceCustomIndexEXT.
m.RDAccelerationStructureInstance.mask: Visibility mask used to control which rays can intersect this instance.
m.RDAccelerationStructureInstance.transfor: Transform applied to the referenced BLAS for this instance.
m.RDAttachmentFormat.samples: The number of samples used when sampling the attachment.
m.RDAttachmentFormat.usage_flags: The attachment's usage flags, which determine what can be done with it.
m.RDFramebufferPass.color_attachments: Color attachments in order starting from 0. If this attachment is not used by the shader, pass ATTACHMENT_UNUSED to skip.
m.RDFramebufferPass.depth_attachment: Depth attachment. ATTACHMENT_UNUSED should be used if no depth buffer is required for this pass.
m.RDFramebufferPass.input_attachments: Used for multipass framebuffers (more than one render pass). Converts an attachment to an input. Make sure to also supply it properly in the RDUniform for the uniform set.
m.RDFramebufferPass.preserve_attachments: Attachments to preserve in this pass (otherwise they are erased).
m.RDFramebufferPass.resolve_attachments: If the color attachments are multisampled, non-multisampled resolve attachments can be provided.
m.RDHitGroup.any_hit_shader: Any-hit shader for this hit group. Executed for each potential intersection. Can be null.
m.RDHitGroup.closest_hit_shader: Closest-hit shader for this hit group. Executed for the closest intersection. Can be null.
m.RDHitGroup.intersection_shader: Intersection shader for this hit group. Required for non-triangle geometry. Must be null when using for triangle geometry.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendState.attachments: The attachments that are blended together.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendState.blend_constant: The constant color to blend with. See also RenderingDevice.draw_list_set_blend_constants().
m.RDPipelineColorBlendState.enable_logic_o: If true, performs the logic operation defined in logic_op.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendState.logic_op: The logic operation to perform for blending. Only effective if enable_logic_op is true.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendStateAttachment.alph: The blend mode to use for the alpha channel.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendStateAttachment.colo: The blend mode to use for the red/green/blue color channels.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendStateAttachment.dst_: Controls how the blend factor for the alpha channel is determined based on the destination's fragments.
Controls how the blend factor for the color channels is determined based on the destination's fragments.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendStateAttachment.enab: If true, performs blending between the source and destination according to the factors defined in src_color_blend_factor, dst_color_blend_factor, src_alpha_blend_factor and dst_alpha_blend_factor. The blend modes color_blend_op and alpha_blend_op are also taken into account, with write_r, write_g, write_b and write_a controlling the output.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendStateAttachment.set_: Convenience method to perform standard mix blending with straight (non-premultiplied) alpha. This sets enable_blend to true, src_color_blend_factor to RenderingDevice.BLEND_FACTOR_SRC_ALPHA, dst_color_blend_factor to RenderingDevice.BLEND_FACTOR_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, src_alpha_blend_factor to RenderingDevice.BLEND_FACTOR_SRC_ALPHA and dst_alpha_blend_factor to RenderingDevice.BLEND_FACTOR_ONE_MINU…
m.RDPipelineColorBlendStateAttachment.src_: Controls how the blend factor for the alpha channel is determined based on the source's fragments.
Controls how the blend factor for the color channels is determined based on the source's fragments.
m.RDPipelineColorBlendStateAttachment.writ: If true, writes the new alpha channel to the final result.
If true, writes the new blue color channel to the final result.
If true, writes the new green color channel to the final result.
If true, writes the new red color channel to the final result.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.back_op_comp: The method used for comparing the previous back stencil value and back_op_reference.
Selects which bits from the back stencil value will be compared.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.back_op_dept: The operation to perform on the stencil buffer for back pixels that pass the stencil test but fail the depth test.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.back_op_fail: The operation to perform on the stencil buffer for back pixels that fail the stencil test.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.back_op_pass: The operation to perform on the stencil buffer for back pixels that pass the stencil test.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.back_op_refe: The value the previous back stencil value will be compared to.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.back_op_writ: Selects which bits from the back stencil value will be changed.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.depth_compar: The method used for comparing the previous and current depth values.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.depth_range_: The maximum depth that returns true for enable_depth_range.
The minimum depth that returns true for enable_depth_range.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.enable_depth: If true, each depth value will be tested to see if it is between depth_range_min and depth_range_max. If it is outside of these values, it is discarded.

If true, enables depth testing which allows objects to be automatically occluded by other objects based on their depth. This also allows objects to be partially occluded by other objects. If false, objects will appear in the order they were drawn (like in Godot's 2D renderer).
If true, writes to the depth buffer whenever the depth test returns true. Only works when enable_depth_test is also true.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.enable_stenc: If true, enables stencil testing. There are separate stencil buffers for front-facing triangles and back-facing triangles. See properties that begin with "front_op" and properties with "back_op" for each.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.front_op_com: The method used for comparing the previous front stencil value and front_op_reference.
Selects which bits from the front stencil value will be compared.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.front_op_dep: The operation to perform on the stencil buffer for front pixels that pass the stencil test but fail the depth test.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.front_op_fai: The operation to perform on the stencil buffer for front pixels that fail the stencil test.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.front_op_pas: The operation to perform on the stencil buffer for front pixels that pass the stencil test.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.front_op_ref: The value the previous front stencil value will be compared to.
m.RDPipelineDepthStencilState.front_op_wri: Selects which bits from the front stencil value will be changed.
m.RDPipelineMultisampleState.enable_alpha_: If true, alpha to coverage is enabled. This generates a temporary coverage value based on the alpha component of the fragment's first color output. This allows alpha transparency to make use of multisample antialiasing.
If true, alpha is forced to either 0.0 or 1.0. This allows hardening the edges of antialiased alpha transparencies. Only relevant if enable_alpha_to_coverage is true.
m.RDPipelineMultisampleState.enable_sample: If true, enables per-sample shading which replaces MSAA by SSAA. This provides higher quality antialiasing that works with transparent (alpha scissor) edges. This has a very high performance cost. See also min_sample_shading. See the per-sample shading Vulkan documentation [https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#primsrast-sampleshading] for more details.
m.RDPipelineMultisampleState.min_sample_sh: The multiplier of sample_count that determines how many samples are performed for each fragment. Must be between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive). Only effective if enable_sample_shading is true. If min_sample_shading is 1.0, fragment invocation must only read from the coverage index sample. Tile image access must not be used if enable_sample_shading is not 1.0.
m.RDPipelineMultisampleState.sample_count: The number of MSAA samples (or SSAA samples if enable_sample_shading is true) to perform. Higher values result in better antialiasing, at the cost of performance.
m.RDPipelineMultisampleState.sample_masks: The sample mask array. See the sample mask Vulkan documentation [https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#fragops-samplemask] for more details.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.cull_mode: The cull mode to use when drawing polygons, which determines whether front faces or backfaces are hidden.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.depth_bias_: A limit for how much each depth value can be offset. If negative, it serves as a minimum value, but if positive, it serves as a maximum value.
A constant offset added to each depth value. Applied after depth_bias_slope_factor.
If true, each generated depth value will by offset by some amount. The specific amount is generated per polygon based on the values of depth_bias_slope_factor and depth_bias_constant_factor.
A constant scale applied to the slope of each polygons' depth. Applied before depth_bias_constant_factor.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.discard_pri: If true, primitives are discarded immediately before the rasterization stage.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.enable_dept: If true, clamps depth values according to the minimum and maximum depth of the associated viewport.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.front_face: The winding order to use to determine which face of a triangle is considered its front face.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.line_width: The line width to use when drawing lines (in pixels). Thick lines may not be supported on all hardware.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.patch_contr: The number of control points to use when drawing a patch with tessellation enabled. Higher values result in higher quality at the cost of performance.
m.RDPipelineRasterizationState.wireframe: If true, performs wireframe rendering for triangles instead of flat or textured rendering.
m.RDPipelineShader.shader: Shader resource. The required stage is selected by the pipeline.
m.RDPipelineShader.specialization_constant: Specialization constants applied to the selected shader stage at pipeline creation time.
m.RDPipelineSpecializationConstant.constan: The identifier of the specialization constant. This is a value starting from 0 and that increments for every different specialization constant for a given shader.
m.RDPipelineSpecializationConstant.value: The specialization constant's value. Only bool, int and float types are valid for specialization constants.
m.RDSamplerState.anisotropy_max: Maximum anisotropy that can be used when sampling. Only effective if use_anisotropy is true. Higher values result in a sharper sampler at oblique angles, at the cost of performance (due to memory bandwidth). This value may be limited by the graphics hardware in use. Most graphics hardware only supports values up to 16.0.
m.RDSamplerState.border_color: The border color that will be returned when sampling outside the sampler's bounds and the repeat_u, repeat_v or repeat_w modes have repeating disabled.
m.RDSamplerState.compare_op: The compare operation to use. Only effective if enable_compare is true.
m.RDSamplerState.enable_compare: If true, returned values will be based on the comparison operation defined in compare_op. This is a hardware-based approach and is therefore faster than performing this manually in a shader. For example, compare operations are used for shadow map rendering by comparing depth values from a shadow sampler.
m.RDSamplerState.lod_bias: The mipmap LOD bias to use. Positive values will make the sampler blurrier at a given distance, while negative values will make the sampler sharper at a given distance (at the risk of looking grainy). Recommended values are between -0.5 and 0.0. Only effective if the sampler has mipmaps available.
m.RDSamplerState.mag_filter: The sampler's magnification filter. It is the filtering method used when sampling texels that appear bigger than on-screen pixels.
m.RDSamplerState.max_lod: The maximum mipmap LOD bias to display (lowest resolution). Only effective if the sampler has mipmaps available.
m.RDSamplerState.min_filter: The sampler's minification filter. It is the filtering method used when sampling texels that appear smaller than on-screen pixels.
m.RDSamplerState.min_lod: The minimum mipmap LOD bias to display (highest resolution). Only effective if the sampler has mipmaps available.
m.RDSamplerState.mip_filter: The filtering method to use for mipmaps.
m.RDSamplerState.repeat_u: The repeat mode to use along the U axis of UV coordinates. This affects the returned values if sampling outside the UV bounds.
m.RDSamplerState.repeat_v: The repeat mode to use along the V axis of UV coordinates. This affects the returned values if sampling outside the UV bounds.
m.RDSamplerState.repeat_w: The repeat mode to use along the W axis of UV coordinates. This affects the returned values if sampling outside the UV bounds. Only effective for 3D samplers.
m.RDSamplerState.unnormalized_uvw: If true, the texture will be sampled with coordinates ranging from 0 to the texture's resolution. Otherwise, the coordinates will be normalized and range from 0 to 1.
m.RDSamplerState.use_anisotropy: If true, perform anisotropic sampling. See anisotropy_max.
m.RDShaderFile.base_error: The base compilation error message, which indicates errors not related to a specific shader stage if non-empty. If empty, shader compilation is not necessarily successful (check RDShaderSPIRV's error message members).
m.RDShaderFile.get_spirv: Returns the SPIR-V intermediate representation for the specified shader version.
m.RDShaderFile.get_version_list: Returns the list of compiled versions for this shader.
m.RDShaderFile.set_bytecode: Sets the SPIR-V bytecode that will be compiled for the specified version.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_any_hit: The SPIR-V bytecode for the any hit shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_closest_hit: The SPIR-V bytecode for the closest hit shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_compute: The SPIR-V bytecode for the compute shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_fragment: The SPIR-V bytecode for the fragment shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_intersection: The SPIR-V bytecode for the intersection shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_miss: The SPIR-V bytecode for the miss shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_raygen: The SPIR-V bytecode for the ray generation shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_tesselation_contr: The SPIR-V bytecode for the tessellation control shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_tesselation_evalu: The SPIR-V bytecode for the tessellation evaluation shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.bytecode_vertex: The SPIR-V bytecode for the vertex shader stage.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_any_hit: The compilation error message for the any hit shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_closest_hit: The compilation error message for the closest hit shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_compute: The compilation error message for the compute shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_fragment: The compilation error message for the fragment shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_intersection: The compilation error message for the intersection shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_miss: The compilation error message for the miss shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_raygen: The compilation error message for the ray generation shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_tesselation_: The compilation error message for the tessellation control shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
The compilation error message for the tessellation evaluation shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.compile_error_vertex: The compilation error message for the vertex shader stage (set by the SPIR-V compiler and Godot). If empty, shader compilation was successful.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.get_stage_bytecode: Equivalent to getting one of bytecode_compute, bytecode_fragment, bytecode_tesselation_control, bytecode_tesselation_evaluation, bytecode_vertex.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.get_stage_compile_error: Returns the compilation error message for the given shader stage. Equivalent to getting one of compile_error_compute, compile_error_fragment, compile_error_tesselation_control, compile_error_tesselation_evaluation, compile_error_vertex.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.set_stage_bytecode: Sets the SPIR-V bytecode for the given shader stage. Equivalent to setting one of bytecode_compute, bytecode_fragment, bytecode_tesselation_control, bytecode_tesselation_evaluation, bytecode_vertex.
m.RDShaderSPIRV.set_stage_compile_error: Sets the compilation error message for the given shader stage to compile_error. Equivalent to setting one of compile_error_compute, compile_error_fragment, compile_error_tesselation_control, compile_error_tesselation_evaluation, compile_error_vertex.
m.RDShaderSource.get_stage_source: Returns source code for the specified shader stage. Equivalent to getting one of source_compute, source_fragment, source_tesselation_control, source_tesselation_evaluation or source_vertex.
m.RDShaderSource.language: The language the shader is written in.
m.RDShaderSource.set_stage_source: Sets source code for the specified shader stage. Equivalent to setting one of source_compute, source_fragment, source_tesselation_control, source_tesselation_evaluation or source_vertex.
m.RDShaderSource.source_any_hit: Source code for the shader's any hit stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_closest_hit: Source code for the shader's closest hit stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_compute: Source code for the shader's compute stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_fragment: Source code for the shader's fragment stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_intersection: Source code for the shader's intersection stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_miss: Source code for the shader's miss stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_raygen: Source code for the shader's ray generation stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_tesselation_contro: Source code for the shader's tessellation control stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_tesselation_evalua: Source code for the shader's tessellation evaluation stage.
m.RDShaderSource.source_vertex: Source code for the shader's vertex stage.
m.RDTextureFormat.add_shareable_format: Adds format as a valid format for the corresponding RDTextureView's RDTextureView.format_override property. If any format is added as shareable, then the main format must also be added.
m.RDTextureFormat.array_layers: The number of layers in the texture. Only relevant for 2D texture arrays.
m.RDTextureFormat.depth: The texture's depth (in pixels). This is always 1 for 2D textures.
m.RDTextureFormat.is_discardable: If a texture is discardable, its contents do not need to be preserved between frames. This flag is only relevant when the texture is used as target in a draw list.
m.RDTextureFormat.is_resolve_buffer: The texture will be used as the destination of a resolve operation.
m.RDTextureFormat.mipmaps: The number of mipmaps available in the texture.
m.RDTextureFormat.remove_shareable_format: Removes format from the list of valid formats that the corresponding RDTextureView's RDTextureView.format_override property can be set to.
m.RDTextureFormat.samples: The number of samples used when sampling the texture.
m.RDTextureFormat.usage_bits: The texture's usage bits, which determine what can be done using the texture.
m.RDTextureView.format_override: Optional override for the data format to return sampled values in. The corresponding RDTextureFormat must have had this added as a shareable format. The default value of RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_MAX does not override the format.
m.RDTextureView.swizzle_a: The channel to sample when sampling the alpha channel.
m.RDTextureView.swizzle_b: The channel to sample when sampling the blue color channel.
m.RDTextureView.swizzle_g: The channel to sample when sampling the green color channel.
m.RDTextureView.swizzle_r: The channel to sample when sampling the red color channel.
m.RDUniform.add_id: Binds the given id to the uniform. The data associated with the id is then used when the uniform is passed to a shader.
m.RDUniform.clear_ids: Unbinds all ids currently bound to the uniform.
m.RDUniform.get_ids: Returns an array of all ids currently bound to the uniform.
m.RDVertexAttribute.binding: The index of the buffer in the vertex buffer array to bind this vertex attribute. When set to -1, it defaults to the index of the attribute.
m.RDVertexAttribute.format: The way that this attribute's data is interpreted when sent to a shader.
m.RDVertexAttribute.frequency: The rate at which this attribute is pulled from its vertex buffer.
m.RDVertexAttribute.location: The location in the shader that this attribute is bound to.
m.RDVertexAttribute.offset: The number of bytes between the start of the vertex buffer and the first instance of this attribute.
m.RDVertexAttribute.stride: The number of bytes between the starts of consecutive instances of this attribute.
m.RID.get_id: Returns the ID of the referenced low-level resource.
m.RID.is_valid: Returns true if the RID is not 0.
m.RandomNumberGenerator.rand_weighted: Returns a random integer between 0 and the size of the array that is passed as a parameter. Each value in the array should be a floating-point number that represents the relative likelihood that it will be returned as an index. A higher value means the value is more likely to be returned as an index, while a value of 0 means it will never be returned as an index.
m.RandomNumberGenerator.randf: Returns a pseudo-random float between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).
m.RandomNumberGenerator.randf_range: Returns a pseudo-random float between from and to (inclusive).
m.RandomNumberGenerator.randfn: Returns a normally-distributed [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution], pseudo-random floating-point number from the specified mean and a standard deviation. This is also known as a Gaussian distribution.
m.RandomNumberGenerator.randi: Returns a pseudo-random 32-bit unsigned integer between 0 and 4294967295 (inclusive).
m.RandomNumberGenerator.randi_range: Returns a pseudo-random 32-bit signed integer between from and to (inclusive).
m.RandomNumberGenerator.randomize: Sets up a time-based seed for this RandomNumberGenerator instance. Unlike the @GlobalScope random number generation functions, different RandomNumberGenerator instances can use different seeds.
m.RandomNumberGenerator.seed: Initializes the random number generator state based on the given seed value. A given seed will give a reproducible sequence of pseudo-random numbers.
m.RandomNumberGenerator.state: The current state of the random number generator. Save and restore this property to restore the generator to a previous state:
m.Range._value_changed: Called when the Range's value is changed (following the same conditions as value_changed).
m.Range.allow_greater: If true, value may be greater than max_value.
m.Range.allow_lesser: If true, value may be less than min_value.
m.Range.changed: Emitted when min_value, max_value, page, or step change.
m.Range.exp_edit: If true, and min_value is greater or equal to 0, value will be represented exponentially rather than linearly.
m.Range.max_value: Maximum value. Range is clamped if value is greater than max_value.
m.Range.min_value: Minimum value. Range is clamped if value is less than min_value.
m.Range.page: Page size. Used mainly for ScrollBar. A ScrollBar's grabber length is the ScrollBar's size multiplied by page over the difference between min_value and max_value.
m.Range.rounded: If true, value will always be rounded to the nearest integer.
m.Range.set_value_no_signal: Sets the Range's current value to the specified value, without emitting the value_changed signal.
m.Range.share: Binds two Ranges together along with any ranges previously grouped with either of them. When any of range's member variables change, it will share the new value with all other ranges in its group.
m.Range.step: If greater than 0.0, value will always be rounded to a multiple of this property's value above min_value. For example, if min_value is 0.1 and step is 0.2, then value is limited to 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and so on. If rounded is also true, value will first be rounded to a multiple of this property's value, then rounded to the nearest integer.
m.Range.unshare: Stops the Range from sharing its member variables with any other.
m.Range.value: Range's current value. Changing this property (even via code) will trigger value_changed signal. Use set_value_no_signal() if you want to avoid it.
m.Range.value_changed: Emitted when value changes. When used on a Slider, this is called continuously while dragging (potentially every frame). If you are performing an expensive operation in a function connected to value_changed, consider using a debouncing Timer to call the function less often.
m.RayCast2D.add_exception: Adds a collision exception so the ray does not report collisions with the specified node.
m.RayCast2D.add_exception_rid: Adds a collision exception so the ray does not report collisions with the specified RID.
m.RayCast2D.clear_exceptions: Removes all collision exceptions for this ray.
m.RayCast2D.collide_with_areas: If true, collisions with Area2Ds will be reported.
m.RayCast2D.collide_with_bodies: If true, collisions with PhysicsBody2Ds will be reported.
m.RayCast2D.collision_mask: The ray's collision mask. Only objects in at least one collision layer enabled in the mask will be detected. See Collision layers and masks in the documentation for more information.
m.RayCast2D.enabled: If true, collisions will be reported.
m.RayCast2D.exclude_parent: If true, this raycast will not report collisions with its parent node. This property only has an effect if the parent node is a CollisionObject2D. See also Node.get_parent() and add_exception().
m.RayCast2D.force_raycast_update: Updates the collision information for the ray immediately, without waiting for the next _physics_process call. Use this method, for example, when the ray or its parent has changed state.
m.RayCast2D.get_collider: Returns the first object that the ray intersects, or null if no object is intersecting the ray (i.e. is_colliding() returns false).
m.RayCast2D.get_collider_rid: Returns the RID of the first object that the ray intersects, or an empty RID if no object is intersecting the ray (i.e. is_colliding() returns false).
m.RayCast2D.get_collider_shape: Returns the shape ID of the first object that the ray intersects, or 0 if no object is intersecting the ray (i.e. is_colliding() returns false).
m.RayCast2D.get_collision_mask_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.RayCast2D.get_collision_normal: Returns the normal of the intersecting object's shape at the collision point, or Vector2(0, 0) if the ray starts inside the shape and hit_from_inside is true.
m.RayCast2D.get_collision_point: Returns the collision point at which the ray intersects the closest object, in the global coordinate system. If hit_from_inside is true and the ray starts inside of a collision shape, this function will return the origin point of the ray.
m.RayCast2D.hit_from_inside: If true, the ray will detect a hit when starting inside shapes. In this case the collision normal will be Vector2(0, 0). Does not affect concave polygon shapes.
m.RayCast2D.is_colliding: Returns whether any object is intersecting with the ray's vector (considering the vector length).
m.RayCast2D.remove_exception: Removes a collision exception so the ray can report collisions with the specified node.
m.RayCast2D.remove_exception_rid: Removes a collision exception so the ray can report collisions with the specified RID.
m.RayCast2D.set_collision_mask_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.RayCast2D.target_position: The ray's destination point, relative to this raycast's Node2D.position.
m.RayCast3D.add_exception: Adds a collision exception so the ray does not report collisions with the specified node.
m.RayCast3D.add_exception_rid: Adds a collision exception so the ray does not report collisions with the specified RID.
m.RayCast3D.clear_exceptions: Removes all collision exceptions for this ray.
m.RayCast3D.collide_with_areas: If true, collisions with Area3Ds will be reported.
m.RayCast3D.collide_with_bodies: If true, collisions with PhysicsBody3Ds will be reported.
m.RayCast3D.collision_mask: The ray's collision mask. Only objects in at least one collision layer enabled in the mask will be detected. See Collision layers and masks in the documentation for more information.
m.RayCast3D.debug_shape_custom_color: The custom color to use to draw the shape in the editor and at run-time if Visible Collision Shapes is enabled in the Debug menu. This color will be highlighted at run-time if the RayCast3D is colliding with something.
m.RayCast3D.debug_shape_thickness: If set to 1, a line is used as the debug shape. Otherwise, a truncated pyramid is drawn to represent the RayCast3D. Requires Visible Collision Shapes to be enabled in the Debug menu for the debug shape to be visible at run-time.
m.RayCast3D.enabled: If true, collisions will be reported.
m.RayCast3D.exclude_parent: If true, this raycast will not report collisions with its parent node. This property only has an effect if the parent node is a CollisionObject3D. See also Node.get_parent() and add_exception().
m.RayCast3D.force_raycast_update: Updates the collision information for the ray immediately, without waiting for the next _physics_process call. Use this method, for example, when the ray or its parent has changed state.
m.RayCast3D.get_collider: Returns the first object that the ray intersects, or null if no object is intersecting the ray (i.e. is_colliding() returns false).
m.RayCast3D.get_collider_rid: Returns the RID of the first object that the ray intersects, or an empty RID if no object is intersecting the ray (i.e. is_colliding() returns false).
m.RayCast3D.get_collider_shape: Returns the shape ID of the first object that the ray intersects, or 0 if no object is intersecting the ray (i.e. is_colliding() returns false).
m.RayCast3D.get_collision_face_index: Returns the collision object's face index at the collision point, or -1 if the shape intersecting the ray is not a ConcavePolygonShape3D.
m.RayCast3D.get_collision_mask_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.RayCast3D.get_collision_normal: Returns the normal of the intersecting object's shape at the collision point, or Vector3(0, 0, 0) if the ray starts inside the shape and hit_from_inside is true.
m.RayCast3D.get_collision_point: Returns the collision point at which the ray intersects the closest object, in the global coordinate system. If hit_from_inside is true and the ray starts inside of a collision shape, this function will return the origin point of the ray.
m.RayCast3D.hit_back_faces: If true, the ray will hit back faces with concave polygon shapes with back face enabled or heightmap shapes.
m.RayCast3D.hit_from_inside: If true, the ray will detect a hit when starting inside shapes. In this case the collision normal will be Vector3(0, 0, 0). Does not affect shapes with no volume like concave polygon or heightmap.
m.RayCast3D.is_colliding: Returns whether any object is intersecting with the ray's vector (considering the vector length).
m.RayCast3D.remove_exception: Removes a collision exception so the ray can report collisions with the specified node.
m.RayCast3D.remove_exception_rid: Removes a collision exception so the ray can report collisions with the specified RID.
m.RayCast3D.set_collision_mask_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.RayCast3D.target_position: The ray's destination point, relative to this raycast's Node3D.position.
m.Rect2.abs: Returns a Rect2 equivalent to this rectangle, with its width and height modified to be non-negative values, and with its position being the top-left corner of the rectangle.
m.Rect2.encloses: Returns true if this rectangle completely encloses the b rectangle.
m.Rect2.end: The ending point. This is usually the bottom-right corner of the rectangle, and is equivalent to position + size. Setting this point affects the size.
m.Rect2.expand: Returns a copy of this rectangle expanded to align the edges with the given to point, if necessary.
m.Rect2.get_area: Returns the rectangle's area. This is equivalent to size.x * size.y. See also has_area().
m.Rect2.get_center: Returns the center point of the rectangle. This is the same as position + (size / 2.0).
m.Rect2.get_support: Returns the vertex's position of this rect that's the farthest in the given direction. This point is commonly known as the support point in collision detection algorithms.
m.Rect2.grow: Returns a copy of this rectangle extended on all sides by the given amount. A negative amount shrinks the rectangle instead. See also grow_individual() and grow_side().
m.Rect2.grow_individual: Returns a copy of this rectangle with its left, top, right, and bottom sides extended by the given amounts. Negative values shrink the sides, instead. See also grow() and grow_side().
m.Rect2.grow_side: Returns a copy of this rectangle with its side extended by the given amount (see Side constants). A negative amount shrinks the rectangle, instead. See also grow() and grow_individual().
m.Rect2.has_area: Returns true if this rectangle has positive width and height. See also get_area().
m.Rect2.has_point: Returns true if the rectangle contains the given point. By convention, points on the right and bottom edges are not included.
m.Rect2.intersection: Returns the intersection between this rectangle and b. If the rectangles do not intersect, returns an empty Rect2.
m.Rect2.intersects: Returns true if this rectangle overlaps with the b rectangle. The edges of both rectangles are excluded, unless include_borders is true.
m.Rect2.is_equal_approx: Returns true if this rectangle and rect are approximately equal, by calling Vector2.is_equal_approx() on the position and the size.
m.Rect2.is_finite: Returns true if this rectangle's values are finite, by calling Vector2.is_finite() on the position and the size.
m.Rect2.merge: Returns a Rect2 that encloses both this rectangle and b around the edges. See also encloses().
m.Rect2.position: The origin point. This is usually the top-left corner of the rectangle.
m.Rect2.size: The rectangle's width and height, starting from position. Setting this value also affects the end point.
m.Rect2i.abs: Returns a Rect2i equivalent to this rectangle, with its width and height modified to be non-negative values, and with its position being the top-left corner of the rectangle.
m.Rect2i.encloses: Returns true if this Rect2i completely encloses another one.
m.Rect2i.end: The ending point. This is usually the bottom-right corner of the rectangle, and is equivalent to position + size. Setting this point affects the size.
m.Rect2i.expand: Returns a copy of this rectangle expanded to align the edges with the given to point, if necessary.
m.Rect2i.get_area: Returns the rectangle's area. This is equivalent to size.x * size.y. See also has_area().
m.Rect2i.get_center: Returns the center point of the rectangle. This is the same as position + (size / 2).
m.Rect2i.grow: Returns a copy of this rectangle extended on all sides by the given amount. A negative amount shrinks the rectangle instead. See also grow_individual() and grow_side().
m.Rect2i.grow_individual: Returns a copy of this rectangle with its left, top, right, and bottom sides extended by the given amounts. Negative values shrink the sides, instead. See also grow() and grow_side().
m.Rect2i.grow_side: Returns a copy of this rectangle with its side extended by the given amount (see Side constants). A negative amount shrinks the rectangle, instead. See also grow() and grow_individual().
m.Rect2i.has_area: Returns true if this rectangle has positive width and height. See also get_area().
m.Rect2i.has_point: Returns true if the rectangle contains the given point. By convention, points on the right and bottom edges are not included.
m.Rect2i.intersection: Returns the intersection between this rectangle and b. If the rectangles do not intersect, returns an empty Rect2i.
m.Rect2i.intersects: Returns true if this rectangle overlaps with the b rectangle. The edges of both rectangles are excluded.
m.Rect2i.merge: Returns a Rect2i that encloses both this rectangle and b around the edges. See also encloses().
m.Rect2i.position: The origin point. This is usually the top-left corner of the rectangle.
m.Rect2i.size: The rectangle's width and height, starting from position. Setting this value also affects the end point.
m.RefCounted.init_ref: Initializes the internal reference counter. Use this only if you really know what you are doing.
m.RefCounted.reference: Increments the internal reference counter. Use this only if you really know what you are doing.
m.RefCounted.unreference: Decrements the internal reference counter. Use this only if you really know what you are doing.
m.ReferenceRect.border_color: Sets the border color of the ReferenceRect.
m.ReferenceRect.border_width: Sets the border width of the ReferenceRect. The border grows both inwards and outwards with respect to the rectangle box.
m.ReferenceRect.editor_only: If true, the ReferenceRect will only be visible while in editor. Otherwise, ReferenceRect will be visible in the running project.
m.ReflectionProbe.AMBIENT_COLOR: Apply custom ambient lighting inside the ReflectionProbe's box defined by its size. See ambient_color and ambient_color_energy.
m.ReflectionProbe.AMBIENT_DISABLED: Do not apply any ambient lighting inside the ReflectionProbe's box defined by its size.
m.ReflectionProbe.AMBIENT_ENVIRONMENT: Apply automatically-sourced environment lighting inside the ReflectionProbe's box defined by its size.
m.ReflectionProbe.UPDATE_ALWAYS: Update the probe every frame. This provides better results for fast-moving dynamic objects (such as cars). However, it has a significant performance cost. Due to the cost, it's recommended to only use one ReflectionProbe with UPDATE_ALWAYS at most per scene. For all other use cases, use UPDATE_ONCE.
m.ReflectionProbe.UPDATE_ONCE: Update the probe once on the next frame (recommended for most objects). The corresponding radiance map will be generated over the following six frames. This takes more time to update than UPDATE_ALWAYS, but it has a lower performance cost and can result in higher-quality reflections. The ReflectionProbe is updated when its transform changes, but not when nearby geometry changes. You can force a R…
m.ReflectionProbe.ambient_color: The custom ambient color to use within the ReflectionProbe's box defined by its size. Only effective if ambient_mode is AMBIENT_COLOR.
m.ReflectionProbe.ambient_color_energy: The custom ambient color energy to use within the ReflectionProbe's box defined by its size. Only effective if ambient_mode is AMBIENT_COLOR.
m.ReflectionProbe.ambient_mode: The ambient color to use within the ReflectionProbe's box defined by its size. The ambient color will smoothly blend with other ReflectionProbes and the rest of the scene (outside the ReflectionProbe's box defined by its size).
m.ReflectionProbe.blend_distance: Defines the distance in meters over which a probe blends into the scene.
m.ReflectionProbe.box_projection: If true, enables box projection. This makes reflections look more correct in rectangle-shaped rooms by offsetting the reflection center depending on the camera's location.
m.ReflectionProbe.cull_mask: Sets the cull mask which determines what objects are drawn by this probe. Every VisualInstance3D with a layer included in this cull mask will be rendered by the probe. It is best to only include large objects which are likely to take up a lot of space in the reflection in order to save on rendering cost.
m.ReflectionProbe.enable_shadows: If true, computes shadows in the reflection probe. This makes the reflection probe slower to render; you may want to disable this if using the UPDATE_ALWAYS update_mode.
m.ReflectionProbe.intensity: Defines the reflection intensity. Intensity modulates the strength of the reflection.
m.ReflectionProbe.interior: If true, reflections will ignore sky contribution.
m.ReflectionProbe.max_distance: The maximum distance away from the ReflectionProbe an object can be before it is culled. Decrease this to improve performance, especially when using the UPDATE_ALWAYS update_mode.
m.ReflectionProbe.mesh_lod_threshold: The automatic LOD bias to use for meshes rendered within the ReflectionProbe (this is analog to Viewport.mesh_lod_threshold). Higher values will use less detailed versions of meshes that have LOD variations generated. If set to 0.0, automatic LOD is disabled. Increase mesh_lod_threshold to improve performance at the cost of geometry detail, especially when using the UPDATE_ALWAYS update_mode.
m.ReflectionProbe.origin_offset: Sets the origin offset to be used when this ReflectionProbe is in box_projection mode. This can be set to a non-zero value to ensure a reflection fits a rectangle-shaped room, while reducing the number of objects that "get in the way" of the reflection.
m.ReflectionProbe.reflection_mask: Sets the reflection mask which determines what objects have reflections applied from this probe. Every VisualInstance3D with a layer included in this reflection mask will have reflections applied from this probe. See also cull_mask, which can be used to exclude objects from appearing in the reflection while still making them affected by the ReflectionProbe.
m.ReflectionProbe.size: The size of the reflection probe. The larger the size, the more space covered by the probe, which will lower the perceived resolution. It is best to keep the size only as large as you need it.
m.ReflectionProbe.update_mode: Sets how frequently the ReflectionProbe is updated. Can be UPDATE_ONCE or UPDATE_ALWAYS.
m.RegEx.clear: This method resets the state of the object, as if it was freshly created. Namely, it unassigns the regular expression of this object.
m.RegEx.compile: Compiles and assign the search pattern to use. Returns @GlobalScope.OK if the compilation is successful. If compilation fails, returns @GlobalScope.FAILED and when show_error is true, details are printed to standard output.
m.RegEx.create_from_string: Creates and compiles a new RegEx object. See also compile().
m.RegEx.get_group_count: Returns the number of capturing groups in compiled pattern.
m.RegEx.get_names: Returns an array of names of named capturing groups in the compiled pattern. They are ordered by appearance.
m.RegEx.get_pattern: Returns the original search pattern that was compiled.
m.RegEx.is_valid: Returns whether this object has a valid search pattern assigned.
m.RegEx.search: Searches the text for the compiled pattern. Returns a RegExMatch container of the first matching result if found, otherwise null.
m.RegEx.search_all: Searches the text for the compiled pattern. Returns an array of RegExMatch containers for each non-overlapping result. If no results were found, an empty array is returned instead.
m.RegEx.sub: Searches the text for the compiled pattern and replaces it with the specified string. Escapes and backreferences such as $1 and $name are expanded and resolved. By default, only the first instance is replaced, but it can be changed for all instances (global replacement).
m.RegExMatch.get_end: Returns the end position of the match within the source string. The end position of capturing groups can be retrieved by providing its group number as an integer or its string name (if it's a named group). The default value of 0 refers to the whole pattern.
m.RegExMatch.get_group_count: Returns the number of capturing groups.
m.RegExMatch.get_start: Returns the starting position of the match within the source string. The starting position of capturing groups can be retrieved by providing its group number as an integer or its string name (if it's a named group). The default value of 0 refers to the whole pattern.
m.RegExMatch.get_string: Returns the substring of the match from the source string. Capturing groups can be retrieved by providing its group number as an integer or its string name (if it's a named group). The default value of 0 refers to the whole pattern.
m.RegExMatch.names: A dictionary of named groups and its corresponding group number. Only groups that were matched are included. If multiple groups have the same name, that name would refer to the first matching one.
m.RegExMatch.strings: An Array of the match and its capturing groups.
m.RegExMatch.subject: The source string used with the search pattern to find this matching result.
m.RemoteTransform2D.force_update_cache: RemoteTransform2D caches the remote node. It may not notice if the remote node disappears; force_update_cache() forces it to update the cache again.
m.RemoteTransform2D.remote_path: The NodePath to the remote node, relative to the RemoteTransform2D's position in the scene.
m.RemoteTransform2D.update_position: If true, the remote node's position is updated.
m.RemoteTransform2D.update_rotation: If true, the remote node's rotation is updated.
m.RemoteTransform2D.update_scale: If true, the remote node's scale is updated.
m.RemoteTransform2D.use_global_coordinates: If true, global coordinates are used. If false, local coordinates are used.
m.RemoteTransform3D.force_update_cache: RemoteTransform3D caches the remote node. It may not notice if the remote node disappears; force_update_cache() forces it to update the cache again.
m.RemoteTransform3D.remote_path: The NodePath to the remote node, relative to the RemoteTransform3D's position in the scene.
m.RemoteTransform3D.update_position: If true, the remote node's position is updated.
m.RemoteTransform3D.update_rotation: If true, the remote node's rotation is updated.
m.RemoteTransform3D.update_scale: If true, the remote node's scale is updated.
m.RemoteTransform3D.use_global_coordinates: If true, global coordinates are used. If false, local coordinates are used.
m.RenderData.get_camera_attributes: Returns the RID of the camera attributes object in the RenderingServer being used to render this viewport.
m.RenderData.get_environment: Returns the RID of the environment object in the RenderingServer being used to render this viewport.
m.RenderData.get_render_scene_buffers: Returns the RenderSceneBuffers object managing the scene buffers for rendering this viewport.
m.RenderData.get_render_scene_data: Returns the RenderSceneData object managing this frames scene data.
m.RenderDataExtension._get_camera_attribut: Implement this in GDExtension to return the RID for the implementation's camera attributes object.
m.RenderDataExtension._get_environment: Implement this in GDExtension to return the RID of the implementation's environment object.
m.RenderDataExtension._get_render_scene_bu: Implement this in GDExtension to return the implementation's RenderSceneBuffers object.
m.RenderDataExtension._get_render_scene_da: Implement this in GDExtension to return the implementation's RenderSceneDataExtension object.
m.RenderSceneBuffers.configure: This method is called by the rendering server when the associated viewport's configuration is changed. It will discard the old buffers and recreate the internal buffers used.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.fsr_shar: FSR Sharpness applicable if FSR upscaling is used.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.internal: The size of the 3D render buffer used for rendering.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.msaa_3d: The MSAA mode we're using for 3D rendering.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.render_t: The render target associated with these buffer.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.scaling_: The requested scaling mode with which we upscale/downscale if internal_size and target_size are not equal.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.screen_s: The requested screen space AA applied in post processing.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.target_s: The target (upscale) size if scaling is used.
m.RenderSceneBuffersConfiguration.view_cou: The number of views we're rendering.
m.RenderSceneBuffersExtension._configure: Implement this in GDExtension to handle the (re)sizing of a viewport.
m.RenderSceneBuffersExtension._set_anisotr: Implement this in GDExtension to change the anisotropic filtering level.
m.RenderSceneBuffersExtension._set_fsr_sha: Implement this in GDExtension to record a new FSR sharpness value.
m.RenderSceneBuffersExtension._set_texture: Implement this in GDExtension to change the texture mipmap bias.
m.RenderSceneBuffersExtension._set_use_deb: Implement this in GDExtension to react to the debanding flag changing.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.clear_context: Frees all buffers related to this context.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.create_texture: Create a new texture with the given definition and cache this under the given name. Will return the existing texture if it already exists.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.create_texture_from: Create a new texture using the given format and view and cache this under the given name. Will return the existing texture if it already exists.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.create_texture_view: Create a new texture view for an existing texture and cache this under the given view_name. Will return the existing texture view if it already exists. Will error if the source texture doesn't exist.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_color_layer: Returns the specified layer from the color texture we are rendering 3D content to.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_color_texture: Returns the color texture we are rendering 3D content to. If multiview is used this will be a texture array with all views.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_depth_layer: Returns the specified layer from the depth texture we are rendering 3D content to.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_depth_texture: Returns the depth texture we are rendering 3D content to. If multiview is used this will be a texture array with all views.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_fsr_sharpness: Returns the FSR sharpness value used while rendering the 3D content (if get_scaling_3d_mode() is an FSR mode).
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_internal_size: Returns the internal size of the render buffer (size before upscaling) with which textures are created by default.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_msaa_3d: Returns the applied 3D MSAA mode for this viewport.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_render_target: Returns the render target associated with this buffers object.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_scaling_3d_mode: Returns the scaling mode used for upscaling.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_screen_space_aa: Returns the screen-space antialiasing method applied.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_target_size: Returns the target size of the render buffer (size after upscaling).
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_texture: Returns a cached texture with this name.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_texture_format: Returns the texture format information with which a cached texture was created.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_texture_samples: Returns the number of MSAA samples used.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_texture_slice: Returns a specific slice (layer or mipmap) for a cached texture.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_texture_slice_s: Returns the texture size of a given slice of a cached texture.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_texture_slice_v: Returns a specific view of a slice (layer or mipmap) for a cached texture.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_use_debanding: Returns true if debanding is enabled.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_use_taa: Returns true if TAA is enabled.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_velocity_layer: Returns the specified layer from the velocity texture we are rendering 3D content to.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_velocity_textur: Returns the velocity texture we are rendering 3D content to. If multiview is used this will be a texture array with all views.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.get_view_count: Returns the view count for the associated viewport.
m.RenderSceneBuffersRD.has_texture: Returns true if a cached texture exists for this name.
m.RenderSceneData.get_cam_projection: Returns the camera projection used to render this frame.
m.RenderSceneData.get_cam_transform: Returns the camera transform used to render this frame.
m.RenderSceneData.get_uniform_buffer: Return the RID of the uniform buffer containing the scene data as a UBO.
m.RenderSceneData.get_view_count: Returns the number of views being rendered.
m.RenderSceneData.get_view_eye_offset: Returns the eye offset per view used to render this frame. This is the offset between our camera transform and the eye transform.
m.RenderSceneData.get_view_projection: Returns the view projection per view used to render this frame.
m.RenderSceneDataExtension._get_cam_projec: Implement this in GDExtension to return the camera Projection.
m.RenderSceneDataExtension._get_cam_transf: Implement this in GDExtension to return the camera Transform3D.
m.RenderSceneDataExtension._get_uniform_bu: Implement this in GDExtension to return the RID of the uniform buffer containing the scene data as a UBO.
m.RenderSceneDataExtension._get_view_count: Implement this in GDExtension to return the view count.
m.RenderSceneDataExtension._get_view_eye_o: Implement this in GDExtension to return the eye offset for the given view.
m.RenderSceneDataExtension._get_view_proje: Implement this in GDExtension to return the view Projection for the given view.
