m.RenderingDevice.buffer_clear: Clears the contents of the buffer, clearing size_bytes bytes, starting at offset.
m.RenderingDevice.buffer_copy: Copies size bytes from the src_buffer at src_offset into dst_buffer at dst_offset.
m.RenderingDevice.buffer_get_data: Returns a copy of the data of the specified buffer, optionally offset_bytes and size_bytes can be set to copy only a portion of the buffer.
m.RenderingDevice.buffer_get_data_async: Asynchronous version of buffer_get_data(). RenderingDevice will call callback in a certain amount of frames with the data the buffer had at the time of the request.
m.RenderingDevice.buffer_get_device_addres: Returns the address of the given buffer which can be passed to shaders in any way to access underlying data. Buffer must have been created with this feature enabled.
m.RenderingDevice.buffer_update: Updates a region of size_bytes bytes, starting at offset, in the buffer, with the specified data.
m.RenderingDevice.capture_timestamp: Creates a timestamp marker with the specified name. This is used for performance reporting with the get_captured_timestamp_cpu_time(), get_captured_timestamp_gpu_time() and get_captured_timestamp_name() methods.
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_add_barrier: Raises a Vulkan compute barrier in the specified compute_list.
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_begin: Starts a list of compute commands created with the compute_* methods. The returned value should be passed to other compute_list_* functions.
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_bind_comput: Tells the GPU what compute pipeline to use when processing the compute list. If the shader has changed since the last time this function was called, Godot will unbind all descriptor sets and will re-bind them inside compute_list_dispatch().
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_bind_unifor: Binds the uniform_set to this compute_list. Godot ensures that all textures in the uniform set have the correct Vulkan access masks. If Godot had to change access masks of textures, it will raise a Vulkan image memory barrier.
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_dispatch: Submits the compute list for processing on the GPU. This is the compute equivalent to draw_list_draw().
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_dispatch_in: Submits the compute list for processing on the GPU with the given group counts stored in the buffer at offset. Buffer must have been created with STORAGE_BUFFER_USAGE_DISPATCH_INDIRECT flag.
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_end: Finishes a list of compute commands created with the compute_* methods.
m.RenderingDevice.compute_list_set_push_co: Sets the push constant data to buffer for the specified compute_list. The shader determines how this binary data is used. The buffer's size in bytes must also be specified in size_bytes (this can be obtained by calling the PackedByteArray.size() method on the passed buffer).
m.RenderingDevice.compute_pipeline_create: Creates a new compute pipeline. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.compute_pipeline_is_vali: Returns true if the compute pipeline specified by the compute_pipeline RID is valid, false otherwise.
m.RenderingDevice.create_local_device: Create a new local RenderingDevice. This is most useful for performing compute operations on the GPU independently from the rest of the engine.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_command_begin_label: Create a command buffer debug label region that can be displayed in third-party tools such as RenderDoc [https://renderdoc.org/]. All regions must be ended with a draw_command_end_label() call. When viewed from the linear series of submissions to a single queue, calls to draw_command_begin_label() and draw_command_end_label() must be matched and balanced.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_command_end_label: Ends the command buffer debug label region started by a draw_command_begin_label() call.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_command_insert_labe: Deprecated: Inserting labels no longer applies due to command reordering.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin: Starts a list of raster drawing commands created with the draw_* methods. The returned value should be passed to other draw_list_* functions.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin_for_scre: High-level variant of draw_list_begin(), with the parameters automatically being adjusted for drawing onto the window specified by the screen ID.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin_split: Deprecated: Split draw lists are used automatically by RenderingDevice.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_bind_index_arr: Binds index_array to the specified draw_list.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_bind_render_pi: Binds render_pipeline to the specified draw_list.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_bind_uniform_s: Binds uniform_set to the specified draw_list. A set_index must also be specified, which is an identifier starting from 0 that must match the one expected by the draw list.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_bind_vertex_ar: Binds vertex_array to the specified draw_list.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_bind_vertex_bu: Binds a set of vertex_buffers directly to the specified draw_list using vertex_format without creating a vertex array RID. Provide the number of vertices in vertex_count; optional per-buffer byte offsets may also be supplied.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_disable_scisso: Removes and disables the scissor rectangle for the specified draw_list. See also draw_list_enable_scissor().
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_draw: Submits draw_list for rendering on the GPU. This is the raster equivalent to compute_list_dispatch().
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_draw_indirect: Submits draw_list for rendering on the GPU with the given parameters stored in the buffer at offset. Parameters being integers: vertex count, instance count, first vertex, first instance. And when using indices: index count, instance count, first index, vertex offset, first instance. Buffer must have been created with STORAGE_BUFFER_USAGE_DISPATCH_INDIRECT flag.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_enable_scissor: Creates a scissor rectangle and enables it for the specified draw_list. Scissor rectangles are used for clipping by discarding fragments that fall outside a specified rectangular portion of the screen. See also draw_list_disable_scissor().
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_end: Finishes a list of raster drawing commands created with the draw_* methods.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_set_blend_cons: Sets blend constants for the specified draw_list to color. Blend constants are used only if the graphics pipeline is created with DYNAMIC_STATE_BLEND_CONSTANTS flag set.
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_set_push_const: Sets the push constant data to buffer for the specified draw_list. The shader determines how this binary data is used. The buffer's size in bytes must also be specified in size_bytes (this can be obtained by calling the PackedByteArray.size() method on the passed buffer).
m.RenderingDevice.draw_list_switch_to_next: Switches to the next draw pass.
Deprecated: Split draw lists are used automatically by RenderingDevice.
m.RenderingDevice.framebuffer_create: Creates a new framebuffer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.framebuffer_create_empty: Creates a new empty framebuffer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.framebuffer_create_multi: Creates a new multipass framebuffer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.framebuffer_format_creat: Creates a new framebuffer format with the specified attachments and view_count. Returns the new framebuffer's unique framebuffer format ID.
Creates a new empty framebuffer format with the specified number of samples and returns its ID.

Creates a multipass framebuffer format with the specified attachments, passes and view_count and returns its ID. If view_count is greater than or equal to 2, enables multiview which is used for VR rendering. This requires support for the Vulkan multiview extension.
m.RenderingDevice.framebuffer_format_get_t: Returns the number of texture samples used for the given framebuffer format ID (returned by framebuffer_get_format()).
m.RenderingDevice.framebuffer_get_format: Returns the format ID of the framebuffer specified by the framebuffer RID. This ID is guaranteed to be unique for the same formats and does not need to be freed.
m.RenderingDevice.framebuffer_is_valid: Returns true if the framebuffer specified by the framebuffer RID is valid, false otherwise.
m.RenderingDevice.free_rid: Tries to free an object in the RenderingDevice. To avoid memory leaks, this should be called after using an object as memory management does not occur automatically when using RenderingDevice directly.
m.RenderingDevice.full_barrier: Deprecated: Barriers are automatically inserted by RenderingDevice.
m.RenderingDevice.get_captured_timestamp_c: Returns the timestamp in CPU time for the rendering step specified by index (in microseconds since the engine started). See also get_captured_timestamp_gpu_time() and capture_timestamp().
m.RenderingDevice.get_captured_timestamp_g: Returns the timestamp in GPU time for the rendering step specified by index (in microseconds since the engine started). See also get_captured_timestamp_cpu_time() and capture_timestamp().
m.RenderingDevice.get_captured_timestamp_n: Returns the timestamp's name for the rendering step specified by index. See also capture_timestamp().
m.RenderingDevice.get_captured_timestamps_: Returns the total number of timestamps (rendering steps) available for profiling.
Returns the index of the last frame rendered that has rendering timestamps available for querying.
m.RenderingDevice.get_device_allocation_co: Returns how many allocations the GPU has performed for internal driver structures.
m.RenderingDevice.get_device_allocs_by_obj: Same as get_device_allocation_count() but filtered for a given object type.
m.RenderingDevice.get_device_memory_by_obj: Same as get_device_total_memory() but filtered for a given object type.
m.RenderingDevice.get_device_name: Returns the name of the video adapter (e.g. "GeForce GTX 1080/PCIe/SSE2"). Equivalent to RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_name(). See also get_device_vendor_name().
m.RenderingDevice.get_device_pipeline_cach: Returns the universally unique identifier for the pipeline cache. This is used to cache shader files on disk, which avoids shader recompilations on subsequent engine runs. This UUID varies depending on the graphics card model, but also the driver version. Therefore, updating graphics drivers will invalidate the shader cache.
m.RenderingDevice.get_device_total_memory: Returns how much bytes the GPU is using.
m.RenderingDevice.get_device_vendor_name: Returns the vendor of the video adapter (e.g. "NVIDIA Corporation"). Equivalent to RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_vendor(). See also get_device_name().
m.RenderingDevice.get_driver_allocation_co: Returns how many allocations the GPU driver has performed for internal driver structures.
m.RenderingDevice.get_driver_allocs_by_obj: Same as get_driver_allocation_count() but filtered for a given object type.
m.RenderingDevice.get_driver_and_device_me: Returns string report in CSV format using the following methods:
m.RenderingDevice.get_driver_memory_by_obj: Same as get_driver_total_memory() but filtered for a given object type.
m.RenderingDevice.get_driver_resource: Returns the unique identifier of the driver resource for the specified rid. Some driver resource types ignore the specified rid. index is always ignored but must be specified anyway.
m.RenderingDevice.get_driver_total_memory: Returns how much bytes the GPU driver is using for internal driver structures.
m.RenderingDevice.get_frame_delay: Returns the frame count kept by the graphics API. Higher values result in higher input lag, but with more consistent throughput. For the main RenderingDevice, frames are cycled (usually 3 with triple-buffered V-Sync enabled). However, local RenderingDevices only have 1 frame.
m.RenderingDevice.get_memory_usage: Returns the memory usage in bytes corresponding to the given type. When using Vulkan, these statistics are calculated by Vulkan Memory Allocator [https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator].
m.RenderingDevice.get_perf_report: Returns a string with a performance report from the past frame. Updates every frame.
m.RenderingDevice.get_tracked_object_name: Returns the name of the type of object for the given type_index. This value must be in range [0; get_tracked_object_type_count - 1]. If get_tracked_object_type_count() is 0, then type argument is ignored and always returns the same string.
m.RenderingDevice.get_tracked_object_type_: Returns how many types of trackable objects there are.
m.RenderingDevice.has_feature: Returns true if the feature is supported by the GPU.
m.RenderingDevice.hit_sbt_create: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.hit_sbt_range_alloc: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.hit_sbt_range_free: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.hit_sbt_range_update: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.hit_sbt_set_pipeline: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.index_array_create: Creates a new index array. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.index_buffer_create: Creates a new index buffer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.limit_get: Returns the value of the specified limit. This limit varies depending on the current graphics hardware (and sometimes the driver version). If the given limit is exceeded, rendering errors will occur.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_list_begin: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_list_bind_ray: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_list_bind_uni: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_list_end: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_list_set_push: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_list_trace_ra: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_pipeline_crea: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.raytracing_pipeline_is_v: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.render_pipeline_create: Creates a new render pipeline. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.render_pipeline_is_valid: Returns true if the render pipeline specified by the render_pipeline RID is valid, false otherwise.
m.RenderingDevice.sampler_create: Creates a new sampler. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.sampler_is_format_suppor: Returns true if implementation supports using a texture of format with the given sampler_filter.
m.RenderingDevice.screen_get_framebuffer_f: Returns the framebuffer format of the given screen.
m.RenderingDevice.screen_get_height: Returns the window height matching the graphics API context for the given window ID (in pixels). Despite the parameter being named screen, this returns the window size. See also screen_get_width().
m.RenderingDevice.screen_get_width: Returns the window width matching the graphics API context for the given window ID (in pixels). Despite the parameter being named screen, this returns the window size. See also screen_get_height().
m.RenderingDevice.set_resource_name: Sets the resource name for id to name. This is used for debugging with third-party tools such as RenderDoc [https://renderdoc.org/].
m.RenderingDevice.shader_compile_binary_fr: Compiles a binary shader from spirv_data and returns the compiled binary data as a PackedByteArray. This compiled shader is specific to the GPU model and driver version used; it will not work on different GPU models or even different driver versions. See also shader_compile_spirv_from_source().
m.RenderingDevice.shader_compile_spirv_fro: Compiles a SPIR-V from the shader source code in shader_source and returns the SPIR-V as an RDShaderSPIRV. This intermediate language shader is portable across different GPU models and driver versions, but cannot be run directly by GPUs until compiled into a binary shader using shader_compile_binary_from_spirv().
m.RenderingDevice.shader_create_from_bytec: Creates a new shader instance from a binary compiled shader. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.shader_create_from_spirv: Creates a new shader instance from SPIR-V intermediate code. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.shader_create_placeholde: Create a placeholder RID by allocating an RID without initializing it for use in shader_create_from_bytecode(). This allows you to create an RID for a shader and pass it around, but defer compiling the shader to a later time.
m.RenderingDevice.shader_get_vertex_input_: Returns the internal vertex input mask. Internally, the vertex input mask is an unsigned integer consisting of the locations (specified in GLSL via. layout(location = ...)) of the input variables (specified in GLSL by the in keyword).
m.RenderingDevice.storage_buffer_create: Creates a storage buffer [https://vkguide.dev/docs/chapter-4/storage_buffers/] with the specified data and usage. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.submit: Pushes the frame setup and draw command buffers then marks the local device as currently processing (which allows calling sync()).
m.RenderingDevice.sync: Forces a synchronization between the CPU and GPU, which may be required in certain cases. Only call this when needed, as CPU-GPU synchronization has a performance cost.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_buffer_create: Creates a new texture buffer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_clear: Clears the specified texture by replacing all of its pixels with the specified color. base_mipmap and mipmap_count determine which mipmaps of the texture are affected by this clear operation, while base_layer and layer_count determine which layers of a 3D texture (or texture array) are affected by this clear operation. For 2D textures (which only have one layer by design), base_layer must be 0 an…
m.RenderingDevice.texture_copy: Copies the from_texture to to_texture with the specified from_pos, to_pos and size coordinates. For 2-dimensional textures, from_pos and to_pos must have a Z axis of 0, and size must have a Z axis of 1. Source and destination mipmaps/layers must also be specified, with these parameters being 0 for textures without mipmaps or single-layer textures. Returns @GlobalScope.OK if the texture copy was s…
m.RenderingDevice.texture_create: Creates a new texture. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_create_from_exte: Returns an RID for an existing image (VkImage) with the given type, format, samples, usage_flags, width, height, depth, layers, and mipmaps. This can be used to allow Godot to render onto foreign images.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_create_shared: Creates a shared texture using the specified view and the texture information from with_texture.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_create_shared_fr: Creates a shared texture using the specified view and the texture information from with_texture's layer and mipmap. The number of included mipmaps from the original texture can be controlled using the mipmaps parameter. Only relevant for textures with multiple layers, such as 3D textures, texture arrays and cubemaps. For single-layer textures, use texture_create_shared().
m.RenderingDevice.texture_get_data: Returns the texture data for the specified layer as raw binary data. For 2D textures (which only have one layer), layer must be 0.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_get_data_async: Asynchronous version of texture_get_data(). RenderingDevice will call callback in a certain amount of frames with the data the texture had at the time of the request.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_get_format: Returns the data format used to create this texture.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_get_native_handl: Deprecated: Use get_driver_resource() with DRIVER_RESOURCE_TEXTURE instead.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_is_discardable: Returns true if the texture is discardable, false otherwise. See RDTextureFormat or texture_set_discardable().
m.RenderingDevice.texture_is_format_suppor: Returns true if the specified format is supported for the given usage_flags, false otherwise.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_is_shared: Returns true if the texture is shared, false otherwise. See RDTextureView.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_is_valid: Returns true if the texture is valid, false otherwise.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_resolve_multisam: Resolves the from_texture texture onto to_texture with multisample antialiasing enabled. This must be used when rendering a framebuffer for MSAA to work. Returns @GlobalScope.OK if successful, @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER otherwise.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_set_discardable: Updates the discardable property of texture.
m.RenderingDevice.texture_update: Updates texture data with new data, replacing the previous data in place. The updated texture data must have the same dimensions and format. For 2D textures (which only have one layer), layer must be 0. Returns @GlobalScope.OK if the update was successful, @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER otherwise.
m.RenderingDevice.tlas_build: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.tlas_create: Experimental: This method may be changed or removed in future versions.
m.RenderingDevice.uniform_buffer_create: Creates a new uniform buffer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.uniform_set_create: Creates a new uniform set. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.uniform_set_is_valid: Checks if the uniform_set is valid, i.e. is owned.
m.RenderingDevice.vertex_array_create: Creates a vertex array based on the specified buffers. Optionally, offsets (in bytes) may be defined for each buffer.
m.RenderingDevice.vertex_buffer_create: Creates a new vertex buffer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingDevice.vertex_format_create: Creates a new vertex format with the specified vertex_descriptions. Returns a unique vertex format ID corresponding to the newly created vertex format.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_COLOR: Array is a vertex color array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_COMPRESS_FLAGS_BAS: Shift of first compress flag. Compress flags should be passed to ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays() and SurfaceTool.commit().
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM0: Array is a custom data array for the first set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM1: Array is a custom data array for the second set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM2: Array is a custom data array for the third set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM3: Array is a custom data array for the fourth set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_MAX: Represents the size of the ArrayCustomFormat enum.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM: Custom data array contains 8-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are normalized, signed floating-point in the [-1.0, 1.0] range.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM: Custom data array contains 8-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are normalized, unsigned floating-point in the [0.0, 1.0] range.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_FLOAT: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF: Custom data array contains 16-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are floating-point in half precision.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGB_FLOAT: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red/green/blue color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_FLOAT: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red/green color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF: Custom data array contains 16-bit-per-channel red/green color data. Values are floating-point in half precision.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_CUSTOM_R_FLOAT: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FLAG_COMPRESS_ATTR: Flag used to mark that a mesh is using compressed attributes (vertices, normals, tangents, UVs). When this form of compression is enabled, vertex positions will be packed into an RGBA16UNORM attribute and scaled in the vertex shader. The normal and tangent will be packed into an RG16UNORM representing an axis, and a 16-bit float stored in the A-channel of the vertex. UVs will use 16-bit normalize…
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_CURREN: Flag used to record the current version that the engine expects. Currently this is the same as ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_2.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSIO: Flag used to record the format used by prior mesh versions before the introduction of a version.

Flag used to record the second iteration of the mesh version flag. The primary difference between this and ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_1 is that this version supports ARRAY_FLAG_COMPRESS_ATTRIBUTES and in this version vertex positions are de-interleaved from normals and tangents.
Flag used to mark the start of the bits used to store the mesh version.
Flag used to isolate the bits used for mesh version after using ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_SHIFT to shift them into place.
Flag used to shift a mesh format int to bring the version into the lowest digits.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FLAG_USES_EMPTY_VE: Flag used to mark that the mesh does not have a vertex array and instead will infer vertex positions in the shader using indices and other information.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FLAG_USE_2D_VERTIC: Flag used to mark that the array contains 2D vertices.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FLAG_USE_8_BONE_WE: Flag used to mark that the array uses 8 bone weights instead of 4.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FLAG_USE_DYNAMIC_U: Flag used to mark that the mesh data will use GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW on GLES. Unused on Vulkan.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_BLEND_SHAPE: Mask of mesh channels permitted in blend shapes.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_BONES: Flag used to mark a bone information array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_COLOR: Flag used to mark a vertex color array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM0: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the first set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM0_SHI: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 0.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM1: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the second set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM1_SHI: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 1.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM2: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the third set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM2_SHI: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 2.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM3: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the fourth set of custom data.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM3_SHI: Amount to shift ArrayCustomFormat for custom channel index 3.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_BITS: Number of format bits per custom channel. See ArrayCustomFormat.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_MASK: Mask of custom format bits per custom channel. Must be shifted by one of the SHIFT constants. See ArrayCustomFormat.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_INDEX: Flag used to mark an index array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_NORMAL: Flag used to mark a normal array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_TANGENT: Flag used to mark a tangent array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_TEX_UV: Flag used to mark a UV coordinates array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_TEX_UV2: Flag used to mark a UV coordinates array for the second UV coordinates.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_VERTEX: Flag used to mark a vertex position array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_FORMAT_WEIGHTS: Flag used to mark a weights array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_MAX: Represents the size of the ArrayType enum.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_TEX_UV: Array is a UV coordinates array.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_TEX_UV2: Array is a UV coordinates array for the second set of UV coordinates.
m.RenderingServer.ARRAY_VERTEX: Array is a vertex position array.
m.RenderingServer.BAKE_CHANNEL_ALBEDO_ALPH: Index of Image in array of Images returned by bake_render_uv2(). Image uses Image.FORMAT_RGBA8 and contains albedo color in the .rgb channels and alpha in the .a channel.
m.RenderingServer.BAKE_CHANNEL_EMISSION: Index of Image in array of Images returned by bake_render_uv2(). Image uses Image.FORMAT_RGBAH and contains emission color in the .rgb channels and nothing in the .a channel.
m.RenderingServer.BAKE_CHANNEL_NORMAL: Index of Image in array of Images returned by bake_render_uv2(). Image uses Image.FORMAT_RGBA8 and contains the per-pixel normal of the object in the .rgb channels and nothing in the .a channel. The per-pixel normal is encoded as normal * 0.5 + 0.5.
m.RenderingServer.BAKE_CHANNEL_ORM: Index of Image in array of Images returned by bake_render_uv2(). Image uses Image.FORMAT_RGBA8 and contains ambient occlusion (from material and decals only) in the .r channel, roughness in the .g channel, metallic in the .b channel and sub surface scattering amount in the .a channel.
m.RenderingServer.BLEND_SHAPE_MODE_RELATIV: Blend shapes are relative to base weight.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_CLIP_A: Parent is used for clipping child, but parent is also drawn underneath child as normal before clipping child to its visible area.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_CLIP_O: Parent is used for the purposes of clipping only. Child is clipped to the parent's visible area, parent is not drawn.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_DISABL: Child draws over parent and is not clipped.

m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILT: Uses the default filter mode for this Viewport.
The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance.

The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance.

The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPE: Uses the default repeat mode for this Viewport.
Disables textures repeating. Instead, when reading UVs outside the 0-1 range, the value will be clamped to the edge of the texture, resulting in a stretched out look at the borders of the texture.

Enables the texture to repeat when UV coordinates are outside the 0-1 range. If using one of the linear filtering modes, this can result in artifacts at the edges of a texture when the sampler filters across the edges of the texture.
Flip the texture when repeating so that the edge lines up instead of abruptly changing.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_LIGHT_BLEND_MODE_: Adds light color additive to the canvas.
The light adds color depending on transparency.
Adds light color subtractive to the canvas.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_MAX: Max value of the CanvasLightShadowFilter enum.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_NONE: Do not apply a filter to canvas light shadows.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_PCF1: Use PCF13 filtering to filter canvas light shadows.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_PCF5: Use PCF5 filtering to filter canvas light shadows.
m.RenderingServer.CANVAS_OCCLUDER_POLYGON_: Culling of the canvas occluder is clockwise.
Culling of the canvas occluder is counterclockwise.

m.RenderingServer.PIPELINE_SOURCE_SURFACE: Pipeline compilation that was triggered by building the surface cache before rendering the scene.
m.RenderingServer.PRIMITIVE_LINES: Primitive to draw consists of lines.
m.RenderingServer.PRIMITIVE_LINE_STRIP: Primitive to draw consists of a line strip from start to end.
m.RenderingServer.PRIMITIVE_MAX: Represents the size of the PrimitiveType enum.
m.RenderingServer.PRIMITIVE_POINTS: Primitive to draw consists of points.
m.RenderingServer.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES: Primitive to draw consists of triangles.
m.RenderingServer.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIP: Primitive to draw consists of a triangle strip (the last 3 vertices are always combined to make a triangle).
m.RenderingServer.REFLECTION_PROBE_AMBIENT: Apply custom ambient lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size. See reflection_probe_set_ambient_color() and reflection_probe_set_ambient_energy().
Do not apply any ambient lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size.
Apply automatically-sourced environment lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size.
m.RenderingServer.REFLECTION_PROBE_UPDATE_: Reflection probe will update each frame. This mode is necessary to capture moving objects.
Reflection probe will update reflections once and then stop.
m.RenderingServer.RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_ME: Buffer memory used (in bytes). This includes vertex data, uniform buffers, and many miscellaneous buffer types used internally.
m.RenderingServer.RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by the 2D canvas renderer.

Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered while drawing the scene. These compilations will show up as stutters during gameplay the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.
Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by loading meshes. These compilations will show up as longer loading times the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.
Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered to optimize the current scene. These compilations are done in the background and should not cause any stutters whatsoever.

Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by building the surface cache before rendering the scene. These compilations will show up as a stutter when loading a scene the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.
m.RenderingServer.RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_DRA: Number of draw calls performed to render in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.
m.RenderingServer.RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_OBJ: Number of objects rendered in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.
m.RenderingServer.RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_PRI: Number of points, lines, or triangles rendered in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.
m.RenderingServer.RENDERING_INFO_VIDEO_MEM: Video memory used (in bytes). When using the Forward+ or Mobile renderers, this is always greater than the sum of RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED and RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED, since there is miscellaneous data not accounted for by those two metrics. When using the Compatibility renderer, this is equal to the sum of RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED and RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED.
m.RenderingServer.SHADER_MAX: Represents the size of the ShaderMode enum.
m.RenderingServer.SHADER_PARTICLES: Shader is a particle shader (can be used in both 2D and 3D).
m.RenderingServer.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_D: Disable backface culling when rendering the shadow of the object. This is slightly slower but may result in more correct shadows.
m.RenderingServer.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_S: Only render the shadows from the object. The object itself will not be drawn.
m.RenderingServer.SHADOW_QUALITY_HARD: Lowest shadow filtering quality (fastest). Soft shadows are not available with this quality setting, which means the Light3D.shadow_blur property is ignored if Light3D.light_size and Light3D.light_angular_distance is 0.0.
m.RenderingServer.SHADOW_QUALITY_MAX: Represents the size of the ShadowQuality enum.
m.RenderingServer.SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_HIGH: High low shadow filtering quality (slow). When using this quality setting, Light3D.shadow_blur is automatically multiplied by 1.5× to better make use of the high sample count. This increased blur also improves the stability of dynamic object shadows. This multiplier only applies to lights whose Light3D.light_size or Light3D.light_angular_distance is 0.0).
m.RenderingServer.SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_ULTR: Highest low shadow filtering quality (slowest). When using this quality setting, Light3D.shadow_blur is automatically multiplied by 2× to better make use of the high sample count. This increased blur also improves the stability of dynamic object shadows. This multiplier only applies to lights whose Light3D.light_size or Light3D.light_angular_distance is 0.0).
m.RenderingServer.SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_VERY: Very low shadow filtering quality (faster). When using this quality setting, Light3D.shadow_blur is automatically multiplied by 0.75× to avoid introducing too much noise. This division only applies to lights whose Light3D.light_size or Light3D.light_angular_distance is 0.0).
m.RenderingServer.SKY_MODE_AUTOMATIC: Automatically selects the appropriate process mode based on your sky shader. If your shader uses TIME or POSITION, this will use SKY_MODE_REALTIME. If your shader uses any of the LIGHT_* variables or any custom uniforms, this uses SKY_MODE_INCREMENTAL. Otherwise, this defaults to SKY_MODE_QUALITY.
m.RenderingServer.SKY_MODE_INCREMENTAL: Uses the same high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map as SKY_MODE_QUALITY, but updates over several frames. The number of frames is determined by ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers. Use this when you need highest quality radiance maps, but have a sky that updates slowly.
m.RenderingServer.SKY_MODE_QUALITY: Uses high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map. In general, this results in much higher quality than SKY_MODE_REALTIME but takes much longer to generate. This should not be used if you plan on changing the sky at runtime. If you are finding that the reflection is not blurry enough and is showing sparkles or fireflies, try increasing ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_ref…
m.RenderingServer.SKY_MODE_REALTIME: Uses the fast filtering algorithm to process the radiance map. In general this results in lower quality, but substantially faster run times. If you need better quality, but still need to update the sky every frame, consider turning on ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/fast_filter_high_quality.
m.RenderingServer.SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_COVE: Stretches the image to cover the entire screen while preserving aspect ratio.
m.RenderingServer.SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_IGNO: Stretches the image to cover the entire screen but doesn't preserve aspect ratio.
m.RenderingServer.SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_KEEP: Stretches image to fullscreen while preserving aspect ratio.
Stretches the width of the image based on the height of the screen.
Stretches the height of the image based on the width of the screen.
m.RenderingServer.SUB_SURFACE_SCATTERING_Q: Disables subsurface scattering entirely, even on materials that have BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_enabled set to true. This has the lowest GPU requirements.
High subsurface scattering quality. This has the highest GPU requirements.
m.RenderingServer.TEXTURE_DRAWABLE_FORMAT_: OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 8.
OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 8.
OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA32F where there are four components, each a 32-bit floating-point value.
OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA16F where there are four components, each a 16-bit "half-precision" floating-point value.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_4X: Use 4× anisotropic filtering. This is the default value.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_MAX: Represents the size of the ViewportAnisotropicFiltering enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_CLEAR_ALWAYS: Always clear the viewport's render target before drawing.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_CLEAR_NEVER: Never clear the viewport's render target.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_CLEAR_ONLY_NEXT: Clear the viewport's render target on the next frame, then switch to VIEWPORT_CLEAR_NEVER.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUS: Draws the Decal cluster. Clustering determines where decals are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for decals.
Draws the OmniLight3D cluster. Clustering determines where lights are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for lighting.

Draws the ReflectionProbe cluster. Clustering determines where reflection probes are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for reflection probes.
Draws the SpotLight3D cluster. Clustering determines where lights are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for lighting.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DECA: Draws the decal atlas that stores decal textures from Decals.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DIRE: Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from DirectionalLight3Ds in the upper left quadrant of the Viewport.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DISA: Debug draw is disabled. Default setting.
Disable mesh LOD. All meshes are drawn with full detail, which can be used to compare performance.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_GI_B: Draws the global illumination buffer from VoxelGI or SDFGI. Requires VoxelGI (at least one visible baked VoxelGI node) or SDFGI (Environment.sdfgi_enabled) to be enabled to have a visible effect.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_INTE: Internal buffer is drawn instead of regular scene so you can see the per-pixel output that will be used by post-processing effects.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_LIGH: Objects are displayed with only light information.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_MOTI: Draws the motion vectors buffer. This is used by temporal antialiasing to correct for motion that occurs during gameplay.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_NORM: Normal buffer is drawn instead of regular scene so you can see the per-pixel normals that will be used by post-processing effects.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_OCCL: Draws the occlusion culling buffer. This low-resolution occlusion culling buffer is rasterized on the CPU and is used to check whether instances are occluded by other objects.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_OVER: Objects are displayed semi-transparent with additive blending so you can see where they are drawing over top of one another. A higher overdraw (represented by brighter colors) means you are wasting performance on drawing pixels that are being hidden behind others.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_PSSM: Colors each PSSM split for the DirectionalLight3Ds in the scene a different color so you can see where the splits are. In order (from closest to furthest from the camera), they are colored red, green, blue, and yellow.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SCEN: Draws the estimated scene luminance. This is a 1×1 texture that is generated when autoexposure is enabled to control the scene's exposure.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SDFG: Draws SDFGI cascade data. This is the data structure that is used to bounce lighting against and create reflections.
Draws SDFGI probe data. This is the data structure that is used to give indirect lighting dynamic objects moving within the scene.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SHAD: Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from OmniLight3Ds and SpotLight3Ds in the upper left quadrant of the Viewport.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SSAO: Draws the screen space ambient occlusion texture instead of the scene so that you can clearly see how it is affecting objects. In order for this display mode to work, you must have Environment.ssao_enabled set in your WorldEnvironment.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SSIL: Draws the screen space indirect lighting texture instead of the scene so that you can clearly see how it is affecting objects. In order for this display mode to work, you must have Environment.ssil_enabled set in your WorldEnvironment.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_UNSH: Objects are displayed without light information.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_VOXE: Objects are displayed with only the albedo value from VoxelGIs. Requires at least one visible VoxelGI node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
Objects are displayed with only the emission color from VoxelGIs. Requires at least one visible VoxelGI node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
Objects are displayed with only the lighting value from VoxelGIs. Requires at least one visible VoxelGI node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_WIRE: Debug draw draws objects in wireframe.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_DIS: Disable rendering of 3D environment over 2D canvas.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_ENA: Enable rendering of 3D environment over 2D canvas.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_INH: Inherit enable/disable value from parent. If the topmost parent is also set to VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_INHERIT, then this has the same behavior as VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_ENABLED.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_MAX: Represents the size of the ViewportEnvironmentMode enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_MSAA_2X: Multisample antialiasing uses 2 samples per pixel for 3D. This has a moderate impact on performance.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_MSAA_4X: Multisample antialiasing uses 4 samples per pixel for 3D. This has a high impact on performance.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_MSAA_8X: Multisample antialiasing uses 8 samples per pixel for 3D. This has a very high impact on performance. Likely unsupported on low-end and older hardware.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_MSAA_DISABLED: Multisample antialiasing for 3D is disabled. This is the default value, and also the fastest setting.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_MSAA_MAX: Represents the size of the ViewportMSAA enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_OCCLUSION_BUILD: High occlusion culling BVH build quality (as defined by Embree). Results in the highest CPU usage, but most effective culling.
Low occlusion culling BVH build quality (as defined by Embree). Results in the lowest CPU usage, but least effective culling.
Medium occlusion culling BVH build quality (as defined by Embree).
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_DRA: Number of draw calls during this frame.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_MAX: Represents the size of the ViewportRenderInfo enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_OBJ: Number of objects drawn in a single frame.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_PRI: Number of points, lines, or triangles drawn in a single frame.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_TYP: Canvas item rendering. This includes all 2D rendering.
Represents the size of the ViewportRenderInfoType enum.
Shadow render pass. Objects will be rendered several times depending on the number of amounts of lights with shadows and the number of directional shadow splits.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE: Use bilinear scaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using Viewport.scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in undersampling while values greater than 1.0 will result in supersampling. A value of 1.0 disables scaling.

Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using Viewport.scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in the viewport being upscaled using FSR. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 disables scaling.

Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2.2 upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using Viewport.scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in the viewport being upscaled using FSR2. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 will use FSR2 at native resolution as a TAA solution.
Represents the size of the ViewportScaling3DMode enum.

Use MetalFX spatial upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using Viewport.scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in the viewport being upscaled using MetalFX. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 disables scaling.

Use MetalFX temporal upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using Viewport.scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in the viewport being upscaled using MetalFX. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 will use MetalFX at native resolution as a TAA solution.

Use nearest-neighbor filtering for the viewport's 3D buffer. This looks crisper than VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_BILINEAR and has no additional rendering cost. The amount of scaling can be set using Viewport.scaling_3d_scale. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 disables scaling.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SCREEN_SPACE_AA: Do not perform any antialiasing in the full screen post-process.

Use fast approximate antialiasing. FXAA is a popular screen-space antialiasing method, which is fast but will make the image look blurry, especially at lower resolutions. It can still work relatively well at large resolutions such as 1440p and 4K.
Represents the size of the ViewportScreenSpaceAA enum.
Use subpixel morphological antialiasing. SMAA may produce clearer results than FXAA, but at a slightly higher performance cost.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_10: Do not oversize the 2D signed distance field. Occluders may disappear when touching the viewport's edges, and GPUParticles3D collision may stop working earlier than intended. This has the lowest GPU requirements.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_12: 2D signed distance field covers 20% of the viewport's size outside the viewport on each side (top, right, bottom, left).
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_15: 2D signed distance field covers 50% of the viewport's size outside the viewport on each side (top, right, bottom, left).
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_20: 2D signed distance field covers 100% of the viewport's size outside the viewport on each side (top, right, bottom, left). This has the highest GPU requirements.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_MA: Represents the size of the ViewportSDFOversize enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_100_P: Full resolution 2D signed distance field scale. This has the highest GPU requirements.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_25_PE: Quarter resolution 2D signed distance field scale on each axis (6.25% of the viewport pixel count). This has the lowest GPU requirements.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_50_PE: Half resolution 2D signed distance field scale on each axis (25% of the viewport pixel count).
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_MAX: Represents the size of the ViewportSDFScale enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_UPDATE_ALWAYS: Always update the viewport's render target.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_UPDATE_DISABLED: Do not update the viewport's render target.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_UPDATE_ONCE: Update the viewport's render target once, then switch to VIEWPORT_UPDATE_DISABLED.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_PAR: Update the viewport's render target only when its parent is visible.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_VIS: Update the viewport's render target only when it is visible. This is the default value.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_VRS_MAX: Represents the size of the ViewportVRSMode enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_VRS_TEXTURE: Variable rate shading uses a texture. Note, for stereoscopic use a texture atlas with a texture for each view.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_ALWA: The input texture for variable rate shading will be processed each frame.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_DISA: The input texture for variable rate shading will not be processed.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_MAX: Represents the size of the ViewportVRSUpdateMode enum.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_ONCE: The input texture for variable rate shading will be processed once.
m.RenderingServer.VIEWPORT_VRS_XR: Variable rate shading texture is supplied by the primary XRInterface. Note that this may override the update mode.
m.RenderingServer.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DE: Fade-in the given instance's dependencies when reaching its visibility range limits.
m.RenderingServer.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DI: Disable visibility range fading for the given instance.
m.RenderingServer.VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_SE: Fade-out the given instance when it approaches its visibility range limits.
m.RenderingServer.VOXEL_GI_QUALITY_HIGH: High VoxelGI rendering quality using 6 cones.
m.RenderingServer.VOXEL_GI_QUALITY_LOW: Low VoxelGI rendering quality using 4 cones.
m.RenderingServer.area_light_create: Creates a new area light and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID can be used in most light_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.bake_render_uv2: Bakes the material data of the Mesh passed in the base parameter with optional material_overrides to a set of Images of size image_size. Returns an array of Images containing material properties as specified in BakeChannels.
m.RenderingServer.call_on_render_thread: As the RenderingServer actual logic may run on a separate thread, accessing its internals from the main (or any other) thread will result in errors. To make it easier to run code that can safely access the rendering internals (such as RenderingDevice and similar RD classes), push a callable via this function so it will be executed on the render thread.
m.RenderingServer.camera_attributes_create: Creates a camera attributes object and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all camera_attributes_ RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.camera_attributes_set_au: Sets the parameters to use with the auto-exposure effect. These parameters take on the same meaning as their counterparts in CameraAttributes and CameraAttributesPractical.
m.RenderingServer.camera_attributes_set_do: Sets the parameters to use with the DOF blur effect. These parameters take on the same meaning as their counterparts in CameraAttributesPractical.
Sets the shape of the DOF bokeh pattern to shape. Different shapes may be used to achieve artistic effect, or to meet performance targets.
Sets the quality level of the DOF blur effect to quality. use_jitter can be used to jitter samples taken during the blur pass to hide artifacts at the cost of looking more fuzzy.
m.RenderingServer.camera_attributes_set_ex: Sets the exposure values that will be used by the renderers. The normalization amount is used to bake a given Exposure Value (EV) into rendering calculations to reduce the dynamic range of the scene.
m.RenderingServer.camera_create: Creates a 3D camera and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all camera_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_camera_attrib: Sets the camera_attributes created with camera_attributes_create() to the given camera.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_compositor: Sets the compositor used by this camera. Equivalent to Camera3D.compositor.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_cull_mask: Sets the cull mask associated with this camera. The cull mask describes which 3D layers are rendered by this camera. Equivalent to Camera3D.cull_mask.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_environment: Sets the environment used by this camera. Equivalent to Camera3D.environment.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_frustum: Sets camera to use frustum projection. This mode allows adjusting the offset argument to create "tilted frustum" effects.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_orthogonal: Sets camera to use orthogonal projection, also known as orthographic projection. Objects remain the same size on the screen no matter how far away they are.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_perspective: Sets camera to use perspective projection. Objects on the screen becomes smaller when they are far away.
m.RenderingServer.camera_set_use_vertical_: If true, preserves the horizontal aspect ratio which is equivalent to Camera3D.KEEP_WIDTH. If false, preserves the vertical aspect ratio which is equivalent to Camera3D.KEEP_HEIGHT.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_create: Creates a canvas and returns the assigned RID. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all canvas_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_animatio: Subsequent drawing commands will be ignored unless they fall within the specified animation slice. This is a faster way to implement animations that loop on background rather than redrawing constantly.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_circle: Draws a circle on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_circle().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_clip_ign: If ignore is true, ignore clipping on items drawn with this canvas item until this is called again with ignore set to false.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_ellipse: Draws an ellipse with semi-major axis major and semi-minor axis minor on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_ellipse().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_line: Draws a line on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_line().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_mesh: Draws a mesh created with mesh_create() with given transform, modulate color, and texture. This is used internally by MeshInstance2D.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_multilin: Draws a 2D multiline on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_multiline() and CanvasItem.draw_multiline_colors().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_multimes: Draws a 2D MultiMesh on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_multimesh().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_nine_pat: Draws a nine-patch rectangle on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_particle: Draws particles on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_polygon: Draws a 2D polygon on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. If you need more flexibility (such as being able to use bones), use canvas_item_add_triangle_array() instead. See also CanvasItem.draw_polygon().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_polyline: Draws a 2D polyline on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_polyline() and CanvasItem.draw_polyline_colors().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_primitiv: Draws a 2D primitive on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_primitive().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_rect: Draws a rectangle on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_rect().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_set_tran: Sets a Transform2D that will be used to transform subsequent canvas item commands.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_texture_: Draws a 2D textured rectangle on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_texture_rect() and Texture2D.draw_rect().
Draws the specified region of a 2D textured rectangle on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. See also CanvasItem.draw_texture_rect_region() and Texture2D.draw_rect_region().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_triangle: Draws a triangle array on the CanvasItem pointed to by the item RID. This is internally used by Line2D and StyleBoxFlat for rendering. canvas_item_add_triangle_array() is highly flexible, but more complex to use than canvas_item_add_polygon().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_attach_skele: Attaches a skeleton to the CanvasItem. Removes the previous skeleton.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_clear: Clears the CanvasItem and removes all commands in it.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_create: Creates a new CanvasItem instance and returns its RID. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all canvas_item_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_get_instance: Returns the value of the per-instance shader uniform from the specified canvas item instance. Equivalent to CanvasItem.get_instance_shader_parameter().
Returns the default value of the per-instance shader uniform from the specified canvas item instance. Equivalent to CanvasItem.get_instance_shader_parameter().
Returns a dictionary of per-instance shader uniform names of the per-instance shader uniform from the specified canvas item instance.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_reset_physic: Prevents physics interpolation for the current physics tick.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_canvas_g: Sets the canvas group mode used during 2D rendering for the canvas item specified by the item RID. For faster but more limited clipping, use canvas_item_set_clip() instead.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_clip: If clip is true, makes the canvas item specified by the item RID not draw anything outside of its rect's coordinates. This clipping is fast, but works only with axis-aligned rectangles. This means that rotation is ignored by the clipping rectangle. For more advanced clipping shapes, use canvas_item_set_canvas_group_mode() instead.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_copy_to_: Sets the CanvasItem to copy a rect to the backbuffer.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_custom_r: If use_custom_rect is true, sets the custom visibility rectangle (used for culling) to rect for the canvas item specified by item. Setting a custom visibility rect can reduce CPU load when drawing lots of 2D instances. If use_custom_rect is false, automatically computes a visibility rectangle based on the canvas item's draw commands.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_default_: Sets the default texture filter mode for the canvas item specified by the item RID. Equivalent to CanvasItem.texture_filter.
Sets the default texture repeat mode for the canvas item specified by the item RID. Equivalent to CanvasItem.texture_repeat.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_distance: If enabled is true, enables multichannel signed distance field rendering mode for the canvas item specified by the item RID. This is meant to be used for font rendering, or with specially generated images using msdfgen [https://github.com/Chlumsky/msdfgen].
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_draw_beh: If enabled is true, draws the canvas item specified by the item RID behind its parent. Equivalent to CanvasItem.show_behind_parent.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_draw_ind: Sets the index for the CanvasItem.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_instance: Sets the per-instance shader uniform on the specified canvas item instance. Equivalent to CanvasItem.set_instance_shader_parameter().
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_interpol: If interpolated is true, turns on physics interpolation for the canvas item.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_light_ma: Sets the light mask for the canvas item specified by the item RID. Equivalent to CanvasItem.light_mask.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_material: Sets a new material to the canvas item specified by the item RID. Equivalent to CanvasItem.material.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_modulate: Multiplies the color of the canvas item specified by the item RID, while affecting its children. See also canvas_item_set_self_modulate(). Equivalent to CanvasItem.modulate.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_parent: Sets a parent CanvasItem to the CanvasItem. The item will inherit transform, modulation and visibility from its parent, like CanvasItem nodes in the scene tree.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_self_mod: Multiplies the color of the canvas item specified by the item RID, without affecting its children. See also canvas_item_set_modulate(). Equivalent to CanvasItem.self_modulate.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_sort_chi: If enabled is true, child nodes with the lowest Y position are drawn before those with a higher Y position. Y-sorting only affects children that inherit from the canvas item specified by the item RID, not the canvas item itself. Equivalent to CanvasItem.y_sort_enabled.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_transfor: Sets the transform of the canvas item specified by the item RID. This affects where and how the item will be drawn. Child canvas items' transforms are multiplied by their parent's transform. Equivalent to Node2D.transform.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_use_pare: Sets if the CanvasItem uses its parent's material.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_visibili: Sets the rendering visibility layer associated with this CanvasItem. Only Viewport nodes with a matching rendering mask will render this CanvasItem.

Sets the given CanvasItem as visibility notifier. area defines the area of detecting visibility. enter_callable is called when the CanvasItem enters the screen, exit_callable is called when the CanvasItem exits the screen. If enable is false, the item will no longer function as notifier.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_visible: Sets the visibility of the CanvasItem.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_z_as_rel: If this is enabled, the Z index of the parent will be added to the children's Z index.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_z_index: Sets the CanvasItem's Z index, i.e. its draw order (lower indexes are drawn first).
m.RenderingServer.canvas_item_transform_ph: Transforms both the current and previous stored transform for a canvas item.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_attach_to_c: Attaches the canvas light to the canvas. Removes it from its previous canvas.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_create: Creates a canvas light and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all canvas_light_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_occluder_at: Attaches a light occluder to the canvas. Removes it from its previous canvas.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_occluder_cr: Creates a light occluder and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all canvas_light_occluder_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_occluder_re: Prevents physics interpolation for the current physics tick.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_occluder_se: Enables or disables using the light occluder as a signed distance field for 2D particle collision.
If interpolated is true, turns on physics interpolation for the light occluder.
The light mask. See LightOccluder2D for more information on light masks.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_occluder_tr: Transforms both the current and previous stored transform for a light occluder.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_reset_physi: Prevents physics interpolation for the current physics tick.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_blend_m: Sets the blend mode for the given canvas light to mode. Equivalent to Light2D.blend_mode.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_color: Sets the color for a light.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_enabled: Enables or disables a canvas light.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_interpo: If interpolated is true, turns on physics interpolation for the canvas light.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_item_cu: The light mask. See LightOccluder2D for more information on light masks.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_item_sh: The binary mask used to determine which layers this canvas light's shadows affects. See LightOccluder2D for more information on light masks.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_layer_r: The layer range that gets rendered with this light.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_mode: Sets the mode of the canvas light.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_shadow_: Sets the color of the canvas light's shadow.
Enables or disables the canvas light's shadow.
Sets the canvas light's shadow's filter.
Smoothens the shadow. The lower, the smoother.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_texture: Sets the texture to be used by a PointLight2D. Equivalent to PointLight2D.texture.
Sets the offset of a PointLight2D's texture. Equivalent to PointLight2D.offset.
Sets the scale factor of a PointLight2D's texture. Equivalent to PointLight2D.texture_scale.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_set_z_range: Sets the Z range of objects that will be affected by this light. Equivalent to Light2D.range_z_min and Light2D.range_z_max.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_light_transform_p: Transforms both the current and previous stored transform for a canvas light.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_occluder_polygon_: Creates a new light occluder polygon and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all canvas_occluder_polygon_* RenderingServer functions.
Sets an occluder polygon's cull mode.
Sets the shape of the occluder polygon.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_set_disable_scale: If disable is true, makes 2D rendering ignore the canvas scale defined for each canvas layer. This affects CanvasLayers with the CanvasLayer.follow_viewport_enabled property set to true.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_set_item_mirrorin: A copy of the canvas item will be drawn with a local offset of the mirroring.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_set_item_repeat: A copy of the canvas item will be drawn with a local offset of the repeat_size by the number of times of the repeat_times. As the repeat_times increases, the copies will spread away from the origin texture.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_set_modulate: Modulates all colors in the given canvas.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_set_shadow_textur: Sets the ProjectSettings.rendering/2d/shadow_atlas/size to use for Light2D shadow rendering (in pixels). The value is rounded up to the nearest power of 2.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_texture_create: Creates a canvas texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all canvas_texture_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_texture_set_chann: Sets the channel's texture for the canvas texture specified by the canvas_texture RID. Equivalent to CanvasTexture.diffuse_texture, CanvasTexture.normal_texture and CanvasTexture.specular_texture.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_texture_set_shadi: Sets the base_color and shininess to use for the canvas texture specified by the canvas_texture RID. Equivalent to CanvasTexture.specular_color and CanvasTexture.specular_shininess.
m.RenderingServer.canvas_texture_set_textu: Sets the texture filter mode to use for the canvas texture specified by the canvas_texture RID.
Sets the texture repeat mode to use for the canvas texture specified by the canvas_texture RID.
m.RenderingServer.compositor_create: Creates a new compositor and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingServer.compositor_effect_create: Creates a new rendering effect and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned.
m.RenderingServer.compositor_effect_set_ca: Sets the callback type (callback_type) and callback method(callback) for this rendering effect.
m.RenderingServer.compositor_effect_set_fl: Sets the flag (flag) for this rendering effect to true or false (set).
m.RenderingServer.compositor_set_composito: Sets the compositor effects for the specified compositor RID. effects should be an array containing RIDs created with compositor_effect_create().
m.RenderingServer.create_local_rendering_d: Creates a RenderingDevice that can be used to do draw and compute operations on a separate thread. Cannot draw to the screen nor share data with the global RenderingDevice.
m.RenderingServer.debug_canvas_item_get_re: Returns the bounding rectangle for a canvas item in local space, as calculated by the renderer. This bound is used internally for culling.
m.RenderingServer.decal_create: Creates a decal and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all decal_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_albedo_mix: Sets the albedo_mix in the decal specified by the decal RID. Equivalent to Decal.albedo_mix.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_cull_mask: Sets the cull mask in the decal specified by the decal RID. Equivalent to Decal.cull_mask.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_distance_fade: Sets the distance fade parameters in the decal specified by the decal RID. Equivalent to Decal.distance_fade_enabled, Decal.distance_fade_begin and Decal.distance_fade_length.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_emission_energ: Sets the emission energy in the decal specified by the decal RID. Equivalent to Decal.emission_energy.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_fade: Sets the upper fade (above) and lower fade (below) in the decal specified by the decal RID. Equivalent to Decal.upper_fade and Decal.lower_fade.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_modulate: Sets the color multiplier in the decal specified by the decal RID to color. Equivalent to Decal.modulate.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_normal_fade: Sets the normal fade in the decal specified by the decal RID. Equivalent to Decal.normal_fade.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_size: Sets the size of the decal specified by the decal RID. Equivalent to Decal.size.
m.RenderingServer.decal_set_texture: Sets the texture in the given texture type slot for the specified decal. Equivalent to Decal.set_texture().
m.RenderingServer.decals_set_filter: Sets the texture filter mode to use when rendering decals. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-decal basis.
m.RenderingServer.directional_light_create: Creates a directional light and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID can be used in most light_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.directional_shadow_atlas: Sets the size of the directional light shadows in 3D. See also ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/size. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-viewport basis.
m.RenderingServer.directional_soft_shadow_: Sets the filter quality for directional light shadows in 3D. See also ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/soft_shadow_filter_quality. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-viewport basis.
m.RenderingServer.environment_bake_panoram: Generates and returns an Image containing the radiance map for the specified environment RID's sky. This supports built-in sky material and custom sky shaders. If bake_irradiance is true, the irradiance map is saved instead of the radiance map. The radiance map is used to render reflected light, while the irradiance map is used to render ambient light. See also sky_bake_panorama().
m.RenderingServer.environment_create: Creates an environment and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all environment_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.environment_glow_set_use: If enable is true, enables bicubic upscaling for glow which improves quality at the cost of performance. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/glow/upscale_mode.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_adjustme: Sets the values to be used with the "adjustments" post-process effect. See Environment for more details.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_ambient_: Sets the values to be used for ambient light rendering. See Environment for more details.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_backgrou: Sets the environment's background mode. Equivalent to Environment.background_mode.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_bg_color: Color displayed for clear areas of the scene. Only effective if using the ENV_BG_COLOR background mode.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_bg_energ: Sets the intensity of the background color.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_camera_i: Sets the camera ID to be used as environment background.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_canvas_m: Sets the maximum layer to use if using Canvas background mode.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_fog: Configures fog for the specified environment RID. See fog_* properties in Environment for more information.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_fog_dept: Configures fog depth for the specified environment RID. Only has an effect when the fog mode of the environment is ENV_FOG_MODE_DEPTH. See fog_depth_* properties in Environment for more information.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_glow: Configures glow for the specified environment RID. See glow_* properties in Environment for more information.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_sdfgi: Configures signed distance field global illumination for the specified environment RID. See sdfgi_* properties in Environment for more information.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_sdfgi_fr: Sets the number of frames to use for converging signed distance field global illumination. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/sdfgi/frames_to_converge.

Sets the update speed for dynamic lights' indirect lighting when computing signed distance field global illumination. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/sdfgi/frames_to_update_lights.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_sdfgi_ra: Sets the number of rays to throw per frame when computing signed distance field global illumination. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/sdfgi/probe_ray_count.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_sky: Sets the Sky to be used as the environment's background when using BGMode sky. Equivalent to Environment.sky.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_sky_cust: Sets a custom field of view for the background Sky. Equivalent to Environment.sky_custom_fov.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_sky_orie: Sets the rotation of the background Sky expressed as a Basis. Equivalent to Environment.sky_rotation, where the rotation vector is used to construct the Basis.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_ssao: Sets the variables to be used with the screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO) post-process effect. See Environment for more details.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_ssao_qua: Sets the quality level of the screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO) post-process effect. See Environment for more details.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_ssil_qua: Sets the quality level of the screen-space indirect lighting (SSIL) post-process effect. See Environment for more details.
