m.RenderingServer.environment_set_ssr: Sets the variables to be used with the screen-space reflections (SSR) post-process effect. See Environment for more details.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_ssr_half: Sets whether screen-space reflections will be rendered at full or half size. Half size is faster, but may look pixelated or cause flickering.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_ssr_roug: Deprecated: This option no longer does anything.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_tonemap: Sets the variables to be used with the "tonemap" post-process effect. See Environment for more details.
m.RenderingServer.environment_set_volumetr: Sets the variables to be used with the volumetric fog post-process effect. See Environment for more details.
Enables filtering of the volumetric fog scattering buffer. This results in much smoother volumes with very few under-sampling artifacts.

Sets the resolution of the volumetric fog's froxel buffer. size is modified by the screen's aspect ratio and then used to set the width and height of the buffer. While depth is directly used to set the depth of the buffer.
m.RenderingServer.fog_volume_create: Creates a new fog volume and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all fog_volume_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.fog_volume_set_material: Sets the Material of the fog volume. Can be either a FogMaterial or a custom ShaderMaterial.
m.RenderingServer.fog_volume_set_shape: Sets the shape of the fog volume to either FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_ELLIPSOID, FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CONE, FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CYLINDER, FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_BOX or FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_WORLD.
m.RenderingServer.fog_volume_set_size: Sets the size of the fog volume when shape is FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_ELLIPSOID, FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CONE, FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CYLINDER or FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_BOX.
m.RenderingServer.force_draw: Forces redrawing of all viewports at once. Must be called from the main thread.
m.RenderingServer.force_sync: Forces a synchronization between the CPU and GPU, which may be required in certain cases. Only call this when needed, as CPU-GPU synchronization has a performance cost.
m.RenderingServer.frame_post_draw: Emitted at the end of the frame, after the RenderingServer has finished updating all the Viewports.
m.RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw: Emitted at the beginning of the frame, before the RenderingServer updates all the Viewports.
m.RenderingServer.free_rid: Tries to free an object in the RenderingServer. To avoid memory leaks, this should be called after using an object as memory management does not occur automatically when using RenderingServer directly.
m.RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_dr: Returns the name of the current rendering driver. This can be vulkan, d3d12, metal, opengl3, opengl3_es, or opengl3_angle. See also get_current_rendering_method().
m.RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_me: Returns the name of the current rendering method. This can be forward_plus, mobile, or gl_compatibility. See also get_current_rendering_driver_name().
m.RenderingServer.get_default_clear_color: Returns the default clear color which is used when a specific clear color has not been selected. See also set_default_clear_color().
m.RenderingServer.get_frame_setup_time_cpu: Returns the time taken to setup rendering on the CPU in milliseconds. This value is shared across all viewports and does not require viewport_set_measure_render_time() to be enabled on a viewport to be queried. See also viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu().
m.RenderingServer.get_rendering_info: Returns a statistic about the rendering engine which can be used for performance profiling. See also viewport_get_render_info(), which returns information specific to a viewport.
m.RenderingServer.get_shader_parameter_lis: Returns the parameters of a shader.
m.RenderingServer.get_test_cube: Returns the RID of the test cube. This mesh will be created and returned on the first call to get_test_cube(), then it will be cached for subsequent calls. See also make_sphere_mesh().
m.RenderingServer.get_test_texture: Returns the RID of a 256×256 texture with a testing pattern on it (in Image.FORMAT_RGB8 format). This texture will be created and returned on the first call to get_test_texture(), then it will be cached for subsequent calls. See also get_white_texture().
m.RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_api_ve: Returns the version of the graphics video adapter currently in use (e.g. "1.2.189" for Vulkan, "3.3.0 NVIDIA 510.60.02" for OpenGL). This version may be different from the actual latest version supported by the hardware, as Godot may not always request the latest version. See also OS.get_video_adapter_driver_info().
m.RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_name: Returns the name of the video adapter (e.g. "GeForce GTX 1080/PCIe/SSE2").
m.RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_type: Returns the type of the video adapter. Since dedicated graphics cards from a given generation will usually be significantly faster than integrated graphics made in the same generation, the device type can be used as a basis for automatic graphics settings adjustment. However, this is not always true, so make sure to provide users with a way to manually override graphics settings.
m.RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_vendor: Returns the vendor of the video adapter (e.g. "NVIDIA Corporation").
m.RenderingServer.get_white_texture: Returns the ID of a 4×4 white texture (in Image.FORMAT_RGB8 format). This texture will be created and returned on the first call to get_white_texture(), then it will be cached for subsequent calls. See also get_test_texture().
m.RenderingServer.gi_set_use_half_resoluti: If half_resolution is true, renders VoxelGI and SDFGI (Environment.sdfgi_enabled) buffers at halved resolution on each axis (e.g. 960×540 when the viewport size is 1920×1080). This improves performance significantly when VoxelGI or SDFGI is enabled, at the cost of artifacts that may be visible on polygon edges. The loss in quality becomes less noticeable as the viewport resolution increases. Ligh…
m.RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_: Creates a new global shader uniform.
Returns the value of the global shader uniform specified by name.
Returns the list of global shader uniform names.
Returns the type associated to the global shader uniform specified by name.
Removes the global shader uniform specified by name.
Sets the global shader uniform name to value.
Overrides the global shader uniform name with value. Equivalent to the ShaderGlobalsOverride node.
m.RenderingServer.has_changed: Returns true if changes have been made to the RenderingServer's data. force_draw() is usually called if this happens.
m.RenderingServer.has_feature: Deprecated: This method has not been used since Godot 3.0.
m.RenderingServer.has_os_feature: Returns true if the OS supports a certain feature. Features might be s3tc, etc, and etc2.
m.RenderingServer.instance_attach_object_i: Attaches a unique Object ID to instance. Object ID must be attached to instance for proper culling with instances_cull_aabb(), instances_cull_convex(), and instances_cull_ray().
m.RenderingServer.instance_attach_skeleton: Attaches a skeleton to an instance. Removes the previous skeleton from the instance.
m.RenderingServer.instance_create: Creates a visual instance and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all instance_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.instance_create2: Creates a visual instance, adds it to the RenderingServer, and sets both base and scenario. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all instance_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_get_sh: Returns the value of the per-instance shader uniform from the specified 3D geometry instance. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.get_instance_shader_parameter().
Returns the default value of the per-instance shader uniform from the specified 3D geometry instance. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.get_instance_shader_parameter().

Returns a dictionary of per-instance shader uniform names of the per-instance shader uniform from the specified 3D geometry instance. The returned dictionary is in PropertyInfo format, with the keys name, class_name, type, hint, hint_string and usage. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.get_instance_shader_parameter().
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_ca: Sets the shadow casting setting. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow.
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_fl: Sets the flag for a given instance to enabled.
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_li: Sets the lightmap GI instance to use for the specified 3D geometry instance. The lightmap UV scale for the specified instance (equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.gi_lightmap_scale) and lightmap atlas slice must also be specified.
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_lo: Sets the level of detail bias to use when rendering the specified 3D geometry instance. Higher values result in higher detail from further away. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.lod_bias.
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_ma: Sets a material that will be rendered for all surfaces on top of active materials for the mesh associated with this instance. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay.
Sets a material that will override the material for all surfaces on the mesh associated with this instance. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.material_override.
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_sh: Sets the per-instance shader uniform on the specified 3D geometry instance. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.set_instance_shader_parameter().
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_tr: Sets the transparency for the given geometry instance. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.transparency.
m.RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_vi: Sets the visibility range values for the given geometry instance. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin and related properties.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_base: Sets the base of the instance. A base can be any of the 3D objects that are created in the RenderingServer that can be displayed. For example, any of the light types, mesh, multimesh, particle system, reflection probe, decal, lightmap, voxel GI and visibility notifiers are all types that can be set as the base of an instance in order to be displayed in the scenario.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_blend_shape: Sets the weight for a given blend shape associated with this instance.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_custom_aabb: Sets a custom AABB to use when culling objects from the view frustum. Equivalent to setting GeometryInstance3D.custom_aabb.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_extra_visib: Sets a margin to increase the size of the AABB when culling objects from the view frustum. This allows you to avoid culling objects that fall outside the view frustum. Equivalent to GeometryInstance3D.extra_cull_margin.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_ignore_cull: If true, ignores all culling on the specified 3D geometry instance, including frustum culling, occlusion culling, and layer culling. This is not the same as GeometryInstance3D.ignore_occlusion_culling, which only ignores occlusion culling but leaves frustum and layer culling intact.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_layer_mask: Sets the render layers that this instance will be drawn to. Equivalent to VisualInstance3D.layers.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_pivot_data: Sets the sorting offset and switches between using the bounding box or instance origin for depth sorting.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_scenario: Sets the scenario that the instance is in. The scenario is the 3D world that the objects will be displayed in.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_surface_ove: Sets the override material of a specific surface. Equivalent to MeshInstance3D.set_surface_override_material().
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_transform: Sets the world space transform of the instance. Equivalent to Node3D.global_transform.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_visibility_: Sets the visibility parent for the given instance. Equivalent to Node3D.visibility_parent.
m.RenderingServer.instance_set_visible: Sets whether an instance is drawn or not. Equivalent to Node3D.visible.
m.RenderingServer.instance_teleport: Resets motion vectors and other interpolated values. Use this after teleporting a mesh from one position to another to avoid ghosting artifacts.
m.RenderingServer.instances_cull_aabb: Returns an array of object IDs intersecting with the provided AABB. Only 3D nodes that inherit from VisualInstance3D are considered, such as MeshInstance3D or DirectionalLight3D. Use @GlobalScope.instance_from_id() to obtain the actual nodes. A scenario RID must be provided, which is available in the World3D you want to query. This forces an update for all resources queued to update.
m.RenderingServer.instances_cull_convex: Returns an array of object IDs intersecting with the provided convex shape. Only 3D nodes that inherit from VisualInstance3D are considered, such as MeshInstance3D or DirectionalLight3D. Use @GlobalScope.instance_from_id() to obtain the actual nodes. A scenario RID must be provided, which is available in the World3D you want to query. This forces an update for all resources queued to update.
m.RenderingServer.instances_cull_ray: Returns an array of object IDs intersecting with the provided 3D ray. Only 3D nodes that inherit from VisualInstance3D are considered, such as MeshInstance3D or DirectionalLight3D. Use @GlobalScope.instance_from_id() to obtain the actual nodes. A scenario RID must be provided, which is available in the World3D you want to query. This forces an update for all resources queued to update.
m.RenderingServer.is_on_render_thread: Returns true if our code is currently executing on the rendering thread.
m.RenderingServer.light_area_set_normalize: Defines whether the energy of an AreaLight3D is normalized (divided) by its area. If set to true, changing the size does not affect the total energy output. Equivalent to AreaLight3D.area_normalize_energy.
m.RenderingServer.light_area_set_size: Sets the extents (width and height) in meters for this area light. Equivalent to AreaLight3D.area_size.
m.RenderingServer.light_directional_set_bl: If true, this directional light will blend between shadow map splits resulting in a smoother transition between them. Equivalent to DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_blend_splits.
m.RenderingServer.light_directional_set_sh: Sets the shadow mode for this directional light. Equivalent to DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_mode.
m.RenderingServer.light_directional_set_sk: If true, this light will not be used for anything except sky shaders. Use this for lights that impact your sky shader that you may want to hide from affecting the rest of the scene. For example, you may want to enable this when the sun in your sky shader falls below the horizon.
m.RenderingServer.light_omni_set_shadow_mo: Sets whether to use a dual paraboloid or a cubemap for the shadow map. Dual paraboloid is faster but may suffer from artifacts. Equivalent to OmniLight3D.omni_shadow_mode.
m.RenderingServer.light_projectors_set_fil: Sets the texture filter mode to use when rendering light projectors. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-light basis.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_bake_mode: Sets the bake mode to use for the specified 3D light. Equivalent to Light3D.light_bake_mode.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_color: Sets the color of the light. Equivalent to Light3D.light_color.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_cull_mask: Sets the cull mask for this 3D light. Lights only affect objects in the selected layers. Equivalent to Light3D.light_cull_mask.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_distance_fade: Sets the distance fade for this 3D light. This acts as a form of level of detail (LOD) and can be used to improve performance. Equivalent to Light3D.distance_fade_enabled, Light3D.distance_fade_begin, Light3D.distance_fade_shadow, and Light3D.distance_fade_length.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_max_sdfgi_casc: Sets the maximum SDFGI cascade in which the 3D light's indirect lighting is rendered. Higher values allow the light to be rendered in SDFGI further away from the camera.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_negative: If true, the 3D light will subtract light instead of adding light. Equivalent to Light3D.light_negative.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_param: Sets the specified 3D light parameter. Equivalent to Light3D.set_param().
m.RenderingServer.light_set_projector: Sets the projector texture to use for the specified 3D light. Equivalent to Light3D.light_projector.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_reverse_cull_f: If true, reverses the backface culling of the mesh. This can be useful when you have a flat mesh that has a light behind it. If you need to cast a shadow on both sides of the mesh, set the mesh to use double-sided shadows with instance_geometry_set_cast_shadows_setting(). Equivalent to Light3D.shadow_reverse_cull_face.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_shadow: If true, light will cast shadows. Equivalent to Light3D.shadow_enabled.
m.RenderingServer.light_set_shadow_caster_: Sets the shadow caster mask for this 3D light. Shadows will only be cast using objects in the selected layers. Equivalent to Light3D.shadow_caster_mask.
m.RenderingServer.lightmap_create: Creates a new lightmap global illumination instance and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all lightmap_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.lightmap_get_probe_captu: Returns the BSP tree data used for accelerating probe lookups. The BSP data is structured as a series of six signed 32-bit values per BSP node in this order: float plane_x, float plane_y, float plane_z, float plane_distance, int32_t over, int32_t under. An empty leaf is denoted by the value -2147483648 (the minimum 32-bit signed integer). See also lightmap_set_probe_capture_data().

Returns the local space positions of each lightmap probe capture point. Keep in mind the lightmap instance may have a non-zero transform, which will affect the position of the probe capture points. See also lightmap_set_probe_capture_data().

Returns the L0, L1, and L2 spherical harmonics [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_harmonics] data for each lightmap probe capture point. This is specified as 9 Color values per probe, which means the size of the returned data is always 9 times the number of probe points. See also lightmap_set_probe_capture_data().

Returns the tetrahedralization data used for interpolating between lightmap probe capture points. Each tetrahedron is specified as a series of 4 numbers, each being an index into the probe capture points array returned by lightmap_get_probe_capture_points(). See also lightmap_set_probe_capture_data().
m.RenderingServer.lightmap_set_baked_expos: Used to inform the renderer what exposure normalization value was used while baking the lightmap. This value will be used and modulated at run time to ensure that the lightmap maintains a consistent level of exposure even if the scene-wide exposure normalization is changed at run time. For more information see camera_attributes_set_exposure().
m.RenderingServer.lightmap_set_probe_bound: Sets the bounds that this lightmap instance should visually affect, both in terms of static lightmap baking and probe-based global illumination.
m.RenderingServer.lightmap_set_probe_captu: Sets the probe capture data for the given lightmap instance. See lightmap_get_probe_capture_points(), lightmap_get_probe_capture_sh(), lightmap_get_probe_capture_tetrahedra(), and lightmap_get_probe_capture_bsp_tree() for the expected data formats.

The framerate-independent update speed when representing dynamic object lighting from LightmapProbes. Higher values make dynamic object lighting update faster. Higher values can prevent fast-moving objects from having "outdated" indirect lighting displayed on them, at the cost of possible flickering when an object moves from a bright area to a shaded area. See also ProjectSettings.rendering/light…
m.RenderingServer.lightmap_set_probe_inter: Sets whether the lightmap instance should be considered as interior (when interior is true). If the lightmap is marked as interior, environment lighting is ignored when baking lightmaps.
m.RenderingServer.lightmap_set_textures: Set the textures on the given lightmap GI instance to the texture array pointed to by the light RID. If the lightmap texture was baked with LightmapGI.directional set to true, then uses_sh must also be true.
m.RenderingServer.lightmaps_set_bicubic_fi: Toggles whether a bicubic filter should be used when lightmaps are sampled. This smoothens their appearance at a performance cost.
m.RenderingServer.make_sphere_mesh: Returns a mesh of a sphere with the given number of horizontal subdivisions, vertical subdivisions and radius. See also get_test_cube().
m.RenderingServer.material_create: Creates an empty material and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all material_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.material_get_param: Returns the value of a certain material's parameter.
m.RenderingServer.material_set_use_debandi: When using the Mobile renderer, material_set_use_debanding() can be used to enable or disable the debanding feature of 3D materials (BaseMaterial3D and ShaderMaterial).
m.RenderingServer.mesh_add_surface: Creates a new surface on the given mesh. Equivalent to mesh_add_surface_from_arrays(), but takes a single Dictionary argument instead of separate arguments. The dictionary must follow this structure:
m.RenderingServer.mesh_add_surface_from_ar: Creates a new surface on the given mesh. mesh_get_surface_count() will become the surface index for this new surface.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_clear: Removes all surfaces from a mesh.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_create: Creates a new mesh and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all mesh_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_create_from_surface: Creates a new mesh with predefined surfaces for it and adds the mesh to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all mesh_* RenderingServer functions. This method is more efficient for creating meshes with multiple surfaces compared to creating an empty mesh with mesh_create() and adding surfaces one by one with mesh_add_surface().
m.RenderingServer.mesh_get_blend_shape_cou: Returns a mesh's blend shape count.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_get_blend_shape_mod: Returns a mesh's blend shape mode.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_get_surface: Returns a mesh's surface as a dictionary following the same structure as described in mesh_add_surface().
m.RenderingServer.mesh_get_surface_count: Returns a mesh's number of surfaces.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_set_blend_shape_mod: Sets a mesh's blend shape mode.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_set_shadow_mesh: Sets an optional second mesh which can be used for rendering shadows and the depth prepass. Can be used to increase performance by supplying a mesh with fused vertices and only vertex position data (without normals, UVs, colors, etc.).
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_arrays: Returns a mesh's surface's buffer arrays.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_blend_s: Returns a mesh's surface's arrays for blend shapes.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_format_: Returns the stride of the attribute buffer for a mesh with given format.
Returns the stride of the index buffer for a mesh with the given format.

Returns the stride of the combined normals and tangents for a mesh with given format. Note importantly that, while normals and tangents are in the vertex buffer with vertices, they are only interleaved with each other and so have a different stride than vertex positions.
Returns the offset of a given attribute by array_index in the start of its respective buffer.
Returns the stride of the skin buffer for a mesh with given format.

Returns the stride of the vertex positions for a mesh with given format. Note importantly that vertex positions are stored consecutively and are not interleaved with the other attributes in the vertex buffer (normals and tangents).
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_remove: Removes the surface at the given index from the Mesh, shifting surfaces with higher index down by one.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_attr: Updates the attribute buffer of the mesh surface with the given data. The expected data per attribute is 8 or 12 bytes (4 bytes per float, 2 floats per Vector2, and 3 floats per Vector3) depending on if the mesh is using Vector2 or Vector3 vertices. This value can be determined with mesh_surface_get_format_attribute_stride() instead.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_inde: Updates the index buffer of the mesh surface with the given data. The expected data are 16 or 32-bit unsigned integers, which can be determined with mesh_surface_get_format_index_stride().
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_skin: Updates the skin buffer of the mesh surface with the given data. The expected data per skin is 8 or 12 bytes (4 bytes per float, 2 floats per Vector2, and 3 floats per Vector3) depending on if the mesh is using Vector2 or Vector3 vertices. This value can be determined with mesh_surface_get_format_skin_stride() instead.
m.RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_vert: Updates the vertex buffer of the mesh surface with the given data. The expected data per vertex is 8 or 12 bytes (4 bytes per float, 2 floats per Vector2, and 3 floats per Vector3) depending on if the mesh is using Vector2 or Vector3 vertices. This value can be determined with mesh_surface_get_format_vertex_stride() instead.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_allocate_data: Sets up the multimesh using the specified data. The number of instances is set by instances. The format of the instance transforms is set by transform_format, which should be set according to whether the multimesh is meant to be rendered in 2D or 3D. If color_format is true, each instance will have a color associated with it. If custom_data_format is true, each instance will have a custom data ve…
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_create: Creates a new multimesh on the RenderingServer and returns an RID handle. This RID will be used in all multimesh_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_aabb: Calculates and returns the axis-aligned bounding box that encloses all instances within the multimesh.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_buffer: Returns the MultiMesh data (such as instance transforms, colors, etc.). See multimesh_set_buffer() for details on the returned data.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_buffer_rd_: Returns the RenderingDevice RID handle of the MultiMesh, which can be used as any other buffer on the Rendering Device.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_command_bu: Returns the RenderingDevice RID handle of the MultiMesh command buffer. This RID is only valid if use_indirect is set to true when allocating data through multimesh_allocate_data(). It can be used to directly modify the instance count via buffer.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_custom_aab: Returns the custom AABB defined for this MultiMesh resource.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_instance_c: Returns the number of instances allocated for this multimesh.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_mesh: Returns the RID of the mesh that will be used in drawing this multimesh.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_get_visible_in: Returns the number of visible instances for this multimesh.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_get_c: Returns the color by which the specified instance will be modulated.
Returns the custom data associated with the specified instance.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_get_t: Returns the Transform3D of the specified instance.
Returns the Transform2D of the specified instance. For use when the multimesh is set to use 2D transforms.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_reset: Prevents physics interpolation for the specified instance during the current physics tick.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_set_c: Sets the color by which this instance will be modulated. Equivalent to MultiMesh.set_instance_color().
Sets the custom data for this instance. Custom data is passed as a Color, but is interpreted as a vec4 in the shader. Equivalent to MultiMesh.set_instance_custom_data().
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_set_t: Sets the Transform3D for this instance. Equivalent to MultiMesh.set_instance_transform().
Sets the Transform2D for this instance. For use when multimesh is used in 2D. Equivalent to MultiMesh.set_instance_transform_2d().
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_instances_rese: Prevents physics interpolation for all instances during the current physics tick.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_set_buffer: Set the entire data to use for drawing the multimesh at once to buffer (such as instance transforms and colors). buffer's size must match the number of instances multiplied by the per-instance data size (which depends on the enabled MultiMesh fields). Otherwise, an error message is printed and nothing is rendered. See also multimesh_get_buffer().
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_set_buffer_int: Alternative version of multimesh_set_buffer() for use with physics interpolation.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_set_custom_aab: Sets the custom AABB for this MultiMesh resource.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_set_mesh: Sets the mesh to be drawn by the multimesh. Equivalent to MultiMesh.mesh.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_set_physics_in: Turns on and off physics interpolation for this MultiMesh resource.
Sets the physics interpolation quality for the MultiMesh.
m.RenderingServer.multimesh_set_visible_in: Sets the number of instances visible at a given time. If -1, all instances that have been allocated are drawn. Equivalent to MultiMesh.visible_instance_count.
m.RenderingServer.occluder_create: Creates an occluder instance and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all occluder_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.occluder_set_mesh: Sets the mesh data for the given occluder RID, which controls the shape of the occlusion culling that will be performed.
m.RenderingServer.omni_light_create: Creates a new omni light and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID can be used in most light_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.particles_collision_crea: Creates a new 3D GPU particle collision or attractor and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID can be used in most particles_collision_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.particles_collision_heig: Requests an update for the 3D GPU particle collision heightfield. This may be automatically called by the 3D GPU particle collision heightfield depending on its GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.update_mode.
m.RenderingServer.particles_collision_set_: Sets the attenuation curve for the 3D GPU particles attractor specified by the particles_collision RID. Only used for attractors, not colliders. Equivalent to GPUParticlesAttractor3D.attenuation.

Sets the directionality amount for the 3D GPU particles attractor specified by the particles_collision RID. Only used for attractors, not colliders. Equivalent to GPUParticlesAttractor3D.directionality.
Sets the strength for the 3D GPU particles attractor specified by the particles_collision RID. Only used for attractors, not colliders. Equivalent to GPUParticlesAttractor3D.strength.

Sets the extents for the 3D GPU particles collision by the particles_collision RID. Equivalent to GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D.size, GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.size, GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.size, GPUParticlesAttractorBox3D.size or GPUParticlesAttractorVectorField3D.size depending on the particles_collision type.
Sets the collision or attractor shape type for the 3D GPU particles collision or attractor specified by the particles_collision RID.

Sets the cull mask for the 3D GPU particles collision or attractor specified by the particles_collision RID. Equivalent to GPUParticlesCollision3D.cull_mask or GPUParticlesAttractor3D.cull_mask depending on the particles_collision type.

Sets the signed distance field texture for the 3D GPU particles collision specified by the particles_collision RID. Equivalent to GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D.texture or GPUParticlesAttractorVectorField3D.texture depending on the particles_collision type.
Sets the heightfield mask for the 3D GPU particles heightfield collision specified by the particles_collision RID. Equivalent to GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.heightfield_mask.
Sets the heightmap resolution for the 3D GPU particles heightfield collision specified by the particles_collision RID. Equivalent to GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.resolution.

Sets the radius for the 3D GPU particles sphere collision or attractor specified by the particles_collision RID. Equivalent to GPUParticlesCollisionSphere3D.radius or GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D.radius depending on the particles_collision type.
m.RenderingServer.particles_create: Creates a GPU-based particle system and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all particles_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.particles_emit: Manually emits particles from the particles instance.
m.RenderingServer.particles_get_current_aa: Calculates and returns the axis-aligned bounding box that contains all the particles. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.capture_aabb().
m.RenderingServer.particles_get_emitting: Returns true if particles are currently set to emitting.
m.RenderingServer.particles_is_inactive: Returns true if particles are not emitting and particles are set to inactive.
m.RenderingServer.particles_request_proces: Add particle system to list of particle systems that need to be updated. Update will take place on the next frame, or on the next call to instances_cull_aabb(), instances_cull_convex(), or instances_cull_ray().
Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
m.RenderingServer.particles_restart: Reset the particles on the next update. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.restart().
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_amount: Sets the number of particles to be drawn and allocates the memory for them. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.amount.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_amount_rat: Sets the amount ratio for particles to be emitted. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.amount_ratio.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_collision_: Sets the base size for particle collision. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.collision_base_size.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_custom_aab: Sets a custom axis-aligned bounding box for the particle system. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.visibility_aabb.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_draw_order: Sets the draw order of the particles. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.draw_order.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_draw_pass_: Sets the mesh to be used for the specified draw pass. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_1, GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_2, GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_3, and GPUParticles3D.draw_pass_4.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_draw_passe: Sets the number of draw passes to use. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.draw_passes.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_emission_t: Sets the Transform3D that will be used by the particles when they first emit.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_emitter_ve: Sets the velocity of a particle node, that will be used by ParticleProcessMaterial.inherit_velocity_ratio.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_emitting: If true, particles will emit over time. Setting to false does not reset the particles, but only stops their emission. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.emitting.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_explosiven: Sets the explosiveness ratio. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.explosiveness.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_fixed_fps: Sets the frame rate that the particle system rendering will be fixed to. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.fixed_fps.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_fractional: If true, uses fractional delta which smooths the movement of the particles. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.fract_delta.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_interp_to_: Sets the value that informs a ParticleProcessMaterial to rush all particles towards the end of their lifetime.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_interpolat: Sets whether particles should use interpolation between fixed steps. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.interpolate.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_lifetime: Sets the lifetime of each particle in the system. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.lifetime.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_mode: Sets whether the GPU particles specified by the particles RID should be rendered in 2D or 3D according to mode.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_one_shot: If true, particles will emit once and then stop. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.one_shot.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_pre_proces: Sets the preprocess time for the particles' animation. This lets you delay starting an animation until after the particles have begun emitting. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.preprocess.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_process_ma: Sets the material for processing the particles.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_randomness: Sets the emission randomness ratio. This randomizes the emission of particles within their phase. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.randomness.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_speed_scal: Sets the speed scale of the particle system. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.speed_scale.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_subemitter: Sets the subemitter particles for the particle system. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.sub_emitter.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_trail_bind: Sets the trail bind poses for the particle system. This specified as an array of Transform3Ds representing the bind pose for each draw pass. See GPUParticles3D.draw_skin, Skin.get_bind_count(), and Skin.get_bind_pose(). Set the value for each draw pass to Transform3D.IDENTITY to use the default behavior, which is what built-in trails use (RibbonTrailMesh and TubeTrailMesh).
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_trails: If enable is true, enables trails for the particles with the specified length_sec in seconds. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.trail_enabled and GPUParticles3D.trail_lifetime.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_transform_: Sets the transform alignment for the particle system. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.transform_align.
Sets which axis to use for transform alignment.
When using Z-Billboarding, which CUSTOM channel to read from.
m.RenderingServer.particles_set_use_local_: If true, particles use local coordinates. If false they use global coordinates. Equivalent to GPUParticles3D.local_coords.
m.RenderingServer.positional_soft_shadow_f: Sets the filter quality for omni and spot light shadows in 3D. See also ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/positional_shadow/soft_shadow_filter_quality. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-viewport basis.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_create: Creates a reflection probe and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all reflection_probe_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_amb: Sets the reflection probe's custom ambient light color. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.ambient_color.
Sets the reflection probe's custom ambient light energy. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.ambient_color_energy.
Sets the reflection probe's ambient light mode. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.ambient_mode.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_as_: If true, reflections will ignore sky contribution. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.interior.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_ble: Sets the distance in meters over which a probe blends into the scene.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_cul: Sets the render cull mask for this reflection probe. Only instances with a matching layer will be reflected by this probe. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.cull_mask.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_ena: If true, uses box projection. This can make reflections look more correct in certain situations. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.box_projection.
If true, computes shadows in the reflection probe. This makes the reflection much slower to compute. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.enable_shadows.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_int: Sets the intensity of the reflection probe. Intensity modulates the strength of the reflection. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.intensity.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_max: Sets the max distance away from the probe an object can be before it is culled. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.max_distance.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_mes: Sets the mesh level of detail to use in the reflection probe rendering. Higher values will use less detailed versions of meshes that have LOD variations generated, which can improve performance. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.mesh_lod_threshold.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_ori: Sets the origin offset to be used when this reflection probe is in box project mode. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.origin_offset.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_ref: Sets the render reflection mask for this reflection probe. Only instances with a matching layer will have reflections applied from this probe. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.reflection_mask.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_res: Deprecated: This method has not done anything since Godot 3.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_siz: Sets the size of the area that the reflection probe will capture. Equivalent to ReflectionProbe.size.
m.RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_upd: Sets how often the reflection probe updates. Can either be once or every frame.
m.RenderingServer.render_loop_enabled: If false, disables rendering completely, but the engine logic is still being processed. You can call force_draw() to draw a frame even with rendering disabled.
m.RenderingServer.request_frame_drawn_call: Schedules a callback to the given callable after a frame has been drawn.
m.RenderingServer.scenario_create: Creates a scenario and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all scenario_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.scenario_set_camera_attr: Sets the camera attributes (effects) that will be used with this scenario. See also CameraAttributes.
m.RenderingServer.scenario_set_compositor: Sets the compositor (compositor) that will be used with this scenario. See also Compositor.
m.RenderingServer.scenario_set_environment: Sets the environment that will be used with this scenario. See also Environment.
m.RenderingServer.scenario_set_fallback_en: Sets the fallback environment to be used by this scenario. The fallback environment is used if no environment is set. Internally, this is used by the editor to provide a default environment.
m.RenderingServer.screen_space_roughness_l: Sets the screen-space roughness limiter parameters, such as whether it should be enabled and its thresholds. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/screen_space_roughness_limiter/enabled, ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/screen_space_roughness_limiter/amount and ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/screen_space_roughness_limiter/limit.
m.RenderingServer.set_boot_image_with_stre: Sets a boot image. The color defines the background color. The value of stretch_mode indicates how the image will be stretched (see SplashStretchMode for possible values). If use_filter is true, the image will be scaled with linear interpolation. If use_filter is false, the image will be scaled with nearest-neighbor interpolation.
m.RenderingServer.set_debug_generate_wiref: If generate is true, generates debug wireframes for all meshes that are loaded when using the Compatibility renderer. By default, the engine does not generate debug wireframes at runtime, since they slow down loading of assets and take up VRAM.
m.RenderingServer.set_default_clear_color: Sets the default clear color which is used when a specific clear color has not been selected. See also get_default_clear_color().
m.RenderingServer.shader_create: Creates an empty shader and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all shader_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.shader_get_code: Returns a shader's source code as a string.
m.RenderingServer.shader_get_default_textu: Returns a default texture from a shader searched by name.
m.RenderingServer.shader_get_parameter_def: Returns the default value for the specified shader uniform. This is usually the value written in the shader source code.
m.RenderingServer.shader_set_code: Sets the shader's source code (which triggers recompilation after being changed).
m.RenderingServer.shader_set_default_textu: Sets a shader's default texture. Overwrites the texture given by name.
m.RenderingServer.shader_set_path_hint: Sets the path hint for the specified shader. This should generally match the Shader resource's Resource.resource_path.
m.RenderingServer.skeleton_allocate_data: Allocates data for this skeleton using the number of bones specified in bones. If is_2d_skeleton is true, the skeleton will be treated as a 2D skeleton instead of a 3D skeleton. See also skeleton_get_bone_count().
m.RenderingServer.skeleton_bone_get_transf: Returns the Transform3D set for a specific bone of this skeleton.
Returns the Transform2D set for a specific bone of this skeleton.
m.RenderingServer.skeleton_bone_set_transf: Sets the Transform3D for a specific bone of this skeleton.
Sets the Transform2D for a specific bone of this skeleton.
m.RenderingServer.skeleton_create: Creates a skeleton and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all skeleton_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.skeleton_get_bone_count: Returns the number of bones allocated for this skeleton. See also skeleton_allocate_data().
m.RenderingServer.skeleton_set_base_transf: Sets the base Transform2D to use for the specified skeleton.
m.RenderingServer.sky_bake_panorama: Generates and returns an Image containing the radiance map for the specified sky RID. This supports built-in sky material and custom sky shaders. If bake_irradiance is true, the irradiance map is saved instead of the radiance map. The radiance map is used to render reflected light, while the irradiance map is used to render ambient light. See also environment_bake_panorama().
m.RenderingServer.sky_create: Creates an empty sky and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all sky_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.sky_set_material: Sets the material that the sky uses to render the background, ambient and reflection maps.
m.RenderingServer.sky_set_mode: Sets the process mode of the sky specified by the sky RID. Equivalent to Sky.process_mode.
m.RenderingServer.sky_set_radiance_size: Sets the radiance_size of the sky specified by the sky RID (in pixels). Equivalent to Sky.radiance_size.
m.RenderingServer.spot_light_create: Creates a spot light and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID can be used in most light_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.sub_surface_scattering_s: Sets ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_quality to use when rendering materials that have subsurface scattering enabled.

Sets the ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_scale and ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_depth_scale to use when rendering materials that have subsurface scattering enabled.
m.RenderingServer.texture_2d_create: Creates a 2-dimensional texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all texture_2d_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.texture_2d_get: Returns an Image instance from the given texture RID.
m.RenderingServer.texture_2d_layer_get: Returns an Image instance from the given texture RID and layer.
m.RenderingServer.texture_2d_layered_creat: Creates a 2-dimensional layered texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all texture_2d_layered_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.texture_2d_layered_place: Creates a placeholder for a 2-dimensional layered texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all texture_2d_layered_* RenderingServer functions, although it does nothing when used. See also texture_2d_placeholder_create().
m.RenderingServer.texture_2d_placeholder_c: Creates a placeholder for a 2-dimensional layered texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all texture_2d_layered_* RenderingServer functions, although it does nothing when used. See also texture_2d_layered_placeholder_create().
m.RenderingServer.texture_2d_update: Updates the texture specified by the texture RID with the data in image. A layer must also be specified, which should be 0 when updating a single-layer texture (Texture2D).
m.RenderingServer.texture_3d_create: Note: The equivalent resource is Texture3D.
m.RenderingServer.texture_3d_get: Returns 3D texture data as an array of Images for the specified texture RID.
m.RenderingServer.texture_3d_placeholder_c: Creates a placeholder for a 3-dimensional texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all texture_3d_* RenderingServer functions, although it does nothing when used.
m.RenderingServer.texture_3d_update: Updates the texture specified by the texture RID's data with the data in data. All the texture's layers must be replaced at once.
m.RenderingServer.texture_create_from_nati: Creates a texture based on a native handle that was created outside of Godot's renderer.
m.RenderingServer.texture_drawable_blit_re: Draws to rect on up to 4 given Drawable textures, using a TextureBlit Shader from material. modulate and up to 4 source_textures are uniforms for the Shader to process with. to_mipmap can specify to perform this draw to a lower mipmap level.
m.RenderingServer.texture_drawable_create: Creates a 2-dimensional texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all texture_drawable* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.texture_drawable_generat: Calculates new MipMaps for the given Drawable texture.
m.RenderingServer.texture_drawable_get_def: Returns a ShaderMaterial with the default texture_blit Shader.
m.RenderingServer.texture_get_format: Returns the format for the texture.
m.RenderingServer.texture_get_native_handl: Returns the internal graphics handle for this texture object. For use when communicating with third-party APIs mostly with GDExtension.
m.RenderingServer.texture_get_path: Returns the resource path (starting with res:// or uid://) for the specified texture RID. Returns an empty String if the resource is built-in. See also texture_set_path().
m.RenderingServer.texture_get_rd_texture: Returns a texture RID that can be used with RenderingDevice.
m.RenderingServer.texture_proxy_create: Deprecated: ProxyTexture was removed in Godot 4.
m.RenderingServer.texture_proxy_update: Deprecated: ProxyTexture was removed in Godot 4.
m.RenderingServer.texture_rd_create: Creates a new texture object based on a texture created directly on the RenderingDevice. If the texture contains layers, layer_type is used to define the layer type.
m.RenderingServer.texture_replace: Replaces texture's texture data by the texture specified by the by_texture RID, without changing texture's RID.
m.RenderingServer.texture_set_force_redraw: Sets whether the texture RID should force redrawing when it's visible on screen when OS.low_processor_usage_mode is true. This is used by AnimatedTexture to force redrawing.
m.RenderingServer.texture_set_path: Sets the resource path for this texture RID. See also texture_get_path().
m.RenderingServer.texture_set_size_overrid: Sets the size at which the texture should be displayed in 2D, ignoring its original size. This does not rescale the texture data itself, only how it is drawn in 2D. Set width and height to 0 to disable the size override.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_attach_to_scree: Copies the viewport to a region of the screen specified by rect. If viewport_set_render_direct_to_screen() is true, then the viewport does not use a framebuffer and the contents of the viewport are rendered directly to screen. However, note that the root viewport is drawn last, therefore it will draw over the screen. Accordingly, you must set the root viewport to an area that does not cover the a…
m.RenderingServer.viewport_create: Creates an empty viewport and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all viewport_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_re: Returns the CPU time taken to render the last frame in milliseconds. This only includes time spent in rendering-related operations; scripts' _process functions and other engine subsystems are not included in this readout. To get a complete readout of CPU time spent to render the scene, sum the render times of all viewports that are drawn every frame plus get_frame_setup_time_cpu(). Unlike Engine.…

Returns the GPU time taken to render the last frame in milliseconds. To get a complete readout of GPU time spent to render the scene, sum the render times of all viewports that are drawn every frame. Unlike Engine.get_frames_per_second(), this method accurately reflects GPU utilization even if framerate is capped via V-Sync or Engine.max_fps. See also viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu().
m.RenderingServer.viewport_get_render_info: Returns a statistic about the rendering engine which can be used for performance profiling. This is separated into render pass types, each of them having the same infos you can query (different passes will return different values).
m.RenderingServer.viewport_get_render_targ: Returns the render target for the viewport.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_get_texture: Returns the viewport's last rendered frame.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_remove_canvas: Detaches a viewport from a canvas.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_active: If true, sets the viewport active, else sets it inactive.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_anisotropic: Sets the maximum number of samples to take when using anisotropic filtering on textures (as a power of two). A higher sample count will result in sharper textures at oblique angles, but is more expensive to compute. A value of 0 forcibly disables anisotropic filtering, even on materials where it is enabled.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_canvas_cull: Sets the rendering mask associated with this Viewport. Only CanvasItem nodes with a matching rendering visibility layer will be rendered by this Viewport.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_canvas_stac: Sets the stacking order for a viewport's canvas.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_canvas_tran: Sets the transformation of a viewport's canvas.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_clear_mode: Sets the clear mode of a viewport.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_debug_draw: Sets the debug draw mode of a viewport.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_default_can: Sets the default texture filtering mode for the specified viewport RID.
Sets the default texture repeat mode for the specified viewport RID.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_disable_2d: If true, the viewport's canvas (i.e. 2D and GUI elements) is not rendered.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_disable_3d: If true, the viewport's 3D elements are not rendered.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_environment: Sets the viewport's environment mode which allows enabling or disabling rendering of 3D environment over 2D canvas. When disabled, 2D will not be affected by the environment. When enabled, 2D will be affected by the environment if the environment background mode is ENV_BG_CANVAS. The default behavior is to inherit the setting from the viewport's parent. If the topmost parent is also set to VIEWPO…
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_fsr_sharpne: Determines how sharp the upscaled image will be when using the FSR upscaling mode. Sharpness halves with every whole number. Values go from 0.0 (sharpest) to 2.0. Values above 2.0 won't make a visible difference.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_global_canv: Sets the viewport's global transformation matrix.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_ren: Sets the measurement for the given viewport RID (obtained using Viewport.get_viewport_rid()). Once enabled, viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu() and viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu() will return values greater than 0.0 when queried with the given viewport.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_msaa_2d: Sets the multisample antialiasing mode for 2D/Canvas on the specified viewport RID. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_2d or Viewport.msaa_2d.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_msaa_3d: Sets the multisample antialiasing mode for 3D on the specified viewport RID. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_3d or Viewport.msaa_3d.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_occlusion_c: Sets the ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/bvh_build_quality to use for occlusion culling. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-viewport basis.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_occlusion_r: Sets the ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/occlusion_rays_per_thread to use for occlusion culling. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-viewport basis.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_parent_view: Sets the viewport's parent to the viewport specified by the parent_viewport RID.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_positional_: Sets the number of subdivisions to use in the specified shadow atlas quadrant for omni and spot shadows. See also Viewport.set_positional_shadow_atlas_quadrant_subdiv().

Sets the size of the shadow atlas's images (used for omni and spot lights) on the viewport specified by the viewport RID. The value is rounded up to the nearest power of 2. If use_16_bits is true, use 16 bits for the omni/spot shadow depth map. Enabling this results in shadows having less precision and may result in shadow acne, but can lead to performance improvements on some devices.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_render_dire: If true, render the contents of the viewport directly to screen. This allows a low-level optimization where you can skip drawing a viewport to the root viewport. While this optimization can result in a significant increase in speed (especially on older devices), it comes at a cost of usability. When this is enabled, you cannot read from the viewport or from the screen_texture. You also lose the b…
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_scaling_3d_: Sets the 3D resolution scaling mode. Bilinear scaling renders at different resolution to either undersample or supersample the viewport. FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0, abbreviated to FSR, is an upscaling technology that produces high quality images at fast framerates by using a spatially aware upscaling algorithm. FSR is slightly more expensive than bilinear, but it produces significantly highe…

Scales the 3D render buffer based on the viewport size uses an image filter specified in ViewportScaling3DMode to scale the output image to the full viewport size. Values lower than 1.0 can be used to speed up 3D rendering at the cost of quality (undersampling). Values greater than 1.0 are only valid for bilinear mode and can be used to improve 3D rendering quality at a high performance cost (sup…
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_scenario: Sets a viewport's scenario. The scenario contains information about environment information, reflection atlas, etc.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_screen_spac: Sets the viewport's screen-space antialiasing mode. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/screen_space_aa or Viewport.screen_space_aa.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_sdf_oversiz: Sets the viewport's 2D signed distance field ProjectSettings.rendering/2d/sdf/oversize and ProjectSettings.rendering/2d/sdf/scale. This is used when sampling the signed distance field in CanvasItem shaders as well as GPUParticles2D collision. This is not used by SDFGI in 3D rendering.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_size: Sets the viewport's width and height in pixels. Optionally the view_count can be set to increase the number of view layers for stereo rendering.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_snap_2d_tra: If true, canvas item transforms (i.e. origin position) are snapped to the nearest pixel when rendering. This can lead to a crisper appearance at the cost of less smooth movement, especially when Camera2D smoothing is enabled. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_snap_2d_ver: If true, canvas item vertices (i.e. polygon points) are snapped to the nearest pixel when rendering. This can lead to a crisper appearance at the cost of less smooth movement, especially when Camera2D smoothing is enabled. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_texture_mip: Affects the final texture sharpness by reading from a lower or higher mipmap (also called "texture LOD bias"). Negative values make mipmapped textures sharper but grainier when viewed at a distance, while positive values make mipmapped textures blurrier (even when up close). To get sharper textures at a distance without introducing too much graininess, set this between -0.75 and 0.0. Enabling tem…
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_transparent: If true, the viewport renders its background as transparent.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_update_mode: Sets when the viewport should be updated.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_use_hdr_2d: If true, 2D rendering will use a high dynamic range (HDR) RGBA16 format framebuffer. Additionally, 2D rendering will be performed on linear values and will be converted using the appropriate transfer function immediately before blitting to the screen (if the Viewport is attached to the screen).
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_use_occlusi: If true, enables occlusion culling on the specified viewport. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/use_occlusion_culling.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_use_taa: If true, use temporal antialiasing. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/use_taa or Viewport.use_taa.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_use_xr: If true, the viewport uses augmented or virtual reality technologies. See XRInterface.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_vrs_mode: Sets the Variable Rate Shading (VRS) mode for the viewport. If the GPU does not support VRS, this property is ignored. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/vrs/mode.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_vrs_texture: The texture to use when the VRS mode is set to VIEWPORT_VRS_TEXTURE. Equivalent to ProjectSettings.rendering/vrs/texture.
m.RenderingServer.viewport_set_vrs_update_: Sets the update mode for Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for the viewport. VRS requires the input texture to be converted to the format usable by the VRS method supported by the hardware. The update mode defines how often this happens. If the GPU does not support VRS, or VRS is not enabled, this property is ignored.
m.RenderingServer.visibility_notifier_crea: Creates a new 3D visibility notifier object and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all visibility_notifier_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.visibility_notifier_set_: Sets the AABB of the specified visibility notifier.
Sets the methods to be called when the notifier enters or exits the view.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_allocate_data: Allocates and initializes the voxel GI data for the specified voxel_gi RID. octree_cells must be a multiple of 32. octree_cells must be double the size of data_cells. The allocated data can be retrieved later using the various voxel_gi_get_* methods.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_create: Creates a new voxel-based global illumination object and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all voxel_gi_* RenderingServer functions.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_data_cells: Returns the data cells for the specified voxel GI data instance. See also voxel_gi_allocate_data().
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_distance_fi: Returns the distance field data for the specified voxel GI data instance. See also voxel_gi_allocate_data().
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_level_count: Returns the level counts for the specified voxel GI data instance. See also voxel_gi_allocate_data().
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_octree_cell: Returns the octree cell data for the specified voxel GI data instance. See also voxel_gi_allocate_data().
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_octree_size: Returns the octree size for the specified voxel GI data instance, which corresponds to the number of subdivisions per axis. This can be viewed in the editor by hovering the Bake VoxelGI button at the top of the 3D editor viewport when a VoxelGI node is selected and looking at the Subdivisions field in the tooltip.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_to_cell_xfo: Returns the transform to cell space for the specified voxel GI data instance. See also voxel_gi_allocate_data().
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_baked_expos: Used to inform the renderer what exposure normalization value was used while baking the voxel gi. This value will be used and modulated at run time to ensure that the voxel gi maintains a consistent level of exposure even if the scene-wide exposure normalization is changed at run time. For more information see camera_attributes_set_exposure().
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_bias: Sets the VoxelGIData.bias value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_dynamic_ran: Sets the VoxelGIData.dynamic_range value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_energy: Sets the VoxelGIData.energy value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_interior: Sets the VoxelGIData.interior value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_normal_bias: Sets the VoxelGIData.normal_bias value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_propagation: Sets the VoxelGIData.propagation value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_quality: Sets the ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/voxel_gi/quality value to use when rendering. This parameter is global and cannot be set on a per-VoxelGI basis.
m.RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_use_two_bou: Sets the VoxelGIData.use_two_bounces value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
m.Resource.DEEP_DUPLICATE_ALL: Every subresource found will be duplicated, even if it has a non-local path. In other words, even potentially big resources stored separately will be duplicated.
m.Resource.DEEP_DUPLICATE_INTERNAL: Only subresources without a path or with a scene-local path will be duplicated.
m.Resource.DEEP_DUPLICATE_NONE: No subresources at all are duplicated. This is useful even in a deep duplication to have all the arrays and dictionaries duplicated but still pointing to the original resources.
m.Resource._get_rid: Override this method to return a custom RID when get_rid() is called.
m.Resource._reset_state: For resources that store state in non-exported properties, such as via Object._validate_property() or Object._get_property_list(), this method must be implemented to clear them.
m.Resource._set_path_cache: Override this method to execute additional logic after set_path_cache() is called on this object.
m.Resource._setup_local_to_scene: Override this method to customize the newly duplicated resource created from PackedScene.instantiate(), if the original's resource_local_to_scene is set to true.
m.Resource.changed: Emitted when the resource changes, usually when one of its properties is modified. See also emit_changed().
m.Resource.copy_from_resource: Copies the data from resource into this resource. Both resources must share the same class.
m.Resource.duplicate: Duplicates this resource, returning a new resource with its exported or @GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE properties copied from the original.
m.Resource.duplicate_deep: Duplicates this resource, deeply, like duplicate() when passing true, with extra control over how subresources are handled.
m.Resource.emit_changed: Emits the changed signal. This method is called automatically for some built-in resources.
m.Resource.generate_scene_unique_id: Generates a unique identifier for a resource to be contained inside a PackedScene, based on the current date, time, and a random value. The returned string is only composed of letters (a to y) and numbers (0 to 8). See also resource_scene_unique_id.
m.Resource.get_id_for_path: From the internal cache for scene-unique IDs, returns the ID of this resource for the scene at path. If there is no entry, an empty string is returned. Useful to keep scene-unique IDs the same when implementing a VCS-friendly custom resource format by extending ResourceFormatLoader and ResourceFormatSaver.
m.Resource.get_local_scene: If resource_local_to_scene is set to true and the resource has been loaded from a PackedScene instantiation, returns the root Node of the scene where this resource is used. Otherwise, returns null.
m.Resource.get_rid: Returns the RID of this resource (or an empty RID). Many resources (such as Texture2D, Mesh, and so on) are high-level abstractions of resources stored in a specialized server (DisplayServer, RenderingServer, etc.), so this function will return the original RID.
m.Resource.is_built_in: Returns true if the resource is saved on disk as a part of another resource's file.
m.Resource.reset_state: Makes the resource clear its non-exported properties. See also _reset_state(). Useful when implementing a custom resource format by extending ResourceFormatLoader and ResourceFormatSaver.
m.Resource.resource_local_to_scene: If true, the resource is duplicated for each instance of all scenes using it. At run-time, the resource can be modified in one scene without affecting other instances (see PackedScene.instantiate()).
m.Resource.resource_name: An optional name for this resource. When defined, its value is displayed to represent the resource in the Inspector dock. For built-in scripts, the name is displayed as part of the tab name in the script editor.
m.Resource.resource_path: 资源在 res:// 中的路径。
m.Resource.resource_scene_unique_id: A unique identifier relative to this resource's scene. If left empty, the ID is automatically generated when this resource is saved inside a PackedScene. If the resource is not inside a scene, this property is empty by default.
m.Resource.set_id_for_path: In the internal cache for scene-unique IDs, sets the ID of this resource to id for the scene at path. If id is empty, the cache entry for path is cleared. Useful to keep scene-unique IDs the same when implementing a VCS-friendly custom resource format by extending ResourceFormatLoader and ResourceFormatSaver.
m.Resource.set_path_cache: Sets the resource's path to path without involving the resource cache. Useful for handling CacheMode values when implementing a custom resource format by extending ResourceFormatLoader and ResourceFormatSaver.
m.Resource.setup_local_to_scene: Deprecated: This method should only be called internally.
m.Resource.setup_local_to_scene_requested: Deprecated: This signal is only emitted when the resource is created. Override _setup_local_to_scene() instead.
m.Resource.take_over_path: Sets the resource_path to path, potentially overriding an existing cache entry for this path. Further attempts to load an overridden resource by path will instead return this resource.
m.ResourceFormatLoader.CACHE_MODE_IGNORE: Neither the main resource (the one requested to be loaded) nor any of its subresources are retrieved from cache nor stored into it. Dependencies (external resources) are loaded with CACHE_MODE_REUSE.
m.ResourceFormatLoader.CACHE_MODE_IGNORE_D: Like CACHE_MODE_IGNORE, but propagated recursively down the tree of dependencies (external resources).
m.ResourceFormatLoader.CACHE_MODE_REPLACE: Like CACHE_MODE_REUSE, but the cache is checked for the main resource (the one requested to be loaded) as well as for each of its subresources. Those already in the cache, as long as the loaded and cached types match, have their data refreshed from storage into the already existing instances. Otherwise, they are recreated as completely new objects.
m.ResourceFormatLoader.CACHE_MODE_REPLACE_: Like CACHE_MODE_REPLACE, but propagated recursively down the tree of dependencies (external resources).
m.ResourceFormatLoader.CACHE_MODE_REUSE: The main resource (the one requested to be loaded), its subresources, and its dependencies (external resources) are retrieved from cache if present, instead of loaded. Those not cached are loaded and then stored into the cache. The same rules are propagated recursively down the tree of dependencies (external resources).

m.ResourceFormatLoader._get_dependencies: Should return the dependencies for the resource at the given path. Each dependency is a string composed of one to three sections separated by ::, with trailing empty sections omitted:
m.ResourceFormatLoader._get_recognized_ext: Gets the list of extensions for files this loader is able to read.
m.ResourceFormatLoader._get_resource_scrip: Returns the script class name associated with the Resource under the given path. If the resource has no script or the script isn't a named class, it should return "".
m.ResourceFormatLoader._get_resource_type: Gets the class name of the resource associated with the given path. If the loader cannot handle it, it should return "".
m.ResourceFormatLoader._get_resource_uid: Should return the unique ID for the resource associated with the given path. If this method is not overridden, a .uid file is generated along with the resource file, containing the unique ID.
m.ResourceFormatLoader._handles_type: Tells which resource class this loader can load.
m.ResourceFormatLoader._load: Loads a resource when the engine finds this loader to be compatible. If the loaded resource is the result of an import, original_path will target the source file. Returns a Resource object on success, or an Error constant in case of failure.
m.ResourceFormatLoader._recognize_path: Tells whether or not this loader should load a resource from its resource path for a given type.
m.ResourceFormatLoader._rename_dependencie: If implemented, renames dependencies within the given resource and saves it. renames is a dictionary { String => String } mapping old dependency paths to new paths.
m.ResourceFormatSaver._get_recognized_exte: Returns the list of extensions available for saving the resource object, provided it is recognized (see _recognize()).
m.ResourceFormatSaver._recognize: Returns whether the given resource object can be saved by this saver.
m.ResourceFormatSaver._recognize_path: Returns true if this saver handles a given save path and false otherwise.
m.ResourceFormatSaver._save: Saves the given resource object to a file at the target path. flags is a bitmask composed with SaverFlags constants.
m.ResourceFormatSaver._set_uid: Sets a new UID for the resource at the given path. Returns @GlobalScope.OK on success, or an Error constant in case of failure.
m.ResourceImporter.IMPORT_ORDER_SCENE: The import order for scenes, which ensures scenes are imported after all other core resources such as textures. Custom importers should generally have an import order lower than 100 to avoid issues when importing scenes that rely on custom resources.
m.ResourceImporter._get_build_dependencies: Called when the engine compilation profile editor wants to check what build options an imported resource needs. For example, ResourceImporterDynamicFont has a property called ResourceImporterDynamicFont.multichannel_signed_distance_field, that depends on the engine to be build with the "msdfgen" module. If that resource happened to be a custom one, it would be handled like this:
m.ResourceImporterBMFont.compress: If true, uses lossless compression for the resulting font.
m.ResourceImporterBMFont.fallbacks: List of font fallbacks to use if a glyph isn't found in this bitmap font. Fonts at the beginning of the array are attempted first.
m.ResourceImporterBitMap.create_from: The data source to use for generating the bitmap.
m.ResourceImporterBitMap.threshold: The threshold to use to determine which bits should be considered enabled or disabled. See also create_from.
m.ResourceImporterCSVTranslation.delimiter: The delimiter to use in the CSV file. The default value matches the common CSV convention. Tab-separated values are sometimes called TSV files.
m.ResourceImporterCSVTranslation.unescape_: If true, message keys in the CSV file are unescaped using String.c_unescape() during the import process.
If true, message translations in the CSV file are unescaped using String.c_unescape() during the import process.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.allow_system: If true, automatically use system fonts as a fallback if a glyph isn't found in this dynamic font. This makes supporting CJK characters or emoji more straightforward, as you don't need to include a CJK/emoji font in your project. See also fallbacks.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.antialiasing: The font antialiasing method to use.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.compress: If true, uses lossless compression for the resulting font.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.disable_embe: If set to true, embedded font bitmap loading is disabled (bitmap-only and color fonts ignore this property).
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.fallbacks: List of font fallbacks to use if a glyph isn't found in this dynamic font. Fonts at the beginning of the array are attempted first, but fallback fonts that don't support the glyph's language and script are attempted last (see language_support and script_support). See also allow_system_fallback.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.force_autohi: If true, forces generation of hinting data for the font using FreeType [https://freetype.org/]'s autohinter. This will make hinting effective with fonts that don't include hinting data.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.generate_mip: If true, this font will have mipmaps generated. This prevents text from looking grainy when a Control is scaled down, or when a Label3D is viewed from a long distance (if Label3D.texture_filter is set to a mode that displays mipmaps).
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.hinting: The hinting mode to use. This controls how aggressively glyph edges should be snapped to pixels when rasterizing the font. Depending on personal preference, you may prefer using one hinting mode over the other. Hinting modes other than None are only effective if the font contains hinting data (see force_autohinter).
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.keep_roundin: If set to true, when aligning glyphs to the pixel boundaries rounding remainders are accumulated to ensure more uniform glyph distribution. This setting has no effect if subpixel positioning is enabled.
