m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.language_sup: Override the list of languages supported by this font. If left empty, this is supplied by the font metadata. There is usually no need to change this. See also script_support.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.modulate_col: If set to true, color modulation is applied when drawing colored glyphs, otherwise it's applied to the monochrome glyphs only.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.msdf_pixel_r: The width of the range around the shape between the minimum and maximum representable signed distance. If using font outlines, msdf_pixel_range must be set to at least twice the size of the largest font outline. The default msdf_pixel_range value of 8 allows outline sizes up to 4 to look correct.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.msdf_size: Source font size used to generate MSDF textures. Higher values allow for more precision, but are slower to render and require more memory. Only increase this value if you notice a visible lack of precision in glyph rendering. Only effective if multichannel_signed_distance_field is true.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.multichannel: If set to true, the font will use multichannel signed distance field (MSDF) for crisp rendering at any size. Since this approach does not rely on rasterizing the font every time its size changes, this allows for resizing the font in real-time without any performance penalty. Text will also not look grainy for Controls that are scaled down (or for Label3Ds viewed from a long distance).
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.opentype_fea: The OpenType features to enable, disable or set a value for this font. This can be used to enable optional features provided by the font, such as ligatures or alternative glyphs. The list of supported OpenType features varies on a per-font basis.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.oversampling: If set to a positive value, overrides the oversampling factor of the viewport this font is used in. See Viewport.oversampling. This value doesn't override the oversampling parameter of draw_* methods.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.preload: The glyph ranges to prerender. This can avoid stuttering during gameplay when new characters need to be rendered, especially if subpixel_positioning is enabled. The downside of using preloading is that initial project load times will increase, as well as memory usage.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.script_suppo: Override the list of language scripts supported by this font. If left empty, this is supplied by the font metadata. There is usually no need to change this. See also language_support.
m.ResourceImporterDynamicFont.subpixel_pos: Subpixel positioning improves font rendering appearance, especially at smaller font sizes. The downside is that it takes more time to initially render the font, which can cause stuttering during gameplay, especially if used with large font sizes. This should be set to Disabled for fonts with a pixel art appearance.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.ascent: Font ascent (number of pixels above the baseline). If set to 0, half of the character height is used.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.character_marg: Margin applied around every imported glyph. If your font image contains guides (in the form of lines between glyphs) or if spacing between characters appears incorrect, try adjusting character_margin.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.character_rang: The character ranges to import from the font image. This is an array that maps each position on the image (in tile coordinates, not pixels). The font atlas is traversed from left to right and top to bottom. Characters can be specified with decimal numbers (126), hexadecimal numbers (0x007e or U+007e), or between single quotes ('~'). Ranges can be specified with a hyphen between characters.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.columns: Number of columns in the font image. See also rows.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.compress: If true, uses lossless compression for the resulting font.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.descent: Font descent (number of pixels below the baseline). If set to 0, half of the character height is used.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.fallbacks: List of font fallbacks to use if a glyph isn't found in this bitmap font. Fonts at the beginning of the array are attempted first.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.image_margin: Margin to cut on the sides of the entire image. This can be used to cut parts of the image that contain attribution information or similar.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.kerning_pairs: Kerning pairs for the font. Kerning pair adjust the spacing between two characters.
m.ResourceImporterImageFont.rows: Number of rows in the font image. See also columns.
m.ResourceImporterMP3.bar_beats: The number of beats within a single bar in the audio track. This is only relevant for music that wishes to make use of interactive music functionality, not sound effects.
m.ResourceImporterMP3.beat_count: The length of the audio track, in beats. The actual duration of the audio file might be longer than what is indicated by this property. This is only relevant for music that wishes to make use of interactive music functionality, not sound effects.
m.ResourceImporterMP3.bpm: The tempo of the audio track, measured in beats per minute. This should match the BPM measure that was used to compose the track. This is only relevant for music that wishes to make use of interactive music functionality, not sound effects.
m.ResourceImporterMP3.loop: If enabled, the audio will begin playing either from the beginning or from loop_offset, after playback ends by either reaching the end of the audio or reaching the end of the last beat according to the amount specified in beat_count.
m.ResourceImporterMP3.loop_offset: Determines where audio will start to loop after playback reaches the end of the audio. This can be used to only loop a part of the audio file, which is useful for some ambient sounds or music. The value is determined in seconds relative to the beginning of the audio. A value of 0.0 will loop the entire audio file.
m.ResourceImporterOBJ.force_disable_mesh_c: If true, mesh compression will not be used. Consider enabling if you notice blocky artifacts in your mesh normals or UVs, or if you have meshes that are larger than a few thousand meters in each direction.
m.ResourceImporterOBJ.generate_lightmap_uv: If true, generates UV2 on import for LightmapGI baking.
Controls the size of each texel on the baked lightmap. A smaller value results in more precise lightmaps, at the cost of larger lightmap sizes and longer bake times.
m.ResourceImporterOBJ.generate_lods: If true, generates lower detail variants of the mesh which will be displayed in the distance to improve rendering performance. Not all meshes benefit from LOD, especially if they are never rendered from far away. Disabling this can reduce output file size and speed up importing. See Mesh level of detail (LOD) for more information.
m.ResourceImporterOBJ.generate_shadow_mesh: If true, enables the generation of shadow meshes on import. This optimizes shadow rendering without reducing quality by welding vertices together when possible. This in turn reduces the memory bandwidth required to render shadows. Shadow mesh generation currently doesn't support using a lower detail level than the source mesh (but shadow rendering will make use of LODs when relevant).
m.ResourceImporterOBJ.generate_tangents: If true, generate vertex tangents using Mikktspace [http://www.mikktspace.com/] if the source mesh doesn't have tangent data. When possible, it's recommended to let the 3D modeling software generate tangents on export instead of relying on this option. Tangents are required for correct display of normal and height maps, along with any material/shader features that require tangents.
m.ResourceImporterOBJ.offset_mesh: Offsets the mesh's data by the specified value. This can be used to work around misaligned meshes without having to modify the source file.
m.ResourceImporterOBJ.scale_mesh: Scales the mesh's data by the specified value. This can be used to work around misscaled meshes without having to modify the source file.
m.ResourceImporterOggVorbis.bar_beats: The number of beats within a single bar in the audio track. This is only relevant for music that wishes to make use of interactive music functionality, not sound effects.
m.ResourceImporterOggVorbis.beat_count: The length of the audio track, in beats. The actual duration of the audio file might be longer than what is indicated by this property. This is only relevant for music that wishes to make use of interactive music functionality, not sound effects.
m.ResourceImporterOggVorbis.bpm: The tempo of the audio track, measured in beats per minute. This should match the BPM measure that was used to compose the track. This is only relevant for music that wishes to make use of interactive music functionality, not sound effects.
m.ResourceImporterOggVorbis.loop: If enabled, the audio will begin playing either from the beginning or from loop_offset, after playback ends by either reaching the end of the audio or reaching the end of the last beat according to the amount specified in beat_count.
m.ResourceImporterOggVorbis.loop_offset: Determines where audio will start to loop after playback reaches the end of the audio. This can be used to only loop a part of the audio file, which is useful for some ambient sounds or music. The value is determined in seconds relative to the beginning of the audio. A value of 0.0 will loop the entire audio file.
m.ResourceImporterSVG.base_scale: Texture scale. 1.0 is the original SVG size. Higher values result in a larger image.
m.ResourceImporterSVG.color_map: If set, remaps texture colors according to Color-Color map.
m.ResourceImporterSVG.compress: If true, uses lossless compression for the SVG source.
m.ResourceImporterSVG.fix_alpha_border: If true, puts pixels of the same surrounding color in transition from transparent to opaque areas. For textures displayed with bilinear filtering, this helps to reduce the outline effect when exporting images from an image editor.
m.ResourceImporterSVG.premult_alpha: An alternative to fixing darkened borders with fix_alpha_border is to use premultiplied alpha. By enabling this option, the texture will be converted to this format. A premultiplied alpha texture requires specific materials to be displayed correctly:
m.ResourceImporterScene._subresources: Contains properties for the scene's subresources. This is an internal option which is not visible in the Import dock.
m.ResourceImporterTextureAtlas.atlas_file: Path to the atlas spritesheet. This must be set to valid path to a PNG image. Otherwise, the atlas will fail to import.
m.ResourceImporterTextureAtlas.crop_to_reg: If true, discards empty areas from the atlas. This only affects final sprite positioning, not storage. See also trim_alpha_border_from_region.
m.ResourceImporterTextureAtlas.import_mode: Region: Imports the atlas in an AtlasTexture resource, which is rendered as a rectangle. This is fast to render, but transparent areas still have to be rendered if they can't be trimmed effectively by trim_alpha_border_from_region. This can reduce performance when rendering large sprites on screen.
m.ResourceImporterTextureAtlas.trim_alpha_: If true, trims the region to exclude fully transparent pixels using a clipping rectangle (which is never rotated). This can be used to save memory. See also crop_to_region.
m.ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_IGNORE: Neither the main resource (the one requested to be loaded) nor any of its subresources are retrieved from cache nor stored into it. Dependencies (external resources) are loaded with CACHE_MODE_REUSE.
m.ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_IGNORE_DEEP: Like CACHE_MODE_IGNORE, but propagated recursively down the tree of dependencies (external resources).
m.ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_REPLACE: Like CACHE_MODE_REUSE, but the cache is checked for the main resource (the one requested to be loaded) as well as for each of its subresources. Those already in the cache, as long as the loaded and cached types match, have their data refreshed from storage into the already existing instances. Otherwise, they are recreated as completely new objects.
m.ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_REPLACE_DEEP: Like CACHE_MODE_REPLACE, but propagated recursively down the tree of dependencies (external resources).
m.ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_REUSE: The main resource (the one requested to be loaded), its subresources, and its dependencies (external resources) are retrieved from cache if present, instead of loaded. Those not cached are loaded and then stored into the cache. The same rules are propagated recursively down the tree of dependencies (external resources).
m.ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_FAILED: Some error occurred during loading and it failed.
m.ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_INVALID_RESOU: The resource is invalid, or has not been loaded with load_threaded_request().
m.ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS: The resource is still being loaded.
m.ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_LOADED: The resource was loaded successfully and can be accessed via load_threaded_get().
m.ResourceLoader.add_resource_format_loade: Registers a new ResourceFormatLoader. The ResourceLoader will use the ResourceFormatLoader as described in load().
m.ResourceLoader.exists: Returns whether a recognized resource exists for the given path.
m.ResourceLoader.get_cached_ref: Returns the cached resource reference for the given path.
m.ResourceLoader.get_dependencies: Returns the dependencies for the resource at the given path.
m.ResourceLoader.get_recognized_extensions: Returns the list of recognized extensions for a resource type.
m.ResourceLoader.get_resource_uid: Returns the ID associated with a given resource path, or -1 when no such ID exists.
m.ResourceLoader.has_cached: Returns whether a cached resource is available for the given path.
m.ResourceLoader.list_directory: Lists a directory, returning all resources and subdirectories contained within. The resource files have the original file names as visible in the editor before exporting. The directories have "/" appended.
m.ResourceLoader.load: Loads a resource at the given path, caching the result for further access.
m.ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get: Returns the resource loaded by load_threaded_request().
m.ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get_status: Returns the status of a threaded loading operation started with load_threaded_request() for the resource at path.
m.ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request: Loads the resource using threads. If use_sub_threads is true, multiple threads will be used to load the resource, which makes loading faster, but may affect the main thread (and thus cause game slowdowns).
m.ResourceLoader.set_abort_on_missing_reso: Changes the behavior on missing sub-resources. The default behavior is to abort loading.
m.ResourcePreloader.add_resource: Adds a resource to the preloader with the given name. If a resource with the given name already exists, the new resource will be renamed to "name N" where N is an incrementing number starting from 2.
m.ResourcePreloader.get_resource: Returns the resource associated to name.
m.ResourcePreloader.get_resource_list: Returns the list of resources inside the preloader.
m.ResourcePreloader.has_resource: Returns true if the preloader contains a resource associated to name.
m.ResourcePreloader.remove_resource: Removes the resource associated to name from the preloader.
m.ResourcePreloader.rename_resource: Renames a resource inside the preloader from name to newname.
m.ResourceSaver.add_resource_format_saver: Registers a new ResourceFormatSaver. The ResourceSaver will use the ResourceFormatSaver as described in save().
m.ResourceSaver.get_recognized_extensions: Returns the list of extensions available for saving a resource of a given type.
m.ResourceSaver.get_resource_id_for_path: Returns the resource ID for the given path. If generate is true, a new resource ID will be generated if one for the path is not found. If generate is false and the path is not found, ResourceUID.INVALID_ID is returned.
m.ResourceSaver.save: Saves a resource to disk to the given path, using a ResourceFormatSaver that recognizes the resource object. If path is empty, ResourceSaver will try to use Resource.resource_path.
m.ResourceSaver.set_uid: Sets the UID of the given resource path to uid. You can generate a new UID using ResourceUID.create_id().
m.ResourceUID.INVALID_ID: The value to use for an invalid UID, for example if the resource could not be loaded.
m.ResourceUID.add_id: Adds a new UID value which is mapped to the given resource path.
m.ResourceUID.create_id: Generates a random resource UID which is guaranteed to be unique within the list of currently loaded UIDs.
m.ResourceUID.create_id_for_path: Like create_id(), but the UID is seeded with the provided path and project name. UIDs generated for that path will be always the same within the current project.
m.ResourceUID.ensure_path: Returns a path, converting path_or_uid if necessary. Fails and returns an empty string if an invalid UID is provided.
m.ResourceUID.get_id_path: Returns the path that the given UID value refers to.
m.ResourceUID.has_id: Returns whether the given UID value is known to the cache.
m.ResourceUID.id_to_text: Converts the given UID to a uid:// string value.
m.ResourceUID.path_to_uid: Converts the provided resource path to a UID. Returns the unchanged path if it has no associated UID.
m.ResourceUID.remove_id: Removes a loaded UID value from the cache.
m.ResourceUID.set_id: Updates the resource path of an existing UID.
m.ResourceUID.text_to_id: Extracts the UID value from the given uid:// string.
m.ResourceUID.uid_to_path: Converts the provided uid to a path. Prints an error if the UID is invalid.
m.RetargetModifier3D.enable: Flags to control the process of the transform elements individually when use_global_pose is disabled.
m.RetargetModifier3D.is_position_enabled: Returns true if enable has TRANSFORM_FLAG_POSITION.
m.RetargetModifier3D.is_rotation_enabled: Returns true if enable has TRANSFORM_FLAG_ROTATION.
m.RetargetModifier3D.is_scale_enabled: Returns true if enable has TRANSFORM_FLAG_SCALE.
m.RetargetModifier3D.profile: SkeletonProfile for retargeting bones with names matching the bone list.
m.RetargetModifier3D.use_global_pose: If false, in case the target skeleton has fewer bones than the source skeleton, the source bone parent's transform will be ignored.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.SHAPE_CROSS: Gives the mesh two perpendicular flat faces, making a cross shape.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.SHAPE_FLAT: Gives the mesh a single flat face.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.curve: Determines the size of the ribbon along its length. The size of a particular section segment is obtained by multiplying the baseline size by the value of this curve at the given distance. For values smaller than 0, the faces will be inverted. Should be a unit Curve.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.section_length: The length of a section of the ribbon.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.section_segments: The number of segments in a section. The curve is sampled on each segment to determine its size. Higher values result in a more detailed ribbon at the cost of performance.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.sections: The total number of sections on the ribbon.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.shape: Determines the shape of the ribbon.
m.RibbonTrailMesh.size: The baseline size of the ribbon. The size of a particular section segment is obtained by multiplying this size by the value of the curve at the given distance.
m.RichTextEffect._process_custom_fx: Override this method to modify properties in char_fx. The method must return true if the character could be transformed successfully. If the method returns false, it will skip transformation to avoid displaying broken text.
m.RichTextLabel.IMAGE_UNIT_EM: Images drawn with this unit will be in percentages of the surrounding font size.
m.RichTextLabel.IMAGE_UNIT_PERCENT: Images drawn with this unit will be in percentages of the control width.
m.RichTextLabel.IMAGE_UNIT_PIXEL: Images drawn with this unit will be in pixels.
m.RichTextLabel.LIST_DOTS: Each list item has a filled circle marker.
m.RichTextLabel.LIST_LETTERS: Each list item has a letter marker.
m.RichTextLabel.LIST_NUMBERS: Each list item has a number marker.
m.RichTextLabel.LIST_ROMAN: Each list item has a roman number marker.
m.RichTextLabel.MENU_MAX: Represents the size of the MenuItems enum.
m.RichTextLabel.META_UNDERLINE_ALWAYS: If meta_underlined is true, meta tag always display an underline.
m.RichTextLabel.META_UNDERLINE_NEVER: Meta tag does not display an underline, even if meta_underlined is true.
m.RichTextLabel.META_UNDERLINE_ON_HOVER: If meta_underlined is true, meta tag display an underline when the mouse cursor is over it.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_ALIGNMENT: If this bit is set, update_image() changes image inline alignment.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_COLOR: If this bit is set, update_image() changes image color.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_PAD: If this bit is set, update_image() changes image padding.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_REGION: If this bit is set, update_image() changes image texture region.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_SIZE: If this bit is set, update_image() changes image size.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_TEXTURE: If this bit is set, update_image() changes image texture.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_TOOLTIP: If this bit is set, update_image() changes image tooltip.
m.RichTextLabel.UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT: If this bit is set, update_image() changes the units used to calculate image size.
m.RichTextLabel.add_hr: Adds a horizontal rule that can be used to separate content.
m.RichTextLabel.add_image: Adds an image's opening and closing tags to the tag stack, optionally providing a width and height to resize the image, a color to tint the image and a region to only use parts of the image.
m.RichTextLabel.add_text: Adds raw non-BBCode-parsed text to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.append_text: Parses bbcode and adds tags to the tag stack as needed.
m.RichTextLabel.autowrap_mode: If set to something other than TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF, the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle.
m.RichTextLabel.autowrap_trim_flags: Autowrap space trimming flags. See TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_START_EDGE_SPACES and TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_END_EDGE_SPACES for more info.
m.RichTextLabel.bbcode_enabled: If true, the label uses BBCode formatting.
m.RichTextLabel.clear: Clears the tag stack, causing the label to display nothing.
m.RichTextLabel.context_menu_enabled: If true, a right-click displays the context menu.
m.RichTextLabel.custom_effects: The currently installed custom effects. This is an array of RichTextEffects.
m.RichTextLabel.deselect_on_focus_loss_ena: If true, the selected text will be deselected when focus is lost.
m.RichTextLabel.drag_and_drop_selection_en: If true, allow drag and drop of selected text.
m.RichTextLabel.finished: Triggered when the document is fully loaded.
m.RichTextLabel.fit_content: If true, the label's minimum size will be automatically updated to fit its content, matching the behavior of Label.
m.RichTextLabel.get_character_line: Returns the line number of the character position provided. Line and character numbers are both zero-indexed.
m.RichTextLabel.get_character_paragraph: Returns the paragraph number of the character position provided. Paragraph and character numbers are both zero-indexed.
m.RichTextLabel.get_content_height: Returns the height of the content.
m.RichTextLabel.get_content_width: Returns the width of the content.
m.RichTextLabel.get_line_count: Returns the total number of lines in the text. Wrapped text is counted as multiple lines.
m.RichTextLabel.get_line_height: Returns the height of the line found at the provided index.
m.RichTextLabel.get_line_offset: Returns the vertical offset of the line found at the provided index.
m.RichTextLabel.get_line_range: Returns the indexes of the first and last visible characters for the given line, as a Vector2i.
m.RichTextLabel.get_line_width: Returns the width of the line found at the provided index.
m.RichTextLabel.get_menu: Returns the PopupMenu of this RichTextLabel. By default, this menu is displayed when right-clicking on the RichTextLabel.
m.RichTextLabel.get_paragraph_count: Returns the total number of paragraphs (newlines or p tags in the tag stack's text tags). Considers wrapped text as one paragraph.
m.RichTextLabel.get_paragraph_offset: Returns the vertical offset of the paragraph found at the provided index.
m.RichTextLabel.get_parsed_text: Returns the text without BBCode mark-up.
m.RichTextLabel.get_selected_text: Returns the current selection text. Does not include BBCodes.
m.RichTextLabel.get_selection_from: Returns the current selection first character index if a selection is active, -1 otherwise. Does not include BBCodes.
m.RichTextLabel.get_selection_line_offset: Returns the current selection vertical line offset if a selection is active, -1.0 otherwise.
m.RichTextLabel.get_selection_to: Returns the current selection last character index if a selection is active, -1 otherwise. Does not include BBCodes.
m.RichTextLabel.get_total_character_count: Returns the total number of characters from text tags. Does not include BBCodes.
m.RichTextLabel.get_visible_content_rect: Returns the bounding rectangle of the visible content.
m.RichTextLabel.get_visible_line_count: Returns the number of visible lines.
m.RichTextLabel.get_visible_paragraph_coun: Returns the number of visible paragraphs. A paragraph is considered visible if at least one of its lines is visible.
m.RichTextLabel.hint_underlined: If true, the label underlines hint tags such as [hint=description]{text}[/hint].
m.RichTextLabel.horizontal_alignment: Controls the text's horizontal alignment. Supports left, center, right, and fill (also known as justify).
m.RichTextLabel.install_effect: Installs a custom effect. This can also be done in the Inspector through the custom_effects property. effect should be a valid RichTextEffect.
m.RichTextLabel.invalidate_paragraph: Invalidates paragraph and all subsequent paragraphs cache.
m.RichTextLabel.is_finished: If threaded is enabled, returns true if the background thread has finished text processing, otherwise always return true.
m.RichTextLabel.is_menu_visible: Returns whether the menu is visible. Use this instead of get_menu().visible to improve performance (so the creation of the menu is avoided).
m.RichTextLabel.language: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.
m.RichTextLabel.menu_option: Executes a given action as defined in the MenuItems enum.
m.RichTextLabel.meta_clicked: Triggered when the user clicks on content between meta (URL) tags. If the meta is defined in BBCode, e.g. Text, then the parameter for this signal will always be a String type. If a particular type or an object is desired, the push_meta() method must be used to manually insert the data into the tag stack. Alternatively, you can convert the String input to the desired type based on its contents (s…
m.RichTextLabel.meta_hover_ended: Triggers when the mouse exits a meta tag.
m.RichTextLabel.meta_hover_started: Triggers when the mouse enters a meta tag.
m.RichTextLabel.meta_underlined: If true, the label underlines meta tags such as {text}. These tags can call a function when clicked if meta_clicked is connected to a function.
m.RichTextLabel.newline: Adds a newline tag to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.parse_bbcode: The assignment version of append_text(). Clears the tag stack and inserts the new content.
m.RichTextLabel.parse_expressions_for_valu: Parses BBCode parameter expressions into a dictionary.
m.RichTextLabel.pop: Terminates the current tag. Use after push_* methods to close BBCodes manually. Does not need to follow add_* methods.
m.RichTextLabel.pop_all: Terminates all tags opened by push_* methods.
m.RichTextLabel.pop_context: Terminates tags opened after the last push_context() call (including context marker), or all tags if there's no context marker on the stack.
m.RichTextLabel.progress_bar_delay: The delay after which the loading progress bar is displayed, in milliseconds. Set to -1 to disable progress bar entirely.
m.RichTextLabel.push_bgcolor: Adds a [bgcolor] tag to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.push_bold: Adds a [font] tag with a bold font to the tag stack. This is the same as adding a [b] tag if not currently in a [i] tag.
m.RichTextLabel.push_bold_italics: Adds a [font] tag with a bold italics font to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.push_cell: Adds a [cell] tag to the tag stack. Must be inside a [table] tag. See push_table() for details. Use set_table_column_expand() to set column expansion ratio, set_cell_border_color() to set cell border, set_cell_row_background_color() to set cell background, set_cell_size_override() to override cell size, and set_cell_padding() to set padding.
m.RichTextLabel.push_color: Adds a [color] tag to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.push_context: Adds a context marker to the tag stack. See pop_context().
m.RichTextLabel.push_customfx: Adds a custom effect tag to the tag stack. The effect does not need to be in custom_effects. The environment is directly passed to the effect.
m.RichTextLabel.push_dropcap: Adds a [dropcap] tag to the tag stack. Drop cap (dropped capital) is a decorative element at the beginning of a paragraph that is larger than the rest of the text.
m.RichTextLabel.push_fgcolor: Adds a [fgcolor] tag to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.push_font: Adds a [font] tag to the tag stack. Overrides default fonts for its duration.
m.RichTextLabel.push_font_size: Adds a [font_size] tag to the tag stack. Overrides default font size for its duration.
m.RichTextLabel.push_hint: Adds a [hint] tag to the tag stack. Same as BBCode [hint=something]{text}[/hint].
m.RichTextLabel.push_indent: Adds an [indent] tag to the tag stack. Multiplies level by current tab_size to determine new margin length.
m.RichTextLabel.push_italics: Adds a [font] tag with an italics font to the tag stack. This is the same as adding an [i] tag if not currently in a [b] tag.
m.RichTextLabel.push_language: Adds language code used for text shaping algorithm and Open-Type font features.
m.RichTextLabel.push_list: Adds [ol] or [ul] tag to the tag stack. Multiplies level by current tab_size to determine new margin length.
m.RichTextLabel.push_meta: Adds a meta tag to the tag stack. Similar to the BBCode {text}, but supports non-String metadata types.
m.RichTextLabel.push_mono: Adds a [font] tag with a monospace font to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.push_normal: Adds a [font] tag with a normal font to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.push_outline_color: Adds a [outline_color] tag to the tag stack. Adds text outline for its duration.
m.RichTextLabel.push_outline_size: Adds a [outline_size] tag to the tag stack. Overrides default text outline size for its duration.
m.RichTextLabel.push_paragraph: Adds a [p] tag to the tag stack.
m.RichTextLabel.push_strikethrough: Adds a [s] tag to the tag stack. If color's alpha value is 0.0, the current font's color with its alpha multiplied by strikethrough_alpha is used.
m.RichTextLabel.push_table: Adds a [table=columns,inline_align] tag to the tag stack. Use set_table_column_expand() to set column expansion ratio. Use push_cell() to add cells. name is used as the table name for assistive apps.
m.RichTextLabel.push_underline: Adds a [u] tag to the tag stack. If color's alpha value is 0.0, the current font's color with its alpha multiplied by underline_alpha is used.
m.RichTextLabel.reload_effects: Reloads custom effects. Useful when custom_effects is modified manually.
m.RichTextLabel.remove_paragraph: Removes a paragraph of content from the label. Returns true if the paragraph exists.
m.RichTextLabel.scroll_active: If true, the scrollbar is visible. Setting this to false does not block scrolling completely. See scroll_to_line().
m.RichTextLabel.scroll_following: If true, the window scrolls down to display new content automatically.
m.RichTextLabel.scroll_following_visible_c: If true, the window scrolls to display the last visible line when visible_characters or visible_ratio is changed.
m.RichTextLabel.scroll_to_line: Scrolls the window's top line to match line.
m.RichTextLabel.scroll_to_paragraph: Scrolls the window's top line to match first line of the paragraph.
m.RichTextLabel.scroll_to_selection: Scrolls to the beginning of the current selection.
m.RichTextLabel.selection_enabled: If true, the label allows text selection.
m.RichTextLabel.set_cell_border_color: Sets color of a table cell border.
m.RichTextLabel.set_cell_padding: Sets inner padding of a table cell.
m.RichTextLabel.set_cell_row_background_co: Sets color of a table cell. Separate colors for alternating rows can be specified.
m.RichTextLabel.set_cell_size_override: Sets minimum and maximum size overrides for a table cell.
m.RichTextLabel.set_table_column_expand: Edits the selected column's expansion options. If expand is true, the column expands in proportion to its expansion ratio versus the other columns' ratios.
m.RichTextLabel.set_table_column_name: Sets table column name for assistive apps.
m.RichTextLabel.shortcut_keys_enabled: If true, shortcut keys for context menu items are enabled, even if the context menu is disabled.
m.RichTextLabel.structured_text_bidi_overr: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.
Set additional options for BiDi override.
m.RichTextLabel.tab_size: The number of spaces associated with a single tab length. Does not affect \t in text tags, only indent tags.
m.RichTextLabel.tab_stops: Aligns text to the given tab-stops.
m.RichTextLabel.text: The label's text in BBCode format. Is not representative of manual modifications to the internal tag stack. Erases changes made by other methods when edited.
m.RichTextLabel.threaded: If true, text processing is done in a background thread.
m.RichTextLabel.update_image: Updates the existing images with the key key. Only properties specified by mask bits are updated. See add_image().
m.RichTextLabel.vertical_alignment: Controls the text's vertical alignment. Supports top, center, bottom, and fill.
m.RichTextLabel.visible_characters: The number of characters to display. If set to -1, all characters are displayed. This can be useful when animating the text appearing in a dialog box.
m.RichTextLabel.visible_characters_behavio: The clipping behavior when visible_characters or visible_ratio is set.
m.RichTextLabel.visible_ratio: The fraction of characters to display, relative to the total number of characters (see get_total_character_count()). If set to 1.0, all characters are displayed. If set to 0.5, only half of the characters will be displayed. This can be useful when animating the text appearing in a dialog box.
m.RigidBody2D.CCD_MODE_CAST_RAY: Continuous collision detection enabled using raycasting. This is faster than shapecasting but less precise.
m.RigidBody2D.CCD_MODE_CAST_SHAPE: Continuous collision detection enabled using shapecasting. This is the slowest CCD method and the most precise.
m.RigidBody2D.CCD_MODE_DISABLED: Continuous collision detection disabled. This is the fastest way to detect body collisions, but can miss small, fast-moving objects.
m.RigidBody2D.CENTER_OF_MASS_MODE_AUTO: In this mode, the body's center of mass is calculated automatically based on its shapes. This assumes that the shapes' origins are also their center of mass.
m.RigidBody2D.CENTER_OF_MASS_MODE_CUSTOM: In this mode, the body's center of mass is set through center_of_mass. Defaults to the body's origin position.
m.RigidBody2D.DAMP_MODE_COMBINE: In this mode, the body's damping value is added to any value set in areas or the default value.
m.RigidBody2D.DAMP_MODE_REPLACE: In this mode, the body's damping value replaces any value set in areas or the default value.
m.RigidBody2D.FREEZE_MODE_KINEMATIC: Kinematic body freeze mode. Similar to FREEZE_MODE_STATIC, but collides with other bodies along its path when moved. Useful for a frozen body that needs to be animated.
m.RigidBody2D.FREEZE_MODE_STATIC: Static body freeze mode (default). The body is not affected by gravity and forces. It can be only moved by user code and doesn't collide with other bodies along its path.
m.RigidBody2D._integrate_forces: Called during physics processing, allowing you to read and safely modify the simulation state for the object. By default, it is called before the standard force integration, but the custom_integrator property allows you to disable the standard force integration and do fully custom force integration for a body.
m.RigidBody2D.add_constant_central_force: Adds a constant directional force without affecting rotation that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_force = Vector2(0, 0).
m.RigidBody2D.add_constant_force: Adds a constant positioned force to the body that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_force = Vector2(0, 0).
m.RigidBody2D.add_constant_torque: Adds a constant rotational force without affecting position that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_torque = 0.
m.RigidBody2D.angular_damp: Damps the body's rotation. By default, the body will use the ProjectSettings.physics/2d/default_angular_damp setting or any value override set by an Area2D the body is in. Depending on angular_damp_mode, you can set angular_damp to be added to or to replace the body's damping value.
m.RigidBody2D.angular_velocity: The body's rotational velocity in radians per second.
m.RigidBody2D.apply_central_force: Applies a directional force without affecting rotation. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
m.RigidBody2D.apply_central_impulse: Applies a directional impulse without affecting rotation.
m.RigidBody2D.apply_force: Applies a positioned force to the body. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
m.RigidBody2D.apply_impulse: Applies a positioned impulse to the body.
m.RigidBody2D.apply_torque: Applies a rotational force without affecting position. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
m.RigidBody2D.apply_torque_impulse: Applies a rotational impulse to the body without affecting the position.
m.RigidBody2D.body_entered: Emitted when a collision with another PhysicsBody2D or TileMap occurs. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. TileMaps are detected if the TileSet has Collision Shape2Ds.
m.RigidBody2D.body_exited: Emitted when the collision with another PhysicsBody2D or TileMap ends. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. TileMaps are detected if the TileSet has Collision Shape2Ds.
m.RigidBody2D.body_shape_entered: Emitted when one of this RigidBody2D's Shape2Ds collides with another PhysicsBody2D or TileMap's Shape2Ds. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. TileMaps are detected if the TileSet has Collision Shape2Ds.
m.RigidBody2D.body_shape_exited: Emitted when the collision between one of this RigidBody2D's Shape2Ds and another PhysicsBody2D or TileMap's Shape2Ds ends. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. TileMaps are detected if the TileSet has Collision Shape2Ds.
m.RigidBody2D.can_sleep: If true, the body can enter sleep mode when there is no movement. See sleeping.
m.RigidBody2D.center_of_mass: The body's custom center of mass, relative to the body's origin position, when center_of_mass_mode is set to CENTER_OF_MASS_MODE_CUSTOM. This is the balanced point of the body, where applied forces only cause linear acceleration. Applying forces outside of the center of mass causes angular acceleration.
m.RigidBody2D.center_of_mass_mode: Defines the way the body's center of mass is set.
m.RigidBody2D.constant_force: The body's total constant positional forces applied during each physics update.
m.RigidBody2D.constant_torque: The body's total constant rotational forces applied during each physics update.
m.RigidBody2D.contact_monitor: If true, the RigidBody2D will emit signals when it collides with another body.
m.RigidBody2D.custom_integrator: If true, the standard force integration (like gravity or damping) will be disabled for this body. Other than collision response, the body will only move as determined by the _integrate_forces() method, if that virtual method is overridden.
m.RigidBody2D.freeze: If true, the body is frozen. Gravity and forces are not applied anymore.
m.RigidBody2D.freeze_mode: The body's freeze mode. Determines the body's behavior when freeze is true.
m.RigidBody2D.get_colliding_bodies: Returns a list of the bodies colliding with this one. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions.
m.RigidBody2D.get_contact_count: Returns the number of contacts this body has with other bodies. By default, this returns 0 unless bodies are configured to monitor contacts (see contact_monitor).
m.RigidBody2D.gravity_scale: Multiplies the gravity applied to the body. The body's gravity is calculated from the ProjectSettings.physics/2d/default_gravity project setting and/or any additional gravity vector applied by Area2Ds.
m.RigidBody2D.inertia: The body's moment of inertia. This is like mass, but for rotation: it determines how much torque it takes to rotate the body. The moment of inertia is usually computed automatically from the mass and the shapes, but this property allows you to set a custom value.
m.RigidBody2D.linear_damp: Damps the body's movement. By default, the body will use the ProjectSettings.physics/2d/default_linear_damp setting or any value override set by an Area2D the body is in. Depending on linear_damp_mode, you can set linear_damp to be added to or to replace the body's damping value.
m.RigidBody2D.linear_velocity: The body's linear velocity in pixels per second. Can be used sporadically, but don't set this every frame, because physics may run in another thread and runs at a different granularity. Use _integrate_forces() as your process loop for precise control of the body state.
m.RigidBody2D.lock_rotation: If true, the body cannot rotate. Gravity and forces only apply linear movement.
m.RigidBody2D.max_contacts_reported: The maximum number of contacts that will be recorded. Requires a value greater than 0 and contact_monitor to be set to true to start to register contacts. Use get_contact_count() to retrieve the count or get_colliding_bodies() to retrieve bodies that have been collided with.
m.RigidBody2D.physics_material_override: The physics material override for the body.
m.RigidBody2D.set_axis_velocity: Sets the body's velocity on the given axis. The velocity in the given vector axis will be set as the given vector length. This is useful for jumping behavior.
m.RigidBody2D.sleeping: If true, the body will not move and will not calculate forces until woken up by another body through, for example, a collision, or by using the apply_impulse() or apply_force() methods.
m.RigidBody2D.sleeping_state_changed: Emitted when the physics engine changes the body's sleeping state.
m.RigidBody3D.CENTER_OF_MASS_MODE_AUTO: In this mode, the body's center of mass is calculated automatically based on its shapes. This assumes that the shapes' origins are also their center of mass.
m.RigidBody3D.CENTER_OF_MASS_MODE_CUSTOM: In this mode, the body's center of mass is set through center_of_mass. Defaults to the body's origin position.
m.RigidBody3D.DAMP_MODE_COMBINE: In this mode, the body's damping value is added to any value set in areas or the default value.
m.RigidBody3D.DAMP_MODE_REPLACE: In this mode, the body's damping value replaces any value set in areas or the default value.
m.RigidBody3D.FREEZE_MODE_KINEMATIC: Kinematic body freeze mode. Similar to FREEZE_MODE_STATIC, but collides with other bodies along its path when moved. Useful for a frozen body that needs to be animated.
m.RigidBody3D.FREEZE_MODE_STATIC: Static body freeze mode (default). The body is not affected by gravity and forces. It can be only moved by user code and doesn't collide with other bodies along its path.
m.RigidBody3D._integrate_forces: Called during physics processing, allowing you to read and safely modify the simulation state for the object. By default, it is called before the standard force integration, but the custom_integrator property allows you to disable the standard force integration and do fully custom force integration for a body.
m.RigidBody3D.add_constant_central_force: Adds a constant directional force without affecting rotation that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_force = Vector3(0, 0, 0).
m.RigidBody3D.add_constant_force: Adds a constant positioned force to the body that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_force = Vector3(0, 0, 0).
m.RigidBody3D.add_constant_torque: Adds a constant rotational force without affecting position that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_torque = Vector3(0, 0, 0).
m.RigidBody3D.angular_damp: Damps the body's rotation. By default, the body will use the ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_angular_damp project setting or any value override set by an Area3D the body is in. Depending on angular_damp_mode, you can set angular_damp to be added to or to replace the body's damping value.
m.RigidBody3D.angular_velocity: The RigidBody3D's rotational velocity in radians per second.
m.RigidBody3D.apply_central_force: Applies a directional force without affecting rotation. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
m.RigidBody3D.apply_central_impulse: Applies a directional impulse without affecting rotation.
m.RigidBody3D.apply_force: Applies a positioned force to the body. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
m.RigidBody3D.apply_impulse: Applies a positioned impulse to the body.
m.RigidBody3D.apply_torque: Applies a rotational force without affecting position. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
m.RigidBody3D.apply_torque_impulse: Applies a rotational impulse to the body without affecting the position.
m.RigidBody3D.body_entered: Emitted when a collision with another PhysicsBody3D or GridMap occurs. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. GridMaps are detected if the MeshLibrary has Collision Shape3Ds.
m.RigidBody3D.body_exited: Emitted when the collision with another PhysicsBody3D or GridMap ends. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. GridMaps are detected if the MeshLibrary has Collision Shape3Ds.
m.RigidBody3D.body_shape_entered: Emitted when one of this RigidBody3D's Shape3Ds collides with another PhysicsBody3D or GridMap's Shape3Ds. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. GridMaps are detected if the MeshLibrary has Collision Shape3Ds.
m.RigidBody3D.body_shape_exited: Emitted when the collision between one of this RigidBody3D's Shape3Ds and another PhysicsBody3D or GridMap's Shape3Ds ends. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions. GridMaps are detected if the MeshLibrary has Collision Shape3Ds.
m.RigidBody3D.can_sleep: If true, the body can enter sleep mode when there is no movement. See sleeping.
m.RigidBody3D.center_of_mass: The body's custom center of mass, relative to the body's origin position, when center_of_mass_mode is set to CENTER_OF_MASS_MODE_CUSTOM. This is the balanced point of the body, where applied forces only cause linear acceleration. Applying forces outside of the center of mass causes angular acceleration.
m.RigidBody3D.center_of_mass_mode: Defines the way the body's center of mass is set.
m.RigidBody3D.constant_force: The body's total constant positional forces applied during each physics update.
m.RigidBody3D.constant_torque: The body's total constant rotational forces applied during each physics update.
m.RigidBody3D.contact_monitor: If true, the RigidBody3D will emit signals when it collides with another body.
m.RigidBody3D.continuous_cd: If true, continuous collision detection is used.
m.RigidBody3D.custom_integrator: If true, the standard force integration (like gravity or damping) will be disabled for this body. Other than collision response, the body will only move as determined by the _integrate_forces() method, if that virtual method is overridden.
m.RigidBody3D.freeze: If true, the body is frozen. Gravity and forces are not applied anymore.
m.RigidBody3D.freeze_mode: The body's freeze mode. Determines the body's behavior when freeze is true.
m.RigidBody3D.get_colliding_bodies: Returns a list of the bodies colliding with this one. Requires contact_monitor to be set to true and max_contacts_reported to be set high enough to detect all the collisions.
m.RigidBody3D.get_contact_count: Returns the number of contacts this body has with other bodies. By default, this returns 0 unless bodies are configured to monitor contacts (see contact_monitor).
m.RigidBody3D.get_inverse_inertia_tensor: Returns the inverse inertia tensor basis. This is used to calculate the angular acceleration resulting from a torque applied to the RigidBody3D.
m.RigidBody3D.gravity_scale: This is multiplied by ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_gravity to produce this body's gravity. For example, a value of 1.0 will apply normal gravity, 2.0 will apply double the gravity, and 0.5 will apply half the gravity to this body.
m.RigidBody3D.inertia: The body's moment of inertia. This is like mass, but for rotation: it determines how much torque it takes to rotate the body on each axis. The moment of inertia is usually computed automatically from the mass and the shapes, but this property allows you to set a custom value.
m.RigidBody3D.linear_damp: Damps the body's movement. By default, the body will use the ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_linear_damp project setting or any value override set by an Area3D the body is in. Depending on linear_damp_mode, you can set linear_damp to be added to or to replace the body's damping value.
m.RigidBody3D.linear_velocity: The body's linear velocity in units per second. Can be used sporadically, but don't set this every frame, because physics may run in another thread and runs at a different granularity. Use _integrate_forces() as your process loop for precise control of the body state.
m.RigidBody3D.lock_rotation: If true, the body cannot rotate. Gravity and forces only apply linear movement.
m.RigidBody3D.max_contacts_reported: The maximum number of contacts that will be recorded. Requires a value greater than 0 and contact_monitor to be set to true to start to register contacts. Use get_contact_count() to retrieve the count or get_colliding_bodies() to retrieve bodies that have been collided with.
m.RigidBody3D.physics_material_override: The physics material override for the body.
m.RigidBody3D.set_axis_velocity: Sets an axis velocity. The velocity in the given vector axis will be set as the given vector length. This is useful for jumping behavior.
m.RigidBody3D.sleeping: If true, the body will not move and will not calculate forces until woken up by another body through, for example, a collision, or by using the apply_impulse() or apply_force() methods.
m.RigidBody3D.sleeping_state_changed: Emitted when the physics engine changes the body's sleeping state.
m.RootMotionView.animation_path: Path to an AnimationMixer node to use as a basis for root motion.
m.RootMotionView.cell_size: The grid's cell size in 3D units.
m.RootMotionView.radius: The grid's radius in 3D units. The grid's opacity will fade gradually as the distance from the origin increases until this radius is reached.
m.RootMotionView.zero_y: If true, the grid's points will all be on the same Y coordinate (local Y = 0). If false, the points' original Y coordinate is preserved.
m.SceneMultiplayer.allow_object_decoding: If true, the MultiplayerAPI will allow encoding and decoding of object during RPCs.
m.SceneMultiplayer.auth_callback: The callback to execute when receiving authentication data sent via send_auth(). If the Callable is empty (default), peers will be automatically accepted as soon as they connect.
m.SceneMultiplayer.auth_timeout: If set to a value greater than 0.0, the maximum duration in seconds peers can stay in the authenticating state, after which the authentication will automatically fail. See the peer_authenticating and peer_authentication_failed signals.
m.SceneMultiplayer.clear: Clears the current SceneMultiplayer network state (you shouldn't call this unless you know what you are doing).
m.SceneMultiplayer.complete_auth: Mark the authentication step as completed for the remote peer identified by id. The MultiplayerAPI.peer_connected signal will be emitted for this peer once the remote side also completes the authentication. No further authentication messages are expected to be received from this peer.
m.SceneMultiplayer.disconnect_peer: Disconnects the peer identified by id, removing it from the list of connected peers, and closing the underlying connection with it.
m.SceneMultiplayer.get_authenticating_peer: Returns the IDs of the peers currently trying to authenticate with this MultiplayerAPI.
m.SceneMultiplayer.max_delta_packet_size: Maximum size of each delta packet. Higher values increase the chance of receiving full updates in a single frame, but also the chance of causing networking congestion (higher latency, disconnections). See MultiplayerSynchronizer.
m.SceneMultiplayer.max_sync_packet_size: Maximum size of each synchronization packet. Higher values increase the chance of receiving full updates in a single frame, but also the chance of packet loss. See MultiplayerSynchronizer.
m.SceneMultiplayer.peer_authenticating: Emitted when this MultiplayerAPI's MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer connects to a new peer and a valid auth_callback is set. In this case, the MultiplayerAPI.peer_connected will not be emitted until complete_auth() is called with given peer id. While in this state, the peer will not be included in the list returned by MultiplayerAPI.get_peers() (but in the one returned by get_authenticating_peers(…
m.SceneMultiplayer.peer_authentication_fai: Emitted when this MultiplayerAPI's MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer disconnects from a peer for which authentication had not yet completed. See peer_authenticating.
m.SceneMultiplayer.peer_packet: Emitted when this MultiplayerAPI's MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer receives a packet with custom data (see send_bytes()). ID is the peer ID of the peer that sent the packet.
m.SceneMultiplayer.refuse_new_connections: If true, the MultiplayerAPI's MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer refuses new incoming connections.
m.SceneMultiplayer.root_path: The root path to use for RPCs and replication. Instead of an absolute path, a relative path will be used to find the node upon which the RPC should be executed.
m.SceneMultiplayer.send_auth: Sends the specified data to the remote peer identified by id as part of an authentication message. This can be used to authenticate peers, and control when MultiplayerAPI.peer_connected is emitted (and the remote peer accepted as one of the connected peers).
m.SceneMultiplayer.send_bytes: Sends the given raw bytes to a specific peer identified by id (see MultiplayerPeer.set_target_peer()). Default ID is 0, i.e. broadcast to all peers.
m.SceneMultiplayer.server_relay: Enable or disable the server feature that notifies clients of other peers' connection/disconnection, and relays messages between them. When this option is false, clients won't be automatically notified of other peers and won't be able to send them packets through the server.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.REPLICATION_MODE_: Replicate the given property on process by constantly sending updates using unreliable transfer mode.
Do not keep the given property synchronized.
Replicate the given property on process by sending updates using reliable transfer mode when its value changes.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.add_property: Adds the property identified by the given path to the list of the properties being synchronized, optionally passing an index.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.get_properties: Returns a list of synchronized property NodePaths.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.has_property: Returns true if the given path is configured for synchronization.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.property_get_inde: Finds the index of the given path.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.property_get_repl: Returns the replication mode for the property identified by the given path.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.property_get_spaw: Returns true if the property identified by the given path is configured to be synchronized on spawn.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.property_set_repl: Sets the synchronization mode for the property identified by the given path.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.property_set_spaw: Sets whether the property identified by the given path is configured to be synchronized on spawn.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.property_set_sync: Deprecated: Use property_set_replication_mode() with REPLICATION_MODE_ALWAYS instead.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.property_set_watc: Deprecated: Use property_set_replication_mode() with REPLICATION_MODE_ON_CHANGE instead.
m.SceneReplicationConfig.remove_property: Removes the property identified by the given path from the configuration.
m.SceneState.GEN_EDIT_STATE_DISABLED: If passed to PackedScene.instantiate(), blocks edits to the scene state.
m.SceneState.GEN_EDIT_STATE_INSTANCE: If passed to PackedScene.instantiate(), provides inherited scene resources to the local scene.
m.SceneState.GEN_EDIT_STATE_MAIN: If passed to PackedScene.instantiate(), provides local scene resources to the local scene. Only the main scene should receive the main edit state.
m.SceneState.GEN_EDIT_STATE_MAIN_INHERITED: If passed to PackedScene.instantiate(), it's similar to GEN_EDIT_STATE_MAIN, but for the case where the scene is being instantiated to be the base of another one.
m.SceneState.get_base_scene_state: Returns the SceneState of the scene that this scene inherits from, or null if it doesn't inherit from any scene.
m.SceneState.get_connection_binds: Returns the list of bound parameters for the signal at idx.
m.SceneState.get_connection_count: Returns the number of signal connections in the scene.
m.SceneState.get_connection_flags: Returns the connection flags for the signal at idx. See ConnectFlags constants.
m.SceneState.get_connection_method: Returns the method connected to the signal at idx.
m.SceneState.get_connection_signal: Returns the name of the signal at idx.
m.SceneState.get_connection_source: Returns the path to the node that owns the signal at idx, relative to the root node.
m.SceneState.get_connection_target: Returns the path to the node that owns the method connected to the signal at idx, relative to the root node.
m.SceneState.get_connection_unbinds: Returns the number of unbound parameters for the signal at idx.
m.SceneState.get_node_count: Returns the number of nodes in the scene.
m.SceneState.get_node_groups: Returns the list of group names associated with the node at idx.
m.SceneState.get_node_index: Returns the node's index, which is its position relative to its siblings. This is only relevant and saved in scenes for cases where new nodes are added to an instantiated or inherited scene among siblings from the base scene. Despite the name, this index is not related to the idx argument used here and in other methods.
m.SceneState.get_node_instance: Returns a PackedScene for the node at idx (i.e. the whole branch starting at this node, with its child nodes and resources), or null if the node is not an instance.
m.SceneState.get_node_instance_placeholder: Returns the path to the represented scene file if the node at idx is an InstancePlaceholder.
m.SceneState.get_node_name: Returns the name of the node at idx.
m.SceneState.get_node_owner_path: Returns the path to the owner of the node at idx, relative to the root node.
m.SceneState.get_node_path: Returns the path to the node at idx.
m.SceneState.get_node_property_count: Returns the number of exported or overridden properties for the node at idx.
m.SceneState.get_node_property_name: Returns the name of the property at prop_idx for the node at idx.
m.SceneState.get_node_property_value: Returns the value of the property at prop_idx for the node at idx.
m.SceneState.get_node_type: Returns the type of the node at idx.
m.SceneState.get_path: Returns the resource path to the represented PackedScene.
m.SceneState.is_node_instance_placeholder: Returns true if the node at idx is an InstancePlaceholder.
m.SceneTree.GROUP_CALL_DEFAULT: Call nodes within a group with no special behavior (default).
m.SceneTree.GROUP_CALL_DEFERRED: Call nodes within a group at the end of the current frame (can be either process or physics frame), similar to Object.call_deferred().
m.SceneTree.GROUP_CALL_REVERSE: Call nodes within a group in reverse tree hierarchy order (all nested children are called before their respective parent nodes).
m.SceneTree.GROUP_CALL_UNIQUE: Call nodes within a group only once, even if the call is executed many times in the same frame. Must be combined with GROUP_CALL_DEFERRED to work.
m.SceneTree.auto_accept_quit: If true, the application automatically accepts quitting requests.
m.SceneTree.call_group: Calls method on each node inside this tree added to the given group. You can pass arguments to method by specifying them at the end of this method call. Nodes that cannot call method (either because the method doesn't exist or the arguments do not match) are ignored. See also set_group() and notify_group().
m.SceneTree.call_group_flags: Calls the given method on each node inside this tree added to the given group. Use flags to customize this method's behavior (see GroupCallFlags). Additional arguments for method can be passed at the end of this method. Nodes that cannot call method (either because the method doesn't exist or the arguments do not match) are ignored.
m.SceneTree.change_scene_to_file: Changes the running scene to the one at the given path, after loading it into a PackedScene and creating a new instance.
m.SceneTree.change_scene_to_node: Changes the running scene to the provided Node. Useful when you want to set up the new scene before changing.
m.SceneTree.change_scene_to_packed: Changes the running scene to a new instance of the given PackedScene (which must be valid).
m.SceneTree.create_timer: 创建一次性计时器。await create_timer(1.0).timeout 等待 1 秒。
m.SceneTree.create_tween: Creates and returns a new Tween processed in this tree. The Tween will start automatically on the next process frame or physics frame (depending on its TweenProcessMode).
m.SceneTree.current_scene: 当前运行场景的根节点。
m.SceneTree.debug_collisions_hint: If true, collision shapes will be visible when running the game from the editor for debugging purposes.
m.SceneTree.debug_navigation_hint: If true, navigation polygons will be visible when running the game from the editor for debugging purposes.
m.SceneTree.debug_paths_hint: If true, curves from Path2D and Path3D nodes will be visible when running the game from the editor for debugging purposes.
m.SceneTree.edited_scene_root: The root of the scene currently being edited in the editor. This is usually a direct child of root.
m.SceneTree.get_first_node_in_group: Returns the first Node found inside the tree, that has been added to the given group, in scene hierarchy order. Returns null if no match is found. See also get_nodes_in_group().
m.SceneTree.get_frame: Returns how many physics process steps have been processed, since the application started. This is not a measurement of elapsed time. See also physics_frame. For the number of frames rendered, see Engine.get_process_frames().
m.SceneTree.get_multiplayer: Searches for the MultiplayerAPI configured for the given path, if one does not exist it searches the parent paths until one is found. If the path is empty, or none is found, the default one is returned. See set_multiplayer().
m.SceneTree.get_node_count: Returns the number of nodes inside this tree.
m.SceneTree.get_node_count_in_group: Returns the number of nodes assigned to the given group.
m.SceneTree.get_nodes_in_group: Returns an Array containing all nodes inside this tree, that have been added to the given group, in scene hierarchy order.
m.SceneTree.get_processed_tweens: Returns an Array of currently existing Tweens in the tree, including paused tweens.
m.SceneTree.has_group: Returns true if a node added to the given group name exists in the tree.
m.SceneTree.is_accessibility_enabled: Returns true if accessibility features are enabled, and accessibility information updates are actively processed.
m.SceneTree.is_accessibility_supported: Returns true if accessibility features are supported by the OS and enabled in project settings.
m.SceneTree.multiplayer_poll: If true (default value), enables automatic polling of the MultiplayerAPI for this SceneTree during process_frame.
m.SceneTree.node_added: Emitted when the node enters this tree.
m.SceneTree.node_configuration_warning_cha: Emitted when the node's Node.update_configuration_warnings() is called. Only emitted in the editor.
m.SceneTree.node_removed: Emitted when the node exits this tree.
m.SceneTree.node_renamed: Emitted when the node's Node.name is changed.
m.SceneTree.notify_group: Calls Object.notification() with the given notification to all nodes inside this tree added to the group. See also Godot notifications and call_group() and set_group().
m.SceneTree.notify_group_flags: Calls Object.notification() with the given notification to all nodes inside this tree added to the group. Use call_flags to customize this method's behavior (see GroupCallFlags).
m.SceneTree.paused: If true, the scene tree is considered paused. This causes the following behavior:
m.SceneTree.physics_frame: Emitted immediately before Node._physics_process() is called on every node in this tree.
m.SceneTree.physics_interpolation: If true, the renderer will interpolate the transforms of objects (both physics and non-physics) between the last two transforms, so that smooth motion is seen even when physics ticks do not coincide with rendered frames.
m.SceneTree.process_frame: Emitted immediately before Node._process() is called on every node in this tree.
m.SceneTree.queue_delete: Queues the given obj to be deleted, calling its Object.free() at the end of the current frame. This method is similar to Node.queue_free().
m.SceneTree.quit_on_go_back: If true, the application quits automatically when navigating back (e.g. using the system "Back" button on Android).
m.SceneTree.reload_current_scene: Reloads the currently active scene, replacing current_scene with a new instance of its original PackedScene.
m.SceneTree.scene_changed: Emitted after the new scene is added to scene tree and initialized. Can be used to reliably access current_scene when changing scenes.
m.SceneTree.set_group: Sets the given property to value on all nodes inside this tree added to the given group. Nodes that do not have the property are ignored. See also call_group() and notify_group().
m.SceneTree.set_group_flags: Sets the given property to value on all nodes inside this tree added to the given group. Nodes that do not have the property are ignored. Use call_flags to customize this method's behavior (see GroupCallFlags).
m.SceneTree.set_multiplayer: Sets a custom MultiplayerAPI with the given root_path (controlling also the relative subpaths), or override the default one if root_path is empty.
m.SceneTree.tree_changed: Emitted any time the tree's hierarchy changes (nodes being moved, renamed, etc.).
m.SceneTree.tree_process_mode_changed: Emitted when the Node.process_mode of any node inside the tree is changed. Only emitted in the editor, to update the visibility of disabled nodes.
m.SceneTree.unload_current_scene: If a current scene is loaded, calling this method will unload it.
m.Script.can_instantiate: Returns true if the script can be instantiated.
m.Script.get_base_script: Returns the script directly inherited by this script.
m.Script.get_global_name: Returns the class name associated with the script, if there is one. Returns an empty string otherwise.
m.Script.get_property_default_value: Returns the default value of the specified property.
m.Script.get_rpc_config: Returns a Dictionary mapping method names to their RPC configuration defined by this script.
m.Script.get_script_constant_map: Returns a dictionary containing constant names and their values.
m.Script.get_script_method_list: Returns the list of methods in this Script.
m.Script.get_script_property_list: Returns the list of properties in this Script.
m.Script.get_script_signal_list: Returns the list of signals defined in this Script.
m.Script.has_script_method: Returns true if the script, or a base class, defines a method with the given name.
m.Script.has_script_signal: Returns true if the script, or a base class, defines a signal with the given name.
m.Script.has_source_code: Returns true if the script contains non-empty source code.
m.Script.instance_has: Deprecated: Compare this script with Object.get_script() instead.
m.Script.is_abstract: Returns true if the script is an abstract script. An abstract script does not have a constructor and cannot be instantiated.
m.Script.is_tool: Returns true if the script is a tool script. A tool script can run in the editor.
m.Script.reload: Reloads the script's class implementation. Returns an error code.
m.Script.source_code: The script source code or an empty string if source code is not available. When set, does not reload the class implementation automatically.
m.ScriptBacktrace.format: Converts the backtrace to a String, where the entire string will be indented by indent_all number of spaces, and the individual stack frames will be additionally indented by indent_frames number of spaces.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_frame_count: Returns the number of stack frames in the backtrace.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_frame_file: Returns the file name of the call site represented by the stack frame at the specified index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_frame_function: Returns the name of the function called at the stack frame at the specified index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_frame_line: Returns the line number of the call site represented by the stack frame at the specified index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_global_variable_coun: Returns the number of global variables (e.g. autoload singletons) in the backtrace.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_global_variable_name: Returns the name of the global variable at the specified index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_global_variable_valu: Returns the value of the global variable at the specified index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_language_name: Returns the name of the script language that this backtrace was captured from.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_local_variable_count: Returns the number of local variables in the stack frame at the specified index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_local_variable_name: Returns the name of the local variable at the specified variable_index in the stack frame at the specified frame_index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_local_variable_value: Returns the value of the local variable at the specified variable_index in the stack frame at the specified frame_index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_member_variable_coun: Returns the number of member variables in the stack frame at the specified index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_member_variable_name: Returns the name of the member variable at the specified variable_index in the stack frame at the specified frame_index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.get_member_variable_valu: Returns the value of the member variable at the specified variable_index in the stack frame at the specified frame_index.
m.ScriptBacktrace.is_empty: Returns true if the backtrace has no stack frames.
m.ScriptCreateDialog.config: Prefills required fields to configure the ScriptCreateDialog for use.
m.ScriptCreateDialog.script_created: Emitted when the user clicks the OK button.
m.ScriptEditor.clear_docs_from_script: Removes the documentation for the given script.
m.ScriptEditor.close_file: Closes the file at the given path, discarding any unsaved changes.
m.ScriptEditor.editor_script_changed: Emitted when user changed active script. Argument is a freshly activated Script.
m.ScriptEditor.get_current_editor: Returns the ScriptEditorBase object that the user is currently editing.
m.ScriptEditor.get_current_script: Returns a Script that is currently active in editor.
m.ScriptEditor.get_open_script_editors: Returns an array with all ScriptEditorBase objects which are currently open in editor.
m.ScriptEditor.get_open_scripts: Returns an array with all Script objects which are currently open in editor.
m.ScriptEditor.get_unsaved_files: Returns an array of file paths of scripts with unsaved changes open in the editor.
m.ScriptEditor.goto_help: Opens help for the given topic. The topic is an encoded string that controls which class, method, constant, signal, annotation, property, or theme item should be focused.
m.ScriptEditor.goto_line: Goes to the specified line in the current script.
m.ScriptEditor.open_script_create_dialog: Opens the script create dialog. The script will extend base_name. The file extension can be omitted from base_path. It will be added based on the selected scripting language.
m.ScriptEditor.register_syntax_highlighter: Registers the EditorSyntaxHighlighter to the editor, the EditorSyntaxHighlighter will be available on all open scripts.
m.ScriptEditor.reload_open_files: Reloads all currently opened files. This should be used when opened files are changed outside of the script editor. The user may be prompted to resolve file conflicts, see EditorSettings.text_editor/behavior/files/auto_reload_scripts_on_external_change.
m.ScriptEditor.script_close: Emitted when editor is about to close the active script. Argument is a Script that is going to be closed.
m.ScriptEditor.unregister_syntax_highlight: Unregisters the EditorSyntaxHighlighter from the editor.
m.ScriptEditor.update_docs_from_script: Updates the documentation for the given script.
m.ScriptEditorBase.add_syntax_highlighter: Adds an EditorSyntaxHighlighter to the open script.
m.ScriptEditorBase.get_base_editor: Returns the underlying Control used for editing scripts. For text scripts, this is a CodeEdit.
m.ScriptEditorBase.go_to_help: Emitted when the user requests a specific documentation page.
m.ScriptEditorBase.go_to_method: Emitted when the user requests to view a specific method of a script, similar to request_open_script_at_line.
m.ScriptEditorBase.name_changed: Emitted after script validation or when the edited resource has changed.
m.ScriptEditorBase.replace_in_files_reques: Emitted when the user request to find and replace text in the file system.
m.ScriptEditorBase.request_help: Emitted when the user requests contextual help.
m.ScriptEditorBase.request_open_script_at_: Emitted when the user requests to view a specific line of a script, similar to go_to_method.
m.ScriptEditorBase.request_save_history: Emitted when the user contextual goto and the item is in the same script.
m.ScriptEditorBase.request_save_previous_s: Emitted when the user changes current script or moves caret by 10 or more columns within the same script.
m.ScriptEditorBase.search_in_files_request: Emitted when the user request to search text in the file system.

m.ScriptLanguageExtension.LOCATION_OTHER: The option is from other engine code, not covered by the other enum constants - e.g. built-in classes.
m.ScriptLanguageExtension.LOCATION_OTHER_U: The option is from user code which is not local and not in a derived class (e.g. Autoload Singletons).
m.ScriptLanguageExtension.LOCATION_PARENT_: The option is from the containing class or a parent class, relative to the location of the code completion query. Perform a bitwise OR with the class depth (e.g. 0 for the local class, 1 for the parent, 2 for the grandparent, etc.) to store the depth of an option in the class or a parent class.
