m.TileSet.move_occlusion_layer: Moves the occlusion layer at index layer_index to the given position to_position in the array. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.move_physics_layer: Moves the physics layer at index layer_index to the given position to_position in the array. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.move_terrain: Moves the terrain at index terrain_index for terrain set terrain_set to the given position to_position in the array. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.move_terrain_set: Moves the terrain set at index terrain_set to the given position to_position in the array. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.remove_alternative_level_tile_pr: Removes an alternative-level proxy for the given identifiers.
m.TileSet.remove_coords_level_tile_proxy: Removes a coordinates-level proxy for the given identifiers.
m.TileSet.remove_custom_data_layer: Removes the custom data layer at index layer_index. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.remove_navigation_layer: Removes the navigation layer at index layer_index. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.remove_occlusion_layer: Removes the occlusion layer at index layer_index. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.remove_pattern: Remove the TileMapPattern at the given index.
m.TileSet.remove_physics_layer: Removes the physics layer at index layer_index. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.remove_source: Removes the source with the given source ID.
m.TileSet.remove_terrain: Removes the terrain at index terrain_index in the given terrain set terrain_set. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.remove_terrain_set: Removes the terrain set at index terrain_set. Also updates the atlas tiles accordingly.
m.TileSet.set_alternative_level_tile_proxy: Create an alternative-level proxy for the given identifiers. A proxy will map set of tile identifiers to another set of identifiers.
m.TileSet.set_coords_level_tile_proxy: Creates a coordinates-level proxy for the given identifiers. A proxy will map set of tile identifiers to another set of identifiers. The alternative tile ID is kept the same when using coordinates-level proxies.
m.TileSet.set_custom_data_layer_name: Sets the name of the custom data layer identified by the given index. Names are identifiers of the layer therefore if the name is already taken it will fail and raise an error.
m.TileSet.set_custom_data_layer_type: Sets the type of the custom data layer identified by the given index.
m.TileSet.set_navigation_layer_layer_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified navigation layer of the TileSet navigation data layer identified by the given layer_index, given a navigation_layers layer_number between 1 and 32.
m.TileSet.set_navigation_layer_layers: Sets the navigation layers (as in the navigation server) for navigation regions in the given TileSet navigation layer.
m.TileSet.set_occlusion_layer_light_mask: Sets the occlusion layer (as in the rendering server) for occluders in the given TileSet occlusion layer.
m.TileSet.set_occlusion_layer_sdf_collisio: Enables or disables SDF collision for occluders in the given TileSet occlusion layer.
m.TileSet.set_physics_layer_collision_laye: Sets the collision layer (as in the physics server) for bodies in the given TileSet physics layer.
m.TileSet.set_physics_layer_collision_mask: Sets the collision mask for bodies in the given TileSet physics layer.
m.TileSet.set_physics_layer_collision_prio: Sets the collision priority for bodies in the given TileSet physics layer.
m.TileSet.set_physics_layer_physics_materi: Sets the physics material for bodies in the given TileSet physics layer.
m.TileSet.set_source_level_tile_proxy: Creates a source-level proxy for the given source ID. A proxy will map set of tile identifiers to another set of identifiers. Both the atlas coordinates ID and the alternative tile ID are kept the same when using source-level proxies.
m.TileSet.set_terrain_color: Sets a terrain's color. This color is used for identifying the different terrains in the TileSet editor.
m.TileSet.set_terrain_set_mode: Sets a terrain mode. Each mode determines which bits of a tile shape is used to match the neighboring tiles' terrains.
m.TileSet.tile_layout: For all half-offset shapes (Isometric, Hexagonal and Half-Offset square), changes the way tiles are indexed in the TileMapLayer grid.
m.TileSet.tile_offset_axis: For all half-offset shapes (Isometric, Hexagonal and Half-Offset square), determines the offset axis.
m.TileSet.tile_size: The tile size, in pixels. For all tile shapes, this size corresponds to the encompassing rectangle of the tile shape. This is thus the minimal cell size required in an atlas.
m.TileSet.uv_clipping: Enables/Disable uv clipping when rendering the tiles.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.TILE_ANIMATION_MODE_D: Tile animations start at same time, looking identical.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.TILE_ANIMATION_MODE_M: Represents the size of the TileAnimationMode enum.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.TILE_ANIMATION_MODE_R: Tile animations start at random times, looking varied.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.TRANSFORM_FLIP_H: Represents cell's horizontal flip flag. Should be used directly with TileMapLayer to flip placed tiles by altering their alternative IDs.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.clear_tiles_outside_t: Removes all tiles that don't fit the available texture area. This method iterates over all the source's tiles, so it's advised to use has_tiles_outside_texture() beforehand.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.create_alternative_ti: Creates an alternative tile for the tile at coordinates atlas_coords. If alternative_id_override is -1, give it an automatically generated unique ID, or assigns it the given ID otherwise.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.create_tile: Creates a new tile at coordinates atlas_coords with the given size.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_atlas_grid_size: Returns the atlas grid size, which depends on how many tiles can fit in the texture. It thus depends on the texture's size, the atlas margins, and the tiles' texture_region_size.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_next_alternative_: Returns the alternative ID a following call to create_alternative_tile() would return.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_runtime_texture: If use_texture_padding is false, returns texture. Otherwise, returns an internal ImageTexture created that includes the padding.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_runtime_tile_text: Returns the region of the tile at coordinates atlas_coords for the given frame inside the texture returned by get_runtime_texture().
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_animation_co: Returns how many columns the tile at atlas_coords has in its animation layout.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_animation_fr: Returns the animation frame duration of frame frame_index for the tile at coordinates atlas_coords.
Returns how many animation frames has the tile at coordinates atlas_coords.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_animation_mo: Returns the tile animation mode of the tile at atlas_coords. See also set_tile_animation_mode().
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_animation_se: Returns the separation (as in the atlas grid) between each frame of an animated tile at coordinates atlas_coords.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_animation_sp: Returns the animation speed of the tile at coordinates atlas_coords.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_animation_to: Returns the sum of the sum of the frame durations of the tile at coordinates atlas_coords. This value needs to be divided by the animation speed to get the actual animation loop duration.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_at_coords: If there is a tile covering the atlas_coords coordinates, returns the top-left coordinates of the tile (thus its coordinate ID). Returns Vector2i(-1, -1) otherwise.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_data: Returns the TileData object for the given atlas coordinates and alternative ID.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_size_in_atla: Returns the size of the tile (in the grid coordinates system) at coordinates atlas_coords.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tile_texture_regi: Returns a tile's texture region in the atlas texture. For animated tiles, a frame argument might be provided for the different frames of the animation.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.get_tiles_to_be_remov: Returns an array of tiles coordinates ID that will be automatically removed when modifying one or several of those properties: texture, margins, separation or texture_region_size. This can be used to undo changes that would have caused tiles data loss.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.has_room_for_tile: Returns whether there is enough room in an atlas to create/modify a tile with the given properties. If ignored_tile is provided, act as is the given tile was not present in the atlas. This may be used when you want to modify a tile's properties.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.has_tiles_outside_tex: Checks if the source has any tiles that don't fit the texture area (either partially or completely).
m.TileSetAtlasSource.margins: Margins, in pixels, to offset the origin of the grid in the texture.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.move_tile_in_atlas: Move the tile and its alternatives at the atlas_coords coordinates to the new_atlas_coords coordinates with the new_size size. This functions will fail if a tile is already present in the given area.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.remove_alternative_ti: Remove a tile's alternative with alternative ID alternative_tile.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.remove_tile: Remove a tile and its alternative at coordinates atlas_coords.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.separation: Separation, in pixels, between each tile texture region of the grid.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.set_alternative_tile_: Change a tile's alternative ID from alternative_tile to new_id.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.set_tile_animation_co: Sets the number of columns in the animation layout of the tile at coordinates atlas_coords. If set to 0, then the different frames of the animation are laid out as a single horizontal line in the atlas.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.set_tile_animation_fr: Sets the animation frame duration of frame frame_index for the tile at coordinates atlas_coords.
Sets how many animation frames the tile at coordinates atlas_coords has.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.set_tile_animation_mo: Sets the tile animation mode of the tile at atlas_coords to mode. See also get_tile_animation_mode().
m.TileSetAtlasSource.set_tile_animation_se: Sets the margin (in grid tiles) between each tile in the animation layout of the tile at coordinates atlas_coords has.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.set_tile_animation_sp: Sets the animation speed of the tile at coordinates atlas_coords has.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.texture_region_size: The base tile size in the texture (in pixel). This size must be bigger than or equal to the TileSet's tile_size value.
m.TileSetAtlasSource.use_texture_padding: If true, generates an internal texture with an additional one pixel padding around each tile. Texture padding avoids a common artifact where lines appear between tiles.
m.TileSetScenesCollectionSource.create_sce: Creates a scene-based tile out of the given scene.
m.TileSetScenesCollectionSource.get_next_s: Returns the scene ID a following call to create_scene_tile() would return.
m.TileSetScenesCollectionSource.get_scene_: Returns whether the scene tile with id displays a placeholder in the editor.
Returns the scene tile ID of the scene tile at index.
Returns the PackedScene resource of scene tile with id.
Returns the number or scene tiles this TileSet source has.
m.TileSetScenesCollectionSource.has_scene_: Returns whether this TileSet source has a scene tile with id.
m.TileSetScenesCollectionSource.remove_sce: Remove the scene tile with id.
m.TileSetScenesCollectionSource.set_scene_: Sets whether or not the scene tile with id should display a placeholder in the editor. This might be useful for scenes that are not visible.
Changes a scene tile's ID from id to new_id. This will fail if there is already a tile with an ID equal to new_id.
Assigns a PackedScene resource to the scene tile with id. This will fail if the scene does not extend CanvasItem, as positioning properties are needed to place the scene on the TileMapLayer.
m.TileSetSource.get_alternative_tile_id: Returns the alternative ID for the tile with coordinates ID atlas_coords at index index.
m.TileSetSource.get_alternative_tiles_coun: Returns the number of alternatives tiles for the coordinates ID atlas_coords.
m.TileSetSource.get_tile_id: Returns the tile coordinates ID of the tile with index index.
m.TileSetSource.get_tiles_count: Returns how many tiles this atlas source defines (not including alternative tiles).
m.TileSetSource.has_alternative_tile: Returns if the base tile at coordinates atlas_coords has an alternative with ID alternative_tile.
m.TileSetSource.has_tile: Returns if this atlas has a tile with coordinates ID atlas_coords.
m.Time.MONTH_APRIL: The month of April, represented numerically as 04.
m.Time.MONTH_AUGUST: The month of August, represented numerically as 08.
m.Time.MONTH_DECEMBER: The month of December, represented numerically as 12.
m.Time.MONTH_FEBRUARY: The month of February, represented numerically as 02.
m.Time.MONTH_JANUARY: The month of January, represented numerically as 01.
m.Time.MONTH_JULY: The month of July, represented numerically as 07.
m.Time.MONTH_JUNE: The month of June, represented numerically as 06.
m.Time.MONTH_MARCH: The month of March, represented numerically as 03.
m.Time.MONTH_MAY: The month of May, represented numerically as 05.
m.Time.MONTH_NOVEMBER: The month of November, represented numerically as 11.
m.Time.MONTH_OCTOBER: The month of October, represented numerically as 10.
m.Time.MONTH_SEPTEMBER: The month of September, represented numerically as 09.
m.Time.WEEKDAY_FRIDAY: The day of the week Friday, represented numerically as 5.
m.Time.WEEKDAY_MONDAY: The day of the week Monday, represented numerically as 1.
m.Time.WEEKDAY_SATURDAY: The day of the week Saturday, represented numerically as 6.
m.Time.WEEKDAY_SUNDAY: The day of the week Sunday, represented numerically as 0.
m.Time.WEEKDAY_THURSDAY: The day of the week Thursday, represented numerically as 4.
m.Time.WEEKDAY_TUESDAY: The day of the week Tuesday, represented numerically as 2.
m.Time.WEEKDAY_WEDNESDAY: The day of the week Wednesday, represented numerically as 3.
m.Time.get_date_dict_from_system: Returns the current date as a dictionary of keys: year, month, day, and weekday.
m.Time.get_date_dict_from_unix_time: Converts the given Unix timestamp to a dictionary of keys: year, month, day, and weekday.
m.Time.get_date_string_from_system: Returns the current date as an ISO 8601 date string (YYYY-MM-DD).
m.Time.get_date_string_from_unix_time: Converts the given Unix timestamp to an ISO 8601 date string (YYYY-MM-DD).
m.Time.get_datetime_dict_from_datetime_str: Converts the given ISO 8601 date and time string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) to a dictionary of keys: year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, and second.
m.Time.get_datetime_dict_from_system: Returns the current date as a dictionary of keys: year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second, and dst (Daylight Savings Time).
m.Time.get_datetime_dict_from_unix_time: Converts the given Unix timestamp to a dictionary of keys: year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, and second.
m.Time.get_datetime_string_from_datetime_d: Converts the given dictionary of keys to an ISO 8601 date and time string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS).
m.Time.get_datetime_string_from_system: Returns the current date and time as an ISO 8601 date and time string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS).
m.Time.get_datetime_string_from_unix_time: Converts the given Unix timestamp to an ISO 8601 date and time string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS).
m.Time.get_offset_string_from_offset_minut: Converts the given timezone offset in minutes to a timezone offset string. For example, -480 returns "-08:00", 345 returns "+05:45", and 0 returns "+00:00".
m.Time.get_ticks_msec: Returns the amount of time passed in milliseconds since the engine started.
m.Time.get_ticks_usec: Returns the amount of time passed in microseconds since the engine started.
m.Time.get_time_dict_from_system: Returns the current time as a dictionary of keys: hour, minute, and second.
m.Time.get_time_dict_from_unix_time: Converts the given time to a dictionary of keys: hour, minute, and second.
m.Time.get_time_string_from_system: Returns the current time as an ISO 8601 time string (HH:MM:SS).
m.Time.get_time_string_from_unix_time: Converts the given Unix timestamp to an ISO 8601 time string (HH:MM:SS).
m.Time.get_time_zone_from_system: Returns the current time zone as a dictionary of keys: bias and name.
m.Time.get_unix_time_from_datetime_dict: Converts a dictionary of time values to a Unix timestamp.
m.Time.get_unix_time_from_datetime_string: Converts the given ISO 8601 date and/or time string to a Unix timestamp. The string can contain a date only, a time only, or both.
m.Time.get_unix_time_from_system: Returns the current Unix timestamp in seconds based on the system time in UTC. This method is implemented by the operating system and always returns the time in UTC. The Unix timestamp is the number of seconds passed since 1970-01-01 at 00:00:00, the Unix epoch [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time].
m.Timer.TIMER_PROCESS_IDLE: Update the timer every process (rendered) frame (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS).
m.Timer.TIMER_PROCESS_PHYSICS: Update the timer every physics process frame (see Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS).
m.Timer.autostart: If true, the timer will start immediately when it enters the scene tree.
m.Timer.ignore_time_scale: If true, the timer will ignore Engine.time_scale and update with the real, elapsed time.
m.Timer.is_stopped: Returns true if the timer is stopped or has not started.
m.Timer.one_shot: If true, the timer will stop after reaching the end. Otherwise, as by default, the timer will automatically restart.
m.Timer.paused: If true, the timer is paused. A paused timer does not process until this property is set back to false, even when start() is called. See also stop().
m.Timer.process_callback: Specifies when the timer is updated during the main loop.
m.Timer.start: 启动计时器。start(time) 或 start()。
m.Timer.timeout: Emitted when the timer reaches the end.
m.TorusMesh.inner_radius: The inner radius of the torus.
m.TorusMesh.outer_radius: The outer radius of the torus.
m.TorusMesh.ring_segments: The number of edges each ring of the torus is constructed of.
m.TorusMesh.rings: The number of slices the torus is constructed of.
m.TouchScreenButton.action: The button's action. Actions can be handled with InputEventAction.
m.TouchScreenButton.is_pressed: Returns true if this button is currently pressed.
m.TouchScreenButton.passby_press: If true, the pressed and released signals are emitted whenever a pressed finger goes in and out of the button, even if the pressure started outside the active area of the button.
m.TouchScreenButton.pressed: Emitted when the button is pressed (down).
m.TouchScreenButton.released: Emitted when the button is released (up).
m.TouchScreenButton.shape_centered: If true, the button's shape is centered in the provided texture. If no texture is used, this property has no effect.
m.TouchScreenButton.shape_visible: If true, the button's shape is visible in the editor.
m.TouchScreenButton.texture_normal: The button's texture for the normal state.
m.TouchScreenButton.texture_pressed: The button's texture for the pressed state.
m.Transform2D.IDENTITY: The identity Transform2D. This is a transform with no translation, no rotation, and a scale of Vector2.ONE. This also means that:
m.Transform2D.affine_inverse: Returns the inverted version of this transform. Unlike inverse(), this method works with almost any basis, including non-uniform ones, but is slower.
m.Transform2D.basis_xform: Returns a copy of the v vector, transformed (multiplied) by the transform basis's matrix. Unlike the multiplication operator (*), this method ignores the origin.
m.Transform2D.basis_xform_inv: Returns a copy of the v vector, transformed (multiplied) by the inverse transform basis's matrix (see inverse()). This method ignores the origin.
m.Transform2D.determinant: Returns the determinant [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant] of this transform basis's matrix. For advanced math, this number can be used to determine a few attributes:
m.Transform2D.get_origin: Returns this transform's translation. Equivalent to origin.
m.Transform2D.get_rotation: Returns this transform's rotation (in radians). This is equivalent to x's angle (see Vector2.angle()).
m.Transform2D.get_scale: Returns the length of both x and y, as a Vector2. If this transform's basis is not skewed, this value is the scaling factor. It is not affected by rotation.
m.Transform2D.interpolate_with: Returns the result of the linear interpolation between this transform and xform by the given weight.
m.Transform2D.inverse: Returns the inverted version of this transform [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertible_matrix].
m.Transform2D.is_conformal: Returns true if this transform's basis is conformal. A conformal basis is both orthogonal (the axes are perpendicular to each other) and uniform (the axes share the same length). This method can be especially useful during physics calculations.
m.Transform2D.is_equal_approx: Returns true if this transform and xform are approximately equal, by running @GlobalScope.is_equal_approx() on each component.
m.Transform2D.is_finite: Returns true if this transform is finite, by calling @GlobalScope.is_finite() on each component.
m.Transform2D.looking_at: Returns a copy of the transform rotated such that the rotated X-axis points towards the target position, in global space.
m.Transform2D.origin: The translation offset of this transform, and the column 2 of the matrix. In 2D space, this can be seen as the position.
m.Transform2D.orthonormalized: Returns a copy of this transform with its basis orthonormalized. An orthonormal basis is both orthogonal (the axes are perpendicular to each other) and normalized (the axes have a length of 1.0), which also means it can only represent a rotation.
m.Transform2D.rotated: Returns a copy of this transform rotated by the given angle (in radians).
m.Transform2D.rotated_local: Returns a copy of the transform rotated by the given angle (in radians).
m.Transform2D.scaled: Returns a copy of the transform scaled by the given scale factor.
m.Transform2D.scaled_local: Returns a copy of the transform scaled by the given scale factor.
m.Transform2D.translated: Returns a copy of the transform translated by the given offset.
m.Transform2D.translated_local: Returns a copy of the transform translated by the given offset.
m.Transform2D.x: The transform basis's X axis, and the column 0 of the matrix. Combined with y, this represents the transform's rotation, scale, and skew.
m.Transform2D.y: The transform basis's Y axis, and the column 1 of the matrix. Combined with x, this represents the transform's rotation, scale, and skew.
m.Transform3D.IDENTITY: The identity Transform3D. This is a transform with no translation, no rotation, and a scale of Vector3.ONE. Its basis is equal to Basis.IDENTITY. This also means that:
m.Transform3D.affine_inverse: Returns the inverted version of this transform. Unlike inverse(), this method works with almost any basis, including non-uniform ones, but is slower. See also Basis.inverse().
m.Transform3D.basis: The Basis of this transform. It is composed by 3 axes (Basis.x, Basis.y, and Basis.z). Together, these represent the transform's rotation, scale, and shear.
m.Transform3D.interpolate_with: Returns the result of the linear interpolation between this transform and xform by the given weight.
m.Transform3D.inverse: Returns the inverted version of this transform [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertible_matrix]. See also Basis.inverse().
m.Transform3D.is_equal_approx: Returns true if this transform and xform are approximately equal, by running @GlobalScope.is_equal_approx() on each component.
m.Transform3D.is_finite: Returns true if this transform is finite, by calling @GlobalScope.is_finite() on each component.
m.Transform3D.looking_at: Returns a copy of this transform rotated so that the forward axis (-Z) points towards the target position.
m.Transform3D.origin: The translation offset of this transform. In 3D space, this can be seen as the position.
m.Transform3D.orthonormalized: Returns a copy of this transform with its basis orthonormalized. An orthonormal basis is both orthogonal (the axes are perpendicular to each other) and normalized (the axes have a length of 1.0), which also means it can only represent a rotation. See also Basis.orthonormalized().
m.Transform3D.rotated: Returns a copy of this transform rotated around the given axis by the given angle (in radians).
m.Transform3D.rotated_local: Returns a copy of this transform rotated around the given axis by the given angle (in radians).
m.Transform3D.scaled: Returns a copy of this transform scaled by the given scale factor.
m.Transform3D.scaled_local: Returns a copy of this transform scaled by the given scale factor.
m.Transform3D.translated: Returns a copy of this transform translated by the given offset.
m.Transform3D.translated_local: Returns a copy of this transform translated by the given offset.
m.Translation.add_message: Adds a message if nonexistent, followed by its translation.
m.Translation.add_plural_message: Adds a message involving plural translation if nonexistent, followed by its translation.
m.Translation.get_message_count: Returns the number of existing messages.
m.Translation.get_message_list: Returns the keys of all messages, that is, the context and untranslated strings of each message.
m.Translation.get_plural_message: Returns a message's translation involving plurals.
m.Translation.plural_rules_override: The plural rules string to enforce. See GNU gettext [https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/html_node/Plural-forms.html] for examples and more info.
m.TranslationDomain.enabled: If true, translation is enabled. Otherwise, translate() and translate_plural() will return the input message unchanged regardless of the current locale.
m.TranslationDomain.find_translations: Returns the Translation instances that match locale (see TranslationServer.compare_locales()). If exact is true, only instances whose locale exactly equals locale will be returned.
m.TranslationDomain.get_locale_override: Returns the locale override of the domain. Returns an empty string if locale override is disabled.
m.TranslationDomain.get_translations: Returns all available Translation instances as added by add_translation().
m.TranslationDomain.has_translation: Returns true if this translation domain contains the given translation.
m.TranslationDomain.has_translation_for_lo: Returns true if there are any Translation instances that match locale (see TranslationServer.compare_locales()). If exact is true, only instances whose locale exactly equals locale are considered.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_acc: Replace all characters with their accented variants during pseudolocalization.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_dou: Double vowels in strings during pseudolocalization to simulate the lengthening of text due to localization.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_ena: If true, enables pseudolocalization for the project. This can be used to spot untranslatable strings or layout issues that may occur once the project is localized to languages that have longer strings than the source language.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_exp: The expansion ratio to use during pseudolocalization. A value of 0.3 is sufficient for most practical purposes, and will increase the length of each string by 30%.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_fak: If true, emulate bidirectional (right-to-left) text when pseudolocalization is enabled. This can be used to spot issues with RTL layout and UI mirroring that will crop up if the project is localized to RTL languages such as Arabic or Hebrew.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_ove: Replace all characters in the string with *. Useful for finding non-localizable strings.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_pre: Prefix that will be prepended to the pseudolocalized string.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_ski: Skip placeholders for string formatting like %s or %f during pseudolocalization. Useful to identify strings which need additional control characters to display correctly.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalization_suf: Suffix that will be appended to the pseudolocalized string.
m.TranslationDomain.pseudolocalize: Returns the pseudolocalized string based on the message passed in.
m.TranslationDomain.set_locale_override: Sets the locale override of the domain.
m.TranslationDomain.translate: Returns the current locale's translation for the given message and context.
m.TranslationDomain.translate_plural: Returns the current locale's translation for the given message, plural message and context.
m.TranslationServer.add_translation: Adds a translation to the main translation domain.
m.TranslationServer.clear: Removes all translations from the main translation domain.
m.TranslationServer.compare_locales: Compares two locales and returns a similarity score between 0 (no match) and 10 (full match).
m.TranslationServer.find_translations: Returns the Translation instances in the main translation domain that match locale (see compare_locales()). If exact is true, only instances whose locale exactly equals locale will be returned.
m.TranslationServer.format_number: Converts a number from Western Arabic (0..9) to the numeral system used in the given locale.
m.TranslationServer.get_all_countries: Returns an array of known country codes.
m.TranslationServer.get_all_languages: Returns array of known language codes.
m.TranslationServer.get_all_scripts: Returns an array of known script codes.
m.TranslationServer.get_country_name: Returns a readable country name for the country code.
m.TranslationServer.get_language_name: Returns a readable language name for the language code.
m.TranslationServer.get_loaded_locales: Returns an array of all loaded locales of the project.
m.TranslationServer.get_locale: Returns the current locale of the project.
m.TranslationServer.get_locale_name: Returns a locale's language and its variant (e.g. "en_US" would return "English (United States)").
m.TranslationServer.get_or_add_domain: Returns the translation domain with the specified name. An empty translation domain will be created and added if it does not exist.
m.TranslationServer.get_percent_sign: Returns the percent sign used in the given locale.
m.TranslationServer.get_plural_rules: Returns the default plural rules for the locale.
m.TranslationServer.get_script_name: Returns a readable script name for the script code.
m.TranslationServer.get_tool_locale: Returns the current locale of the editor.
m.TranslationServer.get_translations: Returns all available Translation instances in the main translation domain as added by add_translation().
m.TranslationServer.has_domain: Returns true if a translation domain with the specified name exists.
m.TranslationServer.has_translation: Returns true if the main translation domain contains the given translation.
m.TranslationServer.has_translation_for_lo: Returns true if there are any Translation instances in the main translation domain that match locale (see compare_locales()). If exact is true, only instances whose locale exactly equals locale are considered.
m.TranslationServer.parse_number: Converts number from the numeral system used in the given locale to Western Arabic (0..9).
m.TranslationServer.pseudolocalization_ena: If true, enables the use of pseudolocalization on the main translation domain. See ProjectSettings.internationalization/pseudolocalization/use_pseudolocalization for details.
m.TranslationServer.pseudolocalize: Returns the pseudolocalized string based on the message passed in.
m.TranslationServer.reload_pseudolocalizat: Reparses the pseudolocalization options and reloads the translation for the main translation domain.
m.TranslationServer.remove_domain: Removes the translation domain with the specified name.
m.TranslationServer.remove_translation: Removes the given translation from the main translation domain.
m.TranslationServer.set_locale: Sets the locale of the project. The locale string will be standardized to match known locales (e.g. en-US would be matched to en_US).
m.TranslationServer.standardize_locale: Returns a locale string standardized to match known locales (e.g. en-US would be matched to en_US). If add_defaults is true, the locale may have a default script or country added.
m.TranslationServer.translate: Returns the current locale's translation for the given message and context.
m.TranslationServer.translate_plural: Returns the current locale's translation for the given message, plural message and context.
m.Tree.DROP_MODE_INBETWEEN: Enables "above item" and "below item" drop sections. The "above item" drop section covers the top half of the item, while the "below item" drop section covers the bottom half, and extends downward to the left of any children.
m.Tree.DROP_MODE_ON_ITEM: Enables the "on item" drop section. This drop section covers the entire item.
m.Tree.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_BOTH: Scroll hints will be shown at the top and bottom.
m.Tree.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_BOTTOM: Only the bottom scroll hint will be shown.
m.Tree.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_DISABLED: Scroll hints will never be shown.
m.Tree.SCROLL_HINT_MODE_TOP: Only the top scroll hint will be shown.
m.Tree.SELECT_MULTI: Allows selection of multiple cells at the same time. From the perspective of items, multiple items are allowed to be selected. And there can be multiple columns selected in each selected item.
m.Tree.SELECT_ROW: Allows selection of a single row at a time. From the perspective of items, only a single items is allowed to be selected. And all the columns are selected in the selected item.
m.Tree.SELECT_SINGLE: Allows selection of a single cell at a time. From the perspective of items, only a single item is allowed to be selected. And there is only one column selected in the selected item.
m.Tree.allow_reselect: If true, the currently selected cell may be selected again.
m.Tree.allow_rmb_select: If true, a right mouse button click can select items.
m.Tree.allow_search: If true, allows navigating the Tree with letter keys through incremental search.
m.Tree.auto_tooltip: If true, tree items with no tooltip assigned display their text as their tooltip. See also TreeItem.get_tooltip_text() and TreeItem.get_button_tooltip_text().
m.Tree.button_clicked: Emitted when a button on the tree was pressed (see TreeItem.add_button()).
m.Tree.cell_selected: Emitted when a cell is selected.
m.Tree.check_propagated_to_item: Emitted when TreeItem.propagate_check() is called. Connect to this signal to process the items that are affected when TreeItem.propagate_check() is invoked. The order that the items affected will be processed is as follows: the item that invoked the method, children of that item, and finally parents of that item.
m.Tree.clear: Clears the tree. This removes all items.
m.Tree.column_title_clicked: Emitted when a column's title is clicked with either @GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT or @GlobalScope.MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT.
m.Tree.column_titles_visible: If true, column titles are visible.
m.Tree.create_item: Creates an item in the tree and adds it as a child of parent, which can be either a valid TreeItem or null.
m.Tree.custom_item_clicked: Emitted when an item with TreeItem.CELL_MODE_CUSTOM is clicked with a mouse button.
m.Tree.custom_popup_edited: Emitted when a cell with the TreeItem.CELL_MODE_CUSTOM is clicked to be edited.
m.Tree.deselect_all: Deselects all tree items (rows and columns). In SELECT_MULTI mode also removes selection cursor.
m.Tree.drop_mode_flags: The drop mode as an OR combination of flags. See DropModeFlags constants. Once dropping is done, reverts to DROP_MODE_DISABLED. Setting this during Control._can_drop_data() is recommended.
m.Tree.edit_selected: Edits the selected tree item as if it was clicked.
m.Tree.empty_clicked: Emitted when a mouse button is clicked in the empty space of the tree.
m.Tree.enable_drag_unfolding: If true, tree items will unfold when hovered over during a drag-and-drop. The delay for when this happens is dictated by dragging_unfold_wait_msec.
m.Tree.enable_recursive_folding: If true, recursive folding is enabled for this Tree. Holding down Shift while clicking the fold arrow or using ui_right/ui_left shortcuts collapses or uncollapses the TreeItem and all its descendants.
m.Tree.ensure_cursor_is_visible: Makes the currently focused cell visible.
m.Tree.get_button_id_at_position: Returns the button ID at position, or -1 if no button is there.
m.Tree.get_column_at_position: Returns the column index at position, or -1 if no item is there.
m.Tree.get_column_expand_ratio: Returns the expand ratio assigned to the column.
m.Tree.get_column_title_direction: Returns column title base writing direction.
m.Tree.get_column_title_tooltip_text: Returns the column title's tooltip text.
m.Tree.get_column_width: Returns the column's width in pixels.
m.Tree.get_custom_drawing_canvas_item: Returns the internal canvas item designated for custom drawing. See TreeItem.set_custom_draw_callback().
m.Tree.get_custom_popup_rect: Returns the rectangle for custom popups. Helper to create custom cell controls that display a popup. See TreeItem.set_cell_mode().
m.Tree.get_drop_section_at_position: Returns the drop section at position, as permitted by enabled DropModeFlags.
m.Tree.get_edited: Returns the currently edited item. Can be used with item_edited to get the item that was modified.
m.Tree.get_edited_column: Returns the column for the currently edited item.
m.Tree.get_item_area_rect: Returns the rectangle area for the specified TreeItem. If column is specified, only get the position and size of that column, otherwise get the rectangle containing all columns. If a button index is specified, the rectangle of that button will be returned.
m.Tree.get_item_at_position: Returns the tree item at the specified position (relative to the tree origin position).
m.Tree.get_next_selected: Returns the next selected TreeItem after the given one, or null if the end is reached.
m.Tree.get_pressed_button: Returns the last pressed button's index.
m.Tree.get_root: Returns the tree's root item, or null if the tree is empty.
m.Tree.get_selected: Returns the currently focused item, or null if no item is focused.
m.Tree.get_selected_column: Returns the currently focused column, or -1 if no column is focused.
m.Tree.hide_folding: If true, the folding arrow is hidden.
m.Tree.hide_root: If true, the tree's root is hidden.
m.Tree.is_column_clipping_content: Returns true if the column has enabled clipping (see set_column_clip_content()).
m.Tree.is_column_expanding: Returns true if the column has enabled expanding (see set_column_expand()).
m.Tree.item_activated: Emitted when an item is double-clicked, or selected with a ui_accept input event (e.g. using Enter or Space on the keyboard).
m.Tree.item_collapsed: Emitted when an item is expanded or collapsed by clicking on the folding arrow or through code.
m.Tree.item_edited: Emitted when an item is edited.
m.Tree.item_icon_double_clicked: Emitted when an item's icon is double-clicked. For a signal that emits when any part of the item is double-clicked, see item_activated.
m.Tree.item_mouse_selected: Emitted when an item is selected with a mouse button.
m.Tree.item_selected: Emitted when an item is selected.
m.Tree.multi_selected: Emitted instead of item_selected if select_mode is set to SELECT_MULTI.
m.Tree.nothing_selected: Emitted when a left mouse button click does not select any item.
m.Tree.scroll_hint_mode: The way which scroll hints (indicators that show that the content can still be scrolled in a certain direction) will be shown.
m.Tree.scroll_to_item: Causes the Tree to jump to the specified TreeItem.
m.Tree.select_mode: Allows single or multiple selection. See the SelectMode constants.
m.Tree.set_column_clip_content: Allows to enable clipping for column's content, making the content size ignored.
m.Tree.set_column_custom_minimum_width: Overrides the calculated minimum width of a column. It can be set to 0 to restore the default behavior. Columns that have the "Expand" flag will use their "min_width" in a similar fashion to Control.size_flags_stretch_ratio.
m.Tree.set_column_expand: If true, the column will have the "Expand" flag of Control. Columns that have the "Expand" flag will use their expand ratio in a similar fashion to Control.size_flags_stretch_ratio (see set_column_expand_ratio()).
m.Tree.set_column_expand_ratio: Sets the relative expand ratio for a column. See set_column_expand().
m.Tree.set_column_title: Sets the title of a column.
m.Tree.set_column_title_alignment: Sets the column title alignment. Note that @GlobalScope.HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_FILL is not supported for column titles.
m.Tree.set_column_title_direction: Sets column title base writing direction.
m.Tree.set_column_title_language: Sets the language code of the given column's title to language. This is used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If language is empty, the current locale is used.
m.Tree.set_column_title_tooltip_text: Sets the column title's tooltip text.
m.Tree.set_selected: Selects the specified TreeItem and column.
m.Tree.tile_scroll_hint: If true, the scroll hint texture will be tiled instead of stretched. See scroll_hint_mode.
m.TreeItem.CELL_MODE_CHECK: Cell shows a checkbox, optionally with text and an icon. The checkbox can be pressed, released, or indeterminate (via set_indeterminate()). The checkbox can't be clicked unless the cell is editable.
m.TreeItem.CELL_MODE_CUSTOM: Cell shows as a clickable button. It will display an arrow similar to OptionButton, but doesn't feature a dropdown (for that you can use CELL_MODE_RANGE). Clicking the button emits the Tree.item_edited signal. The button is flat by default, you can use set_custom_as_button() to display it with a StyleBox.
m.TreeItem.CELL_MODE_ICON: Cell shows an icon. It can't be edited nor display text. The icon is always centered within the cell.
m.TreeItem.CELL_MODE_RANGE: Cell shows a numeric range. When editable, it can be edited using a range slider. Use set_range() to set the value and set_range_config() to configure the range.
m.TreeItem.CELL_MODE_STRING: Cell shows a string label, optionally with an icon. When editable, the text can be edited using a LineEdit, or a TextEdit popup if set_edit_multiline() is used.
m.TreeItem.add_button: Adds a button with Texture2D button to the end of the cell at column column. The id is used to identify the button in the according Tree.button_clicked signal and can be different from the buttons index. If not specified, the next available index is used, which may be retrieved by calling get_button_count() immediately before this method. Optionally, the button can be disabled and have a tooltip_…
m.TreeItem.add_child: Adds a previously unparented TreeItem as a direct child of this one. The child item must not be a part of any Tree or parented to any TreeItem. See also remove_child().
m.TreeItem.call_recursive: Calls the method on the actual TreeItem and its children recursively. Pass parameters as a comma separated list.
m.TreeItem.clear_buttons: Removes all buttons from all columns of this item.
m.TreeItem.clear_custom_bg_color: Resets the background color for the given column to default.
m.TreeItem.clear_custom_color: Resets the color for the given column to default.
m.TreeItem.collapsed: If true, the TreeItem is collapsed.
m.TreeItem.create_child: Creates an item and adds it as a child.
m.TreeItem.disable_folding: If true, folding is disabled for this TreeItem.
m.TreeItem.erase_button: Removes the button at index button_index in column column.
m.TreeItem.get_auto_translate_mode: Returns the column's auto translate mode.
m.TreeItem.get_autowrap_mode: Returns the text autowrap mode in the given column. By default it is TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF.
m.TreeItem.get_autowrap_trim_flags: Returns the autowrap trim flags for the given column. By default, both TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_START_EDGE_SPACES and TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_END_EDGE_SPACES are enabled.
m.TreeItem.get_button: Returns the Texture2D of the button at index button_index in column column.
m.TreeItem.get_button_by_id: Returns the button index if there is a button with ID id in column column, otherwise returns -1.
m.TreeItem.get_button_color: Returns the color of the button with ID id in column column. If the specified button does not exist, returns Color.BLACK.
m.TreeItem.get_button_count: Returns the number of buttons in column column.
m.TreeItem.get_button_id: Returns the ID for the button at index button_index in column column.
m.TreeItem.get_button_tooltip_text: Returns the tooltip text for the button at index button_index in column column.
m.TreeItem.get_child: Returns a child item by its index (see get_child_count()). This method is often used for iterating all children of an item.
m.TreeItem.get_child_count: Returns the number of child items.
m.TreeItem.get_children: Returns an array of references to the item's children.
m.TreeItem.get_custom_bg_color: Returns the custom background color of column column.
m.TreeItem.get_custom_color: Returns the custom color of column column.
m.TreeItem.get_custom_draw_callback: Returns the custom callback of column column.
m.TreeItem.get_custom_font: Returns custom font used to draw text in the column column.
m.TreeItem.get_custom_font_size: Returns custom font size used to draw text in the column column.
m.TreeItem.get_custom_stylebox: Returns the given column's custom StyleBox used to draw the background.
m.TreeItem.get_description: Returns the given column's description for assistive apps.
m.TreeItem.get_expand_right: Returns true if expand_right is set.
m.TreeItem.get_icon: Returns the given column's icon Texture2D. Error if no icon is set.
m.TreeItem.get_icon_max_width: Returns the maximum allowed width of the icon in the given column.
m.TreeItem.get_icon_modulate: Returns the Color modulating the column's icon.
m.TreeItem.get_icon_overlay: Returns the given column's icon overlay Texture2D.
m.TreeItem.get_icon_region: Returns the icon Texture2D region as Rect2.
m.TreeItem.get_index: Returns the node's order in the tree. For example, if called on the first child item the position is 0.
m.TreeItem.get_metadata: Returns the metadata value that was set for the given column using set_metadata().
m.TreeItem.get_next: Returns the next sibling TreeItem in the tree or a null object if there is none.
m.TreeItem.get_next_in_tree: Returns the next TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
m.TreeItem.get_next_visible: Returns the next visible TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
m.TreeItem.get_parent: Returns the parent TreeItem or a null object if there is none.
m.TreeItem.get_prev: Returns the previous sibling TreeItem in the tree or a null object if there is none.
m.TreeItem.get_prev_in_tree: Returns the previous TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
m.TreeItem.get_prev_visible: Returns the previous visible sibling TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
m.TreeItem.get_range: Returns the value of a CELL_MODE_RANGE column.
m.TreeItem.get_range_config: Returns a dictionary containing the range parameters for a given column. The keys are "min", "max", "step", and "expr".
m.TreeItem.get_structured_text_bidi_overri: Returns the BiDi algorithm override set for this cell.
Returns the additional BiDi options set for this cell.
m.TreeItem.get_suffix: Gets the suffix string shown after the column value.
m.TreeItem.get_text_alignment: Returns the given column's text alignment.
m.TreeItem.get_text_direction: Returns item's text base writing direction.
m.TreeItem.get_text_overrun_behavior: Returns the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the item's bounding rectangle in the given column. By default it is TextServer.OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS.
m.TreeItem.get_tooltip_text: Returns the given column's tooltip text.
m.TreeItem.get_tree: Returns the Tree that owns this TreeItem.
m.TreeItem.is_accepting_children: Returns true if this TreeItem is allowed to accept children.
m.TreeItem.is_any_collapsed: Returns true if this TreeItem, or any of its descendants, is collapsed.
m.TreeItem.is_button_disabled: Returns true if the button at index button_index for the given column is disabled.
m.TreeItem.is_checked: Returns true if the given column is checked.
m.TreeItem.is_custom_set_as_button: Returns true if the cell was made into a button with set_custom_as_button().
m.TreeItem.is_edit_multiline: Returns true if the given column is multiline editable.
m.TreeItem.is_editable: Returns true if the given column is editable.
m.TreeItem.is_indeterminate: Returns true if the given column is indeterminate.
m.TreeItem.is_selectable: Returns true if the given column is selectable.
m.TreeItem.is_selected: Returns true if the given column is selected.
m.TreeItem.is_visible_in_tree: Returns true if visible is true and all its ancestors are also visible.
m.TreeItem.move_after: Moves this TreeItem right after the given item.
m.TreeItem.move_before: Moves this TreeItem right before the given item.
m.TreeItem.propagate_check: Propagates this item's checked status to its children and parents for the given column. It is possible to process the items affected by this method call by connecting to Tree.check_propagated_to_item. The order that the items affected will be processed is as follows: the item invoking this method, children of that item, and finally parents of that item. If emit_signal is false, then Tree.check_pr…
m.TreeItem.remove_child: Removes the given child TreeItem and all its children from the Tree. Note that it doesn't free the item from memory, so it can be reused later (see add_child()). To completely remove a TreeItem use Object.free().
m.TreeItem.select: Selects the given column. If set_as_cursor is true, the Tree's cursor will be moved to this item (only matters if Tree.select_mode is set to Tree.SELECT_MULTI).
m.TreeItem.set_accept_children: Sets TreeItem's ability to accept children.
m.TreeItem.set_auto_translate_mode: Sets the given column's auto translate mode to mode.
m.TreeItem.set_autowrap_mode: Sets the autowrap mode in the given column. If set to something other than TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF, the text gets wrapped inside the cell's bounding rectangle.
m.TreeItem.set_autowrap_trim_flags: Sets the autowrap trim flags for the given column. These flags control whether leading and trailing spaces are trimmed on wrapped lines. Set to 0 to disable all trimming.
m.TreeItem.set_button: Sets the given column's button Texture2D at index button_index to button.
m.TreeItem.set_button_color: Sets the given column's button color at index button_index to color.
m.TreeItem.set_button_description: Sets the given column's button description at index button_index for assistive apps.
m.TreeItem.set_button_disabled: If true, disables the button at index button_index in the given column.
m.TreeItem.set_button_tooltip_text: Sets the tooltip text for the button at index button_index in the given column.
m.TreeItem.set_cell_mode: Sets the given column's cell mode to mode. This determines how the cell is displayed and edited.
m.TreeItem.set_checked: If checked is true, the given column is checked. Clears column's indeterminate status.
m.TreeItem.set_collapsed_recursive: Collapses or uncollapses this TreeItem and all the descendants of this item.
m.TreeItem.set_custom_as_button: Makes a cell with CELL_MODE_CUSTOM display as a non-flat button with a StyleBox.
m.TreeItem.set_custom_bg_color: Sets the given column's custom background color and whether to just use it as an outline.
m.TreeItem.set_custom_color: Sets the given column's custom color.
m.TreeItem.set_custom_draw_callback: Sets the given column's custom draw callback. Use an empty Callable (Callable()) to clear the custom callback. The cell has to be in CELL_MODE_CUSTOM to use this feature.
m.TreeItem.set_custom_font: Sets custom font used to draw text in the given column.
m.TreeItem.set_custom_font_size: Sets custom font size used to draw text in the given column.
m.TreeItem.set_custom_stylebox: Sets the given column's custom StyleBox used to draw the background.
m.TreeItem.set_description: Sets the given column's description for assistive apps.
m.TreeItem.set_edit_multiline: If multiline is true, the given column is multiline editable.
m.TreeItem.set_editable: If enabled is true, the given column is editable.
m.TreeItem.set_expand_right: If enable is true, the given column is expanded to the right.
m.TreeItem.set_icon: Sets the given cell's icon Texture2D. If the cell is in CELL_MODE_ICON mode, the icon is displayed in the center of the cell. Otherwise, the icon is displayed before the cell's text. CELL_MODE_RANGE does not display an icon.
m.TreeItem.set_icon_max_width: Sets the maximum allowed width of the icon in the given column. This limit is applied on top of the default size of the icon and on top of Tree.icon_max_width. The height is adjusted according to the icon's ratio.
m.TreeItem.set_icon_modulate: Modulates the given column's icon with modulate.
m.TreeItem.set_icon_overlay: Sets the given cell's icon overlay Texture2D. The cell has to be in CELL_MODE_ICON mode, and icon has to be set. Overlay is drawn on top of icon, in the bottom left corner.
m.TreeItem.set_icon_region: Sets the given column's icon's texture region.
m.TreeItem.set_indeterminate: If indeterminate is true, the given column is marked indeterminate.
m.TreeItem.set_language: Sets the language code of the given column's text to language. This is used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If language is empty, the current locale is used.
m.TreeItem.set_metadata: Sets the metadata value for the given column, which can be retrieved later using get_metadata(). This can be used, for example, to store a reference to the original data.
m.TreeItem.set_range: Sets the value of a CELL_MODE_RANGE column.
m.TreeItem.set_range_config: Sets the range of accepted values for a column. The column must be in the CELL_MODE_RANGE mode.
m.TreeItem.set_selectable: If selectable is true, the given column is selectable.
m.TreeItem.set_structured_text_bidi_overri: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text. Has effect for cells that display text.
Set additional options for BiDi override. Has effect for cells that display text.
m.TreeItem.set_suffix: Sets a string to be shown after a column's value (for example, a unit abbreviation).
m.TreeItem.set_text: Sets the given column's text value.
m.TreeItem.set_text_alignment: Sets the given column's text alignment to text_alignment.
m.TreeItem.set_text_direction: Sets item's text base writing direction.
m.TreeItem.set_text_overrun_behavior: Sets the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the item's bounding rectangle in the given column.
m.TreeItem.set_tooltip_text: Sets the given column's tooltip text.
m.TreeItem.uncollapse_tree: Uncollapses all TreeItems necessary to reveal this TreeItem, i.e. all ancestor TreeItems.
m.TreeItem.visible: If true, the TreeItem is visible (default).
m.TriangleMesh.create_from_faces: Creates the BVH tree from an array of faces. Each 3 vertices of the input faces array represent one triangle (face).
m.TriangleMesh.get_faces: Returns a copy of the geometry faces. Each 3 vertices of the array represent one triangle (face).
m.TriangleMesh.intersect_ray: Tests for intersection with a ray starting at begin and facing dir and extending toward infinity.
m.TriangleMesh.intersect_segment: Tests for intersection with a segment going from begin to end.
m.TubeTrailMesh.cap_bottom: If true, generates a cap at the bottom of the tube. This can be set to false to speed up generation and rendering when the cap is never seen by the camera.
m.TubeTrailMesh.cap_top: If true, generates a cap at the top of the tube. This can be set to false to speed up generation and rendering when the cap is never seen by the camera.
m.TubeTrailMesh.curve: Determines the radius of the tube along its length. The radius of a particular section ring is obtained by multiplying the baseline radius by the value of this curve at the given distance. For values smaller than 0, the faces will be inverted. Should be a unit Curve.
m.TubeTrailMesh.radial_steps: The number of sides on the tube. For example, a value of 5 means the tube will be pentagonal. Higher values result in a more detailed tube at the cost of performance.
m.TubeTrailMesh.radius: The baseline radius of the tube. The radius of a particular section ring is obtained by multiplying this radius by the value of the curve at the given distance.
m.TubeTrailMesh.section_length: The length of a section of the tube.
m.TubeTrailMesh.section_rings: The number of rings in a section. The curve is sampled on each ring to determine its radius. Higher values result in a more detailed tube at the cost of performance.
m.TubeTrailMesh.sections: The total number of sections on the tube.
m.Tween.EASE_IN: The interpolation starts slowly and speeds up towards the end.
m.Tween.EASE_IN_OUT: A combination of EASE_IN and EASE_OUT. The interpolation is slowest at both ends.
m.Tween.EASE_OUT: The interpolation starts quickly and slows down towards the end.
m.Tween.EASE_OUT_IN: A combination of EASE_IN and EASE_OUT. The interpolation is fastest at both ends.
m.Tween.TRANS_BACK: The animation is interpolated backing out at ends.
m.Tween.TRANS_BOUNCE: The animation is interpolated by bouncing at the end.
m.Tween.TRANS_CIRC: The animation is interpolated with a function using square roots.
m.Tween.TRANS_CUBIC: The animation is interpolated with a cubic (to the power of 3) function.
m.Tween.TRANS_ELASTIC: The animation is interpolated with elasticity, wiggling around the edges.
m.Tween.TRANS_EXPO: The animation is interpolated with an exponential (to the power of x) function.
m.Tween.TRANS_QUAD: The animation is interpolated with a quadratic (to the power of 2) function.
m.Tween.TRANS_QUART: The animation is interpolated with a quartic (to the power of 4) function.
m.Tween.TRANS_QUINT: The animation is interpolated with a quintic (to the power of 5) function.
m.Tween.TRANS_SINE: The animation is interpolated using a sine function.
m.Tween.TRANS_SPRING: The animation is interpolated like a spring towards the end.
m.Tween.TWEEN_PAUSE_BOUND: If the Tween has a bound node, it will process when that node can process (see Node.process_mode). Otherwise it's the same as TWEEN_PAUSE_STOP.
m.Tween.TWEEN_PAUSE_PROCESS: The Tween will process regardless of whether SceneTree is paused.
m.Tween.TWEEN_PAUSE_STOP: If SceneTree is paused, the Tween will also pause.
m.Tween.TWEEN_PROCESS_IDLE: The Tween updates after each process frame (see Node._process()).
m.Tween.TWEEN_PROCESS_PHYSICS: The Tween updates after each physics frame (see Node._physics_process()).
m.Tween.bind_node: Binds this Tween with the given node. Tweens are processed directly by the SceneTree, so they run independently of the animated nodes. When you bind a Node with the Tween, the Tween will halt the animation when the object is not inside tree and the Tween will be automatically killed when the bound object is freed. Also TWEEN_PAUSE_BOUND will make the pausing behavior dependent on the bound node.
m.Tween.chain: Used to chain two Tweeners after set_parallel() is called with true.
m.Tween.custom_step: Processes the Tween by the given delta value, in seconds. This is mostly useful for manual control when the Tween is paused. It can also be used to end the Tween animation immediately, by setting delta longer than the whole duration of the Tween animation.
m.Tween.finished: Emitted when the Tween has finished all tweening. Never emitted when the Tween is set to infinite looping (see set_loops()).
m.Tween.get_loops_left: Returns the number of remaining loops for this Tween (see set_loops()). A return value of -1 indicates an infinitely looping Tween, and a return value of 0 indicates that the Tween has already finished.
m.Tween.get_total_elapsed_time: Returns the total time in seconds the Tween has been animating (i.e. the time since it started, not counting pauses etc.). The time is affected by set_speed_scale(), and stop() will reset it to 0.
m.Tween.has_tweeners: Returns true if any Tweener has been added to the Tween and the Tween is valid. Useful when tweeners are added dynamically and the tween can end up empty. Killing an empty tween before it starts will prevent errors.
m.Tween.interpolate_value: This method can be used for manual interpolation of a value, when you don't want Tween to do animating for you. It's similar to @GlobalScope.lerp(), but with support for custom transition and easing.
m.Tween.is_running: Returns whether the Tween is currently running, i.e. it wasn't paused and it's not finished.
m.Tween.is_valid: Returns whether the Tween is valid. A valid Tween is a Tween contained by the scene tree (i.e. the array from SceneTree.get_processed_tweens() will contain this Tween). A Tween might become invalid when it has finished tweening, is killed, or when created with Tween.new(). Invalid Tweens can't have Tweeners appended.
m.Tween.kill: Aborts all tweening operations and invalidates the Tween.
m.Tween.loop_finished: Emitted when a full loop is complete (see set_loops()), providing the loop index. This signal is not emitted after the final loop, use finished instead for this case.
m.Tween.pause: Pauses the tweening. The animation can be resumed by using play().
m.Tween.play: Resumes a paused or stopped Tween.
m.Tween.set_ease: Sets the default ease type for PropertyTweeners and MethodTweeners appended after this method.
m.Tween.set_ignore_time_scale: If ignore is true, the tween will ignore Engine.time_scale and update with the real, elapsed time. This affects all Tweeners and their delays. Default value is false.
m.Tween.set_loops: Sets the number of times the tweening sequence will be repeated, i.e. set_loops(2) will run the animation twice.
m.Tween.set_parallel: If parallel is true, the Tweeners appended after this method will by default run simultaneously, as opposed to sequentially.
m.Tween.set_pause_mode: Determines the behavior of the Tween when the SceneTree is paused.
m.Tween.set_process_mode: Determines whether the Tween should run after process frames (see Node._process()) or physics frames (see Node._physics_process()).
m.Tween.set_speed_scale: Scales the speed of tweening. This affects all Tweeners and their delays.
m.Tween.set_trans: Sets the default transition type for PropertyTweeners and MethodTweeners appended after this method.
m.Tween.step_finished: Emitted when one step of the Tween is complete, providing the step index. One step is either a single Tweener or a group of Tweeners running in parallel.
m.Tween.stop: Stops the tweening and resets the Tween to its initial state. This will not remove any appended Tweeners.
m.Tween.tween_await: Creates and appends an AwaitTweener. This method can be used to await a signal to be emitted and create asynchronous animations or cutscenes.
m.Tween.tween_callback: Creates and appends a CallbackTweener. This method can be used to call an arbitrary method in any object. Use Callable.bind() to bind additional arguments for the call.
m.Tween.tween_interval: 在动画序列中插入等待间隔。
m.Tween.tween_method: Creates and appends a MethodTweener. This method is similar to a combination of tween_callback() and tween_property(). It calls a method over time with a tweened value provided as an argument. The value is tweened between from and to over the time specified by duration, in seconds. Use Callable.bind() to bind additional arguments for the call. You can use MethodTweener.set_ease() and MethodTweene…
m.Tween.tween_subtween: Creates and appends a SubtweenTweener. This method can be used to nest subtween within this Tween, allowing for the creation of more complex and composable sequences.
m.Tweener.finished: Emitted when the Tweener has just finished its job or became invalid (e.g. due to a freed object).
m.TwoBoneIK3D.get_end_bone_direction: Returns the end bone's tail direction when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.get_end_bone_length: Returns the end bone tail length of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.get_pole_node: Returns the pole target node that constructs a plane which the joints are all on and the pole is trying to direct.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.get_target_node: Returns the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.is_end_bone_extended: Returns true if the end bone is extended to have a tail.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.is_using_virtual_end: Returns true if the end bone is extended from the middle bone as a virtual bone.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.set_end_bone_direction: Sets the end bone tail direction when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.set_end_bone_length: Sets the end bone tail length when is_end_bone_extended() is true.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.set_extend_end_bone: If enabled is true, the end bone is extended to have a tail.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.set_pole_node: Sets the pole target node that constructs a plane which the joints are all on and the pole is trying to direct.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.set_target_node: Sets the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.
m.TwoBoneIK3D.set_use_virtual_end: If enabled is true, the end bone is extended from the middle bone as a virtual bone.
m.UDPServer.get_local_port: Returns the local port this server is listening to.
m.UDPServer.is_connection_available: Returns true if a packet with a new address/port combination was received on the socket.
m.UDPServer.is_listening: Returns true if the socket is open and listening on a port.
m.UDPServer.listen: Starts the server by opening a UDP socket listening on the given port. You can optionally specify a bind_address to only listen for packets sent to that address. See also PacketPeerUDP.bind().
m.UDPServer.max_pending_connections: Define the maximum number of pending connections, during poll(), any new pending connection exceeding that value will be automatically dropped. Setting this value to 0 effectively prevents any new pending connection to be accepted (e.g. when all your players have connected).
m.UDPServer.poll: Call this method at regular intervals (e.g. inside Node._process()) to process new packets. Any packet from a known address/port pair will be delivered to the appropriate PacketPeerUDP, while any packet received from an unknown address/port pair will be added as a pending connection (see is_connection_available() and take_connection()). The maximum number of pending connections is defined via max…
m.UDPServer.stop: Stops the server, closing the UDP socket if open. Will close all connected PacketPeerUDP accepted via take_connection() (remote peers will not be notified).
m.UDPServer.take_connection: Returns the first pending connection (connected to the appropriate address/port). Will return null if no new connection is available. See also is_connection_available(), PacketPeerUDP.connect_to_host().
m.UDSServer.listen: Listens on the socket at path. The socket file will be created at the specified path.
m.UDSServer.take_connection: If a connection is available, returns a StreamPeerUDS with the connection.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_CONFLICT_WITH_OTHER_MAP: Conflict with an existing port mapping.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_CONFLICT_WITH_OTHER_MEC: Conflict with other mechanism. May be returned instead of UPNP_RESULT_CONFLICT_WITH_OTHER_MAPPING if a port mapping conflicts with an existing one.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_EXT_PORT_MUST_BE_WILDCA: The external port value must be a wildcard.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_EXT_PORT_WILDCARD_NOT_P: The UPNPDevice does not allow wildcard values for the external port.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_INT_PORT_WILDCARD_NOT_P: The UPNPDevice does not allow wildcard values for the internal port.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_NOT_AUTHORIZED: Not authorized to use the command on the UPNPDevice. May be returned when the user disabled UPNP on their router.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_NO_DEVICES: No devices available. You may need to call discover() first, or discovery didn't detect any valid UPNPDevices.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_NO_GATEWAY: No gateway available. You may need to call discover() first, or discovery didn't detect any valid IGDs (InternetGatewayDevices).
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_NO_PORT_MAPS_AVAILABLE: No port maps are available. May also be returned if port mapping functionality is not available.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_NO_SUCH_ENTRY_IN_ARRAY: No such entry in array. May be returned if a given port, protocol combination is not found on a UPNPDevice.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_ONLY_PERMANENT_LEASE_SU: Only permanent leases are supported. Do not use the duration parameter when adding port mappings.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_PORT_MAPPING_NOT_FOUND: No port mapping was found for the given port, protocol combination on the given UPNPDevice.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_REMOTE_HOST_MUST_BE_WIL: The remote host value must be a wildcard.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_SAME_PORT_VALUES_REQUIR: External and internal port values must be the same.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_SRC_IP_WILDCARD_NOT_PER: The UPNPDevice does not allow wildcard values for the source IP address.
m.UPNP.UPNP_RESULT_SUCCESS: UPNP command or discovery was successful.
m.UPNP.add_device: Adds the given UPNPDevice to the list of discovered devices.
m.UPNP.add_port_mapping: Adds a mapping to forward the external port (between 1 and 65535, although recommended to use port 1024 or above) on the default gateway (see get_gateway()) to the port_internal on the local machine for the given protocol proto (either "TCP" or "UDP", with UDP being the default). If a port mapping for the given port and protocol combination already exists on that gateway device, this method tries…
m.UPNP.clear_devices: Clears the list of discovered devices.
m.UPNP.delete_port_mapping: Deletes the port mapping for the given port and protocol combination on the default gateway (see get_gateway()) if one exists. port must be a valid port between 1 and 65535, proto can be either "TCP" or "UDP". May be refused for mappings pointing to addresses other than this one, for well-known ports (below 1024), or for mappings not added via UPnP. See UPNPResult for possible return values.
m.UPNP.discover: Discovers local UPNPDevices. Clears the list of previously discovered devices.
m.UPNP.discover_ipv6: If true, IPv6 is used for UPNPDevice discovery.
m.UPNP.discover_local_port: If 0, the local port to use for discovery is chosen automatically by the system. If 1, discovery will be done from the source port 1900 (same as destination port). Otherwise, the value will be used as the port.
m.UPNP.discover_multicast_if: Multicast interface to use for discovery. Uses the default multicast interface if empty.

m.UPNP.remove_device: Removes the device at index from the list of discovered devices.
m.UPNP.set_device: Sets the device at index from the list of discovered devices to device.

m.UndoRedo.MERGE_ALL: Merges this action with the previous one if they have the same name.
m.UndoRedo.MERGE_DISABLE: Makes "do"/"undo" operations stay in separate actions.
m.UndoRedo.MERGE_ENDS: Merges this action with the previous one if they have the same name. Keeps only the first action's "undo" operations and the last action's "do" operations. Useful for sequential changes to a single value.
m.UndoRedo.add_do_method: Register a Callable that will be called when the action is committed.
m.UndoRedo.add_do_property: Register a property that would change its value to value when the action is committed.
m.UndoRedo.add_do_reference: Register a reference to an object that will be erased if the "do" history is deleted. This is useful for objects added by the "do" action and removed by the "undo" action.
m.UndoRedo.add_undo_method: Register a Callable that will be called when the action is undone.
m.UndoRedo.add_undo_property: Register a property that would change its value to value when the action is undone.
m.UndoRedo.add_undo_reference: Register a reference to an object that will be erased if the "undo" history is deleted. This is useful for objects added by the "undo" action and removed by the "do" action.
m.UndoRedo.clear_history: Clear the undo/redo history and associated references.
m.UndoRedo.commit_action: Commit the action. If execute is true (which it is by default), all "do" methods/properties are called/set when this function is called.
m.UndoRedo.create_action: Create a new action. After this is called, do all your calls to add_do_method(), add_undo_method(), add_do_property(), and add_undo_property(), then commit the action with commit_action().
m.UndoRedo.end_force_keep_in_merge_ends: Stops marking operations as to be processed even if the action gets merged with another in the MERGE_ENDS mode. See start_force_keep_in_merge_ends().
m.UndoRedo.get_action_name: Gets the action name from its index.
m.UndoRedo.get_current_action: Gets the index of the current action.
m.UndoRedo.get_current_action_name: Gets the name of the current action, equivalent to get_action_name(get_current_action()).
m.UndoRedo.get_history_count: Returns how many elements are in the history.
m.UndoRedo.get_version: Gets the version. Every time a new action is committed, the UndoRedo's version number is increased automatically.
m.UndoRedo.has_redo: Returns true if a "redo" action is available.
m.UndoRedo.has_undo: Returns true if an "undo" action is available.
m.UndoRedo.is_committing_action: Returns true if the UndoRedo is currently committing the action, i.e. running its "do" method or property change (see commit_action()).
m.UndoRedo.max_steps: The maximum number of steps that can be stored in the undo/redo history. If the number of stored steps exceeds this limit, older steps are removed from history and can no longer be reached by calling undo(). A value of 0 or lower means no limit.
m.UndoRedo.redo: Redo the last action. Returns false if there was no action to redo.
m.UndoRedo.start_force_keep_in_merge_ends: Marks the next "do" and "undo" operations to be processed even if the action gets merged with another in the MERGE_ENDS mode. Return to normal operation using end_force_keep_in_merge_ends().
m.UndoRedo.undo: Undo the last action. Returns false if there was no action to undo.
m.UndoRedo.version_changed: Called when undo() or redo() was called.
