m.Vector4.is_zero_approx: Returns true if this vector's values are approximately zero, by running @GlobalScope.is_zero_approx() on each component.
m.Vector4.length: Returns the length (magnitude) of this vector.
m.Vector4.length_squared: Returns the squared length (squared magnitude) of this vector.
m.Vector4.lerp: Returns the result of the linear interpolation between this vector and to by amount weight. weight is on the range of 0.0 to 1.0, representing the amount of interpolation.
m.Vector4.max: Returns the component-wise maximum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4(maxf(x, with.x), maxf(y, with.y), maxf(z, with.z), maxf(w, with.w)).
m.Vector4.max_axis_index: Returns the axis of the vector's highest value. See AXIS_* constants. If all components are equal, this method returns AXIS_X.
m.Vector4.maxf: Returns the component-wise maximum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4(maxf(x, with), maxf(y, with), maxf(z, with), maxf(w, with)).
m.Vector4.min: Returns the component-wise minimum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4(minf(x, with.x), minf(y, with.y), minf(z, with.z), minf(w, with.w)).
m.Vector4.min_axis_index: Returns the axis of the vector's lowest value. See AXIS_* constants. If all components are equal, this method returns AXIS_W.
m.Vector4.minf: Returns the component-wise minimum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4(minf(x, with), minf(y, with), minf(z, with), minf(w, with)).
m.Vector4.normalized: Returns the result of scaling the vector to unit length. Equivalent to v / v.length(). Returns (0, 0, 0, 0) if v.length() == 0. See also is_normalized().
m.Vector4.posmod: Returns a vector composed of the @GlobalScope.fposmod() of this vector's components and mod.
m.Vector4.posmodv: Returns a vector composed of the @GlobalScope.fposmod() of this vector's components and modv's components.
m.Vector4.round: Returns a new vector with all components rounded to the nearest integer, with halfway cases rounded away from zero.
m.Vector4.sign: Returns a new vector with each component set to 1.0 if it's positive, -1.0 if it's negative, and 0.0 if it's zero. The result is identical to calling @GlobalScope.sign() on each component.
m.Vector4.snapped: Returns a new vector with each component snapped to the nearest multiple of the corresponding component in step. This can also be used to round the components to an arbitrary number of decimals.
m.Vector4.snappedf: Returns a new vector with each component snapped to the nearest multiple of step. This can also be used to round the components to an arbitrary number of decimals.
m.Vector4.w: The vector's W component. Also accessible by using the index position [3].
m.Vector4.x: The vector's X component. Also accessible by using the index position [0].
m.Vector4.y: The vector's Y component. Also accessible by using the index position [1].
m.Vector4.z: The vector's Z component. Also accessible by using the index position [2].
m.Vector4i.AXIS_W: Enumerated value for the W axis. Returned by max_axis_index() and min_axis_index().
m.Vector4i.AXIS_X: Enumerated value for the X axis. Returned by max_axis_index() and min_axis_index().
m.Vector4i.AXIS_Y: Enumerated value for the Y axis. Returned by max_axis_index() and min_axis_index().
m.Vector4i.AXIS_Z: Enumerated value for the Z axis. Returned by max_axis_index() and min_axis_index().
m.Vector4i.ZERO: Zero vector, a vector with all components set to 0.
m.Vector4i.abs: Returns a new vector with all components in absolute values (i.e. positive).
m.Vector4i.clamp: Returns a new vector with all components clamped between the components of min and max, by running @GlobalScope.clamp() on each component.
m.Vector4i.clampi: Returns a new vector with all components clamped between min and max, by running @GlobalScope.clamp() on each component.
m.Vector4i.distance_squared_to: Returns the squared Euclidean distance [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance] between this vector and to.
m.Vector4i.distance_to: Returns the Euclidean distance [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance] between this vector and to.
m.Vector4i.length: Returns the length (magnitude) of this vector.
m.Vector4i.length_squared: Returns the squared length (squared magnitude) of this vector.
m.Vector4i.max: Returns the component-wise maximum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4i(maxi(x, with.x), maxi(y, with.y), maxi(z, with.z), maxi(w, with.w)).
m.Vector4i.max_axis_index: Returns the axis of the vector's highest value. See AXIS_* constants. If all components are equal, this method returns AXIS_X.
m.Vector4i.maxi: Returns the component-wise maximum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4i(maxi(x, with), maxi(y, with), maxi(z, with), maxi(w, with)).
m.Vector4i.min: Returns the component-wise minimum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4i(mini(x, with.x), mini(y, with.y), mini(z, with.z), mini(w, with.w)).
m.Vector4i.min_axis_index: Returns the axis of the vector's lowest value. See AXIS_* constants. If all components are equal, this method returns AXIS_W.
m.Vector4i.mini: Returns the component-wise minimum of this and with, equivalent to Vector4i(mini(x, with), mini(y, with), mini(z, with), mini(w, with)).
m.Vector4i.sign: Returns a new vector with each component set to 1 if it's positive, -1 if it's negative, and 0 if it's zero. The result is identical to calling @GlobalScope.sign() on each component.
m.Vector4i.snapped: Returns a new vector with each component snapped to the closest multiple of the corresponding component in step.
m.Vector4i.snappedi: Returns a new vector with each component snapped to the closest multiple of step.
m.Vector4i.w: The vector's W component. Also accessible by using the index position [3].
m.Vector4i.x: The vector's X component. Also accessible by using the index position [0].
m.Vector4i.y: The vector's Y component. Also accessible by using the index position [1].
m.Vector4i.z: The vector's Z component. Also accessible by using the index position [2].
m.VehicleBody3D.brake: Slows down the vehicle by applying a braking force. The vehicle is only slowed down if the wheels are in contact with a surface. The force you need to apply to adequately slow down your vehicle depends on the RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 30 range for hard braking.
m.VehicleBody3D.engine_force: Accelerates the vehicle by applying an engine force. The vehicle is only sped up if the wheels that have VehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction set to true and are in contact with a surface. The RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle has an effect on the acceleration of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 50 range for acceleration.
m.VehicleBody3D.steering: The steering angle for the vehicle. Setting this to a non-zero value will result in the vehicle turning when it's moving. Wheels that have VehicleWheel3D.use_as_steering set to true will automatically be rotated.
m.VehicleWheel3D.brake: Slows down the wheel by applying a braking force. The wheel is only slowed down if it is in contact with a surface. The force you need to apply to adequately slow down your vehicle depends on the RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 30 range for hard braking.
m.VehicleWheel3D.damping_compression: The damping applied to the suspension spring when being compressed, meaning when the wheel is moving up relative to the vehicle. It is measured in Newton-seconds per millimeter (N⋅s/mm), or megagrams per second (Mg/s). This value should be between 0.0 (no damping) and 1.0, but may be more. A value of 0.0 means the car will keep bouncing as the spring keeps its energy. A good value for this is aro…
m.VehicleWheel3D.damping_relaxation: The damping applied to the suspension spring when rebounding or extending, meaning when the wheel is moving down relative to the vehicle. It is measured in Newton-seconds per millimeter (N⋅s/mm), or megagrams per second (Mg/s). This value should be between 0.0 (no damping) and 1.0, but may be more. This value should always be slightly higher than the damping_compression property. For a damping_co…
m.VehicleWheel3D.engine_force: Accelerates the wheel by applying an engine force. The wheel is only sped up if it is in contact with a surface. The RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle has an effect on the acceleration of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 50 range for acceleration.
m.VehicleWheel3D.get_contact_body: Returns the contacting body node if valid in the tree, as Node3D. At the moment, GridMap is not supported so the node will be always of type PhysicsBody3D.
m.VehicleWheel3D.get_contact_normal: Returns the normal of the suspension's collision in world space if the wheel is in contact. If the wheel isn't in contact with anything, returns a vector pointing directly along the suspension axis toward the vehicle in world space.
m.VehicleWheel3D.get_contact_point: Returns the point of the suspension's collision in world space if the wheel is in contact. If the wheel isn't in contact with anything, returns the maximum point of the wheel's ray cast in world space, which is defined by wheel_rest_length + wheel_radius.
m.VehicleWheel3D.get_rpm: Returns the rotational speed of the wheel in revolutions per minute.
m.VehicleWheel3D.get_skidinfo: Returns a value between 0.0 and 1.0 that indicates whether this wheel is skidding. 0.0 is skidding (the wheel has lost grip, e.g. icy terrain), 1.0 means not skidding (the wheel has full grip, e.g. dry asphalt road).
m.VehicleWheel3D.is_in_contact: Returns true if this wheel is in contact with a surface.
m.VehicleWheel3D.steering: The steering angle for the wheel, in radians. Setting this to a non-zero value will result in the vehicle turning when it's moving.
m.VehicleWheel3D.suspension_max_force: The maximum force the spring can resist. This value should be higher than a quarter of the RigidBody3D.mass of the VehicleBody3D or the spring will not carry the weight of the vehicle. Good results are often obtained by a value that is about 3× to 4× this number.
m.VehicleWheel3D.suspension_stiffness: The stiffness of the suspension, measured in Newtons per millimeter (N/mm), or megagrams per second squared (Mg/s²). Use a value lower than 50 for an off-road car, a value between 50 and 100 for a race car and try something around 200 for something like a Formula 1 car.
m.VehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel: This is the distance the suspension can travel. As Godot units are equivalent to meters, keep this setting relatively low. Try a value between 0.1 and 0.3 depending on the type of car.
m.VehicleWheel3D.use_as_steering: If true, this wheel will be turned when the car steers. This value is used in conjunction with VehicleBody3D.steering and ignored if you are using the per-wheel steering value instead.
m.VehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction: If true, this wheel transfers engine force to the ground to propel the vehicle forward. This value is used in conjunction with VehicleBody3D.engine_force and ignored if you are using the per-wheel engine_force value instead.
m.VehicleWheel3D.wheel_friction_slip: This determines how much grip this wheel has. It is combined with the friction setting of the surface the wheel is in contact with. 0.0 means no grip, 1.0 is normal grip. For a drift car setup, try setting the grip of the rear wheels slightly lower than the front wheels, or use a lower value to simulate tire wear.
m.VehicleWheel3D.wheel_radius: The radius of the wheel in meters.
m.VehicleWheel3D.wheel_rest_length: This is the distance in meters the wheel is lowered from its origin point. Don't set this to 0.0 and move the wheel into position, instead move the origin point of your wheel (the gizmo in Godot) to the position the wheel will take when bottoming out, then use the rest length to move the wheel down to the position it should be in when the car is in rest.
m.VehicleWheel3D.wheel_roll_influence: This value affects the roll of your vehicle. If set to 1.0 for all wheels, your vehicle will resist body roll, while a value of 0.0 will be prone to rolling over.
m.VideoStream._instantiate_playback: Called when the video starts playing, to initialize and return a subclass of VideoStreamPlayback.
m.VideoStream.file: The video file path or URI that this VideoStream resource handles.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._get_channels: Returns the number of audio channels.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._get_length: Returns the video duration in seconds, if known, or 0 if unknown.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._get_mix_rate: Returns the audio sample rate used for mixing.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._get_playback_positi: Return the current playback timestamp. Called in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.stream_position getter.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._get_texture: Allocates a Texture2D in which decoded video frames will be drawn.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._is_paused: Returns the paused status, as set by _set_paused().
m.VideoStreamPlayback._is_playing: Returns the playback state, as determined by calls to _play() and _stop().
m.VideoStreamPlayback._play: Called in response to VideoStreamPlayer.autoplay or VideoStreamPlayer.play(). Note that manual playback may also invoke _stop() multiple times before this method is called. _is_playing() should return true once playing.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._seek: Seeks to time seconds. Called in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.stream_position setter.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._set_audio_track: Select the audio track idx. Called when playback starts, and in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.audio_track setter.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._set_paused: Set the paused status of video playback. _is_paused() must return paused. Called in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.paused setter.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._stop: Stops playback. May be called multiple times before _play(), or in response to VideoStreamPlayer.stop(). _is_playing() should return false once stopped.
m.VideoStreamPlayback._update: Ticks video playback for delta seconds. Called every frame as long as both _is_paused() and _is_playing() return true.
m.VideoStreamPlayback.mix_audio: Render num_frames audio frames (of _get_channels() floats each) from buffer, starting from index offset in the array. Returns the number of audio frames rendered, or -1 on error.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.audio_track: The embedded audio track to play.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.autoplay: If true, playback starts when the scene loads.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.buffering_msec: Amount of time in milliseconds to store in buffer while playing.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.bus: Audio bus to use for sound playback.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.expand: If true, the video scales to the control size. Otherwise, the control minimum size will be automatically adjusted to match the video stream's dimensions.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.get_stream_length: The length of the current stream, in seconds.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.get_stream_name: Returns the video stream's name, or "" if no video stream is assigned.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.get_video_texture: Returns the current frame as a Texture2D.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.is_playing: Returns true if the video is playing.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.loop: If true, the video restarts when it reaches its end.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.paused: If true, the video is paused.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.play: Starts the video playback from the beginning. If the video is paused, this will not unpause the video.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.speed_scale: The stream's current speed scale. 1.0 is the normal speed, while 2.0 is double speed and 0.5 is half speed. A speed scale of 0.0 pauses the video, similar to setting paused to true.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.stop: Stops the video playback and sets the stream position to 0.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.stream: The assigned video stream. See description for supported formats.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.stream_position: The current position of the stream, in seconds.
m.VideoStreamPlayer.volume: Audio volume as a linear value.
m.Viewport.ANISOTROPY_4X: Use 4× anisotropic filtering. This is the default value.
m.Viewport.ANISOTROPY_MAX: Represents the size of the AnisotropicFiltering enum.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_AREA_LIGHT_ATLAS: Draws the atlas used by AreaLight3D nodes in the upper left quadrant of the Viewport.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_AREA_LIGHTS: Draws the cluster used by AreaLight3D nodes to optimize light rendering.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_DECALS: Draws the cluster used by Decal nodes to optimize decal rendering.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_OMNI_LIGHTS: Draws the cluster used by OmniLight3D nodes to optimize light rendering.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_REFLECTION_P: Draws the cluster used by ReflectionProbe nodes to optimize reflection probes.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_SPOT_LIGHTS: Draws the cluster used by SpotLight3D nodes to optimize light rendering.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_DECAL_ATLAS: Draws the decal atlas used by Decals and light projector textures in the upper left quadrant of the Viewport.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_A: Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from DirectionalLight3Ds in the upper left quadrant of the Viewport.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_DISABLE_LOD: Draws all of the objects at their highest polycount regardless of their distance from the camera. No low level of detail (LOD) is applied.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_GI_BUFFER: Draws the buffer used for global illumination from VoxelGI or SDFGI. Requires VoxelGI (at least one visible baked VoxelGI node) or SDFGI (Environment.sdfgi_enabled) to be enabled to have a visible effect.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_INTERNAL_BUFFER: Draws the internal resolution buffer of the scene in linear colorspace before tonemapping or post-processing is applied.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_LIGHTING: Objects are displayed without textures and only with lighting information.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_MOTION_VECTORS: Draws vector lines over the viewport to indicate the movement of pixels between frames.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_NORMAL_BUFFER: Objects are displayed without lighting information and their textures replaced by normal mapping.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_OCCLUDERS: Draws the buffer used for occlusion culling.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_OVERDRAW: Objects are displayed semi-transparent with additive blending so you can see where they are drawing over top of one another. A higher overdraw means you are wasting performance on drawing pixels that are being hidden behind others.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_PSSM_SPLITS: Colors each PSSM split for the DirectionalLight3Ds in the scene a different color so you can see where the splits are. In order (from closest to furthest from the camera), they are colored red, green, blue, and yellow.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_SCENE_LUMINANCE: Draws the scene luminance buffer (if available) in the upper left quadrant of the Viewport.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_SDFGI: Draws the cascades used to render signed distance field global illumination (SDFGI).
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_SDFGI_PROBES: Draws the probes used for signed distance field global illumination (SDFGI).
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_SHADOW_ATLAS: Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from OmniLight3Ds and SpotLight3Ds in the upper left quadrant of the Viewport.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_SSAO: Draws the screen-space ambient occlusion texture instead of the scene so that you can clearly see how it is affecting objects. In order for this display mode to work, you must have Environment.ssao_enabled set in your WorldEnvironment.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_SSIL: Draws the screen-space indirect lighting texture instead of the scene so that you can clearly see how it is affecting objects. In order for this display mode to work, you must have Environment.ssil_enabled set in your WorldEnvironment.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_UNSHADED: Objects are displayed without light information.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_VOXEL_GI_ALBEDO: Objects are displayed with only the albedo value from VoxelGIs. Requires at least one visible VoxelGI node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_VOXEL_GI_EMISSION: Objects are displayed with only the emission color from VoxelGIs. Requires at least one visible VoxelGI node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_VOXEL_GI_LIGHTING: Objects are displayed with only the lighting value from VoxelGIs. Requires at least one visible VoxelGI node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
m.Viewport.DEBUG_DRAW_WIREFRAME: Objects are displayed as wireframe models.
m.Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FIL: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance.
Represents the size of the DefaultCanvasItemTextureFilter enum.
The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel only. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter is true). This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance.
The Viewport will inherit the filter from its parent CanvasItem or Viewport.
m.Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REP: Disables textures repeating. Instead, when reading UVs outside the 0-1 range, the value will be clamped to the edge of the texture, resulting in a stretched out look at the borders of the texture.

Enables the texture to repeat when UV coordinates are outside the 0-1 range. If using one of the linear filtering modes, this can result in artifacts at the edges of a texture when the sampler filters across the edges of the texture.
Represents the size of the DefaultCanvasItemTextureRepeat enum.
Flip the texture when repeating so that the edge lines up instead of abruptly changing.
The Viewport will inherit the repeat mode from its parent CanvasItem or Viewport.
m.Viewport.MSAA_2X: Use 2× Multisample Antialiasing. This has a moderate performance cost. It helps reduce aliasing noticeably, but 4× MSAA still looks substantially better.
m.Viewport.MSAA_4X: Use 4× Multisample Antialiasing. This has a significant performance cost, and is generally a good compromise between performance and quality.
m.Viewport.MSAA_8X: Use 8× Multisample Antialiasing. This has a very high performance cost. The difference between 4× and 8× MSAA may not always be visible in real gameplay conditions. Likely unsupported on low-end and older hardware.
m.Viewport.MSAA_DISABLED: Multisample antialiasing mode disabled. This is the default value, and is also the fastest setting.
m.Viewport.MSAA_MAX: Represents the size of the MSAA enum.
m.Viewport.RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME: Amount of draw calls in frame.
m.Viewport.RENDER_INFO_MAX: Represents the size of the RenderInfo enum.
m.Viewport.RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS: Canvas item rendering. This includes all 2D rendering.
m.Viewport.RENDER_INFO_TYPE_MAX: Represents the size of the RenderInfoType enum.
m.Viewport.RENDER_INFO_TYPE_SHADOW: Shadow render pass. Objects will be rendered several times depending on the number of amounts of lights with shadows and the number of directional shadow splits.
m.Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_BILINEAR: Use bilinear scaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in undersampling while values greater than 1.0 will result in supersampling. A value of 1.0 disables scaling.
m.Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_FSR: Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in the viewport being upscaled using FSR. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 disables scaling.
m.Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_FSR2: Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2.2 upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using scaling_3d_scale. Values less than 1.0 will result in the viewport being upscaled using FSR2. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 will use FSR2 at native resolution as a TAA solution.
m.Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_MAX: Represents the size of the Scaling3DMode enum.
m.Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_METALFX_SPATIAL: Use the MetalFX spatial upscaler [https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalfx/mtlfxspatialscaler#overview] for the viewport's 3D buffer.
m.Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_METALFX_TEMPORA: Use the MetalFX temporal upscaler [https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalfx/mtlfxtemporalscaler#overview] for the viewport's 3D buffer.
m.Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_NEAREST: Use nearest-neighbor filtering for the viewport's 3D buffer. This looks crisper than SCALING_3D_MODE_BILINEAR and has no additional rendering cost. The amount of scaling can be set using scaling_3d_scale. Values greater than 1.0 are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of 1.0 disables scaling.
m.Viewport.SCREEN_SPACE_AA_DISABLED: Do not perform any antialiasing in the full screen post-process.
m.Viewport.SCREEN_SPACE_AA_FXAA: Use fast approximate antialiasing. FXAA is a popular screen-space antialiasing method, which is fast but will make the image look blurry, especially at lower resolutions. It can still work relatively well at large resolutions such as 1440p and 4K.
m.Viewport.SCREEN_SPACE_AA_MAX: Represents the size of the ScreenSpaceAA enum.
m.Viewport.SCREEN_SPACE_AA_SMAA: Use subpixel morphological antialiasing. SMAA may produce clearer results than FXAA, but at a slightly higher performance cost.
m.Viewport.SDF_OVERSIZE_100_PERCENT: The signed distance field only covers the viewport's own rectangle.
m.Viewport.SDF_OVERSIZE_120_PERCENT: The signed distance field is expanded to cover 20% of the viewport's size around the borders.
m.Viewport.SDF_OVERSIZE_150_PERCENT: The signed distance field is expanded to cover 50% of the viewport's size around the borders.
m.Viewport.SDF_OVERSIZE_200_PERCENT: The signed distance field is expanded to cover 100% (double) of the viewport's size around the borders.
m.Viewport.SDF_OVERSIZE_MAX: Represents the size of the SDFOversize enum.
m.Viewport.SDF_SCALE_100_PERCENT: The signed distance field is rendered at full resolution.
m.Viewport.SDF_SCALE_25_PERCENT: The signed distance field is rendered at a quarter the resolution of this viewport.
m.Viewport.SDF_SCALE_50_PERCENT: The signed distance field is rendered at half the resolution of this viewport.
m.Viewport.SDF_SCALE_MAX: Represents the size of the SDFScale enum.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_1: This quadrant will only be used by one shadow map.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_10: This quadrant will be split 1024 ways and used by up to 1024 shadow maps. Unless the positional_shadow_atlas_size is very high, the shadows in this quadrant will be very low resolution.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_16: This quadrant will be split 16 ways and used by up to 16 shadow maps.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_25: This quadrant will be split 256 ways and used by up to 256 shadow maps. Unless the positional_shadow_atlas_size is very high, the shadows in this quadrant will be very low resolution.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_4: This quadrant will be split in 4 and used by up to 4 shadow maps.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_64: This quadrant will be split 64 ways and used by up to 64 shadow maps.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_DI: This quadrant will not be used.
m.Viewport.SHADOW_ATLAS_QUADRANT_SUBDIV_MA: Represents the size of the PositionalShadowAtlasQuadrantSubdiv enum.
m.Viewport.VRS_MAX: Represents the size of the VRSMode enum.
m.Viewport.VRS_TEXTURE: Variable Rate Shading uses a texture. Note, for stereoscopic use a texture atlas with a texture for each view.
m.Viewport.VRS_UPDATE_ALWAYS: The input texture for variable rate shading will be processed each frame.
m.Viewport.VRS_UPDATE_DISABLED: The input texture for variable rate shading will not be processed.
m.Viewport.VRS_UPDATE_MAX: Represents the size of the VRSUpdateMode enum.
m.Viewport.VRS_UPDATE_ONCE: The input texture for variable rate shading will be processed once.
m.Viewport.VRS_XR: Variable Rate Shading's texture is supplied by the primary XRInterface.
m.Viewport.anisotropic_filtering_level: Sets the maximum number of samples to take when using anisotropic filtering on textures (as a power of two). A higher sample count will result in sharper textures at oblique angles, but is more expensive to compute. A value of 0 forcibly disables anisotropic filtering, even on materials where it is enabled.
m.Viewport.audio_listener_enable_2d: If true, the viewport will process 2D audio streams.
m.Viewport.audio_listener_enable_3d: If true, the viewport will process 3D audio streams.
m.Viewport.canvas_cull_mask: The rendering layers in which this Viewport renders CanvasItem nodes.
m.Viewport.canvas_item_default_texture_fil: The default filter mode used by CanvasItem nodes in this viewport.
m.Viewport.canvas_item_default_texture_rep: The default repeat mode used by CanvasItem nodes in this viewport.
m.Viewport.canvas_transform: The canvas transform of the viewport, useful for changing the on-screen positions of all child CanvasItems. This is relative to the global canvas transform of the viewport.
m.Viewport.debug_draw: The overlay mode for test rendered geometry in debug purposes.
m.Viewport.find_world_2d: Returns the first valid World2D for this viewport, searching the world_2d property of itself and any Viewport ancestor.
m.Viewport.find_world_3d: Returns the first valid World3D for this viewport, searching the world_3d property of itself and any Viewport ancestor.
m.Viewport.fsr_sharpness: Determines how sharp the upscaled image will be when using the FSR upscaling mode. Sharpness halves with every whole number. Values go from 0.0 (sharpest) to 2.0. Values above 2.0 won't make a visible difference.
m.Viewport.get_audio_listener_2d: Returns the currently active 2D audio listener. Returns null if there are no active 2D audio listeners, in which case the active 2D camera will be treated as listener.
m.Viewport.get_audio_listener_3d: Returns the currently active 3D audio listener. Returns null if there are no active 3D audio listeners, in which case the active 3D camera will be treated as listener.
m.Viewport.get_camera_2d: Returns the currently active 2D camera. Returns null if there are no active cameras.
m.Viewport.get_camera_3d: Returns the currently active 3D camera. Returns null if there are no active cameras.
m.Viewport.get_canvas_cull_mask_bit: Returns an individual bit on the rendering layer mask.
m.Viewport.get_embedded_subwindows: Returns a list of the visible embedded Windows inside the viewport.
m.Viewport.get_final_transform: Returns the transform from the viewport's coordinate system to the embedder's coordinate system.
m.Viewport.get_mouse_position: Returns the mouse's position in this Viewport using the coordinate system of this Viewport.
m.Viewport.get_positional_shadow_atlas_qua: Returns the positional shadow atlas quadrant subdivision of the specified quadrant.
m.Viewport.get_render_info: Returns rendering statistics of the given type.
m.Viewport.get_screen_transform: Returns the transform from the Viewport's coordinates to the screen coordinates of the containing window manager window.
m.Viewport.get_stretch_transform: Returns the automatically computed 2D stretch transform, taking the Viewport's stretch settings into account. The final value is multiplied by Window.content_scale_factor, but only for the root viewport. If this method is called on a SubViewport (e.g., in a scene tree with SubViewportContainer and SubViewport), the scale factor of the root window will not be applied. Using Transform2D.get_scale()…
m.Viewport.get_viewport_rid: Returns the viewport's RID from the RenderingServer.
m.Viewport.get_visible_rect: Returns the visible rectangle in global screen coordinates.
m.Viewport.global_canvas_transform: The global canvas transform of the viewport. The canvas transform is relative to this.
m.Viewport.gui_cancel_drag: Cancels the drag operation that was previously started through Control._get_drag_data() or forced with Control.force_drag().
m.Viewport.gui_disable_input: If true, the viewport will not receive input events.
m.Viewport.gui_drag_threshold: The minimum distance the mouse cursor must move while pressed before a drag operation begins.
m.Viewport.gui_embed_subwindows: If true, sub-windows (popups and dialogs) will be embedded inside application window as control-like nodes. If false, they will appear as separate windows handled by the operating system.
m.Viewport.gui_focus_changed: Emitted when a Control node grabs keyboard focus.
m.Viewport.gui_get_drag_data: Returns the drag data from the GUI, that was previously returned by Control._get_drag_data().
m.Viewport.gui_get_drag_description: Returns the human-readable description of the drag data, used for assistive apps.
m.Viewport.gui_get_focus_owner: Returns the currently focused Control within this viewport. If no Control is focused, returns null.
m.Viewport.gui_get_hovered_control: Returns the Control that the mouse is currently hovering over in this viewport. If no Control has the cursor, returns null.
m.Viewport.gui_is_drag_successful: Returns true if the drag operation is successful.
m.Viewport.gui_is_dragging: Returns true if a drag operation is currently ongoing and where the drop action could happen in this viewport.
m.Viewport.gui_release_focus: Removes the focus from the currently focused Control within this viewport. If no Control has the focus, does nothing.
m.Viewport.gui_set_drag_description: Sets the human-readable description of the drag data to description, used for assistive apps.
m.Viewport.gui_snap_controls_to_pixels: If true, the GUI controls on the viewport will lay pixel perfectly.
m.Viewport.handle_input_locally: If true, this viewport will mark incoming input events as handled by itself. If false, this is instead done by the first parent viewport that is set to handle input locally.
m.Viewport.is_input_handled: Returns whether the current InputEvent has been handled. Input events are not handled until set_input_as_handled() has been called during the lifetime of an InputEvent.
m.Viewport.mesh_lod_threshold: The automatic LOD bias to use for meshes rendered within the Viewport (this is analogous to ReflectionProbe.mesh_lod_threshold). Higher values will use less detailed versions of meshes that have LOD variations generated. If set to 0.0, automatic LOD is disabled. Increase mesh_lod_threshold to improve performance at the cost of geometry detail.
m.Viewport.msaa_2d: The multisample antialiasing mode for 2D/Canvas rendering. A higher number results in smoother edges at the cost of significantly worse performance. A value of MSAA_2X or MSAA_4X is best unless targeting very high-end systems. This has no effect on shader-induced aliasing or texture aliasing.
m.Viewport.msaa_3d: The multisample antialiasing mode for 3D rendering. A higher number results in smoother edges at the cost of significantly worse performance. A value of MSAA_2X or MSAA_4X is best unless targeting very high-end systems. See also bilinear scaling 3D scaling_3d_mode for supersampling, which provides higher quality but is much more expensive. This has no effect on shader-induced aliasing or texture…
m.Viewport.notify_mouse_entered: Inform the Viewport that the mouse has entered its area. Use this function before sending an InputEventMouseButton or InputEventMouseMotion to the Viewport with push_input(). See also notify_mouse_exited().
m.Viewport.notify_mouse_exited: Inform the Viewport that the mouse has left its area. Use this function when the node that displays the viewport notices the mouse has left the area of the displayed viewport. See also notify_mouse_entered().
m.Viewport.oversampling: If true and one of the following conditions are true: SubViewport.size_2d_override_stretch and SubViewport.size_2d_override are set, Window.content_scale_factor is set and scaling is enabled, oversampling_override is set, font and DPITexture oversampling are enabled.
m.Viewport.oversampling_override: If greater than zero, this value is used as the font oversampling factor, otherwise oversampling is equal to viewport scale.
m.Viewport.own_world_3d: If true, the viewport will use a unique copy of the World3D defined in world_3d.
m.Viewport.physics_object_picking: If true, the objects rendered by viewport become subjects of mouse picking process.
m.Viewport.physics_object_picking_first_on: If true, the input_event signal will only be sent to one physics object in the mouse picking process. If you want to get the top object only, you must also enable physics_object_picking_sort.
m.Viewport.physics_object_picking_sort: If true, objects receive mouse picking events sorted primarily by their CanvasItem.z_index and secondarily by their position in the scene tree. If false, the order is undetermined.
m.Viewport.positional_shadow_atlas_16_bits: Use 16 bits for the omni/spot shadow depth map. Enabling this results in shadows having less precision and may result in shadow acne, but can lead to performance improvements on some devices.
m.Viewport.positional_shadow_atlas_quad_0: The subdivision amount of the first quadrant on the shadow atlas.
m.Viewport.positional_shadow_atlas_quad_1: The subdivision amount of the second quadrant on the shadow atlas.
m.Viewport.positional_shadow_atlas_quad_2: The subdivision amount of the third quadrant on the shadow atlas.
m.Viewport.positional_shadow_atlas_quad_3: The subdivision amount of the fourth quadrant on the shadow atlas.
m.Viewport.positional_shadow_atlas_size: The shadow atlas' resolution (used for omni and spot lights). The value is rounded up to the nearest power of 2.
m.Viewport.push_input: Triggers the given event in this Viewport. This can be used to pass an InputEvent between viewports, or to locally apply inputs that were sent over the network or saved to a file.
m.Viewport.push_text_input: Helper method which calls the set_text() method on the currently focused Control, provided that it is defined (e.g. if the focused Control is Button or LineEdit).
m.Viewport.scaling_3d_mode: Sets scaling 3D mode. Bilinear scaling renders at different resolution to either undersample or supersample the viewport. FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0, abbreviated to FSR, is an upscaling technology that produces high quality images at fast framerates by using a spatially aware upscaling algorithm. FSR is slightly more expensive than bilinear, but it produces significantly higher image quality…
m.Viewport.scaling_3d_scale: Scales the 3D render buffer based on the viewport size uses an image filter specified in ProjectSettings.rendering/scaling_3d/mode to scale the output image to the full viewport size. Values lower than 1.0 can be used to speed up 3D rendering at the cost of quality (undersampling). Values greater than 1.0 are only valid for bilinear mode and can be used to improve 3D rendering quality at a high p…
m.Viewport.screen_space_aa: Sets the screen-space antialiasing method used. Screen-space antialiasing works by selectively blurring edges in a post-process shader. It differs from MSAA which takes multiple coverage samples while rendering objects. Screen-space AA methods are typically faster than MSAA and will smooth out specular aliasing, but tend to make scenes appear blurry.
m.Viewport.sdf_oversize: Controls how much of the original viewport's size should be covered by the 2D signed distance field. This SDF can be sampled in CanvasItem shaders and is also used for GPUParticles2D collision. Higher values allow portions of occluders located outside the viewport to still be taken into account in the generated signed distance field, at the cost of performance. If you notice particles falling thr…
m.Viewport.sdf_scale: The resolution scale to use for the 2D signed distance field. Higher values lead to a more precise and more stable signed distance field as the camera moves, at the cost of performance.
m.Viewport.set_canvas_cull_mask_bit: Set/clear individual bits on the rendering layer mask. This simplifies editing this Viewport's layers.
m.Viewport.set_input_as_handled: Stops the input from propagating further up the SceneTree.
m.Viewport.set_positional_shadow_atlas_qua: Sets the number of subdivisions to use in the specified quadrant. A higher number of subdivisions allows you to have more shadows in the scene at once, but reduces the quality of the shadows. A good practice is to have quadrants with a varying number of subdivisions and to have as few subdivisions as possible.
m.Viewport.size_changed: Emitted when the size of the viewport is changed, whether by resizing of window, or some other means.
m.Viewport.snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel: If true, CanvasItem nodes will internally snap to full pixels. Their position can still be sub-pixel, but the decimals will not have effect. This can lead to a crisper appearance at the cost of less smooth movement, especially when Camera2D smoothing is enabled.
m.Viewport.snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel: If true, vertices of CanvasItem nodes will snap to full pixels. Only affects the final vertex positions, not the transforms. This can lead to a crisper appearance at the cost of less smooth movement, especially when Camera2D smoothing is enabled.
m.Viewport.texture_mipmap_bias: Affects the final texture sharpness by reading from a lower or higher mipmap (also called "texture LOD bias"). Negative values make mipmapped textures sharper but grainier when viewed at a distance, while positive values make mipmapped textures blurrier (even when up close).
m.Viewport.transparent_bg: If true, the viewport should render its background as transparent.
m.Viewport.update_mouse_cursor_state: Force instantly updating the display based on the current mouse cursor position. This includes updating the mouse cursor shape and sending necessary Control.mouse_entered, CollisionObject2D.mouse_entered, CollisionObject3D.mouse_entered and Window.mouse_entered signals and their respective mouse_exited counterparts.
m.Viewport.use_debanding: When using the Mobile or Forward+ renderers, set use_debanding to enable or disable the debanding feature of this Viewport. If use_hdr_2d is false, 2D rendering is not affected by debanding unless the Environment.background_mode is Environment.BG_CANVAS. If use_hdr_2d is true, debanding will only be applied if this is the root Viewport and will affect all 2D and 3D rendering, including canvas ite…
m.Viewport.use_hdr_2d: If true, 2D rendering will use a high dynamic range (HDR) RGBA16 format framebuffer. Additionally, 2D rendering will be performed on linear values and will be converted using the appropriate transfer function immediately before blitting to the screen (if the Viewport is attached to the screen).
m.Viewport.use_occlusion_culling: If true, OccluderInstance3D nodes will be usable for occlusion culling in 3D for this viewport. For the root viewport, ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/use_occlusion_culling must be set to true instead.
m.Viewport.use_taa: Enables temporal antialiasing for this viewport. TAA works by jittering the camera and accumulating the images of the last rendered frames, motion vector rendering is used to account for camera and object motion.
m.Viewport.use_xr: If true, the viewport will use the primary XR interface to render XR output. When applicable this can result in a stereoscopic image and the resulting render being output to a headset.
m.Viewport.vrs_mode: The Variable Rate Shading (VRS) mode that is used for this viewport. Note, if hardware does not support VRS this property is ignored.
m.Viewport.vrs_texture: Texture to use when vrs_mode is set to VRS_TEXTURE.
m.Viewport.vrs_update_mode: Sets the update mode for Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for the viewport. VRS requires the input texture to be converted to the format usable by the VRS method supported by the hardware. The update mode defines how often this happens. If the GPU does not support VRS, or VRS is not enabled, this property is ignored.
m.Viewport.warp_mouse: Moves the mouse pointer to the specified position in this Viewport using the coordinate system of this Viewport.
m.Viewport.world_2d: The custom World2D which can be used as 2D environment source.
m.Viewport.world_3d: The custom World3D which can be used as 3D environment source.
m.ViewportTexture.viewport_path: The path to the Viewport node to display. This is relative to the local scene root (see Resource.get_local_scene()), not to the nodes that use this texture.
m.VirtualJoystick.JOYSTICK_DYNAMIC: The joystick is moved to the initial touch position as long as it's within the joystick's bounds. It moves back to its original position when released.
m.VirtualJoystick.JOYSTICK_FOLLOWING: The joystick is moved to the initial touch position as long as it's within the joystick's bounds. It will follow the touch input if it goes outside the joystick's range. It moves back to its original position when released.
m.VirtualJoystick.VISIBILITY_WHEN_TOUCHED: The joystick is only visible when being touched.
m.VirtualJoystick.action_down: The action to trigger when the joystick is moved down.
m.VirtualJoystick.action_left: The action to trigger when the joystick is moved left.
m.VirtualJoystick.action_right: The action to trigger when the joystick is moved right.
m.VirtualJoystick.action_up: The action to trigger when the joystick is moved up.
m.VirtualJoystick.clampzone_ratio: The multiplier applied to the joystick's radius that defines the clamp zone.
m.VirtualJoystick.deadzone_ratio: The ratio of the joystick size that defines the joystick deadzone. The joystick tip must move beyond this ratio before being considered active.
m.VirtualJoystick.flick_canceled: Emitted when the tip enters the deadzone after being outside of it.
m.VirtualJoystick.flicked: Emitted when the tip moved outside the deadzone and the joystick is released. The input_vector contains the last input direction and strength before release. Its length is between 0.0 and 1.0.
m.VirtualJoystick.initial_offset_ratio: The initial position of the joystick as a ratio of the control's size. (0, 0) is top-left and (1, 1) is bottom-right.
m.VirtualJoystick.joystick_size: The size of the joystick in pixels.
m.VirtualJoystick.pressed: Emitted when the joystick is pressed.
m.VirtualJoystick.released: Emitted when the joystick is released. The input_vector is the final input direction and strength, with a length between 0.0 and 1.0.
m.VirtualJoystick.tapped: Emitted when the joystick is released without moving the tip.
m.VirtualJoystick.tip_size: The size of the joystick tip in pixels.
m.VisibleOnScreenEnabler2D.enable_mode: Determines how the target node is enabled. Corresponds to ProcessMode. When the node is disabled, it always uses Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED.
m.VisibleOnScreenEnabler2D.enable_node_pat: The path to the target node, relative to the VisibleOnScreenEnabler2D. The target node is cached; it's only assigned when setting this property (if the VisibleOnScreenEnabler2D is inside the scene tree) and every time the VisibleOnScreenEnabler2D enters the scene tree. If the path is empty, no node will be affected. If the path is invalid, an error is also generated.
m.VisibleOnScreenEnabler3D.enable_mode: Determines how the target node is enabled. Corresponds to ProcessMode. When the node is disabled, it always uses Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED.
m.VisibleOnScreenEnabler3D.enable_node_pat: The path to the target node, relative to the VisibleOnScreenEnabler3D. The target node is cached; it's only assigned when setting this property (if the VisibleOnScreenEnabler3D is inside the scene tree) and every time the VisibleOnScreenEnabler3D enters the scene tree. If the path is empty, no node will be affected. If the path is invalid, an error is also generated.
m.VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D.is_on_screen: If true, the bounding rectangle is on the screen.
m.VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D.screen_entered: Emitted when the VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D enters the screen.
m.VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D.screen_exited: Emitted when the VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D exits the screen.
m.VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D.show_rect: If true, shows the rectangle area of rect in the editor with a translucent magenta fill. Unlike changing the visibility of the VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D, this does not affect the screen culling detection.
m.VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D.is_on_screen: Returns true if the bounding box is on the screen.
m.VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D.screen_entered: Emitted when the VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D enters the screen.
m.VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D.screen_exited: Emitted when the VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D exits the screen.

m.VisualInstance3D.get_aabb: Returns the AABB (also known as the bounding box) for this VisualInstance3D.
m.VisualInstance3D.get_base: Returns the RID of the resource associated with this VisualInstance3D. For example, if the Node is a MeshInstance3D, this will return the RID of the associated Mesh.
m.VisualInstance3D.get_instance: Returns the RID of this instance. This RID is the same as the RID returned by RenderingServer.instance_create(). This RID is needed if you want to call RenderingServer functions directly on this VisualInstance3D.
m.VisualInstance3D.get_layer_mask_value: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the layers is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 20.
m.VisualInstance3D.layers: The render layer(s) this VisualInstance3D is drawn on.
m.VisualInstance3D.set_base: Sets the resource that is instantiated by this VisualInstance3D, which changes how the engine handles the VisualInstance3D under the hood. Equivalent to RenderingServer.instance_set_base().
m.VisualInstance3D.set_layer_mask_value: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the layers, given a layer_number between 1 and 20.
m.VisualInstance3D.sorting_offset: The amount by which the depth of this VisualInstance3D will be adjusted when sorting by depth. Uses the same units as the engine (which are typically meters). Adjusting it to a higher value will make the VisualInstance3D reliably draw on top of other VisualInstance3Ds that are otherwise positioned at the same spot. To ensure it always draws on top of other objects around it (not positioned at the…
m.VisualInstance3D.sorting_use_aabb_center: If true, the object is sorted based on the AABB center. The object will be sorted based on the global position otherwise.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_COLLIDE: A function for the "collide" stage (particle collision handler) of particle shader.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_FOG: A compute shader that runs for each froxel of the volumetric fog map.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_FRAGMENT: A fragment shader, operating on fragments (pixels).
m.VisualShader.TYPE_MAX: Represents the size of the Type enum.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_PROCESS: A function for the "process" stage of particle shader.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_PROCESS_CUSTOM: A function for the "process" stage of particle shader, with customized output.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_START: A function for the "start" stage of particle shader.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_START_CUSTOM: A function for the "start" stage of particle shader, with customized output.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_TEXTURE_BLIT: A shader used to process blit calls to a DrawableTexture.
m.VisualShader.TYPE_VERTEX: A vertex shader, operating on vertices.
m.VisualShader.VARYING_MODE_FRAG_TO_LIGHT: Varying is passed from Fragment function to Light function.
m.VisualShader.VARYING_MODE_MAX: Represents the size of the VaryingMode enum.
m.VisualShader.VARYING_MODE_VERTEX_TO_FRAG: Varying is passed from Vertex function to Fragment and Light functions.
m.VisualShader.VARYING_TYPE_MAX: Represents the size of the VaryingType enum.
m.VisualShader.VARYING_TYPE_UINT: Varying is of type unsigned int.
m.VisualShader.add_node: Adds the specified node to the shader.
m.VisualShader.add_varying: Adds a new varying value node to the shader.
m.VisualShader.attach_node_to_frame: Attaches the given node to the given frame.
m.VisualShader.can_connect_nodes: Returns true if the specified nodes and ports can be connected together.
m.VisualShader.connect_nodes: Connects the specified nodes and ports.
m.VisualShader.connect_nodes_forced: Connects the specified nodes and ports, even if they can't be connected. Such connection is invalid and will not function properly.
m.VisualShader.detach_node_from_frame: Detaches the given node from the frame it is attached to.
m.VisualShader.disconnect_nodes: Connects the specified nodes and ports.
m.VisualShader.get_node: Returns the shader node instance with specified type and id.
m.VisualShader.get_node_connections: Returns the list of connected nodes with the specified type.
m.VisualShader.get_node_list: Returns the list of all nodes in the shader with the specified type.
m.VisualShader.get_node_position: Returns the position of the specified node within the shader graph.
m.VisualShader.get_valid_node_id: Returns next valid node ID that can be added to the shader graph.
m.VisualShader.graph_offset: Deprecated: This property does nothing and always equals to zero.
m.VisualShader.has_varying: Returns true if the shader has a varying with the given name.
m.VisualShader.is_node_connection: Returns true if the specified node and port connection exist.
m.VisualShader.remove_node: Removes the specified node from the shader.
m.VisualShader.remove_varying: Removes a varying value node with the given name. Prints an error if a node with this name is not found.
m.VisualShader.replace_node: Replaces the specified node with a node of new class type.
m.VisualShader.set_mode: Sets the mode of this shader.
m.VisualShader.set_node_position: Sets the position of the specified node.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_BOOLEAN: Boolean type. Translated to bool type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_MAX: Represents the size of the PortType enum.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_SAMPLER: Sampler type. Translated to reference of sampler uniform in shader code. Can only be used for input ports in non-uniform nodes.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_SCALAR: Floating-point scalar. Translated to float type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_SCALAR_INT: Integer scalar. Translated to int type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_SCALAR_UINT: Unsigned integer scalar. Translated to uint type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_TRANSFORM: Transform type. Translated to mat4 type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_VECTOR_2D: 2D vector of floating-point values. Translated to vec2 type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_VECTOR_3D: 3D vector of floating-point values. Translated to vec3 type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.PORT_TYPE_VECTOR_4D: 4D vector of floating-point values. Translated to vec4 type in shader code.
m.VisualShaderNode.clear_default_input_val: Clears the default input ports value.
m.VisualShaderNode.get_default_input_port: Returns the input port which should be connected by default when this node is created as a result of dragging a connection from an existing node to the empty space on the graph.
m.VisualShaderNode.get_default_input_value: Returns an Array containing default values for all of the input ports of the node in the form [index0, value0, index1, value1, ...].
m.VisualShaderNode.get_input_port_default_: Returns the default value of the input port.
m.VisualShaderNode.linked_parent_graph_fra: Represents the index of the frame this node is linked to. If set to -1 the node is not linked to any frame.
m.VisualShaderNode.output_port_for_preview: Sets the output port index which will be showed for preview. If set to -1 no port will be open for preview.
m.VisualShaderNode.remove_input_port_defau: Removes the default value of the input port.
m.VisualShaderNode.set_default_input_value: Sets the default input ports values using an Array of the form [index0, value0, index1, value1, ...]. For example: [0, Vector3(0, 0, 0), 1, Vector3(0, 0, 0)].
m.VisualShaderNode.set_input_port_default_: Sets the default value for the selected input port.
m.VisualShaderNodeBillboard.BILLBOARD_TYPE: Billboarding is disabled and the node does nothing.
A standard billboarding algorithm is enabled.
A billboarding algorithm to rotate around Y-axis is enabled.
Represents the size of the BillboardType enum.
A billboarding algorithm designed to use on particles is enabled.
m.VisualShaderNodeBillboard.billboard_type: Controls how the object faces the camera.
m.VisualShaderNodeBillboard.keep_scale: If true, the shader will keep the scale set for the mesh. Otherwise, the scale is lost when billboarding.
m.VisualShaderNodeBooleanConstant.constant: A boolean constant which represents a state of this node.
m.VisualShaderNodeBooleanParameter.default: A default value to be assigned within the shader.
m.VisualShaderNodeClamp.OP_TYPE_MAX: Represents the size of the OpType enum.
m.VisualShaderNodeClamp.op_type: A type of operands and returned value.
m.VisualShaderNodeColorConstant.constant: A Color constant which represents a state of this node.
m.VisualShaderNodeColorFunc.FUNC_GRAYSCALE: Converts the color to grayscale using the following formula:

If create_visual_debug is true, after baking the light, this will generate a MultiMesh that has a cube representing each solid cell with each cube colored to the cell's albedo color. This can be used to visualize the VoxelGI's dat…
m.VoxelGI.camera_attributes: The CameraAttributes resource that specifies exposure levels to bake at. Auto-exposure and non exposure properties will be ignored. Exposure settings should be used to reduce the dynamic range present when baking. If exposure is too high, the VoxelGI will have banding artifacts or may have over-exposure artifacts.
m.VoxelGI.data: The VoxelGIData resource that holds the data for this VoxelGI.
m.VoxelGI.size: The size of the area covered by the VoxelGI. This must be 1.0 or greater on each axis.
m.VoxelGI.subdiv: Number of times to subdivide the grid that the VoxelGI operates on. A higher number results in finer detail and thus higher visual quality, while lower numbers result in better performance.
m.VoxelGIData.allocate: Initializes this VoxelGIData with the specified data. octree_cells must be a multiple of 32. octree_cells must be double the size of data_cells. The allocated data can be retrieved later using the various getter methods.
m.VoxelGIData.bias: The normal bias to use for indirect lighting and reflections. Higher values reduce self-reflections visible in non-rough materials, at the cost of more visible light leaking and flatter-looking indirect lighting. To prioritize hiding self-reflections over lighting quality, set bias to 0.0 and normal_bias to a value between 1.0 and 2.0.
m.VoxelGIData.dynamic_range: The dynamic range to use (1.0 represents a low dynamic range scene brightness). Higher values can be used to provide brighter indirect lighting, at the cost of more visible color banding in dark areas (both in indirect lighting and reflections). To avoid color banding, it's recommended to use the lowest value that does not result in visible light clipping.
m.VoxelGIData.energy: The energy of the indirect lighting and reflections produced by the VoxelGI node. Higher values result in brighter indirect lighting. If indirect lighting looks too flat, try decreasing propagation while increasing energy at the same time. See also use_two_bounces which influences the indirect lighting's effective brightness.
m.VoxelGIData.get_bounds: Returns the bounds of the baked voxel data as an AABB, which should match VoxelGI.size after being baked (which only contains the size as a Vector3).
m.VoxelGIData.get_data_cells: Returns the baked cell data for this VoxelGIData.
m.VoxelGIData.get_level_counts: Returns the baked level counts for this VoxelGIData.
m.VoxelGIData.get_octree_cells: Returns the baked octree cell data for this VoxelGIData.
m.VoxelGIData.get_octree_size: Returns the baked octree size for this VoxelGIData, which corresponds to the number of subdivisions per axis. This can be viewed in the editor by hovering the Bake VoxelGI button at the top of the 3D editor viewport when a VoxelGI node is selected and looking at the Subdivisions field in the tooltip.
m.VoxelGIData.get_to_cell_xform: Returns the baked cell transform for this VoxelGIData.
m.VoxelGIData.interior: If true, Environment lighting is ignored by the VoxelGI node. If false, Environment lighting is taken into account by the VoxelGI node. Environment lighting updates in real-time, which means it can be changed without having to bake the VoxelGI node again.
m.VoxelGIData.normal_bias: The normal bias to use for indirect lighting and reflections. Higher values reduce self-reflections visible in non-rough materials, at the cost of more visible light leaking and flatter-looking indirect lighting. See also bias. To prioritize hiding self-reflections over lighting quality, set bias to 0.0 and normal_bias to a value between 1.0 and 2.0.
m.VoxelGIData.propagation: The multiplier to use when light bounces off a surface. Higher values result in brighter indirect lighting. If indirect lighting looks too flat, try decreasing propagation while increasing energy at the same time. See also use_two_bounces which influences the indirect lighting's effective brightness.
m.VoxelGIData.use_two_bounces: If true, performs two bounces of indirect lighting instead of one. This makes indirect lighting look more natural and brighter at a small performance cost. The second bounce is also visible in reflections. If the scene appears too bright after enabling use_two_bounces, adjust propagation and energy.

m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.add_peer: Add a new peer to the mesh with the given peer_id. The WebRTCPeerConnection must be in state WebRTCPeerConnection.STATE_NEW.
m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.create_client: Initialize the multiplayer peer as a client with the given peer_id (must be between 2 and 2147483647). In this mode, you should only call add_peer() once and with peer_id of 1. This mode enables MultiplayerPeer.is_server_relay_supported(), allowing the upper MultiplayerAPI layer to perform peer exchange and packet relaying.
m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.create_mesh: Initialize the multiplayer peer as a mesh (i.e. all peers connect to each other) with the given peer_id (must be between 1 and 2147483647).
m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.create_server: Initialize the multiplayer peer as a server (with unique ID of 1). This mode enables MultiplayerPeer.is_server_relay_supported(), allowing the upper MultiplayerAPI layer to perform peer exchange and packet relaying.
m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.get_peer: Returns a dictionary representation of the peer with given peer_id with three keys. "connection" containing the WebRTCPeerConnection to this peer, "channels" an array of three WebRTCDataChannel, and "connected" a boolean representing if the peer connection is currently connected (all three channels are open).
m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.get_peers: Returns a dictionary which keys are the peer ids and values the peer representation as in get_peer().
m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.has_peer: Returns true if the given peer_id is in the peers map (it might not be connected though).
m.WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.remove_peer: Remove the peer with given peer_id from the mesh. If the peer was connected, and MultiplayerPeer.peer_connected was emitted for it, then MultiplayerPeer.peer_disconnected will be emitted.
m.WebRTCPeerConnection.GATHERING_STATE_COM: The ICE agent has finished gathering candidates. If something happens that requires collecting new candidates, such as a new interface being added or the addition of a new ICE server, the state will revert to gathering to gather those candidates.
m.WebRTCPeerConnection.GATHERING_STATE_GAT: The ICE agent is in the process of gathering candidates for the connection.
m.WebRTCPeerConnection.GATHERING_STATE_NEW: The peer connection was just created and hasn't done any networking yet.
m.WebRTCPeerConnection.SIGNALING_STATE_HAV: The local peer has called set_local_description(), passing in SDP representing an offer (usually created by calling create_offer()), and the offer has been applied successfully.

The offer sent by the remote peer has been applied and an answer has been created and applied by calling set_local_description(). This provisional answer describes the supported media formats and so forth, but may not have a complete set of ICE candidates included. Further candidates will be delivered separately later.
The remote peer has created an offer and used the signaling server to deliver it to the local peer, which has set the offer as the remote description by calling set_remote_description().
A provisional answer has been received and successfully applied in response to an offer previously sent and established by calling set_local_description().

m.WebRTCPeerConnection.set_local_descripti: Sets the SDP description of the local peer. This should be called in response to session_description_created.

m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.create_client: Starts a new multiplayer client connecting to the given url. TLS certificates will be verified against the hostname when connecting using the wss:// protocol. You can pass the optional tls_client_options parameter to customize the trusted certification authorities, or disable the common name verification. See TLSOptions.client() and TLSOptions.client_unsafe().
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.create_server: Starts a new multiplayer server listening on the given port. You can optionally specify a bind_address, and provide valid tls_server_options to use TLS. See TLSOptions.server().
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.get_peer: Returns the WebSocketPeer associated to the given peer_id.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.get_peer_addres: Returns the IP address of the given peer.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.get_peer_port: Returns the remote port of the given peer.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.handshake_heade: The extra headers to use during handshake. See WebSocketPeer.handshake_headers for more details.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.handshake_timeo: The maximum time each peer can stay in a connecting state before being dropped.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.inbound_buffer_: The inbound buffer size for connected peers. See WebSocketPeer.inbound_buffer_size for more details.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.max_queued_pack: The maximum number of queued packets for connected peers. See WebSocketPeer.max_queued_packets for more details.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.outbound_buffer: The outbound buffer size for connected peers. See WebSocketPeer.outbound_buffer_size for more details.
m.WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.supported_proto: The supported WebSocket sub-protocols. See WebSocketPeer.supported_protocols for more details.
m.WebSocketPeer.STATE_CLOSED: The connection is closed or couldn't be opened.
m.WebSocketPeer.STATE_CLOSING: The connection is in the process of closing. This means a close request has been sent to the remote peer but confirmation has not been received.
m.WebSocketPeer.STATE_CONNECTING: Socket has been created. The connection is not yet open.
m.WebSocketPeer.STATE_OPEN: The connection is open and ready to communicate.
m.WebSocketPeer.WRITE_MODE_BINARY: Specifies that WebSockets messages should be transferred as binary payload (any byte combination is allowed).
m.WebSocketPeer.WRITE_MODE_TEXT: Specifies that WebSockets messages should be transferred as text payload (only valid UTF-8 is allowed).
m.WebSocketPeer.accept_stream: Accepts a peer connection performing the HTTP handshake as a WebSocket server. The stream must be a valid TCP stream retrieved via TCPServer.take_connection(), or a TLS stream accepted via StreamPeerTLS.accept_stream().
m.WebSocketPeer.connect_to_url: Connects to the given URL. TLS certificates will be verified against the hostname when connecting using the wss:// protocol. You can pass the optional tls_client_options parameter to customize the trusted certification authorities, or disable the common name verification. See TLSOptions.client() and TLSOptions.client_unsafe().
m.WebSocketPeer.get_close_code: Returns the received WebSocket close frame status code, or -1 when the connection was not cleanly closed. Only call this method when get_ready_state() returns STATE_CLOSED.
m.WebSocketPeer.get_close_reason: Returns the received WebSocket close frame status reason string. Only call this method when get_ready_state() returns STATE_CLOSED.
m.WebSocketPeer.get_connected_host: Returns the IP address of the connected peer.
m.WebSocketPeer.get_connected_port: Returns the remote port of the connected peer.
m.WebSocketPeer.get_current_outbound_buffe: Returns the current amount of data in the outbound websocket buffer. Note: Web exports use WebSocket.bufferedAmount, while other platforms use an internal buffer.
m.WebSocketPeer.get_ready_state: Returns the ready state of the connection.
m.WebSocketPeer.get_requested_url: Returns the URL requested by this peer. The URL is derived from the url passed to connect_to_url() or from the HTTP headers when acting as server (i.e. when using accept_stream()).
m.WebSocketPeer.get_selected_protocol: Returns the selected WebSocket sub-protocol for this connection or an empty string if the sub-protocol has not been selected yet.
m.WebSocketPeer.handshake_headers: The extra HTTP headers to be sent during the WebSocket handshake.
m.WebSocketPeer.heartbeat_interval: The interval (in seconds) at which the peer will automatically send WebSocket "ping" control frames. When set to 0, no "ping" control frames will be sent.
m.WebSocketPeer.inbound_buffer_size: The size of the input buffer in bytes (roughly the maximum amount of memory that will be allocated for the inbound packets).
m.WebSocketPeer.max_queued_packets: The maximum amount of packets that will be allowed in the queues (both inbound and outbound).
m.WebSocketPeer.outbound_buffer_size: The size of the input buffer in bytes (roughly the maximum amount of memory that will be allocated for the outbound packets).
m.WebSocketPeer.poll: Updates the connection state and receive incoming packets. Call this function regularly to keep it in a clean state.
m.WebSocketPeer.send: Sends the given message using the desired write_mode. When sending a String, prefer using send_text().
m.WebSocketPeer.send_text: Sends the given message using WebSocket text mode. Prefer this method over PacketPeer.put_packet() when interacting with third-party text-based API (e.g. when using JSON formatted messages).
m.WebSocketPeer.set_no_delay: Disable Nagle's algorithm on the underlying TCP socket (default). See StreamPeerTCP.set_no_delay() for more information.
m.WebSocketPeer.supported_protocols: The WebSocket sub-protocols allowed during the WebSocket handshake.
m.WebSocketPeer.was_string_packet: Returns true if the last received packet was sent as a text payload. See WriteMode.

m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_ASPECT_EXPAND: The content's aspect will be preserved. If the target size has different aspect from the base one, the content will stay in the top-left corner and add an extra visible area in the stretched space.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_ASPECT_IGNORE: The aspect will be ignored. Scaling will simply stretch the content to fit the target size.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_ASPECT_KEEP: The content's aspect will be preserved. If the target size has different aspect from the base one, the image will be centered and black bars will appear on left and right sides.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_ASPECT_KEEP_HEIGHT: The content can be expanded horizontally. Scaling vertically will result in keeping the height ratio and then black bars on top and bottom sides.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_ASPECT_KEEP_WIDTH: The content can be expanded vertically. Scaling horizontally will result in keeping the width ratio and then black bars on left and right sides.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_MODE_CANVAS_ITEMS: The content will be rendered at the target size. This is more performance-expensive than CONTENT_SCALE_MODE_VIEWPORT, but provides better results.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_MODE_DISABLED: The content will not be scaled to match the Window's size (content_scale_size is ignored).
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_MODE_VIEWPORT: The content will be rendered at the base size and then scaled to the target size. More performant than CONTENT_SCALE_MODE_CANVAS_ITEMS, but results in pixelated image.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_STRETCH_FRACTIONAL: The content will be stretched according to a fractional factor. This fills all the space available in the window, but allows "pixel wobble" to occur due to uneven pixel scaling.
m.Window.CONTENT_SCALE_STRETCH_INTEGER: The content will be stretched only according to an integer factor, preserving sharp pixels. This may leave a black background visible on the window's edges depending on the window size.
m.Window.FLAG_ALWAYS_ON_TOP: The window is floating on top of all other windows. This flag is ignored for full-screen windows. Set with always_on_top.
m.Window.FLAG_BORDERLESS: The window do not have native title bar and other decorations. This flag is ignored for full-screen windows. Set with borderless.
m.Window.FLAG_EXCLUDE_FROM_CAPTURE: Windows is excluded from screenshots taken by DisplayServer.screen_get_image(), DisplayServer.screen_get_image_rect(), and DisplayServer.screen_get_pixel().
m.Window.FLAG_EXTEND_TO_TITLE: Window content is expanded to the full size of the window. Unlike borderless window, the frame is left intact and can be used to resize the window, title bar is transparent, but have minimize/maximize/close buttons. Set with extend_to_title.
m.Window.FLAG_MOUSE_PASSTHROUGH: All mouse events are passed to the underlying window of the same application.
m.Window.FLAG_NO_FOCUS: The window can't be focused. No-focus window will ignore all input, except mouse clicks. Set with unfocusable.
m.Window.FLAG_POPUP: Window is part of menu or OptionButton dropdown. This flag can't be changed when the window is visible. An active popup window will exclusively receive all input, without stealing focus from its parent. Popup windows are automatically closed when uses click outside it, or when an application is switched. Popup window must have transient parent set (see transient).
m.Window.FLAG_POPUP_WM_HINT: Signals the window manager that this window is supposed to be an implementation-defined "popup" (usually a floating, borderless, untileable and immovable child window).
m.Window.FLAG_RESIZE_DISABLED: The window can't be resized by dragging its resize grip. It's still possible to resize the window using size. This flag is ignored for full screen windows. Set with unresizable.
m.Window.FLAG_SHARP_CORNERS: Window style is overridden, forcing sharp corners.
m.Window.FLAG_TRANSPARENT: The window background can be transparent. Set with transparent.

m.Window.LAYOUT_DIRECTION_SYSTEM_LOCALE: Automatic layout direction, determined from the system locale.

m.Window.MODE_FULLSCREEN: Full screen mode with full multi-window support.

m.Window.MODE_MINIMIZED: Minimized window mode, i.e. Window is not visible and available on window manager's window list. Normally happens when the minimize button is pressed.
m.Window.MODE_WINDOWED: Windowed mode, i.e. Window doesn't occupy the whole screen (unless set to the size of the screen).
